# Bhavisya-purana 2

## Madhyaparva Part 1

## Chapter 1. Introductory Verses

## \|\| 2.1.1 \|\|

*śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ namaḥ kamaladalanayanābhirāmāya \|*  
*śrīrāmacaṃdrāya \|*  
*svacchaṃ caṃdrāvadātaṃ kavikaramakarakṣobhasaṃjātaphenaṃ bakṣodbhūtiprasūktairvrataniyamaparaiḥ sevitaṃ vipramukhyaiḥ \|*  
*oṃkārālaṃkṛtena tribhuvanaguruṇā brahmaṇā dṛṣṭapūtaṃ saṃbhogābhogagamyaṃ janakaluṣaharaṃ pauṣkaraṃ vaḥ punātu \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Let the auspicious water of Puskara purify your soul. It is spotless, clean, bright like the moon, where rises the foam with the disturbance of Brahma’s hand, like a makara or the crocodile. It is served by the Brahmanas who deliver the discourses on the origin of Brahma and perform all the vratas following the rules. It is beautified with omkara and is purified with the sight of Brahma’s eyes, who happens to be the preceptor of the world. It is approachable by the rich and the poor alike and is the destroyer of the sins of the humans.

## \|\| 2.1.2 \|\|

*jayati bhuvanadīpo bhāskaro lokakartā jayati ca śitidehaḥ śārṅgadhanvā murāriḥ \|*  
*jayati ca śaśimaulī rudranāmābhidheyo jayati sakalamaulirbhānu māṃścitrabhānuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Victory to lord Bhaskara (the Sun) who is the lamp for the world and illuminates all the bhuvanas. He is the creator of the worlds. Lord Murari has the bright complexion and holds a bow in his hand. Victory to him. Victory to lord Rudra with a crescent decorating his head. Victory to the Sungod, who is the foremost of the entire universe, possessing (a thousand) rays.

## \|\| 2.1.3 \|\|

*namaskṛtyāprameyāya devāya brahmarūpiṇe \|*  
*purāṇaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yaduktaṃ brahmayoginā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Salutation to the god, who is unparallel, form of Brahman, I am going to reveal the part of the Puraria, which has been spoken by sage Vyasa - the Brahma-yogi.

## \|\| 2.1.4 \|\|

*purāṇasaṃhitāṃ puṇyāṃ papracchū raumaharṣaṇim \|*  
*vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ purāṇārthaviśārada \|\| 4 \|\|*

4.Once the great Rsis put a question to the sage Romaharsana saying - “O saint well-versed in the texts of the Puranas, you kindly recite to us the auspicious Purana Samhita.”

## \|\| 2.1.5 \|\|

*munīnāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā sūtaḥ paurāṇikottamaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya manasā prāha guruṃ satyavatīsutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The eminent Suta, listening to the words of the Risis, mentally offered his salutation to the sage Vyasa - his preceptor and then addressed the audience.

## \|\| 2.1.6-14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*namaskṛtya jagadyoniṃ brahmarūpadharaṃ harim \|*  
*vakṣye paurāṇikīṃ divyāṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yacchrutvā pāpakarmāṇi sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitramāyuṣyamidānīṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyapurāṇamakhilaṃ yajjagāda gadādharaḥ \|*  
*madhyaparva hyatho vakṣye pratiṣṭhādivinirṇayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dharmapraśaṃsanaṃ cātra brāhmaṇādipraśaṃsanam \|*  
*āpaddharmasya kathanaṃ vidyāmāhātmyavardhanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pratimākaraṇaṃ caiva sthāpanācitralakṣaṇam \|*  
*kālavyavasthāsargādipratisargādilakṣaṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*purāṇalakṣaṇaṃ caiva bhūgolasya ca nirṇayam \|*  
*nirūpaṇaṃ tithīnāṃ ca śrāddhasaṃkalpamantaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mumūrṣorapi yatkarma dānamāhātmyameva ca \|*  
*bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca yugadharmānuśāsanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*uccāvacāvadhānaṃ ca prāyaścittādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*ṣaṣṭyādhikāṣṭasāhasranavaślokaśatodbhavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*paṃcataṃtrasamāyuktaṃ pratitaṃtre ca viṃśatiḥ \|*  
*paṃcottaraṃ tathādhyāyāḥ purāṇe'smindvijottamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

6-14. Suta said- Offering salutation to lord Visnu —the creator of the universe, who took to tire form of Brahman, I am reciting the story of the Puraria, which is divine and is the remover of the sins. Listening to the Parana, the sins are removed and one achieves the best of position or salvation. О Brahmanas, I am revealing all the salient features of the auspicious and sacred text, which bestows long life and which is known as the Bhavisya Parana, which you please listen. These details had been spoken by the lord who is the carrier of club. Accordingly, the name of this Parva would be the Madhyama Parva. The subjects like die creation, the praise of dharma, praise of the Brahmanas, the form of dharma at the time of calamity, the glory of education, creation of the images and their consecration besides their wonderful symptoms, the arrangement of periods like sargas (or creation), the symptoms of pratisargas, the symptoms of the Purdyas, the round shape of the earth, the decision about the tithis or moon days and the samkalpa of the sraddhas have been spelt out. Similarly, the rites to be performed for the people on the death bed, the glory of charities as well as the dharma of the respective yugas, arrangement for the discipline of past and present, besides the regulating of the future has been dealt with. In addition to the above, the high and low type of the repentances have been defined. There are eight thousand nine hundred and eight verses in this parva, besides the five tantras. 0 best of the Brahmanas, each one of the tantra has twenty five chapters.

## \|\| 2.1.15 \|\|

*trayāṇāmāśramāṇāṃ ca gṛhastho yonirucyate \|*  
*anye'pi sūpajīvanti tasmācchreṣṭho gṛhāśramī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The genesis of the three asramas has been attributed to the householder, because it also infuses life in others. Therefore, the life of the householder is the foremost of all the asramas.

## \|\| 2.1.16 \|\|

*ekāśramaṃ gṛhasthasya trayāṇāṃ mūrtidarśanam \|*  
*tasmādgārhasthamevaikaṃ vijñeyaṃ dharmaśāsanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The household is the only visible source of creation of the other Puranas. Therefore, getting linked with the religious discipline, the knowledge of the dharma of a householder is essential.

## \|\| 2.1.17 \|\|

*parityajedarthakāmau yau syātāṃ dharmavarjitau \|*  
*sarvalokaviruddhaṃ ca dharmamapyācarenna tu \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When artha and kama are devoid of dharma, they should be discarded, besides those who are against dharma.

## \|\| 2.1.18-19 \|\|

*taḍāgasya ca sānnidhye taḍāgaṃ parivarjayet \|*  
*prapāsthāne prapā varjyā maṭhasthāne maṭhaṃ tyajet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dharmātsaṃjāyate hyartho dharmātkāmo'bhijāyate \|*  
*dharmādevāpavargo'yaṃ tasmāddharmaṃ samāśrayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. A tank close to another tank and a place for free supply of drinking water should not be created close to the existing one, besides a temple should not be built close to another temple which exists already. Dharma generalize artha and kama, which leads to salvation. Therefore, the following of dharma is essential.

## \|\| 2.1.20 \|\|

*dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca trivargastriguṇo mataḥ \|*  
*sattvaṃ rajastamaśceti tasmāddharmaṃ samāśrayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The dharma, artha and kama are known as Trivarga. The sattva, rajas and tamas are also known as Trivarga. Besides the sattva, rajas and tamas - the three gunas also emerge out of dharma. Therefore, dharma must be followed as prescribed by the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.1.21 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ gacchaṃti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhaṃti rājasāḥ \|*  
*jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchaṃti tāmasāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A person having excess of sattva guna attains the heaven; the one who has rajoguna in excess achieves the earth; and the one who practices the deplorable deeds is known as tamoguni and he falls in the hell.

## \|\| 2.1.22 \|\|

*yasmindharmaḥ samāyukto hyarthakāmau vyavasthitau \|*  
*iha loke sukhī bhūtvā pretyānaṃtyāya kalpate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A person whose artha and kama are religious or auspicious, he enjoying all the comforts in the world, ultimately gets absorbed in lord Ananta.

## \|\| 2.1.23 \|\|

*tasmādarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca yuktvā dharmaṃ samāśrayet \|*  
*dharmātsaṃjāyate kāmo dharmādarthobhijāyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Therefore, one should aspire to achieve auspicious artha and kama through dharma, because kama and artha are said to have emerged out of dharma.

## \|\| 2.1.24 \|\|

*evaṃ dharmasya madhye'yaṃ caturvargaḥ pradarśitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ ca dharmakāmārthaṃ mokṣasyāpi ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ vānutiṣṭhecca sa cānaṃtyāya kalpate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Similarly, the Caturvarga viz., dharma, artha, kama and moksa are said to have been enshrined in dharma. A person thus following dharma, artha and kama, contemplates on the importance of moksa. As a result of this, he achieves the lord Ananta.

## \|\| 2.1.25 \|\|

*tasmādarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca muktvā dharmaṃ samācaret \|*  
*dharmātsaṃjāyate sarvamityāhurbrahmavādinaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Therefore, discarding artha and kama, one should surely follow dharma, because those who are well-versed in Brahman, has ordained that one can achieve everything through dharma.

## \|\| 2.1.26 \|\|

*dharmeṇa dhāryate sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|*  
*anādinidhanā śaktirnaiṣā brāhmī dvijottama \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О best of the Brahmanas, the mobile and immobile world stands with the support of dharma and not that the eternal power of Brahman holds the same.

## \|\| 2.1.27 \|\|

*karmaṇā prāpyate dharmo jñānena ca na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasmājjñānena sahitaṃ karmayogaṃ samācaret \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With the activities based on the divine knowledge, dharma is achieved. There is no doubt about it. Therefore, the (auspicious) activities should be started with the divine knowledge.

## \|\| 2.1.28 \|\|

*pravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca dvividhaṃ karma vaidikam \|*  
*jñānapūrvā nivṛttiḥ syātpravṛttirvartate'nyathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Pravrtti (inclination of mind) and Nivrtti (retirement) are the two types of activities to be followed by a person according to the Vedas. Out of these two, the performing of the activities with consciousness lead the people to renunciation and those without them, to self indulgence.

## \|\| 2.1.29 \|\|

*nivṛttiṃ sevamānastu yāti tatparamaṃ padam \|*  
*tasmānnivṛttaṃ saṃsevyamanyathā saṃsaretpunaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By following the path of renunciation, a person achieves the highest place. Therefore, one should always follow the path of renunciation, otherwise it would be difficult to renounce the world.

## \|\| 2.1.30-32 \|\|

*śamo damo dayā dānamalobhastyāga eva ca \|*  
*ārjavaṃ cānasūyā ca tīrthānusaraṇaṃ tathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*satyaṃ saṃtoṣa āstikyaṃ śraddhā cendriyanigrahaḥ \|*  
*devatābhyarcanaṃ pūjā brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ahiṃsā satyavāditvamapaiśunyaṃ sukalpatā \|*  
*śaucācāraścānukaṃpā sarvavarṇe'bravīnmuniḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Exercising of self control, compassion, mercy, giving of charities, devoid of greed, renunciation, honesty, going on pilgrimage, truthfulness, satisfaction, faith in god, to be a believer in god, control of sense organs, worship of gods including the Brahmanas, nonviolence, to be truthful, not to talk ill of others, to indulge in beautiful imaginations, purity, performing of noble deeds and to be merciful on others, are to be followed by the people of all the varnas, as per the command of the sages.

## \|\| 2.1.33-35 \|\|

*śraddhāpūrvāḥ smṛtā dharmāḥ śraddhāmadhye tu saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*śraddhāniṣṭhāḥ pratiṣṭhāśca dharmāḥ śraddheva kīrtitāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*prājāpatyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ śrutaṃ sthānaṃ kriyāvatām \|*  
*sthānamaindraṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ saṃgrāmeṣvapalāyinām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vaiśyānāmamṛtaṃ sthānaṃ svadharmamanuvartatām \|*  
*gāṃdharvaṃ śūdrajīvānāṃ paricāreṇa vartatām \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. The faith is enshrined in dharma, while dharma is lodged in the faith. A person who is of religious mind, the faith rests in him. For die active Brahmanas, the only resort is the place of Prajapati. Indra is the place for the warriors, who do not flee from the battlefield. The Vaidyas who follow the dharma, for them the amrta-sthana is earmarked and for the Sudras who serve others, the place of Gandharvas is meant.

## \|\| 2.1.36-39 \|\|

*aṣṭāśīti sahasrāṇāṃ munīnāmūrdhvaretasām \|*  
*smṛtaṃ sthānaṃ tu yatsthānaṃ tadeva guruvāsinām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*saptarṣīṇāṃ tu yatsthānaṃ śrutaṃ tadvai vanaukasām \|*  
*prājāpatyaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ sthānamuktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yatīnāṃ yatacittānāṃ tadeva vanavāsinām \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaṃ yatsthānaṃ tasmānnāvartate punaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yogināmamṛtaṃ sthānaṃ vyomākhyaṃ paramākaram \|*  
*ānaṃdamaiśvaraṃ nāma sā kāṣṭhā paramā gatiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. The Balakhilya sages who are said to be eighty eight thousand in number, for them adequate places have been defined. The same place is meant for the householders. The place of Saptarisis can also be used by the other Rsis. For the householders, the place of Prajapati has been fixed by Brahma himself. The yogins can stay in Hiranyagarbha. It is the place, where a person on his reaching there, does not return. Those who are engaged in yogic practices are also supposed to stay at the same place. The yogins are required to occupy the best place known as vyoma, which is also known as Isvarananda and which happens to be the last limit.

## Chapter 2. The Creation

## \|\| 2.2.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*idānīṃ vistaraṃ caiva vibhāgaṃ rūpamaiśvaram \|*  
*vakṣye kalpānusāreṇa manvataraśatānugam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said - I am now speaking about the forms of lord Isvara, besides its fractions and the related expansion. In the same expansion, according to a kalpa (aeon), hundreds of manvantaras (fourteenth part of the day of Brahma) emerge out of the same.

## \|\| 2.2.2 \|\|

*āsīttamomayaṃ sarvamaprajñātamalakṣaṇam \|*  
*tatra caiko mahānāsīdrudraḥ paramakāraṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There was a form of complete darkness, which was spread in the entire universe. No symptoms or description of the same could be provided But Rudra is the primary cause of the same

## \|\| 2.2.3 \|\|

*ātmanā svayamātmānaṃ sañcitya bhagavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*manaḥ saṃsṛjate pūrvamahaṃkāraṃ ca pṛṣṭhataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О all pervading one, the lord himself was then engaged in meditation, first of all created the nund and then the arrogance.

## \|\| 2.2.4 \|\|

*ahaṃkārātprajānāti mahābhūtāni pañca ca \|*  
*aṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ proktā vikārāścaiva ṣoḍaśa \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then out of arrogance or pride were cleared the five Mahabhutas (the five elements vtr.. earth, air, water and fire, besides ether, the eight prakrtis and the sixteen vikaras (deficiencies).

## \|\| 2.2.5 \|\|

*śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca raso gaṃdhastathaiva ca \|*  
*prāṇo'pānaḥ samānaścodānavyānau tathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereafter, the sabda (word), sparsa (touch), rupa (beauty), rasa (essence), gandha (fragrance), prana - the five vital airs, vis., breath, air. wind, strength, etc., also known as prana, apana. samana, udana and vyana

## \|\| 2.2.6 \|\|

*sattvaṃ rajastamaścaiva guṇāḥ proktāstu te trayaḥ \|*  
*tasmādbhāgavato brahmā tasmādviṣṇurajāyata \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The gunas are said to be three viz., sattva, rajas and tamas. Therefore, Brahma was bom from Brahman, while Visnu emerged out of Brahma.

## \|\| 2.2.7-8 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇumohanārthaṃ tataḥ śaṃbhustu tejasā \|*  
*aśarīro vāsudevo hyanutpattirayonijaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vyāmohayitvā tatsarvaṃ tejasā'mohayajjagat \|*  
*tasmātparataraṃ nāsti tasmātparataraṃ na hi \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Then Siva was bom out of the conflict of Brahma and Visnu. Then emerged Vasudeva - the supreme Brahman, without having a physical appearance or a body, who is said to have been bom without human contact, stupefying the world and confusing the entire world There is none better than him, nor is there any possibility of anyone being so in future.

## \|\| 2.2.9-10 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇuśca dvāvetāvudbhūtau bhagavatsutau \|*  
*kalpekalpe tu tatsarvaṃ sṛjate'sau janaṃ jagat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*upasaṃharate caiva nānābhūtāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*dvāsaptatiyugānyeva manvantara iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Two sons of the lord known as Brahma and Visnu were initially born, who resort to creation on each one of the aeon and also destroyed them in due course of time. A Manvantara is said to be composed of the period of seventy two yugas.

## \|\| 2.2.11 \|\|

*caturdaśa tu tānyevaṃ kalpa ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*dinaikaṃ brahmaṇaḥ proktaṃ niśi kalpastathocyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. (A yuga comprises of twelve years) and a period of fourteen yugas (168 years) is known as kalpa. The same kalpa is known to be a day for BrahmS and similar is the case with the night

## \|\| 2.2.12 \|\|

*evaṃ māsaśca varṣaśca tathā cāṣṭaśataṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ buddhīndriyasyāsya viṣṇośca nimiṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О Brahmanas, thus eight hundred months and the time of a year is said to be a nimisa s or the time of the twinkling of an eye for Vi$pu besides the buddhi (intelligence) and sense organs.

## \|\| 2.2.13 \|\|

*brahmādistaṃbaparyaṃtaṃ nimeṣaśca dhruvasya vai \|*  
*nimeṣajīvanaṃ sarvaṃ sarvalokacarācaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The time starting from Brahma and upto Stamba works out to be like the twinkling of eyes for Dhruva. The mobile and immobile of the world are said to be having a short life.

## \|\| 2.2.14 \|\|

*bhūrloko'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarlokaśca prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*janastapaśca satyaṃ ca brahmalokaśca saptamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There are seven lokas viz., : Bhurloka, Bhuvarloka, Svaraloka, Janaloka, Tapaloka, Satyaloka and Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.2.15-16 \|\|

*pātālaṃ vitalaṃ taddhi atalaṃ talameva ca \|*  
*pañcamaṃ viddhi sutalaṃ saptamaṃ ca rasātalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*eteṣu saptavikhyātā adhaḥpātālavāsinaḥ \|*  
*teṣāmādau ca madhye ca aṃte rudraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The nether world has seven lokas viz., Patala, Vitala, Atala, Tala, Viddhi, Sutala and Rasatala. These are the lokas of the nether world. The people of these places are known to be the dwellers of the nether world. Rudra happens to be present at the beginning, middle and at the end of these lokas.

## \|\| 2.2.17 \|\|

*grasate jāyate lokānkrīḍārthaṃ tu maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*brahmalokaparīpsūnāṃ gatirūrdhvaṃ prakīrtitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Mahesvara destroys these lokas for his sport. Such of the people who are desirous of Brahmaloka attain the heaven.

## \|\| 2.2.18-20 \|\|

*pṛthivīṃ cāṃtarikṣaṃ ca diśaśca vidiśastathā \|*  
*samudrāṇāṃ girīṇāṃ ca adhastiryakprasaṃkhyayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*samudrāṇāṃ ca vistāraṃ pramāṇaṃ ca tataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*sthāvarāṇāṃ ca śailānāṃ devānāṃ ca divaukasām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*catuṣpadānāṃ dvipadāṃ tathā dharmaikabhāṣiṇām \|*  
*sahasraguṇamākhyātaṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The earth, space, directions, semidirections, the oceans and the mountains are in slanting position. I am now speaking about the expansion of the oceans, you please listen. The mobiles, die mountains, the gods lodged in the heaven, the quadrupeds, human beings and the spokesman on dharma are said to possess a thousand gunas or virtues.

## \|\| 2.2.21 \|\|

*sahasraguṇaśīlāśca ityāha bhagavānmuniḥ \|*  
*ṛṣistu prathamaṃ kurvanprakṛtiṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Lord Manu too has spoken about their

possessing a thousand gunas each. The Rsis have initially termed the activists as Prakrti.

## \|\| 2.2.22 \|\|

*tasyā brahmā prakṛtyāstu utpannaḥ saha viṣṇunā \|*  
*tasmādbuddhyā prakurute sṛṣṭiṃ naimittikīṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. From the same Prakrti, Brahma and Visnu emerged. Therefore, both of them resort to the casual type of creation.

## \|\| 2.2.23 \|\|

*tasmātsvayaṃbhuvo brahmā brāhmaṇānsamakalpayat \|*  
*pādahīnānkṣatriyāṃśca tasmāddhīnāṃstu vaiśyakān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By the same process, the self-born Brahma created the Brahmanas. Thereafter, the Ksatriyas and Vaisyas were created without the feet who were one fourth less in quantity. The Madras without feet were created, who were deprived of the noble deeds. The earth, the space, the directions, ranges of mountains which surround the seven oceans, islands, oceans, rivers, vast holy places, the clouds, lightning and their thunder, the red rainbows, the comets, the sound produced by the wind, Ketu - a comet and the abodes of light emerge from the body of Brahma and ultimately merge into the same.

## Chapter 3. The Nether World

## \|\| 2.3.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dhruvādūrdhvaṃ maharlokaḥ koṭiyojanavistaraḥ \|*  
*kalpābhikaraṇe tatra saṃsthitā dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said- Above Dhruvaloka, the Maharloka is lodged at a distance of a crore (ten million) of yojanas, in which the best of Brahmanas stay for a kalpa.

## \|\| 2.3.2 \|\|

*janaloko maharlokāttathā koṭidvayātmakaḥ \|*  
*sanaṃdanādayastatra saṃsthitā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Janaloka is located at a distance of two crores of yojanas from Maharloka, in which Sanandana and other sons of Brahma live.

## \|\| 2.3.3 \|\|

*janalokāttapolokaḥ koṭitrayasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*virājaṃte tu devā vai sthitā dāha vivarjitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Tapoloka is located at a distance of three crores of yojanas from Janaloka, where the gods live comfortably.

## \|\| 2.3.4 \|\|

*prājāpatyāttu bhūrlokaḥ koṭiṣaṭkena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sanatkumārakastatra brahmalokastu sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At a distance of six crores of (yojanas) from Prajapatyaloka, Bhurloka is lodged, which is also known as Brahmaloka. It happens to be the abode of Sanatkumara.

## \|\| 2.3.5 \|\|

*tatra loke gururbrahmā viśvātmā viśvatomukhaḥ \|*  
*āste yadyogibhiḥ pītvā yogaṃ mṛtyoḥ paraṃ gatam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The preceptor Brahma, who has the faces io the entire universe, lives there consuming ghe nectar of the yoga. By consuming the same nectar, the yogins after death, achieve the best lace.

## \|\| 2.3.6-7 \|\|

*gāyaṃti yatayo gāthā hyāstikā brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*yoginastāpasāḥ siddhā jāpakāḥ parameṣṭhinam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dvāraṃ tu yogināmekaṃ gacchatāṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*tatra gatvā na śocaṃti sa viṣṇuḥ sa ca śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The Yatis, the believers, spokespersons on Brahman, the Yogins, ascetics, Siddhas and those who recite the scriptures, sing the same story that for the Yogins desirous of achieving emancipation, only Brahma serves as the gate. Reaching, one does not have to face any grief. He happens to be Visnu as well as Siva.

## \|\| 2.3.8 \|\|

*sūryakoṭipratīkāśaṃ puraṃ tasya durāsadam \|*  
*na me varṇayituṃ śakyaṃ jvālāmālāsamākulam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. His abode is beyond vision like crores of suns. No one is able to describe the city which is plunged in resplendence.

## \|\| 2.3.9 \|\|

*tatra nārāyaṇasyāpi bhavanaṃ brahmaṇaḥ pure \|*  
*śeṣe tasya hariḥ śrīmānmāyāsahacaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is a mansion of Narayana in Brahmapuri in which, together with Laksmi, lord Sesasayi (Hari) is lodged.

## \|\| 2.3.10 \|\|

*sa viṣṇurlokakathitaḥ punarāvṛttivarjitaḥ \|*  
*prayāṃti ca mahātmāno ye prapannā janārdanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The place is called as Visnuloka, reaching where a jiva is never reborn. But only such of the people reach there, who have taken refuge with lord Janardana.

## \|\| 2.3.11-12 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ brahmāsanātpūrvaṃ paraṃ jyotirmayaṃ śubham \|*  
*vahninā upari kṣiptaṃ tatrāste bhagavānbhavaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*devyā saha mahādevaścintyamāno manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*yogibhiḥ śatasāhasrairvṛtaikatvaiśca saṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Over the upper part of Brahmaloka, there exists a resplendent town, which appears over the upper part like the fire thrown there. Lord Siva with the goddess Parvati lives there, looking graceful. Hundreds of Yogins and ascetics also live there, meditating upon Siva. They are bent upon meditating there in order to please lord Siva.

## \|\| 2.3.13 \|\|

*tatra te yāṃti niyatā dvijā vai brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*mahādevapareśānāstāpasā brahmavādinaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A regular pilgrimage is performed by the Brahmanas who are the spokespersons on Brahman. They meditate on the Isana form of Siva.

## \|\| 2.3.14 \|\|

*nirmamā nirahaṃkārāḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*drakṣyaṃti brahmaṇā yuktā rudralokaḥ sa vai smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. They are disinterested, devoid of pride, desires and are free from anger all seem to be engaged in adoring the Brahman. It is called Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.3.15 \|\|

*ete sapta maharlokāḥ pṛthivyāṃ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*mahītalādayaścādhaḥ pātālāḥ saṃti vai dvijāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Seven types of Maharloka are said to exist on earth, while Mahitala and Pataloka are lodged below the earth.

## \|\| 2.3.16 \|\|

*mahātalaṃ haimatalaṃ sarvavarṇopaśobhitam \|*  
*prāsādairvividhaiḥ śubhrairdevatāyatanairyutam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Mahatala has the ground which is as beautiful as the glittering gold, which is inhabited by the people of all the castes. Besides there are gigantic temples and beautiful buildings of quite bright colour.

## \|\| 2.3.17 \|\|

*anaṃtena samāyuktaṃ mucukundena dhīmatā \|*  
*nṛpeṇa balinā caiva pātālaṃ svargavāsinā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The intelligent Mucukunda, Ananta - the serpent, besides the king Bali who is desirous of achieving the heaven, have been established in Patalaloka.

## \|\| 2.3.18-26 \|\|

*śailaṃ rasātalaṃ viprāḥ śāṃkaraṃ hi rasātalam \|*  
*pītaṃ sutalamityuktaṃ vitalaṃ vidrumaprabham \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sitaṃ hi vitalaṃ proktaṃ talaṃ caiva sitetaram \|*  
*suvarṇena muniśreṣṭhāstathā vāsukinā śubham \|\| 19 \|\|*

*rasātalamiti khyātaṃ sarvaśobhāsamanvitam \|*  
*vainateyādibhiścaiva kālanemipurogamaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śaṃkukarṇena saṃbhinnaṃ tathā namucipūrvakam \|*  
*tathānyairvivi dhairnāgaistalaṃ caiva suśobhanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*teṣāmadhastānnarakā rauravādyāśca koṭayaḥ \|*  
*pāpinasteṣu pātyaṃte na te'vanamituṃ kṣamāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pātālā nāmadhaścāṃte śeṣākhyā vaiṣṇavī tanuḥ \|*  
*kālāgnirudrayogātmā nārasiṃho'pi mādhavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yo'naṃtaḥ paṭhyate devo nāgarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tadādhāramidaṃ sarvaṃ sakalāgnimupāśritam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tamāviśya mahāyogī kālastadvadanānalaḥ \|*  
*viṣajvālāsamo'naṃto jagatsaṃharati svayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tāmasī śāṃbhavī mūrtiḥ kālātmā parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*sa eva garbhamāśritya prakāśayati nityaśaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

18-26. О Brahmanas, the mountain which is the abode of lord Rasatala, then Sutala is of yellow colour and Vitala is the colour of coralissuing lustre, Tala on the other hand is said to be of black colour. The excellent Rsis, Vasuki of the complexion of gold, resides in that auspicious place, which is quite graceful. Other serpent we have spoken about Rasdtala which is quite charming. The abodes of Vainteya (Garuda) and Kalanemi are also there. Besides Sankukarna and Namuci also live there. At the same place, various types of serpents grace the tala. Under then there are many hells including Raurava and others, which are crores in number. The sinners who fall in the same beg for forgiveness, though they can never be humbled. They are thrown there. Below all the lokas in the netherworld, the serpent Sesa, taking to the form of Vaisnava resides there. He is called as Kala, Agni, Rudra, Yogatma, Narasimha, Madhava and Ananta. The same serpent in the form of Janardana is the solitary support of all the lokas. All types of fires are also lodged there.

## Chapter 4. Circle of Sun

## \|\| 2.4.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*etadbrahmāṃḍamākhyātaṃ caturvidhamidaṃ mahat \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi bhūrlokasya vinirṇayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*taddvīpapradhāno jaṃbūḥ plakṣaḥ śālmala eva ca \|*  
*kuśaḥ krauṃcaśca śākaśca puṣkaraścaiva saptamaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ete sapta mahādvīpāḥ samudraiḥ saptabhirvṛtāḥ \|*  
*dvīpāddvīpo mahānuktaḥ sāgarādapi sāgaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said - I have provided to you the four types of description of the globe. I am now speaking about the Bhuloka. You please listen. There are seven islands in Bhuloka which includes Jambu, Plaksa, Salmall, Kusa, Kraunca, Saka and Puskara. These are the prominent islands. Similarly, the seven oceans have been mentioned. These prominent islands are surrounded by the seven oceans. On island is bigger than the other. Similarly, one ocean is bigger than the other.

## \|\| 2.4.4-6 \|\|

*kṣīrodekṣurasodo'tha kṣārodaśca ghṛtodakaḥ \|*  
*dadhyodaḥ kṣīrasalilo jalodaśceti sāgarāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*paṃcāśatkoṭivistīrṇā samudravalayā smṛtā \|*  
*dvīpaiśca saptabhiryuktā yojanānāṃ samānataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jaṃbūdvīpaḥ samastānāṃ dvīpānāṃ madhyataḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*tasya madhye mahāmerurviśrutaḥ kanakaprabhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. The oceans are known as Ksira-sagara, Iksusagara, Rasasagara, salt water ocean, ocean of ghee, ocean of curd and the ocean of payasam. These are the names of seven oceans. The earth is spread in an area of fifty crores yojanas which have been surrounded from all the sides by the oceans like a garland. The seven oceans are there. Jambudvipa is located in the middle of all the islands, while the Mem mountain with the golden lustre is located in the centre of Jambudvipa.

## \|\| 2.4.7-9 \|\|

*caturāśītisāhasrayojanairasya cocchrayaḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭaḥ ṣoḍaśādhastāddvātriṃśanmūrdhni viṣkṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mūle ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ vistārastasya sarvataḥ \|*  
*bhūpramukhyaśca śailo'sau kalikātvena saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*himavānhimakūṭaśca niṣadhasta sya dakṣiṇe \|*  
*nīlaḥ śvetaśca śṛṃgī ca uttare varṣaparvataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Its height above is of a thousand yojanas. It is sixteen yojanas inside the earth and the breadth above is spread in thirty two yojanas. Its base is spread over the earth upto sixteen thousand yojanas. This is said to be the most prominent of all the mountains. Himalaya, Hemakuta and Nisadha mountains are located to its south. Similarly, the blue, white and Srngi mountains are located to its north.

## \|\| 2.4.10 \|\|

*lakṣapramāṇau dvau madhye daśahīnāstathāpare \|*  
*sahasradvitayaṃ dīrghāstāvadvistāriṇaśca te \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Both the mountains located in the centre is a lakh (of yojanas) and ninety (yojanas) respectively. Their length is two thousand

## \|\| 2.4.11 \|\|

*bhārataṃ dakṣiṇaṃ varṣaṃ tataḥ kiṃpuruṣaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*harivarṣaṃ tathaivānyanmerordakṣiṇato dvijāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О Brahmanas, to the south of the same, Bharatavarsa is located, followed by Kimpurusavarsa, Harivarsa and several other varsas (countries).

## \|\| 2.4.12 \|\|

*caṃpakaṃ cottaraṃ varṣaṃ tathaivāśvahiraṇmayam \|*  
*uttarāḥ kuravaścaiva yathaite bhāratāstathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Campakavarsa is lodged to the north of Meru mountain. Besides Asva, Hirapmaya, Uttarakona and other countries are located like Bharatas as well.

## \|\| 2.4.13-15 \|\|

*navasāhasramekaikameteṣāṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*ilāvṛtaśca tanmadhye tanmadhye merurucchritaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*meroścaturdiśastatra navasāhasraviṣkṛtam \|*  
*ilāvṛtaṃ mahābhāgāścatvārastatra parvatāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*viṣkaṃbhā racitā meroryojanāyutamucchritāḥ \|*  
*pūrveṇa maṃdaro nāma dakṣiṇe gaṃdhamādanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. О best of Brahmanas, the area of each one of these countries is said to be nine thousand yojanas. Ilavarsa is lodged in the middle of all of them. In the middle of all of them and on all the four sides of the Mem mountain, the country of Ratnavrta is located, which is spread in an area of nine thousand yojanas. In that country, four extremely auspicious mountains are located. The Mem mountain is spread in an area of ten thousand yojanas. Mandaracala is located in the east, while Gandhamadana is located in the south.

## \|\| 2.4.16-17 \|\|

*vipulaḥ paścime bhāge supārśvaścottare sthitaḥ \|*  
*kadaṃbeṣveṣu nadyaśca pippalo vaṭa eva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*jaṃbūdvīpasya sā jaṃbūrnāmahetormaharṣayaḥ \|*  
*mahāgajapramāṇāni jaṃbūnyasya phalāni ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The Vipula mountain is located in the west and the Suparsva mountain is lodged in the north. There are several rivers and streams in that country, while a huge holy fig tree (pipala) tree grows in the middle. The fruits of the rose apple tree, which grows in the middle of the Jambudvipa, which make the place to earn its name from the same, are of gigantic nature, like the king elephants.

## \|\| 2.4.18 \|\|

*pataṃti bhūbhṛtaḥ pṛṣṭhe śīryamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*rasena caiva prakhyātā tasya jaṃbūnadī iti \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. These fruits fall at the back of die mountain in a shattered condition. A river named Jambavati with sweet water also flows in this region.

## \|\| 2.4.19 \|\|

*sarittu vartate sāpi pīyate tatra vāsibhiḥ \|*  
*na khedo na ca daurgaṃdhyaṃ na jarā neṃdriyakṣayaḥ \|*  
*utpannāḥ svacchamanaso narāstatra bhavanti vai \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The residents of that island consume the water of that river, which make them free from grief, bad smell and old age. Their sense organs also do not become weak or decline. All those people are possessing spotless hearts.

## \|\| 2.4.20 \|\|

*tīrasūtraṃ samaṃ prāpya vāyunā ca viśoṣitam \|*  
*jāṃbūnadākhyaṃ bhavati suvarṇaṃ siddhabhūṣaṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When the banks of the river dry up, then the gold known as Jambunada emerges from there, the ornaments of which are adorned by the Siddhas and their women.

## \|\| 2.4.21 \|\|

*bhadrāśvaḥ pārśvato meroḥ ketumālaśca paścime \|*  
*varṣe dve tu muniśreṣṭhāstayormadhye ilāvṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О best of sages, close to the Meru mountain lie the two varsas known as Bhadravarsa and Ketumala. In their centre, there is the Ilavrta region.

## \|\| 2.4.22-24 \|\|

*merorupari vipreṃdrā brahmaṇaḥ sthānamuttamam \|*  
*tadūrdhve vāsavasthānaṃ tadūrdhve śaṃkarasya ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tadūrdhvaṃ vaiṣṇavo loko dugārlokastadūrdhvataḥ \|*  
*jyotirmayaṃ paraṃ sthānaṃ nirākāraṃ hiraṇmayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bhaktasthānaṃ tadūrdhvaṃ ca devo hi bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*jyotiścakrasthitaḥ śuddho niścalaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*rāśicakre ca bhramati merorupari sattamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. О best of the monarchs, over the top of the Meru mountain, the beautiful abode of Brahma has been built. Above it is the place of Indra and still above there is the place for Siva above which is Visnuloka. Still above it the place of the goddess Durga is located. Above that place the golden and resplendent abode exists, which has been built for the sake of the devotees. Lord Suryadeva is lodged above them, who getting established over the Jyotiscakra , is pure Paramesvara being immobile lodged over the sign of zodiac and moon around.

## \|\| 2.4.25 \|\|

*biṃbaṣaṭkedrinābhau ca rathacakraṃ divāniśam \|*  
*vātarajjunibaṃdhena dhruvādhāre pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Entering the navel of the mountain in six forms, he is lodged there and the chariot wheel, which moves on the basis of the pole, getting bound with the rope of the wind, it moves throughout the day and night.

## \|\| 2.4.26 \|\|

*dikpālādyā grahāstatra dakṣiṇāduttarāyaṇam \|*  
*pratimāsaṃ gataḥ paṃthā hrāsavṛddhidinakṣayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Mounting over the same, all the planets and the Dikpalas travel through Uttarayana and Daksinayana with the increase and the decrease in the length of days and nights.

## \|\| 2.4.27-29 \|\|

*raviṇā laṃghito māsaścāṃdraḥ khyāto malimlucaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśe bhagavatsūrye pratyahaṃ bhaktasevake \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kṛtvā triṣu tvahorātraṃ tārāmayagataṃ vibhum \|*  
*yāmeyāme codayaśca deśedeśe ca śarvarī \|\| 28 \|\|*

*divā carati yaḥ sūryo rātrau carati candramāḥ \|*  
*nakṣatrāṇi divā rātrau sūryacakre pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. The month in which the sun does not have to pass from one sign of zodiac to the other, it is known as Candramasa or Malamasa (an intercalary month falling once in three years or an extra month). О best of the devotees, out of the twelve months of the Sun-god, in the morning, noon and the evening, according to the distance of the region, both the days and nights are full of stars. The time during which the sun rises, it becomes night in the far off places from that particular place. The sun is established in the Sun-cakra during the day, while the moon is established in the Sun-cakra during the night and then move through die constellations throughout the day and night.

## \|\| 2.4.30 \|\|

*deśānnaṃ cāvagamanaṃ yatra tasmādivābhavat \|*  
*yatra caṃdrakṣayo bhavati yatra sūryaḥ pravartate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In different regions the decline of moon and the rise of the sun is definite, because of them the growth of cereals and the undertakings of the journeys are possible.

## \|\| 2.4.31 \|\|

*rātriṃdivaṃ vijānīyājjyotiścakre pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*udayāstamanaṃ nāsti nakṣatrāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Similarly, the days and nights are established over the heavenly body. Especially the constellations never rise or set.

## \|\| 2.4.32 \|\|

*yannakṣatre ca yo deśaḥ sa teṣāmudayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tatrāsto jīvaśukrāṇāṃ sūryādīnāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The region whichever is established in a particular constellation, it rises in the same region and sets in the same region.

## \|\| 2.4.33 \|\|

*tadā kāle niyoktavyā bhārgavāstādikī kriyā \|*  
*sūryaḥ somo budhaścaṃdro bhārgavaścaiva śīghrakaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The rise of Venus as well as its setting is certain at times. The Sun, the Moon, Mercury and Venus move speedily at times.

## \|\| 2.4.34 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāyanamāsthāya yadā carati raśmimān \|*  
*tadā sarvagrahāṇāṃ sa sūryodhastātprasarpati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When the Sun moves in the Daksinayana, then it moves in the lower parts of the planets.

## \|\| 2.4.35-37 \|\|

*vistīrṇamaṃḍalaṃ kṛtvā tasyordhve carate śaśī \|*  
*nakṣatramaṃḍalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ somādūrdhvaṃ prasarpati \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nakṣatrebhyo budhaścordhvaṃ budhādūrdhvaṃ tu bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*candrastu bhārgavādūrdhvaṃ caṃdrādūrdhvaṃ śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tasmācchanaiścarādūrdhvaṃ tataḥ saptarṣimaṃḍalam \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva saptānāṃ dhruvaścordhvaṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. The Moon with its vast mandala moves above the same. Similarly, all the constellations move in the upper sphere or the regions of the moon. Above the Moon, there is Mercury (Budha), Venus is above Mercury, Moon is above Venus, while Saturn is above Moon. Above Saturn, there are the Saptarsis, the sphere of whom rotates always. North pole is stated to have been lodged over the seven Rsis.

## \|\| 2.4.38-40 \|\|

*kālacakramaye cakre sūryo bhavati sarvadā \|*  
*rāśyarde्dheṣu gatiryatra tithīnāṃ ca tithau smṛtā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*staṃbhate carate śīghraṃ hrāse cāpi dinakṣayaḥ \|*  
*pādāstaṃ cāpi śukrasya mahāstaṃ tatra dṛśyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pādāste pakṣamātraṃ syānmahāste yāmamātrakam \|*  
*cakre pakṣārdhamāsaḥ syādaticāro'ṣṭavāsarān \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. Thus, the Sun-god is established over the Kala-cakrа or the wheel of time. Because of his mounting the chariot, the tithis and zodiac signs in their half portions have to remain present in the half way. The Sun is sometimes shaken or sometimes gains speed. When they are in decline, the length of the days decreases. Venus also, because of his having been seated over a lotus, is said to face padasta or setting for a period. At times, he is said to be completely set. The fortnight is named as Padasta, when he sets for a prahara it is called Mahasta, when Sukra sets for half a fortnight (eight days) the process is known as Aticara or rapid motion

## \|\| 2.4.41 \|\|

*na gaṇyate deśabhede nakṣatreṇa ca gaṇyate \|*  
*bāla vṛddhastu śukrasya deśasthe vā gaṇasya ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The infancy or advancement of Sukra of Venus is not measured with the difference in country, but is solely measured with the constellations.

## \|\| 2.4.42-44 \|\|

*bālyavārddhye kṣatriyasya na gaṇyete sadā budhaiḥ \|*  
*pādādūrdhvaṃ mahāstasya vaiśyasya dvijasa ttamāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*śeṣārdhaṃ bhārgavāstasya śūdrāṇāmatha garhitam \|*  
*abhicāre ca cakre ca na śūdrasya vidhīyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

*varjayedvāsarānsapta iti cātharvaṇī śrutiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. Even the people with wisdom do net measure the infancy of advancement of age of a Ksatriya, but the upper age of a Vaisya is counted with the pada. The half of the same period is the time for the setting of Sukra. This is applicable for the Sudras as well No provision for Sudras exist in abhicara and cakra. Therefore, a Sruti from the Atharvan supports the idea that the seven days should be discarded.

## Chapter 5. Symptoms of good and evil people

## \|\| 2.5.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*trayāṇāmeva varṇānāṃ janmato brāhmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*saṃsṛṣṭā brāhmaṇāḥ pūrvaṃ tapastaptvā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said - О best of the Brahmanas, a Brahmana happens to be the master of all the three castes, which happens to be his birth right. This is because Brahma after performing tapas, initially created the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.5.2-3 \|\|

*havyānāmiha kavyānāṃ sarvasyāpi ca guptaye \|*  
*aśnaṃti ca mukhenāsya havyāni tridivaukasaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kavyāni caiva pitaraḥ kiṃ bhūtamadhikaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*janmanā cottamo'yaṃ ca sarvārcā brāhmaṇo'rhati \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Accordingly, all the havyas and kavyas are required to be protected by the Brahmanas alone, because the gods consume all the havyas through the mouth of the Brahmanas. The p itrs on the other hand consume kavyas. Therefore, no one is superior to them. A Brahmana enjoys the foremost position since his birth. Therefore, he is adorable in all respects.

## \|\| 2.5.4-5 \|\|

*svakīyaṃ brāhmaṇo bhuṃkte vidadhāti dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*trayāṇāmiha varṇānāṃ bhāvābhāvāya vai dvijaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhavedvipro na saṃdehastuṣṭo bhāvāya vai bhavet \|*  
*abhāvāya bhavetkruddhastasmātpūjyaḥ sadā hi saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. A Brahmana consumes his own thing everywhere, besides preserving it. A Brahmana was created for the increase and decrease of all the castes. A Brahmana when completely satisfied is instrumental in their increase. There is no doubt about it. When angered, he becomes the cause of their total destruction. Therefore, the Brahmana is always adorable.

## \|\| 2.5.6 \|\|

*garbhādhānādayaśceha saṃskārā yasya sattamāḥ \|*  
*catvāriṃśattathā cāṣṭau nirvṛttāḥ śāstrato dvijāḥ \|*  
*sa yāti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ brāhmaṇatvena saṃyutaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A Brahmana whose all the sacred rites have been performed appropriately and had completed all the forty eight rules of Sastras, then because of his being foremost of the Brahmanas, he achieves Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.5.7-8 \|\|

*saṃskārapūtaḥ prathamo vedapūto dvitīyakaḥ \|*  
*vidyāpūtastṛtīyaḥ syāttīrthapūtastvanaṃtaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kṣetrapūtaṃ pravijñāya vipūtaṃ pūjayeddvijāḥ \|*  
*svargāpavargaphaladamanyathā śramatāmiyāta \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. He is purified with the first Samskara, secondly he is purified with the study of the Vedas, then he is purified with the learnings or studies, then he is purified with pilgrimage besides having been bom in the auspicious region. Such a purified Brahmana should always be worshipped. A person who does so attains heaven and moksa. When it is not so done, the entire effort becomes useless.

## \|\| 2.5.9 \|\|

*pūtānāṃ paramaḥ pūto gurūṇāṃ paramo guruḥ \|*  
*sarvasattvānvitā vipro nirmito brahmaṇā purā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He is most auspicious of all the sacred people. He is the supreme preceptor of all the preceptors and because of this, Brahmana was produced first of all.

## \|\| 2.5.10 \|\|

*pūjayitvā dvijāndevāḥ svargaṃ bhuñjaṃti cākṣayam \|*  
*manuṣyāścāpi devatvaṃ svaṃsvaṃ rājyaṃ gatena saḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By adoring the Brahmanas, even the gods achieved the everlasting heaven.

## \|\| 2.5.11 \|\|

*yasya viprāḥ prasīdaṃti tasya viṣṇuḥ prasīdati \|*  
*tasmādbrāhmaṇapūjāyāṃ viṣṇustuṣyati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A person with whom a Brahmana is pleased, even lord Visnu remains pleased with him. In fact, lord Visnu gets pleased the moment a Brahmana is adored.

## \|\| 2.5.12 \|\|

*yasmādviṣṇumukhādvipraḥ samudbhūtaḥ purā dvijāḥ \|*  
*vedāstatraiva saṃjātāḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārahetavaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Brahmanas were initially bom out of the face of Visnu. The Vedas were created for the creation and the destruction as well.

## \|\| 2.5.13 \|\|

*tasmādvipramukhe vedāścārpitāḥ puruṣeṇa hi \|*  
*pūjārthaṃ brahmalokānāṃ sarvajñānārthato dhruvam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Therefore, for the enlightenment of all the people and for the worship in Brahmaloka, lord Purusottama surely made the Brahmanas to recite all the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.5.14-15 \|\|

*pitṛyajñavivāheṣu vahnikāryeṣu śāṃtiṣu \|*  
*praśastā brāhmaṇā nityaṃ sarvasvastyayaneṣu ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*devā bhuñjaṃti havyāni baliṃ pretādayo'surāḥ \|*  
*pitaro havyakavyāni viprasyaiva mukhād dhruvam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. For the enlightenment of the people and for the adoration of Brahmaloka, Lord Purusottama had offered all the gods in the mouth of the Brahmanas. For the performing of sraddha, yajnas, marriages, homas, exercising of peaceful rites, besides in all other ceremonies, Brahmanas have been praised. This is also certain that the gods consume havya through the mouth of the Brahmanas. The same is the case with the goblins, (pretas), asuras who accept ball through the same source. The manes also consume havya similarly.

## \|\| 2.5.16 \|\|

*devebhyaśca pitṛbhyaśca yo dadayādyajñakarmasu \|*  
*dānaṃ homaṃ baliṃ caiva vinā vipreṇa niṣphalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The charities in yajnas, homas and the offerings when made without a Brahmana, become infructuous.

## \|\| 2.5.17 \|\|

*vinā vipraṃ ca yo dharmaḥ prayāsaphalamātrakaḥ \|*  
*bhuñjate cāsurāstatra pretā bhūtāśca rākṣasāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In these rites without a Brahmana, only the efforts are successful, because the things so offered including the food are consumed by the Asuras, Pretas, Bhutas and even the Raksasas.

## \|\| 2.5.18 \|\|

*tasmādbrāhmaṇamāhūya tasya pūjāṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*kāle deśe ca pātre ca lakṣakoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Therefore, a Brahmana should be invited in all the big and small functions and should be worshipped, because a charity given in proper country at proper time and to a suitable person, bestows crores of times more reward.

## \|\| 2.5.19 \|\|

*śraddhayā ca dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā prakuryādabhivādanam \|*  
*dīrghāyustasya vākyena ciraṃjīvī bhavennaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On finding a Brahmana, a devotee should at once welcome him, because the moment he blesses a person with long life, the person attains the long life.

## \|\| 2.5.20 \|\|

*anabhivādināṃ vipre dveṣādaśraddhayāpi ca \|*  
*āyuḥ kṣīṇaṃ bhavetpuṃsāṃ bhūmināśaśca durgatiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If a person out of faithlessness or envy does not welcome the Brahmana, the life of that person is shortened besides facing miserable situation and shortening of the age.

## \|\| 2.5.21 \|\|

*āyurvṛddhiryaśorvṛddhirvṛddhirvidyādhanasya ca \|*  
*pūjayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhānbhavennāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By adoring the best of Brahmanas, there is an increase in age, fame, learning and the riches. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.5.22 \|\|

*na viprapādodakakardamāni na vedaśāstrapratigarjitāni \|*  
*svāhāsvadhāsvastivivarjitāni śmaśānatulyāni gṛhāṇi tāni \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A person in whose house the sand docs not get muddy with water used for the washing of the feet of a Brahmana, the sound for the reciting of the Vedas and welfare mantras are not made, the house is such a case is equated with a cremation ground.

## \|\| 2.5.23-30 \|\|

*ṣadviṃśatidoṣamāhurnarā narakabhīravaḥ \|*  
*vimucyaiva vasettīrthe grāme vā pattane vane \|\| 23 \|\|*

*te svarge pitṛloke ca brahmalokeṣvavasthitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*anyathā na vasedvāsastasmātsteyī na pālayet \|*  
*adharmo viṣamaścaiva paśuśca piśunastathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pāpiṣṭho naṣṭakaṣṭau ca ruṣṭo duṣṭaśca muktakaḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭaḥ kuṇṭhaśca andhaśca kāṇaścaiva tathāparaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*caṇḍaḥ khaṇḍaśca vaktā ca dattasyāpaharastathā \|*  
*nīcaḥ khalaśca vācālaḥ kadaryaścapala stathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*malīmasaśca te doṣāḥ ṣaḍviṃśatiramī matāḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ cāpi viprendrāḥ pañcāśītirnigadyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śṛṇudhvaṃ dvijaśārdūlāḥ śāstresminbruvataḥ kramāt \|*  
*adhamo'tra tridhāvidyādviṣamaḥ syādvidhocitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*paśuścaturvidhaścaiva kṛpaṇopi hi vai dvidhā \|*  
*dvidhāthāpi ca pāpiṣṭho naṣṭaḥ saptavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

23-30. The cowardly people of the hell live there with twenty six blemishes. Only such of the people are entitled to achieve the heaven, who temperamentally renounces the world and live in villages, holy places, small villages or the forests somewhere. Such people enjoy Pitraloka or Brahmaloka in the heaven. Or otherwise no place is suitable for their living, where the thieves cannot be served. The twenty six sins of the evil people include discarding of religion, adversity, animal like behaviour, back biting, sinful ways, indulging in evil ways and causing harm and pain to others or getting angry, wickedness, bringing up evil, forcefulness, hunchback, blindness, blind of one eye, of harsh temperament, deformed, talkative, snatching away the things given already, degraded one, wicked, to be too much talkative, coward, talkative and ignorant are the twenty six blemishes of the people. Those who are afraid of the hell should avoid them. О best of Brahmanas, these blemishes are further divided into eighty five parts, which have been mentioned in the scriptures. I am also speaking about them, you please listen. There are three types of the degraded people and two types of uneven minded persons. There are four types of animal like people, besides being miserly who are of two types. The sinners are of two types and the destructive people are of seven types.

## \|\| 2.5.31-37 \|\|

*kaṣṭaḥ syātpañcadhā jñeyo ruṣṭopi syāddvidhā ddvijāḥ \|*  
*duṣṭaḥ syātṣaḍvidho jñeyaḥ puṣṭaścaiva bhaveddvidhā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*hṛṣṭaścāṣṭavidhaḥ proktaḥ kuṇṭhaścaiva tridhoditaḥ \|*  
*andhaḥ kāṇaśca tau dvau dvau syādvai ca saguṇo'guṇaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dvau caṇḍau capalaścaikāvaṇḍacaṇḍo dvigurbhavet \|*  
*daṇḍapaṇḍau tathā jñeyau khalanīcau caturdvayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vācālaśca kadaryaśca kramāttribhirudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*kadaryaścapalaścaiva tathā jñeyo malīmasaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dvāvekau caturaścaiva steyī caikavidho bhavet \|*  
*pṛthaglakṣaṇameteṣāṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*samyagyasya parijñānaṃ naro devatvamāpnuyāt \|*  
*upānacchatradhārī ca gurudevāgrataścaran \|\| 36 \|\|*

*uccāsanaṃ guroragre tīrthayātrāṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*yānamāruhya viprendrāḥ sopyekatrādhamo mataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

31-37. Those who can cause pain are of two types, similarly the wicked people are of six types and those who are over strong are of two types. Those with short bodies are of eight types, those who have bluntness in approach are of three types, who are similar to blind people and those who are blind of one eye, besides those having no virtues at all. They are also of two types each. The fierce people are of two types, the restless one is of single type, the restful people are of three types, the violent and the destroyer have two parts each, while the wicked and the degraded ones have eight parts each. The talkative and the cowardly have three types each. The unsteady or restless and the cowards had three types each. The cowards, the unsteady and ignorant people have respectively two and four divisions. The symptoms of theft have been defined. О best of Brahmanas, by learning about the symptoms of the same, a person becomes a god. Such people are being related by me separately. You please listen. О best of Brahmanas, a person who appears before the god or the preceptor with his shoes on and holding an umbrella over his head or the one who sits over a seat higher than his preceptor or the one who goes on pilgrimage mounted over a vehicle, he is considered to be the degraded one of the first type.

## \|\| 2.5.38 \|\|

*nimajjya tīrthe vidhivadgrāmyadharmeṇa vartayan \|*  
*dvitīyaścādhamaḥ prokto niṃditaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After taking bath at a holy place, one who again behaves like an animal is denounced by all and is known as the second type of a degraded person.

## \|\| 2.5.39 \|\|

*vācaiva madhurā ślakṣṇā hṛdi hālāhalaṃ viṣam \|*  
*vadatyanyatkarotyanyaddvāvetau viṣamau smṛtā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Enshrining the terrific poison in the heart, one who speaks attractive with sweet voice and the one who speaks something else and does something else, he is known as an unbalanced person.

## \|\| 2.5.40 \|\|

*mokṣacintāmatikramya yo'nyacintāpariśramaḥ \|*  
*harisevā vihīno yaḥ sa paśuryonitaḥ paśuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Disregarding the achieving of moksa, the one who is engaged in other matters, getting deprived of the devotion of Hari, he is to be treated as the first among the animals.

## \|\| 2.5.41-42 \|\|

*prayāge vidyamāne'pi yo'nyatra snānamācaret \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ devaṃ parityajya adṛṣṭaṃ bhajate tu yaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*āyuṣastu kṣayārthāya śāstreyamṛṣisaṃmataḥ \|*  
*yogābhyāsaṃ tato hitvā tṛtīyaścādhamaḥ paśuḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Inspite of the existing of Prayaga, one who takes his bath elsewhere and adores the god other than the one who is presently visible, he is treated as the second type of an animal. A person, who discards the yogic practices as prescribed by the ancient R$is and the scriptures, is treated as the third type of animal.

## \|\| 2.5.43 \|\|

*bahūni pustakānīha śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*tasya sāraṃ na jānāti sa eva jaṃbukaḥ paśuḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Keeping a stock of all the books and the religious scriptures, when a person still remains ignorant of the essence of the same, he should be a degraded type of beast or brute.

## \|\| 2.5.44 \|\|

*balena cchalachadmena upāyena prabaṃdhanam \|*  
*so'pi syātpiśunaḥ khyātaḥ praṇayādvā dvitīyakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A person, who using force puts someone in bondage by other deceitful means, he is known as a treacherous person. A person who does the same thing by love-sport, he is also called a treacherous person.

## \|\| 2.5.45-48 \|\|

*madhurānnaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya daive pitrye ca karmaṇi \|*  
*mlānaṃ cāpi ca tiktānnaṃ yaḥ prayacchati durmatiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kṛpaṇaḥ sa tu vijñeyo na svargī na ca mokṣabhāk \|*  
*kudātā ca mudā hīnaḥ sakrodhastu yajeta yaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sa eva kṛpaṇaḥ khyātaḥ sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtaḥ \|*  
*adoṣeṇa śubhatyāgī śubhakāryopavikrayī \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pitṛmātṛgurutyāgī śaucācāravivarjitaḥ \|*  
*pitroragre samaśnāti sa pāpiṣṭhatamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-48. During the festivities of the gods or the pitris, a person who sets aside the sweet dishes, and serves as food the bitter and dry or simple food to the invitees, for consumption, such a wicked person can never achieve heaven or mokpa. Such a person is known as a miserly one. A person with a fading face when gives away in charity the degraded things, besides the one who performs homa getting enraged is also known as a miserly one. He gets discarded from all the dharmas. In case, something is discarded in spite of its being unblemished, the sale of the image of welfare, discarding of the parents and the preceptor, or those who eat in presence of their parents, are known as the most sinful me.

## \|\| 2.5.49 \|\|

*jīvatpitṛparityaktaṃ sutaṃ sevanna vā kvacit \|*  
*dvitīyastu sa pāpiṣṭho homalopī tṛtīyakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. One who discards his living parents or the one who does not bring his son are another types of sinners. The one who does not perform homa is another type of the sinner.

## \|\| 2.5.50-54 \|\|

*sādhvācāraṃ ca pracchāya sevanaṃ cāpi darśayet \|*  
*sa naṣṭa iti vijñeyaḥ krayakrītaṃ ca maithunam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*jīveddevalavṛttiryaḥ bhāryāvipaṇajīvakaḥ \|*  
*kanyāśulkena jīvedvā strīdhanena ca vā kvacit \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ṣaḍeva naṣṭāḥ śāstre ca na svargamokṣabhāginaḥ \|*  
*sadā kruddhaṃ mano yasya hīnaṃ dṛṣṭvā prakopavān \|\| 52 \|\|*

*bhrukuṭīkuṭilaḥ kruddho ruṣṭaḥ paṃcavidhoditaḥ \|*  
*akārye bhramate nityaṃ dharmārthe na vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*nidrālurvyasanāsakto madyapaḥ srtrīniṣevakaḥ \|*  
*duṣṭaiḥ saha sadālāpaḥ sa duṣṭaḥ saptadhā smṛtaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

50-54. A person, who concealing his noble conduct serve others (like slaves), he should be treated as having been destroyed. The one who cohabits on payment, or make his livelihood by the worship of gods or the one who puts his wife on sale in the market to earn his living, the sale of girls or living on the riches of the wife, have been described as the destroyed people in the scriptures. They can never become entitled to achieve heaven. A person whose mind always gets angry and becomes further enraged on spotting a person of lower rank, curves his eyebrows in anger. These are the five type of enraged people. One who wanders daily uselessly, one who makes no arrangement for dharma, one who is drowsy, one who is engaged in evil ways, a drunkard, a debauch, one who remains engaged in conversation with evil-minded people are the seven types of wicked people.

## \|\| 2.5.55-57 \|\|

*ekākī miṣṭamaśnāti vaṃcakaḥ sādhuniṃdakaḥ \|*  
*yathā sūkaraḥ puṣṭaḥ syāttathā puṣṭaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nigamāgamataṃtrāṇi nādhyāpayati yo dvijaḥ \|*  
*na śṛṇoti ca pāpātmā sa duṣṭa iti cocyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

*śrutiḥ smṛtiśca viprāṇāṃ nayane dve vinirmite \|*  
*ekena vikalaḥ kāṇo dvābhyāmaṃdhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Depriving others one who himself eats up the delicious eatables and those who denounce the sages, are known as healthy people resembling the pigs. A Brahmana who does not study the religious scriptures nor does he listens to them, such a sinful person should be taken as the evil one. A Brahmana has two eyes and when he is deprived of knowledge of one of them, he should be treated as blind of one eye and when he is ignorant of both, he should be treated as blind of both the eyes.

## \|\| 2.5.58 \|\|

*vivādaḥ sodaraiḥ sārddhaṃ pitrorapriyakṛdvadet \|*  
*dvijādhamaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sa caṃḍaḥ śāstraniṃditaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A Brahmana who speaks harsh words to his parents, engages in a quarrel between the two brothers, he is called as a Canda and denounced by the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.5.59 \|\|

*piśuno rājagāmī ca śūdrasevaka eva ca \|*  
*śūdrāṃganāgamo vipraḥ sa caṃḍaśca dvijādhamaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A back-biter Brahmana, who goes to the king often, who serves the Sudras and unites with the Madras women, is known as a Canda Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.5.60 \|\|

*pakvānnaṃ śūdragehe ca yo bhuṃkte sakṛdeva vā \|*  
*paṃcarātraṃ śūdragehe nivāsī caṃḍa ucyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A person who takes food in the house of a Sudra once and lives with him for five nights is also known as Canda.

## \|\| 2.5.61 \|\|

*aṣṭakuṣṭhānvitaḥ kuṣṭhī trikuṣṭhī śāstraninditaḥ \|*  
*etaiḥ saha sadālāpaḥ sa bhavettatsamo'dhamaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those who talk with people suffering from five от eight types of leprosy are considered as degraded like them.

## \|\| 2.5.62-63 \|\|

*kīṭavadbhramaṇaṃ yasya kuvyāpārī kupaṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*ajñānācca vadeddharmamagravṛttiḥ pradhāvati \|\| 62 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ parityajya yo'nyadeśe vasecciram \|*  
*sa dvidhā śūkarapaśurniṃditaḥ siddhasaṃmataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Those who wander here and there like insects or the traders who deal in the sale of unsuspicious things, a foolish Brahmana or the Brahmana who describes the dharma in a foolish way or the one who runs first of all for the gaining of livelihood, or the one who leaving his own people lives in other countries for long for earning his living, such a degraded person is known as a degraded brute.

## \|\| 2.5.64 \|\|

*kapolena hi saṃyukto bhrukuṭīkuṭilānanaḥ \|*  
*nṛpavaddaṃḍayedyastu sa daṃḍaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. A person, who creating curves in the cheeks, mouth and eyebrows, pronounces punishment like a king, he is known as a Danda.

## \|\| 2.5.65-66 \|\|

*brahmasvaharaṇaṃ kṛtvā nṛpadeva svameva ca \|*  
*dhanena tena itaraṃ devaṃ vā brāhmaṇānapi \|\| 65 \|\|*

*saṃtarpayati yo'śnāti yaḥ prayacchati vā kvacit \|*  
*sa kharaśca paśuśreṣṭhaḥ sarvavedeṣu niṃditaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. A person who steals the wealth of a Brahmana, a monarch, or the riches of a god, gives the same again to a Brahmana or a god, or uses it for his own purpose or gives it to someone, he is termed as an ass, which is denounced in all the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.5.67 \|\|

*akṣarābhyāsanirataḥ paṭhatyeva na budhyate \|*  
*padaśāstraparityaktaḥ sa paśuḥ syānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. A person who practices on letters spending all his time, or the one who does not understand what is read by him, he is a brute who has discarded the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.5.68 \|\|

*vadatyanyatkarotyanyadgurudevāgrato yataḥ \|*  
*sa nīca iti vijñeyo hyanācārastathāparaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Those who speak before the gods and the preceptors something else and do something differently, such people are devoid of morals and should be considered as the fallen people.

## \|\| 2.5.69 \|\|

*ṣaḍguṇālaṃkṛteḥ sādhordoṣānmṛgayate khalaḥ \|*  
*vane puṣpaphalākīrṇe śalabhaḥ kaṃṭakāniva \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Like a grasshopper who searches for the thorns in the forest leaving aside the flowers and the fruits earns denouncement, similar are the wicked people who find for blemishes in the people of nobility and spotless conduct.

## \|\| 2.5.70 \|\|

*daivena ca vihīno yaḥ kusaṃbhāṣāṃ vadettu yaḥ \|*  
*sa vācāla iti khyāto yo hyapatrapatāyutaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The unfortunate people, speaking foul language and indulging in the shameless activities are known as garrulous people.

## \|\| 2.5.71-72 \|\|

*cāṃḍālaiḥ saha ālāpaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ poṣaṇe rataḥ \|*  
*mārjāraiścāpi saṃbhuṃkte yatkṛtyaṃ makarṭoditam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tṛṇacchedī loṣṭamadī vṛthā māṃsāśanaśca yaḥ \|*  
*capalaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ parabhāryāratastathā \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Those who indulge in conversation with Candalas or rear of the birds, take their food with cots or those who intimate the monkeys, or those who break the straw with their hands without any reason or those who make dust of the stone, those who eat meat, or those who look at the wives of others, are all known as unsteady or restless.

## \|\| 2.5.73 \|\|

*snehodvartanahīno yo gaṃdhacaṃdanavarjitaḥ \|*  
*nityakriyā akurvāṇo nityaṃ sa ca malīmasaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Those who are always deprived of oil or paste and have not touched even the sandal wood or those who do not perform the daily prayers, are all known as untouchables.

## \|\| 2.5.74-75 \|\|

*anyāyena gṛhaṃ viṃdedanyāyena gṛhāndhanam \|*  
*śāstrādanyadgṛha maṃtraṃ sa steyī brahmaghātakaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*devapustakaratnāni maṇimuktāśvameva ca \|*  
*gobhūmisvarṇaharaṇaḥ sa steyīti nigadyate \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. Those who earn the house, wife and the wealth by unfair means, and accept the mantras other than those prescribed in the Nostras are known as the killers of Brahman. The people who steal the books, gems, beads, horses, cows and the gold of the Devas are known as thieves.

## \|\| 2.5.76 \|\|

*devo'pi bhāvayetpaścānmānuṣo'pi na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*anyonyabhāvanā kāryā sa steyī yo na bhāvayet \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The humans should show greater respect to die Devas and thereafter the virtuous people as well. A person who does not do so can be taken as a thief.

## \|\| 2.5.77 \|\|

*guroḥ prasādājjayati pitroścāpi prasādataḥ \|*  
*karoti ca yathārhaṃ ca sa ca svarge mahīyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. One is victorious always by the grace of the parents as well as the preceptors. The one who performs the adequate activities, he achieves the heaven.

## \|\| 2.5.78 \|\|

*na poṣayati duṣṭātmā sa steyī cāparaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Those who support the wicked souls, they are also known as thieves.

## \|\| 2.5.79 \|\|

*upakārijanaṃ prāpya na karoti pariṣkriyām \|*  
*sa taptanarake śete śoṇite ca patatyadhaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. When a person, who does good to others is not properly welcomed in a function, he falls into the hot hell or the hell of blood.

## \|\| 2.5.80 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ ca savarṇānāṃ dharmato brāhmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*pṛthivīpālako rājā dharmacakṣurudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. A Brahmana happens to be a preceptor of all the castes as per the dharma, while the king of the earth has been described as the eyes.

## \|\| 2.5.81 \|\|

*prajāpatermukhodbhūto horātaṃtre yathoditam \|*  
*tadvido gaṇanābhijñā anyaviprāḥ pracakṣate \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The other Brahmanas who were bom out of the face of Brahma, who are well aware of the provisions of the Hora-tantra, they are called as the Astrologers.

## \|\| 2.5.82 \|\|

*gaṃgāhīno hato deśo viprahīnā yathā kriyā \|*  
*horājñaptivihīno yo deśo'sau viplavaplavaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. A country without Ganga gets destroyed as a religious activity is of no use without a Brahmana. The country in which a Brahmana well-versed in Hord-tantra is not there, such a country always has to face disturbances.

## \|\| 2.5.83 \|\|

*apradīpā yathā rātriranādityaṃ yathā nabhaḥ \|*  
*tathā'sāṃvatsaro rājā bhramatyaṃdha ivādhvani \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. As the night is not graceful without a lamp and the day without the sun, similarly a ruler without a Samvatsara (or a year) also wanders here and there, aimlessly.

## \|\| 2.5.84 \|\|

*sthāpayeddharmato vipraṃ bhāvayetkarmavṛddhaye \|*  
*śmaśruyukto dvijaḥ pūjyaḥ sūryo viprastu śmaśrulaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The Brahmanas should be established in dharma, one should make them graceful in their activities. A Brahmana with beard should be honoured, because such a Brahmana is said to be the form of the Sun-god.

## \|\| 2.5.85 \|\|

*pratyakpradarśanātpuṇyaṃ tridinaṃ kalmaṣāpaham \|*  
*darśane vrātyaviprasya sūryaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśudhyati \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. During the evening on a particular day, in case one has an audience with him, he earns great merit. In case one meets him continuously for three days, all his sins get vanished. An outcast from the faith, when has an audience with such a Brahmana, then he is freed from the sin and also gains purity.

## \|\| 2.5.86 \|\|

*na vrātyatvaṃ sūryavipre pūjayedyajñasiddhaye \|*  
*jyotirvedasyādhikāraḥ sūryaviprasya vai dvijāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. A Brahmana with a beard has never to face a fall. One should worship a Brahmana with a beard for gaining success in a yajna. О group of Brahmanas, only the Brahmanas with a grown beard are said to be entitled to gain knowledge of astrology.

## \|\| 2.5.87 \|\|

*jātibhedāśca catvāro bhojakaḥ kathakastathā \|*  
*śivavipraḥ sūryavipraścaturthaḥ paripaṭhyate \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Bhojakas, Kathakas, those who are devoted to lord Siva and Suryavipra are the four castes. These Brahmanas are of the highest order.

## \|\| 2.5.88 \|\|

*kathako madhyamasteṣāṃ sūryaviprastathottamaḥ \|*  
*śivaliṃgārcanarataḥ śivaviprastu niṃditaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The Kathakas out of them are of medium type, those with beards who have grown beards, arc the best. Such of the Brahmanas who worship the tfivalihga ate denounced.

## \|\| 2.5.89 \|\|

*sūryaviprasya viprasya vaidyasya ca nṛpasya ca \|*  
*pravāsayedakṣatena saputrapaśubāṃdhavaḥ \|*  
*avadhyaḥ sarvalokeṣu rājā rājyena pālayet \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The Brahmanas with beards, other Brahmanas, the Vaidyas or physicians as well as the rulers should be worshipped uttering the welfare mantras when proceeding on journey to another country. Besides that in the foreign land, they should get such a type of cooperation from the foreign ruler that they do not feel inconvenienced in any way. Their sons, animals and relatives should not be killed in any place. The king should attend to their well-beings always.

## \|\| 2.5.90-91 \|\|

*vasubhirvastragaṃdhādyairmālyaiśca vividhairapi \|*  
*deśacakravidaḥ pūjyā horācakravidaḥ parāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*sūryacakravidaḥ pūjyā nāvamanyetkathaṃcana \|*  
*siddhavṛddhiṃ ca dhanarddhiṃ ca ya icchedāyuṣā samam \|*  
*gaṇaviprasamaḥ pūjyo daivajñaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

90-91. A person possessing the knowledge about all the countries, should be honoured presenting the fragrance, garlands besides other materials. A Brahmana possessing the knowledge of Hora-cakra is absolutely essential. Besides one who is aware of the secrets of Surya-cakra also should not be neglected in any way. Those who are desirous of the increase in their own lives, siddhi (success), rddhi (prosperity) as well as wealth, they should worship an astrologer like Siva.

## \|\| 2.5.92 \|\|

*jāte bāle nirūpye ca lagnagrahanirūpaṇam \|*  
*saṃsthānaṃ sūryavipro yaḥ sūryaviprasya sattamāḥ \|*  
*dvimātrikāṃ samabhyasya sarvavedaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. О excellent audience, when a son is born to a Surya-vipra then a beard Brahmana should describe his birth details etc. besides the symptoms. With the study of Dvimatrika, one achieves the merit of the study of the Vedas.

## Chapter 6. The Preceptor

## \|\| 2.6.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ nānyo baṃdhuḥ pracakṣate \|*  
*ṛte piturdvijaśreṣṭhā itīyaṃ naigamī smṛtiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*trayo'pi guravaḥ śreṣṭhāstābhyāṃ mātā paro guruḥ \|*  
*ye sodarā jyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhā uttarottarato guruḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said - О best of Brahmanas, no other kind of the people of the four varnas has been described best except the father. This is the opinion of the Nigamas. All the three types of preceptors have been described to be the best, but among them the mother has been held to be the foremost preceptor. Among the real brothers, all the elder brothers are said to be the preceptor.

## \|\| 2.6.3 \|\|

*dvādaśyāṃ tu āmavāsyāmatha vā ravisaṃkrame \|*  
*vāsāṃsi dakṣiṇā deyā maṇimuktā yathāruci \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On the day of the twelfth moon, the moonless day or on the first day of the month, the clothes with gems should be given in charity as per one’s means.

## \|\| 2.6.4 \|\|

*ayane viṣuve caiva caṃdrasūryagrahe tathā \|*  
*prāpte cāparapakṣe tu bhojayeccāpi śaktitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Both the Ayanas, Visuva (equinox), solar or lunar eclipses or on the day of Sraddha, the Brahmanas should be served the food as per one’s means.

## \|\| 2.6.5 \|\|

*paścātpravaṃdayetpādau maṃtreṇānena sattamāḥ \|*  
*vidhivadvaṃdanādeva sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O excellent ones, thereafter, the feet should be washed reciting the mantras. By worshipping them in a proper manner, one achieves the merit of visiting all the holy places.

## \|\| 2.6.6 \|\|

*svargāpavargapradamekamādyaṃ brahmasvarūpaṃ pitaraṃ namāmi \|*  
*yato jagatpaśyati cārurūpaṃ taṃ tarpayāmaḥ salilaistilairyutaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I offer my salutation to the father, who bestows the heaven as well as the moksa, is the best of all, who is the first of all, besides being the form of Brahmana, by the grace of whom, one can achieve the complete knowledge of Siva, the one who is full of beauty and for whom I am offering the water with sesamum seeds.

## \|\| 2.6.7 \|\|

*pitaro janayaṃtīha pitaraḥ pālayaṃti ca \|*  
*pitaro brahmarūpā hi tebhyo nityaṃ namonamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It is the father who produces and then brings up the son. Therefore, salutation to the father who is the form of Brahman.

## \|\| 2.6.8 \|\|

*yasmādvijayate lokastasmāddharmaḥ pravartate \|*  
*namastubhyaṃ pitaḥ sākṣādbrahmarūpa namo'stu te \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. One becomes victorious in the world by his grace and he is the founder of dharma. Therefore, O father the form of Brahman, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.6.9 \|\|

*yā kukṣivivare kṛtvā svayaṃ rakṣati sarvataḥ \|*  
*namāmi jananīṃ devīṃ parāṃ prakṛtirūpiṇīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The one who keeping in her womb, always protects, salution to such a mother, who is the form of Prakrti.

## \|\| 2.6.10-11 \|\|

*kṛcchreṇa mahatā devyā dhārito'haṃ yathodare \|*  
*tvatprasādājjagaddṛṣṭaṃ mātarnityaṃ namo'stu te \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni sāgarādīni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*vasaṃti yatra tāṃ naumi mātaraṃ bhūtihetave \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. О mother, keeping me in you womb, facing all the painful situations, you kept me safe. By your pleasure alone, I had been able to visualize the world. Therefore, salutation to you always. All the holy places on earth and all the oceans are dwelling in your limbs, therefore I offer my salutation to the mother, for the sake of achieving the fortunes.

## \|\| 2.6.12 \|\|

*gurudevaprasādena labdhā vidyā yaśaskarī \|*  
*śivarūpa namastasmai saṃsārārṇavasetave \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By the grace of the preceptor, I could achieve the famous education. Therefore, salutation to the one who is instrumental in getting me cross over the ocean of the universe.

## \|\| 2.6.13 \|\|

*veda vedāṃgaśāstrāṇāṃ tattvaṃ yatra pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*ādhāraḥ sarvabhūtānāmagrajanmannamo'stu te \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Salutation to the Brahmana who is well-versed in all the Vedas with their parts and is the base of all the living beings and was born ahead of all.

## \|\| 2.6.14 \|\|

*brāhmaṇo jagatāṃ tīrthaṃ pāvanaṃ paramaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*bhūdeva hara me pāpaṃ viṣṇurūpinnamo'stu te \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О Bhudeva, you kindly remove all my sins, because the Brahmana is the form of Visnu and the most auspicious one in the world, besides being a tirtha. Salutation to you

## \|\| 2.6.15 \|\|

*pitāmahaṃ ca praṇametsarvādau mātaraṃ gurum \|*  
*mātāmahaṃ ca tadanu ācāryamatha ṛtvijam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. First of all, I offer my salutation to the grandsire, the mother as a preceptor, maternal grandfather, Acaryas, besides the Ritvijas

## \|\| 2.6.16-17 \|\|

*mātṛmaṃtraiśca prathamaṃ praṇamedbhaktibhāvataḥ \|*  
*yathāgrajastathā jyeṣṭhaḥ pitṛvyo'pi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭādṛṣṭe ca sa gururgururmātā tathā guruḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭādṛṣṭastṛtīyaḥ syātsūryo'gniścaṃdra eva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. О best of the Brahmanas, I also offer my salutation with devotion to the mantras of the mother and thereafter to the uncles because they are also elders and the best. In the presence of the preceptor, he is adorable no doubt, but in his absence, mother serves as a preceptor. Similarly, in the visible as well as invisible form all the three i.e., Surya (the sun), the moon and the fire too are taken to be the preceptors of the third stage.

## \|\| 2.6.18 \|\|

*maṃtradātā guruḥ khyātassaptamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*kabhojanaguruḥ śreṣṭhaḥ svargāpavargahetukaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Brahmana who bestows the mantra also become the famous preceptor. The tapas by preceptor bestows heaven as well as moksa. Therefore, he happens to be the best of all of them.

## \|\| 2.6.19 \|\|

*dṛṣṭadevaṃ ca yo hitvā adṛṣṭaṃ ca niṣevate \|*  
*pāpātmā paramaḥ saikastiryagyoniṃ ca gacchati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A person, who discaids the visible god. but worships the invisible god, he is considered to be a grave sinner. He has to be born as a bird.

## \|\| 2.6.20 \|\|

*yathā pitā jyeṣṭhapitā kanīyāṃśca tathā dvijāḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitṛtulyo mānyaḥ satkārabhāgyataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О Brahmana, the elder brother and the younger brother of the father, besides the elder brother of a person, are all equal to the father and have to be respected accordingly.

## \|\| 2.6.21 \|\|

*ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*mātā syānpṛthivīmūrtirbhrātaro mūrtirātmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. An Acarya is the form of Brahma, the father is the form of Prajapati, the mother is the form of earth, the Matrkas are the form of one’s ownself.

## \|\| 2.6.22 \|\|

*pitā merurva śiṣṭhaḥ syāddharmamūrtiḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*sa cāpi dṛṣṭadevaḥ syāttadājñāṃ paripālayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The father, the Meru mountain, Vasistha and dharma are the eternal apparent Devas. Therefore, their command should always be accepted and obeyed.

## \|\| 2.6.23 \|\|

*pitāmahaṃ ca pitragre havyakavyaiśca tarpayet \|*  
*sa yāti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ yasmānnāvartate punaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A person who pleases the grandsire with havya and kavya, he achieves such a place of Brahma, from where one does not have to return.

## \|\| 2.6.24 \|\|

*tasya pādodakasnānādgaṃgā nārhati kevalam \|*  
*tathāvalokanāttasya jyotirliṃgaśataiśca kim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By taking bath with the water with which his feet once washed, its importance exceeds even the holy water of the Ganga. Not only this with the mere sight of such a person, the performer achieves the merit, which one cannot achieve by worshipping of hundreds of Jyotirlingas.

## \|\| 2.6.25 \|\|

*dvātriṃ śatkuṃḍakaśilāsparśane yādṛśaṃ phalam \|*  
*tādṛśaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ pitāmahapradakṣiṇe \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With the touch of the slab with thirty two kundas, the merits which are achieved by a person, one gets crores of times more merits by going round the grandfather.

## \|\| 2.6.26 \|\|

*śatamātṛvariṣṭhāśca pitāmahyāśca poṣaṇe \|*  
*guṇāstaddarśane viprāḥ saṃsāre na punarviśet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The grandmother is better than hundreds of mothers, one earns merit by simply looking at her and the person who does so is never reborn on earth.

## Chapter 7. The Preceptor

## \|\| 2.7.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*samākhyāmīha vipreṃdrā itihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*śravaṇepi ca dharmātmañchrūyatāṃ yanmayā purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said - О Dharma’s soul, while listening to the ancient history and the Puranas in earlier times, the same is being repeated by me.

## \|\| 2.7.2-3 \|\|

*pṛṣṭovocanmahātejā viriṃco bhagavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*haṃta te kathayāmyeṣa purāṇaśravaṇe vidhim \|\| 2 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇāni śrutvā bhaktyā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyo brahmahatyāśataṃ ca yat \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Whatever had lord Brahma spoken to me, on my asking him, the same procedure for the listening of the Puranas is being repeated by me. О best of the Brahmanas, by listening to the Itihasa and the Puranas with devotion, all the sins including the Brahmahatyas get destroyed.

## \|\| 2.7.4 \|\|

*sāyaṃ prātastathā rātrau śucirbhūtvā śṛṇoti yaḥ \|*  
*tasya viṣṇustathā brahmā tuṣyate śaṃkarastathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. During the evenings, mornings as well as at noon times, one who with an auspicious mind listens to the same with devotion, the three gods Brahma, Visnu and Siva get pleased with him.

## \|\| 2.7.5 \|\|

*pratyūṣe bhagavānbrahmā dināṃte tuṣyate hariḥ \|*  
*mahādevastathā rātrau śṛṇvatāṃ paṭhatāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By listening to it in the morning lord Visnu is pleased, by listening to the puranas in the evening Brahma gets pleased and when one listens at night, lord Siva is pleased.

## \|\| 2.7.6-11 \|\|

*śuklavastradharaścaiva cailājinakuśottaraḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇatrayaṃ kuryādyā tasmindevatā gurau \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ svāsanaṃ bhajate tataḥ \|*  
*dikpatibhyo namaskṛtya ūṃkārādhiṣṭhitānapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pustakaṃ dharmaśāstrasya dharmādhiṣṭhānaśāśvatam \|*  
*āgamānāṃ śivo devastaṃtrādīnāṃ ca śāradā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*jāmalānāṃ gaṇapatirḍāmarāṇāṃ śatakratuḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇo bhāratasya tathā rāmāyaṇasya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vāsudevo bhaveddevaḥ saptānāṃ śṛṇu sattama \|*  
*ādityo vāsudevaśca mādhavo rāmakeśavau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vanamālī mahādevaḥ saptānāṃ saptaparvasu \|*  
*viṣṇudharmādikānāṃ ca śivo jñeyaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*atha cādipurāṇasya viriṃciḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. Getting clad in white costumes and getting seated over the seat of kusa grass, one should go round the preceptor thrice, one should be seated over a seat which should neither be too high nor too low and should offer his salutation with Omkara to the Dikpalas, because the book on the Dharmasastras happens to be the formal form of dharma. Lord Siva is the foremost of all the Devas, Siva also is the foremost lord of the Vedas. Sarada is the goddess of the tantras, Ganapati is the lord of Jamala-tantra, Satakratu (Indra) is the lord of Damaras, Narayana is the lord of the Mahabharata, Vasudeva is the lord of the Ramayana. Besides this, Aditya, Vasudeva, Madhava, Rama, Kesava, Vanamali and Mahadeva are the lords of all the seven parvas. Similarly, Siva is the lord of Vaisnava dharma. He is eternal, without destruction while Brahma is the lord of Siva and other Puranas.

## \|\| 2.7.12-13 \|\|

*śuddhaudanaṃ yavakṣīraṃ pāyasaṃ kṛśaraṃ tathā \|*  
*kṛśarānnaṃ ca vā dadyātkramādbaligaṇaṃ viduḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śālibhaktaṃ sagodhūmaṃ tilākṣatavimiśritam \|*  
*gavyaṃ ca saphalaṃ caiva deyaścaibhyastvayaṃ baliḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. The rice should be boiled with purity, payasam of barley as well as of rice, besides the mixed food (like rice and pulses) should be offered to the gods. Then the boiled Sali rice, the wheat with sesamum, unbroken rice and cows’ milk with fruits should also be offered.

## \|\| 2.7.14 \|\|

*pṛthakpṛthakcaiva kāṃsye vinyaseddikṣu madhyataḥ \|*  
*paṭheccāpi vidhānena sa yāgaḥ ṣaṇmayaḥ paraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*
