67\. Of course it has to be discarded during the month of Kartika. Even when it is patronised in the month of Magha, one has to fall in the hell. When it is combined with the Sravana constellation in the month of Bhadrapada, vrata should be performed during the aforesaid Vijaya-tithi which is of great importance.

## \|\| 2.29.68 \|\|

*ekādaśyāmuttarato dvādaśī ca divānvitā \|*  
*niśipūrṇā dvādaśī ca śravaṇenāpi saṃyutā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In case Dvadasi combines with Ekadasi for the whole day combined with the Sravana constellation, it should be taken as quite meritorious.

## \|\| 2.29.69-70 \|\|

*saphalā dvādaśī jñeyā upoṣyaiṣā mahāphalā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*dvādaśyāṃ viṣṇuviddhāyāṃ vāsudevaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*kṛṣṇāyāṃ tu vrataṃ kuryādbahuduḥkhaṃ samācareta \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Lord Vgsudeva should be adored when Ekadasi is combined with Dvadasi without performing the vrata, because with the performing of vrata one has to face enormous miseries. Vratas are required to be performed during the dark fortnight alone.

## \|\| 2.29.71 \|\|

*dvādaśī kāmaviddhā cenmanyate nāpyupoṣaṇam \|*  
*hanyātpurākṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ trayodaśyāmupoṣaṇam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. When Dvadadi is known to be combined with Kama, the fasting should not be done. In case the fast is extended to Trayodadl, all the merits earned by a person earlier, are lost.

## \|\| 2.29.72 \|\|

*prahareprahare snānaṃ śarvaryāṃ ca vidhīyate \|*  
*pūjanaṃ cāgnikāryaṃ ca ṣaṭsu kāryaṃ vratī caret \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. During each prahara, a person who performs the vrata should take bath, perform Нота and other religious rites.

## \|\| 2.29.73 \|\|

*ekādaśīṃ dvādaśīṃ ca prāpnoti śravaṇe yadi \|*  
*ekādaśyāmupoṣyātha dvādaśyāmapyupāvaset \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. On the day of Sravapa constellation when Ekadasi or Dvadasi falls at the same time, the fasting should be done during Ekadasi only But certain scriptures permit fasting to be done on the Dvadasi as well.

## \|\| 2.29.74 \|\|

*pāraṇaṃ tu trayodaśyāṃ dvādaśī cenna labhyate \|*  
*āmiṣānnaṃ na bhuñjīta haviṣyānnena pāraṇam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The fast should be broken on the day of Trayodasi by consuming the food of harm and not with non-vegetarian food.

## \|\| 2.29.75 \|\|

*yadā tu pāraṇāyogyā labhyate dvādaśī tadā \|*  
*tasyāṃ nātikramo yuktastadabhāve trayodaśī \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. On the finding of a Dvadasi for the breaking of the fast, it should never be discarded. The food should be taken in Trayodasi only in the absence of Dvadasi.

## \|\| 2.29.76 \|\|

*ekādaśī dvādaśī ca śravaṇarkṣeṇa saṃyutā \|*  
*viṣṇuśṛṃkhalako nāma budhavāre viśiṣyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. When Ekadasi or Dvadasi falls during the Sravana constellation on Wednesday, then it is known as Visnu-Srnkhala, which enhances the prestige of the performer as well.

## \|\| 2.29.77 \|\|

*daśamyāṃ saṃyato bhūtvā prātarekādaśīdine \|*  
*kṛtvā tu saṅgame snānaṃ prahareprahare dvijāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. О Brahmanas, according to the method prescribed for adoration, one should remain disciplined during the Dadami tithi, and one should take bath at each prahara at the confluence of the rivers.

## \|\| 2.29.78 \|\|

*anena vidhinā kṛtvā vijayāyāṃ vratottamam \|*  
*sarvapāpaṃ kṣayaṃ nītvā viṣṇuloke vasennaraḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. With this process, following the method of Vijaya Ekadasi, a person is relieved of all the sins and then reaches the abode of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.29.79 \|\|

*caturyugānāṃ divyānāṃ yāvatsyādviṣṇurūpadhṛka \|*  
*tāvadeva hi sarvatra sārvabhaumo bhavennaraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Then he takes to the divine form of Visnu during all the four yugas and becomes the universal monarch.

## \|\| 2.29.80 \|\|

*tretāyāṃ daśajanmāni madhyadeśeṣu bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*tataśca bhārate varṣe vedavedāṃtasāravit \|*  
*putrapautradhanairyukto lakṣado nṛpasannibhaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Then he attain ten births in Tretayuga in the middle country, he is reborn in Bharata, well-versed in the Vedas and possesses enormous wealth. He earns grace from the rulers and gives lakhs in charities.

## \|\| 2.29.81 \|\|

*jāyate daśa janmāni tretāyāṃ brāhmaṇottamaḥ \|*  
*sapatnīkaśca dīrghāyurdharmakarmasu pūjitaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. During the Tretayuga for ten births, he is bom in an excellent Brahmana family. He achieves long life with his wife and is respected in all the religious rites.

## \|\| 2.29.82 \|\|

*bhādre māsi site pakṣe dvādaśyāṃ pṛthivīpatim \|*  
*śatrumutthāpayetprāhṇe śubhalagne śubhakṣaṇe \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. On the bright Dasami day of the month of Bhadrapada, during the forenoon, at an auspicious time and with the sight of the auspicious planets, the enemy who is the lord of earth, should be praised.

## \|\| 2.29.83-88 \|\|

*śalyaśālmalikasyāpi saptaparṇīyakasya ca \|*  
*eṣāmanyatamaṃ vṛkṣaṃ caṃpakasyārjunasya vā \|\| 83 \|\|*

*bṛhatkadaṃbavṛkṣasya dvicatvāriṃśadaṃgulaiḥ \|*  
*dvātriṃśadaṃgulairvāpi mānadvayamathāpi vā \|*  
*trivyāyāmaṃ ca prathamaṃ dvāviṃśahastameva vā \|\| 84 \|\|*

*hastaḥ ṣoḍaśavārasya gṛhasthasya viśiṣyate \|*  
*hastatrayeṇa viprasya dvādaśa kṣatriyasya tu \|\| 85 \|\|*

*aṣṭahastaṃ tu vaiśyasya śūdrasya pañcahastakam \|*  
*abhrataḥ śvetacchatraṃ syātpatākā ca purepure \|\| 86 \|\|*

*ghanasārasamāyuktāṃ karpūramaṃḍanānvitām \|*  
*raktavastraparicchannāṃ puṣpamālyairalaṃkṛtām \|\| 87 \|\|*

*mañcasthāṃ kārayetpūjāṃ bhaktyā ca sudṛḍho naraḥ \|*  
*saptarātraṃ caretpūjāmaindramantreṇa mantravit \|\| 88 \|\|*

83-88. An umbrella of thorny tree, silk cotton tree, Saptaparni tree, Michelia champica or the vast Neuleo orctalis trees should be made with spokes of thirty two or forty two angulas or as long as the spokes sticks, or spokes of twenty cubits should be placed in it resembling an umbrella, resembling the one used during the race. It should be sixteen measures or of the size of a cubit for householders; for Brahmanas, it should be of three cubits length; for Ksatriyas, it should be of twelve cubits length; eight cubits for Vaisyas and five cubits for a Sudra. In one of the village, a white umbrella as well as a flag should be established. They should be plastered with camphor and covered with red cloth, decorated further with the auspicious garlands. They should be worshipped with devotion, placing them over pedestals. Then they should be worshipped with devotion for seven nights.

## \|\| 2.29.89-92 \|\|

*kākādīnna spṛśejjātu vairapakṣe viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*patākāyā nipāte tu rāṣṭrahāniṃ samādiśet \|\| 89 \|\|*

*patāke nissṛte bhagne mahiṣāṇāṃ vināśanam \|*  
*sthūṇāpāte ca bhagne vā cāśvahāniṃ samādiśet \|\| 90 \|\|*

*taskaraśca kule tasya prāyaścittaṃ samācaret \|*  
*tadviṣṇoriti maṃtreṇa śatapadmasamanvitam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*viṣṇumuddiśya juhuyādayutaṃ pippalasya ca \|*  
*grahāṇāṃ ca tribhāgena cāyutaṃ juhuyādbudhaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

89-92. Both of them should not be touched by the crows with enmity, because with the fall of the flag, the nation is likely to fall. With the fall of the flag, the nation could also shatter. The people of their race become thieves. Therefore, its repentance must be performed. The wood of the pipala tree should be dropped with a hundred lotus flowers for the sake of lord Visnu reciting the relevant mantra, besides the offerings of ten thousand should also be made For pleasing the planets, the offering of a third part should be poured.

## \|\| 2.29.93 \|\|

*ādityasyādbhutamidaṃ dvijapāte tu bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*kapotapāte śukrasya kākādau bhaumamādiśet \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Brahmana, at the fall of the birds like pigeon etc. over them, the Sun should be worshipped. At the fall of the parrot and the crow, the planet Mars should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.29.94-95 \|\|

*bhūkaṃpe jāyate viṣṭaṃ guroradbhutamādiśet \|*  
*kīṭaviddhe kṛte viprāścandrasyādbhutamādiśet \|\| 94 \|\|*

*patāke nissṛte bhagne rāhoradbhutamādiśet \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. During earthquake, Jupiter should be worshipped. When they are infested with worms, the moon should be worshipped. With the uprooting of the flag or its damage, Rahu should be worshipped, because at that point of time, only such planets create disturbance.

## \|\| 2.29.96 \|\|

*śivā ruvaṃti cāndrasya vānaro vā spṛśetkvacit \|*  
*ketoradbhutamuddiṣṭaṃ bhūmikaṃpe tu te dvijāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. At the cry of the female jackal and when the flag comes in touch with a monkey, the moon is to be worshipped. With the shaking of the earth, Ketu should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.29.97 \|\|

*trayodaśīṃ sitāṃ prāpya puṣpairnānāvidhairapi \|*  
*kāmadevaṃ samabhyarcedgandhādyaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. On the Trayodas day of bright fortnight, Kamadeva should be worshipped with fragrant flowers.

## \|\| 2.29.98 \|\|

*caitre māsi sitāṣṭamyāṃ śanau śatabhiṣā yadi \|*  
*gaṃgāyā yadi labhyeta sūryagrahaśataiḥ samā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. During the dark Astami of the month of Caitra, at the Satabhisa constellation, it is meritorious like hundreds of solar eclipses. Therefore, on that particular day, one must take a bath in the Ganga

## \|\| 2.29.99 \|\|

*seyaṃ mahāvāruṇīti khyātā kṛṣṇatrayodaśī \|*  
*asyāṃ snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca śrāddhaṃ vākṣayamucyate \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. With the same combination on the dark Trayodasi, it is called Maha-varuni taking bath, performing meditation or sraddha, one achieves the everlasting reward.

## \|\| 2.29.100 \|\|

*madhumāse site pakṣe dambhabhañjī caturdaśī \|*  
*tasyāṃ madanamūle ca akṣaraṃ kāmamarcayet \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The bright Caturthi of the month of Caitra is known by the name of Damba-bhanji. During that day, the everlasting Kamadeva should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.29.101 \|\|

*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ madanasya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*jugupsitavacobhistu samyaktuṣṭo manobhavaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. With the influence of Kamadeva, the person who does so achieves the best of the place. By uttering the vulgar words on that particular day, Kamadeva gets immensely pleased.

## \|\| 2.29.102 \|\|

*anantasya vrataṃ vakṣye sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*anantaṃ sukhamāpnoti yaḥ kuryādbhaktimānnaraḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Now I am speaking out the method of the removal of all the sins and the related vratas by following which a devoted person earns great comforts.

## \|\| 2.29.103 \|\|

*dvādaśyāṃ pūjite śakre dhvajake vāstuyaṣṭiṣu \|*  
*tataḥ śuklacaturdaśyāmanantaṃ pūjayeddharim \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Performing puja for the flag of Indra which is hoisted over the top of the house on the day of Dvadasi, then lord Ananta is worshipped on the day of Caturdasl.

## \|\| 2.29.104 \|\|

*kṛtvā darbhamayānantaṃ vāridhānyānvitaṃ tathā \|*  
*pūjayeccandanairgandhairnaivedyairvividhairapi \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Thereafter, an image of darbha grass should be made of the lord and it should be consecrated with paddy The sandalpasle and fragrant flowers should then be offered to the same, besides the eatables of various types, adoring him at the same time.

## \|\| 2.29.105-107 \|\|

*caturdaśa phalairmūlairjalajaiḥ kusumairapi \|*  
*yavagodhūmaśālīnāṃ cūrṇairnaikatamasya ca \|\| 105 \|\|*

*kṛtvā pūpāhvayaṃ tasmai dadyādekaṃ śrutekṣitam \|*  
*svayamekaṃ tu bhuñjīta dadyātsatrasya dorakam \|\| 106 \|\|*

*caturdaśagranthiyutaṃ kuṃkumena vilepitam \|*  
*caturdaśasūtramayaṃ sūtraṃ kārpāsameva ca \|\| 107 \|\|*

105-107. Then fourteen types of fruits, flowers like lotus etc., besides barley, wheat, rice powder, and the fried cakes should be offered. One of the cakes should be eaten by the Brahmana himself. Then he should offer fourteen strings of the thread with knots, soaked in vermilion. These threads should be made with cotton and should be offered in worship of the god.

## \|\| 2.29.108 \|\|

*ataḥ preta caturdaśyāṃ bhojayitvā tapodhanān \|*  
*dānaṃ dattvā dvijebhyaśca yamalokaṃ na gacchati \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Thereafter, on the day of Preta-Caturdasi, food should be served to the ascetics and charities should be given to the Brahmanas and by doing so, one does not have to travel to the place of Yama.

## \|\| 2.29.109-110 \|\|

*tataḥ pretakathāṃ śrutvā śākairnaktaṃ samācaret \|*  
*caturdaśaṃ dvādaśaṃ vā saptamaṃ vāpi pañcamam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*mānamātrādikaṃ kṛtvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. Then, listening to the story of Preta, fourteen, twelve, seven or five Brahmanas should be served with food for the night fast and by so doing, all the sins vanish in no time.

## \|\| 2.29.111 \|\|

*māghe māsi vaṭāpāyaḥ kasya pāpaṃ punīmahe \|*  
*snātvā tatra caturdaśyāṃ samaye tārakāmaye \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. To injure the banyan tree in the month of Magha is said to be extremely sinful During Brahma muhurta (early morning) when the stars are still visible in the sky, one does not get relieved of the sin by taking the bath to that extent.

## \|\| 2.29.112 \|\|

*saṃbhavetphālgune māsi yā ca kṛṣṇā caturdaśī \|*  
*śivarātririti khyātā sā jagatsarvakāmadā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The dark Calurdasi of the month of Phalguna is known as Siva-ratri, which fulfils all the desires in the world.

## \|\| 2.29.113 \|\|

*divā tasyā alābhe tu rātriyoge vrataṃ caret \|*  
*caturdaśī amāviddhā tadvrataṃ parivarjayet \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. In case the same tithi is not available during the day, then the fast should be observed at night. But the combined Caturdasi should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.29.114 \|\|

*tithiyoge ca śarvaryāṃ saṃpūrṇe vratamācaret \|*  
*kāmaviddhā sā ca pūjyā rātriyoge caredvratī \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. When the said tithi is available throughout the night, which fulfils all the desires, the vrata should be observed and the worship of lord Siva should be performed.

## \|\| 2.29.115-116 \|\|

*prahareprahare snānaṃ svayaṃ snātvā śivasya ca \|*  
*kārayedvidhivadbhaktyā homaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi \|\| 115 \|\|*

*atha vakṣyāmi caitrādimāse tu pūrṇimā yathā \|*  
*citrānakṣatrasaṃyukto gurupūrṇo vidhuryadi \|*  
*mahācaitrīti sā jñeyā pūrṇimākṣayapuṇyadā \|\| 116 \|\|*

115-116. At every prahara of the night, the devotee should himself take bath and bathe Sivalinga also with devotion. Thereafter, the homa should be performed appropriately. Now, I am highlighting the importance of the full moon days of Caitra and other months. When the Purnima falls in the Citra constellation with the combination of the moon and Jupiter, then the same is called as Maha-Caitri Panama, which bestows everlasting merit.

## \|\| 2.29.117 \|\|

*viśākhādiṣu bhedeṣu pūrṇacandro guruścaret \|*  
*mahāvaiśākhikādyāstu pūrṇimā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Similarly, in the month of Vaisakha, when the full moon appears in the Vaisakha constellation in union with Jupiter, it is known as Maha Vaisakhi Purnima. Similar is the case with all the Purnimas of the year.

## \|\| 2.29.118 \|\|

*mahājyaiṣṭhī viśeṣo'yaṃ prājāpatye yathā raviḥ \|*  
*gurupūrṇacandro jyeṣṭhāyāṃ mahājyaiṣṭhīti sā smṛtā \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Mahajyesthi Purnima has its own importance. When the Sun joins Prajapatya, on that particular day if the Jupiter joins with moon, then it is called Maha-Jyesthi Purnima.

## \|\| 2.29.119 \|\|

*vināpi guruṇā candraḥ kṛttikā pūrṇimā tathā \|*  
*tathā mahākārttikī sā tithiḥ puṇyatamā bhavet \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. During the month of Karttika in case the full moon without Jupiter enters Krttika constellation, it is known as Maha Karttiki which is the most auspicious one.

## \|\| 2.29.120 \|\|

*rohiṇyāṃ tu sthitaścandraḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu kārttike \|*  
*mahākārttikī tathāpi syātsvargaloke'pi durlabhā \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. During the month of Kirttika in case the full moon appears in the Rohini constellation on the same day, it is also called as the Maha Kartika Purnima. Access to the same makes a person reach the heaven.

## \|\| 2.29.121 \|\|

*citrā vā yadi vā pūrṇā yadā syātpūrṇimātithiḥ \|*  
*mahācaitrī tathāpi syādaśvamedhaphalapradā \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. In case Purnima falls in Citra constellation or there is Purnima in the Citra constellation, it is called Maha Caitri, which bestows the merit of Asvamedha yajna.

## \|\| 2.29.122 \|\|

*raviṇā kṛttikāyogādravivāre ca pūrṇimā \|*  
*mahācaitrī tathāpi syāddattasyākṣayakārikā \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. In case the combination of the Sun with Krttika compilation falls on a Sunday, then the said Purnima too bestows the everlasting merit and is known as Maha Caitri.

## \|\| 2.29.123-124 \|\|

*evaṃ gurau guroryoge mahācaitrī prakīrtitā \|*  
*tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca japo niyama eva ca \|\| 123 \|\|*

*sarvamakṣayatāṃ yāti phalaṃ caivāśvamedhikam \|*  
*pitarastarpitā yāṃti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokamakṣayam \|\| 124 \|\|*

123-124. Similarly, on the day of Jupiter, when the planet is combined with the tithi, it is called as Maha Caitri. The taking of bath, giving away of charities, performing of japam etc. on this tithi bestow the reward equivalent to the performing o f Asvamedha sacrifice. The Pitrs get pleased with the same and the devotees gain the everlasting abode of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.29.125 \|\|

*bharaṇyāṃ kārttike māsi yadi syātpūrṇimā tithiḥ \|*  
*gaṃgādvāre tu mahatī vaiśākhī puṇyadā smṛtā \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. During the Bharani constellation in the month of Karttika in case Purnima also appears, then it bestows great merit Similarly, holy dip in Ganga in the month of Vaisakha bestows great merit.

## \|\| 2.29.126-127 \|\|

*śālagrāme mahācaitrī kṛtapuṇyā mahātithiḥ \|*  
*gaṃgādvāre tu mahatī vaiśākhī puṇyadā smṛtā \|\| 126 \|\|*

*puruṣottame mahājyaiṣṭhī mahāṣāḍhī tu śṛṃkhale \|*  
*mahāśrāvaṇī kedāre mahāpuṇyatamā matā \|\| 127 \|\|*

126-127. In the Salagrama tirtha, the auspicious Mahacaitri Purnima and Mahavaisnavi Purnima at Gangadvara bestows great merit. Mahajyesthi bestows merit at Purusottama Ksetra, Mahasadhi at Srnkhala and Mahasravani at Kedara tirtha are known to be extremely auspicious.

## \|\| 2.29.128-129 \|\|

*mahābhādrī badaryāṃ ca kujo'pi syānnarastathā \|*  
*mahākārttikī puṣkare ca kānyakubje tathottaraṃ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*mahatī mārgaśīrṣe syādayodhyāyāṃ tathottare \|*  
*mahāpauṣī puṇyatamā mahāmāghī prayāgataḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

128-129. By taking bath at Badrikasrama during the Mahabhadri Purnima in the month of Bhadrapada, the people with deformed bodies attain beautiful bodies. Similarly, on the day of Mahakartiki Purnima (by taking bath at) Puskara, Kanyakubja and the northern region, one earns great merits besides the auspicious form. During the month of Margasirsa on the day of full moon, one earns merit by bathing at Ayodhya and its northern region. On the day of Mahapausa Purnima as well as during Mahamagha, (bath at) Prayaga is quite important

## \|\| 2.29.130 \|\|

*mahāphālgunī naimiṣe ca nirdiṣṭāḥ syurmahāphalāḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Similarly, Mahaphalguni is quite important for Naimisaranya and yields great merit.

## \|\| 2.29.131-132 \|\|

*atra sma vihitaṃ karma śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham \|*  
*sarvamakṣayatāṃ yāti varddhate cādhikaṃ phalam \|\| 131 \|\|*

*āśvine paurṇamāsī tu kaumudīti prakīrtitā \|*  
*asyāṃ candrodaye lakṣmīṃ pūjayedvidhivannaraḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

131-132. The auspicious deeds performed on these days bestow everlasting merits, which go on increasing. The Purnima of Asvina month is known as Kaumudl, during which a person should worship Laksmi at the time of moon rise in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 2.29.133 \|\|

*nirvatayenna yaḥ śrāddhaṃ prabhāte paitṛkaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*indukṣaye māsimāsi prāyaścittīyate tu saḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. The Brahmapas who do not offer sraddha on the moonless day in every month for the sake of the manes, they have to perform repentance rites.

## \|\| 2.29.134 \|\|

*candrāśvine tu kṛṣṇāyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*kṛtvā snānādikaṃ karma sopavāso dinaṃ nayet \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. On the moonless day of the month of Asvina, one should observe fast and taking bath and performing all appropriate rites, should spend the time.

## \|\| 2.29.135 \|\|

*pradoṣasamaye lakṣmīṃ pūjayitvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*dīpavṛkṣānyathā vṛkṣāṃllakṣmīprītyai samutsṛjet \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. After performing the worship of Laksmi during the evening time, lamps should be lighted under the trees.

## \|\| 2.29.136 \|\|

*nadītīre girau goṣṭhe śmaśāne vṛkṣamūlataḥ \|*  
*catuṣpathe nijāgāre catvare tānnidhāpayet \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Similarly, the lamps should be lighted over the river bank, mountain peaks, cow-pens, cremation ground, roots of the trees, crossings, in the house as well as on pedestal.

## \|\| 2.29.137 \|\|

*dvirbhojanamamāvāsyāṃ na kartavyaṃ kadācana \|*  
*śarvaryāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa māghaphālgunayornaraiḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. On the moonless day and particularly during the nights of Magha and Phalguna, person should not take food twice a day.

## Chapter 30. The Pravaras (Progenitor)

## \|\| 2.30.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vakṣye pravarasaṃtānaṃ yathākramamiti dvijāḥ \|*  
*yadvinā vyatyayo yasmāttasmācchāstrānusārataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said- О Brahmanas, I am now talking above the Pravaras as per provision of the scriptures, because without their knowledge some confusion becomes inevitable.

## \|\| 2.30.2-5 \|\|

*pravaratrayaṃ kāśyapasya kāśyapāśāvanairdhruvam \|*  
*pañcāśvagautamasyādya gautamaścoya eva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*cyavano jāmadagnyaśca āplavāyanameva ca \|*  
*mokunyāṃgirasabhāsyājjāmadagnyāplavāyanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śāṃḍilyāsitadaivalāḥ pravaratrayameva ca \|*  
*parāśarasya ca tathā svayaṃ śāṃbavaśiṣṭhakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ātreyamācāryaṇasyābālapravarameva hi \|*  
*vātsyavāsyāyanau caiva urukaṃṭaka eva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. There are three Pravaras of Kasyapa-gotra, which are known as Kasyapa, Savana and Gautama. Gautama has the Pravaras known as Pancasva Gautama, Jamadagnya, Aplavayana, Mokunya, Angirasa, Bhasya, Sandilya, Asita, Devala. Parasara has three Pravaras known as Samba, Vasistha. Atreya has Atreya, Acaryana, Syabala, Vatsya, Vatsyayana and Urukantaka.

## \|\| 2.30.6-9 \|\|

*arthakṣīramitrāvaruṇaṃ pañcamaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*autathyasya trayaṃ vidyādvālmīko'varameva hi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*autathyasya ca vāśiṣṭhamaindre cakraṃ ca krauñcāyanaṃ tathā \|*  
*autathyeti samākhyātaṃ māhiṣyaṃ cyavanaṃ tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*urukaṃṭatrayaṃ vidyātkauśikasya trayaṃ tathā \|*  
*yadgālo devarāṭ khyātaḥ kuśikādyāśca bho dvijāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*iti śrībhaviṇye mahāpurāṇe madhyama parvaṇi dvitīyabhāge navamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. Arthaksira and Mitravaruna is the fifth. Then Autathya, Valmlka and lower Autathya had Vasistha, Aindra, Cakra, Krauncayana, Autathya, Mahisya, Cyavana, Urukantaka and Kausika had three. Similarly, Gala, Devarata, Kusikadi, Visvamitra, Devarat, Ghrtakausika, Visvamitra and Aghamaryana.

## \|\| 2.30.10 \|\|

*caṇḍakauśikasya ca tathā devarāṭ devarātakam \|*  
*viśvāmitre tu vikhyātaḥ sumantoreva eva hi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Canda Kausika had Devarat, Devarataka, which happens to be the pravara of Visvamitra and Sumantu.

## \|\| 2.30.11-12 \|\|

*taruṃkaśākaṭāyanaḥ svayameva pravaratrayam \|*  
*bhramadvayaṃ jaimineśca svayaṃ vāśiṣṭhameva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śaṃkhamāṃgirasacyavanaṃ śaṃkhabhasya trayaṃ matam \|*  
*vātsyasya cyavano nāma āplavāyanakastathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Then there are Tarunka, Sakatayana, Jaimini, Vasistha, Samkhama, Sankha, Angirasa and Cyavana. Vatsalya has three-Cyavana, Aplava and Yanaka.

## \|\| 2.30.13 \|\|

*sāvarṇasya tu sāvarṇyacyavanajāmadagnibhārgavam \|*  
*āplavāyaneti pāṭhīne eka eva tu sattamāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Savarna had Savamya, Cyavana, Jamadagni, Bhargava, Pathina had Aplava.

## \|\| 2.30.14-15 \|\|

*kṛṣṇājinasya kṛṣṇājinaṃ viśvāmitrasya jaiminam \|*  
*kātyāyanasya kātyāyanagārgyāyaṇatrayaṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vātsyāyaneti vikhyātaṃ kuśikasya ca paṃcamam \|*  
*amuṃ ca viśvāmitraṃ ca jāmadagnyāplavāyanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Krsnajina had Krsnajina; Visvamitra had Jaimina; Katyayana had Katyayana, Gargyayana; Kusika had Vatsyayana and five others viz., : Kusika, Visvamitra, Jamadagnya. Aplavayana.

## \|\| 2.30.16 \|\|

*gārgyasya gārgyasāmuṃca tathāṃgirasa eva ca \|*  
*bārhaspatyabharadvāja iti paṃca prakīrtitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Gargya had Gargyasa, Munca, Angirasa. Barhaspatya and Bharadvaja. These were the five Pravaras.

## \|\| 2.30.17-23 \|\|

*vaśiṣṭhasya ca vāsiṣṭhaṃ ca tathāṃgirasa eva ca \|*  
*mitrāvaruṇasaṃyuktaṃ tāvattasya prakīrtitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jāhvakarṇabhavakarṇau pravarau parikīrtitau \|*  
*upamanyurupamanyostathendraḥ saha eva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*taduttameti tritayaṃ mitrāvaruṇasya ca trayam \|*  
*ātreyagautamāṃgirasapravaratrayameva hi \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kamaṃḍalotpalamitrāmitrāvaruṇa eva ca \|*  
*kamaṃḍaluśceti tritayaṃ pravaratrayameva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*cyavanasya tathā jñeyamūrvacyavanāplavāyanam \|*  
*atha sa kasyāṃgirasabārhaspatya eva trayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*āgastyasya agastiśca māhaśca cyavaneti ca \|*  
*viśvāmitre devarāta autathyeti tathaiva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ye noktā ye 'pyavijñātāste proktāḥ kāśyapājjagat \|\| 23 \|\|*

17-23. Vasistha had Vasistha, Angirasa, Mitravaruna, Jahvakama, Bhavakarna; Upamanyu had Upamanyu, Indra; Mitravaruna had Atreya, Gautama, Angirasa; Kamandalu had Angirasa, Berhaspatya; Agastya had three viz.: Agasti, Maha, Cyavana; Visvamitra had Devarata and Autathya as Pravaras. Those whose names have not been mentioned, nothing else can be spoken about them. They are known in the world by the name of Kasyapa.

## Chapter 31. Yajna of architecture

## \|\| 2.31.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vāstuyāgamatho vakṣye balimaṇḍalapūrvakam \|*  
*aṃkurārpaṇakaṃ kṛtvā madhye kuryācca maṃḍalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*trihastā piṃḍikā kāryā caturasrā udakplavā \|*  
*prādeśamātra utsedho darpaṇāṃtarnibho bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said- I am now speaking about the building of houses or the places of the yajnas. Sowing the saplings in the middle of the mandala in such a way that it is surrounded by three cubits on all sides being square, the pedestal should be medium in the centre.

## \|\| 2.31.3 \|\|

*madhye saṃmārjayedvidvānpādānnava yathākramāt \|*  
*koṇe catuṣpadaṃ jñeyaṃ dikṣu tripadakaṃ kramāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By a learned person in the centre, sprinkling should be done. In the comer, fourfooted and in the directions, three-footed figures should be established.

## \|\| 2.31.4 \|\|

*pañcakaṃ yugmapādena caturdikṣu tataḥ param \|*  
*koṇe catuṣpadaṃ sthāpyaṃ catuṣkoṇe vibhāvayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thereafter, in all the four directions, five two-footed figures and in the four comers, four-footed figures should be made.

## \|\| 2.31.5-7 \|\|

*catuṣkoṇaṃ bahiḥ kuryātkoṇe cāpi catuṣṭayam \|*  
*dvātriṃśacca bhavedbāhye cātaścāpi trayodaśa \|\| 5 \|\|*

*catvāriṃśatpañcayutā militvā vāstudevatāḥ \|*  
*śikhī caivātha parjanyo jayaṃtaḥ kuliśāyudhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sūryaḥ satyo vṛṣaścaiva ākāśaṃ vāyureva ca \|*  
*pūṣā ca vitathaścaiva guhānyaśca yamastathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Four triangles should be made in the four exterior sides as well as in the comers. Thirty two gods should be lodged in the exterior and in the interior and thirteen deities should be established. Thus, the Vastu-god (the lords of architecture are said to be forty five). They include Sikhi, Parjanya, Jayanta, Kulisayudha, Surya, Satya, Vrsa, the sky, Pusa, Vitatha, Guha, Yama.

## \|\| 2.31.8-10 \|\|

*gandharvo mṛgarājastu mṛgāḥ pitṛgaṇāstathā \|*  
*dauvāriko'tha sugrīvaḥ puṣpadanto jalādhipaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*asuraḥ paśupāśau ca rogo hi mokṣa eva ca \|*  
*bhallāṭaḥ somasarpau ca aditiśca ditistathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bahirdvādaśa ityetānīśānādīnyathākramam \|*  
*īśānādicatuṣkoṇaṃ saṃsthitānpūjayedbudhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Gandharva, Mrgaraja, Mrgagana, Pitrgana, Dauvarika, Sugriva, Puspadanta, Varuna, Asura, Pasu, Pasa, Roga, Moksa, Bhallata, Soma, Sarpa, Aditi and Diti. Besides twelve gods should be lodged in north-east and other comers, who should be worshipped by the learned people.

## \|\| 2.31.11-12 \|\|

*āpaścaivātha sāvitro jayo rudrastathaiva ca \|*  
*aryamā savitā caiva vivasvānvibudhādhipaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mitro'tha rājayakṣmā ca saptamaḥ pṛthivīdharaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamastvāpavatsastu paridhau brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Jaladeva, Savitra, Jaya, Rudra, Aryama, Savita, Vivasvan, Vibudhadhipa (Indra), Mitra, Rajayaksama, seventh Prthvidhara and Apavatsa —the eighth one, are lodged within limit of Brahma individually.

## \|\| 2.31.13-14 \|\|

*pūrvādiṣu tathā pūjyā gandhapuṣpaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*paṃcacatvāriṃśadetaccarakyā ca caturthakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*militvā ūnapañcāśaduttamā vāstudevatāḥ \|*  
*nānyatra yojayedviprāḥ prāsāde ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The gods lodged in the east should be worshipped individually with fragrant flowers, in an appropriate manner. Thus the forty five gods who have been spelt out and by adding four more, their number becomes forty nine. О best of the Brahmanas, these deities must be worshipped at the time o f the first entry in the house and not during other functions. They must be adored at the time of entry into a palace.

## \|\| 2.31.15-16 \|\|

*bahiḥ koṇe carakyādi carakaṃ ca vidārikām \|*  
*pūtanāṃ ca tataḥ paścādvāyavye pāparākṣasīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

*svaiḥsvairmaṃtraiśca gaṃdhādyaiḥ pūjayetkusumādinā \|*  
*yathoktena baliṃ dadyātpāyasānnena vā punaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. In the outer comer Caraki and Caraka should be lodged in the north-west comer. In the south-west comer, Vidarika besides Putana —the killer of children (demoness) should be lodged. She should be adored offering the fragrant flowers, reciting the mantra. The offerings of payasam should also be made to them.

## \|\| 2.31.17 \|\|

*rekhāḥ sarvatra śuklena padmaṃ raktena bhāvayet \|*  
*rañjayedeva varṇena bahiṣpañcarajena tu \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The lines drawn on all the sides should be in white colour; the lotus should be of red colour. The exterior surface should be decorated with five different types of colour powders.

## \|\| 2.31.18-19 \|\|

*devavarṇānatho vakṣye yathāvadanuvarṇitāḥ \|*  
*rakto gaurastathā śoṇaḥ sitaraktaḥ sitastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pītaḥ śuklaśca dharmaśca pūṣā raktaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*śyāmaḥ śukraśca kṛṣṇaśca pītaḥ śuklo yathākramam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. I am now speaking about the colours to be used for the making of the image of the deities. The images should be coloured with red, white, blood red, bright red, shining yellow, white, dharma, Рusa —red dark, bright, black, yellow and white bright. In the same sequence, the images should be coloured.

## \|\| 2.31.20-21 \|\|

*pīto bhṛṃgaḥ punaḥ śuklaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śuklastathaiva ca \|*  
*raktaḥ śuklaśca śoṇaśca kṛṣṇaraktastathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dhūmrapīto raktapītaḥ śuklaḥ kṛṣṇaśca śyāmakaḥ \|*  
*raktavarṇena dvātriṃśaddaśa varṇāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Yellow, black like the black wasp, white, black, red, white, red, black, blood-red, yellow, yellow-red, white, black, dark and red colour should be used in this sequence. These are the thirty two colours which are to be used in a sequence.

## \|\| 2.31.22-27 \|\|

*śuklaśoṇaṃ punaḥ śvetaṃ siṃdūrābhaṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*pāṃḍurakuṃkumābhaṃ ca raktaṃ jñeyaṃ ca pītakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śuklapītaṃ ca śvetaṃ ca gauraṃ cetyaṣṭavarṇakam \|*  
*pītaṃ raktaṃ ca śyāmaṃ ca gauraṃ ceti catuṣṭayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dharaṇīmadanaṃ vādye śaṃbhuvarṇādiprakramāt \|*  
*śuklena rañjayeddvārānpuradvāraṃ ca madhyame \|\| 24 \|\|*

*madhyeṃte ūnapañcāśatsarvaṃ ca vāstukarmaṇi \|*  
*catvāriṃśaddvārayutaṃ gṛhadevakule'pi ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mahākūpe tathā śveto anyatrāpi praśasyate \|*  
*sulipte ca śucau deśe sārdhahastapramāṇataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*daśa pūrvāyatā rekhā daśa caivottarāyatāḥ \|*  
*ekādaśīpadaṃ kuryādrekhābhiḥ padakena tu \|\| 27 \|\|*

22-27. White, red, white, vermilion, saffron yellow, red, yellow, whitish yellow, white and bright are the eight colours. Besides these, the yellow, red, black and white are the four colours, with which the images should be decorated. In the sequence of Sambhu colour the use of Dharani-madana colour has been prescribed for the musical instruments. The doors should be painted white. The middle gate of the village or a town, besides the last door also should be painted accordingly. Thus in the science of architecture, all forty nine colours have been prescribed, in which forty colours are for the doors. Similar is the case with die living houses. For great well, white colour should be used, the use of which has been said to be praiseworthy elsewhere as well. In the beautifully plastered place, there should be a pedestal of a cubit and a half over which ten lines should be drawn in the eastwest and ten on the north-south directions. These lines should touch eleven points.

## \|\| 2.31.28-30 \|\|

*sarvavāstuvibhāgena vijñeyā navakā nava \|*  
*padasthānpūjayeddevāṃstriṃśatpañcādaśadeva tu \|\| 28 \|\|*

*dvātriṃśadbāhyataḥ pūjyāḥ pūjyāgāre trayodaśa \|*  
*madhye nava pade brahmā tasyāpyaṣṭau samīpagāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*caturdikṣu ṣaṭpadaṃ tu tripadaṃ tu catuṣpadam \|*  
*padaikaṃ tu catuṣkoṇe eṣa vāstuvinirṇayaḥ \|*  
*carakyādi tato hitvā catvāriṃśacca paṃcakam \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. In all die matters relating to architecture, according to each section, a total number of eighty one places are built. The gods lodged at these places should be adored. There should be thirty two in the outer regions. At the thirteen places of worship and the nine middle places, Brahma and his eight close associates, the sixfooted deities at all the four directions, four-footed at three places besides one each at each one of the four comers, should be established according to the science of architecture. Thus by discarding Caraki etc., only forty five deities are left to be adored.

## \|\| 2.31.31-32 \|\|

*aparaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vakṣye yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*navarekhāprayogeṇa navakoṣṭhānprakalpayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dvicatuṣkoṣṭhakairdikṣu yajetāryamaṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*vivasvaṃtaṃ tato mittraṃ mahīdharamataḥ param \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. According to the scriptures, I am speaking about the description of the second mandala according to which nine cubicals should be created by drawing nine lines. In the eight cubicals of the sides, Aryama (Surya) should be worshipped. Then on the two outer cubicals, Mitra, Vivasvan and Mahidhara should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.31.33-37 \|\|

*koṇeṣu koṣṭhadvaṃdveṣu bāhyādiparikīrtitam \|*  
*sāvitraṃ savitāraṃ ca śakramindraṃ jayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*rudraṃ rudrajayaṃ caiva vāyuṃ jṛṃbhakameva ca \|*  
*pilipicchaṃ ca medhāvī vidārī pūtanā tathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kramādīśānaparyaṃtāṃ jayaṃtaḥ śakrabhāskarau \|*  
*satyovṛṣāṃtarikṣau ca diśi prācyāmavasthitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*agniḥ pūṣā ca vitadho yamaśca gṛharakṣakaḥ \|*  
*gaṃdharvo bhṛṃgarājaśca mṛgo dakṣiṇamāśritāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*nirṛtirdauvārikaśca sugrīvavaruṇau tataḥ \|*  
*puṣpadaṃtasvarau śoṣarogau pratyagdiśi sthitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

33-37. Thereafter, the learned people should worship Savitra, Savita, Sakra, Indra, Jaya, Rudra, Rudrajaya, Vayu, Jrmbhaka, Pilipiccha, Vidari and Putana. The learned person should worship these gods on the north-east. Jayanta, Bhaskara, Sakra, Satya and Vrsntariksa should be adored on the east; Agni, Pusa, Vitatha, Yama, Grharaksaka, Gandharva, Bhrngaraja, Mrgadaksina, Nirrti, Daivarika, Sugriva, Varuna, Puspadanta, Savaracosa and Roga should be worshipped in the west.

## \|\| 2.31.38 \|\|

*prāṇavāyuśca nāgaśca somo bhallāṭa eva ca \|*  
*mudgalākhyo dityaditī kuberasya diśi sthitāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Ghrana, Vayu, Naga, Soma, Bhallata, Mudgala. Diti and Aditi are respected and adored in that direction.

## \|\| 2.31.39 \|\|

*militvā ca tripañcāśattebhyaḥ pūrve baliṃ haret \|*  
*piṇyākaiḥ paramānnairvā pūrvoktairvā yathā kramāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Fifty three more deities have to be added to the above number and established in the eastern direction and then adored. Thereafter, offering oil seeds, besides the excellent food items mentioned above, the offering should be made.

## \|\| 2.31.40 \|\|

*raktamaryamaṇaṃ dhyāyeccaturbhirbahubhirvṛtam \|*  
*śvetāśvavāhanaṃ divyaṃ kirīṭaiḥ svairvibhūṣitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One should then meditate upon Aryama seated in a carriage driven by four white horses, who is adorned with the best of his crown. He is of red complexion and should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.41 \|\|

*ākṛṣṇeneti mantrasya svarṇa ṛṣijagatīchandaḥ savitraryamaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Reciting the mantra— Akrsnena-ti, whose Rsi is Svarna, Jagati is the meter and the Viniyoga is to please Savita and Aryama, which should be performed.

## \|\| 2.31.42-43 \|\|

*vivasvaṃtaṃ pītavarṇaṃ pītāmbaradharaṃ śubham \|*  
*meṣasthaṃ ca mahākāyaṃ devagandharvasevitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*etātaviṣaṃtīti maṃtrasya kardama ṛṣiḥ paṃktiśchandaḥ kamalādevatāvivasvatprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Vivasvan who is clad in yellow lower garment, is mounted over the sheep and served by the gods and the Gandharvas of gigantic sizes, should be adored. The mantra - Etativisami-ti, whose Rsi is Kardama, the meter is Pankti, Kamala is the Devata and the Viniyoga should be red to Vivasvan.

## \|\| 2.31.44-45 \|\|

*mitraṃ dhyāyecchuklavarṇaṃ śvetahaṃsoparisthi tam \|*  
*trinetraṃ tribhujaṃ caiva śvetāṃbaradharaṃ śubham \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kayānaścīti maṃtrasya jayaṃta ṛṣirgāyatrī chandaḥ śaṅkaro devatā mitraprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. For pleasing three-eyed and three-armed Mitra who has bright complexion, is mount») over the swan, clad in white garments, the mantra is- Kayanasci-ti, the Rsi of which is Jayanta, Gayatri is the meter; and Sankara is the god to whom the Viniyoga should be offered.

## \|\| 2.31.46 \|\|

*prītaṃ mahīdharaṃ dhyāyedvṛṣabhopari saṃsthim \|*  
*tribhujaṃ padmahastaṃ ca vyālayajñopavītinam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Lord Mahidhara should be meditated upon who is mounted over a bull, having three arms, decorated with lotus flowers, wearing the sacred thread of a serpent.

## \|\| 2.31.47 \|\|

*tryambakamiti maṃtrasya gargaṛṣistriṣṭup chando haro devatā mahīdharaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. His mantra is - “Tryambakamiti, Rsi of the mantra is Garga; Tristupa is the meter Нага is the god and the Viniyoga has to be made in favour of Mahidhara.

## \|\| 2.31.48-49 \|\|

*sāvitrīṃ śvetavarṇāṃ ca sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutām \|*  
*dvibhujāṃ pītavastrāṃ ca śvetasiṃhāsane sthitām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*raktāmbaradharāṃ raktāṃ raktamālopaśobhitām \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. The goddess Savitri is of white complexion, endowed with all the auspicious symptoms, is two-armed, clad in a Pitambara and is seated over a white lion-throne and is clad in red garments. She is adorned with garlands of red flowers and should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.50 \|\|

*tadvarṣaṃ iti maṃtrasya gautama ṛṣirvirāṭ chandaḥ sūryo devatā savitṛprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Gautama is the Rsi for the mantra-Tadvarsa; Viraja is the meter; Surya is the god and the Viniyoga is for the pleasure of Savita.

## \|\| 2.31.51 \|\|

*śakraṃ dhyāyetpītavarṇaṃ śuklakairāvatasthitam \|*  
*sarvadevaiḥ stūyamānaṃ dvibhujaṃ pītavāsasam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He is of yellow complexion, is riding over the white elephant Airavata. He is adored by all the gods, has two arms. He is clad in a yellow garment who should be adored.

## \|\| 2.31.52 \|\|

*trātāramiti maṃtrasya bhārgava ṛṣistriṣṭup chando narasiṃho devatā indrajayaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Bhargava is the Rsi for the mantra-Tratarami-ti; Tristupa is the meter; Narasimha is the god; and for the pleasure of Indra-Jaya, the Viniyoga is to be performed.

## \|\| 2.31.53 \|\|

*rudraṃ dhyāyecchvetavarṇaṃ vṛṣabhārūḍhavigraham \|*  
*nāgayajñopavītaṃ ca sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Rudradeva is of white complexion, is mounted over the bull, has the serpents swing as the yajnopavlta, has all the auspicious symbols, such a Rudradeva should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.54 \|\|

*namaste rudreti maṃtrasya gāyatrī chaṃdastryaṃbako devatā rudraprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. His mantra is Namaste Rudreti, having Gayatri meter, Tryambaka is the god and the Viniyoga has to be offered for the pleasure of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.31.55 \|\|

*raktaṃ rudraṃ jayaṃ dhyāyedraktapadmopari sthitam \|*  
*raktaśyāmāṃbaradharaṃ dvibhujaṃ raktavāsasam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Rudradeva is two-armed, of red complexion and is seated over the seat of red lotus flowers. He is clad in blackish red garments, having two arms, is clad in red costumes, such a type of Rudra Jayadeva should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.56 \|\|

*tryaṃbakamiti mantrasya gāyatrīcchando maheśo devatā rudrajayaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. His mantra is Tryambaka-iti; Gayatri is the meter; Mahesa is the god and the Viniyoga is meant for the pleasure of Rudra Jaya

## \|\| 2.31.57 \|\|

*api śvetaṃ tato dhyāyedvarābhayakaraṃ param \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ śvetapadmopari sthitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The Svetadeva, possessing all the auspicious symbols, seated over the white lotus scat and bestows protection, should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.58-59 \|\|

*īśāna iti maṃtrasya marīcirṛṣiḥ paṃkticchando vāyurdevatā apāṃ prītaye viniyogaḥ \|*  
*āpavatsaṃ pītavarṇaṃ meṣārūḍhaṃ caturbhujam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*padmaśaṃkhadharaṃ vāme varābhayakaraṃ param \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Marica is the Rsi for Isana mantra; Pankti is the meter; Vayu is the god and the Viniyoga should be offered to please the god Varuna. Then Vatsadeva who is of yellow complexion, has the sheep as his mount. He is four-armed. In his two left hands, he holds a lotus and a conch. He bestows the excellent boons and conjugal pleaure, therefore he should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.60 \|\|

*varuṇasyottaṃbhanamasīti mantrasya narottama ṛṣirvirāṭ chando varuṇo devatā āvayaḥ prītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. His mantra is Varunasyottambhanamasiti; the Rsi is Narottama; Virat is the meter; Varuna is the god and the Viniyoga is for the pleasure of Avayahprityartham.

## \|\| 2.31.61-62 \|\|

*koṇasūtrasyobhayataḥ śvetakoṣṭhadvaye punaḥ \|*  
*śarvaṃ dhyāyedraktavarṇaṃ vṛṣabhopari saṃsthitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*dvibhujaṃ ca trinetraṃ ca jaṭābhāropaśobhitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. In both the white corner cubicals of the rear side, Sarvodeva is lodged. Lord Sarva is lodged seated over the bull. He is of red complexion, having two arms and three eyes. His head is decorated with the locks of hair. He should be adored in this form.

## \|\| 2.31.63 \|\|

*mālā svāheti maṃtrasya bhārgava ṛṣirgāyatrīchando mahādevo devatā śarvaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. For the mantra- “Mala-svaheti' Bhargava is the Risi; Gayatri is the meter; Mahadeva is the god and the Viniyoga is offered for the sake of Sarva.

## \|\| 2.31.64 \|\|

*guhaṃ dhyāyetpītavarṇaṃ pītapadmāsanasthitama \|*  
*nānābharaṇaśobhāḍhyaṃ kuṇḍalādyairalaṅkṛtam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Guhyadeva is of yellow complexion and is seated over the seat of yellow lotus flowers. He is adorned with various types of ornaments including the kundalas. He should be meditated upon in this form.

## \|\| 2.31.65 \|\|

*sa bodha iti mantrasya agastirṛṣirgāyatrī chando haro devatā guhaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Agastya is the Rsi for the verse Sa bodha; Gdyatri is the meter, Нага is the god and the Viniyoga is for the Guha.

## \|\| 2.31.66 \|\|

*aryamṇaṃ dvibhujaṃ raktaṃ raktamālyopaśobhitam \|*  
*raktapadmāsanasthaṃ ca devagandharvasevitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Aryama has two arms, has red complexion and wears also the garlands of red flowers. He is lodged over the red lotus flower and is surrounded by the gods and the Gandharvas. He should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.67 \|\|

*vāto vāreti maṃtrasya kāśyapa ṛṣiranuṣṭupchando vāyurdevatā aryamaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Kasyapa is the Rsi for Vatovara mantra; Anustupa is the meter; Vayu happens to be the god and the Viniyoga has to be performed for the sake of Aryama.

## \|\| 2.31.68 \|\|

*dhyāyecca jambhakaṃ śvetaṃ dvibhujaṃ kuṭilānanam \|*  
*karālavadanaṃ ghoraṃ varāhopari saṃsthitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The god Jrmbhaka is of white complexion, having two arms, crooked face, terrific body, horrible form and is mounted over Varaha or a boar. He should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.69 \|\|

*kuvidogavaya iti mantrasya viśvāmitra ṛṣirjagatī chandaḥ somo devatā jaṃbhakaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Kuvidogavaya is the mantra; Visvamitra is the Risi for it; Jagati is the meter; Soma is the god and for the pleasure of Jambhaka, the Viniyoga is to be offered.

## \|\| 2.31.70 \|\|

*pilapicchaṃ raktavarṇaṃ raktamālyairalaṅkṛtam \|*  
*raktapadmāsanasthaṃ ca raktābharaṇaśobhitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Pilapicchadeva is of red complexion, is adorned with the garlands of the red flowers and is seated over the seat of red lotus flower. He is adorned with the ornaments of red colour. He should thus be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.71 \|\|

*devasya heti mantrasya paṃktiśchaṃdaḥ śacī devatā pilapicchaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Devasyaheti is the mantra for him; Pankti is the meter; Saci is the Devata and the Viniyoga has to be offered for the pleasure of the god Pilapichha.

## \|\| 2.31.72-73 \|\|

*pītāṃ ca carakīṃ dhyāyedraktamālyairalaṃkṛtām \|*  
*sucāruvadanāṃ bhavyāṃ guñjāhāropaśobhitām \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tadvarṣaṃ iti mantrasya jaṭila ṛṣirbṛhatī chando bhavo devatā carakīprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. The goddess Caraki is of yellow complexion, is adorned with garlands of red flowers. She has a beautiful face, a pleasant figure. She is adorned with the garland of Gunja flowers. She should be meditated upon. Tadvarsa is the hymn for her, Jatila is the Rsi; Brhati is the meter; Bhava is the god; and Viniyoga should be performed for the pleasure of Caraki.

## \|\| 2.31.74 \|\|

*śyāmāṃ vidārikāṃ dhyāyettrinetrāṃ ca caturbhujām \|*  
*nānāgaṇayutāṃ devīṃ paṅkajadvayadhāriṇīm \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The goddess Vidarika with three eyes is of dark complexion. She has four arms and is served by several of the gaqas. She holds two lotus flowers in her hands. She should be meditated upon accordingly.

## \|\| 2.31.75 \|\|

*śrīśca te iti mantrasya varuṇa ṛṣirnṛsiṃho devatā vidārikāprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Her mantra is Srisruta and Varuna is the Rsi for the same, while Narasimha is the god and the Viniyoga should be offered for the pleasure of Vidarika.

## \|\| 2.31.76 \|\|

*raktāṃ ca pūtanāṃ dhyāyetpaṅkajasthāṃ suśobhanām \|*  
*sarvābharaṇasaṃpannāṃ sarvālaṃkāraśobhitām \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Putana - the goddess with red complexion, adorned with all the ornaments, is seated over a lotus flower. She is extremely beautiful and should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.77 \|\|

*mayi gṛhṇāmīti maṃtrasya vivasvānṛṣirnārāyaṇo devatā pūtanāprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Her mantra is - Mayi grhnami; the Rsi of which is Vivasvan; Narayana is the god and foe Viniyoga has to be performed for the pleasure of the goddess Putana.

## \|\| 2.31.78-79 \|\|

*pūrvādidikṣu sarvāsu sārdhādyaṃtapadeṣu ca \|*  
*īśānaṃ jaṭilaṃ śvetaṃ śūlahastaṃ mahābhujam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*trinetraṃ vṛṣabhārūḍhaṃ nāgahāro paśobhitam \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. In all the cubicals in the eastern direction, Isanadeva has to be lodged who wears the matted locks of hair, is of white complexion, holding a trident in his hand. He had long arms, three eyes and is mounted over the bull. He is adorned with the ornaments of the snakes, who should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.80 \|\|

*āyuḥśīrṣāṇa iti maṃtrasya vāmadeva ṛṣirbṛhatī chando dharaṇīdharo devatā īśānaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The mantra for him is said to be Ayu-Strfdria; the Rsi of which is Vamadeva; Brhati is the meter; Dharapldhara is the god and the Viniyoga has to be performed for the sake of Капа.

## \|\| 2.31.81 \|\|

*raktaṃ dhyāyecca parjanyaṃ dvibhujaṃ pītavāsasam \|*  
*dakṣiṇe paraśuṃ dhyāyedoṃkāraṃ ca tathāpare \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The god Parjanya is two-armed, of red complexion, is clad in yellow lower garments. He holds a battle-axe in his right hand. One should meditate upon him with Omkara.

## \|\| 2.31.82 \|\|

*kayānaśceti mantrasya dharma ṛṣirbṛhatī chando bhavo devatā parjanya prītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Dharma is the Risi for the hymn Kayanasca; Brhati is the meter; Bhava is the god and the Viniyoga has to be offered for the pleasure of Parjanya.

## \|\| 2.31.83 \|\|

*jayantaṃ śvetaṃ śvetavṛṣabhārūḍhaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*mānastoketi mantrasya śaktyṛṣistriṣṭupchandaḥ śaṅkaro devatā jayaṃtaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Jayantadeva is of white complexion and is mounted over the white bull. He should be mediated upon. His mantra is Menastoke; Sakti is the Rsi; while Tristupa is the meter, Sankara is the god and the Viniyoga has to be performed for the sake of Jayanta.

## \|\| 2.31.84 \|\|

*śuklaṃ pītaṃ dvibhujamairāvatasthaṃ vajradharaṃ dhyātvā mūlabījena sthāpayet \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The god (Indra), holder of a vajra has bright complexion, having two arms and is mounted over the elephant Airavata. He should be meditated upon. Then the said is required to be sown.

## \|\| 2.31.85 \|\|

*bhāskaraṃ raktadvibhujaṃ raktāśvasthaṃ dhyātvā māyābījena pūjayet \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The two-armed Bh3skaradeva had red complexion, is mounted over the red-coloured steed. He should be worshipped with the seeds of lotus flowers.

## \|\| 2.31.86 \|\|

*satyaṃ ca dvibhujaṃ śvetaṃ trinetraṃ pītavāsasaṃ mandakuṃdabījena pūjayet \|*  
*vṛṣaṃ pītaṃ vṛṣabhārūḍhamākāśabījena pūjayet \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Two-armed, white-complexioned, threeeyed and yellow clad lord Satyadeva should be adored with Mandakunda seed. The yellow-complexioned Vrsbhadeva is mounted over a bull and should be worshipped with the seeds of the sky.

## \|\| 2.31.87 \|\|

*ṛkṣaṃ nīlaṃ caturbhujaṃ mahiṣārūḍham \|*  
*ācchīma iti mantrasya hotā yakṣa ṛṣistriṣṭupchandaḥ śaṃkaro devatā ṛkṣaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The four armed Rksadeva, who is of blue complexion and is mounted over a bull, should be meditated upon. Acchima-iti is the mantra and the Rsi for the same is Yak$a; Tristupa is the meter. The Viniyoga is to be performed for the sake of Rksa.

## \|\| 2.31.88 \|\|

*agnimārabhya pūjayet \|*  
*agniṃ raktaṃ saptajihvaṃ raktavāsasaṃ piṅgākṣaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*agnidūtamiti maṃtrasya bharadvāja ṛṣistriṣṭucchandaḥ śaṃkaro devatā agniprītaye vini yogaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The process of the worship is required to be commenced with the adoration of the fire god. Initially, the fire god should be meditated upon. The fire god with seven tongues, having red complexion and yellowish eyes should be meditated upon, reciting the mantra- “Agnim dutamiti’ the Rsi of which is Bharadvaja; Tristupa is the meter; Sankara is the god and the Viniyoga is to be performed to please the fire god.

## \|\| 2.31.89 \|\|

*vitathaṃ raktamajavāhanaṃ dvibhujaṃ dhyātvā gāyatryā pūjayet \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Vitathadeva has a he goat as his mount. He himself is two armed and should be meditated upon with Gayatri

## \|\| 2.31.90 \|\|

*gāyatryā viśvāmitra ṛṣirgāyatrīchandaḥ savitā devatā vitathaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Visvamitra is the Rsi of Gayatri mantra; Gayatri is the meter; Savita is the go and Viniyoga has to be offered to please Vitatha

## \|\| 2.31.91 \|\|

*yamaṃ kṛṣṇamahiṣārūḍhaṃ daṇḍahastaṃ dhyāyet \|*  
*acchiya iti mantrasya triṣṭupchando bhavānī devatā yamaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Yama - the god of death, whose mount is the black coloured he-buffola, holds a stuff in his hand (known as yamadanda). Yama has to be meditated upon accordingly. His mantra is-“Acchiya-iti’ meter of which is Tristupa-, Bhavani is the Devata and the Viniyoga has to be offered for the sake of Yama.

## \|\| 2.31.92 \|\|

*gṛhe kṣetraṃ raktamūrdhvakeśaṃ mahābhujaṃ raktavāsasaṃ dhyātvā vahnibījena pūjayet \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The Ksetradeva with rising hair, long arms and red complexion should be worshipped with vahni seeds.

## \|\| 2.31.93 \|\|

*gandharvaṃ śvetaṃ dvibhujaṃ padmāsanasthaṃ dhyātvā yamabījena pūjayet \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. The Gandharva god clad in white costumes, having two arms and seated over a lotus seat should be worshipped with Yama-seed.

## \|\| 2.31.94 \|\|

*bhṛṅgarājaṃ raktasiṃhāsanārūḍhaṃ divyayajñopavītinaṃ dhyāyet \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The gods Bhrngaraja who is seated over a red lion-throne, wears a divine yajnopavita and should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.31.95 \|\|

*hotā yasketi mantrasya bhārgava ṛṣirgāyatrīchando yaśo devatā bhṛṃgarājaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. His mantra is- “Hota-yasketi', the Rsi of which is Bhargava; meter is Gayatri; Yasa is the god and Viniyoga should be offered for the pleasure of Bhrdgaraja.

## \|\| 2.31.96 \|\|

*mṛgaṃ pītaṃ mṛgārūḍhaṃ pītavāsasaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*kadācaneti mantrasya vāmadevaṛṣirbṛhatī chando vāmadevo devatā mṛgaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The Mrgadeva should be meditated upon, who is of yellow complexion, is seated over a deer and clad in yellow garments. His mantra is- “Kadacaneti', the Risi of the mantra is Vamadeva; Brhati is the meter; Vamadeva is the god and the Viniyoga should be offered to please the god Mrgadeva.

## \|\| 2.31.97 \|\|

*nairṛtārddhapadeṣu ca \|*  
*nirṛtiṃ pītaṃ śvetaṃ padmāsanasthaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*kaidācaneti mantrasya paṃktiśchandaḥ savitā devatā nirṛtiprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Nairrta is of yellow complexion, is clad in white garments and is seated in padmasana or lotus seat He should be meditated upon with mantra- "Kadacaneti’ which is composed in Pankti meter and Savita is the god for the same. The Viniyoga should be offered to please the god Nairfti.

## \|\| 2.31.98 \|\|

*nairṛtārddhapadeṣu ca dauvārikaṃ śvetaśarabhārūḍhaṃ trinetraṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*hotasveti mantrasya narasiṃhaṛṣirbṛhatī chando gaṇeśo devatā dauvārikaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Again at the same place, Dauvarikadeva having two arms and three eyes should be meditated upon adorned with all the ornaments. His mantra is- “Hotasveti’ with Narasimha as the Risi; Brhati is the meter; Gapesa is the god. The Viniyoga should be offered for the pleasure of Dauvarika.

## \|\| 2.31.99 \|\|

*śyāmaṃ sugrīvaṃ kṛṣṇameṣārūḍhaṃ pītavāsasaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*svādityeti mantrasya triṣṭupchando vāmano devatā sugrīvaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The god Sugriva has mount of a black sheep. He himself is of black complexion and wears a pitambara. He should be meditated upon with the mantra- “Svadit yeti’, composed in Tristupa meter, having Vamana as the god. The Viniyoga should be offered to please the god Sugriva,

## \|\| 2.31.100 \|\|

*sumitriyā na iti mantrasya kandarpaṛṣiḥ paṅktiśchandaḥ sūryo devatā varuṇaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The mantra - “Sumitriya na” has Kandarpa as the Rsi. It was composed in Panto meter with Surya as the god, while the Viniyoga has to be offered to please the god Varuna.

## \|\| 2.31.101 \|\|

*puṣpadaṃtaṃ pītaṃ meṣārūḍhaṃ pītavāsasaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*yā oṣadhīriti mantrasya manmatha ṛṣirjagatī chando vāyurdevatā puṣpadaṃtaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The god Puspadanta is of yellow complexion. He is mounted over the yellow sheep and is clad in yellow garment His mantra is- “ Osadhiriti which was composed by Manmatha Rsi in Jagati meter, with Vayu as the god. The Viniyoga should be offered to please Puspadanta.

## \|\| 2.31.102 \|\|

*asuraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇamālyairalaṃkṛtaṃ kṛtvā \|*  
*ākṛṣṇeti mantrasya hiraṇyavarṇa ṛṣirjagatī chandaḥ savitā devatā asuraprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The blаск-complexioned Asuras have to be adorned with garlands of black flowers. The relevant mantra is—“Akrsnetf’ which was composed by Hiranyavarna in Jagati meter having Savita as the god. The Viniyoga should be performed to please the Asuras.

## \|\| 2.31.103 \|\|

*asuraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ nāgahārānvitaṃ padmāsanasthaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*ābrahmanniti maṃtrasya nalina ṛṣistriṣṭupchando bhavānī devatā somaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. The black complexioned Asura adorned with the garland of black cobras and seated over the seat of lotus flower should be meditated upon with the mantra-“Abrahmanniti,” which was composed by Nalina in Tristupa meter and whose god is Bhav3nl. The Viniyoga should be offered to please the god Soma.

## \|\| 2.31.104 \|\|

*rogaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ nīlendīvaradharaṃ śvetavṛṣabhārūḍhaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*namaste rudra iti mantrasya nārada ṛṣiḥ paṃktiśchandaḥ śrīrdevatā rogaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The Roga, which is of black complexion, wearing a blue lotus, is seated over the white bull. His mantra is - "Namaste Rudra iti" which was composed by Devarsi Narada in Pankti meter. The Viniyoga should be offered in favour of the god Roga.

## \|\| 2.31.105 \|\|

*vāyukoṇādārabhya pūjayet \|*  
*vāyuṃ dhūmravarṇaṃ dhvajahastaṃ mṛgārūḍhaṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*devā iti mantrasya bṛhatī chando yamo devatā nāgaprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The process of adoration should be started from the north-west. Vayudeva has the complexion of smoke. He uses a deer as a vehicle. He should be meditated upon with “Deva-iti' mantra composed in Brhati meter. Its god is Yama and the Viniyoga should be offered to please the Naga.

## \|\| 2.31.106 \|\|

*śvetaṃ somaṃ śvetavarṇāsanasthaṃ dhyātvā bhadrabījena pūjayet \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Somadeva is of white complexion who is seated over a white seat and should be worshipped with Bhadrabija.

## \|\| 2.31.107 \|\|

*raktaṃ bhallāṭaṃ pītavāsasaṃ dhyātvā vahnibījena pūjayet \|*  
*pītavāsasamajavāhanaṃ hārakeyūrānvitaṃ vāyubījena maṃdarādyaiḥ pūjayet \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Then one should meditate upon the god Bhallata with Vahni seeds. He is clad in yellow garments and has goat as his vehicle. He is adorned with garlands and bracelets. He should be worshipped with Vayu-bija.

## \|\| 2.31.108 \|\|

*raktāṃ ditiṃ nāgahārānvitāṃ raktapadmāsanasthāṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*mānārthaṃ iti mantrasyeti pūjayet \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. We should meditate upon the goddess Diti who is red-complexioned, adorned with serpent garland and seated over a seat of red lotus using the mantra- ”Manarya iti”.

## \|\| 2.31.109 \|\|

*māno tvā iti maṃtrasya bhārgava ṛṣiḥ paṃktiśchandaḥ pṛthivī devatā ditiprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Her mantra is— “Mano-iti’, said to have been composed by Rsi Bhargava in Pankti meter, with Prthvi Devata. The Viniyoga should be offered to please the goddess Diti.

## \|\| 2.31.110 \|\|

*aditiṃ pītavarṇāṃ siṃhārūḍhāṃ pītāṃbaradharāṃ dhyātvā \|*  
*hiraṇyavarṇa iti maṃtrasya janārdana ṛṣirbṛhatī chandaḥ somo devatā aditiprītaye viniyogaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The goddess Aditi is of yellow complexion, uses the lion as her vehicle. She is clad in pitambara and should be meditated upon with the mantra - “Hiranya varna” composed by Janardana Rsi in Brhati meter with Soma Devata. The Viniyoga should be performed for the pleasure of Aditi.

## \|\| 2.31.111-112 \|\|

*evaṃ yathā vidhāyātha homaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi \|*  
*homāṃte dakṣiṇāṃ dadyātkāñcanaṃ hemasaṃyutam \|\| 111 \|\|*

*taḍāgayāgapakṣe tu suvarṇaṃ cārdhameva vā \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. Thus with the invoking of all the gods and after worshipping them, the homa should be performed in an appropriate manner, after which the Brahmanas should be given the daksina in gold coins. Besides gold or half part of it should be consigned in the lake.

## Chapter 32. The process of Puja (worship)

## \|\| 2.32.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha pūjākramaṃ vakṣye purāṇasmṛticoditam \|*  
*uttare paścime vātha pūrve cāpi samācaret \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said - Hereafter, I shall apeak on the basis of the Puranas ax well ax the Smrtis, the process of performing the puja or worship. You please listen. Its gradual start should be from north, west or alternatively towards the sun.

## \|\| 2.32.2 \|\|

*nadītīre nemiprāṃte daśadvādaśasaṃkhyayā \|*  
*maṃḍalaṃ racayedviprāścarukadvayasaṃyutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Brahmanas, one should perform puja over the bank of a river, close to a well, making twelve or ten mandalas, in which two spots should be there for the making of earn or havi.

## \|\| 2.32.3 \|\|

*tribhāgaṃ vibhajetkṣetraṃ madhyabhāgadvayena tu \|*  
*trihastavedikāṃ kuryāttālotsedhāmudakplavām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. First of all, the area should be divided in three parts. In the middle two parts, there should be two parts of three cubits each. Then two pedestals of the size of three cubits each should be made with the height of the length between the thumb and the middle finger. There should be slope towards the north for the flow of water.

## \|\| 2.32.4 \|\|

*uttarāśe dakṣiṇe cāratnihastāṃtare'pi ca \|*  
*trimekhalāṃ hastamātrāṃ guṇavedīsamanvitām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Similarly, some space of the length of an arm should be towards the south and the north, besides the three chains with Veda and a cubit’s length. These chains should also be made.

## \|\| 2.32.5 \|\|

*mūle sārdhaṃ ca śuklāṃ ca mekhalāṃ tu tathaiva ca \|*  
*caturaṃgulikāṃ vediṃ madhyonnatāṃ prakalpayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At half of the base, there should be a chain of foe length of a cubit and a half of the same type and the pedestal should be of the height of four angulas, the middle portion of which should be raised.

## \|\| 2.32.6 \|\|

*ṣaṭsaptāṃgulikāṃ yoniṃ paścime mekhalopari \|*  
*vinyasennābhisaṃyuktamevaṃ kuṇḍaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A yoni of six or seven angulas should be made over the chain of the western side, an altar with navel should also be made.

## \|\| 2.32.7 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ vṛddhyātmakaṃ kuryātsaṃkalpaṃ mānasaṃ caret \|*  
*śrāddhārthaṃ naiva saṃkalpettathā vai devadarśane \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The performing of the Vyddhi-sraddha as well as the mental sankalpa is also essentially required to be performed For the purpose of sraddha and for having an audience with a Devata, no sankalpa is required to be performed.

## \|\| 2.32.8 \|\|

*gayāśrāddhārthakaṃ cāṣṭatīrthaśrāddhārthameva ca \|*  
*aiśānyāṃ kalaśe devaṃ pūjayedgaṇanāyakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. For the sake of the Gaya-sraddha and Astatirtha-sraddha the kalasa should be placed in the north-east, where Ganes'a should be invoked and worshipped

## \|\| 2.32.9 \|\|

*madhye kuṇḍe mahāṃścaiva viṣṇudevaṃ digīśvarān \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ cāgnikuṇḍe tu svaiḥ svairmantraiḥ prapūjayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the middle of the fire altar, the Dikpalas, Visnu and Brahma are required to be adored.

## \|\| 2.32.10 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmaṃ vidhāyātha bhūtaśuddhiṃ samācaret \|*  
*dhyāyedvāṭavīśapuruṣaṃ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After performing pranayama and Bhutasuddhi, the everlasting eternal Purusa should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.32.11-12 \|\|

*śvetaṃ caturbhujaṃ śāṃtaṃ kuṇḍalādyairalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*pustakaṃ cākṣamālāṃ ca varābhayakaraṃ param \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pitṛvaiśvānaropetaṃ kuṭilabhrūpaśobhitam \|*  
*karālavadanaṃ caiva ājānukaralaṃbitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. He happens to be of white complexion, having four arms, with a peaceful look, decorated with earrings and other ornaments holding a manuscript as well as a rosary, displaying Abhaya-mudra. He is served by pitr Vaisvanara. He has curved eyebrows, a terrific body and long arms falling upto the knees.

## \|\| 2.32.13-18 \|\|

*mūrdhanyagniṃ samāviśya mukhe vāyuḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*pṛthvīdharoryamā caiva tathāṣṭavaneṣṭitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vakṣasthale 'parāṃ saṃdhyāṃ yajeccaiva yathāvidhi \|*  
*netrayorditiparjanyau śrotre ditījyaputrakau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarpendrāvāsanasthau ca vāme dakṣaṃ vibhāvayet \|*  
*satyasomāgnayastatra rāhoḥ paṃca ca paṃca ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*rudraśca rājayakṣmā ca vāmahaste vyavasthitau \|*  
*pārśve tu dakṣiṇe tadvadvirathaśca maharkṣakaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ubhau jñeyau tathā jānvorubhau gandharvapuṣpakau \|*  
*jaṃghayorbhṛṃgasugrīvau sphicordauvāriko gaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jayaśakrau tathā meḍhre padayoḥ pitarastathā \|*  
*evaṃ dhyātvā nyasetpuṣpaṃ some naivaṃ viciṃtayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

13-18. The fire emerged out of his head, the wind in his mouth, besides Prthvidhara, Aryama, Astavana, Astita. At the chest, there is the provision of another Sandhya who should be adored accordingly. Diti should be lodged in his eyes, besides Parjanya. In the ear, Diti and Yajna-putra should be lodged, besides Aryama. Towards the south-west, Viratha and Maharaksaka should be lodged at both the knees. Besides Gandharvas and, Puspaka should also be lodged there. Bhrnga and Sugriva should be lodged at the thighs. The ganas of Dauvarika should be lodged at the anus. Sakra and Jaya have to be lodged in phallus and the pitrs at the feet. Thus getting devoted to the deity, the flowers should be offered to him. Nothing is required to be thought about Soma.

## \|\| 2.32.19-22 \|\|

*mandaraṃ dīrghayuktena ṣaḍaṅgāni samācaret\|*  
*tāvadvīryaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā praṇavaṃ brahmaṇeti ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vāstvīśāya vidmaheti tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt \|*  
*anena snapanaṃ kuryātpūjādravyāṇi prokṣayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*āsanaṃ pūjayetpūrvaṃ dharmeṇāpi svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*ādau tu bhāskaraṃ sūryaṃ śacīnāthaṃ gaṇādhipam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ādhāraśaktiṃ pṛthivīṃ pūjayettatra paṅkajam \|*  
*baṃdīśāsanamityuktaṃ pūjayedāsanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. The huge Mandara mountain and the six limbs should be made; reciting the Pranava mantra, the semen should be established. Then reciting the mantra - “Vastavisaya vidmaheti tanno Visnuh pracodayat,” the abhiseka should be performed and the puja material should then be offered. According to one’s own means, with a five religious belief, the seat should be worshipped first. Thereafter, the gods Surya. Indra, Ganadhipa and earth goddess who is the base, besides the lotus should be adored. This is called the Vedi-Sasana. The seat should be worshipped thereafter.

## \|\| 2.32.23 \|\|

*sitacandanayuktena śvetapuṣpaṃ pragṛhya ca \|*  
*harerdhyānaṃ tataḥ kuryātsthāpayenmadhyamaṇḍale \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Concentrating one’s mind over Hari, holding the white flowers with the white sandal paste, they should he placed in the middle of the mandala.

## \|\| 2.32.24-25 \|\|

*āvāhya cāsanaṃ dadyāttataḥ pādyādikatrayam \|*  
*madhuparkaṃ tato dadyādvāstoṣpatimatheśvaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

*asya mantrasya ca ṛṣiśchando gāyatramīritam \|*  
*devatā ca bhavedbrahmā yojayedaśvamedhakam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. After invoking the gods, the seats should be offered to them, besides the padya (water for the washing of hands and feet). Thereafter, the honey should be offered to Isvara (God). The mantra- “Vastospati” should be recited, which was composed by Gayatra Rsi in Gayatri meter, Its god is Brahma. The same process has to be followed in the Asvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.32.26 \|\|

*maṃdaraṃ vijayaṃ somaṃ mahādevaṃ ca mādhavam \|*  
*rudraṃ haraṃ jayaṃ bhaṃ ca pūrvādidalamūlake \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The basic gods of the group are Mandara, Vijaya, Soma, Mahadeva, Madhava, Rudra, Hara and Purva.

## \|\| 2.32.27 \|\|

*jayā ca vijayā caiva satyā māyā śivāṃbikā \|*  
*hāsinī kāminī caitā dalamūleṣu bhāvayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The basic goddess of the same are Jaya, Vijaya, Satya, Maya, Siva, Ambika, Hasini and Kamini.

## \|\| 2.32.28 \|\|

*puṣpāñjalitrayaṃ dadyādvāstoṣpataya ityapi \|*  
*arghyamaṃtreṇa gaṃdhādyaiḥ pūjayedbhūtimicchatā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Vastospati Deva and the goddesses should be offered three hands full of flowers by a person desirous of getting wealth. Then uttering the arghya mantra, he should worship them all.

## \|\| 2.32.29 \|\|

*vāstoṣpate bhava mate iti dhyātvā ṛtaṃ ceti maṃtreṇa pūjayet \|*  
*ṛṣirnārāyaṇaśchando gāyatrī parikīrtitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Reciting the mantra- “Vastospate bhavamate iti' and the mantra- “Rtam ceti,” the paja should be performed.

## \|\| 2.32.30-32 \|\|

*sūryaśca devatā khyātaḥ prīṇitaḥ kuliśāyudhaḥ \|*  
*sūryaṃ raktāsanārūḍhaṃ dvibhujaṃ raktavāsasam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*raktapadmadvayadharaṃ kuṃḍalādyaiḥ suśobhitam\|*  
*evaṃ dhyātvā tu matimānhaṃsaṃ samaṃtramīśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*haṃsasya iti maṃtrasya ṛṣirautathya īritaḥ \|*  
*paṃktiśchandaḥ svayaṃ devo viniyogastu prītaye \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Then the god Surya should be adored, having a red seat, with two arms, clad in red garments, holding the red lotus flowers, adorned with earrings and the other ornaments. He should be adored reciting the hymn - “Hamsasya iti,” which was composed by Autathya Rsi, in Pankti meter having Hamsa as the Devata. The Viniyoga should be offered in order to please him.

## \|\| 2.32.33-34 \|\|

*nīlotpaladvayadharaṃ satyaṃ mṛtyūparisthitam\|*  
*svacchaśvetāṃbaradharaṃ varadaṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*svaṃ madātvamiti mantreṇa śvetacandanapuṣpakaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā vastrālaṃkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The god holding a couple of blue lotus flowers is the form of truth, seated over the death. He is clad in spotless dress, is bestower of the boons and is the favourite of the devotees. Such a god should be adored uttering the mantra- “Svarfi madatvamiti.” He should be offered the white sandal paste, flowers, costumes, ornaments and should be worshipped with great devotion.

## \|\| 2.32.35 \|\|

*uddharṣaṇa iti maṃtreṇa kṛṣṇapuṣpairathārcayet \|*  
*satyavrata ṛṣiścāsya triṣṭupchando'sya devatā \|*  
*savitā caiva vijñeyaḥ prītaye ca vṛṣasya ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then reciting the mantra - “Uddharsana” black flowers should be offered to him. Satyavrata is the Rsi for the mantra which has been composed in Tristupa meter. Its Devata is Savita and the Viniyoga should be offered to please the Vr$a.

## \|\| 2.32.36-37 \|\|

*śulkavarṇaṃ tathākāśamṛṣṭisaṃghaiśca saṃstutam \|*  
*ghaṭasthaṃ dvibhujaṃ dhyāyedgadāpadmavidhāriṇam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śanno devīti paṭhanādgandhapuṣpādibhiryajet \|*  
*ṛṣiḥ syātkardamo viprāśchando jāgatikā tathā \|*  
*devatā ca bhaveccāgnirākāśaprītaye nyaset \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The god holding a sword in his hand, who is the form of the sky, has white complexion, has two arms holding a club, has the mantra known as “Sannodevi” and should be worshipped offering the fragrant flowers. О Brahmanas, Kardama is the Rsi for this mantra which was composed on Jagati meter. The god is Agni and Akasa or sky and the Viniyoga should be offered to please the sky god.

## \|\| 2.32.38 \|\|

*dhvajahastamahābāhuṃ marudbhiścopasevitam\|*  
*dvibhujaṃ dhūmravarṇaṃ ca vāyuṃ dhyātvā prapūjayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Vayudeva holds a flag in his hand and is served by Marudganas. He is two-armed and has the smoke like complexion. The wind god should therefore be worshipped accordingly but carefully.

## \|\| 2.32.39-41 \|\|

*rājāna iti mantreṇa pūjayetsitataṃḍulaiḥ\|*  
*ṛṣirnārāyaṇacchando gāyatrī devatā dvijāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*devatā ca bhavedvāyuḥ prītaye tasya yojayet \|*  
*pūṣāraktaśca dvibhujo raktapadmāsanasthitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*rājāna iti ca ṛcā pūjayedgandhacandanaiḥ\|*  
*gobhilosya ṛṣiḥ paṅktiśchando'tha jagatī smṛtam \|*  
*devatā ca bhavedvāyuḥ prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. Reciting the hymn- “Rajanaiti,” he should be worshipped with white rice. О Brahmanas, Narayana is the Rsi for this mantra composed in Gayatri meter. The Viniyoga should be performed to please the wind god. The god Pusa is comfortably seated over the red lotus flower. He should be worshipped with the red lotus flowers with die mantra- “Rajana-iti offering the sandal paste. The mantra is attributed to Gobhila Rsi, Pankti is the meter for the same and the related god is Vayu. The Viniyoga should be offered to please him.

## \|\| 2.32.42 \|\|

*vitathaṃ śyāmavarṇaṃ ca caturbhirbāhubhirvṛtam\|*  
*mṛgākṣapāśakhaṭvāṅga śūlaṃ ca dadhataṃ karaiḥ \|*  
*meṣārūḍhaṃ viśālākṣaṃ rājāno mahyamīrayan \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The god who has the dark colour, four arms, Mrga-aksa-pada, holding rosary, pada, a trident and a khatvanga in his hands as arms. Her vehicle is a sheep. The god with vast eyes should be adored with the hymn- “Rajano mahyamirayanniti.

## \|\| 2.32.43 \|\|

*gṛhakṣataṃ tathā śuklaṃ caturbhirgardabhairvṛtam \|*  
*śūlaṃ daṃḍaṃ ca khaḍvāṃgaṃ dadhataṃ vṛṣavāhanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Grhaksata-deva is of white complexion and is surrounded by the donkeys from all the sides. He holds a trident, a staff and khatvanga. He is mounting a bull.

## \|\| 2.32.44 \|\|

*pītavastradharaṃ devaṃ jaṭāmukuṭasaṃyutam \|*  
*āśuḥ śiśāna iti mantreṇa pūjayedgandhacandanaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The god Grhaksata is clad in a yellow lower garment and his hymn is- “Asu-sisina iti" reciting which he should be worshipped offering the fragrant sandal paste.

## \|\| 2.32.45 \|\|

*puṣpadaṃta ṛṣistriṣṭupchandaśca parikīrtitam \|*  
*īśvarasya devatāyā prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Puspadanta is the Rsi for the mantra, Tristupa is the meter and the Viniyoga should be offered to him for the sake of his pleasure.

## \|\| 2.32.46-47 \|\|

*yamaṃ dhyāyetkṛṣṇavarṇaṃ mahiṣasthaṃ dvibāhukam \|*  
*daṇḍapāśadharaṃ caiva keyūrādyairvibhūṣitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*īśāneti ca mantreṇa pūjayetkusumādinā \|*  
*vāmadeva ṛṣiḥ paṃktiśchandaḥ kālosya devatā \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Yamadeva of black complexion is mounted over a he-bufflo, has two arms holding a danda and a pasa (noose). He should be meditated upon with the mantra-“Isaneti.” He is adorned with armlets and other ornaments. His mantra’s Rsi is Vamadeva, the meter is Jagati and the god is Kala-devata.

## \|\| 2.32.48-49 \|\|

*ṣaḍānanaṃ ca gandharvaṃ pītaṃ dhyāyeccaturbhujam \|*  
*pītāṃbaradharaṃ caiva nānābharaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yaddeva iti mantreṇa pūjayetkusumādinā \|*  
*hārītosya ṛṣiḥ prokto jagatīchanda īritam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbho devatāsya prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. There is a four-armed god with yellow complexion, who is clad in yellow lower garment and adorned with all the ornaments. His mantra is- “Yaddevaiti’ with which he should be worshipped together with offering of the flowers. His mantra is related to Harita Rsi, Jagati meter, Hiranyagarbha Devata and the Viniyoga should be offered to please the same god.

## \|\| 2.32.50 \|\|

*bhṛṅgarājaṃ jaṭārūḍhaṃ svacchaṃ pītāṃbaraṃ śubham \|*  
*cakṣuḥ pīteti mantreṇa pūjayedgandhacaṃdanaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The god Bhrngarnja has the matted locks of hair over the head and is clad in yellow lower garment. His mantra is - “Caksuh piteti" and he should Ire worshipped reciting die same mantra offering sandal paste.

## \|\| 2.32.51 \|\|

*ṛṣiścāgastirākhyātastriṣṭupchandaḥ prakīrtitam \|*  
*viśvedevā devatā ca bhṛṅgarājasya prītaye \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Rsi of this mantra is Agasti; the meter is Tristupa; the god is Visvedeva and the Viniyoga should be offered to please Bhringaraja.

## \|\| 2.32.52 \|\|

*pītaṃ mṛgaṃ mṛgārūḍhaṃ jaṭāmukuṭamaṃḍitam \|*  
*paro devā iti maṃtreṇa pūjayedbalipāyasaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The god Mrgadeva wears a crown of the matted locks of hair. He is of yellow complexion. He should be worshipped with die mantra- “Parodeva-iti," and worshipped offering payasam.

## \|\| 2.32.53 \|\|

*kapilaśca ṛṣiḥ prokto gāyatrī chanda īritam \|*  
*varuṇo devatā cāsya prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The mantra is related to Kapila Rsi; Gayatri meter and has Varuni as the god to please whom die Viniyoga should be offered.

## \|\| 2.32.54 \|\|

*dhyāyetpitṛgaṇaṃ śukraṃ caturbhirbāhubhirvṛtam \|*  
*pitṛbhya iti mantreṇa pūjayetkusumādinā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Pitrganas are of white complexion, has four arms. They should be worshipped with the mantra- “Pitrbhya-iti’, offering flowers at the same time.

## \|\| 2.32.55-57 \|\|

*śunaḥśepa ṛṣiścāsya triṣṭupchandaśca devatā \|*  
*viśvedevāḥ samākhyātāḥ pitṛmedhena pūjayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dauvārikaṃ cāṣṭabhujaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ vicintayet \|*  
*raktavastrapiṃgalākṣaṃ kṛṣṇavyāghropari sthitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*yo naḥ piteti mantreṇa pūjayedbhaktitatparaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Sesa is the Rsi for this mantra; Tristupa is the meter; the god is Visvadeva, who should be worshipped with Pitrmedha. Dauvarika Deva on the other hand has eight arms, black complexion, is clad in red garments and has yellow eyes. He is mounted over the black tiger. His mantra is- “Yo nah pibateti’ and he should be worshipped with devotion.

## \|\| 2.32.58 \|\|

*vaiśvānara ṛṣiścāsya gāyatrī chanda īritam \|*  
*devatā ca bhavecchaktirviniyogaśca pūjane \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Vaisvanara is the Rai for this mantra; Gayatri is the meter; Sakti is the Devata and the Viniyoga should be offered to please the same god.

## \|\| 2.32.59-60 \|\|

*śaṃkhābhaṃ caiva sugrīvaṃ dvibhujaṃ cakradhāriṇam \|*  
*haṃsārūḍhaṃ mahākāyaṃ balivijñānakāraṇam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*śaṃkhapadmadharaṃ caiva mahiṣasthaṃ vicintayet\|*  
*sa iṣu hasteti maṃtreṇa pūjayedraktabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Sankhadeva has the complexion of a conch, having a beautiful neck, two arms, carries a Cakra and is mounted over the swan. He possesses a huge body, is the cause of the science of sacrifice, carries a conch and a lotus flowers, and mounted over a he-buffalo. £artkhadeva should be meditated with the mantra- “Sa isu hasteti.” He should be worshipped with red ornaments.

## \|\| 2.32.61-62 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ śaṃkhastathācchandaḥ paṅktiḥ somo'tha devatā \|*  
*śvetaṃ jalādhipaṃ dhyāyedgandharvādyaiśca veṣṭitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ṛṣyāsanagataṃ dhyāyecchvetagandhena carcayet \|*  
*bṛhaspate paridīyā iti maṃtreṇa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Sankha is the Rsi for this mantra, Pankti is the meter, while Soma is the god. He is of white complexion and is served by the Gandharvas. He occupies the seat of a Rsi, the god Varupa should be adored with devotion, reciting the mantra- “Brhaspate paridiya iti. While uttering the mantra, he should be adored with bright fragrance.

## \|\| 2.32.63-64 \|\|

*tryaṃbako'sya ṛṣistriṣṭupchando devo jalādhipaḥ \|*  
*dhyāyecca asuraṃ raktaṃ karālaṃ naravāhanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*daśabhirbāhubhiryuktaṃ kṛṣṇavastrānulepanam \|*  
*śanno devīti maṃtreṇa kṛṣṇapuṣpaiḥ prapūjayet \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Tiyambaka is the fyi of this mantra; Tristupa is the meter, Varuna is the god. He is of red complexion, having a gigantic body, a human as a vehicle, ten arms and clad in black costumes. The imperishable god should be meditated upon with black flowers.

## \|\| 2.32.65-66 \|\|

*ṛṣirvaiśvānaraśchando virāḍityabhidhīyate\|*  
*vaiśvānarottaro devaḥ prītaye tasya yojayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

*śeṣaṃ ṣaḍānanaṃ dhyāyetkṛṣṇaṃ ca madhupiṃgalam \|*  
*meṣasthaṃ kuṇḍalopetaṃ nāgayajñopavītinam \|*  
*udvarṣa iti mantreṇa pūjayedbhūtimicchatā \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Vaisvanara is the Rsi for his mantra and the Viniyoga should be offered to please him. Sesadeva has six faces, black and yellow odour like the honey, mounted over a sheep and adorned with the earrings. He wears a yajnopavita of the serpents. A person desirous of riches should worship the god with mantra-“Udvarsa-iti.”

## \|\| 2.32.67-71 \|\|

*pāpaṃ raktaṃ trinetraṃ ca raktaṃ prānte vicintayet \|*  
*raktaśmaśrudharaṃ caiva varahastaṃ vicintayet \|\| 67 \|\|*

*siddho vīreti mantreṇa kṛṣṇapuṣpairathārcayet\|*  
*yamaṃ ca kṛkarākṣaṃ ca ākuñcanmūrdhaje dvijāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kapilo'sya ṛṣiśchando'nuṣṭup caiva prakīrtitam \|*  
*devatā ca yaśaḥ khyātaṃ prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 69 \|\|*

*yamaṃ ca kṛkarākṣaṃ ca kṣamākuñcitamūrdhajam \|*  
*kharasthaṃ dvibhujaṃ dhyāyedimaṃ mantramudīrayet \|\| 70 \|\|*

*vāsukiḥ syādṛṣiścāsya paṃktiśchandaśca devatā \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbha ityuktaḥ prītaye'sya niyojayet \|\| 71 \|\|*

67-71. The Yasa god is of red complexion, has three red eyes, beard and moustaches. He displays Varada mudra. Yasa should be worshipped with the mantra - “Siddhi-virati". The flowers of black colour should be offered to him. Similarly, he has the eyes like those of the wind god and curly hair of Yama. The mantra is associated with the Kapila Rsi; Anustupa is the meter; Yasodevata to please whom the Viniyoga is offered. Reciting the mantra-“Krka-raksasam”, one should meditate upon him. Vasuki is the Rsi of his mantra; Pankti is the meter; Hiranyagarbha is the god to please whom the Viniyoga should be offered.

## \|\| 2.32.72-73 \|\|

*ardhapītaṃ ca dvibhujaṃ raktākṣaṃ dhūmrameva vā \|*  
*devatābhiśca saṃpannaṃ vāto vāretireva ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

*ṛṣirvāyuśca gāyatrī chando vāyuśca devatā \|\| 73 \|\|*
