72-73. He has two arms, red eyes, has the complexion of smoke and revered by the gods. The mantra is - “Vareti;" Vayu is the Rsi; Gayatri is the meter and Vayu is the Devata.

## \|\| 2.32.74-75 \|\|

*mugdharaktaṃ śaṃkhacakragadāpadmadharaṃ tathā \|*  
*pītavastraṃ pannagasthaṃ hārakeyūramaṃḍitam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*avasṛṣṭā parāpata iti mantreṇa pūjayet \|*  
*agniścāsya ṛṣiḥ proktacchandaḥ somaśca devatā \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. The god attracting the mind is of red complexion, holding in his four arms conch, cakra, gada and lotus. He is clad in yellow garments, and is lodged over a bed. He is adorned with armlets and other ornaments. He should be worshipped with the mantra-“Avasrista-parapata,” which is related to the Rsi Agni and Soma is the Devata.

## \|\| 2.32.76 \|\|

*pītaṃ bhallāṭakaṃ dhyāyetpadmasthaṃ raktabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ padmahastaṃ ca devamevaṃ vicintayet \|*  
*yanmāturiti mantreṇa pūjayetsitataṃḍulaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Bhallatakadeva is yellow-complexioned, seated over a lotus seat, adorned with red-coloured gems, two armed and should be worshipped with the mantra- “Yanmatur iti", offering the white rice to him.

## \|\| 2.32.77 \|\|

*jambhako'sya ṛṣiśchando gāyatrī samudāhṛtā \|*  
*devatā ca bhavetkumbhaḥ prītaye viniyogataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Jambhaka is the Rsi of the mantra; Gayatri is the meter; Kumbha is the god to please whom the Viniyoga should be offered.

## \|\| 2.32.78 \|\|

*somaṃ dhyāyecchyāmarūpaṃ padmāsanagataṃ param \|*  
*nānābharaṇasampannaṃ kirīṭavaradhāriṇam \|*  
*marmāṇiteti mantreṇa gandhādyairapi pūjayet \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Somadeva is of dark complexion, is seated over the lotus seat, is adorned with various types of ornaments and the Kirtta crown. The same Somadeva should be meditated upon rearing the mantra- “Marmani-teti” and then worshipped offering the flowers.

## \|\| 2.32.79-81 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ svārtho vedaśchando jagatītyabhidhīyate \|*  
*devatā ca bhavetsomaḥ prīyate viniyojayet \|\| 79 \|\|*

*darpaṃ dhyāyetkṛṣṇavarṇaṃ kṛṣṇāṃbaradharaṃ tathā \|*  
*nāgayajñopavītiṃ ca śikhistaṃbhaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*paścadīśeti mantreṇa gandhādyaiḥ paripūjayet \|\| 81 \|\|*

79-81. Veda is the Rsi for this mantra; Jagati is the meter, while Soma is the god to please whom, the Viniyoga should be offered. О best of the Brahmanas, then one should meditate upon Darpadeva, who is clad in black costumes, wears the yajnopavita of serpents and having a peacock as the vehicle. The mantra- “Pancadiseti" should be recited offering fragrant flowers and he should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.32.82 \|\|

*mantraścāsya ṛṣiścāsya pañcāyata namīritam \|*  
*paṃktiśchandastathā proktaṃ devaḥ pañcānanaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The mantra has Pancayatana as the Risi; Pankti is the meter; while Pancanana is the god.

## \|\| 2.32.83-84 \|\|

*śyāmavarṇāṃ ditiṃ dhyāyeddvibhujāṃ pītavigrahām \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannāṃ sarvālaṃkāraśobhitām \|\| 83 \|\|*

*suparṇo'sīti mantreṇa pūjayetpītacandanaiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. The goddess Diti is of dark complexion, having two arms and body with yellow complexion, possessing all the noble symptoms and adorned with all the ornaments. She is adored reciting the “Suparno 'siti" mantra and offering the yellow sandal paste.

## \|\| 2.32.85 \|\|

*ṛṣirnārāyaṇaśchando jagatī parikīrtyate \|*  
*bhaveddevo bhārgavaśca iṣṭārthe paripūjayet \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Narayana happens to be the Rsi of this mantra-, Jagati is the meter; Bhargava is the god to please whom the Viniyoga should be offered.

## \|\| 2.32.86 \|\|

*raktābhāmaditiṃ dhyāyetsarvālaṃkārabhūṣitām \|*  
*śukrāṃbhāritimantreṇa gandhādyairabhipūjayet \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The goddess Aditi also, who is of red complexion, adorned with all the ornaments, should be adored uttering the mantra-“Sukrambhariti’, offering the flowers etc.

## \|\| 2.32.87 \|\|

*vāmadeva ṛṣiścāsya gandhādyairabhipūjayet \|*  
*devaḥ śukraḥ samākhyātaḥ stutau ca viniyojayet \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The Rsi for this mantra is Vamadeva, who should be worshipped offering the fragrant materials. Even the god Sukra also attends on her worship.

## \|\| 2.32.88-89 \|\|

*īśānādikoṇagatānpūjayetsusamāhitaḥ \|*  
*āpaṃ dhyāyecchuklavarṇaṃ kuṇḍalādyairvibhūṣitam \|\| 88 \|\|*

*idaṃ viṣṇuriti mantreṇa trigandhena samarcayet \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. Thereafter, the gods of north-east comer should be worshipped. First of all, the watergod adorned with all the ornaments including the kundalas should be meditated upon reciting the mantra- “Idam-Visnuriti' with three types of fragrant (flowers).

## \|\| 2.32.90 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ syātkardamaśchando virāḍityabhidhīyate \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Kardama is the Rsi of this mantra; Virata is the meter; while Soma is the Devata.

## \|\| 2.32.91-92 \|\|

*devaḥ somaḥ samākhyātaḥ prītaye viniyojayet\|*  
*saritaṃ dvibhujaṃ raktaṃ raktaśvetāṃbarānvitam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*payasā śukla iti mantreṇa pūjayetkamalādinā \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. The Viniyoga has to be offered for the pleasure of the Soma. The two-armed goddess Santa has red complexion. She is clad in red as well as the white garments. Haricandana is applied over his body. She bestows the boon. The goddess has to be meditated upon with the mantra- “Payasa sukla iti’ and offering the lotus flowers, she should be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.32.93 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa ṛṣiścāsya paṃktiśchandaḥ prakīrtyate \|*  
*nārāyaṇaḥ svayaṃ devaḥ prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Narayana is the Rsi; Pankti is the meter; Narayana himself is the god and the Viniyoga should be offered to please him.

## \|\| 2.32.94-95 \|\|

*jayaṃ dhyāyetpītavarṇaṃ dvibhujaṃ varahastakam \|*  
*devaṃ kirīṭasampannaṃ sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā pariśruta iti mantreṇānena pūjayet \|*  
*ṛṣirnārāyaṇaśchandaḥ paṃktiḥ somo'tha devatā \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. The two-armed yellow-complexioned Jayadeva is adorned with the Kirita crown and adorned with all die ornaments. He should be meditated upon with the mantra- “Drstva parisruta iti’ and worshipped as well. Narayapa is the Rsi of this mantra; Раnkti is the meter; while Soma is the god.

## \|\| 2.32.96-97 \|\|

*rudraṃ dhyāyedraktavarṇaṃ śītāṃśukṛtaśekharam\|*  
*dvibhujaṃ śūlahastaṃ ca ḍamaruṃ ca parābhavet \|\| 96 \|\|*

*divo mūrdhanniti mantreṇa ṛṣayaḥ samudāhṛtāḥ\|*  
*ṛṣiḥ syātkāśyapaśchando virāḍityabhidhīyate \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. The two-armed Rudradeva who is of red complexion holding a damaru as well as a trident in his hands, should be adorned reciting the mantra - “Divomurdhanniti.” Каsуара is the Rsi; Virat is the meter; Svayam is the Devata. The Viniyoga thus offered is treated as his worship or prayer.

## \|\| 2.32.98-101 \|\|

*svayaṃ devo viniyogaḥ stutau ca viniyojayet \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ raktapadmasya paṃkajadvayadhāriṇam \|\| 98 \|\|*

*asya kirīṭa iti mantreṇa raktasrakcandanādibhiḥ \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā ṛṣirnīla udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*triṣṭupchando devatā syāddhradopi parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*savitāraṃ tathā dhyāyetpadmasthaṃ dvibhujaprabhum\|*  
*nānābharaṇaśobhāḍhyaṃ saptāśvarathamaṃḍitam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*yaddevā iti mantreṇa gandhādyaiḥ paripūjayet \|*  
*ṛṣirautathya ākhyātaḥ prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 101 \|\|*

98-101. Hradadeva has two arms each holding a red lotus flower and should be adored with the mantra- “Asya-kirita' with the mind having been filled with devotion. He should be offered the garland of red flowers as well as the sandal paste. Nila is the Rsi for his mantra, Tristupa is the meter. He is seated over a lotus with two arms. He wears several types of ornaments. He is mounted over a chariot driven by seven steeds. The god Savita should be meditated upon with the mantra-“Yaddeva-iti', also offering the sandal paste as well as the flowers. Autathya is the Rsi for this mantra and Viniyoga has to be offered to please him.

## \|\| 2.32.102 \|\|

*dhyāyedraktaṃ vivasvantaṃ dvibhujaṃ padmavigraham\|*  
*avidyā iti mantreṇa pūjayedgandhacandanaiḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The god Vivasvan with lotus like body, having two arms, should be worshipped with the mantra - “Avidya-iti”, with flagrant sandal pastes.

## \|\| 2.32.103 \|\|

*ṛṣirgandhaḥ samākhyātastriṣṭupchandaśca īritam \|*  
*devatā ca bhavetsomaḥ stutau ca viniyojayet \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Gandha is the Rsi for this mantra; its meter is Tristupa, while Soma is the god. The Viniyoga should be included in his prayer.

## \|\| 2.32.104-105 \|\|

*vibudhādhipaṃ tato dhyāyetpītaṃ vṛṣabhavāhanam \|*  
*caturbhujaṃ yaṣṭihastamakṣamālaikahastakam \|*  
*trinetraṃ raktavastraṃ ca mukuṭādyairalaṃkṛtam \|\| 104 \|\|*

*ṛṣirhārīta ityukto jagatīcchanda īritam \|*  
*devatā ca bhavecchaktiḥ prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 105 \|\|*

104-105. The god Vikramadhipati is four-armed, yellow-complexioned and is mounted over a bull. He holds stick in his hands, besides the rosary. He is three-eyed and is clad in red garments. He is adorned with a crown over the head as well as the ornaments over the body. He should be worshipped. His mantra was composed by Harita Rsi in Jagati meter, which has Sakti as the god. His Viniyoga should be offered to please him.

## \|\| 2.32.106-107 \|\|

*mitraṃ dhyāyecchuklavarṇaṃ varābhayakaraṃ param \|*  
*meṣasthaṃ ca trinetraṃ ca kirīṭavaramaṃḍitam \|\| 106 \|\|*

*dhanākarastviti mantreṇa pūjayeddadhipāyasaiḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

106-107. The three-eyed god Mitra has white complexion, displays Varada and Abhaya mudras in his two hands, he is three-eyed and his head is adorned with kirlta mukuta. He should be meditated upon with the mantra-“Dhandkarastivati.” He should be offered curd as well as payasam while performing his puja.

## \|\| 2.32.108 \|\|

*ṛṣirautathya ityukto jagatī chanda īritam \|*  
*devatā ca bhavedyakṣmā prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Authithya is the Rsi for this mantra composed in Jagati meter, while Yaksma is the god. His Viniyoga should be offered to please him.

## \|\| 2.32.109-110 \|\|

*pītāsyaṃ rājayakṣyāṇaṃ karālaṃ ca viciṃtayet\|*  
*yaśo rūpamiti mantreṇa gandhādyaiḥ paripūjayet \|\| 109 \|\|*

*dadhyaṅṅātharvaṇa ṛṣirgāyatrī chanda īritam \|*  
*yakṣmā ca devatā caiva stutau ca viniyoja yet \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. Не has the yellow face and terrific appearance. He should be adored with the mantra - “Yasorupamiti, adored with the sandalpaste. Dadhyanngarthvana Rsi is associated with this mantra; Gayatri is the meter and Yaksma is the god. This Viniyoga should be made use of while offering prayer to him.

## \|\| 2.32.111 \|\|

*śuklāṃbaradharaṃ dhyāyeddvibhujaṃ śikhivāhanam \|*  
*yamaṃ vineti maṃtreṇa pūjayedbhaktitatparaḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The god who is adorned with white clothes, has two hands and using the peacock as his vehicle, should be meditated upon. The mantra - ''Yamam vinete'' should be recited with devotion.

## \|\| 2.32.112 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ syānnāradaḥ proktaśchandonuṣṭupprakīrtitam \|*  
*vivasvāndevatā caiva kratau ca viniyojayet \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Narada is the Rsi related with this mantra which is composed in Tristupa meter, while Vivasvan is the god. The Viniyoga should be made use of in the yajna.

## \|\| 2.32.113 \|\|

*evaṃ dhyātvā vivasvaṃtaṃ mahākāyaṃ mahodaram \|*  
*abhinnarūpamaṃtreṇa gandhādyaiḥ paripūja yet \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Thus meditating upon the gigantic bodied Vivasavan, the mantra- “Abhinnarupa-iti’, should be recited, offering flowers to him.

## \|\| 2.32.114 \|\|

*kāśyaposya ṛṣiśchandastriṣṭubdevaḥ śacīpatiḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Kasyapa is the Rsi for the mantra which is composed in Tristupa meter, while Sacipati Indra happens to be its Devata.

## \|\| 2.32.115 \|\|

*bahirīśānakoṇeṣu devādīnparipūjayet \|*  
*kūṣmāṇḍairvaraṇāpuṣpaiḥ śaurakairvā samarcayet \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. The gods of the outer north-east comer should be worshipped with pumpkin or with Saurakas.

## \|\| 2.32.116-117 \|\|

*pītāṃ karālikāṃ dhyāyeccarakīṃ varavarṇinīm \|*  
*svabjasthāṃ dvibhujāṃ caiva guñjāhāropaśobhitām \|\| 116 \|\|*

*pītinyarūpamantreṇa pūjayedbhūtimicchukaḥ \|*  
*baladeva ṛṣiścāsya chando gaurī ca devatā \|\| 117 \|\|*

116-117.The two-armed goddess Caraki Devi is of yellow complexion, terrific faced and is seated over the lotus seat. She is decorated with the Gunja flowers. She should be meditated upon reciting the mantra- “Pitinya rupeti" for the sake of achieving riches. Baladeva is the Rsi for this mantra which has been composed in Gauri meter and the same Devata.

## \|\| 2.32.118-119 \|\|

*dhyāyedvidārikāṃ raktāṃ navayauvanasaṃyutām \|*  
*pavitreṇa punīhīti maṃtreṇānena pūjayet \|\| 118 \|\|*

*ṛṣirgargaḥ samākhyātastriṣṭupchandosya devatā \|*  
*rudro'pi ca samākhyātaḥ stutau ca viniyojayet \|\| 119 \|\|*

118-119. The youthful Vidarika should be similarly meditated upon, reciting the mantra-“Pavirena punihiti" which was composed by the sage Garga; Tristupa is the meter; while Rudra is the god. The Viniyoga should be offered in his praise.

## \|\| 2.32.120 \|\|

*pāpādirākṣasīṃ dhyāyetsaurabheyoparisthitām \|*  
*kayā na iti maṃtreṇa pūjayedgandhacandanaiḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. The Siva and the Raksasi should be adored reciting the mantra - “Kaya na iti”, offering the fragrant flowers, sandal paste etc. They are mounted over the bulls.

## \|\| 2.32.121 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ suvarṇa ākhyātaḥ paṅktiśchandaḥ prakīrtitam \|*  
*devatā ca mahādeva iṣṭārthe viniyojayet \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Suvarna is the Rsi of this mantra; Pankti is the meter; while Mahadeva happens to be the god and the Viniyoga should be offered in order to please him.

## \|\| 2.32.122-123 \|\|

*kuṇḍavedyā aṃtare ca sthāpavedvidhivadbudhaḥ \|*  
*parvatāgramṛdaṃ caiva gajadaṃtamṛdaṃ tathā \|\| 122 \|\|*

*valmīke saṃgame caiva rājadvāracatuṣpathāt \|*  
*kuśamūlamṛdaṃ caiva yajñiyasya vanaspateḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

122-123. A learned person should be in the centre of the pedestal in the fire altar, the earth from the mountain as well that dug from an anthill, royal gate, the crossing, the roots of kusa grass and the earth from the sacrificial tree should be collectively placed.

## \|\| 2.32.124-128 \|\|

*indravallī tathākrāṃta amṛtī trapuṣasya ca \|*  
*mālatī caṃpakaṃ caiva tathā urvārukasya ca \|\| 124 \|\|*

*pāribhadrasya patraiśca paritaḥ pariveṣṭanam \|*  
*pañcatuṃgasya parito mukhe kuryātphaṇānvitam \|\| 125 \|\|*

*śrīphalaṃ bījapūraṃ ca nālikeraṃ ca dāḍimam \|*  
*dhātrīṃ jaṃbuphalaṃ caiva anyayā doṣamādiśet \|\| 126 \|\|*

*pañcaraktaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca nikṣipedvaruṇaṃ yajet \|*  
*pañcopacārairvidhivadgandhapuṣpādibhiryajet \|\| 127 \|\|*

*udvartana iti mantreṇa varuṇaṃ ca punaryajet \|\| 128 \|\|*

124-128. The leaves of jasmine, campa (a kind of jasmine), cucumber and nima tree should be placed round the same. Then over all the faces of the same fruits like wood apple, myrobalan, coconut, pomegranate, myrobalan or the silk fruits, five hoods should be created, otherwise the performer shall attract the sin. Five articles of red colour besides the gold pieces should be placed in the pitcher. Thereafter, the god Varuna should be worshipped, offering the fragrant flowers. Then uttering the mantra - “Udvartana iti,” the god Varuna should again be worshipped, which is essential.

## \|\| 2.32.129 \|\|

*asya maṃtrasya ca ṛṣirviṣṇuśchanda udāhṛtam \|*  
*gāyatrī devatā pāśī prītaye viniyojayet \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. This mantra is attributed to Visnu, the meter of which is Gayatri, the god is Varuna and the Viniyoga should be offered for his pleasure alone.

## \|\| 2.32.130-134 \|\|

*pañcagaṃdhānvinikṣipya hastaṃ dattvā paṭhettataḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

*sarve samudrāḥ saritaḥ sarāṃsi ca mahāhradāḥ \|*  
*āyāṃtu sarvapāpaghnāḥ sarvalokasukhāvahāḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

*gaṃgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāstīrthāni jaladāḥ nadāḥ \|*  
*āyāṃtu yajamānasya duritakṣayakārakāḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

*aghorājyaṣṭakakṛtā vāstoṣpataya ityapi \|*  
*śataṃ vā cāṣṭasaṃyuktaṃ sahasraṃ vā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

*śatārdhaṃ vā hunedviprastilairvā taṃḍulaiḥ saha \|*  
*pālāśairvā pippalairvaudumbarairvā samācaret \|\| 134 \|\|*

130-134. All the five flavours should be poured in the pitcher and it should be touched by hand saying at the same time- “All the oceans, rivers, lakes and great tanks remove all the sins all the times, besides bestowing all the comforts to all die people, therefore all of them should be present here. The Ganga and all other rivers, all die holy places, besides the great rivers which give water to the smaller rivers, should arrive here in order to remove the miseries of the yajamana or the performer. The Vastospaganas should also arrive for the sake of lord Siva. When the fire is in flames, a hundred, a thousand or fifty offerings should be poured into the fire flames, comprising of unbroken rice, sesamum seeds, as well as the sacrificial stick of Palasa, holy fig tree and wild fig tree should be offered in the fire flames.

## \|\| 2.32.135-136 \|\|

*payodadhyādibhirvāpi madhvājyairvā viśiṣyate\|*  
*anyeṣāṃ ca vratenaiva ekaikāmatha vāhutim \|\| 135 \|\|*

*aṣṭāviṃśatibhiścānyairaṣṭāṣṭau paṃcapaṃca vā \|\| 136 \|\|*

135-136. In the stuff for homa, the milk, curd, honey and ghi should also be poured by the performer. (Besides the performer) other people (present there) should also drop one, eight, twenty eight or five offerings each in the fire,

## \|\| 2.32.137 \|\|

*carakyādīṃścāsanaiśca piṣṭakairvaṭakena vā \|*  
*raktapuṣpeṇa patreṇa trimadhvaktena yatnataḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. For the sake of Caraki and other goddesses, asana, the red flowers of the banyan tree, or with their leaves, the mixed honey, ghi and sugar should be poured in the homa.

## \|\| 2.32.138-139 \|\|

*vāstoṣpate dṛḍhaṃ japtvā yajedvāstupatiṃ yadā \|*  
*paṃcopacārairvidhivatsāṃgopāṃgairanaṃtaram \|\| 138 \|\|*

*balimāsādayetpaścāddadyādekaikaśaḥ kramāt\|*  
*brāhmaṇaiścaiva dadyācca sadā ājyaṃ samākṣikam \|\| 139 \|\|*

138-139. The name of Vastospati should be firmly recited. Then performing the japam, he should be worshipped in a proper manner. Thereafter, the offerings should be made to all the gods individually in the same way. Further, Brahmapas should be offered the honey as well as the ghi.

## \|\| 2.32.140-142 \|\|

*śālyannaṃ śikhine dadyāttathā nīlotpalāni ca \|*  
*odanaṃ sotpalaṃ dadyātparjanyāya vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

*jayāya piṣṭakaṃ kāryamindrāya ghṛtamodakaḥ \|*  
*sūryāya piṣṭakānnaṃ ca satyāya yavapūlikām \|\| 141 \|\|*

*bhramāya matsyamāṃsānnaṃ śaṣkulīmatha piṣṭakam \|*  
*vāyavye ca tathā saktūnpūṣṇe cāpūpameva hi \|\| 142 \|\|*

140-142. The payasam made of Sali rice, with blue lotus should be offered to the Fire-god. The boiled rice should be given for Parjanya, besides ground pulse. The sweet balls should be given for the sake of Indra; for Surya the food with ground pulse; for Satya the fried cakes of barley should be given. For Bhrama fish, meat and the food should be given, besides curd and ground pulses. For the sake of the gods lodged in the north-west comer, barley powder and for Surya the fried cakes should be given.

## \|\| 2.32.143-147 \|\|

*vitathāya kalāyānnaṃ gṛharkṣāya samākṣikam \|*  
*pūṣṇetha kṛśarānnaṃ ca śālyannaṃ ca nivedayet \|\| 143 \|\|*

*gandharvāya kastūrikānnaṃ kṛśaraṃ bhṛṃgarājake \|*  
*mṛgāya yāvakānnaṃ ca pitṛbhyo mudgapāyasam \|\| 144 \|\|*

*dauvārikāya kṛśarānanaḍuṃhe ca pūpakam \|*  
*pāyasaṃ puṣpadaṃtāya varuṇāya ca piṣṭakam \|\| 145 \|\|*

*asurāya modakāṃścaiva dadyādāpikṣaye surām\|*  
*ghṛtodanaṃ ca somāya kaṇānnaṃ yakṣmaṇe dadet \|\| 146 \|\|*

*rogāya ghṛtalaḍḍūkaṃ sapāyasaguḍaudanam \|*  
*akṣāya vividhānnaṃ ca bhallāṭāya tathaiva ca \|\| 147 \|\|*

143-147. The food should be given for Vitatha. For Grhaksa, food and honey should be given; for Pusa, khica or the rice cooked with sesamum seeds should be given or the payasam of Sail rice. For Gandharvas, the food mixed with musk; Bhmgar&ja should be given the rice cooked with sesamum; for Mrga, the pulp should be given; for Pitris, the sweet balls of green grams should be given; while khiccadi should be given for Dauvarika. For Krsaranana, the fried cakes should be given and payasam should be given for Puspadanta. For Varuna die ground pulse; modakas for the asuras; for Apiksaya, the wine should be given; and for the moon, the mixed rice has to be given. For Yaksma, the food grains should be given; for Roga, the sweet balls of ghi are to be given, besides payasam and sweet boiled rice. For Aksa and Bhallata, various types of food items should be placed.

## \|\| 2.32.148-149 \|\|

*somāya madhuśālyannaṃ nāgāya guḍapiṣṭakam \|*  
*adityai cāpi godhūmaṃ ghṛtapakvaṃ nivedayet \|\| 148 \|\|*

*dityai dadyāttathā kṣīraṃ sitaśarkarayā saha \|*  
*kṣīrānnaṃ caiva pūṣṇe ca āpavatsāya vai dadhi \|\| 149 \|\|*

148-149. For Soma, with honey the boiled Sali rice are prescribed; while for the Naga, sugarcane b alls as well as the ground pulse has to be given. For Aditi, the pudding of wheat flour is to be given. For Diti, milk mixed with sugar is to be given. For Pusa, milk and boiled rice are to be given and for Apavatsa, the curd is to be offered.

## \|\| 2.32.150-152 \|\|

*sāvitryai laḍḍukānnaṃ ca savitre ca guḍaudanam \|*  
*jayāya ghṛtamannaṃ ca miṣṭānnaṃ ca vivasvate \|\| 150 \|\|*

*virūpāya ca taddadyāddharidrānnaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ghṛtaudanaṃ ca citrāya rudrāya ghṛtapāyasam \|\| 151 \|\|*

*māṃsaudanaṃ yakṣmaṇe ca kṛśaraṃ varuṇāya ca \|*  
*aryamṇe śarkarāpūpaṃ bahirdadyāccatuṣṭayam \|\| 152 \|\|*

150-152. The sweet balls are to be given to Savitri; for Savita the sweet rice are to be offered. For Jaya boiled rice and ghi; sweets for Vivasavan, the boiled rice with turmeric for Virupa; ghi and boiled rice for Citra; payasam with ghi to Rudra; and for Yakima meat and boiled rice are to be given. Rice mixed with pulse have to be offered to Varupa; sugar and fried cakes for Aryama, besides four eatables should be offered to be outer space.

## \|\| 2.32.153 \|\|

*citraudanaṃ samāṃsaṃ ca matsyānnaṃ guḍapiṣṭakam \|*  
*pratidevopari kṣīraṃ ghṛtakṣīrasamanvitam \|*  
*tīrthatoyasamāyuktaṃ sugandhena samanvitam \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Several qualities of rice, meat, fish, sugarcane balls, ground pulses, besides ghi and milk mixed with the sacred water of the holy places should be offered to each one of the gods.

## \|\| 2.32.154-155 \|\|

*patākā devavarṇena dadyādbrahmādiṣu kramāt \|*  
*maṃtraṃ japetsvasāmarthyātsvasāmarthyātstutiṃ paṭhet \|\| 154 \|\|*

*puruṣastavasya sūrya ṛṣirjagatī chandaḥ \|*  
*savitā devatā somapāke stutau viniyogaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

154-155. For Brahma and other gods, the flags as per one’s means, offering prayer, recitation and Japam for each one of the gods should be performed. Purusastava mantra has the Surya as the Rsi; is composed in Jagati meter; has Savita as the god, who should be adored while offering Viniyoga to him.

## \|\| 2.32.156-161 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇurjiṣṇurvibhuryajño yajñiyo yajñapālakaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇo naro haṃso viṣvakseno hutāśanaḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

*yajñeśaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sūryaḥ surārcitaḥ \|*  
*ādidevo jagatkartā maṇḍaleśo mahīdharaḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

*padmanābho hṛṣīkeśo dātā dāmodaro hariḥ \|*  
*trivikramastrilokeśo brahmaṇaḥ prītivarddhanaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

*bhaktapriyo'cyutaḥ satyaḥ satyavākyo dhruvaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*saṃnyāsī śāstratattvajñastripaṃcāśadguṇātmakaḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

*vidārī vinayaḥ śāṃtastapasvī vaidyutaprabhaḥ \|*  
*yajñastvaṃ hi vaṣaṭkārastvamoṃkārastvamagnayaḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

*tvaṃ svadhā tvaṃ hi svāhā tvaṃ sudhā ca puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*namo devādidevāya viṣṇave śāsvatāya ca \|*  
*anaṃtāyāprameyāya namaste garuḍadhvaja \|\| 161 \|\|*

156-161. Lord Sankara said - Visnu, Vibhu, Yajniya, Nara, Narayana, Visvakasena, Hutasana, Yajnesa, Pundarikaksa, Krsna, Surya and those adored by the gods, Jagatkarta (creator of the world), Mandalesa (lord of mandala), Mahidhara, Hrsikesa, Data, Damodara, Hari, Trivikrama, Trilokesa, the one who increases devotion towards Brahma, favourite of the devotees, Acyuta, Satya, Satyavakya, Dhruva, Suci, Sanyasi (ascetic) well-versed in the scriptures, possessing fifty three qualities, Vidari, Vinaya (humility), Santa, Tapasvi (performer of tapas), as well as the form of lightening are you alone. Besides these, you are also the Yajna, Vasatkara, Omkara, Agni, Svadha and Purusottama. You represent all. You are the lord of the gods, besides being Visnu, Sasvata (eternal), Ananta (beyond measure), Aprameya (beyond limit), salutation to you. О Garuda-bannered lord, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.32.162-163 \|\|

*brahmastavamimaṃ proktaṃ mahādevena bhāṣitam \|*  
*prayatnādyaḥ paṭhennityamamṛtatvaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 162 \|\|*

*dhyāyaṃti ye nityamanaṃtamacyutaṃ hṛtpadmamadhye svayamāvyavasthitam \|*  
*upāsakānāṃ prabhumekamīśvaraṃ te yāṃti siddhiṃ paramāṃ tu vaiṣṇavīm \|\| 163 \|\|*

162-163. The eulogy which was composed by lord Siva, those who recite it daily making all the efforts, they certainly achieve moksa. Those who daily meditate upon lord Acyuta, they achieve the siddhi of lord Purusottama.

## Chapter 33. The offering of Arghya

## \|\| 2.33.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tato bheryādighoṣeṇa yajamāna udaṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*kanakatoyena gandhena mudgalāgreṇa lepayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said - Thereafter, facing north, the yajamana or the performer should generate the large sound of the beating of the big drums with the forepart of dumb bell and the fragrance mixed with sandal paste should be plastered.

## \|\| 2.33.2 \|\|

*aiśānyāṃ madhyabhāge vā yajedvā susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*vartulākārayedyasmānmana icchati saṃjapan \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the middle of the north-east comer, a circular image should be consecrated. Thereafter, its mantra should be recited.

## \|\| 2.33.3 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ kaṃṭhotha gāyatrī chanda ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*devatā pṛthivī caiva stutau ca viniyojayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The mantra was composed by Rsi Kantha; the god is Prthivi; Gayatri is the meter and prayer should be offered using the Viniyoga.

## \|\| 2.33.4 \|\|

*vivare pūjayetkarma brahmāṇaṃ ca dharādharam \|*  
*pṛthivīṃ gandhapuṣpādyairnaivedyairvividhairapi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The rites should be performed adoring Brahma, Sesa and the Earth goddess, offering various types of flowers and eatables.

## \|\| 2.33.5-12 \|\|

*agrato'ṣṭadalaṃ lekhyaṃ sthāpayetkalaśaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*mukhe vidhāya kanakaṃ rājatena vinirmitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śuktiśaṃkhasamaṃ vāpi viśvāmitrasamudbhavam \|*  
*pūjayettīrthatoyena gandhapuṣpākṣatādinā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*viṣṇukrāṃtā vacākuṣṭhacandanena viloḍitam \|*  
*kṣīraṃ ca mātuliṃgaṃ ca sāvitraṃ ca sadūrvayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dadhyakṣataṃ madhuyutamevamarghyaṃ ca sādhayet \|*  
*sitacandanavastrādyaiḥ śālyaiśca vividhairapi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*avraṇaṃ kalaśaṃ kṛtvā pañcavarṇasamanvitam \|*  
*āvāhayettoyanidhiṃ maṃtreṇānena bhaktitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*āyāhi bhagavandeva toyamūrte jaleśvara \|*  
*hṛdvarṇārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ paritoṣāya te namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gṛhebhyaścaiva somāya tvaṣṭre caiva ca śūline \|*  
*imaṃ me varuṇetyādi pratyekaṃ syādgatitrayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tatorghyadānaṃ vidhivatkṣīreṇa haviṣā madhu \|*  
*yajamānaḥ sapatnīkaḥ kuṃbhaṃ kukṣau nidhāya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

5-12. The eight petalled lotus should be made in the front, over which a silver vase should be placed in which the gold pieces, small shells, conch or anything that emerged from the ocean of Visvimitra are there. The vase should then be consecrated at that place. It should be worshipped with water of the sacred places, fragrance and the flower. After completing its puja and after collecting a creeper (Aparajita), Vaca (or an aromatic root), sandal paste, payasam, myrobalan, Savitra, Durva-grass, curd, unbroken rice and honey, the arghya should be performed. Then puja should be performed with a costume, sandal paste and different types of food items. Thereafter, the vase or a pitcher which should be without a hole, should be painted in five colours. Then, the ocean should be invoked in the pitcher with water, uttering the following speech- “O lord, О god, the form of water, О lord of water, I have offered arghya of the pleasant and attractive stuff. Salutation to you." Similarly, he should worship the gods like Grhesvara, Soma, Tvasta, Siva, offering salutation to them and uttering the mantra-“Imam-me-Varuneti.” After completion of the puja, the yajamana with his wife should pour ghi and honey in the kalasa (pitcher). Then carrying it in his lap, he should offer arghya.

## \|\| 2.33.13-14 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbheti maṃtrasya bharadvājaṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*chandaśca jagatī khyātaṃ devatā ca jalādhipaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*varuṇasyottaṃbhaneti maṃtrasya jalakuṃbhaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*asya maṃtrasya ca ṛṣirnāradaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*virāṭchandaśca īśāno devatā samudāhṛtā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Reciting the mantra- “Hiranyagarbheti composed by Bharadvaja Rsi in Jagati meter and having Varuna as the god, the arghva should be offered. Then uttering the mantra - “ Varunasyottambhaneti", the water should be sprinkled from the kalasa. This mantra has Narada as the Rsi, Virat is the meter and Isvara is the god.

## \|\| 2.33.15-16 \|\|

*mocayenmīnayugmaṃ ca meṣayugmaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*saṃbhave pakṣiyugmaṃ ca āḍīṃ vā cakravākakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*mocayennāgayugmaṃ ca āyuvṛddheśca hetave \|*  
*dikṣu jīvaṃtikāṃ dadyādrākṣasebhyo baliṃ haret \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Again for the enhancing of one’s life, if possible, two fishes, two sheep or two birds should be freed. In the directions, for the sake of the demons, Jivantika (parasites plant) should be offered.

## \|\| 2.33.17-18 \|\|

*nirmitaṃ māṣabhaktena raktapuṣpairalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*kṣātrako lakṣmaṇaścaiva maṇibhadro gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*sabiṃdukena haṃtena dikṣu madhye yathā kramāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ye bhavā bhāvino bhūtā ye ca teṣu mayāsinaḥ \|*  
*āharaṃ tu baliṃ tuṣṭyā prayacchaṃtu śubhaṃ mama \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Then the black gram should be mixed with red flowers and presented to Ksatraka, Laksmana, Manibhadra and Gapesvara and other gods who are lodged in other directions as Bindukas or zero. For the creatures of the past, present and future times, one should say that- “I am making the offerings, accepting which welfare may be bestowed on me.”

## \|\| 2.33.19-22 \|\|

*ityuktvā ca baliṃ dadyānnamaskuryādanaṃtaram \|*  
*dadyātpayasvinīṃ gāṃ ca ācāryāya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*anyeṣāṃ hi hiraṇyaṃ ca gāṃ ca dadyāddvijanmane \|*  
*vyāhṛtidvitayaṃ caiva tato vāruṇapaṃcakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prājāpatyaṃ sviṣṭakṛcca juhuyāttadanaṃtaram \|*  
*ghṛtaiḥ sviṣṭakṛtaṃ nāsti tathā rasavisārakaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*padmotpalairmātuliṃgaiḥ panasairmātuluṃgakaiḥ \|*  
*madhūkairviśvapuṣpaiśca tathāmrātakakāśakaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. Uttering thus and making the offering, the homos called Pancavaruni, Prajapatya and Svistakrita should be performed appropriately. In the Svistakrita homa, the offering of ghi, juice, Visaraka, blue lotus, nima, fruit, Bassia latifolia, Visvapuspa, Amrataka and Кasа have not to be poured in to the fire as offerings.

## \|\| 2.33.23 \|\|

*abhiṣekaṃ tataḥ kuryātsuvāstviti ca vai japan \|*  
*dadyātpūrṇāṃ ca vidhivatsūryāyārghyaṃ nivedayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thereafter, the crowning ceremony, the reciting of Svastiti, Purnahuti (the final offering) should be made for the Sun-god, besides the arghya.

## \|\| 2.33.24 \|\|

*pañcadoṣaṃ puraskṛtya brāhmaṇānumatena ca \|*  
*gṛhaṃ praviśya ca tato brāhmaṇānatha bhojayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. With the permission of the Brahmanas, together with the five blemishes, one should enter the house and serve food to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.33.25-26 \|\|

*dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇe caiva dadyādvittānusārataḥ \|*  
*jñātibhiḥ saha bhuñjīta dadhikṣīrāmiṣaṃ vinā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*na kṣīraṃ ca kaṣāyaṃ ca bharjitaṃ śākameva ca \|*  
*na kāṇḍaṃ ca na puṣpaṃ ca karīraṃ ca kadācana \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The charities should also be given to the poor, blind and shelterless people as per one’s means. Thereafter, one should take food with his kins and relatives. The curd, payasam meat, sour, fried things, flowers and tender bamboos should never be eaten.

## \|\| 2.33.27-29 \|\|

*śālyannaṃ mūlakaṃ caiva panasāmraphalāni ca \|*  
*mastaṃ madhughṛtaguḍaṃ mātuliṃgaṃ sasaiṃdhavam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*badaraṃ dhātakiphalaṃ kunda puṣpaṃ tathā tilam \|*  
*etatpraśastaṃ jānīyānmarīcāni viśeṣataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*trirātramatha saptāhaṃ parityajya khale tataḥ \|*  
*pañcāṃgakaṃ tataḥ kuryātsthāpa yenneti yugmakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. Sail rice, radish, jack fruit, mango fruit, intoxicants, honey, ghi, sugarcane balls, rock salt, nima, jujube, myrobalan, kunda flowers, sesamum, black pepper are the things, the use of which has been said to be praiseworthy. All these things should be put in a grinder and a paste should be made of the same. Keeping them for a week or three nights, thereafter the mixture of five things should be made and not two of them.

## \|\| 2.33.30-31 \|\|

*prathamā cārkahastena dvitīyā daśahastikā \|*  
*vitaste tu bhavecchataṃ dviguṇaṃ tadanaṃtaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śatārdhaṃ tataḥ paścātṣaṣṭihastamanaṃtaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The mixed stuff should be made of the length of twelve cubits, ten cubits, a hundred cubits or of the double this size. The length of the same could be extended to fifty or sixty cubits.

## Chapter 34. Processing of Homa

## \|\| 2.34.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*svagṛhyāgnividhiṃ vakṣye yogabhedeṣu sattamāḥ \|*  
*na paroktaṃ vidhānena bhayadaṃ kīrtidhvaṃsanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said - О Sattama vrnda, while describing the divisions of yoga, the processing of homa has been discussed, which is going to be revealed by me. By following the procedure laid down by others, one gets frightened and has to face loss of fame.

## \|\| 2.34.2 \|\|

*putrā eva ca kanyāśca janiṣyāścāpare sutāḥ \|*  
*gṛhyā iti samākhyātā yajamānasya dāyadāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Again the daughters and the sons who are to be born are considered to be the domestic stuff. They also happen to be the heir.

## \|\| 2.34.3-5 \|\|

*teṣāṃ saṃskārayāgeṣu śāntikarmakriyāsu ca \|*  
*ācāryavihitaḥ kalpastasmāccakṣa iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*trikuśaṃ parigṛhṇāti tataśca kurute dṛḍham \|*  
*ṛṣirdakṣaśca jagatī chando viṣṇuśca devatā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kaśyapastṛpyatāmiti bhūrasīti ca śodhanam \|*  
*ṛṣiḥ suvarṇa gāyatrī jagatī chanda iṣyate \|*  
*devatā ca bhavetsūryaḥ pṛthivīśodhane nyaset \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. In the related Samskara-yajnas and in the performing of peaceful rites, the kalpas established by the Acaryas arc known as Caksas (or false friends). Trikusa on the other hand has described it to make it strong. The mantra has Daksa as the Rsi; Jagati is the meter and Visnu is the god. Reciting the mantra- “Kasyapa strpyatamiti Bhurasiti", the earth should be purified. These mantras have Suvama as Rsi; Gayatri as the meter; the Sun as the god. The Viniyoga should be offered while purifying the earth.

## \|\| 2.34.6-8 \|\|

*aiśānyādikrameṇaiva prādakṣiṇyena yatnataḥ \|*  
*yatpavitreti maṃtreṇa tarjanyaṃguṣṭhayorapi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kuśagarbhatrayeṇāpi bhrāmayedvalayākṛti \|*  
*parisamūhanamityuktaṃ snapanaṃ śṛṇu sattama \|\| 7 \|\|*

*īśānādeśca saṃskāraṃ kuryātparisamūhanam \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāyāṃ caretyādinairṛtyādigrahaṃ makhe \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The gods of the north-east should be circumambulated and while so doing, the thumb and the forefinger should be joined, holding three straws of kusa grass. Making a round is called Parisamuha. О excellent one, I am now talking about the abhisekha. You please listen. At the time of consecration as well as the performing of the yajna, the rites of north-east, Parisamuha, Nairrti and other planets have to be worshipped essentially.

## \|\| 2.34.9 \|\|

*parisamūhanamaindrasya parvato'sya ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*paṃkticchandaḥ samuddiṣṭamindrāṇī cāsya devatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Rsi of Parisamuhana mantra is Parvata; Pankti is the meter, while Indrani is said to be the Devata.

## \|\| 2.34.10 \|\|

*gomayaṃ ca trigaṃdhaṃ ca paṃcamūrtikayāpi ca \|*  
*kaniṣṭhaṃ guhyakaṃ tyaktvā devatārthe na lepayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The plastering of cowdung with the three fragrances, besides the plastering of the secret spots with Pancamurtikas should not be done for the sake of a god.

## \|\| 2.34.11 \|\|

*mānastokeneti ṛcā viśvedevaśca pūjyatām \|*  
*ṛṣiḥ syātkāśyapacchando viśvadevaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Reciting the mantra- “Manastokeneti" the god Visvedeva should be worshipped. Rsi Кasуара is related to this mantra. Visvedeva is the meter as well as the Devata.

## \|\| 2.34.12-13 \|\|

*yojayellepayedvidvānghaṭamābaddhya sattamāḥ \|*  
*madhyamātarjanībhyāṃ ca kuśamārabhya dakṣiṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*caturastrīkṛte kṣetraṃ hastamānaṃ tathānanam \|*  
*yajvabhiriti mantreṇa sūryaḥ prīṇāti sattamāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. О excellent listeners, closing the house, holding the kusa grass with the middle and little fingers, the plastering should be started from the south. In the square area, an image of Surya in which his extended hand and the face are shown, should be worshipped reciting the mantra - “Yajvabhiriti”.

## \|\| 2.34.14 \|\|

*dakṣe sārdhāṃgulaṃ tyaktvā paścimena parityajet \|*  
*uttarāgrāṃ likhedrekhāmanyathā'maṃgalaṃ bhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the southern direction, leaving aside the place of the pedestal of an angula and a half, a line should be drawn towards front northern side. In case it is not so done, there would remain the possibility of the falling of some evil.

## \|\| 2.34.15 \|\|

*āpyāyasveti mantrasya dhanvatari ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*triṣṭupchandaḥ samākhyātaṃ savitā cātra devatā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The “Apyayasveti” hymn has Dhanvantari as the Rsi; Tristupa is the meter; while Savita is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.16 \|\|

*tallagnaṃ dakṣiṇe caikaṃ pūrvārddhadvādaśāṅgulam \|*  
*anyāṃgulāṃtaraṃ caikaṃ tataḥ saptāṃgulaṃ bhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Connected with the same, there is a projection to the southern part, (first half) the pedestal of twelve angulas or seven angulas is also made.

## \|\| 2.34.17-18 \|\|

*kuśamūlena svarṇena pratiṣṭhāyāṃ ca rājate \|*  
*aṃguṣṭhānāmikābhyāṃ ca saṃjyotīti ca saṃjapan \|\| 17 \|\|*

*saṃsmarenmitrā varuṇau ṛṣirautathyasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*paṃktiśchandaḥ śivo devo rekhāmatha ca yojayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. With the golden part of the base of kusa, a line has to be drawn and then joining the thumb and the little finger, reciting the mantra - "Sanjyoti", the earth around the line should be removed. Autathya and Mitravaruna are the Rsis for this mantra; Pankti is the meter; while Siva is the Devata. Al the time of drawing the line, the Viniyoga should be made use of.

## \|\| 2.34.19 \|\|

*tenaivorddhvakarau kuryāddakṣavāme sakṛtsakṛt \|*  
*bhāsvarāya kṣipedagnau tata ūrdhvaṃ raṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Similarly, in the left side of Daksa, the hands should he lifted up once, (the stuff holding the same) should be dropped in the fire known as Bhaskara, which is essential. A rana (lake) is made in the upper region.

## \|\| 2.34.20 \|\|

*sadasaṃpadṛṣiḥ karṇo virāḍiti udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*chanda indro devatā ca pṛthivyā devatā bhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Reciting the mantra - “Sadasampadrsih”, which has Kama virat as the Rsi; Indra as the meter; while Prthivi is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.21 \|\|

*kuśapuṣpodakenāpi devatīrthena sattamāḥ \|*  
*paṃcagavyena matimānpañcaratnodakena ca \|*  
*pañcapallavatoyena mahāyoge viśeṣataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О excellent listeners, the intelligent person should be made to take his bath with Pancagavya, water of the five gems and five leaves.

## \|\| 2.34.22 \|\|

*athonasya ca mantrasya variṣṭhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*chando'tha devī gāyatrī devatā gaṇanāyakaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Vasistha is the Rsi for the mantra-“Athonasya”; Gayatri is the meter; while Gananayaka is said to be the god.

## \|\| 2.34.23 \|\|

*kīśādagniṃ samādāya me gṛhṇāmīti saṃpaṭhan \|*  
*me gṛhṇāmīti maṃtrasya ṛṣirgautama īritaḥ \|*  
*chandonuṣṭupsamākhyātaṃ vāmadevo'tha devatā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thereafter, 'Kisadagni samadaya me grhnami' should be recited. Gautama is the Rsi for this mantra; the meter is Anustupa; while Vamadeva is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.24 \|\|

*kravyādagniṃ parityajya kravyādamagnimīrayan \|*  
*mantreṇānena matimāndakṣiṇasyāṃ vinikṣipet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Leaving aside the fire that burns the dead body, other fire should be accepted and reciting the mantra- “Kravyadagnim miryana”, should be placed towards the south.

## \|\| 2.34.25 \|\|

*asya mantrasya hārīta ṛṣiḥ syācchanda iṣyate \|*  
*devatā vāmadevo'pi dāhepi viniyojayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Harita is the for this mantra, besides being the meter, while Vamadeva is the god. This Viniyoga has been prescribed for the purpose of cremation.

## \|\| 2.34.26 \|\|

*āvāhanaṃ tataḥ kuryātsaṃsarakṣeti saṃjapan \|*  
*saṃsarakṣeti maṃtrasya ṛṣirnīla udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*virāṭ chando'tha vijñeyo devatā ca śatakratuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereafter, uttering the mantra-“Samsaraksetithe invoking should be made. Nila is the Rsi for this mantra; Virat happens to be the meter; while Satakratu is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.27 \|\|

*vaiśvānara iti ṛcā agnisthāpanamīritam \|*  
*maṃtramācāti prīṇāti ṛṣiḥ syātkāśyapaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*anuṣṭup ca bhavecchando devatā havyavāhanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then uttering the mantra- “Vaisvanara-iti ”, the fire is required to be consecrated. Kisyapa is the Rsi for this mantra, Anustapa is the meter and Havya-vahana is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.28 \|\|

*badhnāsīti ca maṃtreṇa agniṃ kuryātpradakṣiṇam \|*  
*ṛṣiḥ svayaṃbhūrākhyāto virāṭchanda udāhṛtam \|*  
*devatā paramātmā ca namaskāreṇa yojayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Uttering the mantra - “Badhnasiti,” one should go round the fire. Svayambhu is the Rsi for god. For the purpose of salutation, Viniyoga is required to be offered.

## \|\| 2.34.29-31 \|\|

*tatognidakṣiṇe bhāge prāgagrakuśakubjake \|*  
*dvihaste bhavataścaiva hastapānāsane atha \|\| 29 \|\|*

*brahmannihopaveśyatāmiti brahmāṇaṃ viniveśayet \|*  
*brahmayajñānṛcā dogdhrī dhenuriti tvṛcā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dvābhyāmiti ca mantrābhyāmiti brahmapraveśanam \|*  
*śakro'sya trāyatāmeti śṛṇu ṛgbhyāmṛṣīdvijāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Then towards the south of the fire, a kubjasana has to be made and a request has to be made to Brahma to be seated over it, reciting the mantra - “Brahmayajnanrca dogdhri dhenuriti tvrca. ” Then Brahma is required to arrive and enter there. Let Suka protect the same and the Rsis be protected with the Vedic Reds.

## \|\| 2.34.32 \|\|

*prajāpatirṛṣiśchandastriṣṭubdevo'tha śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*nāradaśca ṛṣiśchandastriṣṭubdevaḥ śacīpatiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Prajapati is the Rsi for this mantra; Tristupa is the meter; Sankara is the god; besides Narada is the Rsi; Tristupa is the meter; Indra is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.33 \|\|

*agneruttarabhāge ca hastamānāṃtarepi ca \|*  
*praṇītā sthāpanaṃ kuryāddina ehīti saṃjapan \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Reciting the mantra - “Ddina ehiti", a vase should be placed to the north of the fire and then it should be consecrated.

## \|\| 2.34.34 \|\|

*mantrasya ca ṛṣiśchando vāmadevaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*jagatī ca bhavecchando devatā ca śatakratuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Vamadeva is the Rsi for this mantra; Jagati is the meter; and Satakratu (Indra) is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.35-36 \|\|

*śrīparṇīsahakārotthaṃ varuṇasya viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍaṃgulena vistāraṃ viṃśatyaṃgulakena ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dairghyeṇa ca catuḥkhyātakāṃgulaṃ ca pramāṇataḥ \|*  
*dvyaṃgule carakākāyāmāsāsandevakarmaṇi \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. A vase made of mango or jack fruit, tree of the size of six angulas of Varapa, or of twenty angulas and four angulas in width should be made. A Caraki of two angulas in size is also made over it.

## \|\| 2.34.37-38 \|\|

*abhicāre bhavetkāṃsyaṃ tāmraṃ syācchāṃtikarmaṇi \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāyāṃ mṛnmayaṃ ca aṣṭāṃgulamathāpi vā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dvādaśāṃgulaprastāraṃ taijasaṃ mānavarjitam \|*  
*imaṃ me varuṇenarcā praṇītāmatha pūrayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. The vases for abhicara-karma should be made of bronze; for the performing of the rites for peace the vases should be of copper; for consecration the vases of burnt clay should be used, which should be of the size of eight angulas or of twelve angulas. The vases of gold can also be made for the sake of worship. Uttering the mantra- “Imam me Varunenarca" the vase should be filled with water.

## \|\| 2.34.39 \|\|

*sāgarā atha prīyaṃtāmitthamādhyānamācaret \|*  
*sakṛdacchinnadarbheṇa digvidikṣu paristaret \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then reciting the mantra - “Sagara atha priyantamiti, one should meditate upon. Then, cut kusa should be spread around the fire altar in all the directions.

## \|\| 2.34.40 \|\|

*nairṛte dikṣu sītaḥ syādvaiśvadeve tathaiva ca \|*  
*kayā naścitra ityṛcā nāgaḥ prīṇāti sattamāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О best of the ganas, for Vaisvadeva in the western direction, Sita has been prescribed, uttering the hymn - “Kayanascitra”, the Naga is pleased.

## \|\| 2.34.41 \|\|

*asya maṃtrasya ca ṛṣirbharadvāja udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*chando'nuṣṭubdevatā ca īśānaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Bharadvaja is the Risi for this mantra; Anustupa is the meter, while Isana is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.42 \|\|

*prayojanādikaṃ dravyaṃ tata āsādayetkramāt \|*  
*dakṣiṇādi uttarāṃtaṃ dhuvāsa ityṛcāpi ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The articles required should be collected. At that point of time, the mantra - “Daksinadi uttarantam dhruvasa iti' should be recited.

## \|\| 2.34.43 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ syānnāradaśchandonuṣṭupcaivātha devatā \|*  
*śatakratuśca prīṇāti yojayedatha sādarāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Narada is the Rsi for this mantra; Anustupa is the meter; while Satakratu is the god. At that point of time, the respectful use of this mantra is essential.

## \|\| 2.34.44-47 \|\|

*kāṣṭhaṃ ca paścime kuryātprayacchanpaścimena tu \|*  
*purato'nnaṃ pañcavrīhīstilāśca sahasarṣapān \|\| 44 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇe caiva āpūpaṃ bhṛṃgarājaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*phalapatre vāmabhāge piṣṭakaṃ dadhi dugdhakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*panasaṃ nārikelaṃ ca modakaṃ laḍḍukaṃ tathā \|*  
*praṇītāṃ ca digvidikṣu sthāpayedavicārayan \|\| 46 \|\|*

*praṇītāṃ na spṛśejjātu homakāle kathaṃcana \|*  
*snānakuṃbhaṃ ca bho viprā yāvadyāgaḥ pravartate \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. The wood should be placed to the west, the food in the front, besides cereals of five varieties and sesamum seeds with mustard seeds should be placed in the west. Towards the south, the fried cakes; Bhrngaraja fruits and leaves are to be placed on the left; the ground pulse, curd, milk, coconut and the sweet halls, besides the wooden water vase should be placed without much of thought. О Brahmana, while performing homa and upto the time of the performing of the yajna, the kalasas for worship or for taking of bath, should not be touched.

## \|\| 2.34.48-50 \|\|

*uccīrakaṃ mātuliṃgaṃ dūrvāṃ dhātrīphalāni ca \|*  
*tulasīmālatījātī jalajāni viśeṣataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*aiśānyāṃ sthāpayetsarvaṃ yacca vai kaṃkatīmayam \|*  
*nairṛtyeti viśeṣoyaṃ yacca vaikaṃkatī śamī \|\| 49 \|\|*

*yathāyogena tatsarvaṃ grāhyaṃ tatpatrameva ca \|*  
*kṣīrapāke tu kṣīrāṃte carusthālīmathānayet \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. The fruits like Ucciraka, myrobalan, Durva grass, a kind of jasmine and the lotus particularly, Asoka tree (fruits) should be placed in the north-east. In the routh-east direction, Kankati and Sami leaves should be placed besides payasam. In the method for preparing the ksira, for the preparation of earn, a pitcher like vase is required to be used.

## \|\| 2.34.51 \|\|

*pavivacchedanakuśaiśchiṃdyātprādeśikaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*chittvā pavitraṃ prokṣaṇyāṃ sthāpayedbalabhidāmrakam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. For the cutting of the kusa ring or pavitri, a cutter like the one of myrobalan should be used. The same pavitri (kusa ring) should be placed in wooden vase.

## \|\| 2.34.52-55 \|\|

*viṣṇo rarāṭamaṃtreṇa chedayedagrabhāgataḥ \|*  
*pāyasena kāṭhinena pramathnīyātkadācana \|\| 52 \|\|*

*na rasena na kārṣṇena na dṛḍhena kadācana \|*  
*tāmreṇa bhasmanā cātha śuktiśaṃkhena vāgyataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*chedayetpiñjulīṃ cāpi pavitramatha deśikaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇo rarāṭamaṃtrasya hārītaśca ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*paṃktiśchaṃdo bhaveddevaḥ saṃskāre viniyojayet \|*  
*praṇītābhājanaṃ gṛhya prokṣaṇīṃ pūrayettribhiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

52-55. Uttering the mantra- “Visno rarata”, it should be placed in the front. For the vase of ksira, the milk having been turned into curd should be churned. “Vispo rarata" hymn is linked with Harita Rsi; Pankti is its meter and Bhava is the god. Its Viniyoga is offered while performing the samskara rites. After collecting the kusa grass and the auspicious chedana, the wooden vase should be sprinkled with water, covering it with the kusa grass.

## \|\| 2.34.56-58 \|\|

*kāyatīrthena tatkuryāddevatīrthena cetyapi \|*  
*vāmahastatale paścātsthāpayetprokṣaṇīyakam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*madhyamāmadhyamāṃguṣṭha apāmārgeṇa maṃtribhiḥ \|*  
*uttānaṃ tatpavitraṃ ca pavitraṃ teti saṃjapan \|\| 57 \|\|*

*ṛṣiḥ syādgautamaśchando dharmarājo'tha devatā \|*  
*atha sthāpitadravyāṇi prokṣayetsthāpayetkramāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. Covering the vase with Kayatirtha or Devatirtha, the vase should be placed over the palm of the left hand. Two mantras viz.,-“madhyama-madhyamangustha” and “uttanam tatpavitram ca”, the material for the performing of homa should be collected and established. Gautama is the Rsi for this mantra; the same is the meter; and Dharmaraja is the Devata.

## \|\| 2.34.59-60 \|\|

*sakṛddravye tribhiḥ kāṣṭhaistrivāraṃ maṃtrapuṣpakaiḥ \|*  
*sthirasthāne tu saṃprāptapraṇītāyāśca dakṣiṇe \|\| 59 \|\|*

*prādeśāṃtarataścaiva ājyasthālīmathārpayet \|*  
*agrato maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā vahniṃ vipre tu sthāpayet \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. The stuff required for homa should be sprinkled with water thrice and while establishing the vase at its proper place, the vase for warming up of the ghi should be placed. A circular fire altar should then be made before the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.34.61 \|\|

*dyūtaṃ niḥsārayettattu nirūpyāśu krameṇa tu \|*  
*īśāneti ca maṃtreṇa adhiśrapaṇamīritam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Reciting the mantra “Isaneti”, the ghi should be placed over the fire for wanning it up. In case some other material like butter milk etc. is found in it, the same should be quickly removed.

## \|\| 2.34.62-64 \|\|

*ṛṣirnārāyaṇaśchandaḥ paṃktirīśo'tha devatā \|*  
*paryagnikaraṇaṃ kuryādādarāddvayamapyatha \|\| 62 \|\|*

*avekṣya īśamārabhya dakṣiṇāvartakena tu \|*  
*kulāyanīti maṃtreṇa ṛṣicchandādikaṃ smaran \|\| 63 \|\|*

*pariveṣyājyasthālīṃ ca triḥ sakṛdvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*pitarastṛpyatāmiti saṃskāre mātaraḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. Narayana is the Rsi for this mantra; Pankti is the meter; and Isa is the god. After looking into them carefully and finding them unblemished, the ghi should be put in another vase. Uttering the verse “Kulayaniti" while pouring the ghi in another vase is essential. Again reciting the mantra - “Pitarastrpyantam" once or thrice, the vases should be offered to them. Similar procedure is required to be performed during the samskara rites for the mothers.

## \|\| 2.34.65 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ syājjamadagniśca gāyatrī chanda īritam \|*  
*devatā ca pinākī syādagniṣṭome ca yojayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Jamadagni is the Rsi for this mantra; Gayatri is the meter, and Pankti is the god During the Agnistoma yajna, this particular Viniyoga is to be made use of.

## \|\| 2.34.66-67 \|\|

*ghṛtasya ca tathā tvaṃ no brahmā vai tṛpyatāmiti \|*  
*ṣaḍaṃgulaṃ sruvaṃ paścādgṛhītvāgnau pratapya ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

*trirātraṃ tu mahāyoge sakṛdanyatra sattamāḥ \|*  
*saṃmārjayetkuśenāpi mūlādagraṃ tu secayet \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. The ghi should then be placed before Brahma and one should utter “Brahma vai trpyatam” (let Brahma be satisfied). Thus offering him the vase of ghi, a prayer is required to be made to him. A ladle of six angulas in length should then be heated in fire and then water should be sprinkled at its base. O best of Brahmanas, this process is required to be repeated for three night during Mahayoga and once only in other cases.

## \|\| 2.34.68 \|\|

*agrānmūlaṃ punaḥ kuryātsaṃpūjya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tribhistribhiḥ praṇītode prokṣayettadanaṃtaram \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. It’s top and bottom should be worshipped repeatedly, then water from the sacred vase should be sprinkled over it.

## \|\| 2.34.69-70 \|\|

*bhuvaṃ punaḥ pratapyātha prokṣaṇyuttarato nyaset \|*  
*ājyapātraṃ puraskṛtya pavitraṃ ca samāharet \|\| 69 \|\|*

*aṃguṣṭhe dve anāme tu gṛhṇīyāttatpavitrakam \|*  
*aṣṭāṃgulaṃ madhyakṛtvo ghṛtaṃ triḥ pavanaṃ caret \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Then heating it again, it should be placed to the north of the Kusa grass in front of the payasam vase. It should then be purified with the ring of kusa grass tossing it with thumb and little fingers of both the hands.

## \|\| 2.34.71 \|\|

*pātāle tristathākāśe avekṣyājyaṃ tatastribhiḥ \|*  
*prokṣaṇyāṃ ca tathā kuryādadhaḥ saṃprokṣya deśikaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Looking into the ghi carefully, it should be tossed towards the sky and patala thrice. It should then be sprinkled thrice.

## \|\| 2.34.72 \|\|

*tataḥ pāyasamādāya utthāya ca samantra kam \|*  
*tūṣṇīṃ dadyāttathā cāgnau sanniveśena tattvataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thereafter, the payasam should be taken reciting the mantra with the hands wearing the pavitri (kusa ring) and keep quiet. An offering of the same should be poured in the fire.

## \|\| 2.34.73-74 \|\|

*sapavitraṃ dakṣakare gṛhītvā prokṣaṇīyakam \|*  
*aṣṭāṃgule mūlabhāge tajjalena īśāditaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*agniṃ paryukṣayetpaścāddakṣiṇāvartakena ca \|*  
*pavitraṃ ca praṇītāyāṃ nidhāya prokṣaṇīyakam \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. Holding the water in the palm of the hand wearing the pavitri and with its end of eight angulas, sprinkling should be started from the north-east and a mandala of fire should be formed. Thereafter, from the southern side, the pavitri as well as the sprinkling water should be poured in the sacred water vase.

## \|\| 2.34.75-76 \|\|

*saṃyāvārthaṃ ca bho viprā agnivattatra deśikaḥ \|*  
*dhyāyedagniṃ raktavarṇaṃ sruvahastaṃ tribāhukam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*kamaṃḍaluṃ pare haste tato dakṣakareṇa tu \|*  
*sruvaṃ gṛhītvā juhuyāttūṣṇīmeva samāhitaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. О Brahmanas, for the making of the pudding, the fire god should be meditated upon, having red complexion, holding a sruva in his hand. He has three arms, one of the other hands holds a kamandalu. Then holding the ladle in the right hand and keeping silent, the offerings should be made.

## \|\| 2.34.77-80 \|\|

*aṃte ca devatoddeśaṃ prājāpatyaṃ samīrayan \|*  
*praṇavāṃtena juhuyātsarvatra dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vāyukoṇaṃ samārabhya vahnikoṇāntakena tu \|*  
*acchinnena ghṛtenaiva indrāya tadanaṃtaram \|\| 78 \|\|*

*agnīṣomātmakaṃ caiva juhuyādrākṣasāditaḥ \|*  
*aiśānakoṇaparyaṃtaṃ tato naimittikaṃ caret \|\| 79 \|\|*

*paścātsviṣṭaṃ tato dadyāddadyācca matibhistathā \|*  
*vāruṇaṃ pañcakaṃ caiva kṛtvā pūrṇāṃ tato labhet \|\| 80 \|\|*

77-80. In the end, for the sake of the gods starting from Prajapatya, homa should be performed upto Pranava Starting from the north-west direction and upto the end of vahni-kona, an unbroken line of ghi should be made besides making an offering for Indra. After performing the Agni somatmaka homa, starting from the south-west, the offering should be made upto the south-west direction, by the people of wisdom.

## \|\| 2.34.81 \|\|

*udvāha iti maṃtra sya atharvaṇa ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*chaṃdo devī ca gāyatrī devataṃ cāpi vāruṇam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The mantra- “udvaha iti", which has Atharvan as the Rsi; Gayatri as the meter; and Varuna as the god, should be recited.

## \|\| 2.34.82 \|\|

*prakṛte yojayenmantrī stutau cāpi niyojayet \|*  
*tvannogna iti maṃtrasya ṛṣirvāśiṣṭhasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*chaṃdaśca bṛhatī khyātaṃ tadevāgniḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. While performing this yajna and offering the prayer, the use of Viniyoga is also said to be essential. The related mantra is-“Tvagnogna-iti”. Vasistha is its Rsi; Brhati is the meter, while the wind-god is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.83 \|\|

*iḍo gatamiti mantrasya ṛṣiḥ ko guhyasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*chandaśca jagatī khyātaṃ devo viṣṇuḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The mantra - “Idogatamiti" has Brahma as the Rsi; Jagati is the meter; while Visnu is the god.

## \|\| 2.34.84 \|\|

*udvartana iti maṃtrasya ṛṣiḥ ko nu prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*chando devī ca gāyatrī varuṇaścādhidevatā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Brahma is also the Rsi for this mantra -“Udvartan"; Gayatri is the meter; while Varuna is the god.

## Chapter 35. Processing of yajna

## \|\| 2.35.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*makhe sarvatra brahmāṇamṛtvijaṃ varayedatha \|*  
*kuśakaṇḍīṃ svagṛhyena kṛtvāgniṃ cārcayettataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said In all the types of yajnas, Brahma and the sacrificial priest have to be selected and the fire has to be consecrated in the vedi of the fire altar. The fire god has then to be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.35.2-4 \|\|

*āghārājyabhāgau tu mahāvyāhṛtayastrayaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ prāyaścittasaṃjñakaṃ prājāpatyaṃ ca sviṣṭakṛt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*etannityaṃ hi sarvatra home karmaṇi nirdiśet \|*  
*prājāpatye ca indrāya etāvāghārasaṃjñakau \|\| 3 \|\|*

*agnaye caiva somāya ājyabhāgau prakīrtitau \|*  
*bhūrbhuvaḥsvastrayaścaiva mahāvyāhṛtayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Half the kingdom, all the three upper regions, the performer of repentance, Prajapatya, the excellent offerings are made in the performing of homa. Two offerings are made for Indra and Prajapatya. The fire god and Soma have to the given two offerings which are known as Ajya-bhaga and the offering to be made to Bhur, Bhuvah and Svah are known as Maha-vyahrtis.

## \|\| 2.35.5 \|\|

*ayāścāgne iti tathā ye te śatamanuttamam \|*  
*sarvaprāyaścittasaṃjñā ete vai pañca maṃtrakāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The five offerings which are made with the mantras from “Ayascagre-iti” to “ye-te satamanuttamam” are known as the repentance offerings.

## \|\| 2.35.6 \|\|

*prājāpatyāhutiścaikā sviṣṭakṛccāparā smṛtā \|*  
*caturdaśaitāḥ kṛtayo hotavyā nityasaṃjñakāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A single offering is meant for Prajapatya and the other is for Svistakrta. Thus, the homa with these fourteen offerings should be performed regularly. Their regular number has also been prescribed.

## \|\| 2.35.7-8 \|\|

*kṛtvā sakṛddevatoddeśaṃ homaṃ paścātsamācaret \|*  
*somapā ye ca goyāge naramedhāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*anyatra viparītena svāhāṃtena hunedbudhaḥ \|*  
*naimittikaṃ vinā nityaṃ viphalaṃ yāti nānyathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. For the sake of the god, an offering should be poured at least once and the homa should be started thereafter. During the Gomedha, Naramedha and Asvamedha yajnas, the offerings are made for the purpose of a ladder. In case the system is the reverse, then uttering Svaha the offerings should be made to the learned people. But this process is made applicable in the casual or fortuitous functions and not in the regular functions, otherwise there is the possibility of their becoming infructuous.

## \|\| 2.35.9-10 \|\|

*nityaṃ varjyaṃ śatārdhena vaiśvadeve tathaiva ca \|*  
*tryahasādhyādiyāgeṣu yannideśaṃ śṛṇu dvijāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ekāhe vāghārārajyau kṛtvā naimittikīṃ kṛtīḥ \|*  
*samā sviṣṭakṛtaṃ vidyādākṛtyādyāstataḥ param \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. I am now speaking about the yajna which is performed in three days. You please listen. First day is the base in which Ajya Bhdga, casual rites and Svistakrt homa has to be performed. Besides all the casual rites should be performed.

## \|\| 2.35.11 \|\|

*viśeṣatastryahādau tu aghārāvājyapūrvakam \|*  
*paścānnaimittikaṃ kuryātsamāptidivase pyatha \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. For the success of the three days yajna, after finishing of the Ajya-bhaga and Aghara rites, other casual rites should also be completed.

## \|\| 2.35.12 \|\|

*āghārārājyapūrveṇa tato naimittikaṃ caret \|*  
*sviṣṭakṛdvyāhṛtiścaiva vāruṇādyāstathā hi ṣaṭ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After completing the Aghara as well as the Ajya rites, the casual rites should also be performed. Thus with the combination of Svistakrt, Vyahrta and Varuni rites, all the six rites are started at a time.

## \|\| 2.35.13 \|\|

*dvijātiḥ patito yatra dvitrikaṃ ca catuścatuḥ \|*  
*ekasmindivase kuryātsomayāge ca śaiśave \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The rites in which the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and Vaisyas are fallen and for their redemption, the related yajna comprising of two, three or four performances can be accomplished with the performing of the Soma-yaga or Saisava yaga in a day.

## \|\| 2.35.14 \|\|

*dvijātīnāṃ vivāhe tu naityikaṃ prathamaṃ bhavet \|*  
*ekasmindivase kuryādagnikāryaṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. During the marriage ceremonies of the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and Vaisyas, initially the routine rites are performed. On that very day, the homa is performed separately.

## \|\| 2.35.15-17 \|\|

*dadyādekaṃ ca nityaṃ ca pṛthaṅ nityaṃ na cācaret \|*  
*dvijātiḥ patito yatra dvitrikaṃ ca catuścatuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ekasmindivase kuryāttatrāpi naittikaṃ tyajet \|*  
*home brahmā stute viṣṇuḥ sruve caiva maheśvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ajasyāniyame cendro'dhiśrayaṇaṃ vivasvataḥ \|*  
*paryagnikaraṇe caiva udvāhe mātaraḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The completion of the same single rite is therefore essential. This should not be performed separately. With the performing of one, two or three rites for those who have fallen from the caste, the casual rites should be discarded. Brahma is to be adored while performing homa; Visnu is to be adored while offering prayer and Mahesvara is to be adored in ladle. Ajasya is to be adored in fire rites; Indra during eating; Vivasvan in Paryagni; and the Matrkas are to be adored in the marriage ceremonies. They should be consecrated and worshipped.

## \|\| 2.35.18 \|\|

*candrādityau cotpavane vīkṣaṇe ca diśastathā \|*  
*prokṣaṇyāṃ sthāpane durgā ime lakṣmī pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Similarly, in the purification ceremonies the sun and moon are to be adored; the directions for inspection; Durga in the spray of water, besides Laksmi who should be adored.

## \|\| 2.35.19 \|\|

*homaṃ kuryāddvijaśreṣṭhā vidhiṃ kuryātsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*eteṣu devatāḥ proktā dvijātīnāṃ hitāya ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О best of Brahmanas, the performing of homa should be completed with all the essential rites. The twice bom are required to worship all the gods which bestows welfare on them.

## \|\| 2.35.20-21 \|\|

*yajetsupaśubaddheṣu saṃskāre caiva parvaṇi \|*  
*devatāḥ sarvā jñātavyā etā yajñe samāhitaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*adhidaivena jānīyātkaravalyāṃ paṃcaphalaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena devatāmatha vinyaset \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. During the ceremonies connected with the domestication of animals, besides other yajna ceremonies, one should worship all the above gods carefully. Because of their being the presiding deities, the performer gets five rewards. Therefore, these gods should be adored making all the efforts.

## Chapter 36. Contemplation for the Goddesses

## \|\| 2.36.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha vakṣyāmi saccaiṣāṃ devānāṃ dhyānamuttamam \|*  
*asya yajñe parijñānājjihvā samyakphalapradā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said- I am now speaking about the excellent form of contemplation of the god which when followed appropriately, bestows the best of merit.

## \|\| 2.36.2-3 \|\|

*hiraṇyavarṇāṃ prathamāṃ vahnijihvāṃ mahādyutim \|*  
*kanakāḍhyakarāṃ devīṃ hiraṇyākhyeṣṭasiddhaye \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kanakāṃ dvibhujāṃ śuklāṃ hastābhyāṃ darbhasaṃyutām \|*  
*kamaṃḍaluṃ ca bibhrāṇāṃ numaḥ sādhakasiddhidām \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The first fire is extremely resplendent like the lustre of the gold. For the achieving of the desired success, the kanakddya has to be performed. The deity is of white complexion, with two hands carrying kusa grass as well as the kamandalu. The goddess bestows success to the devotees and we offer salutation to her.

## \|\| 2.36.4 \|\|

*udyadindunibhāṃ raktāṃ caturbhirbhujapa llavaiḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhacakrābhayavarāndadhatīṃ praṇamāmyaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She is beautiful like the rising moon and has red complexion. She is four-armed in the form of Brahmanas and carries conch, disc, abhaya and varada mudras. I offer my salutation to the said goddess.

## \|\| 2.36.5 \|\|

*bhinnāṃjanacayaprakhyāṃ svarṇakuṃbhaṃ tu vāmataḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇena varāraktāṃ dhārayaṃtīṃ namāmyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The (other) goddess having the black complexion of collyrium, clad in red garments, holds a golden pitcher in her left hand and displays the varada-mudra with her right hand. I offer my salutation to her.

## \|\| 2.36.6 \|\|

*suprabhāmaṇḍalābhā ca karābhyāṃ tatkṛtāñjaliḥ \|*  
*padmāsanasthā kauśeyavasanā me prasīdatu \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The goddess with prabhamandala of excellent lustre, holding both the hands in anjali mudra is seated over the lotus seat. She is clad in silken garments. Let the same goddess be pleased with me.

## \|\| 2.36.7 \|\|

*japākusumasaṃkāśā bahurūpā sakhe mama \|*  
*śubhadā syādbhujaiḥ śubhrā sahasraṃ dadhatī parān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. She has the complexion of a Chinese rose and takes to many forms. She destroys several enemies with her arms. Let she bestows welfare on me.

## \|\| 2.36.8 \|\|

*nīlotpalanibhe devi vahnivarṇaparābhave \|*  
*japāpuṣpadhare nityaṃ satīrūpe prasīda me \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O goddess, resembling the form of Sati, she has the complexion of a blue lotus. She is quite beautiful. She puts the lustre of the fire to shame. She is always adored with flowers of Chinese rose. Let the goddess be pleased with me.

## \|\| 2.36.9 \|\|

*mūlena vīkṣayetsthānaṃ maṃtreṇa khananaṃ matam \|*  
*trisūtrīkaraṇaṃ kuryāccatuḥsūtraṃ nipātayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thus contemplating upon, the ground should be examined and dig up reciting the mantras and then divided in three or four sutras.

## Chapter 37. Meditation of Gods

## \|\| 2.37.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāyāḥ pūrvadine kuryāddevādhivāsanam \|*  
*dhānyapratiṣṭhāṃ tasyaiva yūpaṃ cāpi yathāvidhi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said- Before consecration, the god should be offered the fragrance and cereals. Besides his yuра-stambha of the yajna should be installed.

## \|\| 2.37.2 \|\|

*rātrau mūlāgre ca ghaṭe sthāpayedgaṇanāyakam \|*  
*saṃpūjya ca vidhānena digīśāṃśca tathā grahān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. During the night, the image of Ganesa should be installed in the forecourt. He should then be worshipped along with the planets as well as Dikpalas.

## \|\| 2.37.3-4 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ ca taḍāgeṣu varuṇaṃ śāntiyāgake \|*  
*somaṃ ca maṃḍale sūryaṃ pāde viṣṇuṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śaive śaivaṃ tathā proktaṃ prapāyāmatha vāruṇam \|*  
*ārāme caiva brahmāṇaṃ pādyādyairapi cārcayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. During the yajnas for the tanks, Brahma is to be adored. During the yajnas for peace, Varuna is to be worshipped. Soma is to be adored in the mandala. Visnu and Surya are to be adored in the root of the tree. During the rites of Siva, the lord himself is to be worshipped. At the water hose in which water is supplied to the thirsty people, Varuna is to be adored. In the orchard, Brahma should be worshipped appropriately, offering the pddya and arghya.

## \|\| 2.37.5-8 \|\|

*drupadādīti mantreṇa snāpayetprathamaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*gāyatryā ca tataḥ paścādgandhadvāreti tailakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sunābheti ca maṃtreṇa dvābhyāmeva viśiṣyate \|*  
*śrīśca te iti kusumaṃ phalinīti ca vai phalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kāṃḍāditi ca maṃtreṇa dadyāddūrvāśataṃ tataḥ \|*  
*siṃdoriveti siṃdūraṃ viśvāmiti ca mārjanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*samicchetyañjanaṃ dadyādduḥsthaṃ surāsurā japan \|*  
*candanaṃ yajvabhirjaptvā mānastoketi candanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. The learned people should initially recite the verse drupadaditi. At the time of offering bath, Gayatri is to be adored reciting the mantra - "Gandha dvareti and sunabheti” and the oil should be offered. Then uttering “Srisca te iti" mantra, flowers should be offered, while the fruits should be offered uttering the verse “Phaliniti.” A hundred durvas should be offered reciting the mantra-“Kandaditi". The vermilion should be offered with the mantra- “Sindoriveti.” Then reciting the mantra- “Visvamiti', the water should be sprinkled. Reciting the mantra - “Duhstham-surasureti”, the collyrium should be offered. The sandal paste should be offered reciting the mantra- “Manastoketi."

## \|\| 2.37.9 \|\|

*yūpe caiva viśeṣoyamuttarāgraṃ pravinyaset \|*  
*adyaiva tena maṃtreṇa sthāpayedatha vāriṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Placing the sacrificial post towards the north, it should be consecrated on the same day, uttering the same mantra.

## \|\| 2.37.10-11 \|\|

*gāyatryā prathamaṃ caiva āpo hiṣṭheti vai japan \|*  
*śanno devīti drupadāṃ snāpayettadanantaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

*abhimantryātha brahmeti trirātraṃ maṃtramīrayan \|*  
*yogaṃ yogadṛḍhaṃ japtvā pavitraṃ vinyasettataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Reciting the Gayatri mantra, besides “Apohistheti’ and “Samodeviti,” one should take bath. Thereafter, the mantra- “Atha-brahmeti" should be repeated for three nights. Then the mantra - “Yogam yogadrdham”, pavitri is to the thrown there.

## \|\| 2.37.12-15 \|\|

*tvaṃ gandharveti mantreṇa tathā subhābha ityapi \|*  
*dvābhyāṃ tailagaṃdhayutaṃ śrīsūktenāpi puṣpakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dhūrasīti ca tathā dhūpamāsrajyotirbhirdīpakam \|*  
*anumīmahatāti dadyāddūrvākṣataṃ tataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*viśvāmīti ca nimnyaṃtakāṃḍāditi tathākṣatam \|*  
*siṃdoriveti sindūraṃ samidheti tathāñjanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pādo'syetyatha bhuktaṃ syādyāḥ phalinīti punaḥ phalam \|*  
*rūpaṃ neti dahedrūpaṃ na sociti ca pūjanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Then uttering the two mantras - "Tvam gandharveti" and “Subhabha-itt", the oil as well as perfume should be offered with flowers etc. Then reciting the mantra - “Dhurasiti", the incense should be offered, while the lamp should be offered uttering the mantra - “Asrajyotirbhiriti', the lamp has to be offered. The unbroken rice should be offered, uttering the verses- “Visvamiti and “Nimnyantakanda iti.” Then uttering the mantra - “Sindorive” the vermilion should be offered. Reciting the mantra - “Samidheti," the collyrium should be given. Then reciting the mantra - “Pado’syeti,” the food is to be offered. Thereafter, reciting the mantra - "Phaliniti" fruit should again be offered. Then “Rupam neti dahedrupam na sociti’ mantra should be recited while performing the adoration.

## \|\| 2.37.16-17 \|\|

*yuvā suvāseti vastraṃ nāgagandheti candanam \|*  
*tato yamagṛhādbāhye maṇḍapāṃtaramāśritaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sunātīti vaco dadyāttataścāvāhayetprabhum \|*  
*tatrādhivāsanaṃ kuryādrakṣayecca surakṣibhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Uttering the hymn- “Yuva suvaseti', costume should be given and by uttering-“Nagagandeiti,” the sandal paste has to be offered. Then out of the abode of Yama and outside the house, inside the mandapa, reciting the hymn- “Yuva-suvaseti,” the lord should be invoked and then established and well guarded by the competent guards.

## \|\| 2.37.18 \|\|

*ācāryo yajamānaśca ṛtvigbhojanamācaret \|*  
*akṣāralavaṇānyāsī dadhi viśvaṃ tilāṃstyajet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then the Acarya, the Yajamana as well as the Rtvika should be served with food comprising of salt and curd. The food should be served without sesamum etc.

## \|\| 2.37.19-20 \|\|

*ādhāraṇaṃ cādhivāsaṃ vakṣye tatrānusārataḥ \|*  
*sunāteti vaco dadyāttailaṃ caiva śive tribhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pañcabhirbrāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ gandharvā iti vismaran \|*  
*dadyādgandhaṃ tailayutaṃ gandhadvāretyṛcā punaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Now, I am talking about the consecration of the gods as per the provision of the scriptures. You please listen. Reciting the hymn “Sunateti", the sesamum oil should be I poured over Siva by three Brahmanas and the fragrance should be poured over Siva by five Brahmanas. Then uttering the mantra “Gandhadvareti”, the fragrance should again be poured over Siva.

## \|\| 2.37.21-23 \|\|

*yāḥ phalinīti ca phalaṃ pūgatānāmavarjanam \|*  
*kauśikīruttamosīti dadyātkhaḍgaṃ sutīkṣṇakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*rūpena veti mantreṇa mudgaraṃ ca nivedayet \|*  
*śrīśca te iti kusumaṃ viśvānīti ca saṃpaṭhan \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nirmathanaṃ tataḥ kāryamiti sādhāraṇo vidhiḥ \|*  
*tatodhivāsakalpe tu pradeśe tu samācaret \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Uttering the hymn “Yah phaliniti", the betel nut should be offered; with the mantra- Kausikiruttamositi”, the sharp edged sword and with the “Rupena veti mantrena," club should be offered. Uttering “Srisca te iti" mantra and “Visvaniti" mantra, the flowers should be offered and the fire should be ignited. This is the simple process. Subsequently, the process establishing the god should be performed again.

## \|\| 2.37.24 \|\|

*vinādhivāsanaṃ viprāḥ pratiṣṭhānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*na tatphalamavāpnoti vivāhe śaraṇaṃ diśet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Without performing the rite of establishing the god by a Brahmana, the entire process becomes useless.

## \|\| 2.37.25 \|\|

*tataḥ prayatnataḥ kāryaṃ pūrvāhne rātriyogataḥ \|*  
*nitye naimittike kāmye kārayetkuṇḍamaṇḍapam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Therefore, during the start of the night, the rite of establishing the god must be performed making all the efforts. A kunda-mandapa should be made ahead of performing casual as well as regular yajna rites.

## \|\| 2.37.26-31 \|\|

*sthaṃḍile hasta mātreṇa vālukānirmite'pi ca \|*  
*trayodaśāṃgule haste dvihaste cāpi varddhate \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ekaikāṃgulako viprāḥ pīṭhe nāsti vicāraṇā \|*  
*navapañcaka kuṇḍe ca lakṣādāvapi śaṃkayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tato daśāṃgule pakṣe daśāṃgaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|*  
*kāṣṭhaṃ pattraṃ ca puṣpaṃ ca modakaṃ piṣṭakaṃ tathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*annaṃ ca paramānnaṃ ca hyavekṣyaṃ tilameva ca \|*  
*etadvai gṛhapakṣe ca viṣṇupakṣe tilāditaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śaive yavāditaḥ kāryā śākte puṣpādito bhavet \|*  
*sūrye pakṣe piṣṭakādi gopāle kṛśarāditaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇe ca karavīrādi śrīphalāni ca traipure \|*  
*sārasvate ca śrīvṛkṣe mokṣakāme nigadyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

26-31. A pedestal of a single cubit, even if it is made in sand, must be arranged which should be quite beautiful. A pedestal of thirteen angulas, a cubit or of two cubits should be made, the size of which could be increased by an angula. Thus, it is not necessary to deeply think over the size of the pedestal. Even when fourteen altars are required to be made in which a lakh of offerings are to be poured, the same process has to be adopted. О Brahmanas, I am speaking about the things which are related to the ten angulas. You please listen, they are wood, leaves, flowers, sweet balls, powder, special food and sesamum. These are to be offered from the household side. The sesamum seeds are to be offered for the sake of Vi?nu; barley for the sake of Siva; flowers are needed for the performing the Sakti rites; ground gram is needed for the Sun; khicadi (mixed cereals) oleander for Sri Krsna; and Sriphala for performing the Tripura rites. For Sarasvati, Sri-vrksa and Sriphala is used for moksa rites at the start.

## Chapter 38. Contemplation of the Gods

## \|\| 2.38.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*aṣṭau hotāro dvārapālāthāṣṭau aṣṭau kāryā brāhmaṇā yājakāśca \|*  
*sarve śuddhā lakṣitā lakṣaṇādyairekaḥ kāryo jāpakosminmahātmā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said- There should be eight hotas (performing priests), eight gatekeepers and eight performers of the yajnas. These should be Brahmanas with auspicious symbols. Out of these learned Brahmanas, one of them should be entrusted with the duty of performing the japam or recitation.

## \|\| 2.38.2 \|\|

*divyairgaṃdhairgaṃdhamālyaiḥ suvarṇaistailaṃ kāryaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ pañcaviṃśāḥ \|*  
*āvāpyaistu dviguṇairvai balīyo divyairvastrairarhaṇādakṣiṇābhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. These twenty five Brahmanas should be offered oil, costumes and daksina. Their earning should be double. They should be offered divine fragrance, garlands and gold.

## \|\| 2.38.3 \|\|

*nārhayitvā yathoktena kaścitpatraṃ niveśayet \|*  
*anarhiteṣu vipreṣu na samyakphalamāpnuyāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. No vase should be allowed to be entered in the yajnas without its purification followed by the above process. Because in case the process is performed by the non-adorable Brahmanas, one does not achieve the desired merit.

## \|\| 2.38.4-5 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhādiṣu sarveṣu samyagviprānathārhayet \|*  
*kuśadvijaṃ tu sarvatra arghyaṃ viṣṭaramātrakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pradadyādarhaṇaṃ samyakpaścātpātraṃ nivedayet \|*  
*vinārhaṇaṃ kṛte tasminnarake paripacyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. In all the consecration ceremonies, the Brahmanas should be very well adored. All the performers should be well classified, otherwise they should have to fall in the hell

## \|\| 2.38.6 \|\|

*pratyekaṃ brāhmaṇā yajñe vedamantreṣu pāragāḥ \|*  
*ācāryo yadi kāryeṣu varayeddaśa govrajān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Each and every Brahmana in a yajna should be well-versed in the Vedic hymns. Therefore, for the performing of all the duties (in the yajna), ten Govrajas should select the Acarya.

## \|\| 2.38.7 \|\|

*viśiṣṭānāmabhāve'pi kuryātkuśamayāndvijān \|*  
*kuśapratikṛtau cāpi svagotraṃ svaṃ dvijaṃ vinā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the absence of the specific people of learnings, the Kusamaya Brahmana should be conceived (or a figure of Brahmana of kusa grass should be made). While making the figure of a Brahmana with kusa, one should discard his own gotra.

## \|\| 2.38.8 \|\|

*na kuryāccaraṇoddeśaṃ tathā praharasaṃhatim \|*  
*gotrādikīrtanāṃteṣu svanāmoddeśamīrayan \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Discarding the branch (sakha) and without thinking about the respective group, only after the uttering of one’s own gotra, one’s own name should be uttered.

## \|\| 2.38.9 \|\|

*tulāpuruṣadāne ca tathā ca hāṭakācale \|*  
*kanyādāne tathotsarge kīrtayetpravarādikam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. During tula-dana (weighing a person in cereals etc.), giving away of the Meru mountain, giving away of the daughter, or in separation ceremonies, a person’s Pravara should also be mentioned.

## \|\| 2.38.10-15 \|\|

*na pātraṃ pratikṛtyarthaṃ na cālaṃ sodakaṃ tathā \|*  
*mṛtabhāryyo hyabhāryaśca aputro mṛtaputrakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śūdrasaṃskārakaścaiva kṛpaṇo gaṇayājakaḥ \|*  
*prāyaścittagṛhītaśca rājayājakapaiśunau \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śūdragehanivāsī ca śūdrapreraka eva ca \|*  
*svalpakaṇṭho vāmanaśca vṛṣalīpatireva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bandhudveṣī gurudveṣī bhāryādveṣī tathaiva ca \|*  
*hīnāṃgaścaiva vṛddhāṃgo bhagnadaṃtaśca dāṃbhikaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pratigrāhī ca kunakhaḥ pāradārika eva ca \|*  
*śvitrī kuṣṭhī kulodbhūto nidrālurvyasanārthakaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*adīkṣitaḥ kadaryaśca caṃḍarogī galadvraṇaḥ \|*  
*mahāvraṇī ca udarī yajñapātraṃ na kārayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

10-15. For the sake of images, the participants are never thought of, similarly one cannot think of a real brother for the sake of the movement. A person should not be considered suitable to participate in a yajna in case his wife is dead, or is without a wife, or whose son has died, who has been readmitted into the faith after performing of repentance rites, one who performs the yajnas with the rulers, one who indulges in back biting, one who lives in the house of a Sudra or is inspired by a Sudra, one who cannot speak clearly, a dwarf, one who has married a Sudra woman, a close relative, one who is envious of the preceptor or his wife, one who is short of a limb or have an excess limb, broken teeth, treacherous one, one who accepts charities, one having deformed nails, one who enjoys the wives of others, one who suffers from leucoderma, a lepor, one who sleeps much, a criminal, who has not been initiated, a coward, a furious person, with a septic wound and the one with a big wound and the. one having an ailment in the belly, should not be allowed to participate in the yajna.

## \|\| 2.38.16 \|\|

*varaṇāṃte tu pātrāṇāṃ pūjāmantrāñchṛṇu dvija \|*  
*pratimantreṇa gandhādyairarcayenmantravittamaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Brahmanas, after the selection of the participants of the yajna, I am speaking about their adoration, which you please listen. The one who recites the mantras should be worshipped with the reciting of the mantras.

## \|\| 2.38.17 \|\|

*brahmamūrtistvamācāryaḥ saṃsārātpāhi māṃ vibho \|*  
*tvatprasādādguro yajñaṃ prāptosmi yanmayepsitam \|\| 17 \|\|*
