17\. One should say - “You are the form of Brahman, besides being my Аcarуа. О excellent one, you please protect me in this world. О my preceptor, with your pleasure, I have started my yajna.

## \|\| 2.38.18 \|\|

*ciraṃ me śāśvatī kīrtiryāvallokāścarācarāḥ \|*  
*prasīda tvaṃ maheśāna pratiṣṭhākarmasiddhaye \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Till such time the mobile and immobile creations would remain on earth, let my fame spread in the world upto that time. О Mahesan, the success of the yajna started by me has to be achieved by your grace. You kindly be pleased.

## \|\| 2.38.19 \|\|

*tvamādiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃsārārṇava tārakaḥ \|*  
*jñānāmṛtapradācāryo yajurveda namo'stu te \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. You are the start of all the living beings and make them cross over the ocean of the universe. You are also an Аcarуа to bestow the nectar of knowledge. О Yajurveda, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.38.20 \|\|

*brahmaṇaiva samudbhūta prakāśitadigantara \|*  
*śuddhajāṃbūnadaprakhya yajurveda namo'stu te \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. This Yajurveda had been created by Brahma, it is pervading in all the directions, possess the lustre of JambQnada gold. Salutation to the same Yajurveda.

## \|\| 2.38.21 \|\|

*prataptakanakābhāsa bhāsitadyutibhūtala \|*  
*mantraprakhyānasaṃsthāna yajurveda namo'stu te \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Like the heated gold, it issues the rays of light on earth. With the discourses enshrined in the mantras, Yajurveda serves as an institution. Salutation to Yajurveda.

## \|\| 2.38.22 \|\|

*praphullakanakābhāsa bhāsvarāsurabhūṣita \|*  
*prakīrṇamantrasaṃbhāravidhijña praṇato'smi te \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Salutation to the one with the glitter of gold, who is respected among the Asuras and is well-versed in the interpretation of the mantras, besides possessing the complete knowledge of the mantras. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.38.23 \|\|

*ṣaḍaṃgavedavedajña ṛtviṅgamokṣaprado bhava \|*  
*praviśya maṇḍalaṃ viprā svasthāne sthāpayetkramāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A Brahmana who is well-versed in all the Vedas with their six angas (parts), should be the cause of achieving moksa by the performer of the yajna. Thus speaking, all the Brahmanas should be lodged in their respective places in the mandala.

## \|\| 2.38.24-30 \|\|

*vedyāḥ paścimabhāge tu ācāryaṃ sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*kuṇḍasyāgre tu brahmāṇaṃ maṇḍalasyaiva paścime \|\| 24 \|\|*

*hotāraṃ sthāpayettatra vidhijñamatha cottare \|*  
*dvaudvau kṛtvā jñāpakau ca khaḍgadhārakameva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dvāridvāri prayatnena dvārapālānanukramāt \|*  
*vakṣyamāṇena maṃtreṇa pratyekamatha sthāpayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pūjayedgandhapuṣpādyairvāsaso yugalena tu \|*  
*yajñe savitate yo'sau pūjyate puruṣaḥ sadā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇasvarūpeṇa yajñaṃ me saphalaṃ kuru \|*  
*yajñeṣu sākṣī sarveṣu yajurvedārthatattvavit \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ṛgvedārthasya tattvajña indrarūpa namo'stu te \|*  
*makhaśreṣṭheṣu sarveṣu yena maṃtrāḥ suvistṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yajurvedārthatattvajña brahmarūpa namo'stu te \|*  
*makhaśreṣṭheṣu sarveṣu eṣa eva vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

24-30. A Learned person should lodge the Acarya to the west of die pedestal (vedi), Brahma in the forefront of the kunja or altar, the performer (the one who drops offerings in the fire) to the west of mandala and the one who is aware of the processing (of the activities) should be established towards the north over a seat. At every gate, two jnapakas holding swords in their hands, should be made to stand like the gatekeepers. They should also be adored individually offering the fragrant flowers and two costumes to each one of them. They must be worshipped saying- “In the vast yajna a person who is always worshipped, he alone taking to the form of Narayana should bestow success to my yajna. Salutation to the form of Indra, who is well-versed in the tattvas of the Vedas, who has been exhaustively praised with mantras in all the yajnas. Salutation to the form of Brahma.” This has been prescribed to be the process of performing all the yajnas.

## \|\| 2.38.31 \|\|

*māṃgalyaṃ karmaṇāṃ nityaṃ sarvajñaṃ jñānarūpi ṇam \|*  
*siddhaye mama yajñasya namāmi śivarūpiṇam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I offer my salutation to lord Siva, who is the form of welfare for all the activities, who is omniscient, eternal, form of knowledge and welfare, for the success of my yajna.

## \|\| 2.38.32-34 \|\|

*pālaya tvaṃ diśaḥ sarvā vidiśaśca tathā imam \|*  
*dikpālarūpiṇaṃ vipraṃ yajñasiddhau namā myaham \|*  
*na saṃkalpaṃ caredyāgaṃ vrataṃ devārcanaṃ tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*saṃkalpamūlaḥ kāmo vai yajñāḥ saṃkalpasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*saṃkalpena vinā viprā yatkiñcitkurute naraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*phalaṃ cālpālpakaṃ tasya dharmasyārddhakṣayo bhavet \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena yāgaṃ saṃkalpayetsudhīḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. You protect all the directions and their intermediate points. Then I also offer my salutation to the Brahmana serving as a gatekeeper. No yajna, vrata or the worship of the gods should be performed without performing the samkalpa, because the success can be achieved with the desire based on samkalpa and similarly, with the samkalpa, success is achieved in the yajna. Therefore, О Brahmanas, a person who does anything without a samkalpa, half of the merit of the yajna so performed, is lost to him. Therefore, the learned people should perform the yajnas with samkalpa making all the efforts.

## \|\| 2.38.35-36 \|\|

*kāmātparo naiva bhavenniṣkāmo'pi na śobhanaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkāmamayaṃ dharmaṃ vinā mokṣaṃ na cācaret \|\| 35 \|\|*

*saṃkalpena vinā yastu dharmaṃ carati mānavaḥ \|*  
*na tasya phalamāpnoti nityanaimittikasya ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. To be free from the desires or discarding of the desires totally would not be proper, therefore, the dharma with desires to make efforts for achieving moksa would be of no use. By vowing a firm resolve or a sankalpa, but following the casual or regular dharma, one is deprived of the merit accrued therefrom.

## \|\| 2.38.37 \|\|

*na kuryātsthāpane caiva kuryādvai maṃḍalāṃtare \|*  
*gṛhītvauduṃbaraṃ pātraṃ vāripūrṇaṃ guṇānvitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A vase of wild fig tree filled with water should not be consecrated in the middle of the mandapa.

## \|\| 2.38.38 \|\|

*jalāśayārāmakūpa saṃkalpe pūrvadiṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*sādhāraṇe cottarāsyo grahayajñe tu saṃmukhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The lakes, orchards and the well when being consecrated, the samkalpa has to be performed, facing east. Similarly, for ordinary jobs one should do so facing north and for the yajnas, it should be done facing the front.

## \|\| 2.38.39 \|\|

*mahāvrate pratiṣṭhāyāṃ pātraṃ tāmraṃ hiraṇmayam \|*  
*rājatāśmamayaṃ sāṃgaṃ yadyajñeṣu praśasyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. During Mahavrata and the functions of consecration, the vases and other articles are required to be made of copper, gold, silver and stone.

## \|\| 2.38.40 \|\|

*yajñīyapātrapuṭakaṃ hastasthāne prakīrtitam \|*  
*aiśyānyāṃ nikṣipettoyaṃ pratiṣṭhāyāṃ ca pūrvataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In place of the hand in the vases of yajnas, the lotus flowers or folders are made use of. The water of the vase has to be dropped towards the north-east direction, while at the time of consecration, it should be dropped towards the east.

## \|\| 2.38.41 \|\|

*ākāśe nikṣipedyāge vrate īśepi nityake \|*  
*pitṛmedhe ca goyāge naramedhe ca dakṣiṇe \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. During the regular vrata as well as the yajna of Siva, the water is to be thrown towards the sky, while in the Pitrmedha, Gomedha and Naramedha yajnas, the water has to be dropped towards the south and in other cases it is forbidden.

## \|\| 2.38.42 \|\|

*śuktikāṃsyādihastaiśca tāmraraupyādibhistathā \|*  
*saṃkalpo naiva kartavyo mṛnmaye ca kadācana \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Samkalpa should not be offered with the hands of shell, bronze, copper or silver and of clay.

## \|\| 2.38.43 \|\|

*praṇavaṃ pūrvamuccārya yajedyajñeśvaraṃ smaret \|*  
*gaṅgā cādityacaṃdrau ca dyaurbhūmī rātrivāsarau \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. First of all uttering Pranava, lord Yajnesvara and Gangs, the sun, the moon, the sky, the earth, the day and night should be remembered.

## \|\| 2.38.44 \|\|

*sūryaḥ somo yamaḥ kālo mahābhūtāni paṃca ca \|*  
*ete śubhāśubhāsyeha karmaṇo nava sākṣiṇaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The sun, moon, Yama, Kala, the five Mahabhutas, (Prthivi, Agni, Jala, Vayu and Akasa) serve as witness to all the good or bad deeds of every living being.

## \|\| 2.38.45-46 \|\|

*ityuccārya nyaseddharmaṃ dhyātvā puṣpāñjaliṃ sṛjet \|*  
*amṛtaṃ kṛtyapātre ca oṃ tatsaditi nirdiśet \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dharmaḥ śubhravapuḥ sitāṃbaradharaḥ kāryordhvadeśe vṛṣo hastābhyāmabhayaṃ varaṃ ca satataṃ rūpaṃ paraṃ yo dadhat \|*  
*sarvaprāṇisukhāvahaḥ kṛtadhiyāṃ mokṣaikahetuḥ sadā soyaṃ pātu jagaṃti caiva satataṃ bhūyātsatāṃ bhūtaye \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Thus uttering, with both hands flowers should be offered. The nectar lies in the vases' in use. Then uttering the mantra- “Оm tatsaditi, the prayer should be started to the deity having white complexion body and clad in white garments. He is the dharma, in whose upper part vrsabha, hasya, besides abhaya and varada mudras are held, who bestows comforts to all the living beings and moksa to those who have achieved the best of knowledge. Let him protect me always and bestow all the comforts and wealth to the noble people.

## \|\| 2.38.47-48 \|\|

*yajñasaṃbaṃdhiviprāṃśca ekāhenaiva yojayet \|*  
*havirdravyāṇi yāni syuraṣṭayāgāṃtarepi ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

*punaḥpunarniyojyāni brāhmaṇā haviragnayaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The stuff for the yajna: and the Brahmanas should be deputed on one and the same day. The same process has also been prescribed in the eighth part, because the Brahmanas, Havl and Agni are to be made use of again and again.

## Chapter 39. Consecration of Yoga

## \|\| 2.39.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*māghādimāseṣvapi ṣaṭsu kāryā yogapratiṣṭhā ṛṣibhiḥ praṇītā \|*  
*devādisaṃsthāpanamā huratra yāvanna supto madhusūdanaśca \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said - Starting from the month of Magha, till the arrival of the day of Madhusudana’s sleep works out to be the period of six months. In this period, the yoga-pratistha as well as the consecration of the gods and other deities, has been prescribed in the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.39.2 \|\|

*vāre bhṛgordevagurorbudhasya somasya sarvāḥ śubhadā bhavaṃti \|*  
*lagne śubhasthe śubhavīkṣite vā kāryā pratiṣṭhā ca jalāśayānām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Friday, thursday, Wednesday and monday are all considered to be auspicious. During these days and the favourable stars, the tanks or lakes can be consecrated.

## \|\| 2.39.3-4 \|\|

*śuddhā dvitīyā ca tathā tṛtīyā trayodaśī cāpi tathaiva viprāḥ \|*  
*tathāpi saptamyapi paurṇamāsī daśamyasau cāpyatha paṃcamī ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*prāṇapratiṣṭhā ca jalāśayāderetāḥ praśastāstithayo bhavaṃti \|*  
*aprāpya caitāni śubhāni yāni kāryā pratiṣṭhā viṣuvadvaye ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. О Brahmanas, the auspicious tithis of the second day of moon dvitiya, trtiya, trayodasi, saptami, purnima, dasami and pancami have been said to be praiseworthy for the purpose of consecration. In the absence of these auspicious tithis (moon days), the task of consecration of Vaisnavas should be performed.

## \|\| 2.39.5 \|\|

*ṣaḍaśītilokāpyayanadvayena yugādike puṇyādine śubhe ca \|*  
*kāryā taḍāgādijalāśayasya prācyāṃ pratiṣṭhā atha cottare vā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The equinoxal points of the eighty six Iokas are combined at the same time. During these auspicious times, the tanks should be consecrated towards the east or the north.

## \|\| 2.39.6-7 \|\|

*sucāru īṣatpravaṇe ca deśe suvartulaḥ ṣoḍaśahastamaṃḍapaḥ \|*  
*dvāraiścaturbhiḥ prathitairupetaścaturmukhaścāpi bhavetsuretāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pūrvādidvāreṣu catuṣṭayeṣu plakṣādibhistoraṇakaiḥ sureśaḥ \|*  
*plakṣastathoduṃbarapippalau ca nyagrodhakaṃ cāpi yathākrameṇa \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. In a beautiful slopy land, a circular mandapa of sixteen cubits should be prepared with four exit gates made in a beautiful way. The beautiful image of Brahma should be decorated therein. All the four eastern gates or toranas should be made of holy fig tree or citron tree and should be decorated with toranas of fig tree, udumbara, pipala and banyan trees.

## \|\| 2.39.8 \|\|

*ūrdhve ca hastānamitāni yāni vicitramālyāṃbarabhūṣitāni \|*  
*bhūmau yathā prīti ca hastakāni bhavaṃti caitānyapi toraṇāni \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A garland of a cubit in length as well as the cloth should be used to decorate them, while hanging them, adding to the beauty of the place. As the lovable hands are described in relation to the land, this is also known as the combat.

## \|\| 2.39.9 \|\|

*sarvatra yāgepi hi maṃḍapasya kāryā dhvajā dikṣu vidikṣu śubhrāḥ \|*  
*dikpālavarṇābhapatākayuktā madhye ca vai nīlapatākayuktāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In all the parts of the mandapa in the four directions, the flags of white colour should be hoisted. Half of each one of the flag be of the colour of the respective Dikpalas, while the other half should be of blue colour.

## \|\| 2.39.10 \|\|

*dhvajāśca yasmindaśahastasammitāstasminpatākā api pañcahastāḥ \|*  
*aratnimātrā yadi mūlabhāge paṃcāṃgu lāgre vinibaddhagūḍhāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The flag pole should be of the height of ten cubits, while the flag should be half of its size. Above five angulas at the base, the wooden drill should be of a cubit in size and should be firmly fixed.

## \|\| 2.39.11 \|\|

*dvāre ca tasmiṃśca nirūpitā vā raṃbhā supuṣpā sukhaśāḍvalāśca \|*  
*vacābhivṛkṣottarapaṃcahastāḥ sapaṃcaśākhā api tora ṇāni \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The trunks of the banana tree should be installed, further decorated with beautiful flowers. The grassy land, which should provide comfort to the people, should be developed. The trees which are planted within the radius of five cubits should be known by the names of the respective toranas.

## \|\| 2.39.12-13 \|\|

*muṃjodbhavairbarhisamudbhavairvā suraṃjitaścettritapadmapallavaiḥ \|*  
*puṣṭadvaye sūtritaṃ veṣṭayecca tathekṣukāṇḍairatha yāgamaṇḍapam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vedistathā maṃḍapa madhyabhāge kāryā ca koṇesthituṣādihīnā \|*  
*hastocchritā reravavatī surekhapariṣkṛtā hastacatuṣṭayena \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Jute (seeds), kusa grass and three types of lotus flower petals should be spread around the flag posts as well as the yajna-mandapa, which should be bound with strings (where necessary). In the middle of the mandapa, two pedestals (vedis) each with cubits’s height should be established, decorated with lines quite beautifully. These pedestals should be of the size of four cubits each and over each one of their comers, the bones should not be there.

## \|\| 2.39.14 \|\|

*vedyāṃ parityajya daśāṃgulāni aiśānyata strīṇi tathā parāṇi \|*  
*kuṃḍāya dadyāccaturasramekamavasthitaṃ tryaṃgulamekhalojjvalam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the said pedestals, beyond ten angulas in the north-east and other corners and leaving aside space for three angulas, a square altar should be made in which there should be a chain of white colour of the size of three angulas.

## \|\| 2.39.15 \|\|

*prāsāde ca taḍāge ca mahārāme tathaiva ca \|*  
*maṃḍalaṃ sarvatobhadraṃ prayatnenaiva kārayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A palace, a lake or a vast orchard, а mandala or a sarvatobhadra should be made, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 2.39.16 \|\|

*kuṃḍaṃ cāpi prakurvīta yathābhyantaramekhalam \|*  
*bahiryonigataṃ śvetaṃ niścitraṃ samasūtrakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The making of such a type of altar has been prescribed. A chain should be made in it and in the yoni made about, white colour should be shown. It should be without painting and should be equally distributed with threads.

## \|\| 2.39.17 \|\|

*kuṃḍāni kuryānnava kuṃḍapakṣe vedyāstathoccairavidikṣu caiva \|*  
*sarvāṇi sarvatra ca mekhalāni ṣaḍasrapaṃcāsrasamekhalāni \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The altars should then be made. This is required for the new altars. These altars should have such types of pedestals, which are raised from all the sides and the chain is complete, irrespective of the fact, whether the pedestals is hexagonal or pentagonal.

## \|\| 2.39.18-19 \|\|

*aṣṭāsrajānyabjatrikoṇakāni tathārddhacandraṃ caturasrakaṃ ca \|*  
*kuṇḍasya pūrvottaradigvibhāge sthāpyo ghaṭaścandanacāruliptaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mālyāmbarācchāditapūrṇapāthāḥ savṛttapatraśca suvarṇagarbhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The octagonal, triangular, crescent type or square altars are also prepared in the same way. Towards the north-east of the altar, the water pitcher should be consecrated which should be beautifully decorated with the lines drawn with the sandal paste, the flower garlands and clothes. It should be filled with water. The gold piece should be poured in it and should be placed over a circular base.

## Chapter 40. Worship of the abode of gods

## \|\| 2.40.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*gato yāgagṛhādanyanmaṇḍalāṃtaramāśritaḥ \|*  
*yajamānastathā nityaṃ karma kṛtvā yathāvidhi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said- The performer should go in an appropriate manner in the other part of the mandala in the yajna palace and should complete his daily routine there.

## \|\| 2.40.2-7 \|\|

*paṃca devānnamaskṛtya tathā yajñeśvaraṃ harim \|*  
*saṃkalpaṃ ca tataḥ kṛtvā brāhmaṇānāmanujñayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*etasminpuṇyadeśe tu phalaṃ gotraśca vai yamaḥ \|*  
*vedavyāsādipraṇītaṃ yathāśāstranidarśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yathāyathā svatantroktaṃ puṇyā raṇyābhidhāyakam \|*  
*jalāśayapratiṣṭhāyāṃ kariṣye vidhivaddvijāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yathāyathā ca kalpoktaṃ yathākuṇḍaṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*sādhivāsaṃ yathaivaikaḥ puṇyāraṇyavidhāyakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jalāśayapratiṣṭhāṃ ca kariṣye vidhivaddvijāḥ \|*  
*saṃkalpamevaṃ kṛtvā tu vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ samācaret \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mātṛyāgaṃ puraskṛtya vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ samāpayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

2-7. After offering his salutation to all the five presiding deities of the yajna, then he should receive command from the Brahmanas and offer the samkalpa. In this auspicious ceremony, Yama is the enhancer of the gotra and the merits. As per the command of the Sastras composed by Maharsi Vyasa and others, they have uttered speeches, phrases or statements- “I shall perform all of them completely, while consecrating this lake in an appropriate manner. According to the procedure laid down during many kalpas, I shall build the altar in an appropriate manner. Then performing adhivasa at the Punyaranya, I shall complete all the formalities while establishing this tank or the lake. After uttering this samkalpa and performing Vrddhi sraddha and Matr-yaga, I shall complete all the formalities.”

## \|\| 2.40.8 \|\|

*bheryādighoṣeṇa sumaṃgalena padyaṃ likhedatra saṣoḍaśākṣaram \|*  
*indrādidikpālavarāyudhāni samullikhedeva diśi sthitāni \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The musical sound should be produced besides the beating of the big drums. A passage of sixteen letters should be written and the excellent weapons of Indra and other gods should be created in all the directions.

## \|\| 2.40.9-11 \|\|

*brahmeśānvarayetsarvānācāryaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*svarṇakuṃḍalayugmena tathā tāmrādibhājanaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*nānāratnaiśca vastraiśca ācāryaṃ varayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*hemālaṃkārayugmaiśca vāsobhirvividharaipi \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yathāmānaṃ yathāśakti yathābhivṛṇuyādbudhaḥ \|*  
*racitā yajamānena dhruvaṃ svastyastu te iti \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. After selecting the Brahmanas, the acarya should be particularly offered gold earrings, vases of copper, a number of gems and costumes, as well as to the other Brahmanas. Two ornaments of gold and several types of costumes as per one’s means, should be given, while selecting the Brahmanas. After the Brahmanas are selected by the yajamana. or the performer, they should bless him saying-“Dhruvarh Svastyastu" (let you meet with welfare).

## \|\| 2.40.12 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvauṣadhībhiśca yajamānaḥ sapatnikaḥ \|*  
*āpohiṣṭhetimantreṇa snāpayāmāsuraprajāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The host with his wife and children should take bath with water mixed with herbs, reciting the mantra- “Apohistheti.'' He should bathe himself and also his wife.

## \|\| 2.40.13 \|\|

*yavagodhūmanīvāratilaśyāmākaśālayaḥ \|*  
*priyaṃguvrīhayaścāṣṭau sarvauṣadhigaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The cereals known as barley, wheat, wild rice, sesamum, syamaka, sali paddy, long pepper and cereals are known as Sarvausadhis.

## \|\| 2.40.14-16 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ \|*  
*sarvauṣadhyudakasnātaḥ snāpito vedapuṅgavaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇairabhyanujñātaḥ purohitapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*nānāmaṃgalaghoṣeṇa bherīpaṭahanisvanaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yajamānaḥ sapatnīkaḥ putrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*paścimaṃ dvāramāsādya praviśed yāgamaṇḍapam \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Then wearing the white garments, wearing the garland of white flowers, applying the sandal paste over the body, taking bath with the water of all the ausadhis with the permission of the Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas, following the priest and with the sounding of the welfare musical instruments, accompanied with his wife and son, he should enter the yajna-mandapa.

## \|\| 2.40.17-22 \|\|

*carake pūjayedvighnaṃ gaṃgāṃ ca yamunāṃ tathā \|*  
*pārśvayoścārdhato lakṣmīṃ pratihāramanukramāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vediṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya namaskuryādyathāvidhi \|*  
*upaviśya tatastasminbrāhmaṇānumate sthitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*svasti vācyaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā paṃca devānprapūjayet \|*  
*bhūtotsādaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vikirānvikiredbhuvi \|\| 19 \|\|*

*apakrāmaṃtu ye bhūtā ye cāsminviprakārakāḥ \|*  
*yasmānno nāmni vartaṃte yajñamātraṃ pravartatām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pūjayedāsanaṃ paścātsvakīyaṃ puṣpacaṃdanaiḥ \|*  
*namonaṃtāsanāyeti tathā padmāsanāya ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vimalāsanāya ca namo namaḥ sārāsanāya ca \|*  
*yogāsanāya ca namaḥ pṛthivyai nama ityapi \|\| 22 \|\|*

17-22. In Caraka the Vighna, Ganga, Yamuna and Laksmi in the rear half should be worshipped in the sequence of Dvarapalas or gatekeepers. They should go round the pedestals (vedi) appropriately there and offering salutation to them, they should take their seats. Then in consultation with the Brahmanas, welfare mantras (Svastivacana) should be recited. Adoring the five deities, the rite of bhutasuddhi and for the removal of blemishes, charities should be given. The Brahmanas should command—“Such of the goblins, who have arrived to create obstruction in this yajna, should leave this place atonce for the successful completion of the yajna." For making the goblins to flee from the place, an asana is required to be worshipped with flowers and sandal paste thus- “Salutation to Anantasana, Padmasana, Vimalasana, Sarasana and Yogasana again and again, all types of salutation to the earth.”

## \|\| 2.40.23-26 \|\|

*tato bhūmitale vāmahastaṃ dattvā paṭhennaraḥ \|*  
*pṛthvi tvayā dhṛtā lokā devi tvaṃ viṣṇunā dhṛtā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tvaṃ ca dhāraya māṃ nityaṃ pavitramāsanaṃ kuru \|*  
*sūryāyārghyaṃ tato dattvā guruṃ natvā kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*devaṃ hṛtpadmake nītvā prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ caret \|*  
*tato'rcayedvighnarājamaiśānyāṃ ca ghaṭopari \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gandhapuṣpaistathā vastrairnaivedyairvividhairapi \|*  
*gaṇānāṃ tveti maṃtreṇa brahmāṇaṃ tadanaṃtaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. Thereafter, placing the left hand over the ground, the following prayer should be made-“O Prthivi, you are holding the entire globe, with all the lokas, while you had been held by lord Visnu. Holding me always, you should also purify this sect. An arghya should then be offered to the Sun-god and offering salutation to the preceptor with folded hands, the presiding deity should by meditated in the lotus like heart and the pranayama should be performed thrice. Then over the kalasa in the north-east direction, Ganesa - the lord of obstructions, should be worshipped with perfume, flowers, costumes and eatables of various kinds. With the recitation of the mantra- “Gananam tveti ’, the adoration of Ganesa should be completed.

## \|\| 2.40.27-28 \|\|

*ābrahmanniti ṛcā tadviṣṇoriti saṃsmaran \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ tataḥ paścādbalibhirgandhacaṃdanaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tato devaśarīraṃ tu navamāsādya triṃśatam \|*  
*vedyāśca paritaḥ sarvānsvesve sthāne yathākramam \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Reciting the mantra - “Abrahmanniti ’ and “Tadvisnoriti, lord Vasudeva should be worshipped offering the presents, perfume, sandal paste and other things. Thereafter, worship of the thirty new bodies of the gods, who had been lodged over their respective places around the pedestal (vedi), should be performed.

## \|\| 2.40.29-34 \|\|

*tato rājādhirājena bhūtaśuddhiṃ samācaret \|*  
*tato budbudamadhye tu śvetapadmāsanasthitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ śaṃkhakundendusaprabham \|*  
*kirīṭakuṇḍalayutaṃ sitaṃ paṃkajadhāriṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śuklamālyāṃbaraṃ śuklaṃ śuklagaṃdhānulepanam \|*  
*ahituṇḍāsanasthaṃ ca pāśahastaṃ mahābalam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*stūyamānaṃ suragaṇaiḥ siddhagaṃdharvasevitam \|*  
*sucāruvadanaṃ devaṃ padmamālopaśobhitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*rājīvalocanaṃ nityaṃ nāgalokopaśobhitam \|*  
*makaragrāhakūrmādyairnānājalacarairvṛtam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jalāśayagataṃ devaṃ ciṃtayejjalaśāyinam \|*  
*tato nyāsaṃ prakurvīta pacāṃgatvāvaśobhitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

29-34. With the reciting of the mantra-“Rajadhirajena”, purification from the bhutas is done. Then in the middle of the water bubble, the lord is seated over white lotus seat, holding a conch, resembling the pure crystal gem, wearing the kirita crown issuing the lustre of white lotus or the moon, holding a white lotus, wearing a garland of white lotus flowers, with white complexion of the body over which the white paste had been applied. He is seated over the seat of a serpent hood. He holds a noose in his hand. He is being praised by the gods and served by the Siddhas and the Gandharvas. He has a beautiful face, adorned with the garland of lotus flowers. His eyes resembled the lotus flowers and is always respected in the Nagaloka. He is lodged in an ocean filled with crocodile, alligators, tortoises and other aquatic animals. He is lodged in the oceanic water. Thus meditating upon, the Pancanga-nyasa has to be performed.

## \|\| 2.40.35-38 \|\|

*arghyapātraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā tribhāgajalapūritam \|*  
*aṣṭadhā mūlamaṃtraṃ ca japtvā tenodakena ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*āsanaṃ yāgavastūni prokṣayettena vāriṇā \|*  
*aruṇāya vidmahe tamoghnāya ca dhīmahi \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tanno aruṇaḥ pracodayāditi snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*tato gaṇeśamaiśānyāmāgneyyāṃ gurupādukām \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dharmādharmādikānsarvāntsattvādīnatha cārcayet \|*  
*sūryasomajalādīnāṃ maṇḍalāni yathākramam \|\| 38 \|\|*

35-38. Then the oblation vase, the three-fourth part of which has been filled with water (should be lifted up) and reciting the mula-mantra eight times then the same water should be sprinkled upon over the seat as well as the other articles of the yajna, purifying them and uttering the mantra- “Arunaya vidmahe,” all the deities should be bathed including Ganesa lodged in the north-eastern corner, besides the preceptor’s sandals placed in the south-east should be worshipped, besides all the noble or evil elements has been desired. Similarly, the mandalas of the moon, Surya as well as Varuna should also be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.40.39-42 \|\|

*madhye śaktiṃ ca kṣīrodamanaṃtaṃ pṛthivīṃ tathā \|*  
*kūrmaṃ cādhāraśaktiṃ ca sumeruṃ mandaraṃ tathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pañcatattvaṃ samabhyarcya sāṃgopāgamanaṃtaram \|*  
*tataḥ śvetaṃ ca kusumaṃ sākṣataṃ yogamāyayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā pūrvavaddeśe sthāpayetkalaśopari \|*  
*āvāhanaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā mantreṇānena maṃtravit \|\| 41 \|\|*

*ehyehi bhagavanvaruṇa eṣa yajñaḥ pravartate \|*  
*yajñabhāgaṃ gṛhāṇedaṃ tvāmevāvāhayāmyaham \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-42. In the middle part, Sakti, the ocean of milk, serpent Ananta, the earth goddess, tortoise, Sumeru and Mandara mountains, and Panca-tattvas have also to be worshipped with full devotion. Then in the eastern region, the goddess Yogamaya lodged over the kalasa in the eastern region should be worshipped, offering to her the white flowers as well as the unbroken rice with the mantra which means, “O lord Varuna, come here, come here, the yajha is going to start. You kindly accept your part of the yajna. I am invoking you for the same purpose.”

## \|\| 2.40.43 \|\|

*evamāvāhya lokeśamaṣṭau mudrāḥ pradarśayet \|*  
*gāyatryā snāpayitvā tu dadyātpādyādikatrayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By thus invoking Varuna, the Lokesa should be shown the eight hand signs (hand mudras). Reciting the Gayatri mantra, the water for bath and padya should be offered.

## \|\| 2.40.44 \|\|

*puṣpāñjaliṃ tato dattvā mūlamaṃtreṇa deśikaḥ \|*  
*pūrvādipatramūleṣu dharmādīnpūjayedbudhaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Again the hand cup full of flowers should be offered and then the deities lodged over the tree leaves in the eastern and other sides including Dharma and gods, should also be worshipped by the concerned Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.40.45-47 \|\|

*sattvādyāḥ pūjayettatra teṣāmeva varāṃganāḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ dharmaṃ ca somaṃ ca rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamastathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*pūrvādipatramadhye tu grahānaṣṭau prapūjayet \|*  
*patrāgre lokapālānāmagnyā dīnāyudhāṃstathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*karṇikādakṣiṇe pūrvaṃ vāme cāpi śacīpatim \|*  
*pūrvapatre tu brahmāṇaṃ pūjayetsitapaṅkajaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Worshipping them with their wives, thereafter, Agnideva and Lokapalas lodged over the foreparts of the leaves besides other deities should be worshipped. Towards the southern part of the pericarp, initially towards the west, Indra, Stlrya and Brahma lodged over the leaves should be worshipped with white lotus flowers.

## \|\| 2.40.48-49 \|\|

*nairṛtye varuṇa syātha madhye'naṃtaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*pīṭhamantreṣu pūrvādibrahmāṇaṃ ca śivaṃ tathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*viṣṇuṃ cāpi gaṇeśaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ gaṃdhacandanaiḥ \|*  
*japenmantraṃ sāṣṭaśataṃ sahasraṃ vijapedbudhaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. To the south-east, Varupa is lodged; Ananta is in the middle; besides those lodged over the pedestal in the sequence of east etc. Brahma, Siva, Visnu, Gapesa and the earth goddess should be worshipped with fragrance and sandal paste. Thereafter, japam of the mantra a thousand and eight hundred times should be made, which is essential for a Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.40.50-55 \|\|

*jānubhyāmavanīṃ gatvā vijayākhyastavaṃ paṭhet \|*  
*īśānādipīṭhakoṇeṣu kamalāmaṃbikāṃ tathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*nairṛtyāṃ viśvakarmāṇaṃ vāyavye tu sarasvatīm \|*  
*pūrvādidvāradeśe tu marutaṃ cāvahādikam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*āvahaṃ pravahaṃ caiva tathaivodvahasaṃvahau \|*  
*vinyasetpaścime dvāri nivahaṃ ca parīvaham \|\| 52 \|\|*

*vinyaseduttaradvāri marutaṃ ca parābhavam \|*  
*āgneyādiṣu koṇeṣu bahiṣpīṭhaṃ tato jayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

*piśācānrākṣasānbhūtānvetālāṃśca tathā kramāt \|*  
*kṣobhakaḥ kāmarūpaśca saubhadro marutastathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*gomukho nandabhadraśca dvijihvo malinastathā \|*  
*hastikarṇo viśālākhyaḥ saptarakṣogaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

50-55. Kneeling with both the knees on earth, the Vijaya-stotra should be recited in the northeast and other comers of the pedestal, the deities like Kamala, Ambika in the south-west; Visvakarma, Sarasvati is in the north-west should be adored. The doorkeepers lodged in the eastern and other gates are known as Maruta, Avaha, Pravaha, Udvaha, Samvaha. On the western gate, the guards are known by the names of Nivaha, Parivaha; on the northern gate, the guards are known by the names of Maruta and Parabhava. All of them should be consecrated and worshipped. Then in the south-east comer, on the exterior, Pisacas, Raksasas, Bhutas (goblins) and Vetalas should be worshipped in a sequence. The seven Raksasa ganas are known by the names of - Ksobhaka, Kamarupa, Saubhadra, Maruta, Gomukha, Nandabhadra, Dvijihva, Malina, Hastikarna and Visala.

## \|\| 2.40.56 \|\|

*bhūmido varadaścaiva jayaṃtaḥ kṣobhakastathā \|*  
*vivasvaṃtaḥ sudaṃtaśca ete bhūtagaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The six bhutaganas are known by the names of Bhumida, Varada, Jayanta, Ksobhaka, Vivasvanta and Sudanta.

## \|\| 2.40.57 \|\|

*aṃgado nīlakarṇo'sau vasaṃto yāvakastathā \|*  
*ghorarūpā mahākāyaḥ vetālāśca prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Vetalas or goblins are also seven in number and are known by the name of Angada, Nila, Kama, Vasanta, Yavaka, Ghorarupa and Mahakaya.

## \|\| 2.40.58 \|\|

*gaṃdhapuṣpākṣatairbhaktaṃ sarve devā grahādayaḥ \|*  
*dhyānavarṇānurūpeṇa pūjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. All the gods and others grahas should be worshipped and offerings should be made to them as per their forms, with fragrance, flowers, unbroken rice and other things, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 2.40.59-61 \|\|

*dhyāyedādityamāraktaṃ raktapadmāsanasthitam \|*  
*raktāṃbaradharaṃ raktaṃ raktamālyānulepanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yavavidrumasaṃkāśaṃ siṃdūrāruṇasaprabham \|*  
*ākṛṣṇeneti maṃtreṇa sthāpayetkalaśopari \|\| 60 \|\|*

*ihāgaccheti cāvāhya pādyārghyaiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ \|*  
*gaṃdhapuṣpādibhirbhaktyā pūjayettaṃ yathāvidhi \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. The god Adityadeva should be meditated upon, being of red complexion, seated over a red lotus flower, clad in red garments and wearing a rosary of red beads. His body is plastered with red paste, has the prabha-mandala of lustre of red vermilion. He should be invoked with the mantra- “Akrsneti and should be consecrated over the каlasа. Thereafter, uttering the mantra— “Ihagachheti" he should be invoked. Then, he should be worshipped offering padya, arghya and several types of perfumes and flowers, with devotion.

## \|\| 2.40.62 \|\|

*baliṃ ca lohitaṃ dadyātpāyasaṃ dadhikhaṃḍakam \|*  
*ghṛtaliptaṃ ca śālyannaṃ patākāṃ raktavarṇikām \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then the offering of red colour, payasam, curd, sugar, ghi, mixed fall rice which is well-cooked, should also be presented to the god with a flag of red colour.

## \|\| 2.40.63-66 \|\|

*śvetāṃbaradharaṃ śvetaṃ śuklagaṃdhānu lepanam \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ varadaṃ devaṃ gadāhastaṃ mahābalam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇasaṃpannaṃ siddhagaṃdharvasevitam \|*  
*śuklapadmāsanasthaṃ cāśvaṃ dadyācchvetabhūṣitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*imaṃ devā iti maṃtreṇa sthāpayetpūrvadigdale \|*  
*sitavastraiśca puṣpaiśca śuklamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pāyasaiḥ śvetabalibhirdadhibhaktaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*dhūpaiḥ śvetapatākābhirnaivedyairvividhairapi \|\| 66 \|\|*

63-66. The god of white complexion, clad in white garments, plastered with white paste, having two arms, displaying varada mudra and a club in hands, adorned with all the ornaments, served by the Siddhas and Gandharvas, lodged over the white lotus, should be offered a white horse decorated with white ornaments. Then reciting the mantra-“Imam Deva iti,” he should be established in the eastern direction. He should be offered white garments, white rosary, while paste, payasam and curd, besides incense, white flag and various types of red food items.

## \|\| 2.40.67-69 \|\|

*raktamālyāṃbaraṃ devaṃ raktābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*sucārunayanaṃ raktaṃ raktapadmāsanasthitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*kirīṭakuṃḍaladharaṃ meṣakaṃṭhaṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*varadaṃ yajñanāśaṃ ca śūlaśaktigadādharam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*sarvakāmapradaṃ devaṃ siddhagaṃdharvasevitam \|*  
*ciṃtayetparayā bhaktyā maṃgalaṃ dharaṇīsutam \|\| 69 \|\|*

67-69. Mangala - the Mars, wears a red rosary, red garments and ornaments, has beautiful eyes, is seated over the red lotus flowers. He is adorned with kirita crown besides the earrings. He has the neck of a sheep and four arms. He bestows boons and is the destroyer of the yajnas. His hand attributes also include the trident, sakti and club. He fulfills all the desires and is served by the Siddhas and Gandharvas. The planet Mangala - the son of the earth, should be thus meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.40.70-75 \|\|

*agnimīḷetimaṃtreṇa sthāpayedagnidigdale \|*  
*pūjayedraktapuṣpaiśca raktamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*dhūpai raktapatākābhirguḍabhaktanive danaiḥ \|*  
*atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ karṇikārasamaprabham \|\| 71 \|\|*

*rauhiṇeyaṃ mahākāyaṃ nīlanīrajalocanam \|*  
*praśāṃtavadanaṃ devaṃ pītavastraṃ caturbhujam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*khaṅgacarmadharaṃ tadvadgadāparaśudhāriṇam \|*  
*padmāsanagataṃ devaṃ pītapadmāsanasthitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇasaṃpūrṇaṃ mṛgendravaravāhanam \|*  
*udbudhyasveti maṃtreṇa yā myāṃ tu sthāpayedbudham \|\| 74 \|\|*

*pūjayedgandhapuṣpādyaiḥ pītagaṃdhānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*vastraiḥ pītapatākābhirbalibhiḥ kṛśarānvitaiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

70-75. Reciting the mantra- “Agni-mileti" the god should be established in the south-east direction. He should then be worshiped offering red flowers, red garland, red paste, incense, red flag and the sugarcane balls. He has the complexion of linseed flowers. He has the lustre of the lotus petals, has gigantic body. His eyes resemble the blue lotus. His face is extremely peaceful. He is clad in yellow garments. He has four arms and holds a sword, a shield, club and a battle-axe. He is seated over the yellow lotus seat. His body is decorated with various types of ornaments. He is having an excellent lion as his vehicle. Such a planet Budha - son of Rohini, should be lodged in the southern direction, reciting the mantra-“Udbudhyasveti.” He should be offered perfume, flowers, yellow fragrance paste, yellow garments, a flag of the same colour and mixed food.

## \|\| 2.40.76-79 \|\|

*pītavarṇaṃ guruṃ dhyāyetpītapadmāsanasthitam \|*  
*pītābharaṇasaṃpannaṃ pītavastraṃ caturbhujam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*varadaṃ daṃḍahastaṃ ca sākṣasūtrakamaṃḍalum \|*  
*pūjyamānaṃ sugaṃdharvaiḥ sendrairdevagaṇairapi \|\| 77 \|\|*

*bṛhaspataya iti maṃtreṇa nairṛtyāṃ diśi saṃsthitam \|*  
*pītacandanagaṃdhaiśca pītavastrādibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*dhūpaiḥ pītapatākābhiḥ pītodakanivedanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā puraṃdarapurohitam \|\| 79 \|\|*

76-79. The preceptor Brhaspati seated over the yellow lotus flowers, adorned with the ornaments of yellow colour, clad in a yellow lower garment, possess four arms displaying the rosary, varada-mudra, a danda, rosary of Rudraksa, and should be meditated upon reciting the mantra- “Brhaspataya iti,” who is adored by the Devas, having the yellow complexion. He should be meditated upon and established in the south-west direction and should be offered the yellow sandal paste, perfume, yellow costumes and ornaments, incense, and a yellow flag. Then he should worship the priest or the preceptor like Indra.

## \|\| 2.40.80-91 \|\|

*dhyāyecchukraṃ bhṛgusutaṃ śvetapadmāsanasthitam \|*  
*caturbhujaṃ mahākāyaṃ varadaṃ daṃḍadhāriṇam \|\| 80 \|\|*

*mahābāhuṃ viśālākṣaṃ sākṣasūtrakamaṃḍalum \|*  
*stūyamānaṃ muniśreṣṭhaiḥ sevitaṃ daityapuṅgavaiḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*siṃhāsanagataṃ devaṃ nīlendīvaralocanam \|*  
*vilasatpuṇḍarīkasya mālābhirupaśobhitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*nānādaityendraputrāṃśca pāṭhayantaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*nānāśastrāstracaturaṃ nānāśāstraviśāradam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*evaṃ dhyātvā bhṛguśreṣṭhaṃ japannannātparisrutam \|*  
*manasā bhaktiyuktena sthāpayetpaścime dale \|\| 84 \|\|*

*sitacaṃdanavastraiśca dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*dhūpaiḥ śvetapatākābhiḥ saktubhiḥ kṣīrasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā puṃḍarīkākṣatairapi \|*  
*dhyāyetsauriṃ caturbāhuṃ śūlahastaṃ varapradam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*indranīlanibhaṃ śyāmaṃ divya bāṇadhanurdharam \|*  
*indīvarāsanasthaṃ ca sarojavarasaprabham \|\| 87 \|\|*

*nīlāṃbaradharaṃ nīlapadmamālopaśobhitam \|*  
*ghorarūpaṃ mahākāyaṃ chāyāhṛdayanandanam \|\| 88 \|\|*

*śannodevīti maṃtreṇa vāyavyāṃ diśi vinyaset \|*  
*kṛṣṇacaṃdanavastraiśca kṛṣṇamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*dhūpairnīlapatākābhirbalibhirmāṣamiśritaiḥ \|*  
*dhūmravarṇaṃ sadā ketuṃ gadāhastaṃ varapradam \|\| 90 \|\|*

*dvibhujaṃ bhīmakāyaṃ ca dhūmrākṣaṃ dhūmravāsasam \|*  
*ketuṃ kṛṇvanniti mantreṇa aiśā nyāṃ sthāpayeddiśi \|\| 91 \|\|*

80-91. Thereafter, four-armed Sukradeva seated over white lotus seat, having gigantic body and long arms falling upto the knees, displaying the varada-mudra and a danda as attribute, having vast eyes, holding a rosary of Rudraksa as well as the kamandalu, being praised by the best of the race of Bhrgu and the son of the sage Bhrgu, should be meditated upon, uttering the mantra - “Annatparisrutam iti”. Concentrating one’s mind, he should be established in the western direction. Then the white sandal paste, incense, garland, paste, white flag, the powdered cereal mixed in milk and lotus flowers should be offered, besides unbroken rice should be offered to him with devotion. Thereafter, four-armed Saturn, holding a trident in his hand, who is bestower of boons, having the complexion of sapphire, holding the divine bow and arrow, seated over the blue lotus flower, having the lustre of the louts flower, clad in blue garments, having a terrific form, the one who had delighted the goddess Chaya, such a Saturn - the son of Surya, should be consecrated reciting the mantra- “Sanna deviti” and he should be established in the north-west direction in an appropriate manner. He should be offered black sandal paste, black costumes, black garland, black paste, incense, blue flag and offering made of black grams. The planet Ketu has the complexion of smoke, holds a club in his hand and varada-mudra in both the hands. He has a gigantic body, has smoky eyes, clad in costume of smoke colour, who should always be consecrated in the north-east, reciting the mantra - “Ketum krnvanniti”

## \|\| 2.40.92-93 \|\|

*dhūmravarṇaiśca mālyaiśca dhūmragaṃdhānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*dhūmradhūmrapatākābhirbalibhirmāṣamiśritaiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā ketuṃ sarvārthasiddhidam \|*  
*lokapālānahaṃ vakṣye sarvasiddhipradāyakān \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. A garland of the colour of smoke and fragrance, besides the paste, the flag of the smoke colour and offering mixed with the black gram should be offered for the achieving of all the success with devotion to the planet Ketu adoring him at the same time. Now I am speaking about the method of worship of the Lokapalas, who bestow all the success.

## \|\| 2.40.94-97 \|\|

*yeṣu pūjitamātreṣu nālabhyaṃ vidyate kvacit \|*  
*devarājaṃ tato dhyāyetpuṣpabāṇacayaprabham \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ pītasaṃkāśaṃ nīlendīvaralocanam \|\| 94 \|\|*

*raktotpaladharaṃ tadvatpītavāsasamanvitam \|*  
*cāmarāsaktahastaiśca kanyāratnaiśca śobhitam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*indrāṇīṃ ciṃtayedvāme utpaladvayadhāriṇīm \|*  
*evaṃ saṃpūjayedbhaktyā surarājaṃ jagatprabhum \|*  
*trātāramiti mantreṇa sthāpayetkarṇikottare \|\| 96 \|\|*

*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā dhṛpagaṃdhānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*nānāvidhopahāraiśca patākābhirdhvajairapi \|\| 97 \|\|*

94-97. By worshipping them, nothing remains beyond the reach of a person. One achieves the complexion as bright as the lord Kamadeva, two arms and yellow complexion. Then Indra having the eyes resembling the blue lotus flowers has to be meditated upon, who carries the red lotus flowers, clad in a pitambara, holding a flywhisk in his hand, served by the young girls. Indrani - the spouse of Indra, stands to the left of Indra and she should also be worshipped with meditation. Thus Indra -the lord of the universe, should be worshipped with devotion. Thereafter, the incense, lamp, fragrance, paste, various food items, the flag and banners of various types should be offered, while concluding his worship.

## \|\| 2.40.98-102 \|\|

*baliṃ kṣīrānvitaṃ dadyānmodakaṃ sitaśarkarām \|*  
*uttaptasvarṇasaṃkāśaṃ vītihotraṃ caturbhujam \|\| 98 \|\|*

*ardhacandrasamasthaṃ ca ajavāhanamuttamam \|*  
*jvālāvitānasaṃraktaṃ mūrdhni saptaśikhānvitam \|\| 99 \|\|*

*varadaṃ vibhayaṃ mālāṃ dakṣe sūtraṃ kamaṇḍalum \|*  
*trinetraṃ raktanayanaṃ jaṭāmukuṭamaṃḍitam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇasaṃpannaṃ siddhagandharvasevitam \|*  
*agnijihveti maṃtreṇa snāpayedagnidigdale \|\| 101 \|\|*

*pūjayedraktapuṣpaiśca raktamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*dhūpai raktapatākābhirbalibhiḥ pāyasairapi \|\| 102 \|\|*

98-102. The offerings should include payasam with sweet balls and white sugar. His four arms resemble the molten gold or the crescent moon. The goat is his vehicle. He looks red with various types of fire flames. His head is decorated with seven tufts. He bestows boons, free from fear, holding a rosary, garland of beads, having three red eyes, his head is adorned with the matted locks of hair, is served by the Siddhas and Gandharvas. The Fire-god of the southern direction should be worshipped reciting the mantra- “Agnijihveti” and his image should be consecrated and bathed. Thereafter, he is to be bathed offering red flowers, fragrance, incense, as well as the payasam. The red flag should also be offered and the worship should be concluded.

## \|\| 2.40.103-109 \|\|

*nīlāñjanacayaprakhyaṃ nīlasiṃhāsanasthitam \|*  
*mahāmahiṣamārūḍhaṃ daṃḍapāśadhara vibhum \|\| 103 \|\|*

*karālavadanaṃ bhīmaṃ jvālā ghūrṇitalocanam \|*  
*ghoradaṃṣṭrākarālaiśca kiṃkarāṇāṃ gaṇairvṛtam \|*  
*mahiṣaṃ ciṃtayedvāme citraguptaṃ ca dakṣiṇe \|\| 104 \|\|*

*acchīyasa iti maṃtreṇa sthāpayedyamadigdale \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā dharmarājaṃ jagadgurum \|*  
*rākṣasendraṃ mahākāyaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ dvibāhukam \|\| 105 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇasaṃpannaṃ khaṅgahastaṃ mahāba lam \|*  
*varamuktāvimānasthaṃ ghorarūpaṃ jaleśvaram \|\| 106 \|\|*

*eṣa ta iti maṃtreṇa nairṛtyāṃ sthāpayeddiśi \|*  
*kṛṣṇacandanavastraiśca kṛṣṇamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*dhūpaiḥ kṛṣṇapatākābhirbalibhirmāṣamiśritaiḥ \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ śaṃkhakundendusaprabham \|\| 108 \|\|*

*dvibhujaṃ pāśahastaṃ ca sundarāṅgaṃ varapradam \|*  
*varuṇasyeti maṃtreṇa sthāpayetpaścime dale \|\| 109 \|\|*

103-109. Yama - the god of death, who has the complexion of blue collyrium, seated over a simhasana or a lion throne, riding over a great he-buffalo, carrying a danda in his hand, having a terrific face, an awful eyebrow, the eyes have the flames issuing from them, has awful and terrific horns and teeth. He is surrounded by the attendants. The he-buffalo is on the left side, while Citragupta appears to his right. He should be worshipped in the southern direction. Reciting the mantra-“Acchiyasa iti", a person with utmost devotion, should meditate upon Dharmaraja -the preceptor of the world, worshipping him at the same time. Thereafter, Nairrti who happens to be the Indra of the Raksasas, having a gigantic body and black complexion, two arms, adorned with ornaments of various types, holding a sword in his hand, the valorous one should be meditated upon. Varuna whose plane is decorated with the best of beads, is seated over it. He has a terrific form. He is the lord of waters. He should be adored reciting the mantra - “Esa-te-iti” and the image should be consecrated in the southwest. He should be offered the black sandal paste, black costumes, black rosary, paste, incense, flag of black colour and the offering mixed with black gram. Then having the complexion like the spotless pure crystal gem and the lustre of white lotus flowers, having conch and the moon, having two arms in which he carries two splinters of noose, having the beautiful limbs, granter of boons, should be worshipped towards the west, uttering the mantra- “Varunasyeti.”

## \|\| 2.40.110-113 \|\|

*sitacandanadhūpaiśca patākābhirdhvajairapi \|\| 110 \|\|*

*samīraṇaṃ kuñjaravarṇasannibhaṃ mṛgādhirūḍhaṃ dvibhujaṃ dvinetram \|*  
*dhvajāṃbaraṃ cāpi dadhānamekaṃ nīlāṃbaraṃ meghagaṇairvṛtaṃ ca \|\| 111 \|\|*

*nīlacandanavastraiśca nīlamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā patākābhirdhvajairapi \|\| 112 \|\|*

*dhūpairnīlapatākābhirbalibhiḥ pāyasairapi \|\| 113 \|\|*

110-113. He should be worshipped offering the incense, white sandal paste, flag and banner. Thereafter, the Wind-god, having the complexion of an elephant, riding over a stag, having two arms, two eyes, wearing the blue garments and blue flag, served by the clouds, such a Wind-god should be worshipped with blue sandal paste, costumes, rosary, paste, flag, banner, incense, blue flag, besides the payasam as a present. Thea he should be meditated upon.

## \|\| 2.40.114-119 \|\|

*dhyāyeddvinetraṃ dvibhujaṃ dhaneśaṃ pītāṃbaraṃ vai naravāhanaṃ ca \|*  
*gadādharaṃ bhaktavarapradaṃ ca āvāhayeduttarapadmapatre \|\| 114 \|\|*

*gandhacaṃdanavastraiśca pītamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*dhūpaiḥ pītapatākābhirbalibhiḥ pāyasairapi \|\| 116 \|\|*

*snigdhakarpūrasaṃkāśaṃ tuṣārakiraṇaprabham \|*  
*triśūlatumburudharaṃ tathābhayavarapradam \|\| 117 \|\|*

*uttaṃgavṛṣabhārūḍhaṃ trinetraṃ bhasmabhūṣitam \|*  
*kapālamālinaṃ tadvatkhaṇḍeṃdukṛtaśekharam \|\| 118 \|\|*

*evaṃ dhyātvā maheśānaṃ sthāpayedīśadigdale \|\| 119 \|\|*

114-119. Then the two-armed, two-eyed Kubera should be adored. He should have a human as a carrier. He holds a gada and grants boon to his devotees. He should be seated over the lotus flowers towards the north. Then he should be worshipped offering sandal paste, yellow rosary and paste besides the incense, yellow flag and offering of payasam Then lord Siva should be meditated upon. He has the complexion of camphor, the lustre of the snow, carries a trident as well as a musical pipe of hollow gourd, bestower of protection, riding over the bull Nandi, with considerable height. He has three eyes, has the body plastered with ashes, is adorned with a garland of human skulls. His head is adorned with a crescent moon. He should thus be meditated upon. He should then be consecrated in the north-east direction over a lotus leaf.

## \|\| 2.40.120-121 \|\|

*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā bhakṣyabhojyairanekaśaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*sitadhvajapatākābhirbalibhiḥ pāyasādibhiḥ \|*  
*tvamīśāna iti maṃtreṇa ṛṣiṃ chandaḥ samīrayan \|\| 121 \|\|*

120-121. Several types of eatables, a flag of white colour, besides the offering of payasam should be made. The worship should then be concluded with the reciting of- “Tvamlsana-iti” mantra with devotion.

## \|\| 2.40.122-127 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ raktagaurāgaṃ śoṇa padmasamaprabham \|*  
*rājīvalocanaṃ tadvatpadmagarbhasamaprabham \|\| 122 \|\|*

*padmāsanasthitaṃ tadvacchvetavastraṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*caturmukhaṃ suraśreṣṭhaṃ meghagambhīranisvanam \|\| 123 \|\|*

*rājahaṃsasamāyuktaṃ vimānavarasaṃsthitam \|*  
*sruksruvau dakṣiṇe haste vāme daṃḍaṃ kamaṇḍalum \|\| 124 \|\|*

*kurvāṇamiva lokāṃstrīnsiddhagandharvasevitam \|*  
*ājyasthālīṃ tathaivāgre kuśāṃśca samidhaṃ tathā \|\| 125 \|\|*

*vāmapārśve tu sāvitrīṃ dakṣiṇe tu sarasvatīm \|*  
*ābrahmanniti maṃtreṇa sthāpayetpūrva digdale \|\| 126 \|\|*

*nānābhakṣyopacāraiśca pūjayedgaṃdhacandanaiḥ \|*  
*dhūpaiḥ śvetapatākābhirbalibhiścājyapāyasaiḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

122-127. Then four-armed Brahma - the best among the gods, who has the complexion of red and white, the lustre of the red lotus flowers, the eyes resembling the lotus flowers, who is seated over a lotus seat, is clad in white garments. His four faces resemble the cloud and the speech is quite sober. He is seated in a plane, driven by the swans. He holds Sruka and Sruva in his right hand and in his left hand, he holds a danda as well as the kamandalu. While creating the lokas, he is being served by the Siddhas and the Gandharvas. The vase of ghi and the kusa grass have been placed in front of him, besides the burning sticks. The goddess Sarasvati stands to his right, while Savitri stands to his left Brahma - the best of the gods, should be worshipped reciting the mantra-“Abrahmannitr mantra. Reciting this mantra, BrahmS - the foremost of the gods, should be lodged to the eastern direction, seated over a lotus leaf. Thereafter, he should be offered the eatables, fragrant sandal paste, incense, white flag, besides the offering of payasam mixed with ghi. He should then be worshipped in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 2.40.128-139 \|\|

*anantaśuklavarṇābhaṃ pītavastraṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*śaṃkhacakragadāpadmadhāriṇaṃ jagadīśvaram \|\| 128 \|\|*

*ādhārabhūtaṃ jagatāṃ svarṇayajñopavītinam \|*  
*nānābharaṇasampannaṃ phaṇāśatasamanvitam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*oṃ namostviti maṃtreṇa sthāpayedvaruṇāṃtare \|*  
*pūjayedbhakṣyabhojyaiśca dīpagandhānulepanaiḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

*dhūpaiḥ śvetapatākābhirbalibhiścaiva nirmitaiḥ \|*  
*tato maṇḍalapūrve tu brahmāṇaṃ pītavāsasam \|\| 131 \|\|*

*caturbhujaṃ caturvaktraṃ sruvahastaṃ varapradam \|*  
*bibhrataṃ ca śrutaṃ tadvattathā daṃḍakamaṇḍalū \|\| 132 \|\|*

*ābrahmanniti mantreṇa pūjayedgandhacandanaiḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇe tryaṃbakaṃ dhyāyecchūlakhaṭvāṃdhāriṇam \|\| 133 \|\|*

*varadaṃ ḍamarudharaṃ nāgayajñopavītinam \|*  
*nibaddha jṛṭacandrārdhaṃ śuddhasphaṭikasannibham \|\| 134 \|\|*

*kapālamālinaṃ devaṃ bhujaṃgābharaṇānvitam \|*  
*trinetraṃ kundasaṃkāśaṃ bhūtapretagaṇairvṛtam \|\| 135 \|\|*

*tryaṃbakaṃ ceti mantreṇa pūjayenmadhupāyasaiḥ \|*  
*atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ hārakeyūrabhūṣitam \|\| 136 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇasaṃpannaṃ pītavastraṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*dakṣiṇe ca gadāṃ cakraṃ vāme śaṃkhaṃ sapadmakam \|\| 137 \|\|*

*śriyā dakṣiṇato vāme sarasvatyā samanvitam \|*  
*tadviṣṇoriti maṃtreṇa sthāpayetpaścime tataḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

*pūjayedgandhapuṣpādyaiḥ pāyasena ghṛtena ca \|*  
*gaṇeśaṃ tu caturbāhuṃ vyālayajñopavītinam \|\| 139 \|\|*

128-139. Lord Ananta, who is of white complexion, clad in a pitambara, having four arms, holding a sankha (conch), cakra (a disc), gada (a club) besides a lotus in four arms as the attributes, is the leader of the universe, the base of the world, who is adorned with a yajnopavita of golden colour. He has hundreds of Brahmas with him. Such a lord Ananta should be worshipped reciting the mantra- “Оm namostvit" and Varuna should be consecrated in the centre. Thereafter, the eatables, lamp, fragrance, paste, incense and the white flag should be offered to him, while worshipping him. He should be lodged in the eastern part of the masala. He has four faces and four arms. He holds a sruva, varada-mudra, the Vedas, besides the danda and a kamandalu. Then reciting the mantra— “Abrahmanniti” he should be worshipped. In his right hands, he should hold a trident, a khatvanga, varada-mudra and damaru. A serpent should be sewed him as a yajnopavita. The crescent moon should adorn his matted locks of hair. He should wear the garland of pure crystal skulls. The serpents should serve as his ornaments. He should be of three eyes resembling the lotus flowers and should be surrounded by the spirits and the goblins. This god should be adored with the reciting of the mantra “Trayambakam iti” and offering to him the honey, payasam etc. He has the complexion of the linseed flowers and should be adorned with a garland, armlets and several other ornaments. He should be clad in yellow garments. He should have four arms. In the right hands, he should hold a gada ana a cakra. In the left hands, he should hold a conch and a lotus. Laksmi should stand to his south and on his left stands Sarasvati He should be adored by reciting the mantra - “Tadvisnoriti” He should be worshipped facing west, offering fragrance, flowers, payasam with ghi, besides other eatables. He should thus be worshipped.

## \|\| 2.40.140-142 \|\|

*gajendravadanaṃ devaṃ śvetavastraṃ caturbhujam \|*  
*paraśuṃ laguḍaṃ vāme dakṣiṇe daṃḍamutpalam \|\| 140 \|\|*

*mūṣakasthaṃ mahākāyaṃ śaṅkhakundeṃdusaprabham \|*  
*yuktaṃ buddhikubuddhibhyāmekadaṃtaṃ bhayāpaham \|\| 141 \|\|*

*nānābharaṇasaṃpannaṃ sarvāpattivināśanam \|*  
*gaṇānāṃ tviti mantreṇa vinyaseduttare dhruvam \|\| 142 \|\|*

140-142. Lord Ganesa should be adored, who has four arms, wears a serpent as a yajnopavita, has the face of an elephant and is clad in white garments. He holds a battle axe and a stick in both his left hands, besides a danda and a lotus in the right hands. He is mounted over a mouse, with a gigantic body and has a complexion of lotus flowers or the moon. He is accompanied with Subuddhi and Durbuddhi and has a single tusk and a terrific appearance. He is adorned with various types of ornaments. He removes all the obstructions. Such a Ganesa should be consecrated towards the north reciting the mantra- “Gandnam tviti”.

## \|\| 2.40.143-145 \|\|

*uttaptajāṃbūnadahemasannibhāṃ lakṣmīṃ sarojāsanasaṃsthitāṃ śubhām \|*  
*vāme sarojaṃ dadhatīṃ tathaiva haste ca dakṣe dhṛtacāmarāṃ ca \|\| 143 \|\|*

*śrīśca teti ca mantreṇa aiśānyāṃ maṃḍalādbahiḥ \|*  
*sthāpayetpūjayedbhaktyā sitacandana paṅkajaiḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

*modakaṃ paramānnaṃ ca yavakṣīraṃ nivedayet \|\| 145 \|\|*

143-145. Laksmi has the complexion of the molten gold and is seated over the lotus seat. She holds lotus in the left hand and the flywhisk in the right hand. She should be made to stand in the north-east direction outside the mandala, reciting the mantra - “Sri Sakti”, offering the white sandal paste, besides the lotus, sweet balls, excellent eatables, payasam of barley and other edible stuff. She should then be worshipped accordingly.

## \|\| 2.40.146-151 \|\|

*tato devīmaṃbikāṃ divyarūpāṃ brahmeṃdrādyaiḥ stūyamānāṃ trinetrām \|*  
*siṃheśasthāṃ taptajāṃbūnadābhāṃ candrārddhenābaddhamauliṃ jaṭābhiḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

*divyairvastrairbāhubhiḥ sāgralambairdivyairmālyairbhūṣaṇaiḥ svairupetām \|*  
*brahmeṃdrādyairdurjayāṃ māhiṣāsyaṃ tīkṣṇairastrairdānavaṃ mardayaṃtīm \|\| 147 \|\|*

*śūlaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ bāṇaśaktī ca tīkṣṇe khaḍgaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ bibhratīṃ dakṣiṇena \|*  
*cāpaṃ pāśaṃ kheṭakaṃ cāṃkuśaṃ ca ghaṇṭāṃ vāme bibhratīṃ vai kuṭhāram \|\| 148 \|\|*

*śiraśchedādardhajātaṃ kabandhaṃ khaḍgaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ bibhratīṃ daityarājam \|*  
*nāgaiḥ pāśairveṣṭayitvā samaṃ tācchūlenainaṃ nighnatīṃ dehamadhye \|\| 149 \|\|*

*sendrairdevaiḥ stūyamānāṃ suveṇīṃ gaṃdharvādyaiḥ siddhasaṃghaiśca sevyām \|*  
*nānāvastrairbhūṣaṇairdīpyamānāṃ dhyāyeddevīmaṃbikāmujvalaṃtīm \|\| 150 \|\|*

*vastrairmālyairyakṣadhūpairvitānairbhakṣyairbhojyairmodakaiḥ pāyasaiśca \|*  
*māṃsaiḥ piṣṭaiśchāgalāḍhyairaśeṣaiḥ pūjyā devī caṃḍikā'bhīṣṭadā ca \|\| 151 \|\|*

146-151. Thereafter, the goddess Ambika, having the divine form, who is eulogised by Brahma and other gods, should be worshipped. She has three eyes, mounted over the lion, having the lustre of the molten gold, whose body is decorated with crescent moon, with matted locks of hair well-arranged over the head and decorated with a crescent. She is clad in divine garments, has the arms falling upto the knees. She is decorated with divine garlands and is invincible by Indra and other gods. She is the one who killed Mahisasura, with the use of her sharp weapons and holds a trident in her right hands besides an arrow, a Sakti, sharp-edged sword. In her left hands, she holds a sharp edged sword, a bow, splinter of a noose, khetaka, goad, a bell and the battle axe, besides the head of the demon, which was cut off with the strike of the sword. She bound the daitya with the serpent noose and attacked him in the chest with a trident. She is eulogised by the gods like Indra and others. She has a beautiful vent. She is served by the groups of Siddhas and Gandharvas. She wears several types of costumes and ornaments. Such a goddess Ambika should be meditated upon and then the costumes, garlands, incense, canopy, eatables like the sweet balls, payasam, meat of a he-goat when offered to her, yields the desired result. Such a goddess Candika should be adored.

## \|\| 2.40.152-160 \|\|

*śyāmāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ dhyāyetpaṃkajadvayadhāriṇīm \|\| 152 \|\|*

*maṇḍūkasthāṃ dvibhujāṃ syonā pṛthivīti cārcayet \|*  
*nairṛtyāṃ viśvakarmāṇaṃ dvibhujaṃ ṭaṃkadhāriṇam \|\| 153 \|\|*

*utpalaṃ dakṣiṇe haste padmasthaṃ pītavāsasam \|*  
*evaṃ dhyātvā tato brahmanniti maṃtreṇa pūjayet \|\| 154 \|\|*

*svasthāṃ sarasvatīṃ dhyāyedvaradābhayadāyinīm \|*  
*pītavastrāṃ sumukuṭāṃ devagandharvasevitām \|\| 155 \|\|*

*yāmadhā iti mantreṇa pūjayetsitacaṃdanaiḥ \|*  
*baliṃ śveta caruṃ dadyātkṛśaraṃ yāvakaṃ tathā \|\| 156 \|\|*

*sthāpayedvāmadigbhāge kuṃdapuṣpaiḥ prapūjayet \|*  
*pūrvādidvāradeśe tu pūjayecca marudgaṇaiḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

*agnyādiṣu ca koṇeṣu bahirbhūtānsamācaret \|*  
*piśācā rākṣasā bhūtā vetālakapijātayaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

*nirṇāsāścaiva te sarve raudrā vikṛtarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*tato maṇḍala madhye tu vāruṇaṃ pūrvavartmanā \|\| 159 \|\|*

*pūrayetkalaśe tatra suvarṇādivinirmitam \|*  
*kūrmaṃ kūrmākṛtiṃ kuryācchuddhasvarṇena sattamāḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

152-160. The Earth goddess carrying two lotus flowers, seated over a frog, has the complexion of smoke, and should be worshipped reciting the mantra- “Syamam ca prthivi.” Thereafter, Visvakarma, who is lodged in the south-west having two arms, holding a chisel in the hand and a lotus in the right hand, who is seated over a lotus seat and is clad in yellow garments, such a Visvakarma should be meditated upon, uttering the mantra - “Brahmanniti.” Thereafter, he should be eulogised. The goddess Sarasvati, with a healthy physique, who bestows boon as well as shelter, should be meditated upon reciting “Yamadha" mantra. Then the white sandal paste, havi, mixed cereals paste and other eatables should be offered to her. She should be established towards the left. Then she should be adored offering the golden flowers. The gods with Marudganas lodged over the eastern gates, besides the Raksasas and Pisacas lodged in the exterior of the south eastern direction, the goblins, vetalas and those who are without noses, terrific in appearance, besides being deformed, should be adored. Thereafter, a golden pitcher filled with water should be placed and Varuna should be worshipped in that form. Then, a figure of tortoise made in gold, should be placed in the said pitcher.

## \|\| 2.40.161-165 \|\|

*bṛhatparva pramāṇena rājatasya ca durlabham \|*  
*pādaṃ pādena mānena aṃgulaṃ parimaṇḍalam \|\| 161 \|\|*

*prauṣṭhīmatsyaṃ tathā kuryātkulīraṃ tāmranirmitam \|*  
*tenaikasya vinirmāṇaṃ dvyaṃgulāyāmavistṛtam \|\| 162 \|\|*

*tathā mānena maṇḍūkaṃ tāṃ bhūmiṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*śiśumāraṃ ca vai samyaktolakadvayanirmitam \|\| 163 \|\|*

*aṃgulatrayadīrghaṃ ca yathā tasyākṛtirbhavet \|*  
*sitacandanavastraiśca pūjanīyāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*yāvakaiśca viśeṣeṇa bahumaṃtraviśāradān \|*  
*bahvṛcau pūrvamatsyārthe dakṣiṇe tu yajurvidau \|\| 165 \|\|*

161-165. Its circumference should be equal to the knuckle of a finger. It could be made of silver as well. Its length should be equal to that of a crab and its length and breadth should be equal to that of two fingers and could be made of copper as well. Thereafter, an image of porpoise of the size of a frog should be made weighing two tolas, which should be three fingers in width. It should be covered from all the sides with the white sandal paste as well as the white cloth and then it should be worshipped. To the south of the figure, the two Brahmanas, well-versed in Yajurveda, should be lodged.

## \|\| 2.40.166-171 \|\|

*sāsanau paścime cātha uttare'tharvaṇau smṛtau \|*  
*jayadhvamiti tānbrūyāddhotṛkānpunareva hi \|\| 166 \|\|*

*sthāpayitvā pṛthaksūtre sarpaṃ ca mātaruddīpameva ca \|*  
*pañcāṃgaṃ śivasūktaṃ ca yathā viṣṇorharasya ca \|\| 167 \|\|*

*jayāgrataḥ puruṣasūktamadbhyaḥ saṃbhūtameva ca \|*  
*āśuḥ śiśānamārabhya vayaṃ moṣāṃgarudrake \|\| 168 \|\|*

*yajjāgrataścāgneśca viṣṇorarāṭameva ca \|*  
*samastādhyāyarudreṇa śatarudrākhyamīritam \|\| 169 \|\|*

*home pravartamāne tu ūktānanāśca vai japet \|*  
*prajapadrāsaṇaṃ sūktaṃ tathā ca pālṛktakam \|\| 170 \|\|*

*rātrisūktaṃ ca raudraṃ ca pādamānaṃ samucjvalam \|*  
*japecca pausbaṃ saktaṃ saravatovarataṃ pṛthak \|\| 171 \|\|*

166-171. Towards the west, two seats should be placed and towards the north also, two seats should be placed for those who are well-versed in the Atharvaveda, uttering the words “Jayadhvajam”. Then like the serpents who enrage their mothers, the Siva-sukta as well as Purusa-sukta should be recited with Pancanga in the same way as is done for the sake of Siva or Visnu. Starting from the mantra - “Yajjagrata iti” from Purusa-sukta upto the mantra- “Vayam mosanga Rudrake” upto “Asuh-sisana iti” should be recited. Thereafter, then “Visno-rarat-iti” mantra should be recited together with the recitation of “Rudradhyaya” which is well known and popular as Rudradhyayi or Satarudri. Pancanga Rudra has Puspadanta as the Rsi; Gayatri is the meter; Vedaham is the seed; Srischate is sakti; “Namaste Rudra-iti is the leader; and Parama Rudra is the Devata. In the supreme prayer, Viniyoga is made use of. Then Saptanga Rudra uttering Trayambakamiti, the thumb is to be touched; uttering Tripadurdhva, the forefinger is to be touched; then uttering Vedahaniti the middle finger is to be touched; saying Amisa citramiti the ring finger and while uttering Yavangu Soma iti, the little finger is to be touched. Uttering the verse Parito-dhanumiti, the back of the palm is to be touched, performing the nyasa. Similarly, the hrdya nyasa is also to be performed. Starting from the verse Yajjagrata iti, the heart is to be touched; reciting Sahasra-sirsa the head is to be touched; with the uttering of Adbhya sambhuti, the tuft is to be touched. Then uttering Namaste Rudra-iti the eyes have to be touched. Thereafter, the passage Rudham brahmanniti, Astraya phat should be spoken. Thereafter, the posture of Chotika should be displayed on all the sides. Similarly, this has been stated to be quite important because of the performance with all the limbs. At the start of the performing of the homa, the recitation of other Saktas is also said to be quite essential. Similarly, the recitation of Ratrisukta, Raudra, Samujjvala of Pavamana and of Purusasukta should also be made.

## \|\| 2.40.172-175 \|\|

*śāktaṃ raudram ca saumyaṃ ca kūṣmāṇḍaṃ jātavedasam \|*  
*g ca yajato dakṣiṇena yajuvidaḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

*vairājaṃ pauruṣaṃ g sauvarṇaṃ sadrasaṃhitām \|*  
*śaśava yañcanirayaṃ gāyatāṃ jyeṣṭhasāma ca \|\| 173 \|\|*

*vāmadevya bṛhatsāma tathā yaiva rathantaram \|*  
*godrataṃ ca vikarṇaṃ ca rodhanaṃ pāvanaṃ spṛtam \|\| 174 \|\|*

*gāyanta drāhmaṇā ye ca pūravādiśāradeśataḥ \|*  
*st iti pañcaparva sauramṛktakam \|\| 175 \|\|*

172-175. Besides a person who is well-versed in the Yajurveda should also recite Sukta, Raudra, Saumya, Jataveda, Saura, Yaja, Vairaja and Paurusa suktas, Sauvarni Rudra Samhita, Saisava-pancaniryam, Gayatri-jyestha-Sama, Vamadeva, Brhatsama, Rathantara, Govrata, and Vikarna. The recitation of the aforesaid text is instrumental in the destruction of the demon forces. They are also termed as the most auspicious ones. From the eastern gate, the Brahmanas should enter while reciting the Saura-Sukta.

## \|\| 2.40.176-180 \|\|

*sudradhyāyaṃ ca pañcāṅga raudra ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*āpyāyasveti dha catuḥ saumyam suttam pracadate \|\| 176 \|\|*

*īśovetyādi svāṅgaṃ ca kaupmāṇḍaṃ daśamaṃ spṛtam \|*  
*agre vṛhatniti navasūktaṃ vai jātavedasam \|\| 177 \|\|*

*ṣoḍaśaṃ tu vibhrāḍ vṛhatsaura sṛtaṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*saurasṛkta dhvosīti iṣavo maṅgalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 178 \|\|*

*rātrasūtraṃ hi yajvāna rakṣoghna śaivamūktakam \|*  
*-gaṇānānyeti pañca āpohiṣṭheti ca trayam \|\| 179 \|\|*

*pavamānaṃ tu tadviddhi pāvamānaṃ tu ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*samastaṃ devayāgeṣu tadrārau tu tadarvakam \|*  
*tadaddhādhaṃ ca ārāpe kūpe tvekaṛchacaṃ jayet \|\| 180 \|\|*

176-180. The Pancanga with Saumya-Sukta together with Isovetyadi parts are called the tenth Kausmanda. Then the Agravanti and others nine Suktas are called Jatavedas. The sixteenth Vibhrad Brhat iti is called the Saura-sukta. Dhruvositi is the welfare passage and is called the Ratri sukta. The Saiva sukta is called Raks oghna sukta, similarly the passage known as gananamtva and the five apohistheti, the three Pavamanas besides the sixteen Reds are called : Pavamanas. In all the Deva yajnas during the night, the upper part of the Rea should be recited at the time of setting up a well. In the setting up of a garden, one fourth of it should be recited; while during the digging up of a well a single Red should be recited.

## \|\| 2.40.175-188 \|\|

*gāyanta drāhmaṇā ye ca pūravādiśāradeśataḥ \|*  
*st iti pañcaparva sauramṛktakam \|\| 175 \|\|*

*sudradhyāyaṃ ca pañcāṅga raudra ityabhidhīyate \|*  
*āpyāyasveti dha catuḥ saumyam suttam pracadate \|\| 176 \|\|*

*īśovetyādi svāṅgaṃ ca kaupmāṇḍaṃ daśamaṃ spṛtam \|*  
*agre vṛhatniti navasūktaṃ vai jātavedasam \|\| 177 \|\|*

*ṣoḍaśaṃ tu vibhrāḍ vṛhatsaura sṛtaṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*saurasṛkta dhvosīti iṣavo maṅgalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 178 \|\|*

*rātrasūtraṃ hi yajvāna rakṣoghna śaivamūktakam \|*  
*-gaṇānānyeti pañca āpohiṣṭheti ca trayam \|\| 179 \|\|*

*pavamānaṃ tu tadviddhi pāvamānaṃ tu ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*samastaṃ devayāgeṣu tadrārau tu tadarvakam \|*  
*tadaddhādhaṃ ca ārāpe kūpe tvekaṛchacaṃ jayet \|\| 180 \|\|*

*svagṛhamoktavidhānena pratikuṇḍeṣu homayet \|*  
*saṃsakarādīkṣaṇācacaiśca sampūjya ca parasparam \|\| 181 \|\|*

*prajvālyāgni ca viṣivaddhoṣaṃ kuryādanantaram \|*  
*vāgīśvaraṃ samabhyacyaṃ vāgīśo samanvitam \|\| 182 \|\|*

*yasya devasya yo yāgaḥ pratiṣṭhā yasya kasyacit \|*  
*prāgeva tasya juhuyātsahasvaṃ ca śataṃ tathā \|\| 183 \|\|*

*tilājyaiḥ payasaurvatha patrapuspasatena ca*  
*grahebhyo vidhivatsarvaṃ tathenadrāyeśvarāya ca \|\| 184 \|\|*

*marudye lokapālebhyo vidhivadvakarmaṇe \|*  
*urjena samidhā kuryādaṣṭāṭau svagṛhaṣūvapi \|\| 185 \|\|*

*idedharamārutānāṃ tilājyena dhṛtena vā \|*  
*ekaikāmāhati dadyātah svurmamantrairyatharkamat \|\| 186 \|\|*

*digīśānāṃ ca pratyekamṭāṣṭau ca viroṣataḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmaniti manreṇa kṛtvā ācyāhutitrayam \|\| 187 \|\|*

*samitrayaṃ palāśasya athavāśvatyasambhavam \|*  
*ekaikāmāhuti dadayādājyena ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 188 \|\|*

175-188. According to the provision of several Grhyasutras texts, homa should be performed in each one of the fire altars. During the rites, with the recitation of Reds, Vagisvari and Vagisvara are to be worshipped performing the homa in the flames of the burning fire altar. The god for whose sake the yajna is performed, for his sake a hundred or a thousand offerings should be dropped in the fire altar initially. Sesamum seeds, ghi, payasam or leaves, flowers and unbroken rice should be appropriately offered to the planets, Indra, Marudganas, Lokapalas in the yajna fire. Similarly, for Visvakarma, eight sacrificial sticks should be poured in the fire and also for Indra, Isvara and Marudganas. An offering with ghi should also be poured for each one of the above gods. Eight offerings each should be poured in the fire for each one of Dikpalas. Then reciting the mantra Visvakarmanniti, three offerings of ghi should also be poured for them. Three yajna sticks of plasa or pipala tree should be offered thrice, soaked in ghi, which have been prescribed.

## \|\| 2.40.189-192 \|\|

*śivaṃ prajāpati viṇaṃ durgā ca kapalāpapi \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ ca viṣivatapṛthivayā iti pāvakaṃ: \|\| 189 \|\|*

*bhūteṣyo'yahati dadiva mamadyam kramat \|*  
*avyeṣāṃpayurāena tilalādhairayaṇākaramam \|\| 190 \|\|*

*viṣṇum caivaṃ tu vāyavye durgayasca tathettare*  
*kamalāyāsca īśāne īśānasya sabhūtakam \|\| 191 \|\|*

*ekakuṇaḍe tu ekasninhomam kuryadhathavidhi*  
*paksi vai pancakunde tu pūrvādāna krameṇa tu \|\| 192 \|\|*

189-192. Reciting the mantra Prthivyam iti, the offerings should be made appropriately. Similarly, for bhutas (goblins), for two months the sesamum seeds mixed with honey should be offered besides the fried paddy. Visnu should be lodged in the north-west zone; the goddess Durga in the north; and Kamala, in the north-west. For Siva with the ganas, homa should be performed collectively at one and the same time. The offerings should be dropped in the five fire altars. This has been prescribed.

## \|\| 2.40.193-194 \|\|

*ekakuṇḍe barahānkṛtvā kṛtvā balabhidā saha \|*  
*dakṣiṇe kramataścaivaṃ lokaca tethaiva śacaṃ \|\| 193 \|\|*

*paścime yasya yāgasya g durgayaksottare disi \|*  
*īśāne bhutayaksana ca juhuyadaśikottamaḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

193-194. In a single fire altar, offerings should be dropped for the sake of Indra and all the planets from the south, then the offering should be dropped for the Lokapalas in the west and the offerings should be poured for the main deity for whom the sacrifice is organised. Durga should be offered the offerings in the north. Thereafter, the offerings should be in favour of the deity for whom the yajna has been organised. The offerings should be made for Durga and Isana as well.

## \|\| 2.40.195-200 \|\|

*viṣvādidevatānāṃ ca agkuṇḍe vidhīyate \|*  
*prathame divase kuyadivatānāṃ ca sthāpanam \|*  
*dvitīye pūjanaṃ kuryāddhomaṃ kuryādyathāviṣi \|\| 195 \|\|*

*balidānaṃ tatīya tu catardhīkaṃ caturdhake \|*  
*nīrājanaṃ paccame tu pañcāhasādhyako vidhiḥ \|*  
*vahasya tṛtīye tu navāhe tvatha pañcame \|\| 196 \|\|*

*udaḍmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vāyaiśānyādikrameṇa tu \|*  
*prādakṣiṇyena yajñaṃ tu manaiḥ parisamūhanam \|*  
*manrapūvaṃ sāganikānā niramestuṣṭakina tu \|\| 197 \|\|*

*bikaśena mahāyāge vivāhādau davipatrakam \|*  
*vaiśvadeve tavekapatramiti sādhāraṇo vidhiḥ \|\| 198 \|\|*

*diṣvidikca paristīyaṃ mahāyāgeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*di mātraṃ nityake ca viśvadeve tathaiva ca \|\| 199 \|\|*

*kṛtvā karma nityaṃ ca vṛdhā naimittikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tasmākatatvā lanaiāmitdatakaṃ aicararat \|\| 200 \|\|*

195-200. Similarly, the offerings for the sake of Visnu and other gods has been prescribed to be dropped in the foreparts of the kunda. The deities are required to be consecrated at the proper places on the first day. On the second day, the worship of the deities as well as the homa has to be performed appropriately. The offerings have to be made on the third day, on the fourth day Caturthika should be performed and on the fifth day, the lights should be offered to the deities. This is the procedure for the performing of the yajna for five days. Similarly, the procedure for the performing of the yajna for three days has been prescribed. For the yajna of nine days, the yajna concluding ceremony is performed on the fifth day with the offering of the lights. Facing north or the east, with the sequence of the north-east direction, one should circumambulate in due order, reciting the mantras. The performer of the yajna should extinguish the fire in an appropriate manner. In the great yajnas, the ceremonies are concluded with three kusas; during the marriage ceremonies the conclusion is made with two leaves and in the Vaisvadeva ceremonies the conclusion is made with a single leaf. This has been prescribed in the ordinary procedures. In the great yajnas, the kusa grass is spread in all the directions and in the Vaisvadeva ceremonies, the kusa grass is spread in all the directions. The regular and casual performance should not be done. Because by so doing, the yajnas become infructuous. Therefore, the casual performances should be resorted to after the proper conclusion of the yajna.

## \|\| 2.40.201-206 \|\|

*parāycate vaiśvadeve sāyaṃprātaḥ pratīṣu ca \|\| 201 \|\|*

*māraṇoccāṭhomevu tathā saṅkalpitākṛtī \|*  
*pratyavāyakule vavāpi tatra nityākṛtiṃ vinā \|\| 202 \|\|*

*śatārdhaṃ juhuyādatara tatara nityaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*turyahomah tataḥ kṛtvā taṣṇīmeva jitiddhivaḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

*prajapedidramagni ca somāya ca yathākramam \|*  
*tatastu samidhāhomaṃ vyāhatidanantaram \|\| 204 \|\|*

*bhūrbhuvaḥ svāheti tathā tvanna ityādi pañcakam \|*  
*ante siviṣṭakṛte dadyāma tasya bhoḥ śaraṇu \|\| 205 \|\|*

*pṛtāhuti sviṣṭakṛcca dvijasaṃskāra karmasu \|*  
*pataiḥ sviṣṭakṛtaṃ dadayādyāgādau parivarjayet \|\| 206 \|\|*

201-206. The rites of daily routine are not required to be performed during the repentance rites, Vaisvadeva rites, the rites which are performed during the morning and evening, the rites for destruction of others and the homa rites or homas for separation or uprooting, besides during the activities relating to the destruction or obstructions, the routine prayers etc. are not to be performed. The same procedure has to be followed while pouring fifty offering in the homa. Thereafter, the performer, observing silence, after concluding of the homa for the Sungod, should perform japam for Indra, Agni and Soma, and pour offerings also in the fire, with yajna sticks.

Thereafter, he should pour the offering five times reciting the mantra bhur bhuvah svaheti and tvannaityadi and at the end, the Svistakrta homa should be performed, the procedure of which is being described by me. You please listen. During the Samaskara ceremonies of the Dvijas, the Svistakrta homa is required to be performed, pouring the offering of ghi. But during the performance of the rites like yajnas and others, the Svistakrta homa with the offering of ghi is strictly prohibited.

## \|\| 2.40.207-215 \|\|

*sarvauṣyudakasānaṃ karidantolayamuṣṇayā \|*  
*rathyāvalmīkagoṣṭhasya tathāśvasya śurasya ca \|\| 207 \|\|*

*trigakhaṃ ca vriśītaṃ ca kuśamūlasya pṛttikāḥ \|*  
*niksipetrananakunbhesu ācāryādīsatu sthāpayet \|\| 208 \|\|*

*yajamānaḥ puraḥ kṛtvā dantakāṣṭapuraḥ saram \|*  
*rātrau ca bhṣyabhojyādayaiḥ paritoṣya yavāṣatam \|\| 209 \|\|*

*kṛtvā yathoktakālena pujayettailadhārayā \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāte vimale snānaṃ karyāyathāvidhi \|\| 210 \|\|*

*snānamabaivairmanraḥ sūktena puruṣeṇa tu \|*  
*vāruṇena ca sūktena surāstvādi yathākramam \|\| 211 \|\|*

*surāsvāmabhiṣiñcanu brahaviṣṇumaheśavarāḥ \|*  
*vāsudevo jagannāthastathā saṅkarṣaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 212 \|\|*

*ākhaṇḍalonirbhagavānyamo vai nikaṛratistathā \|*  
*varuṇaḥ pavanaścaiva dhanādhyakṣastathā śivaḥ \|\| 213 \|\|*

*brahmaṇāṃ sahitaḥ śeṣo dikpālāḥ pāntu te sadā \|*  
*kirtirlakshmirdhutormedha puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā matiḥ \|\| 214 \|\|*

*buddhirlajjā vapuḥ śāntistuṣṭiḥ kāniśca mātaraḥ \|*  
*etāstvamabhiṣiñntu devapalyaḥ samāhitāḥ \|\| 215 \|\|*

207-215. One should be made to bathe with the water mixed with all the herbs. Besides the dust dug up with the tusk of the elephant, the hot sand of the street, sand collected by white ants, the earth of cowpens, the dust scratched with the hoofs of the horses, all the three types of fragrances, the three types of cooking things, the sand taken from the roots of the kusa grass, should also be mixed in the same water. Thereafter, the priest for the performing of the adoration should be selected. Then the worship should be completed. With the tooth sticks collected in one’s presence and served with other eatables, the Brahmanas should be fully pleased. Thereafter, the yajamana should take his bath with the water mixed with barley, rice and pouring the oil in water. Thus the bath should be performed in the early morning in an appropriate manner, while taking bath the Varuna mantras should be recited. Besides the recitation of Purusa sukta as well as Varuna sukta should be carried out for the purpose of abhiseka. Then the prayer of the gods should be thus made. Let the gods like Brahma, Visnu, Mahesvara, Vasudeva, Jagannatha, Sankarsana, Prabhu, Indra, Agni, Bhagavan, Yama, Nirrti (Raksasa), Varuna, Kubera and Siva perform abhiseka for you. Let Brahma with Sesa and Dikpalas protect you. Besides, let Kirti, Laksmi, Dhrti, Medha, Pusti, Sraddha, Kriya, Mati, Buddhi, Lajja, Vapu, Santi, Tusti, Kanti, the Matrkas and all the Apsaras with a firm mind, perform abhiseka for you.

## \|\| 2.40.216-221 \|\|

*ādityaścandramā bhaumo budhajīvasitārkajāḥ\|*  
*grahāstvāmabhiṣiṃcaṃtu rāhuḥ ketuśca tarpitāḥ \|\| 216 \|\|*

*devadānavagaṃdharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo manavo devā devamātara eva ca \|\| 217 \|\|*

*devapatnyo drumā nāgā daityāścāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*astrāṇi sarvaśastrāṇi rājāno vāhanāni ca \|\| 218 \|\|*

*auṣadhāni ca ratnāni kālasyāvayavāśca ye \|*  
*saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailāstīrthāni jaladā nadāḥ \|\| 219 \|\|*

*ete tvāmabhiṣiṃcaṃtu sarvakāmārthasiddhaye \|*  
*snānaṃ samāpya vidhivatsvagaṇenānu lepayet \|\| 220 \|\|*

*gavāmaṣṭottaraśataṃ tadardhaṃ cātha viṃśatim \|*  
*ācāryāyābhirūpāya pradadiyādabhipūjayan \|\| 221 \|\|*

216-221. Let Adityas, the gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Raksasas, serpents, Rsis, Manudevas, mothers of the gods, wives of the gods, the trees, the mountains, Daityas, Apsaras, all the weapons, the kings, all the vehicles, herbs or greenery, the gems, the rivers, the oceans, the hills, the places of pilgrimage, the tanks and the rivers perform your abhiseka for the fulfilment of all the desires. Thus by taking the bath in an appropriate manner, the servants should apply paste over the body. Thereafter, while worshipping the acarya, he should be given in donation a hundred and eight cows, or fifty four, or twenty cows.

## \|\| 2.40.222-228 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale jale samṛvatārayet \|*  
*śuddhāṃ ca kapilāṃ dogdhrīṃ ghaṭācāmaravarjitām \|\| 222 \|\|*

*sāmagāya tato dadyātsuvarṇadakṣiṇānvitām \|*  
*yūpamādāya saṃsthāpya snāpayedvāruṇaṃ japan \|\| 223 \|\|*
