*pūrvedyū rātrisamaye piṣṭa kāṣṭau nivedayet \|*  
*aṣṭau nirmāṇayetpaścādbaliṃ cāṣṭau vidhānavit \|\| 26 \|\|*

*parivāragaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ pūjayetprayataḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*samīraṇaṃ tato dadyācchivaṃ sūryaṃ yajetpunaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*pāyasānnaiśca juhuyāttridinaṃ lipipūjanam \|*  
*kumārīpūjanaṃ kuryādagnikāryaṃ dinatrayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*paśudānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ vibhave sati sattamāḥ \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryānmaṭhotsavapuraḥsaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

19-29. О excellent Brahmana, I am now speaking about the consecration of Surya, Ganesa and Brahma. Close to a banyan tree, a pitcher should be consecrated and worshipped. Thereafter, the Sungod should be worshipped with red lotus flowers, by the entire family. Then twenty eight offerings should be poured in the sacrificial fire. The deities should then be consecrated. Thereafter, keeping the images secretly in the sky for a day or three days, after worshipping them for three days, the homa should be performed. The Brahmanas should then be served with food. The gold should be given to them in daksina. In the process of consecrating the goddesses Varahi as well as Tripura-sundari, the use of coconut water has been prescribed. Thereafter, the vermilion should be used in their decoration. Then giving away the flowering tree, puja and homa should be performed. An animal of six mouths should be sacrificed. Then one should bathe with five types of water. The unmarried girls should be served with the food at night and daksina should be given in gold. For the images of the goddess Bhuvanesi, Mahamaya, Ambika, Kamaksi, Indrani and Aparajita, on the first day at night, eight eatables made in pudding should be given in eight types of sacrifice. They should then be worshipped by the whole family intelligently. Again the fruitful tree should be given in charity. Then, Siva and the Sungod should be worshipped for three days, offering ahutis for three days. Then the unmarried girls should be worshipped and homa should be performed for three days. As per one’s means, the animals should be given in charity. During the festivities of the establishment, one has to keep himself awake during the night.

## Chapter 61. Pacifying the disturbance in the household

## \|\| 2.61.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*durnimittānyatho vakṣye śṛṇvaṃtu munisattamāḥ \|*  
*yasya ye grahadoṣāḥ syusteṣāṃ śāṃtiṃ yathākramāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*divyaṃtarikṣe bhaume cetyevaṃ triḥ parikīrtitam \|*  
*graharkṣādyaiḥ kṛtaṃ divyamāntarikṣaṃ nibodha me \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ulkāhito diśo dāhaḥ pariveṣastathaiva ca \|*  
*jalāśayānāṃ vai kṛtyaṃ bhaumaṃ tadapi kīrtitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said- О best of the sages, I am now narrating the bad omens which are indicative of disturbance or the blemishes and which create evil effects in the household and the means to pacify them. All of you should listen. The evil omens are indicative of misfortunes. The process of their pacification is always essential. The disturbances which are created by the constellations are invisible. While falling from the sky, they make a thin line. This boundary is known as space as well.

## \|\| 2.61.4 \|\|

*bhaumaṃ cālpaphalaṃ jñeyaṃ divyāntarikṣameva ca \|*  
*saptāhamaphalaṃ dadyāddaivaṃ cāpi ca tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The limited effect of Mars space is indicative of evil which results after a week, while that of the divine one is visible at once.

## \|\| 2.61.5 \|\|

*devānāṃ hasanaṃ caiva kalkanaṃ rudhirasravaḥ \|*  
*akasmādvyasanaṃ tatra yatra nirghātanirdayaḥ \|*  
*sarpādyārohaṇaṃ caiva daivaṃ tadapi kīrtitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The laughing of the gods, their quarrels, flow of the blood and heartless attack (like the falling of vajra, make the people to face several types of miseries). Similarly, the riding over the serpents has also been described to be quite divine.

## \|\| 2.61.6 \|\|

*tato meghātsamutpannā yadi vṛṣṭiḥ śilātale \|*  
*saptāhābhyaṃtare jīvamutpannaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By riding over a serpent, in case the rains fall over the stone rock, then the jivas which are born in a week, get destroyed.

## \|\| 2.61.7 \|\|

*ekarāśisthitāḥ pāpāḥ śanibhaumadivākarāḥ \|*  
*pṛthvī dhūmākulā tatra rudaṃti bahavo janāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When the evil planets like Saturn, Mars and the Sun reach a particular Zodiac sign, the earth is covered with smoke which makes the tears to flow from the eyes of the people in streams.

## \|\| 2.61.8 \|\|

*abhicāraṃ gate jīve śanau ca tatra nāgate \|*  
*tatra paśyati rājendraḥ ko dharāṃ dhārayiṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the Jupiter reaches the stage of incantation and when Saturn is combined with the same, then the rulers become apprehensive as to how the earth could remain stable and by whose grace.

## \|\| 2.61.9-11 \|\|

*sūryamapaśyano dvaṃdvaṃ digdāhaśca tathaiva ca \|*  
*darśanaṃ dhūmaketośca nakṣatre dhūmadarśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhūkampa eva māse ca ekamāse tathā dine \|*  
*rājño janmadine vātha śakracāpaṃ dināṃtare \|\| 10 \|\|*

*darśanaṃ kharavātasya grahayuddhasya darśanam \|*  
*māsatraye tu grahaṇamulkāpātaprapātanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. A person who cannot visualise the Sungod, he has to face suffering from heat and cold. Similarly, when the comet appears in the directions, there occurs the earthquake on the same day or after a month. When the rainbow appears on the birthday of the ruler, the strong winds blow. In case the conflicts among the planets become visible or the eclipse appears in three months, one has to face miseries like the fall of the comets.

## \|\| 2.61.12-14 \|\|

*ākāśe'pyatha bhūmau ca tatra maṇḍūkameva ca \|*  
*haridrāvṛṣṭiḥ pāṣāṇe siṃhabilvākṛtiryadi \|*  
*darśane rāṣṭradurbhikṣamakaraṃ nṛpatikṣayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*caitre kumbhe nadīvegadarśane viplavo bhavet \|*  
*arka syādbhutametaddhi srugyuktaṃ śrapayeccarum \|\| 13 \|\|*

*1 ākṛṣṇeneti mantreṇa atha vārkeṇa yatnataḥ \|*  
*prāsādatoraṇaṃ tatra dvāraṃ343 prākāraveśma ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. At that point of time, in case frogs appear in the sky or the land, or the rain of yellow colour resembling the colour of turmeric fall over the rocks, or the figures of lion or wood apple become visible, then there the country has to face draught and the destruction of the king. During the month of Caitra, when the Sun is in the tenth sign of zodiac known as Aquarius, if the river flows with great force, there appears disturbance in the country. This disturbance is created by the Sungod. For the pacification of the same, offerings are to be made with ladle in the homa reciting the hymns- “Akrsneti" in the mandala which should be decorated with torana as in the palaces.

## \|\| 2.61.15-21 \|\|

*dhānyasāraṃ gavāṃ sāraṃ kūpe kumbhapradarśanam \|*  
*ādityasyādbhutaṃ vidyātkamalaṃ juhuyāttataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sahasraṃ juhuyādvātha tataḥ śāṃtirbhaveddhruvam \|*  
*vikṛtāḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva pāṃḍukapotakāstataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śvetolūko bṛhaṃścaiva droṇakākaśca kokilaḥ \|*  
*krauṃcaśca varddhanī caiva nipataṃti gṛhe yadi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gṛhe tasya mahotpāto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sthūlabhaṅgapragrahaṇaṃ prarohaṇamathāpi vā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*hārāḥ kaṭakaṭāyaṃte jātasya daṃtasambhavaḥ \|*  
*hasatā devatānāṃ ca gātre svedaśca jāyate \|*  
*sarpamaṇḍūkaprasavaḥ kuṃbhe vāpi kvacidbhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nimittānyevamādīni jāyaṃte yasya veśmani \|*  
*ṣaḍbhirmāsaiśca mriyate gṛhiṇī ca śubhā ca yā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*aśaniḥ patate yatra gṛhe vajraṃ ca pādape \|*  
*śuklā vahnisphuliṃgāśca tasya viddhi mahadbhayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

15-21. When the dhanya tattva, Gotattva or a pitcher in the well is found, it is said to have been seated by Aditya. For its sure pacification, a hundred offerings of the lotus flowers should be made. When an owl, a wooden trough, a crow, a cuckoo, kraunca bird or a broom falls in a house, it is indicative of a grave misfortune. There is no doubt about it When sweating is found over the bodies of the laughing gods, a serpent is found in a pitcher and the producing of the offshoots of the frogs are the bad omens. When they appear in the house of a person, his excellent wife is bound to meet with her death within six months. A person in whose house the vajra is struck over the chest, causing the fire sparks of white colour, he should be considered to have been overpowered with a grave danger.

## \|\| 2.61.22-24 \|\|

*kharjūra udarāvarte nikocagarale'pi ca \|*  
*phalivṛkṣe tinduke ca yatra nirjāyate kvacit \|\| 22 \|\|*

*udyāne devagehe ca svagṛhe caityavṛkṣake \|*  
*kuryādādityavāre vā ayutaṃ tilapāyasam \|*  
*tataḥ śāṃtirbhavedāśu dhenuṃ dadyācca dakṣiṇām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pāyasaṃ tilamudgau ca puṣpaṃ vā tālavṛntakam \|*  
*ikṣumodakapiṇyākāñjuhuyādravimuddiśan \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. When the lightning falls over a palm tree, whirlpools, walnut tree, the roots of the grass, the green laden with fruits, ebony tree, the orchard, the temple, the residential house, the pipala tree, then on Sunday offerings of the payasam mixed with sesamum seeds, ten thousand in number should be poured in the fire altar. Besides a cow and daksina should also be given. By so doing, one achieves peace. The offering of payasam, sesamum, green gram, flowers, tala, fruit with bunches, sugarcane balls and solid drops of sesamum seeds can be given for the sake of the Sun.

## \|\| 2.61.25-28 \|\|

*siṃhāsanaṃ rathacchatraṃ dhvajaścāmarabhūṣite \|*  
*akasmāddṛśyate yatra rājño vānyatra kutracit \|\| 25 \|\|*

*nadayaṃti ca satyasyojjvalanaṃ strīpuruṣayoḥ \|*  
*āgamasya ca dṛṣṭvaiva bhaṃgaḥ kaṭakaṭāyanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*upariṣṭādbhavedyasya mahotpāto bhavedayam \|*  
*calatvaṃ cādharasyāpi tathā kaṭakaṭāyanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ruditaṃ kokilasyāpi ulūkopyaśubhaṃ vadet \|*  
*rājāmātyavināśāya mahīṃ ca tatsuto'pi vā \|*  
*hastino madayuktāśca mriyaṃte nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. The sudden vision of the throne of the king or his chariot, flag, flywhisk, chatra, with kings pleasure the burning of the desires of a human couple and clicking of the teeth at the sight of the Vedas are taken to be the bad omens, and the householder has to face enormous danger. Similarly, with the flickering of the lower lip or cries of the cuckoo, the horrible sound of the owl or the appearing of the king, his minister or their sons, are indicative of enormous destruction, while causing the death of an intoxicated elephant. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.61.29-31 \|\|

*tāḍīpūgādayo yatra yamau syātāṃ pramādataḥ \|*  
*gehī tatra vinaśyeta sadāraḥ putrasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*baddhapuṣpe yadā puṣpaṃ phalaṃ vā yadi dṛśyate \|*  
*akṣatādarśanāttatra somasyādbhutadarśanam \|*  
*dadhi madhu ghṛtaṃ caiva juhuyādayutaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*pālāśaṃ somamuddiśya somasya ca bhaveddine \|*  
*2 imaṃdevā iti maṃtreṇa somāya śrapayeccarum \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. A person in whose house, out of arrogance, the palm tree as well as the betel nut tree are grown together as twins, then that person and his wife die together. In case another flower of fruit is found in a flower, it becomes inauspicious and for the pacification of the same, ten thousand offerings of curd, honey, ghi and plasa twigs should be poured into the fire on Monday for the sake of Soma. Reciting the mantra— “Imam deva iti ” the payasam should also be offered. This trouble is believed to be created by Soma himself.

## \|\| 2.61.32-37 \|\|

*utpataṃti gṛhe yasya yavā māṣāśca puṣkalāḥ \|*  
*dadhikṣīrājyapākeṣu rudhiraṃ dṛśyate yadi \|\| 32 \|\|*

*akasmādgṛhadāhastu anagnijvalanaṃ yathā \|*  
*meghahīnā bhavedvidyudvṛṣasyodgamanaṃ tathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vyādhilīnā vinaśyaṃti nikhilāḥ paśumānuṣāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhavaṃtyakārake dhruvam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*rājāmātyavināśāya gehe gehī vinaśyati \|*  
*prāṇanāśāya viprāyāhutyā ca prabhavaṃti hi \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā vābhadramatyugraṃ juhuyādayutaṃ kramāt \|*  
*dadhimadhughṛtairyuktaṃ khādirodumbare'pi ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*3 agnirmūddheṃti maṃtreṇa śrapitaṃ lohitaṃ carum \|*  
*triviprānbhojayeddadyāddakṣiṇāṃ lohitaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*svarṇamaṃgāramuddiśya tataḥ śāṃtiḥ prajāyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

32-37. A person in whose house the barley, black grams with straw are found flying in the air and blood is found in the curd, payasam or ghi while cooking, then his house is sure to catch fire. When the lightning appears without the clouds, where the bulls rush in an upward direction, then all the people besides the animals catch ailments and die. If they are not pacified, all the living beings, including the ruler and the minister, the head of the household, all get destroyed. In order to save their lives, the Brahmana should be given the food and offerings should be poured in the fire. When a violent omen appears, ten thousand offerings of curd, honey and ghi should be poured over the twigs of catechu, wild fig tree, reciting the hymn-“AgnimUrddhetih.” The payasam of red colour should also be offered. Three Brahmanas should be served With food, giving daksina of red metal or the gold for the sake of Mars. By so doing, one achieves peace quickly.

## \|\| 2.61.38-42 \|\|

*puṣpaṃ vā pātayedyatra phalaṃ vāpi tathaiva ca \|*  
*dadhyannaṃ ca ghṛtairmiśraṃ raupyaṃ hiraṇyameva ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

*hastyaśvamahiṣā gāvo dārāpatyadhanāni ca \|*  
*tuṣṭenāṃgārakeṇaiva sarvametatpradīyatām \|*  
*āṃgārakeṇa maṃtreṇa khādiraṃ cākṣatairyutam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāṃ ca yathāśakti dadyādviprāya vā punaḥ \|*  
*lohitaṃ ca baliṃ dadyāttataḥ saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 40 \|\|*

*dhāvaṃti cordhvapucchāśca gṛhe gāvaḥ svayaṃ yadi \|*  
*ārohaṃti gṛhaṃ viprāḥ sārameyāśca sūkarāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gṛhe yasya bhavaṃtyete tasya bhāryā vinaśyati \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ vā bhavenmṛtyurvaṃdhyā gaurvā prajāyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-42. The flowers, fruit, curd, food mixed with ghi, silver, gold, elephants, horses, cows, women, son, riches and all other things should be given over for the sake of the planet Mars. When he is pleased, he bestows everything. At that point of time, reciting the hymn, the offerings should be poured with unbroken rice in the burning fire of catechu wood and the Brahmanas should be adored together with appropriate daksina. By making the offering in red colour, one meets with welfare. О Brahmanas, when the cows in a house run raising their tails, while the pigs as well as the goats wander in the house freely, the house wife gets destroyed in the house. Or alternatively, all have to meet with destruction and the cows become dry.

## \|\| 2.61.43-48 \|\|

*mithyāvādena gehī ca rājñā vādaiśca tiṣṭhati \|*  
*atha vā yadgṛhe gāvo nardayaṃti hasaṃti ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*dharaṇīhananaṃ yatra dvayorāskadanaṃ tathā \|*  
*nimittānyevamādīni gośvajātāni sattamāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yasya gehe bhavaṃtyete nāśastasya bhaveddhruvam \|*  
*maṇḍūkasarpakūṣmāṃḍāḥ prasuvaṃti yathā striyaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*akasmādyadi caitāni budhasyotpātalakṣaṇam \|*  
*śāṃtiṃ tatra pravakṣyāmi yathā saṃpadyate sukham \|\| 46 \|\|*

*dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca apāmārgaṃ tathā punaḥ \|*  
*ayutaṃ budhavāre ca juhuyācchraddhayā yutaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*aṃbaketi ca maṃtreṇa budhāya śrapayeccarum \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ budhamuddiśya gāṃ ca dadyātpayasvinīm \|\| 48 \|\|*

43-48. Or otherwise, the householders who uselessly quarrel (is condemned). Those who enter into discussion become the rulers, or otherwise, those householders in whose house the cows are bellowing or laughing or digging the earth, or the two cows are always in fight with each other or the horses are indulged in the same types of practices, then such a house with bad omens surely meets with destruction. Like the women, in case frogs or snakes when suddenly produce their young ones in a pumpkin all of a sudden, then this evil is said to be called by Budha or Mercury. For the removal of its evil effect and for gaining of comfort, I am going to speak out the related remedy. On a Wednesday, one should devotedly pour ten thousand offerings in fire comprising of the curd, honey and ghi mixed with (apamarga) a medicinal plant, reciting the hymn- “Ambiketi.” Then for the sake of the planet Mercury, the payasam should also be given. Thereafter, the daksina of gold should also be given over to the Brahmanas, together with a milching cow.

## \|\| 2.61.49-52 \|\|

*suvarṇaṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca suphalaṃ cākṣataṃ tathā \|*  
*gṛhe prāṃgaṇake yasya nipataṃti kadācana \|\| 49 \|\|*

*alaṃkārayutāṃ vāpi sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām \|*  
*gṛhamadhye tu yaḥ paśye tkṣīṇāmaṃtarhitāṃ striyam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*akasmānmālatīpuṣpaṃ jātaṃ syāttasya vā gṛhe \|*  
*somāya na ca saṃtuṣṭaḥ sarvametatpradṛśyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā putra aiśvaryaṃ ca varastriyaḥ \|*  
*sabhṛtyāśca mahiṣyaśca mariṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-52. When the rain of gold, flowers, beautiful fruits, unbroken rice, suddenly falls in the courtyard from the above or when a lean and thin lady adorned with all the ornaments appears in that house suddenly and then at once disappears or the jasmine flowers suddenly start blossoming in that house, then the queen surely dies with riches, cereals, sons, fortunes, the excellent house wife and the servants.

## \|\| 2.61.53-54 \|\|

*śrīścateti ca mantreṇa apāmārgaṃ tathā budhaḥ \|*  
*sahasraṃ budhavāre ca juhuyād ghṛtasaṃyutam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*payasvinīṃ tathā gāṃ ca vāsoyugasamanvitam \|*  
*dvijāya śraddhayā dadyāttataḥ saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. For the pacification of the evil effect, reciting the hymn- “Sriscateti" and soaking apamarga (a medicinal plant), a thousand offerings of the same should be poured into the fire by a learned person. Then a milk giving cow and two clothes should be given over to the Brahmanas. By so doing, one has the evil effect removed and earns peace.

## \|\| 2.61.55 \|\|

*raktasrāvo bhavedyatra tatra ṛtvikprasūyate \|*  
*siṃhavyāghragavādīnāṃ dhanahānivipatkaraḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Wherever the blood flows, it is known as the ritvik-prasava. As a result of the evil effect of the same, one has to face danger from lions and tigers. Also there is the loss of riches and he has to face the misfortune.

## \|\| 2.61.56-63 \|\|

*eko vṛṣastrayo gāvaḥ saptāṣṭa nava daṃtinaḥ \|*  
*saṃvatsareṇa tasyaikā prasūtirvihatā punaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*punaḥpunarvrataṃ cāśu akāle maithunaṃ tathā \|*  
*gāvo yatra prasūyaṃte yamau doṣakarāvimau \|\| 57 \|\|*

*bhuñjīkṛtāni dhānyāni vrīhayo yavataṃḍulāḥ \|*  
*grāvimārjāramaṃḍūkāḥ sthūṇābhaṃge ca prāṅgaṇe \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vikiraṃti nakhairbhūmiṃ prarohaṃti grahaṃ tathā \|*  
*gṛhe yasya prajāyaṃte tasyā mṛtyurna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*ṣaṇmāsābhyantare yatra śmaśānaṃ yāsyati dhruvam \|*  
*kalahaṃ jñātivairaṃ ca vyādhipīḍā bhaviṣyati \|\| 60 \|\|*

*vipralāpo mitra nāśa iṣṭeṣvaniṣṭadarśanam \|*  
*bhāryāputravināśaśca bhavedeṣu viniścitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*kriyāvaṃtaṃ yadā kurvankurvīta gṛdhrabilvake \|*  
*tadā rājñāṃ vibhramaśca tathā gṛhavināśanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*amātyavargāśca pure rājñāṃ rājyaparāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspatiṃ samuddiśya gāṃ ca dadyātpayasvinīm \|\| 63 \|\|*

56-63. If three cows unite with a bull once in a year, but in case they conceive in shorter time and get untimely united, then in that case, the flow of the cow is considered to be blemished. The pounding of cereals, the paddy and other types of rice are carefully stored. At that point of time in the courtyard with a broken pillar, if the cats, frogs dig the ground, or jump over here and there in the house, then the householder is sure to meet with his end. There is no doubt about it. Besides it, within six months, one has to go to the cremation ground. There also develops struggle in the house, enmity with the relatives and pain from ailment has to be faced. Then there is separation, one faces evil even in happy events. Besides these, there is the loss of wife, son and the friend. While creating something energetic, if a person unintentionally creates a vulture or a wood apple, then the king gets confused and the household gets destroyed. The ministers conduct themselves against the king in the capital city itself. Therefore, for the pacification of the adverse situation, for Jupiter’s sake, a milk giving cow should be given over to (a Brahmana).

## \|\| 2.61.64-67 \|\|

*vārimaṃḍe ca kūpe ca vāpyāṃ ca madhukāṃjike \|*  
*kṣīraṃ dadhighṛtaṃ caiva jātaṃ yadi bhaviṣyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

*akasmāttatra vṛkṣaśca phalena saha saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*gṛhamadhye prajāyeta tataḥ saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 65 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatestu tuṣṭasya sarvametannidarśanam \|*  
*gauraṃ bṛhaspateścaiva prakuryātprāyadakṣiṇām \|\| 66 \|\|*

*aśubhaṃ hi śubhenaiva śāṃtiṃ homaṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*tatraiva rākṣasaṃ yatra ghaṭakaṃ pariśoṣaṇam \|\| 67 \|\|*

64-67. In case honey and vinegar are dropped in a reservoir, a well, a step-well and in case the milk is turned into curd and ghi, then in the house of the said person when a tree grows with fruits, becomes auspicious or not. It is believed that all these disturbances are created by Jupiter. Therefore, in order to please him, white mustard seeds, lotus and saffron should be given away in charity. The evil is warded off with the noble deeds. Therefore, it is essential to perform homa for this purpose. This is because it is some demonic force which dries up the nobility.

## \|\| 2.61.68-70 \|\|

*kesarī śarkarā tailaṃ rājataṃ tāṃḍavaṃ sthitam \|*  
*māṣabhaktaṃ tathā dhānyaṃ suvarṇaṃ rajatāni ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tāmraṃ kāṃsyaṃ tathā lohaṃ sīsakaṃ pittalaṃ tathā \|*  
*sthāpitānīva dṛśyaṃte gṛhe caitāni yasya vai \|\| 69 \|\|*

*dhananāśo bhavettasya svarga bhaṃgo hyathāpi vā \|*  
*vyādhipīḍe tathā ghore rājopadravabaṃdhane \|*  
*gajāśvapaśubhṛtyānāṃ vināśo jāyate dhruvam \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. When the brown sugar, oil, Tandava dance, cooked black gram, cereals, gold, silver, copper, bronze, iron and brass suddenly appear in the house of a person, then he has destruction of wealth, disruption of the journey to the heaven, attracting a grave ailment or has to face imprisonment at the command of the king and face death. Besides this, elephants, horses, animals and the servants surely meet with their end.

## \|\| 2.61.71-80 \|\|

*yasyaitāni pradṛśyaṃte parvataḥ kanakāni ca \|*  
*saṃpattasya prajāyeta niścalā sukhadā sadā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*daṃtottareṣu daṃtāśca paṃktimākramya saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*te'pi doṣakarāḥ sarve śalā kākṛtinastathā \|*  
*upadaṃtāśca sarve te na te doṣakarāḥ kvacit \|\| 72 \|\|*

*bhāṃḍe kuṃbhe yadā caiva śrūyate ghanagarjitam \|*  
*kaṃcukānāṃ gṛhe caiva prākāraḥ śrūyate yadi \|\| 73 \|\|*

*mūṣikānāṃ mukhe caiva jvalaṃtī yasya paśyati \|*  
*gehī tatraiva naśyeta śukrasyādbhutadarśanam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*śāṃtiṃ tatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham \|*  
*śamīpatraṃ nirmitaṃ ca yavairyuktaṃ gṛhiṇyapi \|*  
*dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca juhuyādbhārgave dine \|\| 75 \|\|*

*śuklavāsoyugaṃ caiva gāṃ ca śuklāṃ payasvinīm \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ śraddhayā caiva dadyādviprāya dakṣiṇām \|\| 76 \|\|*

*devāgāre yadā bhūmirlohitā yasya dṛśyate \|*  
*puṣpitā dṛśyate loke tatra viddhi mahadbhayam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*rājā vā rājaputro vā rājyaṃ vāpi vinaśyati \|*  
*maṃtriṇo maṃtriputrāśca mriyaṃte nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*yatra vā dṛśyate loke gṛhe yasya supūjitāḥ \|*  
*puṣpitāśca gṛhastaṃbhāḥ śarīraṃ ca ghaṭastathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*hastyaśvamahiṣāścaiva ajā gāvastathaiva ca \|*  
*nityaṃ svāmivadhārthāya puṣpitāṃ pravahaṃti ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

71-80. A person who finds the gold (in dream), he surely achieves the everlasting comfort and the fortunes. The teeth of the upper jaw when appear in one line or those which are protruding, are surely inauspicious. But in some texts, they are said to be without blemish. When the sound of thundering of clouds is heard in a pitcher or the gorge is found in the house of a servant or when the face of the mice illumines, then the householder meets with his death. This defect emerges because of the Venus. I am speaking about the removal of the same and for meeting welfare. On Friday, the householder along with his wife, placing barley, honey and ghi over the leaf of Acacia, should make the offering. Then with two white clothes, a milching cow and daksina should be given over to a Brahmana with devotion. When the land of the house or a temple built by a person becomes red or bulging, it causes grave danger. This results in the death of a king or a prince or the minister. There is no doubt about it. When the house pillar or the body of elephant, horse, pitcher, male buffalo, goat or cow appear like swelling in bodies, then the householder meets with his end.

## \|\| 2.61.81-84 \|\|

*gṛhe haṃso gṛhe samyaṅmaṇḍūkā jalacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*dvāre praviśya sarpaśca pratimāyāḥ prakalpanam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*akasmāddhaṭaśabdopi yatra kutrāpi jāyate \|*  
*sravaṃti pramadā yatra bhinnāste syurnavāṃgikāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*gṛhī tatra vinaśyeta saputrapaśubāṃdhavaḥ \|*  
*dhanuḥkhaḍgadharā rātrau madhyāhne cāndrake tathā \|\| 83 \|\|*

*udito dṛśyate vyomni jvalitaḥ pāvakastathā \|*  
*manuṣyāṅganānāṃ maraṇaṃ tathā syādrāṣṭraviplavaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

81-84. When a swan, a frog, an aquatic animal or a snake reaching the door stays there like an imaginary image, then the place at which the sound of the pitcher is heard and when the blood from the newly-wedded bride flows, or some limb gets injured, then the son of the householder, his animals together with other relatives meet with their end. When someone is found carrying a bow and a sword at night or the man is sighted at noon, while the burning fire is sighted in the sky, both man and the woman die, besides there occurs a national calamity.

## \|\| 2.61.85-87 \|\|

*rasasiddhāni vastūni surādyāścāpi vā punaḥ \|*  
*hastino madayuktāśca aśvā dhīritahiṃsakāḥ \|*  
*vinaśyaṃti sadā caite śaneradbhutadarśane \|\| 85 \|\|*

*nagare vā tathā grāme jāyante tasya vairiṇaḥ \|*  
*divā vā yadi vā rātrau śaneradbhutadarśanam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*mṛgavyāghrādirakṣāṃsi tathā gomahiṣā api \|*  
*utpataṃti yadā caite śaneradbhutamādiśet \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. The things which are prepared with juices, wine, intoxicated elephants and the biting horses are indicative of destruction. These as well as other disturbances are caused by the planet Saturn always. The disturbance is created by the Saturn during the day or night. Then all the people of the village or the town become his enemy. The disturbance of Saturn becomes visible through the deer, tigers and other wild animals.

## \|\| 2.61.88-98 \|\|

*nidhimaṃtraṃ pravakṣyāmi yena saṃpadyate śubham \|*  
*juhuyādayutaṃ samyaksasyāṃśca samidhaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*śanno devīti maṃtreṇa śubhārthaṃ śanivāsare \|*  
*caruṃ ca śrapayettatra samuddiśya śanaiścaram \|\| 89 \|\|*

*gāṃ ca nīlāṃ tato dadyājjīvadvatsāṃ payasvinīm \|*  
*vāsoyugaṃ ca viprāya suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā \|\| 90 \|\|*

*dattvā tu śraddhayā samyagdakṣiṇāṃ śirasi sthitām \|*  
*vidhiṃ homāvasāne tu tataḥ saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 91 \|\|*

*yadā dvāre godhikā ca śaṃkhinī praviśedgṛham \|*  
*tadā'śubhaṃ vijānīyādrājapīḍā dhanakṣayaḥ \|*  
*ayutaṃ juhuyātsamyaktataḥ saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 92 \|\|*

*vinā garjitameghena śilāvṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate \|*  
*raktamiśrā hi pāṃḍuśca patantī yatra dṛśyate \|\| 93 \|\|*

*tatra saṃdṛśyate cābhraṃ vṛkṣā vātavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*śakradhvajastathā cāpaṃ patanaṃ sumanasya ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

*divā śivā purā rauti ulūko vā niśācaraḥ \|*  
*niśi nipatya kākutsthe pradeśe rauti vā vṛṣaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*adharmaprabalā deśā rājā dharmaparāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*anyonyaṃ ca jighāṃsaṃti gobrāhmaṇamathāpi vā \|\| 96 \|\|*

*gṛhe gṛhī vinaśyecca saputrapaśubāṃdhavaḥ \|*  
*utsānaṃ dvāradeśe'sya maraṇaṃ rāṣṭravibhramaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*rājyanāśo bhavedrājño maraṇaṃ vāhanasya ca \|*  
*viparītāni deśāni kramataḥ saṃbhavaṃti hi \|\| 98 \|\|*

88-98. О Brahmana, I am going to speak out the auspicious hymn known as nidhi-mantra. Ten thousand twigs together with the tender grass should be poured in the fire reciting the hymn “Sanno-deviti” Thereafter, a milk giving cow of blue colour with a living calf, with two costumes should be given to a Brahmana with the daksina of gold and silver. The homa should be performed thereafter, which yields welfare. In case a lizard and Sankhini enter the house through the entrance gate, it is taken to be inauspicious. Some trouble is caused to the householder by the ruler besides one has to face the loss of riches. Therefore, in order to negate the ill effect of the same, ten thousand offerings should be poured in the fire. By so doing, a person meets with welfare. When therein stones fall without thunder which is of reddish pale colour, then with the sight of such a rainfall, the clouds, the moving trees, the rainbow, the flag are seen and evil speech is heard. During the night, the cries of someone while jumping among the bulls are heard. The evil is spread in the country when the king is devoid of dharma. The people indulge in violence killing the cows as well as the Brahmanas. In the household, the sons, animals and the relatives perish. The householder either meets with his end in his own house or in some other country. Then disturbance is created in the country, even the king gets destroyed and due to the adverse conduct in the entire country, the people fall from human values.

## \|\| 2.61.99-113 \|\|

*rāhuṇā grastasūryo'pi niśi cātha yadā divā \|*  
*tārakāgaṇavaccaiva rājñāṃ nidhanakārakaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*sahāmātyā vinaśyaṃti svarge ye ca sudurjayāḥ \|*  
*paracakreṇa pātyaṃte rājāno nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*chāyādhvajaśca gagane dṛśyate cetkadācana \|*  
*darśanādeva rājñastu vināśaḥ saharāṣṭrakaiḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*jvalito dṛśyate yatra pāvakaśca sakṛjjale \|*  
*vajre śirasi gātre vā jīvitaṃ tasya durlabham \|\| 102 \|\|*

*dvāropāṃte tathā staṃbhe āgnirvā dhūma eva vā \|*  
*puruṣasya tu tatraiva maraṇaṃ jāyate dhruvam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*gagane'śanighātaśca śaktihastena vā punaḥ \|*  
*abdasyābhyaṃtare tasya maraṇaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*śikhāvalayamadhye tu sadhūmaḥ pāvakodgamaḥ \|*  
*dṛśyate nagare madhye tatraivādbhutadarśanam \|\| 105 \|\|*

*śavasya nīyamānasya utthānaṃ vā pramādataḥ \|*  
*sthāpitasya ca liṃgasya anyatra gamanaṃ tathā \|\| 106 \|\|*

*nirghātaścāpi bhūkaṃpo nivātolkāpradarśanam \|*  
*akāle puṣpitā vṛkṣāḥ phalaṃ cākālasaṃbhavam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*animittāni sarvāṇi dūramāgatya nirbharam \|*  
*animittasya nāśo yaḥ saiṃhikeyakṛtasya ca \|\| 108 \|\|*

*narāṇāmāsanaṃ caiva gavāṃ vā mānuṣīgirā \|*  
*pakṣamātrāṃtare tasya putrasya maraṇaṃ diśet \|\| 109 \|\|*

*ayutaṃ juhuyāttatra rāhumuddiśya yatnataḥ \|*  
*śāṃtimatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 110 \|\|*

*dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca kuryāddūrvākṣataṃ tathā \|*  
*kalāyu iti mantreṇa juhuyādravivāsare \|\| 111 \|\|*

*caruṃ ca śrapayettatra rāhumudiśya saṃśrayāt \|*  
*homaṃ kuryāttato gāṃ ca kapilāṃ ca payasvinīm \|\| 112 \|\|*

*atasī tilaśaṃkhau vā vāsoyugamathāpi vā \|*  
*śraddhayā rāhumuddiśya dadyādviprāya dakṣiṇām \|\| 113 \|\|*

99-113. Rahu eclipses the sun during the night in the same way as is done during the day. The appearing of the stars during the day are indicative of the death of the monarch. The king who is considered to be invincible in the heaven even, meets with his death quickly. There is no doubt about it. In case a flag suddenly appears in the sky, then the king with the kingdom perishes. When even once the fire flames are spotted in the water, in vajra, the head and the body, then the concerned person should have no hope of living. In case the fire or smoke is found near the door or the pillar, then the householder surely meets with his death. When the vajra falls from the sky or when someone is injured with a sakti held in hand, then he is sure to meet with his end within a year. There is no doubt about it. In case in a Siva temple located in the centre of a city, when there appears fire with smoke and its rising coming in contact with a dead body, shifting of a consecrated Sivalinga to some other place, the stretching of the vajra, sight of a comet without the blowing of the wind and the untimely flowering and fruitition of the trees are all indicative of evil. When a person leaves and goes away from that place, he escapes the evil effect of the same. By so doing, the evil effect of the Rahu becomes infructuous. Otherwise the sons of the humans as well as the calves of the cows meet with their end in a fortnight’s time. Therefore, for the sake of pleasing Rahu, ten thousand offerings should be made. I am speaking out the process of yielding of auspicious results. On Sundays, reciting the hymn- “Kalayu-iti” the durva grass should be mixed with curd, honey, ghi, unbroken rice and payasam which should be poured as an offering in the fire. Thereafter, a milk giving white cow should be given to a Brahmana together with sesamum, conch, two costumes, besides the daksina.

## \|\| 2.61.114-123 \|\|

*duritasya vināśāya tasya saṃpadyate śubham \|*  
*dadhimadhughṛtakṣīreṇa vāruṇena ca vāruṇe \|\| 114 \|\|*

*dṛśyate cādbhutaṃ teṣu viśiṣṭairdoṣadarśibhiḥ \|*  
*gṛhī tatra vinaṣṭaśca bhavetsapaśubāṃdhavaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*dṛśyaṃte tatra krauñcāśca jaṃbukā gṛdhravāyasāḥ \|*  
*dāruṇaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ ghoraṃ nṛtyaṃti ca hasaṃti ca \|\| 116 \|\|*

*maithunāni ca sarveṣāṃ yasya vāse bhavedyadi \|*  
*mṛtyustasya bhavedāśu īśvarasya ca śāsanāt \|\| 117 \|\|*

*dhūmaketuryadā vyomni jvalatpāvaka sannibhaḥ \|*  
*sthānātsthānāṃtaraṃ yāti bhūmau vā patate bhṛśam \|*  
*sabaṃdhurasyate rājā paracakraiḥ sa pīḍitaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*durbhikṣaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva ciraṃ rāṣṭre bhaviṣyati \|*  
*gāvo markaṭakuṃbhā va viśaṃte gṛhaveśmani \|\| 119 \|\|*

*gāvaśca tasya naśyaṃti dārāpatyadhanāni ca \|*  
*anyasya doṣo bhavati gṛhe yāṃti pramādataḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*abdāṃtare bhavenmṛtyurvirajā hi bhaviṣyati \|*  
*śāṃtimatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 121 \|\|*

*saptāśvarathasaṃyuktaṃ hemacchatravibhūṣitam \|*  
*viprāya maṃḍapaṃ dadyādbilvapatramathāpi vā \|\| 122 \|\|*

*aiṃdreṇaiva tu mantreṇa homaḥ kāryo dvijātibhiḥ \|*  
*akasmācchālatālākṣakhadirotpalaserakāḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

114-123. Further for the removal of the evil, curd, honey, ghi and payasam should be poured in the fire as the offering, which yields good results. Otherwise, whatever evil signs are visible to the people, they are also being narrated by me. The householder perishes with his sons, animals as well as the relatives. This is definite. A person, at whose place the Kraunca birds, jackals, vultures, dreadful crows dance and enjoy love sports, then according to the provision of the lord, the householder meets with his end soon. The time when a comet like the burning flame travels from one place to the other, or it falls over the ground, at the same time the related king is harassed by the other kings with his attendants and servants. Besides, there arises in the country the terrific draught and destruction for a long time. A person in whose home crows, cows, monkeys and kumbha enter, his cows, wife and riches get quickly destroyed. Be has also to share the faults of others. Within a year, he is deprived of his entire force and riches and then faces destruction. He then having been deprived of his entire strength, falls over the death bed. Therefore, I am speaking out the relevant remedy for peace for him, which is sure to yield him relief. He should give away to a Brahmana a chariot with a golden chatra in which seven horses are yoked, or wood apple leaves. He should also pour the offerings of teak, palm, myrobalan, catechu, blue lotus, kaseru, reciting the hymns.

## \|\| 2.61.124-130 \|\|

*gṛhamadhye prajāyeta ketoradbhutadarśanam \|*  
*haṃso vā droṇakāko vā mayūro vā gṛhopari \|\| 124 \|\|*

*gṛhe tasya mahotpātaḥ ketoradbhutadarśanam \|*  
*śāṃtimatra pravakṣyāmi yayā saṃpadyate śubham \|\| 125 \|\|*

*dadhimadhughṛtāktaṃ ca juhuyādayutaṃ kuśam \|*  
*4 tryaṃbakaṃ ceti mantreṇa ketavebhivape ccarum \|\| 126 \|\|*

*nīlāṃ dhenuṃ savatsāṃ ca bahukṣīrapradāṃ tathā \|*  
*mṛttikāṃ hemavāsaśca nānālaṃkārameva ca \|\| 127 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāṃ ca pravakṣyāmi yasya nāsti pratikriyā \|*  
*devamuddiśya dānena homena caruṇā tathā \|\| 128 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi cchāyāṃ yaḥ paśyedātmanaḥ svayam \|*  
*svacchāyāṃ pādukasyaiva paśyetpañcaśirodvayam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*evamevaiva yacchinnaṃ śinaṣṭi ca tato hitam \|*  
*śīghraṃ nāśamavāpnoti saptāhānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

124-130. In the middle of the house, the planet Ketu sometimes causes great upheaval and with the fall of the swan, the terrific crow or the peacock, the disturbance is created. In order to pacify the evil and for earning auspiciousness, one should follow the process being described by me. The offering for Ketu should comprise of curd, honey and ghi besides the kusa grass, which should be poured into the fire flame reciting the hymn - “Tryambaketi.” The payasam should also be offered. The blue milk giving cow with calf, the earth, the costumes studded with gems and various types of ornaments should be given to a Brahmana with daksina. Because in order to please Ketu, charities have to be given, besides performing homa and offering of payasam, which pacify him. By so doing, there is no possibility of any further reaction from the planet. Those who sight their own shadow in the southern direction breaking the head and which is shattered at the same time, then it should be taken to be auspicious, otherwise he is bound to meet with destruction within a week. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.61.131-135 \|\|

*uccāvacānpravakṣyāmi yathā śāstreṇa coditam \|*  
*kākamārjāraśūkānāṃ kapotānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*maithunaṃ dṛśyate yatra tacca rāhormahādbhutam \|\| 131 \|\|*

*śanimuddiśya juhuyādayutaṃ śanivāsare \|*  
*pūjayedarkapuṣpeṇa śatena juhuyāccarum \|\| 132 \|\|*

*kṛtvā tatraiva paśyeta śaneradbhutadarśanam \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśaṃ caruṃ kṛtvā tataḥ śāṃtirbhaveddhruvam \|\| 133 \|\|*

*bhujapadostathā cakṣuḥspaṃdane maraṇaṃ diśet \|*  
*tattu somādbhutaṃ vidyādvāmadakṣiṇataḥ kramāt \|\| 134 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇapakṣe bhavedvāme viparīte'dbhutaṃ diśet \|*  
*aniṣṭasūcakaṃ yasmāttasmācchāṃtiṃ prakalpayet \|\| 135 \|\|*

131-135. I am now speaking the high and low inauspicious deeds. The uniting of the crows, cats, parrots and particularly the pigeons when sighted by a person are considered to be inauspicious. These are caused by Rahu. On Saturday, for the sake of Saturn, ten thousand offerings besides a hundred offerings of payasam with coral flowers should be poured in the fire. In case the evil symptoms of Saturn are again sighted at the same place, then twenty eight offerings of payasam should again be offered in fire. By so doing, one surely gets the relief. In case his left and right limbs flutter, including the arms, feet and the eyes, they are indicative of the death. Such an evil is caused by Soma or the moon. This should be well understood. In the dark fortnight particularly, the right limbs of a woman and the left limbs of a man when flutter, they are indicative of some evil. Therefore, action should be taken to pacify the same.

## \|\| 2.61.136 \|\|

*śatārddhaṃ ravimuddiśya śāntyarthe homamācaret \|*  
*carupākavidhānena yavaistilasusarpiṣā \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. For the pacification of the Sungod, the cooked payasam, barely, sesamum and ghi should be poured in the fire in the form of fifty offerings, which has been prescribed.

## \|\| 2.61.137-138 \|\|

*pustake yajñasūtraṃ ca asatpātre carau tu vā \|*  
*śakravastrapradagdhe ca sūryasyādbhutadarśanam \|\| 137 \|\|*

*hayamāraṃ trimadhvaktaṃ juhuyādiṣṭasiddhaye \|*  
*devapustakaratnāni maṇikāṃcanameva ca \|\| 138 \|\|*

137-138. In case the string of the book and the payasam in the vase or the costume of Indra is burnt out, it should be considered to has been caused by the Sun. For the pacification of the evil, the offerings of oleander should be poured, soaked in tri-madhu (honey, sugar and ghi). It which should be poured in the ghi, which bestows the desired effect. Then for the success of one’s efforts, book of the lord, gems, diamond and gold should be given over to a Brahmana as daksina

## \|\| 2.61.139-141 \|\|

*lohitasyādbhutaṃ vidyātsahasraṃ ca viśodhanam \|*  
*devāgāre tathā godhā śaṃkhinī praviśetkvacit \|\| 139 \|\|*

*droṇakāko bakaścaiva ulūkadvayameva ca \|*  
*raktakaṃṭhaḥ kapotaśca vyāghra eṇaśca vā viśet \|\| 140 \|\|*

*yasya devagṛhaṃ paśyettasya tasyāyutaṃ hunet \|*  
*na cātra gṛhavaikṛtyaṃ hasanaṃ yadi dṛśyate \|*  
*saṃpattisūcakaṃ gehe maraṇaṃ duḥkhadarśanam \|\| 141 \|\|*

139-141. Similarly, the disturbance caused by Mars can be removed by pouring a thousand offerings in the fire. When a lizard, Sankhini, omen, the wicked crow, two owls, bird with red neck, pigeon, a tiger or a deer is seen, ten thousand offerings should be poured in the fire in order to remove its ill effect. With their smiles on the face, no harm is caused. To the contrary, one achieves the riches. In case they are found in a painful condition, it is indicating of death for a person.

## \|\| 2.61.142-149 \|\|

*kraṃdane hatarājyena gajāśvavāhane kvacit \|*  
*sūryamuddiśya juhuyādayutaṃ sarvasiddhaye \|\| 142 \|\|*

*pramādātkaṃpane hāniḥ svede jāte vipadbhavet \|*  
*kṣīrasrāve ca rudhire tatra rājye mahadbhayam \|\| 143 \|\|*

*gocchāgau vātha gomāyurgṛhopari pranṛtyati \|*  
*yadā rauti divā pherustadā nāśo bhaveddhruvam \|\| 144 \|\|*

*śvajaṃbukāvatha vyāghro yathāśakti ca dhāvati \|*  
*īśāne mahiṣastadvattadā deśe ca viplavaḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

*rāhoradbhutamudiśya sahasraṃ juhuyāccarum \|*  
*vṛkṣādbhutaṃ yadā paśyettatra tasyāṃ parityajet \|*  
*yadgṛheṣu hutaṃ yāti deśaviplavamādiśet \|\| 146 \|\|*

*deśe vā nagare grāme āraṇyapaśubandhanam \|*  
*sarpe vā viparītaṃ ca māṃsapiṃḍamathāpi vā \|*  
*tadgṛhe maraṇaṃ caiva deśa viplavamādiśet \|\| 147 \|\|*

*divādbhute'yutaṃ rātrau dviguṇaṃ ca bhaveddhruvam \|*  
*dviguṇaṃ cāpi saṃdhyāyāmardharātre caturguṇam \|\| 148 \|\|*

*akāle tatra maraṇamakāle gṛhiṇīmṛtiḥ \|*  
*saurādbhutaṃ vijānīyādaśubhe vā viśodhanam \|\| 149 \|\|*

142-149. The cry of a horse and an elephant results in the destruction of the kingdom. Therefore, in order to achieve all round success, ten thousand offerings should be made for the sake of the Sungod. Out of arrogance, in case there is a shaking, it results in loss. In case one perspires, he has to face the misery. With the flowing of milk or blood, grave danger appears in the kingdom. In case, a cow, goat or a jackal dances over the roof of the house, or the jackal cries during the day, it results in definite destruction. When the dog, jackal, tiger and the he buffalo runs in the north-east direction, a grave disturbance is caused in the country. Therefore, for the removal of its ill effect, a thousand offerings in milk should be made in form of Rahu. In case a bed omen is caused due to a tree, the offerings should be made at the same place. In case the offerings are made in home on return, then in that case the disturbance would surely be caused in the country. In a town, province or a village, when the wild animals are kept in captivity, or the capture of a snake, or to find a piece of meat, then that house is bound to face the death of a person, while the disturbance is sure to be caused in the country. By witnessing evil during the day, one has to pour ten thousand offerings in the fire and during the night, the number would be doubled. It would be four times more during the dead of night. The evil caused by the sun results in death of the householder or his wife, which is untimely. Therefore, the inauspicious has to be pacified necessarily.

## \|\| 2.61.150-157 \|\|

*ekaikasyāyutaṃ yatra kuryāttatraiva homayet \|*  
*sāṃgopāṃgena sahita maṣṭāvaṣṭau hutaṃ ca vā \|\| 150 \|\|*

*adhipratyadhisahitaṃ gṛhapakṣe'pi sattamāḥ \|*  
*tanmānena hutaṃ viprā kuryāttatraiva bhūṣaṇam \|\| 151 \|\|*

*ekaikasyāhutaṃ viprā aṣṭāvaṣṭau hutaṃ ca vā \|*  
*adhipratyadhidevānāṃ yāścānyāścāṃgadevatāḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*mānāṃtaṃ ca dadetpūrṇāṃ dattvā pūrṇāṃ na homayet \|*  
*vakṣye grahamakhe mānaṃ yena mānena sidhyati \|\| 153 \|\|*

*amānakaraṇe doṣastasmānmānaṃ na hāpayet \|*  
*paṃkticatvāriṃśadādyaiścaturdhā vibhajennaraḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

*aniṣṭāya tato dadyāccaruhomaṃ vibhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*adhipratyadhidevānāmaṣṭāvaṣṭa hyudāhṛtam \|\| 155 \|\|*

*5 tryaṃbakādiṣu maṃtreṣu homatrayamudāhṛtam \|*  
*dhanaṃjaye tathā dadyāccaruhomaṃ vibhāgataḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

*ādityāyāṣṭāvaṣṭāvadhikakalpayetsudhīḥ \|*  
*śatahome tu sarvatra daśāṃgaṃ kalpayennaraḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

150-157. Thus for each one of the inauspicious event, the pouring of ten thousand offerings has to be resorted to with the following of all other rites. For the god who is the cause of such evil, eight thousand offerings shall have to be made (in addition to the ten thousand stated above). Similarly, in the context of the construction of a house, guardian deity or the Pratyadhi-deva (subsidiary deity), the homa of the same pattern should be performed that adds to his grace. Each one of Adhideva or Pratyadhi-deva besides their associated gods, should be offered eight offerings each. This is the standard fixed for them, which should be offered to them. After giving the final offering, there is also a provision for the performing of the homa again. Therefore, I am speaking about the homa yajna standard making use of which, one meets with success. In case it is made without following the standard, one has to earn blemish. Therefore, one should never disown the standard. A person should first of all divide it into ten parts each. Thereafter, in the sequence of the department, for the removal of evil, the offering of payasam should be made, which is beneficial for all. For the sake of the prominent and the subsidiary gods, eight offerings should be made for each one of them making use of the hymn - “Tryambaka iti.” Three homas should be performed. Similarly, for Dhananjaya, according to the divisions, caru should be used as offering. For the Sungod, eight additional offerings should be made. Out of the hundred offerings, a tenth of them are to be received by them.

## \|\| 2.61.158-159 \|\|

*aniṣṭāya yugāṃgaṃ tu grahebhyo hyaṃganāya ca \|*  
*adhipratyadhidevānāṃ tathaivāṃgaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 158 \|\|*

*dvau tu dadyāttryaṃbakāya tathā dhanaṃjayāya ca \|*  
*tatra homo nāyakāya sarvatraiva vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

158-159. For the removal of the evil, all the planets and semi-planets like the angas of presiding or subsidiary deities are conceived, which is essential. Similarly, making use of Tryambaka and Dhananjaya with two angas each, the homa should be performed by a learned person, as prescribed in the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.61.160-163 \|\|

*sahasre caiva viṃśāṃge aniṣṭāya daśāṃśakam \|*  
*pañcāṃśena grahāṇāṃ ca pañcāṃśena yavānapi \|\| 160 \|\|*

*tatrāniṣṭe paṃcaśataṃ tasyārdhaṃ grahavāgyataḥ \|*  
*ekatriṃśadbhavenmānam anyeṣāṃ tu caturdaśa \|\| 161 \|\|*

*grahādhikaṃ homayugaṃ tatra bhāge prakalpayet \|*  
*adhātaye ca tithyaṃgaṃ pañcāṃgaṃ yasya cādbhutam \|\| 162 \|\|*

*grahebhyaścaiva paṃcāṃgaṃ tatra vāṃgaṃ parānapi \|*  
*ekaikāṃge bhavenmānaṃ ṣaṭśataṃ ṣaṣṭireva ca \|\| 163 \|\|*

160-163. In the thousand offerings when twenty angas are conceived for the removal of evil, tenth part is conceived and for the planets, five offerings are made. It includes barley as the fifth part. In case the evil is witnessed again there, then for five hundred planets, two hundred and fifty offerings should be made. A standard of thirty one has been fixed for the purpose and for others, only fourteen offerings are made. Besides the planets, two homas are made for the planets, in which the tithi is conceived of five parts. For planets, five are conceived, while for others only the limbs are conceived. The standard for each one of the angas has been fixed as six hundred and eight.

## \|\| 2.61.164-167 \|\|

*adhikaṃ ca bhavetṣaṣṭirdaśame bhāgaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*aniṣṭāṃśe trisahasraṃ triśataṃ triṃśataṃ tathā \|\| 164 \|\|*

*catuḥśataṃ grahāṇāṃ ca tathā saptaśatādhikam \|*  
*upagrahebhyo dadyācca paṃcāśītyadhikaṃ śatam \|\| 165 \|\|*

*tithyaṃgabhāgaḥ śeṣeṇa grahe saptaśatādhikam \|*  
*ekaikaṃ tu grahasyaivamādityāya yugaṃ bhavet \|\| 166 \|\|*

*grahāṃge yaḥ sthito bhāgo yugalaṃ bhāgaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tryaṃbakāya ca taddadyāttathā dhanaṃjayāya ca \|\| 167 \|\|*

164-167. The maximum number is sixty or the tenth part is conceived. For the removal of evil, three thousand, three hundred and thirty offerings have been prescribed. For the planets, four hundred or seven hundred have been prescribed. For satellites, one hundred and eighty five parts have been prescribed. The remaining fifteenth part which is said to be seven hundred for the planets, but the planets get only a single part while the sun has four of them. For the parts of the planets the remaining two parts, while for Tryambaka and Dhananjaya have to receive two parts each.

## \|\| 2.61.168-175 \|\|

*śāṃtike pauṣṭike kāmye yadīcchetsukhamātmanaḥ \|*  
*grahāṇāṃ cāyutaṃ homaṃ tryahasādhyena homayet \|\| 168 \|\|*

*tryahasādhye vidhānaṃ yatpuraivodīritaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*idānīṃ prakrameṇaiva yo bhāgaḥ sa nigadyate \|\| 169 \|\|*

*pūrvasmindivase'niṣṭe sahasraṃ triśatottaram \|*  
*itareṣāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca pratyekaṃ tu śataṃ śatam \|\| 170 \|\|*

*adhipratyadhidevānāṃ paṃcāśaddhoma ucyate \|*  
*prathamehni pradadyācca militvā trisahasrakam \|\| 171 \|\|*

*dvitīyadivase'niṣṭe dvisahasramudāhṛtam \|*  
*prati grahebhyastriśataṃ dadyādaṣṭa śatādhikam \|\| 172 \|\|*

*upagrahebhyo dadyācca ṣoḍaśabhyo yathākramam \|*  
*ekāśītiṃ dadau yatnādaśītiṃ cāṃtyayordvayoḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

*evaṃ dvitīyadivase militvā ṣaṭsahasrakam \|*  
*aniṣṭāya triśataṃ tu tṛtīyadivase matam \|\| 174 \|\|*

*tatpratyekaṃ grahāṇāṃ ca dvācatvāriṃśaducyate \|*  
*adhipratyadhidevānāṃ pratyekaṃ paṃcatriṃśakam \|\| 175 \|\|*

168-175. The performing of the rites for peace, besides for the performing of energetic and kamya rites, for one’s own personal pleasures, the three day anusthana of the planets is patronised, in which ten thousand offerings are poured in the fire. О Brahmanas, the said method of performing the anusthana which is completed in three days, has already been explained. Presently, I am speaking about the remaining part of the same. In case an evil omen appears on the very first day, thirteen hundred offerings are to be made. For other planets, a hundred offerings each should be made. For the subsidiary gods, the number has been fixed as fifty each. Thus, on the very first day, the total number of the offerings to be made should be three thousand. In case a bad omen appears on the second day, the number of offerings to be made should be two thousands, while each planet has to receive three hundred and eight offerings. The sixteen satellites have to be given eighty one offerings each. At the end, eighty each are to be given for both. Thus, on the second day, a total of six thousand offerings are to be given. For the removal of the evil, on the third day, three hundred offerings are to be made. This has been ordained in the scriptures. Thereafter, for each and every planet, forty two offerings are required to be made. The presiding and the subsidiary deities have to be invoked after the chief god and each one of them has to be given thirty five offerings each, which have been prescribed. In other words, each one of them has to be given thirty five offerings each.

## \|\| 2.61.176 \|\|

*tṛtīyadivase dadyānmilitvaikasahasrakam \|*  
*ādityāya yugaṃ dadyādekaṃ tu tryaṃbakāya ca \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. On the third day, a thousand offerings have to be made in a combined manner. Further, two thousand offerings arc required to be made to Aditya, while a thousand of them have to be made to lord Siva, also known as Tryambaka.

## \|\| 2.61.177 \|\|

*dhanaṃjayāya homaikamekaṃ cāyutamucyate \|*  
*tadardhakaṃ grahebhyaśca itarebhyastadardhakam \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. Five hundred offerings have to be made for Dhananjaya, while for others two hundred fifty offerings have to be made individually.

## \|\| 2.61.178-179 \|\|

*grahāṇāṃ trisahasraṃ tu paṃcānāṃ ca sahasrakam \|*  
*trisahasrabhāgaśeṣamādityāya sahasrakam \|\| 178 \|\|*

*tryaṃbakāya tathā dadyāttathā dhanaṃjayāya ca \|*  
*ṣaṭpādādhika ṣaṭaṣaṭkasahasraparisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*navaślokaśatodbhūtaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ syādbhaviṣyakam \|\| 179 \|\|*

178-179. Three thousand offerings have to be made for all the planets, a thousand each have to be given to the five deities. For Aditya, three thousand offerings have to be made, as has already been stated. A thousand offerings should be made for Tryambaka as well as Dhananjaya.

## Pratisargaparva Part 1

## Chapter 62. The Rulers of Satyayuga

## \|\| 2.62.1-2 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca \|*  
*bhaviṣyākhye mahākalpe brahmāyuṣi parārddhake \|*  
*prathame'bdehni tṛtīye prāpte vaivasvate'ntare \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aṣṭāviṃśe satyayuge ke rājāno'bhavanmune \|*  
*teṣāṃ rājyasya varṣāṇi tanme vada vicakṣaṇa \|\| 2 \|\|*

After bowing reverence to Narayana, Nara and the goddess Sarasvati are offered salutation in the beginning. Thereafter, the text of Jaya should be recited.

1-2. Saunaka said- О proficient one, the Bhavisya Mahakalpa is the later half period of Brahma’s life. During the twenty eighth Satyayuga, on the third day of the first year, Vaivasta Manu was bom who was the king ruling there at that point of time. You also kindly let me know the period of his rule.

## \|\| 2.62.3-13 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kalpākhye śvetavārāhe brahmābdasya dinatraye \|*  
*prāpte saptamuhūrte ca manurvaivasva to'bhavata \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sa taptvā sarayūtīre tapo divyaṃ śataṃ samāḥ \|*  
*tacchikkāto'bhavatputra ikṣvākuḥ sa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo varadānena divyaṃ yānaṃ sa āptavān \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ pūjayitvā harau rājyaṃ nivedya ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ṣaṭtriṃśacca sahasrāṇāmabdaṃ rājyaṃ tadā'karot \|*  
*tasmājjāto vikukṣiśca śatahīnaṃ tadabdakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*rājyaṃ kṛtvā divaṃ yātastasmājjāto ripuṃjayaḥ \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tatkakutsthasutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tato'nenāṃsa ātmajaḥ \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasmājjāto nṛpaḥ pṛthuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ viṣvagaśvaśca tatsutaḥ \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasmādārdro nṛpo'bhavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ bhadrāśvastatsuto'bhavat \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ yuvanāśvastu tatsutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ śravasthastatsuto'bhavat \|*  
*satyapādaśca saṃjātaḥ prathamo bhārate'ntare \|\| 11 \|\|*

*udayādastaparyaṃtaṃ tairnṛpairbhūmimaṃḍalam \|*  
*bhuktaṃ nītiparairdevaiḥ śravasthena tu bhūtale \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ bṛhadaśvastato'bhavat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasmātkuvalayāśvakaḥ \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛta rājyaṃ dṛḍhāśvastatsuto'bhavat \|\| 13 \|\|*

3-13. Suta said - In the kalpa known as Sveta-Varaha, on the third day of the first year of Brahma, in the seventh Muhurta, Vaivasvata Manu was born. He performed severe tapas over the bank of the river Sarayu for a hundred divine years. Then he sneezed suddenly, with that sneeze a son named Iksavaku was born to him. With the granting of a boon to him by Brahma, he also achieved a divine vehicle. He ruled the earth for thirty six thousand years, devoting his mind at Narayana. In due course of time, he got a son named Vikuksi. He ruled the country for a hundred years. After the demise of Vikuksi, Ripunjaya was born to him. The period of his rule was a hundred years less than his father. It is said that he had a son named Kakutstha, who also ruled for a hundred years. In due course of time, he got a son named Amsa. He also, like his own father, ruled for a hundred years, after which he got a son named Prthu. Prthu had a son named Visvagasva who had a son named Ardra. Ardra had a son named Bhadrasva and Bhadrasva had a son named Yuvanasva. Yuvanasva had a son named Sravastha. He had been the first step of truth on the land of Bharata. The period of rule of each one of these rulers was shortened by a hundred years successively. Starting from the place of the rising sun, they ruled successively upto the land of the setting sun (or the region which falls between the land of the rising sun to the land of the setting sun was ruled by them). They ruled the land judiciously. Sravastha had a son named Brhadasva, who had a son named Kuvalasva. Drdhasva was the son of Kuvalasva.

## \|\| 2.62.14-21 \|\|

*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tattasmātputro nikuṃbhakaḥ \|*  
*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tatsaṃkaṭāśvastu tatsutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tattasmājjātaḥ prasenajit \|*  
*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tadravaṇāśvastu tatsutaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tanmāṃdhātā tatsuto'bhavat \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ purukutsastu tatsutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ triṃśadaśvastu tatsutaḥ \|*  
*rathe yasya smṛtā vāhā vājinastriṃśato varāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*anaraṇyastato jāto hyaṣṭāviṃśatsahasrakam \|*  
*rājyaṃ dvitīyacaraṇe smṛtaṃ satyayugasya vai \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pṛṣadaśvastato jāto rājyaṃ ṣaṣṭhasahasrakam \|*  
*tadabdaṃ bhūtale kṛtvā pitṛlokamupāyayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

*haryaśvastu tato jāto viṣṇubhaktakule nṛpaḥ \|*  
*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tattatsuto vasumānsmṛtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tattridhanvā tanayastataḥ \|*  
*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tattena rājñā ca satkṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

14-21. The period of their rule also was successively reduced by a hundred years each. Drdhasva had a son named Nikumbha, while Sankatasva was the son of Nikumbha. Prasenajit was the son of Sankatasva, while Ravanasva was the son of Prasenajit. Ravanasva on the other had got a son named Mandhata. It is said that the period of rule of these rulers was successively reduced by a thousand years. His chariot was driven by thirty horses. Therefore, he was also known by the name of Trimsadasva. He had a son named Anaranya, who in the second stage of Satyayuga had ruled over the earth for a period of twenty eight thousand years. He got a son named Prsdasva who ruled his country for six thousand years. He ultimately achieved the tranquillity of Pitrloka. In the race of this devotee of Vi$nu was bom Haryasva, who had a son named Vasuman. Vasuman had a son named Tridhanva. The period of rule of all these rulers is said to be on decline by a thousand years successively. Therefore, in the central region of Bharata, the second phase of Satyayuga was completed. This has been stated.

## \|\| 2.62.22-28 \|\|

*satyapādaḥ samāpto'yaṃ dvitīyo bhārate'ntare \|*  
*tridhanvanaśca nṛpatestrapāraṇyastu vai sutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sahasrahīnaṃ rājyaṃ tatkṛtvā svargamupāyayau \|*  
*tasmājjātastriśaṃkuśca rājyaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*chadmanā hīnatāṃ jāto hariścaṃdrastu tatsutaḥ \|*  
*rājyaṃ viṃśatsahasraṃ ca rohito nāma tatsutaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ hārītastanayo'bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ caṃcubhūpaśca tatsutaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pitustulyaṃ hi rājyaṃ tadvijayo nāma tatsutaḥ \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ hi rājyaṃ tadrurūkastanayastataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ sagarastanayo'bhavat \|*  
*bhūpāśca bāhusenāntā vaiṣṇavāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rājyamānaṃ kṛtaṃ samyagbhūpairvaivasvatādibhiḥ \|*  
*maṇisvarṇasamṛddhiśca bahvannaṃ bahudugdhakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

22-28. A son named Тriparanya was bom to the king Tridhanva, who ruled the earth for less than a thousand years and achieved the heaven thereafter. Again, Triparanya had a son named Trisanku, who ruled for a thousand years. Trisanku had a son named Hariscandra, who became a pauper with the giving away of all the riches and wealth to the sage Visvamitra. He had a son named Rohita who ruled the country for thirty thousand years. Rohit had two sons named Harita and Cancubhupa. Out of them, Cancubhupa had a son named Vijaya and Vijaya had a son named Ruruka. Sagara was the son of Ruruka. The rulers upto Bahusena were all Vaisnavas. All these rulers ruled the country upto the same period upto which their father ruled. At the time of the rulers like Vaivasvata Manu, the standard of the kingdoms was based on vast collection of gems and enough of gold. The farm produce was enormous and there flowed the rivers of milk. In this way, dharma was fully present on earth during those days.

## \|\| 2.62.29-35 \|\|

*pūrṇo dharmastadā bhūmyāṃ mune satyayugasya vai \|*  
*tṛtīyacaraṇe madhye sagaro nāma bhūpatiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śivabhaktaḥ sadācārastatputrāḥ sāgarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*triṃśatsahasravarṣaṃ tadrājyaṃ vai munibhiḥ smṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*naṣṭeṣu sāgareṣvevamasamañjasa ātmajaḥ \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyamaṃśumāṃstatsuto'bhavat \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ dilīpastatsuto'bhavat \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasmājjāto bhagīrathaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ śrutasenastato'bhavat \|*  
*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ nābhāgastanayastataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyamambarīṣastato'bhavat \|*  
*śaivāḥ ṣaṭśrutasenāntā nābhāgo vaiṣṇavo nṛpaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*satyapādaḥ samāpto'yaṃ tṛtīyo bhārateṃtare \|*  
*aṃvarīṣeṇa bhūpena śatahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 35 \|\|*

29-35. During the third phase of Satyayuga, the ruler named Sagara was bom. He was a great devotee of Siva and was quite a righteous and pious person. Several sons were bom to him, whose period of rule has been described by the sages to be of thirty thousand years. At the destruction of those sons, Asmanjasa - the son of Sagara, ruled for a period less than a hundred years as compared to his father. Thus, Asmanjasa has the son named Ansuman and Ansuman had a son named Dilipa. Bhagiratha was the son of Dilipa. Bhagiratha had a son named Srutasena and Nabhaga was the son of Srutasena. Ambarisa was the son of Nabhaga. All these rulers successively ruled for less than a hundred years. Out of these, all the rulers upto Srutasena were Saiva, while the king Nabhaga was a Vaisnava. Thus, in the land of Bharata, the third phase of Satyayuga was completed.

*caturthe caraṇe tasya cāṣṭādaśa sahasrakam \|*

*harivarmā śamakajo vaiśyavatsādhupūjakaḥ \|*  
*ūnatriṃśatsahasrāṇi tathā saptaśatāni vai \|\| 43 \|\|*

*harivarmā'karodrājyaṃ tasmāddaśaratho'bhavat \|*

*rājyaṃ daśasahasraṃ tanniyajñaḥ prākṛto nṛpaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tadadharmapratāpena hyanāvṛṣṭistadā'bhavat \|*  
*śatavarṣamanā vṛṣṭissarvarājyaṃ vyanāśayat \|\| 46 \|\|*

36-46. During the fourth phase of Satyayuga, in the land of Bharata which is known as the land of activity, the king Ambarisa ruled the country for eighteen thousand years. The king Ambarisa had a son named Sindhudvipa. He ruled the land thirty years short of a hundred years. Sindhudvipa had a son named Ayutasva. Rtuparna was the son of Ayutasva. Sarvakama was the son of Rtuparna. Kalmasapada was the son of Sarvakama. Kalmasapada had a son named Sudasa. Madayanti, wife of Sudasa was impregnated by the sage Vasistha and a son named Asmaka was born to her. He had a son named Harivarma. The period of rule of all of them is said to be less than a hundred years in succession. In the same sequence, upto the king Saudasa, seven rulers can be counted, who were all devoted to Visnu. Then Asmaka, the son of Saudasa, because of the curse received from his own preceptor Vasistha, he gave away his own kingdom to Vasistha. The ruler Asmaka was the great devotee of Gokarna Sivalinga. Therefore, he was known as a great Saiva. Harivarma happened to be his son, who like other Vaisyas, served the ascetics very well. He ruled the country for nineteen thousand and seven hundred years. He got a son named Dasaratha, who ruled the country as long as his father did. Thereafter, he got a son named Dillivaya and the Visvasaha became the ruler. Though this ruler ruled for ten thousand years, but because of his foolishness and arrogance, he could not perform a single yajna. Because of his evil ways, there was no rainfall in his country for a hundred years and as a result of which the kingdom went to ruins.

47-61. Thereafter, because of the prayer of the queen, Vasistha produced a son named Khatvanga, who holding the Khatvanga weapon and with the help of Indra, ruled the earth for thirty thousand years. Thereafter, getting a boon from the gods, he achieved salvation. Khatvanga had a son named Dirghabahu, who ruled the earth for twenty thousand years. Sudarsana was the son of Dirghabahu, who happened to be a great devotee of the goddess. The three valorous rulers known by the names of Harivarma, Dasaratha and Dilipa were great Vaisnavas. The rulers named Khatvanga and Dirghabahu were also the devotees of Visnu. Then Sudarsana — the valorous one, because of the grace of the great goddess, married the daughter of the king of Kasi. In the battlefield, he conquered all other rulers. Then he put the entire Bharata-khanda under his control, he enjoyed the kingship for five thousand years. Thereafter, the great goddess Kali instructed him in the dream- “O son, you together with your wife and the sage Vasistha should go to Himalaya and live there, because due to the great wind or storm, the destruction of Bharatakhanda is sure to happen. The islands of western ocean, the middle region of eastern ocean and the southern oceanic islands besides the islands of the northern oceans, which had been dug by the sons of Sagara, have already been destroyed. Thus all the well known and famous islands have been destroyed. Because of the complete destruction of these famous islands, the land of Bharata would also face destruction on the seventh day from now. I would submerge in the oceanic waves. Therefore, you better save your life.” Submitting to the command of the great goddess, the king together with all other rulers, Vaisyas and Brahmanas moved to Himalaya and made it as their abode. Thereafter, at five years’ interval, all the elements got destroyed with the force of water and wind. All the tattvas were destroyed. The entire earth was reduced to the particles like sugar. All the living beings on earth perished. The rain continued to fall on earth constantly for five years. Thereafter, becoming peaceful, the wind dried up the entire water. Thus, after ten years, the land became visible.

## Chapter 63. The Kings of Tretayuga

1-13. Suta said- On the bright third moon day of the month of Vaisakha which falls on Thursday, Sudarsana with his relatives, again arrived in the city of Ayodhya. By the grace of Maya Devi, the city which was completely pleasant, well developed, was full of enormous gems and abundant of cereals, he ruled the place for ten thousand years and then reached the abode of Brahma. Dilipa was the son of Sudarsana, Raghu was the son of Dilip, who was bom due to the boon of Nandini. Dilipa ruled the country for ten thousand years, Raghu also ruled the earth for the same length of period. О son of Bhrgu, in the Tretayuga, he started the rule of his dynasty. Then after the boon of a Brahmana, he got a son named Aja. This has been stated. He also ruled the earth for the same period, as was done by his father. Aja then had a son named Dasaratha. Dasaratha had the son named Rama who had been the incarnation of Visnu. Dasaratha had ruled the country for the period equivalent to his own father. Rama, however, ruled the country for eleven thousand years. He had a son named Kusa, who ruled for ten thousand years. Atithi was the son of Kusa, while Nibandha was the son of Atithi. Nibandha had a son named Sakti and Nala was the son of Sakti. Nabha ws the son of Nala, while Nabha had a son named Pundarika. Ksemadhanva was the son of Pundarika. Dvaraka was the son of Ksemadhanva. Dvaraka had a son named Ahinaja. Kuru was the son of Ahinaja, who built in Tretayuga a vast кsetra known as Kuruksetra having an area of a hundred yojana in dimension. The period of rule of all these rulers has been conceived to be the same period in quick succession. Thus in the middle region of Bharata, the first phase of Tretayuga has been concluded.

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ viśvapālastato'bhavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-21. Pariyatra was the son of the king Kuru. Dalapala was the son of Pariyatra. Dalapala’s son was Chadmakari. Chadmakari’s son was Uktha. Vajranabhi was the son of Uktha. Sankhanabhi was the son of Vajranabhi. Sankhnabhi had a son named Vyuthanabhi, who has a son named Visvapala. Visvapala had a son named Svarnanabhi. Svarnanabhi’s son was Puspasena. Puspasena's son was Dhruvasandhi, Dhruvasandhi has a son named Aparvarma. Aparvarma had a son named Sighraganta, who had a son named Marupala. Marupala had a son named PrasuvasSuta who has a son named Susandhi, who starting from the land of the rising sun conquered the area all round. All these rulers ruled the country for the same period as their fathers did. This has been stated.

22-40. Again Susandhi had a son named Mamarba who had a son named Mahasva. Mahasva had a son named Brhadvala. Brhadvala had a son named Brhadaisana, who had a son named Uruksepa. Uruksepa had a son named Vatsapala, who had a son named Vatsavyuha. Vatsavyuha had a son named Prativyoma who had a son named Devakara. Devakra had a son named Sahadeva, who had a son named Brhadasva. Brhadasva had a son named Bhanuratna who had a son named Supratika. Supratika had a son named Marudeva, who had a son named Sunaksetra. Sunaksetra had a son named Kesinara. Kesinara had a son named Antariksa. Antariksa had a son named Suvarnanga, who had a son named Amitrajit. Amitrajit had a son named Brhadraja who had son named Dharmaraja. Dharmaraja had a son named Krtanjaya. Krtanjaya had a son named Rananjaya who had a son named Sanjaya. Sanjaya had a son named Sakyavardhana, who had a son named Krodhadana. Krodhadana had a son named Atulavikrama who had a son named Prasenajit. Prasenajit had a son named Sudraka, who had a son named Suratha. The period of rule of each one of these rulers was successively the same as the one of their fathers. The sixty five rulers of the race of Raghu ruled for half the period as compared to their father. They were the great devotees of the goddess and performed the violent sacrifices. All these rulers achieved the heaven. The sons who became Buddha were termed as illigitimate. During start of the third phase of the Tretayuga, they are said to have regenerated.

41-58. When Indra sent moon - the husband of Rohini on earth, he set up a pleasant city of Prayaga on earth, which was declared as his capital city. The moon was immensely devoted to lord Visnu, but he worshipped Siva as well, everyday. For pleasing the Goddess Maya, he completed the performance of a hundred yajnas. He ruled for eighteen thousand years and left for his heavenly abode, after whom Buddha - his son ruled the country. He is said to be the son of Marudeva. Buddha accepted Ila as his wife in appropriate religious manner and produced from her a son named Pururava, who ruled the country for fourteen thousand years. As per the mutual understanding, he enjoyed the company of UrvasI - the apsara of the heaven and got a son named Ayu, who was quite a religious minded one besides being a devotee of lord Visnu. The king Pururava ruled the country for thirty six thousand years. He even now lives in Gandharvaloka like the gods, enjoying all the comforts. His son Ayu also, like his own father ruled the earth for the same period as was done by his father. Ayu had a son named Nahu§a who enjoyed the kingship as long as his father did. He was subsequently made as Indra. He exercised his control over all the three lokas and ruled the earth for a thousand years. He was ultimately turned as a python, with the curse pronounced by the sage Durvasa. The king Yayati had five sons, out of whom, three were declared as Mlecchas (outcastes), while two of them were accepted as of Arya race. The name of the elder one was Yadu and the younger one was known as Риги. With the influence of his tapas, he enjoyed the kingship for a lakh of years. Ultimately, by the grace of lord Visnu, he achieved the heaven. Kro$fa is said to be the son of Yadu, who ruled the country for sixty thousand years. He had a son named Vrjinaghna who ruled for a period of twenty thousand years. Vrjinaghna had a son named Svaharcana, who had a son named Citraratha, who had a son named Arvinda. All of them also ruled the earth as long as their fathers did so. Arvinda had a son named Srava who was quite illustrious besides being a great devotee of Visnu. He ruled the country for half of period for which his father ruled. Tamasa was the son of Srava, who had a son named Usanasa. Sitamsu had a son known by the name of Kamalamsu. Kamalamsu had a son named Paravata. Jamagha was the son of Paravata. Vidarbha was the son of Krata who had a son named Kuntibhoja, who produced a son from the daughter of Vrsaparva from the nether world.

59-72. While living in the city, Puru produced a son named Mayavidya, who established his capital city in Prajnajyotispura in the vicinity of Prayaga and ruled there for ten thousand years and then proceeded to heaven. The king, who was devoted to the great goddess, had a son named Janamejaya and Janamejaya had a son named Pracinvan, who had a son named Pravira. Pravira had a son named Nabhasya and Nabhasya had a son named Bhavada. Bhavada had a son named Sudyumna who had a son named Bahugara. Bahugara had a son named Samyati who had a son named Dhanayati. Dhanayati had a son named Aindrasva who had a son named Rantinara. Rantinara had a son named Sutapa and Sutapa had a son named Savarana, who retiring to the Himalaya mountain performed tapas for a hundred years. Getting pleased with his tapas, Surya gave away his daughter named Tapati. Thereafter, the king went to Suryaloka. Then, with the influence of Maya (illusion), dissolution of the yuga appeared. There was the water of the oceanic flood everywhere, which destroyed the entire country of Bharata. The entire land together with the mountains remained submerged in oceanic water for two years. Thereafter, with the great force of the wind, the oceanic waters were dried up. Because of the power of Agastya, the dry land could be visible. Within five years, the earth was again covered with greenery and trees. Then at the command of the Sungod, the king Samvarna, the sage Vasistha with the people of all the three varnas, again reached over the earth.

## Chapter 64. Rulers of the Dvapara age

1\. Saunaka said- О Lomaharsana, when did the king Samvama reached here? You also kindly speak about the rulers of the age of Dvapara.

2-16. During the dark fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada, on Friday and on trayodasi tithi, the king Samvarna reached Pratisthanapura with all the sages. The city of Pratisthanapura was built by Visvakarma in an area of five yojanas, which was quite pleasing. There are palaces which have the height of a mile each. In the race of Buddhivamsa, Sakti was the king; in the race of Yaduvarhsa, Satvata was the ruler of Mathura; and in the Mleccha vamsa, Smasrupala was the king of Marudesa. All these rulers devoted their respective kingdoms on earth to the maximum possible extent. The king Samvarna ruled for ten thousand years. Samvarna had a son named Yamarcajna, who had a son named Surijapi. Out of them only, Surijapi had a son named Suryayajna, who always performed yajnas for the Sungod alone. He ruled the country a hundred years less than the period during which his father ruled. Suryayajna had a son named Atithyavardhana, who had a son named Dvadasatama. Divakara was the son of Dvadasatama and Prabhakara was the son of Divakara. Prabhakara had a son named Bhasvadatma, who had a son named Vivasvajjna. Vivasvajjna had a son named Haridasvacana, who had a son named Vaikartana. Vaikartana had a son named Arketiman who had a son named Martandavatsala. He had a son named Mihirartha and Mihirartha had a son Arunpasana. Arunapasana had a son named Dyumanivatsala and Dyumanivatsala had a son named Taraniyajnaka. Taraniyajnaka had a son named Maitrestivardhana who had a son named Citrabhanu. Citrabhanu had a son named Vairocana and Vairocana had a son named Hamsanyayi.

17-34. Hamsanyayi had a son named Vedapravardhana. Vedapravardhana had a son named Savitra. Dhanapala was the son of Savitra. Dhanapala had a son named Mlecchahanta. Anandavardhana was the son of Mlecchahanta. Anandavardhana had a son named Dharmapala. Dharmapala had a son named Brahmabhakta. He had a son named Brahmestivardhana. Out of them, the king Vedapravardhana and Brahmestivardhana ruled for the same duration as their respective fathers did. The rest of the rulers ruled for a hundred years lesser than the period for which their respective fathers ruled the earth. Brahmestivardhana had a son named Atmaprapujaka who had a son named Paramesthi Dhairanyavardhana was the son of Paramesthi. Dhairanyavardhana had a son by the name of Dhatryaji, who ruled the country for a period a little less than a hundred years as compared to the period for which his father ruled. The rest of the rulers ruled for the period during where their respective fathers ruled. Dhatryaji had a son named Vidhatrprapujaka. He had a son named Vaidruhina. Vaidruhina had a son named Vairancya. Vairancya had a son named Kamalasana. He had a son named Samavarti. Samavarti had a son named Sraddhadeva. Sraddhadeva had a son named Pitrvardhana. Pitrvardhana’s son was known as Somadatta, while the son of Somadatta was known as Saumadatti. He had a son named Somavardhana, who had a son named Avamtasa. Avamtasa had a son named Pratamsa, while Pratamsa had a son named Paratamsa. Paratamsa had a son named Ayatamsa. Ayatamsa had a son named Samatamsa. Samatamsa had a son named Anutamsa. Adhitamsa was the son of Anutamsa. The son of Adhitamsa was known as Abhitamsa. His son was known as Samuttamsa, who had a son named Tamsa. Tamsa’s son was Dusyanta. Dusyanta produced a son from the womb of Sakuntala who was known as Bharata. Thereafter, the event of going to heaven occured. The period of rule of all these rulers is said to be equivalent to their respective fathers, leaving the king Kamalasana, who ruled for a period of a hundred years less than this father. The king Bharata was a staunch devotee of the great goddess.
