35-51. By the grace of the great goddess, the period of thirty six years was stretched to thirty six thousand years. The country drives her name from Bharata alone. He divided the earth and established his own kingdom separately. The period of rule is said to be a hundred divine years. Again he had a son named Bharadvaja and Bhardavaja had a son named Manyuman. They ruled the earth for an equal number of years. While ruling the earth for eighteen thousand years, he had a son named Brhatksetra. Brhatksetra had a son named Suhotra and Suhotra had a son named Vltihotra. Vltihotra had a son named Yajnahotra and Yajnahotra had a son named Sakrahotra. Getting pleased with Sakrahotra, Indra granted his stay in the heaven. Out of all them, it was only Vltihotra who ruled for ten thousand years. The rest of the rulers ruled the kingdom successively for the same period as their respective fathers did. A valorous and illustrious king Pratapendra ruled Ayodhya being the lord of that place. He had a son named Mandalika who had a son known as Vijayendra. Vijayendra had a son named Dhanurdipta. These rulers too ruled the country for the same period as was respectively done by their fathers individually. At the same time, at the command of Indra, Sakrahotra together with Ghrtaci - the apsara arrived on earth, conquered Dhanurdipta and started ruling there. Both of them had a son Named Hasti, who riding over Gajendra - the son of Airavata, established a city Hastinapura in the western region. It was located over the bank of Svargaganga and was spread in an area of ten yojanas and looked quite charming. Ue ruled over that place for a period of ten thousand years. He had a son named Ajamidha, while Ajamidha had a son named Raksapala. Raksapala had a son named Susarmyana. Susarmyana had a son named Kuru, who ruled the country for half the period than his father. The rest of the rulers ruled for the same period as was done by their respective fathers. Receiving a boon from Indra, the ruler Kuru reached the heaven with the human body. At that point of time, the king Vrsni of the Satvata race, while living in Mathura, conquered the entire area and put it under his kingdom. With the help of surprising boon of lord Visnu, he ruled that region for five thousand years.

52-75. Thereafter, he had a son named Niravrtti and Niravrtti had a son named Dasari. Dasari had a son named Viyamuna. Viyamuna had a son named Jimuta who had a son named Vikrti. Bhimaratha was the son of Vikrti. Navaratha was the son of Bhimaratha, while Navaratha had a son named Dasaratha. Sakuni was the son of Dasaratha and Kusumbha was the son of Sakuni. Kusumbha had a son named Devaratha, while Devaratha had a son named Devaksetra. Madhu was the son of Devaksetra and Navaratha was the son of Madhu. Kuruvatsa was the son of Navaratha and Anuratha was the son of Kuruvatsa. Anuratha had a son named Puruhotra, while Puruhotra had a son named Citranga. Citranga had a son named Satvatvan and Satvatvan had a son named Bhajaman. Viduratha was the son of Bhajaman. Surabhakta was the son of Viduratha. Surabhakta had a son named Sumana. Sumana had a son named Svayambhuva who had a son named Haridipaka. Haridipaka had a son named Devamedha, who had a son named Surapala. The period of rule of all these rulers was respectively the same as their respective fathers. At the end of the third phase of Dvapara, at the command of Indra - the lord of the heaven, the king Kuru together with his queen known as the Sukesi, arrived in Bharata, and built Kuruksetra, which is also known as the auspicious kseta and was spread in an area of twenty yojanas. Acting as the chief of the region, he graced it for twelve thousand years. Thereafter, he had a son named Jahnu. Suratha was born to Jahnu as a son. Suratha had a son named Viduratha. Viduratha had a son named Sarvabhauma, who had a son named Japasena. Arnava was bom to Japasena as a son who exercised control over all the four oceans. He ruled the country for the same number of years as was done by his father. Aniava had a son named Ayutsya, who ruled the country for ten thousand years. Then Ayutaya had a son named Akrodhana, who had a son named Riksa. Bhimasena was the son of Rksa. Dilipa was the son of Bhimasena. Pratipa was the son of Dilipa, who ruled the country for five thousand years. The rest of the rulers ruled the country for the equivalent number of years, as was done by their respective fathers. Santanu was the son of Pratipa, who ruled the country for a thousand years. He had a son named Vicitravirya, who ruled the country for ten hundred years.

76-97. Pandu was the son of Vicitravirya who ruled the country for five hundred years. Pandu had a son named Yudhisthira, who ruled the country for fifty years. Suyodhana ruled the country for sixty years and he was killed at Kuruksetra by Yudhisthira. In earlier times during the war between gods and the demons, all the daityas who were killed at the hands of asuras, they were reborn in the race of Santanu. In this way, those people had to suffer due to the burden of a lakh of Aksauhini army. Therefore, the goddess earth took refuge with Indra. Thereafter, lord Visnu incarnated on earth from the womb of Devaki - the wife of Vasudeva. Thereafter, the immensely valorous Sri Krsna incarnated on earth, Rohini was killed in due course of time. Sri Krsna made the people on earth comfortable for a hundred and thirty five years and then proceeded to Goloka. The learned people have stated that lord Krsna incarnated on earth during the end of fourth phase of Dvapara. At Hastinapura in Yudhisthira’s family, Abhimanyu was born and Pariksita was born to Abhimanyu, who ruled the country for a thousand years. Again, Janamejaya was born to Pariksita, while Satanika was born of Janamejaya. Yajna was born to Satanika later on. All these rulers ruled for a period of three thousand years. In due course of time, Yajnadatta had a son named Niscakra, who ruled for a period of five thousand years. Niscakra had a son named Ustrapala, who ruled for a thousand years. Citraratha was born to Ustrapala and Dhrtiman was born to Citraratha. Dhrtiman had a son named Susena who had a son named Sunitha. Sunitha had a son named Makhapala. Makhapala’s son was Nacaksu and Nacaksu had a son named Sukhavanta. Pariplava was the son of Sukhavanta who had a son named Sunaya. Sunaya had a son named Medhavi Nrpanjaya was the son of Medhavi, while Mrdu was the son of Nrpanjaya. Mrdu had a son named Tigmajyoti and Brhadratha was the son of Tigmajyoti. Brhadratha had a son named Vasudana, who had a son named Satanika. Udyana was the son of Satanika. Udyana’s son was Ahinara who had a son named Nirmitra. Nirmitra had a son named Ksetraka who disowned his kingdom and set up his dwelling place in a village named Kalapa. Subsequently, he was killed there by the Mleechas, as a result of which he had to fall in the hell. In due course of time, at the advice of Narada, his son Pradyota started performing the Mleccha-yajna in which he destroyed all the Mleechas.

## Chapter 65. The Rulers of Dvapara

## \|\| 2.65.1 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ yajñaḥ kṛtastena pradyotena vicakṣaṇa \|*  
*sarvaṃ kathaya me tāta trikālajña mahāmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Saunaka said- О far-sighted one, О omniscient one, О great ascetic! How did the king Pradyota perform the Mleecha yajna? You kindly speak out the same in detail.

## \|\| 2.65.2-9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ekadā hastinagare pradyotaḥ kṣemakātmajaḥ \|*  
*āsthitaḥ sa kathāmadhye nārado'bhyāgamattadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣito rājā pūjayāmāsa dharmavit \|*  
*sukhopaviṣṭaḥ sa muniḥ pradyotaṃ nṛpamabravīt \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mlecchairhatastava pitā yamalokamato gataḥ \|*  
*mlecchayajñaprabhāveṇa svargatirbhavitā hi saḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tacchrutvā krodhatāmrākṣo brāhmaṇānvedavittamān \|*  
*āhūya sa kurukṣetre mlecchayajñaṃ samārabhat \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yajñakuṃḍaṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ yojanānyeva ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*racitvā devatā dhyātvā mlecchāṃśca juhuyānnṛpaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*hārahūṇānbarbarāṃśca guruṃḍāṃśca śakānkhasān \|*  
*yavanānpallavāṃścaiva romajānkharasaṃbhavān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dvīpa sthitānkāmarūśca cīnānsāgaramadhyagān \|*  
*prāhūya bhasmasātkurvanvedamaṃtraprabhāvataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇāndakṣiṇāṃ dattvā abhiṣekamakārayat \|*  
*kṣemako nāma nṛpatiḥ svargalokaṃ tato gataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

2-9. Suta said- Once in the capital city of Hastinapura, Pradyota - the son of Ksemaka, who was seated over the lion throne and was discussing about the ancient stories, suddenly the sage Narada arrived there. At his arrival, expressing immense delight, the religious-minded king welcomed him appropriately. Taking his seat with comfort, the sage Narada said to the king Pradyota- “Your father has been killed by the Mlecchas, as a result of which he had to proceed to the abode of Yama. Now those Mlecchas can achieve heaven by means of the Mleccha yajna.” Hearing this, getting enraged his eyes became red like the copper. He atonce invited the learned Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas. He started the performing of the Mleccha yajna at Kuruksetra. In the said religious performance, sixteen square yajna-kundas were created. Concentrating his mind on the gods, the king started pouring the offerings of Mlecchas in the fire altar. With the influence of the Vedic hymns, he invoked the Mlecchas from Hara, Huna, Barbara, Gurunda, Saka, Khasa, Yavanas, Pallavas, Romajas, Kharsambhavas, Kamaru - the dwellers of islands, Chinese and those living in the mid-oceanic regions were summoned with the force of the Vedic hymns and were poured in the burning fire flames. They were then reduced to ashes. Thereafter, the king Ksemaka achieved the heaven.

## \|\| 2.65.10-11 \|\|

*mlecchahaṃtā nāma tasya vikhyātaṃ bhuvi sarvataḥ \|*  
*rājyaṃ daśasahasrābdaṃ kṛtaṃ tena mahātmanā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*svargalokaṃ gato rājā tatputro vedavānsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*dvisahasraṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tadā mlecchaḥ kaliḥ svayam \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ pūjayitvā divyāṃ stutimathākarot \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Since that day, the name of the king Pradyota was known in the world as Mleccha-hanta (the killer of Mlecchas). The same king Pradyota, after ruling the earth for ten thousand years, departed for the heaven. After him, his son known by the name of Vedavan, enjoyed the royal pleasures. At that point of time, Mleccha as Kali himself, adoring Narayana, was offering prayer to him with divine stuti.

## \|\| 2.65.12-15 \|\|

*kaliruvāca \|*  
*namo'naṃtāya mahate sarvakālapravartine \|\| 12 \|\|*

*caturyugakṛte tubhyaṃ vāsudevāya sākṣiṇe \|*  
*daśāvatārāya hare namastubhyaṃ namonamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*namaḥ śaktyavatārāya rāmakṛṣṇāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namo matsyāvatārāya mahate gauravāsine \|\| 14 \|\|*

*namo bhaktāvatārāya kalpakṣetranivāsine \|*  
*rājñā vedavatā nātha mama sthānaṃ vināśitam \|*  
*mama priyasya mlecchasya tatpitrā vaṃśanāśanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Kali said- “O Ananta, you are great founder of all the four yugas and the kala, besides being the witness. Salutation to you as Vasudeva. О Hari, salutation to all your ten incarnations. Salutation to the one who incarnated on earth as sakti of Rama and Krsna. Salutation to the great dweller of Gaura country, who is great and incarnated as Matsya. You incarnate for the sake of the devotees and dwell in the Kalpaksetra. Salutation to you. О lord, the king Vedavan has destroyed all my places and his father has destroyed all the Mlecchas.”

## \|\| 2.65.16-24 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti stutastu kalinā mlecchasya saha bhāryayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prāptavānsa hariḥ sākṣādbhagavānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*kaliṃ provāca sa hariryuṣmadarthe yugottamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bahurūpamahaṃ kṛtvā tavecchāṃ pūrayāmyaham \|*  
*ādamo nāma puruṣaḥ patnī havyavatī tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*viṣṇukardamato jātau . mlecchavaṃśapravardhanau \|*  
*haristvantardadhe tatra kalirānaṃdasaṃkulaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*giriṃ nīlācalaṃ prāpya kiṃcitkālamavāsayat \|*  
*putro vedavato jātaḥ sunaṃdo nāma bhūpatiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyamanapatyo mṛtiṃ gataḥ \|*  
*āryadeśāḥ kṣīṇavaṃto mlecchavaṃśā balānvitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyaṃti bhṛguśreṣṭha tasmācca tuhinācalam \|*  
*gatvā viṣṇuṃ samārādhya gamiṣyāmo hareḥ padam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā dvijāḥ sarve naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi gatāste tuhinācalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*viśālāyāṃ samāsādya viṣṇugāthāṃ pracakṣire \|*  
*iti vyāsena kathitaṃ vākyaṃ kaliviśāradam \|*  
*śrotāraṃ sa manaḥ kṛtvā bhaviṣyaṃ samudīrayat \|\| 24 \|\|*

16-24. Suta said- When Mleccha Kali so prayed to the lord who is dear to his devotees, Visnu appeared before him in person. Then the lord Narayana spoke to Kali- “The present yuga is the best for you people. I am prepared to fulfil all your desires in this yuga, taking to any form. A human named Adama and his wife named Havyavati shall expand the race of Mlecchas. Both of them shall be born of Kardama.” Thus speaking, lord Visnu disappeared at the same time and place. At that point of time, Kali was absorbed in bliss. Thereafter, reaching the Nilgiri mountain, he stayed there for sometime. On the other hand, Vedvan had a son named Sunanda who ruled the country for the same period as his father did. But being childless, he left the world. Thereafter, О Brahmanas - the dwellers of Naimisa forest, the Arya country shall decline and the people of Mleccha country shall become more powerful. Therefore, all of us, retiring over Himalaya, should worship lord Visnu so that we may achieve Visnuloka. Listening to the above talk, twenty eight thousand people got ready to proceed to Himalaya. Reaching Visala - the great city, those people propagated the story of Lord Visnu. In this way, making his own mind as the listener, the sage Vyasa, addressing it (his own mind), spoke out all the details relating to the age of Kali.

## \|\| 2.65.25 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*manaḥ śṛṇu tato gāthāṃ bhāvī sūtena varṇitām \|*  
*kaleryugasya pūrṇāṃ tāṃ tacchrutvā tṛptimāvaha \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Vyasa said - “O my mind, the story as narrated by Suta is going to be enacted in the age of Kali. Be peaceful after listening to it.”

## \|\| 2.65.26-35 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ṣoḍaśābdasahasre ca śeṣe taddvāpare yuge \|*  
*bahukīrtimatī bhūmirāryadeśasya kīrtitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kvacidviprāḥ smṛtā bhūpāḥ kvacidrājanyavaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*kvacidvaiśyāḥ kvacicchūdrāḥ kutracidvarṇasaṃkarāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dviśatāṣṭasahasre dve śeṣe tu dvāpare yuge \|*  
*mlecchadeśasya yābhūmirbhavitā kīrtimālinī \|\| 28 \|\|*

*iṃdriyāṇi damitvā yo hyātmadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tasmādādamanāmāsau patnī havyavatī smṛtā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pradānanagarasyaiva pūrvabhāge mahāvanam \|*  
*īśvareṇa kṛtaṃ ramyaṃ catuḥkrośāyataṃ smṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*pāpavṛkṣatale gatvā patnīdarśanatatparaḥ \|*  
*kalistatrāgatastūrṇaṃ sarparūpaṃ hi tatkṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vaṃcitā tena dhūrtena viṣṇvājñā bhaṃgatāṃ gatā \|*  
*khāditvā tatphalaṃ ramyaṃ lokamārgapradaṃ patiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*uduṃbarasya patraiśca tābhyāṃ vāyvaśanaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*sutāḥ putrāstato jātāḥ sarve mlecchā babhūvire \|\| 33 \|\|*

*triṃśottaraṃ navaśataṃ tasyāyuḥ parikīrtitam \|*  
*phalānāṃ havanaṃ kurvanpatnyā saha divaṃ gataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tasmājjātaḥ sutaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ śvetanāmeti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśottaravarṣaṃ ca tasyāyuḥ parikīrtitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

26-35. Suta said - When the sixteen thousand years of Dvapara are left, the land of the Arya country would be losing its glory. At places, the Brahmanas would be the rulers and at places, the Ksatriyas would rule the country. At places, the Vaisyas will rule; at places the Sudras would be the kings; while at places the people of the mixed breed would rule. When eight thousand and two hundred years of Dvapara yuga are left out, the land of Mleccha country which had been glorious, in that land a person who practices spiritualism, he because of that would be known as Adama and his wife Would be known as Havyavati. Over the eastern part of the main city, there is a vast forest which is spread in the four kronas. Going there, under the tree of sins, he expressed his desire to meet his wife. At that point of time, Kali reached there taking to the form of a serpent. The wicked serpent shattered the command of lord Visnu, Thereafter, the divine couple, who was to lead the path of the people, consumed the pleasant and delicious fruit. Then the couple consumed the wind through the leaf of a wild fig tree. Thereafter, the children born to the couple were all Mlecchas. His age is said to be nine hundred and thirty years. Performing the homa with fruits, he left for heavenly abode. With his wife, he had a son named Sveta, who had the age of a hundred and twelve years. He had a son named Anuha, who ruled the country a hundred years less than his father did.

36-46. Again Anuha had a son named Kinasa, who ruled the country for as long as his grandfather did. He had a son named Mahallala who ruled the country for a period of nine hundred and ninety five years. Mahallala had a son named Managara and Managara had a son named Virada, who ruled for a period of nine hundred and sixty years. He established a city also by his name. He had a son named Hanuka, who was immensely devoted to lord Visnu and always performed the homas of fruits. He was well-versed in the parmartha-tattva (or subtle truth). He ruled the country for three hundred and sixty five years. He was the follower of Mleccha dharma and achieved the heaven with his human body. By his conduct and thought, he functioned like a Brahmana and worshipped the gods. Because of this type of his conduct, he got devoted to dharma and did not conduct as a Mleccha. He was a devotee of Visnu, worshipped the fire, practiced non-violence, tapas and self restraint. These are the performance of the people of nobility. О Bhargava, Наnuка had a son named Matocchita, who ruled the country for nine hundred and seventy years. A son named Lomaka was bom to Matocchita, who ruled the country for seven hundred years and after which he proceeded on to the heaven. Nyuha was the son of Lomaka, who ruled for five hundred years. He had three sons, known by the names of Sima, Sama and Bhava. Nyuha was a devotee of lord Visnu. He always followed the vedantic ideology of So ’ham.

*ekadā bhagavānviṣṇustatsvapne tu samāgataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vatsa nyūha śṛṇuṣvedaṃ pralayaḥ saptame'hani \|*

*catvāriṃśaddinānyeva mahāvṛṣṭimakārayat \|*

*nyūhaśca svakulaissārdhaṃ śeṣāssarve vināśitāḥ \|*

47-54. Once lord Visnu informed him in a dream that after a week from this day, there would be a deluge in this world. Therefore, together with your own relatives, you should board a boat and save your life. О best of my devotees, you will be known as the best of my devotees. Accepting the command of the lord, all of them boarded a boat which was three hundred cubits in length and fifty cubits in width, besides being thirty cubits in height. He made all the people of his race besides all the creatures to board the boat and got himself devoted to Visnu. The Samvartaka Megha-gana dropped excessive rain for a period of forty days continuously as a result of which all the four oceans joined together. The whole country of Bharata was submerged in water except the city of Visala. Nyuha, together with twenty eight thousand Rsis well-versed in Brahman and the people of his own race, but all were destroyed except Nyuha. Thereafter, the R$is started eulogising Visnu-maya.

*abdāṃtare mahī sarvā sthalī bhūtvā pradṛśyate \|*

55-60. The Munis said - О goddess Mahakali, salutation to you. О Mahalaksmi, you are the mother of lord Visnu. Salutation to the goddess Radha. Salutation to Revati, Puspavati, Kamaksa and the mother. With the force of Mahavayu and the thunder of the huge clouds, we are facing gross danger because of the terrific water waves. Therefore, О Bhairavl, the protection of all of us is in your hands. Thereafter, the goddess getting pleased, made the water peaceful. After one year, the earth became visible in water. Close to the Himadri, a pari of it was left (without water), the king Nyuha together with all his relatives stepped down from the boat at that place. Thereafter, they lived on land.

## Chapter 66. Rulers of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.66.1 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ vartate yo vai pralayāṃte munīśvara \|*  
*divyadṛṣṭiprabhāvena jñātaṃ brūhi tataḥ param \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Saunaka said- О great sage, the rulers who appeared after the delusion (or the present times) you are well aware of them because of your divine vision. Therefore, you also speak out about them.

## \|\| 2.66.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nyūho nāma smṛto mleccho viṣṇumohaṃ tadākarot \|*  
*tadā prasanno bhagavāṃstasya vaṃśaḥ pravarddhitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*mlecchabhāṣā kṛtā tena vedavākyaparāṅmukhā \|*  
*kaleśca vṛddhaye brāhmīṃ bhāṣāṃ kṛtvā'paśabdagām \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Suta said- The Mleccha king Nyuha pleased lord Visnu with his devotion. The lord, getting pleased with Nytiha, expanded his race. He used Mleccha-language against the Vedas for the development of Kali. Brahmi language was brought in use, creating the end words.

## \|\| 2.66.4-12 \|\|

*nyūhāya dattavāndevo buddhīśo buddhigaḥ svayam \|*  
*vilomaṃ ca kṛtaṃ nāma nyūhena trisutasya vai \|\| 4 \|\|*

*simaśca hāmaśca tathā yākūto nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*yākūtaḥ saptaputraśca jumro mājūja eva saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mādī tathā ca yūnānastūvalomasakastathā \|*  
*tīrāsaśca tathā teṣāṃ nāmabhirdeśa ucyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*jumrā daśa kanābjaśca riphataśca tajarrumaḥ \|*  
*tannāmnā ca smṛtā deśā yūnādyā ye sutāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ilīśastaralīśaśca kittīhūdānirucyate \|*  
*caturbhirnāmabhirdeśāsteṣāṃ teṣāṃ pracakrire \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dvitīyatanayāddhāmātsutāścatvāra eva te \|*  
*kuśo miśraśca kūjaśca kanaāṃstatra nāmabhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*deśāḥ prasiddhā mlecchānāṃ kuśātṣaṭtanayāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*sa vā caiva havīlaśca sarvatoragamastathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tathā savatikā nāma nimarūho mahābalaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ putrāśca kalanaḥ siṃnāroraka ucyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*akkado vāvunaścaiva rasanādeśakāśca te \|*  
*śrāvayitvā munīnsūto yoganidrāvaśaṃ gataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

4-12. The extra intelligent lord of wisdom himself created these languages for Nyuha, bestowing wisdom on him at the same time. Thereafter, using the reverse order, Nyuha gave the names of his three sons as- Sima, Hama and Yakuta. Yakuta - the son of Nyuha, had seven sons known as - Jumra, Majuja, Yunana, Tuva, Lomasaka, Tirasa and Madi. Each one of them had also a country according to their names. These countries are known as- Jumra, Dasakanabja, Riphata, Tajarruma etc. These are the countries for Yunana and his other sons. Ilisa, Taralisa, Kitti and Hudani are known as the four separate countries. His second son had four sons known as- Kanana, Misra, Kuja and Kusa. The Mleccha countries were known after each one of them. The names of Kusa were - Sava, Habila, Sarvatoragma, Savitaka and Nimruha. All of them had the sons named- Akkada, Bavuna, Rasana and Desaka. Listening to these words, all the sages were absorbed in yoganidra.

## \|\| 2.66.13-22 \|\|

*dvisahasre śatābdānte buddhvā punarathābravīta \|*  
*simavaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi simo jyeṣṭhaḥ sa bhūpatiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rājyaṃ paṃcaśataṃ varṣaṃ tena mlecchena satkṛtam \|*  
*arkansadastasya sutaścatustriṃśacca rājyakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*catuśśataṃ punarjñeyaṃ siṃhastattanayo'bhavat \|*

*saptatriṃśacca dviśataṃ tasya rājyaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tasmācca jūja utpannaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*nahūrastasya tanayo vayaḥ ṣaṣṭyuttaraṃ śatam \|*  
*rājyaṃ cakāra nṛpatirbahuśatrūnvihiṃsayan \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tāharastasya tanayaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*tasmātputro'virāmaśca nahūro hāranastrayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evaṃ teṣāṃ smṛtā vaṃśā nāmamātreṇa kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*sarasvatyāśca śāpena mlecchabhāṣā mahādhamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ vṛddhiḥ kalau cāsītsaṃkṣepeṇa prakīrtitā \|*  
*saṃskṛtasyaiva vāṇī tu bhārataṃ varṣamūhyatām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*anyakhaṃḍe gatā saiva mlecchā hyānaṃdino'bhavan \|*  
*evaṃ te vipra kathitaṃ viṣṇubhaktadvijaissaha \|\| 22 \|\|*

13-22. After the lapse of two thousand and eight hundred years, Budha again said— It shall mention about the Sima race in which the king named Sima was first born. The Mleccha king ruled the country for five hundred years. Thereafter, he got a son named Arkansada, who graced the royal throne for four hundred and thirty four years. He was succeeded by his son Simha whose reign extended upto four hundred and eight years. He had a son named Dvra. He ruled the country as long as his father did. Phalaja was the name of his son, who ruled for a period of two hundred years. He had a son named Rau whose reign extended upto two hundred and thirty seven years. His son was known as Juja, who ruled the country like his father. He had a son named Nihura. He ruled the country for a hundred and sixty years. Nuhur’s son was Tahir who also ruled like his father. He had three sons named Avirama, Nahura and Harana. Their race has been mentioned for the name’s sake only. Because of the curse of the goddess Sarasvati, these Mlecchas used the extremely degraded Mleccha language, who have been mentioned in the age of Kaliyuga quite briefly. Sanskrit is the basic language of Bharatavarsa, which delighted those people travelling to the other countries. О dear one, thus the Brahmanas who were devoted to lord Visnu, I have narrated their story and am now concluding it.

## \|\| 2.66.23-26 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā munayassarve viśālāyāṃ nivāsinaḥ \|*  
*naraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ saṃpūjya vinayānvitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dhyānaṃ cakrurmudā yuktā dviśataṃ parivatsarān \|*  
*tatpaścādbodhitāssarve śaunakādyā munīśvarāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saṃdhyātarpaṇadevārcāḥ kṛtvā dhyātvā janārddanam \|*  
*lomaharṣaṇamāsīnaṃ papracchurvinayānvitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vyāsaśiṣya mahābhāga ciraṃ jīva mahāmate \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ vartate yo vai rājā tanme vada prabho \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. Vyasa said- Listening to this narration, the people of the city of Visala, together with all the ascetics and sages, offering prayers to Nara-Narayana and adoring them, delightfully adored them for two hundred years. Thereafter, the ascetics named Saunaka and others achieved the divine knowledge. Performing oblation and worship of the gods and meditating upon lord Janardana, they humbly questioned the sage Lomaharsana. They said- “O disciple of the sage Vyasa and О intelligent one, let you enjoy the long life. О lord you kindly narrate the story of the person who is presently ruling the country.”

*āvante śaṃkhanāmā'sau sāṃprataṃ vartate nṛpaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*mlecchadeśe śakapatiratha rājyaṃ karoti vai \|*

*tacchrutvā munayaḥ sarve rodanaṃ cakrire bahu \|\| 41 \|\|*

27-41. Suta said- О son of Bhargava, after the laps of three thousand years of the age of Kali, during the present time, there is a king named Sankha who is ruling Anantapura. The way in which the race of Sakapati was expanded in the Mleccha country, is being narrated by me. You please listen. When a period of two thousand years will pass in Kaliyuga, the Mleccha-vamsa will expand. During this period, the entire earth would became Mleccha like, several types of sects shall prevail on earth. Besides the Brahmavarta country, in some other land, on the bank of the river Sarasvati, Musa - the aсаrуа of Mlecchas shall propagate the religion of Mlecchas in the entire country. It is stated that the Vedas as well as the language of the Vedas would disappear during the age of Kali. О sage, Mleccha language is of four types. I am going to speak out the related symptoms. You listen. Vrajabhasa, Mahara§trl, YavanI and Gururujika are the four parts of the language of Mlecchas. These languages have four lakhs other parts. When these languages are in vogue, Paniya is known as pani (or water), hunger is called bhukha. At places, paniya is also spoken as papadi. Food or (bhojana) is known as kakkana, while dhuti (offering) is spoken as aju. Instead of jana (thigh), people speak as jainu, while for sapta-sindhu, they speak sapta-hindhu in the languages of Yavanas. Similarly, in the language of the whites Ravaivara is spoken as Sunday, the month of Phalguna is known as the month of February and Sasthi is known as sixty. This has been stated that all the seven puras of Bharata will be facing violence (in one form or the other). This is because in the Arya country, the robbers, Sabaras, Bhilas and fools would prevail. In the Mleccha countries, people inspite of being wise shall follow the Mleccha-dharma, because all the virtues would be in hands of the Mlecchas and all the blemishes shall be possessed by the Aryan people. Mlecchas would rule the Bharatavarsa and other countries. О best of the sags and О Intelligent one, thus realising, you should be devoted to the lord. Listening to these narrations, the people wept bitterly.

## Chapter 67. Rulers of Kali Age

## \|\| 2.67.1-3 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca \|*  
*brahmāvarte kathaṃ mlecchā na prāptāḥ kāraṇaṃ vada \|*  
*sūtaḥ prāha śṛṇuṣvedaṃ sarasvatyāḥ prabhāvataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mlecchāḥ prāptā na tatsthāne kāśyapo nāma vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*kalau prāpte sahasrābde svargātprāptaḥ surājñayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*āryāvatī ca tatpatnī daśa putrānakalmaṣān \|*  
*kāśyapātsā labdhavatī teṣāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said- You listen to the reason for the same. Because of the influence of Sarasvati - the great goddess, the Mlecchas could not reach that country. After the expiry of a thousand years of the age of Kali, at the command of the gods, a Brahmana named Kasyapa reached that country from the heaven. The name of his wife was Aryavati. The divine couple then produced ten sons in an auspicious manner. I am going to speak out their names, you please listen.

## \|\| 2.67.4-7 \|\|

*upādhyāyo dīkṣitaśca pāṭhakaḥ śuklamiśrakau \|*  
*agnihotrī dvivedī ca trivedī pāṇḍya eva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*caturvedīti kathitā nāmatulyaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye kāśyapaśca sarvajñānamasamanvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kāśmīre prāptavānso'pi jagadambāṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*tuṣṭāva pūjanaṃ kṛtvā raktapuṣpaistvathākṣataiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dhūpairdīpaiśca naivedyaiḥ puṣpāṃjalisamanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. They were known by the names of Upadhyaya, Diksita, Pathaka, Sukla, Misra, Agnihotri, Dvivedi, Trivedi, Pandya and Caturvedi. These are the names of those sons and the qualities of each one of them were according to their merits. Kasyaра was the omniscient one. He went to Kasmira and worshipped the goddess Jagadamba Sarasvati, with red flowers and rice. After offering incense, lamp and eatables, he started eulogising her with hand cup full of flowers.

## \|\| 2.67.8-20 \|\|

*kāśyapa uvāca \|*  
*mātaḥ śaṃkaradayite mayi te karuṇā kuto nāsti \|*  
*bho'si tvaṃ jagadaṃbā jagataḥ kiṃ māṃ bahirna yasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*devi tvaṃ surahetordharmadrohiṇamāśu haṃsi mātaḥ \|*  
*uttamasaṃskṛtabhāṣāṃ tvaṃ kuru mlecchāṃśca mohayeḥ śīghram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*aṃba tvaṃ bahurūpā huṃkārā ddhūmralocanaṃ hasi \|*  
*bhīmaṃ durgā daityaṃ hatvā jagatāṃ sukhaṃ nayasi \|\| 10 \|\|*

*daṃbhaṃ mohaṃ ghoraṃ garvaṃ hatvā sadā sukhaṃ śeṣe \|*  
*bodhaya mātarjagato duṣṭānnaṣṭā nkuru tvaṃ vai \|*  
*tadā prasannā sā devī bho munestasya mānase \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vāsaṃ kṛtvā dadau jñānaṃ miśradeśe munirgataḥ \|*  
*sarvānmlecchānmohayitvā kṛtvātha tāndvijanmanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saṃkhyādaśasahasraṃ ca naravṛndaṃ dvijanmanām \|*  
*dvisahasraṃ smṛtā vaiśyāḥ śeṣāḥ śūdrasutāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*taiḥ sārddhamāryadeśe sa sarasvatyāḥ prasādataḥ \|*  
*avasadvai muniśreṣṭho munikāryarataḥ sadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*teṣāmāryasamūhānāṃ devyāśca varadānataḥ \|*  
*vṛddhirbhavati bahulā catuṣkoṭinarāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca tadbhūpaḥ kāśyapo muniḥ \|*  
*viṃśottaraśataṃ varṣaṃ tasya rājyaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*rājyaputrākhyadeśe ca śūdrāścāṣṭasahasrakāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhūpaścāryapṛthustasmājjātassa māgadhaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*māgadhaṃ nāma tatputramabhiṣicya yayau muniḥ \|*  
*iti śrutvā bhṛguśreṣṭhaḥ śaunako harṣamāgataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sūtaṃ paurāṇikaṃ natvā viṣṇudhyānaparo'bhavat \|*  
*punaśca śrutivarṣānte bodhitā munayastathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*nityanaimittikaṃ kṛtvā papracchuridamādarāt \|*  
*lomaharṣaṇa me brūhi ke rājānaśca māgadhāt \|*  
*kalau rājyaṃ kṛtaṃ yaistu vyāsaśiṣya vadasva naḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

8-20. Каsуара said- О mother, why don’t you feel compassionate for me? You are the mother of the universe, then why are you driving me out of the world. О goddess, О mother, you at once destroy the people who are inimical to dharma for the sake of the gods. The excellent Sanskrit language should always predominate. For this purpose, you confuse all the Mlecchas. О mother, you have many forms. You destroyed Dhumralocana with a single humkara. You also killed the terrific daitya named Bhima and by so doing, you made the entire world comfortable. Destroying the cheating, confusion and the arrogance, you always sleep with comfort. Therefore, О mother, bestowing the divine knowledge on me, destroy the wicked people on earth. О sages, the goddess then getting pleased, dwelling in the mind of (Kasyapa) bestowed knowledge on him as a result of which the Maharsi proceeded to the country of Misra. Reaching there, he confused all the Mlecchas. Then he divided the society by declaring ten thousands as Brahmanas and K§atriyas, two thousand as Vaisyas and the rest were declared as the Sudras. After sometime, together with their sons, he reached the Arya country and lived there by the grace of the goddess Sarasvati. The best of the sages then lived there as a great sage. Because of the boon of the goddess, the Aryans expanded immensely. Ultimately, the number of men and women increased to four crores. During the time of their sons and grandsons, the sage Kasyapa functioned as a ruler. He ruled the country for a hundred and twenty years. In the region of the prince, the number of Madras was eight thousand. Arya Prthu happened to be their king, who had a son named Magadha. Crowning the Magadha prince as the king, the sage departed from that place. On hearing this, the best of Bhrgus, known as Saunaka, felt extremely delighted. Offering his salutation to Suta of the Puranas, he again concentrated his mind on lord Visnu. After the lapse of four years, after performing the routine types of activities, the sages getting pleased asked him- “O Lomaharsana. who were the rulers after Magadha who enjoyed to rule the country in the age of Kali? О disciple of Vyasa, you kindly speak about the matter in detail.”

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*māgadho māgadhe deśe prāptavānkāśyapātmajaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pitṛrājyaṃ smṛtaṃ tena tvāryadeśaḥ pṛthakkṛtaḥ \|*  
*pāñcālātpūrvato deśo māgadhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*āgneyyāṃ ca kaliṃgaśca tathāvantastu dakṣiṇe \|*  
*ānartadeśā nairṛtyāṃ siṃdhudeśastu paścime \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vāyavyāṃ kaikayo deśo madradeśastathottare \|*  
*īśāne caiva koṇindaścāryadeśaśca tatkṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*deśanāmnā tasya sutā magadhasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tebhyoṃśāni pradattāni tatpaścātkratumudvahan \|\| 25 \|\|*

*balabhadrastadā tuṣṭo yajñabhāvena bhāvitaḥ \|*  
*śiśunāgaḥ kratorjāto balabhadrāṃśasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*aśītivarṣaṃ rājyaṃ tatkṣetraujāstatsuto'bhavat \|*  
*daśahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ vedamiśrastato'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*daśahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tato'jātaripussutaḥ \|*  
*daśahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ darbhakastanayo'bhavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

*daśahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyamudayāśvastato'bhavat \|*  
*daśahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ naṃdavardhana eva tat \|\| 30 \|\|*

*daśahīnaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasmānnaṃdasuto'bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ śūdrīgarbhasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nandājjātaḥ pranandaśca daśavarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*

*tasmājjātassamānaṃdo viṃśadvarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*tasmājātaḥ priyānaṃdaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*devānaṃdastasya sutaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*yajñabhaṃgaḥ sutastasmātpiturarddhaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*mauryānaṃdastasya sutaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*mahānandastato jātaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 35 \|\|*

21-35. Suta said - Magadha - the son of Kasyapa, reaching the country of Magadha, taking it to be the ancestral kingdom, separated the Arya country from the same. The region to the east of Magadha is known as Pancala country. Similarly, the region to the south-east of the same region is known as Kalinga; Avanta is in the south; while in the south-west Anarta is located. In the western region, the Sindhu country is there and in the north-west region, Kaikeya country is lodged. Madradesa is located in the north. In the north-east, Koninda country is located. A son named Desa was born to Magadha. Giving away his share to him, Magadha started performing a yajna and getting influenced with the same, Balabhadra expressed immense delight. Then from the amsa of Balabhadra, a son named Sisunaga was born who ruled for a hundred years. Sisunaga had a son named Kakavarma who ruled the country for ninety years. Ksemadharma. was the son of Kakavarma, who ruled for eighty years. Ksemadharma had a son named Ksetrauja who ruled for less than ten years than his father. He had a son named Vedamisra who ruled the country ten years less than his father. Vedamisra had a son named Ajataripu and Ajataripu had a son named Dharbhaka. Dharbhaka had a son named Udayasva and Udayasva had a son named Nandavardhana. Nandavardhana had a son named Nanda, who is said to have been bom of a Sudra-woman. He ruled the country for the same period as was done by his father. All the aforesaid rulers ruled the country ten years less than their respective fathers. Again Nanda had a son named Prananda, who ruled the country just for a period of ten years. He had a son named Parananda who ruled the country for the same period for which his father ruled. Parananda had a son named Samananda, who ruled the country for twenty years. Priyananda was the son of Samananda, while Priyananda had a son named Devananda. Devananda had a son named Yajnabhanga, who ruled the country for half of the period as compared to his father. All the aforesaid rulers ruled their countries for the same period for which their fathers did rule. Yajnabhanga had a son named Mauryananda and Mauryananda had a son named Mahananda, who ruled the country for the same duration for which his father did rule.

## \|\| 2.67.36-49 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu kalinā saṃsmṛto hariḥ \|*  
*kāśyapādudbhavo devo gautamo nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bauddhadharmaṃ ca saṃskatya paṭṭaṇe prāptavānhariḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasmācchākyamuniḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*viṃśadvarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasmācchuddhodano'bhavat \|*  
*triṃśadvarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ śākya siṃhastato'bhavat \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śatādrau dvisahasre'bde vyatīte so'bhavannṛpaḥ \|*  
*kaleḥ prathamacaraṇe vedamārgo vināśitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭivarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ sarvabauddhā narāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*

*viṣṇorvīryānusāreṇa jagaddharmaḥ pravarttate \|*  
*tasminharau ye śaraṇaṃ prāptā māyāpatau narāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*api pāpasamācārā mokṣavaṃtaḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*śakyasiṃhādbuddhasiṃhaḥ piturarthaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*caṃdraguptastasya sutaḥ paurasā dhipateḥ sutām \|*  
*sulūvasya tathodvāhya yāvanībauddhatatparaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭivarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ biṃdusārastato'bhavat \|*  
*pitṛstulya kṛtaṃ rājyamaśokastanayo'bhavat \|\| 44 \|\|*

*etasminneva kāle tu kānyakubjo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*arbudaṃ śikharaṃ prāpya brahmahomamathākarot \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vedamaṃtraprabhāvācca jātāścatvāri kṣatriyāḥ \|*  
*pramarassāmavedī ca capahāniryajurvidaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*trivedī ca tathā śuklotharvā sa parihārakaḥ \|*  
*airāvatakule jātāngajānāruhya te pṛthak \|\| 47 \|\|*

*aśokaṃ svavaśaṃ cakussarve bauddhā vināśitāḥ \|*  
*caturlakṣāḥ smṛtā bauddhāḥ divyaśastraiḥ prahāritāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*avante pramaro bhūpaścaturyojanavistṛtām \|*  
*ambāvatīṃ nāma purīmadhyāsya sukhito'bhavat \|\| 49 \|\|*

36-49. At that point of time, praying the lord, Kali pleased him. Hari was born of Kasyapa as Gautama. This is commonly known. Patronising the Buddhist faith, he went to Pattana and ruled for ten years. In due course of time, Sakyamuni was born to him, who ruled for twenty years. Suddhodana was born to Sakyamuni, who ruled for thirty years. He had a son named Sakyasimha. He was born after the lapse of two thousand years of Kali. During the first phase of Kali age, the same ruler destroyed the Vedic faith. He ruled for a period of sixty years. During his rule, all the people accepted the Buddhist faith. The people consider the king to be the form of Visnu and it is well known that as is the king, so are the subjects. This proverb was established. The worldly faiths move according to the strength of Visnu. During that period, the people who take refuge with lord Visnu, they became entitled to achieving moksa inspite of their being the grave sinners. Sakyasimha had a son named Buddhasimha, who ruled the country for half of the period for which his father ruled. Candragupta was the son of Buddhasimha who married the Yavana daughter of Suluvasya. The said Bauddha king ruled the country for a period of sixty years. Bindusara was the son of Candragupta. He ruled the country for the same duration for which his father ruled. Asoka was born to Bindusura. At the same time, a Brahmana known as Kanyakubja started performing a homa over the Arbuda mountain. With the influence of the Vedic hymns, four Ksatriyas were born. Out of these, Pramara belonged to Samaveda, Capahani belonged to Yajurveda. Besides Trivedi were well-versed in the Sukla Atharvaveda. The separate elephants of the race of Airavata were given to each one of them for their use. All of them conquered Asoka and overpowered four lakhs of the Buddhists. They destroyed some of them. Thereafter, the king named Pramara made Ambavati - a city of Ananta Pradesa, as his capital and started living there comfortably.

## Chapter 68. Details of the rulers of Lunar dynasty

## \|\| 2.68.1-4 \|\|

*iti prathamakhaṃḍaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*adhyāsya bauddhahaṃtā sa sukhitobhavadūrjitaḥ \|*  
*rājaputrākhyadeśe ca capahānirmahīpatiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ajamerapuraṃ ramyaṃ vidhiśobhāsamanvitam \|*  
*cāturvarṇyayutaṃ divyamadhyāsya sukhito'bhavat \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śuklo nāma mahīpālo gata ānarta'maṃḍale \|*  
*dvārakāṃ nāma nagarīmadhyāsya sukhito'bhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said- A king named Parihara built up a beautiful city known as Kalinjara, which was

spread into a krosa and made it as his capital city. He made it as his dwelling place. He was the destroyer of the Buddhists and lived his life with comfort there. In the region of Rajaputra, the king Capahani built the city of Ajmera, which was quite beautiful from the artistic and architectural point of view. It was inhabited by the people of all the four varnas. By making that city as his dwelling place, he felt quite comfortable. A ruler known by the name of Sukla built a city named Dvaraka in the Anarta country and felt quite comfortable there.

## \|\| 2.68.5 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca \|*  
*teṣāmagnyudbhavānāṃ ca ye bhūpā rājyasatkṛtāḥ \|*  
*tānme brūhi mahābhāga sūto vākyamathābravīt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Saunaka said- O fortunate one, the rulers who were born of fire, have ruled the country gracefully. You please speak about them too.

## \|\| 2.68.6 \|\|

*gacchadhvaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ sarve yoganidrāvaśo hyaham \|*  
*tacchutvā munayaḥ sarve viṣṇordhyānaṃ pracakrire \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It would be better in case all the Brahmanas leave this place, because I am presently overpowered by sleep (yoganidra) and unable to speak out anything. Listening to these words, all the Brahmanas then meditated upon lord Visnu.

## \|\| 2.68.7-15 \|\|

*pūrṇe dve ca sahasrānte sūto vacanamabravīt \|*  
*saptatriṃśaśate varṣe daśābde cādhike kalau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pramaro nāma bhūpālaḥ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ ca ṣaṭsamāḥ \|*  
*mahāmadastato jātaḥ piturardhaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*devāpistanayastasya pitu stulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*devadūtastasya sutaḥ pitustulyaṃ smṛtaṃ padam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmādgaṃdharvasenaśca paṃcāśadabdabhūpadam \|*  
*kṛtvā ca svasutaṃ śaṃkhamabhiṣicya vanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śaṃkhena tatpadaṃ prāptaṃ rājyaṃ triṃśatsamāḥ kṛtam \|*  
*devāṃganā vīramatī śakreṇa preṣitā tadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*gaṃdharvasenaṃ saṃprāpya putraratnamajījanat \|*  
*sutasya janmakāle tu nabhasaḥ puṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*peturduṃdubhayo nedurvāṃti vātāḥ sukhapradāḥ \|*  
*śivadṛṣṭirdvijo nāma śiṣyaissārddhaṃ vanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*viṃśadbhiḥ karmayogaṃ ca samārādhya śivo'bhavat \|*  
*pūrṇe triṃśacchate varṣe kalau prāpte bhayaṃkare \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śakānāṃ ca vināśārthamāryadharmavivṛddhaye \|*  
*jātaśśivājñayā so'pi kailāsādguhyakālayāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

7-15. After the lapse of two thousand years, Suta again addressed these Rsis. After the expiry of three thousand seven hundred and ten years, the king named Pramara ruled there who ruled the country for six years. Pramara had a son named Mahamada, who ruled the country for half a period than his father did. Mahamada had a son named Deva, who had a son named Devaduta. Gandharvasena was born to Devaduta, who ruled the country for fifty years. The rest of the rulers ruled for the same period for which their respective fathers did. In due course of time, Gandharvasena crowned his own son named Sankha as the ruler and retired to the forest. After the expiry of a period of three years of the rule of Sankha, Indra deputed an apsara named Viramati to Gandharvasena in the forest. Gandharvasena accepted her and produced a son from her. With the birth of the son, there was a rain of flowers from the sky with the sound of kettle drums. The pleasant wind started blowing. Because of Siva being graceful over the child, the Brahmana together with his disciples retired deeper into the forest, where he practiced Karmayoga and finally achieved the form of Siva. After the expiry of three thousand years of the age of Kali, during the terrific times, for the destruction of Sakas and for the expansion of the religion of Aryans, at the command of Siva, he again had to associate himself with the Guhyakas.

## \|\| 2.68.16-26 \|\|

*vikramādityanāmānaṃ pitā kṛtvā mumoda ha \|*  
*sa bālo'pi mahāprājñaḥ pitṛ mātṛpriyaṃkaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pañcavarṣe vayaḥprāpte tapaso'rthe vanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*dvādaśābdaṃ prayatnena vikrameṇa kṛtaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*paścādambāvatīṃ divyāṃ purīṃ yātaḥ śriyānvitaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ ramyaṃ dvātriṃśanmūrtisaṃyutam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śivena preṣitaṃ tasmai sopi tatpadamagrahīt \|*  
*vaitālastasya rakṣārthaṃ pārvatyā nirmito gataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ekadā sa nṛpo vīro mahākāleśaśvarasthalam \|*  
*gatvā sampūjayāmāsa devadevaṃ pinākinam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sabhā dharmamayī tatra nirmitā vyūhavistarā \|*  
*nānādhātukṛtastambhā nānāmaṇivibhūṣitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nānādrumalatākīrṇā puṣpavallībhiranvitā \|*  
*tatra siṃhāsanaṃ divyaṃ sthā pitaṃ tena śaunaka \|\| 22 \|\|*

*āhūya brāhmaṇānmukhyānvedavedāṃgapāragān \|*  
*pūjayitvā vidhānena dharmagāthāmathā'śṛṇot \|\| 23 \|\|*

*etasminnantare tatra vaitālo nāma devatā \|*  
*sa kṛtvā brāhmaṇaṃ rūpa jayāśīrbhiḥ praśasya tam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*upaviśyāsane vipro rājānamidamabravīt \|*  
*yadi te śravaṇe śraddhā vikramādityabhūpate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*varṇayāmi mahākhyānamitihāsasamuccayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

16-26. The father gave the name of Vikramaditya to his son delightfully. The child was an extremely intelligent one and was quite darling of his parents. At the age of five years, he resolved to perform tapas in the forest and for that purpose, he went to the forests. He performed hard tapas for a period of twelve years and achieved immense grace. Thereafter, he returned to the town of the Ambavati. There was a charming lion-throne there, which was carried by thirty two wooden puppets. The said lion-throne had been sent by lord Siva for him, which was accepted by him. For the protection of the boy, Parveti has deputed a goblin or a Vaitala also with the lion-throne. Once the valorous king went to Mahakalesvara and worshipped lord Siva - the carrier of the Pinaka bow. A Dharma-sabha was also constituted there, in which the method of the erecting Vyuhas of the pillars of different metals studded with different types of gems, the painting of flowers and trees, besides creepers decorated the structure. О Saunaka, in the same Dharma-sabha, the divine lionthrone was consecrated. Then all the prominent Brahmanas who were well-Versed with the Vedas and their parts, were invited and were adored. Then religious speeches were heard from them. At the same time, the Vaitala taking to the form of a Brahmana, uttered- “Victory to you.” Then blessing him, he praised the king and taking his seat, he said to the king- “In case you are interested in listening to one, then I can narrate the historical stories of the past.”

On hearing this, the old lady went to the royal palace and told everything to Padmavati. Padmavati then spoke to her in anger- “O immensely wicked woman, you leave this place at once.” Thus speaking, Padmavati soaked her fingers in the sandal paste and struck the old lady’s chest with her palm soaked in sandal paste. She also drew a mark over the face of the old woman with her fingers. The old lady then returned to her place and appraised Buddhidaksa of the factual position. Well understanding the situation, he said to his grieving friend- “O friend, shed away the grief and listen to the message that has been conveyed by the princess through the old lady. Striking of the chest of the woman reveals as to when shall both of us meet? О friend, listening to your words, I have become lustful and am in period. Getting free from my menstrual period, I shall only kiss you.” Listening to the words of his friend, the prince was immensely delighted. After three days, the old lady again went to Padmavati and said to her- “The prince is quite anxious to meet you. Therefore, he is repeatedly expressing his desire to meet you. Therefore, О excellent one, you make your life graceful by serving him today itself.” The words of the old woman delighted her the most. Then she made the old woman to return through the window and implanted her palm soaked with sandal paste over her back. The old lady then returned and conveyed the situation to them.

51-58. Buddhidaksa then disguised himself as a Yogi, while the prince disguised himself as his disciple. Then the intelligent one entrusted the ornaments to the friend for sale in the city. Vajramukuta carried the ornaments to the city for sale. At the same time, the royal men detected the theft of ornaments and their sale by Vajramukuta. The prince was then bound with ropes and produced before the king Dantavakra, who asked the prince- “Where from did you get these ornaments? You tell me the truth.” The disciple having locks of hair said- “O king, my preceptor lives near the cremation ground. These ornaments have been given to me by him for sale.” On hearing this, the king atonce summoned the preceptor and asked him about the ornaments. Then the Yogi said- “You please listen whatever is being spoken by me. I was engaged in performing siddhi or a mantra in the cremation ground. In the mean time, a Pisacini arrived there. I made a mark with my trident over her knee. She handed over the ornaments to me.” Finding that his daughter was the cause of all the trouble, he drove her out of his house. Thereafter, Buddhidaksa together with Vajramukuta and the princess returned his home. Narrating all the story, Vaitala laughed and said to Vikramaditya- “Listen О king, who of these four would be the greatest of all the sinners?”

Suta said- On hearing this, the king Vikramaditya laughed and said- “The king is the greatest sinner, because the minister’s son did the job of a friend, the servants did the duty of their master and the prince did his selfish task. Therefore, the king is the biggest sinner, because of which he earned the hell. A person who does not many his daughter even after the start of her menstruation, such a sinner has to fall in a hell for sixty thousand years. When the girl gets ready for a gandharva type of marriage and a person who causes an obstruction in the same, such a sinful person is punished by Yama. He has to face the sufferings of the hell for a lakh of years. Listening to the touching tale which was conceived by the king as being full of wisdom, the delighted Vaitala called him to be a religious king.

*cakorīva vinā caṃdraṃ kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

1-9. Suta said- O best of the Branmanas, the Vaitala then gladly said to the king, who was occupying the throne at that time. Once at the bank of the river Yamuna, in a beautiful town known by the name of Dharmasthala, which was filled with wealth and cereals and had the population of all the four varnas, was ruled by a king named Gunadhipa. He had a priest known by the name of Hari Sarma, who had a chaste and devoted wife named Susila and a son named Satyasila, who was always ready for prosecuting studies. He also had a virtuous daughter named Madhumati. When she reached the age of twelve years, both the brother and the father got in search of a suitable match for the girl. At the same time, the father went for the marriage of the prince and her brother known by the name of Saptasila who went to Kashi for studies. O king, at that point of time, a Brahmana who was adult and humble, reached the place of Hari Sarma. The girl Madhumati became lustful on meeting the boy. She was getting disturbed and discarded taking food, clothes, drinking water or going to sleep. She then behaved like the she partridge separated from the moon.

## \|\| 2.70.10-16 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā suśīlā taṃ bālā vāmanaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*vārayāmāsa tāṃbūlaiḥ svarṇadravyasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*hariśarmā prayoge ca dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā trivikramam \|*  
*vedavedāṃtattvajñaṃ sutārthe'varayattadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*satyaśīlastu kāśyāṃ vai guruputraṃ ca keśavam \|*  
*varitvā taṃ bhaginyarthe yayau gehaṃ mudānvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*māghakṛṣṇatrayodaśyāṃ bhṛgau lagnaṃ śubhaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*trayo viprāstadā prāptāḥ kanyārthe rūpamohitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasminkāle tu sā kanyā bhujagenaiva daṃśitā \|*  
*mṛtā pretatvamāpannā pūrvakarmaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tadā te brāhmaṇā yatnaṃ kārayāmāsuruttamam \|*  
*na jīvanavatī bālā garalena vimohitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*hariśarmā tu tatsarvaṃ kṛtvā vedavidhānataḥ \|*  
*āyayau maṃdiraṃ rājantsutāguṇavimohitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

10-16. Observing the Brahmana Vamana, Susila - the mother of the girl, took some gold, betel and riches and selected the boy as a match for her girl. On the other hand, Hari Sarnia found a Brahmana boy at Prayaga who was known by the name of Trivikrama and was well-versed in the Vedas and the related literature, and selected him for the girl’s match. On the other hand, Satyasila selected Kesava - the son of his preceptor, as the match for his sister and feeling delighted, he returned home. On Friday, the thirteenth of dark fortnight, all the three Brahmana boys reached the house of the priest. Suddenly a serpent bit the girl and because of her earlier deeds, she had to take to the form of a goblin. At that point of time, all the three Brahmanas made all the efforts to bring the girl back to life, but because of the terrific nature of the poison, she could not be brought back to life. Thereafter, Hari Sarma completed the virtues of the girl and returned home.

## \|\| 2.70.17-19 \|\|

*trivikramastu bahudhā duḥkhaṃ kṛtvā smarānugaḥ \|*  
*kaṃthādhārī yatirbhūtvā deśāddeśātaraṃ yayau \|\| 17 \|\|*

*keśavastu mahāduḥkhī priyāsthīni gṛhītavān \|*  
*tīrthāttīrthāṃtaraṃ prāptaḥ kāmabāṇena pīḍitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhasmagrāhī vāmanastu virahāgniprapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*tasthau citāyāṃ kāmārtaḥ patnīdhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Carrying a sack over his shoulders and recalling the virtues of the Brahmanas, the Brahmana boy Trivikrama left the place for wandering in other countries. On the other hand, feeling extremely painful, Kesava collected the bones of his beloved and feeling lustful, visited one holy place after the other. On the other hand, burning with her separation, carrying her ashes and feeling passionate, Vamana sat over the fire altar.

## \|\| 2.70.20-35 \|\|

*ekadā sarayūtīre lakṣmaṇākhyapure śubhe \|*  
*trivikramastu bhikṣārthe saṃprāpto dvijamaṃdire \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tasmindine rāmaśarmā śivadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*yatinaṃ varayāmāsa bhojanārthaṃ svamaṃdire \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasya patnī viśālākṣī racitvā bahubhojanam \|*  
*āhūya yatinaṃ rājanpātramālabhamākarot \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tasminkāle ca tadbālo mṛtaḥ pāpavaśaṃgataḥ \|*  
*arodīttasya sairaṃdhrī viśālākṣyapi bhartsitā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*na rodanaṃ tyaktavatī putraśokāgnitāpitā \|*  
*rāmaśarmā tadā prāpto maṃtraṃ saṃjīvanaṃ śubham \|\| 24 \|\|*

*japitvā mārjanaṃ kṛtvā jīvayāmāsa bālakam \|*  
*vinayāvanato viprastaṃ ca saṃnyāsinaṃ tadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhojanaṃ kārayitvā tu maṃtraṃ saṃjīvanaṃ dadau \|*  
*trivikramastu taṃ maṃtraṃ paṭhitvā yamunātaṭe \|\| 26 \|\|*

*prāptavānyatra sā nārī dāhitā hariśarmaṇā \|*  
*etasminnantare tatra rājaputro mṛtiṃ gataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dāhitastanayaḥ pitrā śokakartrā tadāmunā \|*  
*jīvanaṃ prāptavānbālastasya maṃtraprabhāvataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*guṇādhipasya tanayo rājño dharmasthalīpateḥ \|*  
*trivikramaṃ vacaḥ prāha vīrabāhurmahābalaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*jīvanaṃ dattavānmahyaṃ varayādya varaṃ mama \|*  
*sa vipraḥ prāha bho rājankeśavo nāma yo dvijaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gṛhītvāsthi gatastīrthe tamanveṣaya mā ciram \|*  
*vīrabāhustathā matvā dūtamārgeṇa taṃ prati \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prāptastaṃ kathayāmāsa yathā prāptaṃ hi jīvanam \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya keśavo'sthisamanvitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*pragatyāsthīni sarvāṇi dadau tasmai dvijātaye \|*  
*punaḥ saṃjīvitā bālā keśavādīnvaco'bravīt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yogyā dharmeṇa yasyāhaṃ tasmai prāyāmi dharmiṇe \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasyā maunavaṃtastrayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*atastvaṃ vikramāditya dharmajña kathayasva me \|*  
*kasmai yogyā ca sā bālā nāmnā madhumatī śubhā \|\| 35 \|\|*

20-35. There was a city named Laksmana at the bank of the river Sarayu where Trivikrama went to the house of a Brahmana for begging alms at his door. Rama Sarma had invited a Yati Brahmana to take food on the occasion of the concluding of the Siva worship. His wife named Visalaksi was serving several types of food items to the invitee. At the same time, her son died due to his own deeds. Then the wife denounced her husband due to the grief, while crying. When she did not stop crying, making use of the sanjivani mantra, Rama Sarma brought his son back to life. Thereafter, the Brahmana served food with all humility to the Yati and also bestowed the knowledge of the auspicious sanjivani mantra. Trivikrama achieved siddhi for that mantra over the bank of the river Yamuna, where Hari Sarma had cremated his daughter. At the same time, the prince of the palace died. His father, getting filled with grief, cremated his son’s body there. The prince also got back his life with the use of the same mantra. Thereafter, the son of the king Gunadhipa, who got back his life due to the said mantra, said to Trivikrama - “You have got my life back to me. Therefore, you ask for a boon you desire.” Brahmana said- “O king, a Brahmana known by the name of Kesava had gone on pilgrimage with the bones of my daughter. He should be searched.” The prince Virabahu related the story to him about his getting back his life. Listening to such talk, he returned with the bones from the mid-way and handed over the bones to the Brahmana. Then getting back her life, the girl spoke to all the three Brahmanas- “I am prepared to accompany the Brahmana who is required to be my husband as per dharma. On learning this, all the Brahmanas kept quiet. Therefore, О Vikramaditya! You are well-versed in dharma and you should tell us as to who should be the husband of Madhumati?

## \|\| 2.70.36-37 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vihasya vikramādityo vaitālaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|*  
*yogyā madhumatī nārī vāmanāya dvijanmane \|\| 36 \|\|*

*prāṇadātā tu yo vipraḥ piteva guṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*asthidātā tu yo vipro bhrātṛtulyassa vedavit \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Suta said- The king Vikramaditya smiled and said to Vaitala - Madhumati should be the wife of Vamana, because the person who gives life is like the father and the one who gives bones is like the brother.

## Chapter 71. Collective history of the age of Kali

## \|\| 2.71.1-12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vipravarya mahābhāga śṛṇu gāthāṃ manoramām \|*  
*vaitālo bhūpatiśreṣṭhaṃ punarvikramamabravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*varddhavannagare ramye nānājananiṣevite \|*  
*tatrābhavanmahīpālo rūpaseno mahābalaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vidvanmālā priyā tasya patisevāparāyaṇā \|*  
*ekadā kṣatriyaḥ kaścinnāmnā vīravaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*putrakanyāsapatnīko vṛttyarthaṃ samupāgataḥ \|*  
*vinayāvanato bhūtvā rūpasenaṃ mahīpatim \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kiṃcicchrutvā dadau svarṇaṃ sahasraṃ pratyahaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*vīrasenastu tallabdhvā vahnau tīrthe dvijātiṣu \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vyayaṃ kṛtvā tu taccheṣaṃ sa kulye bhuktavānsvayam \|*  
*evaṃ varṣe gate rājanrājalakṣmīḥ śivājñayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*parīkṣārthaṃ smaśāne ca rodanaṃ bahu kurvatī \|*  
*ardharātre tadā rājā buddhvā prāha svasevakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*gaccha vīravara tvaṃ vai yato'sau śrūyate ravaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā tatkāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ mahyaṃ śīghraṃ nivedaya \|\| 8 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vīravaraḥ śastrāstrakuśalo balī \|*  
*sa tatra gatvā yatrāste rājalakṣmīḥ śubhānanā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ślakṣṇaṃ vacaśca tāmāha kimarthaṃ rodane sthitā \|*  
*mahatkaṣṭaṃ ca kiṃ prāptaṃ kāraṇaṃ devi me vada \|\| 10 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā rājalakṣmīrvīrasenaṃ tamabravīt \|*  
*rājalakṣmīṃ ca māṃ viddhi rūpasenasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*māsānte pralayaṃ yāsye tasmācchocāmi bho balin \|*  
*sa āha śṛṇu bho devi tvadalpāyussa mīritam \|*  
*kena puṇyena dīrghāyustvaṃ bhaveḥ kāraṇaṃ vada \|\| 12 \|\|*

1-12. Saunaka said- О fortunate one and best of the Brahmanas, I am narrating a beautiful story which you please listen. There lived in the city known by the name of Varddhaman a highly valorous king Rupasena who was ruling the country. Vidyunmala was the name of his wife, who was totally devoted to her husband. Once a person known as Viravara together with his wife and daughter appeared in the court of the king for taking up a job. He was engaged by the king in service and was paid a thousand gold coins daily. Viravara accepted the amount as his wages and spent it for undertaking pilgrimage, yajnas in fire and giving to Brahmanas. After the spending whatever was left out, he used the amount for his daily maintenance. О king, in this way, one year passed. Thereafter, at the command of lord Siva, Rajalaksmi went to test the devotion of Viravara. For that purpose, she went to the cremation ground and started crying there. At the dead of night, the king was awakened and said to the attendant Viravara- “You follow the sound of cries, which is being heard by you and make proper enquiries and inform me quickly.” Hearing the words of the king, Viravara equipped himself with weapons and went to the place where the princess was crying. He spoke to her with pleasant voice- “0 goddess, why are you crying? What is the great trouble with you, you tell me.” On hearing this, Rajalaksmi said- “O valorous one, I am Rajalaksmi of the king Virasena. I am going to be destroyed by the end of this month. This is the cause of grief for me.” Then Viravara said- “O goddess, you are visualising a short life for yourself. But is there any noble deed performing by which your life could be prolonged? You kindly tell me.”

## \|\| 2.71.13-18 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*mahābāho mahāprājña yadi te tanayasya vai \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kapālamarpaya tvaṃ ca caṃḍikāyai tadānagha \|*  
*dīrghāyurbhavitā cāhaṃ svāmikāryaṃ prasādhaya \|\| 14 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vīravaro maṃdiraṃ svayamāgataḥ \|*  
*patnīṃ prāha prasannātmā sutaṃ devyai nivedaya \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tathetyuktvā tu sā sādhvī tanayaṃ prāha nirbhayā \|*  
*rājño'rthe tava dehaṃ vai putra pāsi kuruṣva tat \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tathā matvā tu tatputro bhaginyā mātṛsaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*caṃḍikābhavanaṃ prāpyābravītsvapitaraṃ tadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhostāta me kapālaṃ ca caṃḍikāyai samarpaya \|*  
*dīrghāyuryena yatnena rājalakṣmīśca tatkuru \|\| 18 \|\|*

13-18. The goddess said- “In case you are in a position to offer the head of your own son to the goddess Candi, then О smiling one, my life could be enhanced. Therefore, you should do this for the sake of your master.” On hearing this, Viravara returned to his own house and spoke to his wife with a delightful heart- “You offer your son for the sake of the goddess.” The chaste wife fearlessly agreed to this proposal. Thereafter, he spoke to his own son- “You have been brought up for the sake of the task of the ruler. Therefore, you fulfil the same.” The son agreed to the same. Together with his mother and sister, he reached the temple of Candi and said to his father- “You offer my head for the sake of the goddess Candi to enable the Rajalaksmi to attain long life for the king. The task should be established by us making all the efforts.”

## \|\| 2.71.19-23 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vīrasenaḥ śiraśchittvā samārpayat \|*  
*tasyānujā mṛtā tatra tathā mātā tathā pitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tadrūpa senastu kāraṇaṃ sarvamāditaḥ \|*  
*sevakaṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ ca matvā tu svaśiro'rpayat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tadā prasannā sā devī nṛpamujīvya sābravīt \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhūpāla yatheṣṭaṃ śīghramāpnuyāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sa āha vīrasenastu sakulo jīvamāpnuyāt \|*  
*tathetyuktvā tu sā devī tatraivāṃtarhitābhavat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*rūpasenaḥ prasannātmā svasutāṃ kāmarūpiṇīm \|*  
*dadau sutāya vaitālo nṛpatiṃ prāha vismitaḥ \|*  
*mukhyasnehaṃ kṛtaṃ kena teṣāṃ madhye vadasva me \|\| 23 \|\|*

19-23. On hearing this, Virasena cut off the head of his son and offered it to the goddess. Thereafter, his sister, mother and father were all dead. When the king Rupasena came to know about the entire episode from beginning to end, then realising the truthful conduct of his attendant, he also offered his own head to the goddess. At that point of time, the goddess brought back the king to life and said to him-“You ask for any boon you desire. I am prepared to grant you the same.” The king said- “Let Virasena with his family get back their lives.” The goddess did so and disappeared from the place. Thereafter, getting pleased, the king Rupasena married his own beautiful daughter to the son of Virasena. Then the surprised Vaitala said to Vikrama-“Who was the most loveable of all of them?”

## \|\| 2.71.24-25 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*mukhyasnehaṃ kṛtaṃ rājñā dāsārthe svatanuṃ dadau \|*  
*svarṇasnehī vīravaro dhamarprītiḥ pativratā \|*  
*baṃdhuprītiśca bhaginī pitṛsnehī tu putrakaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mahānsnehaḥ kṛto rājñā rūpasenena dhīmatā \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The king said- “The king was the most loveable one, who sacrificed his own life for the sake of his servant. Viravara loved the gold coins, his wife loved her chastity, while the sister loved her parents and the son loved his father. But the intelligent king Rupasena displayed the height of love for his servants and his family.”

## Chapter 72. Collateral history of the age of Kali

## \|\| 2.72.1-12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa vaitālo rājānamidamabravīt \|*  
*kācidbhogāvatī nāmnā nagarī paramādbhutā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa nṛpatirgaṇeśaṃ dvijasattamam \|*

*gaṇeśopi gatastūrṇaṃ deśe māgadhake śubhe \|*  
*mahādevaṃ ca saṃpūjya cakāra stavanaṃ mudā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*namaḥ śivāya śāṃtāya sarvābhīṣṭapradāyine \|*  
*bhavāya śaṃkarāyaiva rudrāya satataṃ namaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*mṛḍāyānaṃdarūpāya sarvaduḥkhaharāya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ityuktavati vipre ca tadā candravatī śubhā \|*  
*kāmāturābravīccaināṃ nāmnā madanamañjarīm \|\| 10 \|\|*

*mama yogyaśca puruṣaḥ kaścidasti mahītale \|*  
*sāha bho rūpavarmā ca yogyo bhogāpurīpatiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu sā devī durgāṃ vāñchitadāyinīm \|*

1-12. Suta said- On hearing this, Vaitala said to the king again- “There was a great and astonishing type of city named Bhogavati, which was ruled by the king Rupavarma. He had an intelligent parrot with him, who was known by the name of Cudamani. It was lodged in a beautiful cage. After its attaining the age of thirty years, the king asked it- “Is there a beautiful damsel quite suitable for me. In case there be one, you just tell me about her.” On hearing this, the parrot said-“O king, the daughter of the Magadha country, known by the name of Candravati, is best suited for you and you accept her as your wife.” On hearing this, the king deputed a Brahmana named Ganesa with enough of wealth saying- “You move in such a way, by which she could be married with me.” The Brahmana named Ganesa rapidly reached the country of Magadha and prayed to lord Mahadeva. He said- “Salutation to lord Siva, who is peaceful and always bestows the desired things to his devotees. The one who is compassionate and remover of all the miseries, salutation to such a lord. When the Brahmana was so praying to lord Siva, getting passionate, Candravati spoke to the the black bird- “Is there a suitable person for me on the earth?” The bird replied- “The king Rupavarma of Bhogapuri is quite suitable for you.” On hearing this, the princess adored the goddess Durga - the creator of the universe.

## \|\| 2.72.13-16 \|\|

*namonamo jaganmātarmama kāryapradāyini \|*  
*triliṃgajananī tvaṃ vai varṇamūrtiḥ sanātanī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā saṃdhyā namastasyai namonamaḥ \|*  
*nṛpatiṃ rūpavarmāṇaṃ matpatiṃ kuru bhoḥ śive \|\| 14 \|\|*

*iti stutyā prasannābhūjjagadaṃbā jaganmayī \|*  
*pitaraṃ magadheśaṃ ca mohayitvā ca mātaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vivāhaṃ kārayāmāsa māsānte siddharūpiṇī \|*  
*rūpavarmā caṃdravatī bubhujāte paraṃ sukham \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. She said- “О mother of the universe, salutation to you repeatedly. You are the one who could establish my task. You are the creator of the females. You are the eternal form of the varnas. You are also known as Svaha, Svadha and Sandhya. Therefore, salutation to you again and again. О spouse of Siva, you better give me the king Rupavarma as my husband.” At the prayer of the princess, the goddess Jagadamba - the mother of the universe, feeling delighted and confusing the king of Magadha - her father besides the mother, fulfilled her desire. Thereafter, both of them enjoyed the delightful life.

## \|\| 2.72.17-29 \|\|

*ekasmindivase rājanmenāṃ madanamaṃjarīm \|*  
*nṛpaḥ prāha vivāhaṃ tvaṃ suśukena kuruṣva bhoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*menakā prāha bho rājanvivāhāścedṛśo matāḥ \|*  
*uttamādhamamadhyāśca puruṣāstrividhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tathaiva trividhā nārī yathā yogyo varo bhavet \|*  
*uttamā yo bhavennārī yogyāyā cādhamāya vai \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ rājanmayā dṛṣṭaṃ yathā'bhavat \|*  
*ilāpure vasatyeko vaiśyo lakṣapatirdhanī \|\| 20 \|\|*

*anapatyo devayājī tasya patnī pativratā \|*  
*bahuyatnena tanayastasya jāto mahādhamaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dyūtakrīḍāparo nityaṃ surāpāne ratassadā \|*  
*veśyāgāmī mahādhūrto nityaṃ māṃsāśanaḥ khalaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tasya dharmaṃ ca pitarau samālokya vanaṃ gatau \|*  
*naraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ dhyātvā paramaṃ padamāpatuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*madapālastu tanayaḥ kṛtvā sarvadhanavyayam \|*  
*anyadeśe ca vṛttyarthaṃ jagāma dhanavarjitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*prāptaścaṃdrapure ramye yatra hemapatiḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa vaiśyaṃ hemapatiṃ hi saḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*devayājī suto'haṃ vai svalpaṃ vai dhanamāhṛtam \|*  
*deśāntare vikrayārthe sindhumārgeṇa prāptavān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahāvāyu prabhāvena dravyaṃ tanmagnamaṃbhasi \|*  
*tallajjayā na yāsye'haṃ pitaraṃ prati māriṣa \|\| 27 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā hemapatiḥ svapatnīṃ kāmamaṃjarīm \|*  
*vacaḥ prāha prasannātmā saṃyogo vidhinā kṛtaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*caṃdrakāṃtiṃ sutāṃ dāsye tadvarāya tvadājñayā \|*  
*saṃmaṃtrya daṃpatī rājandadau kanyāṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

17-29. Once the king said to Madanamanjari - the bird- “You better marry this parrot.” The mynah - the black bird said- “Only such a type of marriage is considered to be good when the man and the woman are best suited for each other. The men are of three types, i.e. the best, mediocre and the degraded ones. Similarly, the women are also of three types. Therefore, the best woman is not considered suitable for the degraded man. I am speaking out the reason for the same, as has been witnessed by me. You please listen. There once lived a millionaire merchant at Ilapura. His name was Devayaji. He had a chaste wife but had no children. After making all the efforts, he got a wicked son. He indulged in gambling, drinking and visited whores. He also developed the habit of consuming the flesh or meat. Observing the evil ways of her son, the mother and father both went to the forest and meditating for Narayana, achieved the final beatitude. Their son wasted the wealth of his parents over drinking, became a pauper in due course of time. Once he undertook a journey for business and reached the city of Candrapura, where there lived a merchant named Hemapati. He went to him and narrated his story to the merchant saying- “I am the son of the merchant Devayaji. Carrying some wealth with me, I had started on a voyage and have reached this country by sea-route, for the sale of merchandise. But with the storm, all my belongings have been drowned in the ocean. Therefore, I am unable to return to my parents.” On hearing this, feeling delighted, Hemapati said to his wife known by the name of Kamamanjari- “Brahma has presented a beautiful opportunity for us. With your wealth, I would like to marry your daughter Candravati to this boy.” Both of them mutually consulted each other and married their daughter to him.

30-41. They then made their son-in-law, known by the name of Madanapala, to stay in their own house. After his stay there for a month, he humbly said to his father-in-law- “O lord of riches, you permit me to return home quickly.” On hearing this, Hemapati decorated his daughter with enough of gold, arranged a female servant to accompany her and sent his daughter with Madanapala. О king, after travelling some distance, the wicked soul killed the carriers and other servants with the palanquin. Then he killed the slave girl. Then usurping the entire riches, he deserted his wife in a lonely place and reached his home alone. Within a year, he wasted the entire wealth in evil ways and started starving. The wicked person again reached the place of his father-in-law. His wife Candrakanti delightfully spoke to her husband- “I have spoken to my father that my wealth was usurped by the thieves. Therefore, you have no grief and live here in my house forever.” He accepted the words of his wife. The extremely wicked person lived at that place for some time. Finding that his wife was deeply in love with her, on a dark night, he killed her and deserted the place carrying all the wealth and ornaments. Therefore, О king, the marriage of the parrot and the black bird is unsuitable and improper. On hearing this, the parrot said to the king- “I do not intend to have any relationship with such a type of woman, because this black bird mynah is degraded like the woman, besides being black and ugly. I am a parrot of a high race. I narrate to you the reason for the same, which have been witnessed myself. There was a merchant known as Sankhapati, who lived in the city of Kancanapura.

*vivāhamakarottasya jayaśrīpattane śubhe \|*

*jayalakṣmīstu kāmena pīḍitā pitṛmaṃdire \|*

*dūtī mārgeṇa taṃ prāpya vyayaṃ kṛtvā dhanaṃ bahu \|*

*trimāsānte ca tatsvāmī śrīdattaḥ śvaśurālaye \|*

42-48. Sindhugupta was the name of his son. He was quite a virtuous and a wealthy person. His wife was known by the name of Prabhavati. They have a son named Sridatta. He married his son Sridatta with Jayasri - the daughter Somadatta. Subsequently, Sridatta travelled to Kuru country in connection with his business. Earning enormous riches from there, he returned home after twelve years. On the other hand, Jayalaksmi, while living in her parent’s home, once having been filled with passion, developed liking for the son of the minister. The degraded woman, by means of a female messenger, established the contact and started enjoying his company spending enormous wealth. Her husband returned to his father-inlaw’s place after three months. She felt painful on his arrival. At the dead of night, the mother sent her daughter to her husband. Though the lips of Jayalaksmi were fluttering in anger, still she reached her husband somehow.

## \|\| 2.72.49-53 \|\|

*bahumānena svapatisnehaṃ kṛtvālayaṃ yayau \|*

*śūnyālaye homadatto daṃśito bhujagena vai \|*

*vegena ramayāmāsa taṃ jāraṃ viṣamohitam \|*  
*pippalasthaḥ piśācaśca dṛṣṭvā tāṃ jāriṇīṃ śubhām \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śavadehaṃ ca saṃprāpya ramaṇīṃ tāmarīramat \|*  
*khanitvā daśanairnāsāṃ pippalopari so'gamat \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kaphallo nāma caurastu dṛṣṭvā tatkāraṇaṃ tadā \|*  
*kāminyā anugo bhūtvā maṃdiraṃ tatpraviṣṭavān \|\| 53 \|\|*

49-53. Expressing her love with great honour, she returned to her own palace. Thereafter, the wanton woman went to the house of the female messenger and found that Somadatta was lying there dead by a snake bite. But the wicked and degraded woman started uniting with the body of Somadatta. Finding the behaviour of the wicked woman, a pisaca who lived over a tree entered the body of Somadatta and enjoyed the company of the woman. Thereafter, the рisaса cut off the nose of the woman and reverted to the pipala tree. A thief who had arrived there for theft, observed the entire happening and followed the woman to the palace.

*nāsāhīnāṃ sutāṃ dṛṣṭvā somadatto mahādhanaḥ \|*  
*baddhvā jāmātaraṃ śīghraṃ rājāṃtikamupāyayau \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nṛpājñayā rājadūtāstamudbaṃdhanamādadhuḥ \|*  
*tadā kaphallaḥ saṃprāpya sarvaṃ rājñe nyavedayat \|\| 56 \|\|*

*matvā tasya vacaḥ satyaṃ jayalakṣmīṃ mahādhamām \|*
