54-59. The unfortunate woman Jayalaksmi then went to the place of her husband and started crying. All the people assembled there and the wealthy merchant Somadatta, finding the nose of his daughter having been severed, put his son-in-law in bondage and reported the matter to the king. The king ordered his servants and carried Sridatta for hanging him. When they were about to hang Sridatta, the thief reached there and revealed the truth of the matter. Taking his words to b । e true, Jayalaksmi was badly humiliated and disfigured. She was mounted over a donkey and driven out in the forest. Therefore, О king, you believe me. Mynah is not suitable for me. Thus speaking, Vaitala humbly said to Vikramaditya- “You please tell me the maximum number of sins being committed by the women or the men.”

## \|\| 2.72.60-64 \|\|

*vikrama uvāca \|*  
*brahmaṇo'guṇarūpasya māyāvarṇasva rūpiṇī \|*  
*tamo na puṃsakaṃ jñeyaṃ triliṃgaikaṃ tadavyayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*avyayaṃ brahmaṇo dhāma māyā liṃgasvarūpiṇī \|*  
*tayā jātamidaṃ viśvaṃ tadaṃbāyai namonamaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*klībā strī sarvadā śreṣṭhā striyāstu puruṣastathā \|*  
*avyādhikaśca puruṣo nārī karmādhikā matā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*klībamajñānamadhikaṃ kathitaṃ pūrvakovidaiḥ \|*  
*karmaiva bandhanaṃ puṃsāṃ jñānaṃ nirbaṃdhana smṛtam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*ataḥ pāpādhikā nārī puruṣo hīnakilbiṣaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

60-64. Vikrama said- The Maya of absolute Brahman is devoid of gender, form of male or female. It is also not eunuch or darkness. Therefore, one and the same Brahman possesses the three genders. The tejas of Brahman is imperishable and his Maya has no gender. The entire universe has been produced by him. Therefore, salutation to the goddess Ambika. The eunuch female is always the best, neither a man nor a woman. The man or a woman without ailments is considered to be more active. Similarly, the learned people have said that a eunuch has lack of knowledge. For any person, the activity is bondage. Knowledge emerges from the lack of bondage. Therefore, a person, irrespective of being a man or a woman, who indulge in sins is known as karmahina (devoid of karmas).

## Chapter 73. Collateral history of the age of Kali

## \|\| 2.73.1-7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bhṛguvarya mahābhāga śrutvā vaitāla eva saḥ \|*  
*prasannātmā vacaḥ prāha bhūpatiṃ jñānasaṃpadam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ujjayinyāṃ mahārāja mahābala iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*caṃdravaṃśī nṛpaḥ prājño vedaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasya dūto harerdāsaḥ svāmikāryakaraḥ sadā \|*  
*bhaktimālā priyā tasya sādhusevāparāyaṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ jātā rūpavatī kanyā kamalalocanā \|*  
*mahādevīti vikhyātā sarvavidyāviśāradā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*haridāsaṃ ca sā prāha śṛṇu tāta vaco mama \|*  
*matto'dhiko naro yo vai tasmai māṃ tu dadasva bhoḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tathetyuktvā pitā rājanrājñāhūto gataḥ sabhām \|*  
*natvā taṃ nṛpatiḥ prāha haridāsa śṛṇuṣva bhoḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tailaṃgādhipatiṃ gaccha hariścaṃdraṃ mahīpatim \|*  
*tasya kṣemaṃ tathā jñātvā māṃ nivedaya mā ciram \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta said- О best of the race of Bhrgus, О graceful one, getting pleased, Vaitala spoke to the king Vikramaditya - the treasure of knowledge. О lord, in the city of Ujjayini, there was a king known by the name of Chandrabala, who was born in the lunar race and ruled the country. He was well-versed in the Vedas and Sastras. A servant named Haridasa always performed the task of his master quite well. The name of his wife was Bhaktimala, who always devoted her time in the service of the ascetics. The queen produced a daughter who was known by the name of Mahadevi. She had the limbs resembling the lotus flowers, was quite beautiful and was well-versed in all the lores. She said to Haridasa- “O respectable one, you listen to my words. You marry to a person who is more virtuous than myself. The father accepted the words of her daughter, but at the same time they were summoned by the ruler and both of them went to the court of the king. Offering his salutation to him, the king said to Haridasa-“O best of the Brahmanas, the king Hariscandra is the ruler of the Tailanga country. You go to him and after enquiring about his welfare, you communicate the same to me.”

## \|\| 2.73.8-17 \|\|

*iti śrutvā dvijaḥ prāgāddhariścaṃdraṃ mahāmatim \|*  
*kuśalaṃ varṇayāmāsa mahābalanṛpasya vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śrutvā prasannahṛdayo hariścaṃdro mahīpatiḥ \|*

*yadā rājyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena kalerāgamamanaṃ tadā \|*  
*brahmaṇosya mukhājjāta oṃkāraḥ satyapūjitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvitīyāsyācca vividhā bhāṣā loka vimohinī \|*  
*jātā kalerhitārthāya yamalokahitaiṣiṇī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yadā dharmaṃ ca vedoktaṃ viparītaṃ hi dṛśyate \|*  
*kalirājyaṃ tadā jñeyaṃ mlecchā yasya priyāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kalinā'dharmamitreṇa sarve devā nirākṛtāḥ \|*  
*pāpasyaiva mṛṣā bhāryā duḥkhaṃ tattanayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*durgatistasya cārdhāṃgī gehegehe tadā bhavet \|*  
*krodhavaśyāḥ nṛpāḥ sarve brāhmaṇāḥ kāmakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*lobhavaśyāstu dhanino mahattvaṃ śūdrakā gatāḥ \|*  
*nāryo lajjāvihīnāśca kiṃkarāḥ svāmighātakāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*niṣphalā tu mahī jātā kalau prāpte hi dṛśyate \|*  
*ye hareḥ śaraṇaṃ prāptāste sarve muditāḥ kalau \|\| 17 \|\|*

8-17. On hearing this, the Brahmana reached the place of the king Hariscandra and conveyed the welfare of the king Mahabala to him. Listening to the welfare of the king Mahabala, he felt delighted, since he happened to be the father-in-law of Mahabala. Then he enquired Haridasa- “When is Kali scheduled to arrive on earth?” Haridasa said- “He would arrive during the time of Nyuha. At the time of his incarnation, Kali would then arrive. During the time of Kali, only Omkara which would emerge from the mouth of Brahma, would be worshipped as the truth and other languages (other than Sanskrit) would become prominent, which would attract the people in many forms. The cause of Kali would be established with the use of the same language, because it would desire benefit for the Yama’s abode as well. At the time when the Vedic dharma would appear to be the opposite one, that time should be treated as the origion of Kali. This is because the Mlecchas would be his favourite. This has been ordained. With the help of Adharma as a friend, all the gods would become ineffective in the age of Kali. The sin shall have a wife named falsehood, the sufferings shall be his son, and his wife would be known as misfortune, who shall be present in all the abodes. All the rulers shall be under the influence of anger, the Brahmanas would be lustful, the rich people would be overpowered by the greed, while the Madras would gain importance. The ladies would be devoid of modesty and the servants would become the killers of their masters. During the age of Kali, the earth would be deprived of the fruits. Only a person taking refuge with the lord would likely to be happy.

## \|\| 2.73.18-25 \|\|

*iti śrutvā hariścaṃdro dattvā tasmai sudakṣiṇām \|*  
*svagehaṃ prāptavānrājā viprastu śibiraṃ yayau \|\| 18 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare tatra brāhmaṇo buddhikovidaḥ \|*

*haridāsasya tanayo mukuṃdo nāma kovidaḥ \|*

*gururāha ca śiṣyaṃ taṃ śṛṇu vācaṃ mukuṃda me \|*

*tathetyuktvā mukuṃdastu svagehaṃ śīghramāyayau \|*

18-25. Listening to this, the king Hariscandra gave the desired daksina to the Brahmana and took him to his palace. The other Brahmanas retired to their respective camps. At the same time, a Brahmana known by the name of Kovida started displaying his miracles to Haridasa. He produced a plane, which moved swiftly and had been granted to him by the goddess with the reciting of the mantras. It was wonderful and fulfilled the desires. The Brahmana Haridasa was made to board the plane, who observed it carefully, because he was looking at him for the sake of his daughter. Subsequently, he selected him for the sake of his own daughter and returned to his own city. After completion of his studies, Mukunda - the son of Haridasa, enquired his preceptor about the gurudaksina to be paid by him. The preceptor then replied to his pupil - “O Mukunda, you listen to my words. I have a learned son and you give your sister as his wife. Mukunda accepted the words of his preceptor and returned to his abode. At the same time, Mahadevi selected Vamana - a Brahmana boy, who was the disciple of Dronacarya and was well-versed in the shooting of arrow at the sound. She selected him offering daksina and the betel.

## \|\| 2.73.26-31 \|\|

*trayaste brāhmaṇāḥ prāptāḥ sutārthe guṇakovidāḥ \|*  
*etasminnantare kāmī rākṣaso daivamohitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahādevīṃ jahārāśu prāpto viṃdhyācale girau \|*  
*tadā te duḥkhino bhūtvā vilepuḥ kāmapīḍitā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dhīmānnāma dvijo vidvāṃstānprāha gaṇakottamaḥ \|*

*svavimāne samāropya tau dvijau buddhikovidaḥ \|*  
*viṃdhyācale girau prāptaḥ śabdavedhī tadā dhanuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*samāropya śareṇaiva jaghānāśu sa rākṣasam \|*

*mitho vivādavaṃtaste dṛṣṭvā kanyāṃ smarānugāḥ \|*  
*kasmai yogyā bhavetkanyā bhūpa me kṛpayā vada \|\| 31 \|\|*

26-31. At the time, when all the three virtuous Brahmanas boys reached the place of Mahadevi for marriage, at that point of time, unfortunately, a Raksasa getting attracted towards the girl, kidnapped her and moved towards the Vindhyacala mountain. Thereafter, getting lustful, all the Brahmana boys suffered very much. At the same time, a learned astrologer said to them - “The girl is in possession of a Raksasa at Vindhya mountain.” Listening to these words, Kovida made both the Brahmanas to move the plane and took them to the Vindhya mountain. Reaching there, the archer took his bow and arrow and killed the Raksasa. Thereafter, all of them mounted the plane and returned to the city of Ujjainl. Having been influenced with lust, all three of them started quarrelling among themselves for the sake of the woman. Therefore, О king, you kindly tell me who is to be her husband of all the three of them?”

## \|\| 2.73.32-34 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya vikramo nāma bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*praśrayāvanataḥ prāha vaitālaṃ rudrakiṃkaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

*viditvā yo'vadatkanyāṃ pitṛtulyo dvijo hi saḥ \|*  
*yena prāptā vimānena sa tu tadbhrātṛkaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*hatvā yo rākṣasaṃ vīraṃ kanyāyogyo hi so'bhavat \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Suta said- On hearing this, Vikramaditya humbly said to Vaitala - the attendant of Rudra. The one who spoke to the girl after knowing everything is like her father. The one who carried her in his plane was like his brother. Therefore, the Brahmana, who killed the Rak§asa, he happens to be the most suitable person to be the husband of the girl.

## Chapter 74. Collateral history of the age of Kali

## \|\| 2.74.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*punarāha sa vaitālaḥ śṛṇu rājankathāmimām \|*  
*grāme dharmapuraṃ ramye nānājananiṣevite \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatrābhavanmahīpālo dharmaśīlo mahottamaḥ \|*  
*lajjādevī ca mahiṣī tasya bhūpasya bhūpate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aṃdhako nāma tanmaṃtrī nyāyaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*kiyatā caiva kālena devīmaṃdiramuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dharmaśīlena racitaṃ tatra durgā pratiṣṭhitā \|*  
*apatyārthe bhūpatinā kṛtastatra mahotsavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*arddharātre mahāgaurī nṛpaṃ prāha vṛṇīṣva bhoḥ \|*  
*śrutvāmṛtamayaṃ vākyaṃ dharmaśīlo nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*stutiṃ cakāra namrātmā yena durgā prasīdati \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said - Vaitala again said- “O king, you listen to this story. A religious-minded king used to rule a pleasant village of Dharmapura inhabited by the people of several castes. The king was great and excellent one. Lajja Devi was the name of his chief queen, while the minister was known by the name of Andhaka, who was well-versed in the treatises on justice. After some time, for the sake of getting a son, the king built a beautiful temple there in which an image of Durga was consecrated and celebrated the festivities there. At the same time, the goddess Gauri spoke to the king at the dead of night- “O king, you ask for a boon.” Hearing the nectar like words, Dharmasila started offering prayer to her.”

## \|\| 2.74.6-11 \|\|

*dharmaśīla uvāca \|*  
*ekā tu prakṛtirnityā sarvavarṇasvarūpiṇī \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sā tvaṃ bhagavatī sākṣāttvayā sarvamidaṃ tatam \|*  
*tvadājñayā suraśreṣṭho racitvā lokamuttamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mahālakṣmyā tvayā sārddhaṃ bubhuje nirmalaṃ sukham \|*  
*tvadbhaktyā bhagavānviṣṇustrailokyaṃ brahma nirmitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*pālayaṃśca mahālakṣmyā tvayā sārddhaṃ sanātani \|*  
*tvadbalena mahādevi trailokyaṃ viṣṇupālitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mahākālyā tvayā sārddhaṃ bhasma kṛtvā virājate \|*  
*sarve devāstathā daityāḥ pitaro manujāḥ khagāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tvallīlayā ca te jātā jaganmātarnamostu te \|*  
*ityuktavaṃtaṃ nṛpatiṃ vāguvā cāśarīriṇī \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. Dharmasila said- Prakrti is one and eternal. At due time, she get the form of all the varnas. О goddess, you are the same who has expanded the universe. Accepting your command, creating the excellent lokas, the excellent gods enjoy all the spotless comforts with your Laksmi. О eternal one, with your devotion, lord Visnu enjoys all the three lokas created by Brahma with Mahalaksmi. О Manadevi, with your strength, Visnu was maintained by (Siva). Destroying the three worlds with Mahakali, you look graceful with him. All the gods, the Daityas, manes, humans and the birds are created with your sport. Therefore, О mother of the universe, salutation to you.” When the king was thus praying, he viras addressed thus.

## \|\| 2.74.12-23 \|\|

*mahābalo mahāvīryastanayaste bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tava stutyā prasannāhaṃ dāsyāmi vividhaṃ phalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa nṛpatiḥ svagehaṃ prāpya nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*rājñyai nivedayāmāsa devīvacanamuttamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhṛti rājendra mūrtau jātā svayaṃ kila \|*  
*ekasmindivase rājanrajakaḥ kalibhojanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kāśīdāsena sahito grāmaṃ dharmapuraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tatra dṛṣṭvā śubhāṃ kanyāṃ kāmāṃgīṃ nāma viśrutām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pitrānvitāṃ rājamārge gacchaṃtī śramapīḍitām \|*  
*mumoha kāmavegena rajakaḥ kalibhojanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kāmāṃdhaścaṃḍikāṃ prāha jaganmātaḥ sanātani \|*  
*yadi me bhavitā subhrūstarhi dāsyāmi te śiraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jātiyogyā mamaivāsti rajakasya sutā śubhā \|*  
*iti śrutvā tu sā devī vacanaṃ rajakasya vai \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mohayitvā ca pitaraṃ tasyāḥ pāṇigrahaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa sutāṃ kāminīṃ prāpya prasannātmā gṛhaṃ yayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bhuktvā sa vividhaṃ bhogaṃ tayā sārddhaṃ sukhapradam \|*  
*varṣāṃtare śiro devyai gatvā śīghraṃ samārpayat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kāśidāsastu tacchrutvā snehena tvarito'gamat \|*  
*svaśiro dattavāndevyai kāmāṃgī patiśokataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*arpayitvā śiro devyai devīrūpatvamāgatā \|*  
*tadā prasannā sā caṇḍī trīnujjīvyābravīcca tān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*varaṃ varayatāmadya yo yaḥ kāmo hyabhīpsitaḥ \|*  
*kāśidāsastu tāṃ prāha kāmāṃgīṃ māṃ samarpaya \|\| 23 \|\|*

12-23. The Akasavam declared- “O valorous one, you will get a powerful son. I am extremely happy with your prayer. Therefore, I shall grant you several o f the rewards.” On hearing these words, the king reached his palace and repeated the entire episode to his queen. Since that day onwards, she started living in the body of the king. Once a washerman named Kalibhojana accompanied with another person Kasidasa went to Dharampura village. Finding a girl named Kamangi there, who was moving on the road with his father, the washerman was filled with passion and became attracted towards her. He then prayed to the goddess Candl-“O eternal goddess, О mother of the universe, in case this girl accepts me to be her husband, then I shall offer my head to you. She is the daughter of a washerman of my own caste. Because of this, I am praying to have her.” On hearing the words of the washerman, the goddess confused the father of the girl and got her married to the boy of the washer man. Thereafter, the washerman boy, accompanied with his beloved wife, went to his abode and enjoyed several types of pleasures with her and ultimately, he offered his own head to the goddess. On the other hand, because of his love for her, Kasidasa also offered his head to the goddess. Ultimately, Kamangi also grieving for her husband, achieved the form of the goddess. At that point of time, getting pleased, the goddess brought back all the three of them to life and said to them-“All of you should ask for the boon you like.” At this, Kasidasa said- “Give me Kamangi. ”

## \|\| 2.74.24-25 \|\|

*kāmāṃgī sā tu tāṃ prāha svapatiṃ māṃ samarpaya \|*  
*kalibhojana evāsau devīṃ prāha prasannadhīḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mitrāṃgaṃ sundaraṃ mahyaṃ dehi mātarnamonamaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ vācastadā śrutvā sā durgā maunamāsthitā \|*  
*yathākāmaṃ dattavatī varaṃ dārasurūpiṇī \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. However, Kamangi asked- “You give me back my own husband.” Kalibhojana, on the other hand, said- “O mother, the beautiful limb of my friend should be given to me. I offer my salutation to you again and again.” Listening to their words, the goddess Durga kept silent at that time. Subsequently, she granted them the desired boons as well.

## \|\| 2.74.26-28 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo nṛpaṃ prāha vihasya bhoḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kiṃ kṛtaṃ ca tayā devyā teṣāmarthe vadasva me \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa tu bhūpālo vaitālamidamabravīt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kapālamuttamaṃ dehe tayā cchinnaṃ dvayostadā \|*  
*viparītaṃ kṛtaṃ mātrā varaṃ svaṃsvaṃ samāpnuyuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Suta said- Thus speaking, Vaitala laughed and said to the king- “How did the goddess fulfilled their desires? You speak out to me in details.” When so asked by the Vaitala, the king said- “The goddess cut off the heads of both of them. In this way, the goddess did the opposite apparently, but they got the boons as desired by them.”

## Chapter 75. Collateral history of the age of Kali

## \|\| 2.75.1-9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasminkāle sa vaitālo bhṛguvaryaḥ prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*rājānamuttamāṃ gāthāṃ varṇayāmāsa viśrutām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*caṃpāpurī ca vikhyātā campakeśo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*tatrāste balavāndhanvī mahiṣī tatsulocanā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*trilokasuṃdarī nāma kanyā tasyāmajāyata \|*  
*vadanaṃ candravadyasyā bhruvau cāpasame smṛte \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mṛgākṣī kokilaravā komalāṃgī mahottamā \|*  
*devairmanovṛtā bālā kimanyairmānuṣairnṛpa \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasyāḥ svayaṃvaro jāto nṛpā bahuvidhāstadā \|*  
*tasyā yogena saṃprāptā ye bhūpā bhuvi viśrutāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*indro yamaḥ kuberaśca varuṇo vibudhottamaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā naramayaṃ rūpaṃ tadarthe samupāgatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*caṃpakeśamidaṃ prāha śṛṇu rājanvaco mama \|*  
*sarvaśāstreṣu nipuṇaṃ rūpavantaṃ manoramam \|*  
*indradattaṃ ca māṃ viddhi svasutāṃ me samarpaya \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dvitīyastu tadā prāha dharmadattaṃ manoramam \|*  
*dhanurvedeṣu nipuṇaṃ svakanyāṃ dātumarhasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaścāha bho rājandhanapālāya śobhine \|*  
*sarvajīvasya bhāṣāṇāṃ jñāyine guṇarūpiṇe \|*  
*mahyaṃ ca svasutāṃ śīghraṃ samarpaya sukhī bhava \|\| 9 \|\|*

1-9. Suta said- At that point of time, the Vaitala got pleased and then started narrating another story. A king named Campaka once ruled in the city of Campapuri, who was quite strong and a great archer. Sulocana was the name of his chief queen, who gave birth to a daughter named Trilokasundari, who had the face resembling the moon, bow-like eyebrows, the eyes like those of a deer and the speech of a cuckoo. Many of the kings and the rulers were desirous of possessing that girl, then what to speak of the ordinary humans? A marriage ceremony was performed for her, in which all the prominent rulers of the world participated with a desire to possess her. Even the gods like Indra, Yama, Kubera and Varuna reached there taking to the human form. One of them said to the king Campaka - “O king, you listen to my words. I am quite beautiful, well-versed in the use of all the arms and my name is Indradutta. You give your daughter to me.” The other said- “My name is Dharmadatta and I am well-versed in archery. Therefore, you give away your daughter to me.” The third one said- “O king, I am known by the name of Dhanapala and I know all the languages of the world, besides I am virtuous. Therefore, you give your daughter to me and be comfortable.”

## \|\| 2.75.10-15 \|\|

*caturthaścāha bho rājansarvakalāsu kovidaḥ \|*  
*pañcaratnasamudyogī pratyahaṃ bhūpate hyaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

*puṇyārthamekaratnaṃ ca homārthaṃ dvitiyaṃ vasu \|*  
*ātmārthaṃ tṛtiyaṃ ratnaṃ patnyarthe turiyaṃ vasu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śeṣaṃ subhojanārthaṃ ca ratnaṃ nityaṃ mayāhṛtam \|*  
*īdṛgvidhaṃ māṃ puruṣaṃ svasutāṃ dātumarhasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ mohito nṛpatistadā \|*  
*svasutāṃ prāha dharmātmā kasmai dāsyāmi kanyake \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sā devī tu vacaḥ śrutvā vrīḍitā daivamohitā \|*  
*nottaraṃ ca dadau tasmai svapitre dharmaśālinī \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo vihasyovāca bhūpatim \|*  
*kasmai yogyā bhavetkanyā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|\| 15 \|\|*

10-15. The fourth one said- ‘I am well-versed in all the arts and make all the efforts to earn five gems a day. Achieving them, I spend the first gem for the welfare of other, the second gem is used for the performing of homa, the third one is used for self, the fourth for my wife and the fifth one is used for food to the eunuchs. Therefore, you should give away your daughter to a person like me.” Listening to these words, the king was highly influence with him. At once he said to his daughter- “You tell me, to whom should I give you?” The chaste girl, out of modesty, could not give any answer to her father. Thus speaking, the Vaitala said to the king smilingly- “Who was the suitable match for the youthful and the chaste girl?”

## \|\| 2.75.16-18 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa tu bhūpālo vacanaṃ taṃ samabravīt \|*  
*dharmadattāya sā kanyā yogyā bhavati rūpiṇī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarvaśāstreṣu nipuṇaḥ sa dvijo varṇataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhāṣāvettā tu vaṇijo dhanadhānya prasārakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kalājñaḥ sa tu śūdro hi dhanurvedī sa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*savarṇāya ca vaitāla sadā yogyā hi kanyakā \|*  
*ato vivāhitā bālā dharmadattāya śīline \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Suta said- At these words of Vaitala, the king replied to him that the beautiful girl was suitable for Dharmadatta, because he was well-versed in all the Sastras and was a Brahmana by birth. The Vaisya who could increase the wealth, the Sudra was well-versed in all the arts and the Ksatriya was well-versed in the art of archery. The girl is always most suited for her own caste. Therefore, with all the humility, Dharmadatta was married to the girl.

## Chapter 76. Collateral history of the age of Kali

## \|\| 2.76.1-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa vaitālo rājānamidamabravīt \|*  
*videhadeśe bhūpāla nagarī mithilāvatī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*guṇādhipastatra rājā dhanadhānyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*ciraṃdeva iti khyāto rājanyaḥ kaścanāgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vṛttyarthaṃ mithilādeśe tatra vāsaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*varṣāṃte bhūpatiḥ so'pi caturaṅgabalānvitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mṛgayārthe vanaṃ prāptastatra śārdūlamuttamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā taṃ cāvadhīdrājā krodhatāmrekṣaṇo vane \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vyāghra mārgeṇa bhūpālo vanāntaramupāyayau \|*  
*ciraṃdevastu tatpaścādgataḥ sa gahane vane \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭho nṛpatiḥ śramasantāpapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*ciraṃdevamuvācāśu bhojanaṃ dehi me'dya bhoḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Suta said- Hearing the words of Vikrama, Vaitala again said to him- “O king, there is a city named Mithila in the country named Videha. Once a king named Ganadhipa ruled the country which had enough of riches and cereals. Once a prince named Cirandeva reached there for taking up a job there in the city. He started living there. After a year, the king of the land, with his fourfold army, went to the forest for hunting. In the fit of anger, while following a tiger, the king reached a thick forest. The prince Cirandeva also entered the thick forest. Due to thirst, the throat of the king dried up and feeling inconvenienced, the king said to Cirandeva- “You give me food quickly today.”

## \|\| 2.76.7-15 \|\|

*iti śrutvā sa rājanyo hatvā hariṇamuttamam \|*  
*saṃskṛtya pradadau rājñe tanmāṃsaṃ bhūpatipriyam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tuṣṭo bhūpastadā prāha varaṃ varaya sattama \|*  
*vāṃchitaṃ te dadāmyāśu sa hovāca mahīpatim \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tvayā sahasramudrāśca khāditā mama bhūpate \|*  
*gṛhamānīya bhūpāla tāḥ samarpaya mā ciram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śatamudrāstu māsānte mahyaṃ dehi kuṭuṃbine \|*  
*tathetyuktvā sa nṛpatiḥ svagehaṃ śīghramāyayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ekasmindivase rājansa ca rājā guṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*ciraṃdevaṃ svabhṛtyaṃ ca preṣayāmāsa sāgare \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sa gatvā sāgarataṭe devīmūrtiṃ dadarśa ha \|*  
*nāmnā kusumadāṃ devīṃ mārkaṇḍeyasthalasthitām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gandharvatanayāṃ subhrūṃ pūjayitvā prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*prāṃjaliḥ puratastasthau tadā devī samāgatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*varaṃ varaya taṃ prāha ciraṃdevastu cābravīt \|*  
*pāṇiṃ gṛhāṇa me subhrūstvadrūpeṇa vimohitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu sā devī vihasyovāca kāminam \|*  
*adya snānaṃ vidhehi tvaṃ matkuṇḍe devanirmite \|\| 15 \|\|*

7-15. On hearing the words of the king, the prince hunted an excellent deer, cooked its meat and served to the king. Feeling satisfied with the consuming of the meat of the deer, the king said to him- “O excellent one, you ask for a desired boon.” The prince said to the king- “While serving you without wages for a long time, I have consumed a thousand gold coins of a merchant. You kindly call him and clear my dues. Besides that, for the maintenance of my family, you kindly sanction me a salary of a hundred gold coins per month.”. The king accepted the proposal of the prince and returned to his palace. Once the king Gunadhipa sent his servant Cirandeva to the ocean, who reaching there, found the image of goddess Kusumada there, which was lying gracefully at the place of the sage Markandeya. Feeling delighted, he adored the daughter of a Gandharva, stood before the image with folded hands. Then the goddess said - “You ask for a boon.” Cirandeva said- “I am attracted towards your beauty. Therefore, you accept my hand.” On hearing this, the goddess smilingly said to the passionate person- “O Cirandeva, you better have a bath in the Kunda built by the gods.

## \|\| 2.76.16-26 \|\|

*tathetyuktvā gatastoye plāvito mithilāṃ yayau \|*  
*sa sthito bhūpatiṃ prāha kāraṇaṃ vismayapradam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*guṇādhipastu tacchrutvā svabhṛtyena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*prāptavānmaṃdire devyāḥ sā bhūyaḥ prāha puṣpadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gāṃdharveṇa vivāhena māṃ gṛhāṇa guṇādhipa \|*  
*iti śrutvā nṛpaḥ prāha yadi devi vaco mama \|\| 18 \|\|*

*puṇyade tvaṃ gṛhāṇādya tarhi tvāṃ saṃbhajāmyaham \|*  
*tatheti matvā taṃ prāha satvaṃ kāryaṃ nivedaya \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sa hovāca śṛṇu tvaṃ bho mama bhṛtyaṃ ciraṃ suram \|*  
*bhaja tvaṃ capalāpāṃgi devi satyaṃ vacaḥ kuru \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vrīḍitā tu kathāṃ kṛtvā bhūpatiṃ prāha kāminī \|*  
*māṃ bhajasva dayāsiṃdho kāminīṃ śakracoditām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ciraṃdevaṃ tu saṃprāpya kāmāṃdhā tvāṃ samāgatā \|*  
*puṣpadaṃtaruya tanayā gandharvasya śubhānanā \|*  
*śāpitā devadevena narabhogakarī hyaham \|\| 22 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa bhūpālo dharmātmā śīlavigrahaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ bhajāmyahaṃ subhrūḥ snuṣāmiva sudharmiṇīm \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ciraṃdevastu rājanyo matputra iva vartate \|*  
*tasya tvaṃ bhoginī nārī śobhane bhava sāṃpratam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*lajjitā sā tadā devī snuṣevaḥ ca vavarta vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ityuktvā bhūpatiṃ prāha vaitālo rudrakiṃkaraḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ dharmaśca kasyaiva jātastanme vadasva bhoḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

16-26. Obeying the command of the goddess, as soon as Cirandeva had a dip in the water, then he found himself present in the city of Mithila. Then he narrated all the happenings to the king Gunadhipa. Then Cirandeva, together with the king Gunadhipa, reached the temple of the goddess. The goddess then said to the king-“O Gunadhipa, you accept me by means of the Gandharva type of marriage.” Hearing the goddess, the king said to her- О goddess Puspa, in case you accept a condition of mine, then I would be prepared to accept you.” Accepting his words, the goddess said- “You urgently speak out the same.” The king said-“O damsel with wavering eyes, you accept my servant Cirandeva and make my words truthful.” Feeling shy, the passionate damsel said to the king- “O ocean of mercy, you accept me, since I have been sent by Indra for you alone, because I happen to be the daughter of Puspadanta. Having been incited in passion by Cirandeva, I have reached you. I have been cursed by Indra that I shall be used by the humans.” On hearing this, the religious-minded king, who was filled with humility, said to her- “O beautiful one, you are well-versed in dharma, then how can I accept you? Since you are the wife of my son, because the prince Cirandeva is like my son. О graceful one, you are suitable for him alone. You just think over it. Subsequently, feeling ashamed, she behaved like the daughter-in-law of the king. Thus speaking, Vaitala - the attendant of Rudra, said to king Vikrama - “You tell me truthfully as to whom did the damsel belong, according to Dharma?"

## \|\| 2.76.27-30 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bhūpatistaṃ vihasyāha ciraṃdevasya jāyate \|*  
*satyaṃ dharmaśca vetāla śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ śubham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nṛpāṇāṃ paramo dharmaḥ sarvopakaraṇaṃ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṛtopakārabhṛtyasya tena tatkiṃ hi satyatā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*bhṛtyena ca kṛtaṃ karma tacchṛṇuṣva vadāmyaham \|*  
*vinā vṛttiṃ sthito gehe bhūpaterguṇaśālinaḥ \|*  
*sevā vṛttiḥ kṛtā sarvā yathānyairna naraiḥ kṛtā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*paścādbhūpatinā jñātaḥ saṃkaṭe bṛhadāgate \|*  
*ciraṃdevastu tasmācca kāraṇādadhiko mataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. Suta said- The king then replied smilingly- “O Vaitala, according to dharma, the damsel truthfully belonged to Cirandeva and I am going to narrate the reason for the same. You please listen. The king is desired to look at the welfare of one and all. Therefore, the king did good to his servant and there is no truth involved in it. But whatever the servant did, I am going to repeat the same. In the palace of the king, the servant live without any wages and served the king while living there like other servants for long (who were paid the wages). When there arose a misfortune, only then the king became aware of the factual position that he was serving without any (return or wages), and because of this Cirandeva has his own importance.

## Chapter 77

## \|\| 2.77.1-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bho śaunaka mahābuddhe vaitālena mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*mahāpravīṇaśca matastamāha sa ca bhūpatim \|\| 1 \|\|*

*rājankāmapure ramye vīrasiṃho mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*nyāyato dharmataścaiva tatra rājyamacīkarat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*hiraṇyadattastatraiva vaiśyo dhanamadānvitaḥ \|*  
*kāmālasā tasya sutā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*avasatsukhato nityaṃ vasaṃte kusumapriyā \|*  
*kadācitkusumārthaṃ vai vanaṃ bhramaranāditam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*gacchantīṃ tāṃ samālokya dharmadattātmajo balī \|*  
*somadatta iti khyātaḥ pasparśa madanālasām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sā tu taṃ nirjane sthāne provāca vinayānvitā \|*  
*kanyakāhaṃ mahāvīra tyaja māṃ dharmatodya bhoḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Suta said - O immensely wise Saunaka, honouring the immensely competent king, Vaitala said to him- O king, in the pleasant city of Kamapura, the king Virasimha ruled the country judiciously according to the provision of the scriptures. A rich Vaisya known by the name of Hiranyadatta also lived there. He had a daughter who possessed enough of beauty and youthfulness. She was living a comfortable life. She liked the flowers and during the spring season, she was always anxious to possess flowers. Once she went to a flower garden for the collection of flowers, in which the black wasps were hovering over the flowers. At that point of time, she was spotted by Dharmadatta - son of Somadatta and intended to use his force on her. In the secluded and lonely place, she said to him- “O valorous one, I am still a girl, therefore, you free me in the name of dharma.

## \|\| 2.77.7-14 \|\|

*vivāhe sati pūrvaṃ tvāṃ bhajāmi daśame'hani \|*  
*ato daśadinasyaivādeśaṃ dehi dayānidhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tatheti matvā tāṃ tyaktvā nijagehaṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*kāmālasā tu tadgrāme pitrā dattā varāya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*madapālāya vaiśyāya maṇigrīvasutāya ca \|*  
*śvaśurasya gṛhaṃ gatvā svamitraṃ pratyacintayat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*navame'hani tatsvāmī gṛhītvā kāminīṃ balāt \|*  
*kāmāturaḥ sa patnīṃ tāmāliliṃga madānvitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*arudatsā tu tatpatnī mitravākyena karṣitā \|*  
*tāmuvāca tadā vaiśyaḥ śāṃtipūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kiṃ rodiṣi madāpūrṇe satyaṃ kathaya śobhane \|*  
*sā tu satyavatī prāha yathājātaṃ hi kānane \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yadi nāyāmi pārśve tvāṃ somadatta dhanottama \|*  
*tadā vaidhavyatāṃ prāpya bhajāmi vṛjinaṃ hi tat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*iti vākyena baddhāhaṃ yāsyāmyadya tadaṃtike \|*  
*iti śrutvā ca tatsvāmī tāmājñāpya mudānvitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

7-14. I am going to be married shortly and after the tenth day, I shall myself come and serve you here. Therefore, O Ocean of mercy, you free me for ten days. The boy accepted the prayer of the girl and returned home. The father of the daughter married his daughter to a boy Madapala - son of Manigriva. The girl then reaching her inlaw’s house, got worried for her friend. On the ninth day, getting lustful, her husband tried to forcibly embrace her. But his wife reminded him of the earlier incident and started crying. At that point of time, her husband spoke to her peacefully— “Your eyes are filled with lust, then why are you crying? You tell me the truth.” Then the truthful wife narrated the entire incident which occurred in the orchard and also that in case she would not come to him as promised, then she would lead the life of a widow in order to atone the sin. Therefore, because of the promise, I shall surely go to him.” On hearing these words, her husband gladly permitted her to go to her friend.

## \|\| 2.77.15-24 \|\|

*suṣvāpa sā tu tatpārśve hyagamatkāmavihvalā \|*

*caurastāmāha bhoḥ subhrūrbhūṣaṇa dehi me'bale \|*

*āliṃgyopapatiṃ mitraṃ tubhyaṃ dāsyāmi bhūṣaṇam \|*

*dṛṣṭvā tāmabravīdvaiśyaḥ kathaṃ yātā smarālase \|*

*kāmālasā tu tacchrutvā yathā jātaṃ tathā'bravīt \|*

*matvā pativratāṃ nārīṃ parikramya vyasarjayat \|*

*gehe praveśayāmāsa tatpatiryatra tiṣṭhati \|*

*bubhuje viṣayāndivyāndevadevena coditān \|*

15-24. Subsequently, after sleeping at his back for some time, getting her passion ignited, she went to her friend. On the way, finding her moving and having been adorned with all the ornaments, the thief said to her quite greedily-“Where are you going? Who has not honoured you during the night? О woman, you tell me truthfully.” She said to the thief- “Having been hurt with passion, I am going to my friend.” The thief then said to her- “O beautiful one, you hand over all the ornaments to me. Being a thief, I am interested in the wealth.” On hearing this, the lady said- “After embracing my friend, I shall hand over ail the ornaments to you.” Accepting the same, the thief also went to Somadatta. Finding the beautiful damsel, the Vai$ya said- “0 passionate one, how have you been able to reach here? You tell me truthfully. Only then I shall accept your service.” Thereafter, the girl truthfully narrated the entire story to him, listening to which Vi$nudeva, getting enlightened and taking her to be quite a chaste lady, went round her and sent her back gracefully. Having been enlightened by Vi$nudeva, the thief also entered the house of the damsel after her entry. Subsequently, with the influence of her chastity and enjoying all the comforts provided by the god of gods, the passionate woman started spending her life. Thus speaking, Vaitala then said to the king Kovida - “Whose truthfulness was the best and commendable out of these three? You please tell me.”

## \|\| 2.77.25-28 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa tu bhūpālo vaitālamidamabravīt \|\| 25 \|\|*

*caurasya satyatā śreṣṭhā yathā jātā tathā śṛṇu \|*  
*nṛpabhītyā sa vaiśyastu tāṃ nārīṃ na tu bhuktavān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vaidhavyabhītyā sā devī svamitraṃ prati cāgatā \|*

*caurastu satyabhītyā vai tyaktvā tāṃ mudamāgataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. Suta said- At these words of Vaitala, the king Vikrama replied to him- “I am speaking out the reason for the same. The Vaisya could not enjoy the woman for fear of the king. The woman went to her friend, apprehensive of becoming a widow. But the thief only, for the sake of truth, gladly disowned the woman.”

## Chapter 78. Collateral history of the age of Kali

*tanmantrī nirbhayānando jainadharmaparā yaṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kadācidbhūpatiryāto mandire girijāpateḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa taṃ devaṃ sarvavyāpinamīśvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vṛścikastatra saṃprāpya dadaṃśa nṛpatiṃ ruṣā \|*  
*tatkaṣṭena sa bhūpālo mūrchitaḥ patito bhuvi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tadā tu nirbhayānando viṣamuttārya tasya vai \|*  
*bhūpatiṃ varṇayāmāsa jainadharma parāyaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śṛṇu rājanmahābhāga śatrūnṣaṇmānasādhamān \|*  
*kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho ratirhiṃsā ca tṛṣṇikā \|*  
*rajoguṇācca te jātāsteṣāṃ bhedāḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Suta said- О excellent one, Vaitala again said to the king- “O lord, there is a city named Vardhana in the Gauda country. A famous and religious-minded king named Gunasekhara ruled there. He had a courtier named Nirbhayananda, who was the follower of Jaina dharma. Once the king went to the temple of Siva and worshipped the omnipresent lord Siva. At the same time, the king was bitten by a scorpion as a result of which the king was fainted and he fell down on the ground. At that point of time, removing the poison of the scorpion, Nirbhayananda said to the king- “O lord, 0 king, the six enemies who emanate from the pride and are degraded ones, I am speaking about them. You please listen. The desire, anger, greed, love, violence and lust are the six blemishes which emerge out of rajoguna. They are divided separately.

## \|\| 2.78.7-17 \|\|

*moho daṃbho madaścaiva mamatāśā ca garhaṇā \|*  
*tamoguṇācca te jātāstairidaṃ pūritaṃ jagat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kāmī viṣṇustathā rudraḥ krodhī lobhī vidhistathā \|*  
*daṃbhī śakro yamo mohī madī yakṣapatiḥ svayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*māyā vaśyāśca te sarve tarhi tatpūjanena kim \|*  
*ṣaṭśatrubhirjito yo vai sa jino munibhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na jitaḥ sa jino jñeyo'dvaitavādī niraṃjanaḥ \|*  
*tasya dhyānena bhāvena mokṣavaṃto narāḥ sadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tatprasādāya yo dharmaḥ śṛṇu me vasudhādhipa \|*  
*gopūjanena te devāstuṣṭiṃ yānti sadaiva hi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ato gopūjanaṃ śuddhaṃ hiṃsā sarvatra varjitā \|*  
*madapānena sarvātmā jinaḥ kleśaṃ samāpnuyāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasmānmāṃsaṃ ca pānaṃ ca varjitaṃ sarvadaiva hi \|*  
*nyāyenopārjitaṃ vittaṃ bhojayecca bubhukṣitān \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ravirātmā jinasyaiva tatprakāśe hi bhojayet \|*  
*ityevaṃ varṇayitvainaṃ maṃtrī gehamupāyayau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tathaiva matvā sa nṛpo jinadharmaṃ gṛhītavān \|*  
*kiyatā caiva kālena vedamārgo hi laṃghitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadā tu duḥkhitā rājñī śivasya śaraṇaṃ yayau \|\| 16 \|\|*

*varadānena rudrasya putro jāto mahottamaḥ \|*  
*dharmarāja iti khyāto vedavrataparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

7-17. Confusion, cheating, pride and the deplorable hope which is spread in the world, emerged out of tamoguna. Visnu is lustful, Siva is filled with anger, BrahmA is full of greed, Indra is a cheat, Yama creates illusion, while Kubera is filled with pride. Thus all these gods are overpowered by Мaуa. Therefore, what benefit can a person derive by worshipping them? With the aforesaid six enemies, when defeat a person, the Munis have described them as Ajina. A person who has overpowered his enemies, he becomes advaitavadi (believer of the Advaita philosophy), who getting free from attraction is known as Jina. By meditating on the same and getting absorbed in the similar types of thoughts, the people achieve moksa. О lord of earth, the dharma that has been prescribed for the sake of his pleasure, the same is being repeated by me. You please listen. All the gods remain happy with the worship of the cow. Therefore, the worship of the cow is the pure dharma, because the killing of a cow is prohibited everywhere. With the consumption of wine, Jina who happens to be the soul of all, is inconvenienced. Therefore, the eating of meat and the drinking of wine is totally prohibited. Earning of the wealth should be done by judicious means and the hungry should be served with the food. The sun has been stated to be the soul of the Jina. Therefore, the followers of Jina dharma should eat when the sun shines. Thus describing the Jina-dharma, the courtier went to his abode. Accepting his words, the king accepted the Jina dharma. After the lapse of some time, he acted against the Vedic dharma. At that point of time, his queen feeling painful took refuge with lord Siva, along with the excellent son, who was given the name as Dharmaraja and he happened to be the follower of the Vedic dharma.

*guṇaśekhara evāsau paṃcatve nirayaṃ yayau \|*  
*dharmarājastadā rājyaṃ kṛtavāndharmataḥ svayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tasya dharmaprabhāveṇa tatpitā svargamāptavān \|*  
*trayaḥ patnyobhavaṃstasyaguṇarūpā mahottamā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sarovare snāpitavānmadāghūrṇitalocanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-21. In due course of time, the king Gunasekhara died and he had to fall in the hell. Thereafter, Dharmaraja himself started ruling the country on religious lines and with the influence of his dharma, his father achieved the heaven. According to the virtue of Dharmaraja, he had three wives each one of who was of excellent nature. During the spring season, the king went to an orchard with his three queens where the black wasps were hovering over the blossomed flowers and started sporting with them. Inspite the king being of a peaceful nature, he got intoxicated and delightfully started taking bath in a pool.

## \|\| 2.78.22-26 \|\|

*gṛhītvā kusumaṃ pādmaṃ kare rājñyai samārpayat \|*  
*padi hīnatvamāyātā patatā kusumena vai \|\| 22 \|\|*

*duḥkhitaḥ sa tu bhūpālo rājñīṃ tāmacikitsayat \|*  
*rātrau prāpte dvitīyā tu candraśīlena mohitā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*apatadvyākulībhūtvā śuddhaṃ pādamabhūttataḥ \|*  
*patitāyāśca śabdena tṛtīyā jvaritā'bhavat \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tasyā mūrcchā tadā kṣīṇā dvitīyāyā ajāyata \|*  
*nṛpasparśena sā subhrūrjvaratāpaṃ vihāya ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*prabhāte suṃdare jāte sa tābhirgṛhamāyayau \|*  
*ityuktvā sa tu vaitālo bhūpatiṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|*  
*āsāṃ madhye mahārāja kā śreṣṭhā sukumārikā \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. Не took out a lotus flower and presented it to the queen in her hand. But the flower fall over her foot and she became lame. Feeling painful, the king got his queen medically treated. Again during the night, at the rising of the moon, she was upset with the moon rays and fell down on the ground. But the earlier queen recovered and her foot became normal. Listening to the sound of the fall of the second queen, the third queen got fever. At the same time, the second queen who had fainted regained consciousness. When the king touched the third queen, her fever disappeared. At the same time, the swoon of the second queen disappeared. With the touch of the king, the fever of the queen disappeared. With the appearing of the pleasant dawn, the king together with all the queens, returned to his abode. Thus speaking, Vaitala humbly said to the king- “Which one of the queens was of most tender nature?”

## \|\| 2.78.27-31 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*tṛtīyā sukumārī ca tāsāṃ madhye mahottamā \|*

27-31. The king said- Out of all the queens, the third one is the best. The first queen became lame because she was of wineful nature. With the force of cough, the second queen was fainted and the third suffered simply with the hearing of the sound. Therefore, she happens to be the best. Again the king, who was a devotee of Siva, said- “Is the Jaina dharma better or the Vedic dharma?” The king replied- “Because of its being the eternal one, Vedic dharma is the foremost. The manifest Brahma has eight categories viz., Sudra, Vaisya, Ksatriya, Brahmana, Brahmacarl, the householder, forest dweller and Sahyasi. They are said to be the best respectively.

## \|\| 2.78.32-33 \|\|

*yaḥ kṛtvā dārasaṃsargaṃ yativadvartate gṛhī \|*  
*sa pāpī narakaṃ yāti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*gṛheṣu yativaddharmo jainaśāstre prakīrtitaḥ \|*

32-33. The householder coming in the contact with the wife like an ascetic, such a sinner falls in the hell till the time of dissolution. To live like a Sanyasi in the household is the ideology of the Jaina scriptures. Because of this, it has been called as the dharma of false doctrine. The learned people therefore discard the same.

## Chapter 79. Collateral history of the age of Kali

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bhoḥ śaunaka mahābhāga sa vaitālo hi devatā \|*

*rājanpuṇyapure ramye nānājananiṣevite \|*  
*dharmavallabhabhūpālastatra rājyaṃ purākarot \|\| 2 \|\|*

*satyaprakāśastanmaṃtrī lakṣmīścāmātyakāminī \|*

1-5. Suta said- О Saunaka - the excellent one, the same Vaitala again told a religious story which was quite an auspicious one to the king saying, in the pleasant city of Punyapura, a king named Vallabha once ruled there. The name of his courtier was Satyaprakasa, who was served by Laksmi like his beloved. Once the religious minded king said to his courtier-“O excellent one, how many types of pleasures are there in the world? You tell me.” The courtier replied- “O lord, four types of comforts have been described (in the scriptures). Brahmananda is the great bliss in Brahmacarya asrama, which is said to be the best. In the household, the conjugal pleasure is said to be the best, which has been graded as the mediocre type by the learned people.

## \|\| 2.79.6-11 \|\|

*vānaprasthe mahārāja sa dharmānaṃdako'dhamaḥ \|*

*saṃnyaste tu śivānaṃdassa hi sarvottamottamaḥ \|*  
*viṣayānaṃdako rājanstrīpradhānaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*striyaṃ vinā sukhaṃ nāsti gṛhasthāśramake nṛpa \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa bhūpālo deśāṃtaramupāyayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*patnīmanveṣayāmāsa svayogyāṃ dharmatatparām \|*

*sa bhūpo maṃtriṇaṃ prāha nārīmanveṣayādya bhoḥ \|*

*iti śrutvā yayau maṃtrī deśāddeśāṃtaraṃ prati \|*

*tuṣṭāva manasā siṃdhuṃ sarvatīrthapatiṃ śubham \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. О great monarch, dharmdnanda has been described to be the lowest of all as the forest dweller. Although there is no delight in karmakdnda, still it has been described to be the truthful dharma. Sivanahda has been stated to be the delight of Sanydsa or a recluse, it is the best bliss. О king! In the conjugal pleasure, the woman is the foremost because as a householder, no pleasure is possible without a wife.” Thus hearing, he went to the other countries and started searching for a wife who could be quite suitable for him. But inspite of his best efforts, he could not get a wife well suited to his temperament. Then he said to his courtier- “You search a woman for me, otherwise, I say truthfully that I shall end my life.” On hearing this, the courtier started on journey for other countries. Reaching the Sindhu country, he said to the ocean - the lord of all the holy places.

## \|\| 2.79.12-17 \|\|

*buddhiprakāśa uvāca \|*

*ahaṃ te śaraṇaṃ prāptaḥ śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*

12-17. Buddhiprakasa said- О lord, О Sindhudeva, you are the abode of gems. Salutation to you. You are graceful on those who take refuge in you. I take refuge in you. You are the lord of Ganga and other rivers, besides being the lord of waters. Salutation to you. Therefore, you give me a woman for the sake of my king, otherwise I am going to lay down my life. On hearing this, ocean - the lord of all the rivers, produced a tree out of the water, which had the limbs of gold, the leaves were like coral and had the fruits of pearls. The same tree was shown by the ocean to the courtier. A beautiful woman was seated on that tree. But suddenly she drowned in the oceanic water with the tree. Observing this wonder, the courtier returned to the king and narrated the entire story to him. Then he went to the same place along with the king.

18-31. Reaching that place, the king also observed the tree and the damsel. The king then reached the nether world with that woman. Then he spoke to her with all humility- “I have reached here for your sake only. Therefore, you own me by Gandharva type of marriage.” She then smiled and said to the king- “I shall come on the fourth day of the dark fortnight and shall serve you.” On hearing this, the king, feeling lustful on that particular day, holding a sword in his hand, reached the excellent temple of the goddess. But at the same time, a demon mounted over a skylark arrived and touched the damsel, which enraged the king. Then having been blinded by lust, the king killed the demon and fearlessly said to his wife- “O beautiful one, what was he to you and why had he arrived here? You tell me the reason for the same.” She said- “I am the daughter of a Vidyadhara and am the darling of my father. Feeling passionate, I once reached the forest and could not return to the place of my parents at the time of taking food. Then my father realised the truth by means of his yogic powers and pronounced a curse on me, that I shall have to serve a demon on the black fourteenth day. Therefore, on the fourteenth day of the black fortnight, you enjoy the result of your sin on the prescribed day. At the same time, while crying, I said to my manes- “O Deva of excellent vrata, when shall I get redeemed? You tell me the truth about it.” They said- “O damsel, at the time when you would become enjoyable by the valorous person, you would be freed from your curse. O king, with your permission, I intend to go to my parents.” Hearing this, the king said- “You first come to my place and thereafter, I shall accompany you.” This was accepted by the damsel and she departed with the king. At that point of time, the people of the kingdom celebrated huge festivities. But finding the king with a divine woman, the courtier met with his end. What was the reason for it? You tell me.”

32-34. The king said- Buddhiprakasa - the courtier, while looking at the divine damsel, started thinking about the king in his mind. Because the king would be under the control of the woman, the kingdom would get shattered. Finding no alternative to it, realising the danger ahead, he met with his end and proceeded on to the heaven. Because the rulers who are lustful, their kingdoms are shattered. Getting intoxicated with the pride of the women, they always have to face loss.

1-14. Suta said- Then the Vaitala said to the king smilingly. A king named Cudamani lived once in Cudapura. A Brahmana named Devasvami, who was well-versed in Vedas and the allied literature, happened to be his preceptor. His wife with vast eyes was always devoted to her husband. The beautiful damsel adored lord Siva for having a son. With the boon granted to her by lord Siva, she got a beautiful son named Harivarma who was as beautiful as the god of love and had the part of Devas in his body. Possessing all the riches and wealth, he was leading a comfortable life on earth. His wife was known by the name of Rupalavanyika. She was a divine woman and was born from the son of Devala by his curse. Once at the spring time, when greenery was spread everywhere, the beautiful damsel accompanied with her husband was lying over the bed with her husband, when a Gandharva named Sukala felt attracted toward her beauty. He kidnapped her and carrying her over his plane, he brought her in his city. When her husband was awaked, he was upset to find his wife missing and started searching for her. When he could not find her, then getting disgusted, he left the country and retired to the forest. Reaching there and discarding all the activities, he became an ascetic and devoted himself to the lord. Once he became desirous of eating payasam, so he went to a Brahmana suffering from hunger. Getting payasam from there he went under a banyan tree and seated himself there. Then he, keeping the payasam under the tree, went to the river to take his bath there. О king, at the same time, a serpent polluted the payasam with its venom. On his return, the ascetic took the payasam and soon after taking it, he felt intoxicated. Suffering from the pain of venom, he said to the Brahmana- “The payasam is mixed with poison. Therefore, О wicked one, I am going to die, but you shall have to suffer for the sin of Brahmahatya.” Thus speaking, the ascetic met with his death and went to Sivaloka. Getting an illustrious damsel there, he started living comfortably. Thus speaking, the Vaitala asked the king- “Who was responsible for earning the sin of Brahmahatya in this case? You kindly tell me.

15-19. The king said- It is quite natural for a snake to possess venom, who polluted the payasam due to ignorance. Therefore, he is responsible for the sin, but not Brahmahatya. The Brahmana, unfortunately gave alms to a hungry ascetic and by so doing, he performed the dharma of his race. Therefore, he also cannot earn the sin of Brahmahatya. All the people always reap the harvest of their own deeds. Having been humiliated by a Brahmana, he received the poisonous food from the Brahmana. He ate it, had the guest renounced himself, only then the Brahmana would have been entitled to owe the sin of Brahmahatya. Such a Brahmana too is also not suited to earn the sin of Brahmahatya. Such of the people, who while discussing the matter would say-“You have indulged in Brahmahatya,” they would earn the related sin.

1-15. Suta said- Feeling beholden, the Vaitala said to the king with a delightful heart. In a city named Candrahrdaya, once ruled a king named Ranadhira. In the same city, there lived a religious-minded Vaisya named Dharmadhvaja. He had a beautiful girl named Sukhabhavini. Once a man of that city started adoring a demon. Gambling and eating of flesh became his daily routine. A man-eater Raksasa also lived there, known by the name of Vasara. The devotee of the demon offered the meat and the wine for the same Raksasa. The Raksasa once getting pleased with his devotee, said to him- “You ask for a boon you desire. I am prepared to give you everything.” The devotee said- “O man-eater, in case you intend to grant me a boon, then tell me a secret place underground, which could be used by me for storing of the things that I get after stealing.” Hearing this, the demon told him the place, which surprised that person immensely. The devotee started living there with the Raksasa. Once the thief stole and kidnapped a slave girl of the king and he lodged her there at the same place. Thus the thief had seven wives of all the four varnas. Out of all of them, only the slave girl of the king happened to be his favourite. The Raksasa has built that place like royal fort, which could surprise the people of the earth. The thief usurped several types of riches forcibly and kept them there. The people of the country became impatient and said to the king - “The thieves are creating several obstructions in the country. Therefore, we people are the thinking of leaving the city.” On hearing these words, the king summoned his armed guards who were well-versed in subjugating the thieves and deputed them all in all the four sides of the city. But getting confused with the illusion of the RcLk§asa, they became flabbergasted. The thieves on the other hand, using all the force continued to usurp the riches of the people. The people of the city again went to the king and prayed to him, hearing which the king felt surprised. He devoted himself to serve the people.

16-38. Once in the mid of the dark night, the thief asked the king who had arrived there- “Who are you? What is the purpose of your arrival here?” The king replied- “I am also a thief and have arrived here for committing a theft I am prepared to go to the rich people, but you will have to accept my condition. All of you should go with me and usurping various types of riches, you lead a comfortable life.” The thief accepted the condition of the king. They stole several types of riches, making the king to stand outside. Then they entered the fort to safely lodge the booty at the secret place. In the mean time, the slave girl who was the wife of the thief and lived there, spoke to the king- “You at once rush to your house, because the thieves are planning to kill you, while they are inside.” Thus speaking, the slave girl also revealed to the king the secret route of escape. The king then returned home. At the time of spotless dawn when the sun arose, he moved with his entire army and reached the place of the thief. Thereafter, the frightened thief narrated the entire happenings of the night to Vasara - the Raksasa, who laughed and said- “You have I provided me a good food. The unfortunate men who is arriving here today, would be eaten by me. I shall be moving for the same purpose.” Thus speaking, the Raksasa reached the king. He consumed many of the royal soldiers and those who could somehow escape, they flee to different directions. The Raksasa shattered the limbs of the king, confusing him at the same time. In the mean time, getting annoyed the thief reached before the king and said to him-“It would not be proper for a religious-minded king to flee from the battlefield. Hearing these words, the king at once rushed to the temple of the goddess - the powerful one. He meditated on her and received an excellent mantra. Then he reduced to ashes the secret chamber with the Raksasa and caught hold of all the thieves, who stole the riches of the people in the city. All of them were handcuffed. They were all produced with bondages, besides the wealth they had stolen in the kings’ court. All of them were then punished. Thereafter, with the beating of the drums, all the people were requested to produce the evidence against the thieves. The main thief was then mounted over a donkey and taken round the city and ultimately, he was taken to the door of the merchant Dharmadhvaja. At the same time, Sukhabhavini - the daughter of the merchant, fell for the beauty of the thief. Then feeling painful, she said to her father- “You get this thief released urgently.” The merchant then went to the king and said- “I have five hundred gold coins. Kindly accept them and release the thief, otherwise my daughter would meet with her end.” On hearing this, the king spoke with a smile- “He is a thief who had stolen the riches of others. Therefore, this degraded person cannot be pardoned by me on earth.” On hearing this, the merchant was disappointed. The thief was ultimately killed. At the time of crucification, the thief first laughed and then wept. At the same time, the daughter of Vaisya, getting fascinated with the move of Devamaya, carried the body of the thief and reached the fire altar. At the same time, the goddess Durga also getting pleased, brought the thief back to life and bestowing salvation on him, also showered a divine boon on him. Thus speaking, the Vaitala laughed and said to the king Vikrama-“Why did the thief firstly laughed and then wept? What is the reason for it ”

## \|\| 2.81.39-43 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*madarthe sundarī nārī svaprāṇāndātumudyatā \|*  
*tasyai kiṃ ca pradātavyaṃ mayā tatsneharūpiṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ato roditavānpaścāddhasane kāraṇaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*dhanyo'yaṃ bhagavānkṛṣṇo yasya līleyamīdṛśī \|\| 40 \|\|*

*adharmiṇe ca nākasya phalaṃ dātuṃ samarhati \|*  
*dharmiṇe narakasyaiva phalaṃ tasmai namonamaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*ataḥ sa hasitaḥ pūrvaṃ mohito harilīlayā \|*  
*iti śrutvāha vaitālo hareḥ śaraṇamuttamam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vākyaṃ tena kṛtaṃ śūlyāmato jīvitavācchuciḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

39-43. The king said- “The beautiful girl is prepared to sacrifice her life for me. Though I happen to be her beloved, but what can I give her in return? He wept for this reason. Now I shall narrate the reason for his laughing. You please listen. Graceful is lord Krsna, who has such a type of sport that he bestows heaven to the sinner and the Dharma is driven by him to the hell. Salutation to him again and again.” Having been overpowered with the sport of the lord, he first laughed and then on hearing this, the Vaitala said- “It is best to take refuge with the lord, because inspite of his getting crucification, he finally achieved the auspicious life.”

1-13. Suta said- О chief of the race of Bhrgu, О excellent one, Vaitala said to the king- there was a pleasant city called Pu$pSvatI, which was ruled by a king named Suvicara. He was always welcomed to serve the people well. He had a beautiful wife, known by the name of Candraprabha. The said queen once gave birth to a daughter named Candravati. Once she went to the forest for outing with her handmaids, where flowers of different types were blossoming. There she found a Brahmana named Sudeva and she fell for his beauty. On the other hand, the Brahmana boy too was fascinated for her and he fell down on the ground. Having been overpowered with passion, he appeared like a lifeless person. After the departure of the princess, two Brahmanas named Muladeva and Sasi arrived at his gate. Finding the Brahmana possessing great beauty, they enquired of the reason for his feeling lustful. He narrated the factual position to them. On reaching his home, the compassionate Muladeva recited the mantra of Camunda Devi, made two pills and gave them to Sudeva. Using them both, one of them taking to the form of a twelve year old beautiful girl and Muladeva taking to the form of an old man, reached the court of the king. Reaching there, they blessed the king, honouring him at the same time. О Intelligent one, you also listen to the reason for their entry in that palace. He said to the king- “O king, I have a beautiful home in the Tantrika city. A king named Vilapadhvaja wanted to get my beautiful house plundered. Because of this reason, my two sons and my wife have all disappeared and the place where they went is unknown to me. I am wandering in search of my wife and the sons. О lord, this is my daughter-in-law. You keep her with you, till my return,. You protect her.” On hearing his words, the king called for his daughter and entrusted the care of daughter-in-law of the Brahmana to her. The Brahmana then returned to his place.

14-17. At the dead of night, the damsel said to the princess- “Why has your face faded out? You tell me the truth.” She said- “A Brahmana named Sudeva always occupies my heart. Therefore, О handmaid, I always suffer because of her absence.” At this, she said- “In case I produce that Brahmana boy before you, then what will you give me as a reward?” The princess said- “I shall always remain your slave.” On hearing this, the damsel removed the pill from her mouth and regaining the original position (as a boy), he started enjoying the conjugal pleasures with her.

18-34. О king, in due course of time, the princess became pregnant for four months. At that time, the son of the courtier felt attracted towards the wife of the Brahmana. Finding Madanalasa - the son of the courtier as lifeless and because of his love for the courtier, he thought about his condition and consulted the learned men and gave over the damsel to him. Thereafter, the Brahmana damsel said to the son of the courtier- “O son of Amatya, you would become suitable for me after taking bath at holy places for three months. You first try to do the same.” Accepting her words, Madanalasa proceeded with humility for pilgrimage. Thereafter, the passionate person made use of his wife who was as beautiful as the queen herself and was also passionate, and impregnated her for two months. Thereafter, taking to the form of a man, he reached the house of Muladeva and apprised him of the factual position. Feeling delighted, Muladeva turned his friend as the boy of twenty years age and he himself took to the form of an old man and reached the house of the king and said- “O lord of the land, you give back my daughter-in-law to me. Feeling panicky, the king said to him meekly- “MadanSlasa^- the son of the courtier named Rajakara, felt attracted towards that bride. Finding him dying for the damsel, the courtier because of the separation of his son, said to me- “With the permission of the old Brahmanas, I have entrusted her to him. Now, under these circumstances, you get me the command, that could please you.” Then using poisonous or harsh words, Muladeva said- “O king, you give me your daughter for the pleasure of my son.” Accepting the words of the Brahmana, the king gave away his daughter Candravati adorned with all the ornaments and riches, and getting himself relieved of the blemish of Brahmana, he ruled the country. The boy Sasi accompanied with the princess went to his abode. At the same time, feeling painful at heart, Sudeva said to Muladeva- “The princess is meant for my use ” Hearing this, Muladeva felt surprised. Thus speaking, Vaitala - the attendant of lord Siva, said to the king Vikrama- “Who should get the princess^ according to dharma? You kindly tell me.”

35-42. The king said- With the permission of the parents, the girl appeared before the gods, to whomsoever she is given she belongs to him. О Deva, the woman are always treated like the gems in the scriptures. As inspite of the seeds when sown in the field by someone else, the seed remains the property of the owner of the field and out of the one who sows the seed, therefore, the princess would belong to Sasi, but the son in her womb would belong to Sudeva, who should get the same. О Deva, thus I have explained the position according to the Sdstras” The Vaitala again said to the king Vikrama- “Then what did the son of the courtier do? You tell me.” On hearing this, he said- “Madanalasa - the son of the courtier, reaching Vrndavana on the day of astami took his bath in Radhakunda. О best of the rulers, with the influence of that merit, the sin he had committed was removed. Then reciting the name of Govinda in his heart, he offered prayer to him in sweet voice.”

*madanālasa uvāca \|*

*iti stotraprabhāvena devadevena mocitā \|*

43-48. Madanalasa said- О lord Krsna, you have expanded the universe like the ocean, therefore, you are the ocean of mercy. Salutation to you. О god of gods, for the sake of your sport, you create the universe alone and protect it with Radha - your beloved. At the end, you yourself taking to the form of Kala, destroy the universe. Salutation to you again and again. The means by which my thoughts could be purified, you kindly do so quickly.” With the reciting of this prayer, his mind was purified and relieved of the passions. Thereafter, the Ksatri returned to his own home and embracing his wife, he felt immensely delighted. Then the intelligent person, for the removal of the blemish (in which he had indulged against a Brahmapa), called for Sudeva and delightfully gave his own sister in marriage to him. Sudeva, having been overpowered with passion, after getting his marriage performed legally, delightfully returned to his own place. This story of the king was brought to end with the story of Muladeva.

1-5. Suta said- О Brahmana, Vaitala - the attendant of Siva, while praising the king Vikrama, again started telling a story. He said- О lord, in the land of Kanyakubja, there lived a Brahmana, who gave enough of charities. He was truthful and was always devoted to the worship of the goddess. Whatever amount was received by him in charity, he donated it further. Once during the winter season, he started performing the vratas of the goddess Durga. On a particular day, he could do no charity for giving it away. He felt worried for the same. He thought- “What should I do to get some money for serving food to the girls after inviting them. How shall I serve food to them?” Thus feeling worried, he suddenly got five rupees by the grace of the goddess, by which he could complete his vrata.

*sarvākalāsu nipuṇo nāmnā jīmūtavāhanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sa vai pūrvabhave rājanmadhyadeśe mahottame \|*  
*kṣatriyaḥ śūrasenākhyo babhūva vasudhādhipaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*utsavaṃ rāmadivase cakāra vidhivannṛpaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śrutā rāmamayī gāthā tasya puṇyaprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*vidyādharatvamāpanno mumude tatra śakravat \|\| 14 \|\|*

6-15. Не remained without food for nine days and completed his vrata. As the effect of this vrata, the Brahmana after his death, was reborn in the family of gods. He was known as Jimutaketu and was the leader of the Vidyadharas. He enjoyed all the divine pleasures in the pleasant city of Vidyadhara, over the Himacala mountain. In this condition he stayed there for some years. He used to worship the Kalpavrksa daily with devotion. By the grace of that sacred tree, he got a son who was well-versed in all the arts. He was known by the name of Jimutavahana, who was a Ksatriya king named Surasena in the excellent region of Madhyadesa. Once the king, while hunting reached in the forest of lotus flowers. It was the abode of the sage Valmiki. He did not kill any creature on the bright ninth day of the month of Caitra. But the king spent a day and night, celebrating the festivities there. In the leaf hut of the sage Valmiki, he remained awake upto midnight and listened to the stories of lord Rama. As a result of this, he started spending his life as Vidyadhara and spent comfortable life like Indra. The great soul then worshipped the Kalpavrksa for a full one year and thereafter, he said to him- “O excellent one, you ask for a boon.”

*jīmūtavāhanaścaiva pūjārthe maṃdiraṃ yayau \|*  
*bālāṃ dadarśa divyāṃgīṃ sarvabhūṣāsamanvitām \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. Не said- “О great tree, you bestow enough of wealth and cereals on the city of mine.” At these words of his devotee, the holy tree made the city like a royal town. The one who was dependant on some other king, he himself thus became the king. In that city, all the people lived quite comfortable life like a ruler. At the same time, both the father and the son went to the forest for the performing of tapas. Reaching the pleasant place of the Malaya mountain, both of them performed severe tapas. Once the daughter named Kamalaksi of the king Malayadhvaja arrived in Siva temple for the worship of the lord. Jimutavahana also reached there at the same time for worship and saw the beautiful damsel with divine limbs.

22\. At the sight of the princess, Jimutavahana mentally adored the god of love having been hurt with the arrows of love.

*duḥkhitaḥ sa jagāmāśu dayālurdīnavatsalaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vṛddhāmāśvāsya papraccha kenedaṃ duḥkhamāgatam \|*  
*sāha me tanayo deva garuḍāsye gamiṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tadviyogena duḥkhārtā vilapāmi mahākulā \|*  
*iti jñātvā sa nṛpatirgaruḍottuṃgamāyayau \|\| 30 \|\|*

23-30. Jimutavahana said- О god of love, salutation to you. Salutation to the son of Krsna. You took away the life of Sambara and you are the form of four vyuhas. Salutation to you. Salutation again aad again to the five arrows, desire and Pradyumna. You kindly put under me the damsel with five pelvic regions having the lotus like face.” On hearing this, lord Makaradhvaja confused his father and performed the marriage of both of them. The prince of the place known by the name of Visvavasu also reached there with the husband of his sister at Gandhamadana mountain, offering his salutation there. At that point of time, the mother of the serpent Sankhacuda started crying before Jimutavahana, feeling disgusted. The compassionate Jimutavahana assured the old lady and asked her the cause of her pain. She said- “My son would become the food of Garuda. I feel painful because of that reason. О king, on learning this, he also reached the peak of Garuda tinge.

## \|\| 2.83.31-41 \|\|

31-41. Garuda caught hold of the serpent and reached the sky. Then he dropped the damsel over the body of whom the blood spots of her husband could be seen. While flying the sky finding Garuda devouring her husband, she felt painful and cried aloud. At the same time, Garuda also getting frightened, hurriedly reached there and said to Jimutavahana- How have you become my food?” He replied- “O intelligent one, listen, I tell you. The mother of Sankhacuda was feeling extremely painful at the apparent loss of her son. I have arrived here in order to save her son’s life.” О king, at these words of Jimutavahana, the serpent Sankhacuda feeling painful for pain of the serpent, went to his enemy Garuda and said- “O Ocean of mercy, you better tear me up. I have arrived here as your food. О Intelligent one, you leave aside this human, use me as your food.” At that point of time, getting pleased, Garuda bestowed three boons. He said to Vidyadhara - Jimutavahana- “I shall never eat the serpents of the family of Sankhacuda. You would achieve a great kingdom in the country of Vidyadhara and you would rule there for a lakh of years and then shall proceed to Vaikuntha.” Thus speaking, Garuda disappeared, while the prince got the kingdom and returned to his kingdom with his father. Thereafter, ruling the country with his wife for long, he then achieved Vaikuntha. Thus speaking, Vaitala humbly said to the king Vikrama- “Who out of these earned the highest merit?”

## \|\| 2.83.42-44 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*

42-44. The king said- “Out of all of them, Sankhacuda achieved the highest merit, because Brahma has ordained the rulers to do good to the people. Because of the chaste lady, the king got back his life, which pleased Garuda as well, but he could earn no merit. Therefore, becoming fearless, Sankhacuda went to his enemy and offered himself to be killed. Therefore, he got the highest merit.”

1-10. Suta said- Vaitala again spoke to the king Vikrama who was the foremost of all the learned people. The king Candrasekhara has his capital city in the southern region, where a Vaisya named Ratnadatta lived who was quite rich and possessed enough of wealth and cereals. He had a beautiful daughter named Kamavaruthini. Observing her excellent, the merchant said to the king- “O lord, my daughter is extremely beautiful, who is desired even by the gods. О ocean of mercy, you kindly accept her, because BrahmA has created her for your sake only.” On hearing this, the king Candrasekhara said to his courtier named Vidura- “0 wise one, you have a look at the girl and let me know the factual position.” Thus speaking, the king Candrasekhara went to his abode. Syamala - the wife of the trader, on coming to know of the arrival of the king, collecting the incense, lamp and flowers etc., welcomed them appropriately. At the same time, a cow who was being tortured by a tiger, cried aloud, listening to which the king holding a sword in his hand, reached the place (where the cow was being attacked). He at once killed the tiger and was feeling happy, when a danava named Mukula, taking his form from the body of the tiger, humbly spoke to the king- “O master, achieving redemption at your hands, I am reverting to the place of Varuna.”

11-15. I was turned into the form of a tiger due to the curse of Prahlada. Thereafter, the daitya proceeded on to the place of Prahlada and the king also went to his palace, feeling extremely delighted and went to sleep. The next morning after having been waken up, the king reached the royal court. On the other hand, at the command of the king, the courtier went to the girl named Kamavaruthini and having a look at her divine beauty, he thought on to himself. The king would surely feel attracted at the sight of this beauty. Therefore, he said to the king-“The girl is not at all suitable for you. Accepting the words, the courtier did not marry the girl. Thereafter, the girl was married to Balabhadra - the chief commander of the forces of the king Ratnadatta.

16-24. Once the king, having a look at Kamavaruthini, got fainted. Then the chief commander put the king in a palanquin and carried him to his court. On his regaining consciousness there, the king delightfully said to the chief commander- “Who is the husband of this beautiful damsel and where was she bom?” Hearing this, Balabhadra spoke with humility- “This beautiful damsel is my wife and the daughter of Ratnadatta. Since the courtier was apprehensive of the kingdom getting shattered, he did not highlight her beauty before you. But my wife is always suitable for you. О ocean of mercy, you kindly accept her. I am prepared to fulfil your desire. On hearing this, the king with his eyes red in anger, said to him- “This beauty is your wife as per dharma. Therefore, in case, I accept this damsel, the messengers of Yama shall drive me to the hell and I shall have to face an ugly situation there.” Thus speaking, the king burning with the fire of separation from her, at once reached Dharmapura in order to end his life.

25-30. Thus speaking, Vaitala asked the king Vikrama- “After the death of the king, his queen ended her life with him. The chief commander also ended his life with his master. Thereafter, Kamavaruthini also burnt her body and then went to the heaven with all. But then who was most virtuous of all of them?” The king then said to Vaitala- “The death of a servant for the sake of his master is more meritorious. It is also quite appropriate for a chaste lady to end her life with her husband. But a servant offered his beautiful wife to his master, who was not accepted by the king for fear of dharma, though he was attracted towards her. To the contrary, he overpowered his passion and followed dharma. Therefore, the stance of the king is most meritorious.”

*sūta uvāca \|*

1-5. Suta said- The Vaitala who had taken to the form of a Brahmana, again said to the king Vikrama- I am going to narrate a beautiful story to you. You please listen. О virtuous one, once there was a king at Ujjaini, known by the name of Mahasena. In his country, there also lived a Brahmana named Deva Sarma. His son was known by the name of Gunakara, who daily ate meat and consumed wine. The sinful one, atonce destroyed his entire property in gambling. Subsequently, when he was disowned by all the relatives, he started wandering on earth everywhere. As per the move of destiny, be once reached Siddhasrama. A yogi named Kapardi lived there. He tried to welcome the guest keeping the food in a human skull. But considering the yogi to be the son of a Pisaca, he did not take the food.

## \|\| 2.85.6-11 \|\|

*tadātithyaṃ tadarthaṃ sa yakṣiṇīṃ samupāhvayat \|*  
*tayā rātrau mahānandaṃ prāptavānsa dvijaḥ śayī \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prātaḥ kāle tu saṃprāpte kailāsaṃ yakṣiṇī gatā \|*  
*sa dvijastadviyogena yogyaṃtikamupāyayau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kapardī pradadau tasmai vidyāṃ yakṣiṇikarṣiṇīm \|*  
*catvāriṃśaddinānyeva niśīthe jalamadhyagaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sa jajāpa śubhaṃ mantraṃ na prāptā kāmacāriṇī \|*  
*tadā yogyājñayā vipraḥ svayaṃ tu mamatāṃ tyajan \|\| 9 \|\|*

*prāptavānpitarau natvā svagehe nivasanniśi \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pratibodhivanaṃ prāptastacchiṣyatvamupāyayau \|*  
*pañcāgnimadhye sa sthitvā tanmaṃtramajapacchuciḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. The yogi then invoked a Yaksini in order to welcome the guest. On that particular night, the Brahmana slept with the Yaksini and enjoyed the night. In the early morning, Yaksini returned to Kailasa and he getting separated from her felt painful and went to the yogi. Kapardi then bestowed him with the knowledge of attracting the Yaksini. The said Brahmana boy went in the water and started reciting the auspicious mantra. He recited the mantra for forty days, but still could not achieve the Yaksini. Then at the command of the yogi, the Brahmana discarding all the attractions and illusions, honouring his parents, turned himself as a sanyasi or a recluse and deserting his grieving family, went to the Pratibodhi forest.

## \|\| 2.85.12-17 \|\|

*na prāptā yoginī devī tadā cintāturo 'bhavat \|*  
*ityuktvā sa vaitālo nṛpatiṃ jñānakovidam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*punarāha kathaṃ devī na prāptā yakṣiṇī priyā \|*  
*śrutvāha nṛpatirvipra vaitālaṃ rudra kiṃkaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

*trividhaṃ karma bho vipra siddhyarthe sādhakāya vai \|*

*sundarāṃgakṛtaṃ jñeyaṃ punarvākkāyasaṃbhavam \|*
