*pracacāra tato loke satyanārāyaṇārcanam \|*  
*kāmasiddhipradaṃ muktibhuktidaṃ kaluṣāpaham \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. Lord Narayana accepted the same and disappeared from the place. The Brahmana too felt beholden to the lord. Observing this, all the people were extremely surprised. All the people received the prasada, prostrating on earth. Then they praised the Brahmana immensely and proceeded towards their abodes. The worship of lord Satyanarayana started since that time, which fulfils the desires besides bestowing the devotion and salvation, removing all the sins at the same time.

## Chapter 94. Glory of Satyanarayana Vrata

## \|\| 2.94.1-12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*rājāsīddhārmikaḥ kaścitkedāramaṇipūrake \|*  
*candracūḍa iti khyātaḥ prajāpālanatatparaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śāṃto madhuravāgdhīro nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*babhūvuḥ śatravastasya mlecchā viṃdhyanivāsinaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasya tairavabhavadyuddhamatiprabaladāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*bhuśuṃḍīyuddhanipuṇaiḥ kṣepaṇaiḥ parighāyudhaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*candracūḍasya mahatī senā yamapure gatā \|*  
*śataṃ rathāstathā nāgāsahasraṃ tu hayāstathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pattayaḥ paṃcasāhasrā mṛtāḥ svargapuraṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*dasyavaḥ paṃcasāhasrā mṛtāḥ kaitavayodhinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ākrāṃtaḥ sa mahābhāgastairmlecchairdaṃbhayodhibhiḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā rāṣṭraṃ ca nagaraṃ saikākī vanamāyayau \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tīrthavyājena sa nṛpaḥ purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*tatra nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ vaṃdyaṃ sarvagṛhegṛhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dadarśa nagarīṃ caiva dhanadhānyasamanvitām \|*  
*yathā dvārāvatī jñeyā tathā sā ca purī śubhā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vismitaścaṃdracūḍaśca dṛṣṭvāścaryamanuttamam \|*  
*satyena rodhitāṃ lakṣmīṃ śīladharmasamanvitām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā śrutvā sadānaṃdaṃ satyadevaprapūjakam \|*  
*patitvā taccaraṇayoḥ praṇanāma mudā yutaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dvijarāja namastubhyaṃ sadānaṃda mahāmate \|*  
*bhraṣṭarājyaṃ ca māṃ jñātvā kṛpayā māṃ samuddhara \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yathā prasanno bhagavāṃllakṣmīkānto janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tathā tadvada yadyogyaṃ vrataṃ pāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

1-12. Suta said- There was a king named Candracuda who ruled the city of Kedaramani. He was extremely religious-minded and was always engaged in serving the people well, besides being peaceful, sweet-spoken, patient and devoted to Narayana. The Mlecchas who were the dwellers of Vindhya mountain happened to be his big enemies. Once there started a terrific war between the king and the Mlecchas. In the war, the enemy warriors who were well-versed in the use of Bhusundi missiles as well as the Parighas, destroyed the vast enemy of Candracuda. A hundred of his chariots and an equal number of his elephants, a thousand horses and five thousand foot soldiers and an equal member of slaves were also killed. They were fighting with the use of secret methods of warfare. All of them reached the heaven after having been killed in the battleground. Ultimately, the auspicious-souled king was surrounded by the enemy army. Somehow, he alone escaped and reached a forest. Then he started wandering on the pretext of pilgrimage and reached the city of Kasi, where he found lord Narayana having been established in seal at every home, besides he found the city having been filled with enormous wealth and cereals which surprised the king Candracuda. Then observing that Laksmi had been with the truth and dharma, he further felt astonished. Thereafter, finding Sadananda who was the devotee of Satyadeva, he fell at his feet and with his body having been filled with emotions, he offered his salutation to him, placing his head over his feet. He said- “O lord of Brahmanas, О Intelligent one, О Sadananda, salutation to you. My kingdom has been usurped. Therefore, you kindly redeem me. The lord of Laksmi is known as Janardana. You kindly tell me a vrata which could be the destroyer of the sins.”

## \|\| 2.94.13-20 \|\|

*sadānaṃda uvāca \|*  
*duḥkhaśokādiśamanaṃ dhanadhānyapravardhanam \|*  
*saubhāgyasaṃtatikaraṃ sarvatra vijayapradam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*satyanārāyaṇavrataṃ śrīpatestuṣṭikārakam \|*  
*yasminkasmindine bhūpa yajeccaiva niśāmukhe \|\| 14 \|\|*

*toraṇādi prakartavyaṃ kadalīstaṃbhamaṃḍitam \|*  
*paṃcabhiḥ kalaśairyuktaṃ dhvajapaṃcasamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tanmadhye vedikāṃ ramyāṃ kārayetsa vratī dvijaiḥ \|*  
*tatra sthāpya śilārūpaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ svarṇa samanvitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kuryādgaṃdhādibhiḥ pūjāṃ premabhaktisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*bhūmiśāyī hariṃ dhyāyansaptarātraṃ vyatītayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa nṛpatiḥ kāśyāṃ devamapūjayat \|*  
*rātrau prasanno bhagavāndadau rājñe'simuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śatrupakṣakṣayakaraṃ prāpya khaṅgaṃ nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya ca sadānandaṃ kedāramaṇimā yayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

*hatvā dasyūnṣaṣṭiśatāṃsteṣāṃ labdhvā mahaddhanam \|*  
*hariṃ prapūjayāmāsa narmadāyāstaṭe śubhe \|\| 20 \|\|*

13-20. Sadananda said- There is a vrata for Satyanarayanadeva which is the remover of sufferings, grief etc. and bestows enough of wealth, cereals, fortunes, increasing the progeny, besides being instrumental in providing all-round success. This vrata delights the lord of Laksmi. He should be worshipped on any day in the evening time. The banana trunks should be planted and the mandapa should be decorated with arches. The performer should establish five pitchers filled with water along with five banners. In the centre of the same, a pedestal should be made over which the stone image of lord Krsna should be established. It should be worshipped offering fragrance etc. Thereafter, seated on the earth, one should meditate on the lord. The king then adored lord Narayana in the city of Kasi The lord Narayana getting pleased with the devotion of the king, bestowed a sword to him. The sword which could destroy all the enemies was received by the king, who offering his salutation to Sadananda, returned to the city of Kedaramani. He killed six thousand of his enemies there and attained enormous wealth. Thereafter, he performed the vrata as well as рuja of the lord Naraуаnа over the bank of the river Narmada.

## Chapter 95. Glory of Satya-narayana Vrata

## \|\| 2.95.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*athetihāsaṃ śṛṇuta yathā bhillāḥ kṛtārthinaḥ \|*  
*vicaraṃto vane nityaṃ niṣādāḥ kāṣṭhavāhinaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vanātkāṣṭhāni vikretuṃ purīṃ kāśīṃ yayuḥ kvacit \|*  
*ekastṛṣākulo yāto viṣṇudāsāśramaṃ tadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dadarśa vipulaiśvaryaṃ sevitaṃ ca dvijairharim \|*  
*jalaṃ pītvā vismito'bhūdbhikṣukasya kuto dhanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yo dṛṣṭo'kiṃcano vipro dṛśyate'dya mahādhanaḥ \|*  
*iti saṃciṃtya hṛdaye sa papraccha dvijottamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*aiśvaryaṃ te kuto brahmandurgatiste kuto gatā \|*  
*ājñāpaya mahābhāga śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said- Hereafter, you listen to the history in which the Nisadas, who were engaged in the carrying of the wood wandering in the forest daily, were rendered successful. Once the Nisadas after collecting wood from the forest, carried it to the city of Кasi for sale there. One of them, getting upset with thirst, went to the asrama of a devotee of the lord and found there a wealth of Brahmanas, who were engaged in the worship of the lord performing his vrata. He felt extremely surprised. After drinking the water there, he thought, wherefrom the ascetics receive the riches? “A Brahmana, who earlier was seen to be quite poor, how could become so rich presently? What is the reason of it?” Thus thinking in his mind, he ultimately asked the Brahmana- "What is the reason for the removal of your misfortunes and earning of enormous wealth? О excellent one, you kindly inform me about the same.”

## \|\| 2.95.6 \|\|

*sadānaṃda uvāca \|*  
*satyanārāyaṇasyāṃga sevayā kiṃ na labhyate \|*  
*na kiṃcitsukhamāpnoti vinā tasyānukaṃpayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Sadananda said- By serving the lord Satyanarayana, what is beyond the reach of a person? In other words, one can achieve everything. Without his grace, one cannot get even an inch of comfort.

## \|\| 2.95.7-14 \|\|

*niṣāda uvāca \|*  
*aho kimiti māhātmyaṃ satyanārāyaṇārcane \|*  
*vidhānaṃ sopacāraṃ ca hyupadeṣṭuṃ tvamarhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sādhūnāṃ samacittānāmupakāravatāṃ satām \|*  
*na gopyaṃ vidyate kiṃcidārtānāmārtināśanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*iti pṛṣṭo vidhiṃ vaktumitihāsamathābravīt \|*  
*candracūḍo mahīpālaḥ kedāramaṇipūrake \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mamāśramaṃ samāyātaḥ satyanārāyaṇārcane \|*  
*vidhānaṃ śrotukāmo'sau māmāha sādaraṃ vacaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*mayā yatkathitaṃtasmai tannibodha niṣādaja \|*  
*saṃkalpya manasā kāmaṃ niṣkāmo vā janaḥ kvacit \|\| 11 \|\|*

*godhūmacūrṇaṃ pādārdhaṃ seṭakādyaiḥ sucūrṇakam \|*  
*saṃskṛtaṃ madhugaṃdhājyairnaivedyaṃ vibhave'rpayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*paṃcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya candanādyaiśca pūjayet \|*  
*pāyasāpūpasaṃyāvadadhikṣīramathoharet \|\| 13 \|\|*

*uccāvacaḥ phalaiḥ puṣpairdhūpadīpaimarnoramaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayetparayā bhaktyā vibhave sati vistaraiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

7-14. Nisada said- It is quite surprising in case he enjoys such a glory. Then you also kindly apprise me of the method of the worship of lord Satyanarayana, with all the requirements. Because for such type of sages, nothing which remove the misery is secret with them because they always do good to others. For the purpose of revealing the method of adoration, he narrated an ancient story. He said, in the city of Kedaramanipura, there once ruled a king known by the name of Candracuda. He reached my asrama and desired to know the method of the worship of lord Satyanarayana. He respectfully prayed for the same. O son of Nisada, whatever had been spoken by me to him is being repeated by me to you presently. You please listen. The people should mentally think about their requirements, they should mentally resolve in their mind or even otherwise they can take a sera (930 grams) of wheat flour or half or quarter of it and mix it up with honey, ghi and make the best of eatable of the same, which should be offered to the lord Satyanarayana. (Saligrama) should be bathed with pancamrta and adorned with sandalpaste. Then he should be offered payasam, fried cakes, pudding, curd and milk. Similarly, according to one’s means, one should offer fruits, flowers, excellent incense, lamps and worship him with devotion.

## \|\| 2.95.15-28 \|\|

*na tuṣyeddravyasaṃbhārairbhaktyā kevalayā yathā \|*  
*bhagavānparitaḥ pūrṇo na mānaṃ vṛṇuyātkvacit \|\| 15 \|\|*

*duryodhanakṛtāṃ tyatkvā rājapūjāṃ janārdanaḥ \|*  
*vidurasyāśrame vāsamātithyaṃ jagṛhe vibhuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sudāmnastaṃḍulakaṇāñjagdhvā mānuṣyadurlabhāḥ \|*  
*saṃpado'dāddhariḥ prītyā bhaktimātramapekṣyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gopo gṛdhro vaṇigvyādho hanumānsavibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ye'nye pāpātmakā daityā vṛtrakāyādhavādayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇāntikaṃ prāpya modaṃte'dyāpi yadvaśāḥ \|*  
*iti śrutvā narapatiḥ pūjāsaṃbhāramādarāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kṛtavānsa dhanaṃ labdhvā modate narmadātaṭe \|*  
*niṣāda tvamapi prītyā satyanārāyaṇaṃ bhaja \|\| 20 \|\|*

*iha loke sukhaṃ prāpya cānte sānnidhyamāpnuyāḥ \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyo niṣādo'bhūtpraṇamya dvijapuṃgavam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sa gatvā svagaṇānāha māhātmyaṃ harisevane \|*  
*te hṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve samayaṃ cakrurādṛtāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*satyanārāyaṇe pūjāṃ kāṣṭhalabdhena yāvatā \|*  
*vayaṃ kulaiḥ kariṣyāmaḥ puṇyavṛkṣavidhānataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*iti niścitya manasā kāṣṭhaṃ vikrīya lebhire \|*  
*caturguṇaṃ dhanaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ svaṃsvaṃ bhavanamāyayuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mudā strībhyassamācakhyurvṛttāṃtaṃ sarvamāditaḥ \|*  
*tāḥ śrutvā hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pūjanaṃ cakrurādarāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kathānte praṇamanbhaktyā prasādaṃ jagṛhustataḥ \|*  
*svajātibhyaḥ parebhyaśca dadustaccūrṇamuttamam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pūjāprabhāvato bhillāḥ putradārādibhiryutāḥ \|*  
*labdhvā bhūmitale dravyaṃ jñānacakṣurmahottamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bhuktvā bhogānyatheṣṭante daridrāndhā dvijottama \|*  
*jagmuste vaiṣṇavaṃ dhāma yogināmapi durlabham \|\| 28 \|\|*

15-28. The amount of delight the lord earns from devotion of the people, he does not feel so happy with the worldly things. The lord is complete in all respects, therefore one should never take pride in him. Because of this, lord Janardana discarded the services provided by Duryodhana, but accepted the simple food at the place of Vidura accepting his hospitality. He accepted the rice grains of Sudama and after so doing, he bestowed the fortunes on him, which are beyond the reach of a human on earth. Therefore, the lord is only desirous of his devotion. The cowherds, Jatayu - the vulture, Vyadha - hunter, Hanuman, Vibhisana and similarly other sinful Vrtras and gods even today enjoy all the pleasures, living with the lord.” On hearing this, the king collected all the requirements and adored the lord by which he earned the enormous riches. He enjoyed all the comforts over the bank of Narmada. Therefore, О Nisada, you also worship Satyanarayanadeva with love and devotion, by which you enjoying all the pleasures in this world, shall live with him after your leaving the world, enjoying all the comforts. Thereafter, Nisada getting successful, offering his salutation to the best of the Brahmanas, went to his people and narrated to them whatever had been heard by him including the glory of Satyanarayana, listening to which all of them getting delighted respectfully made a resolve that after selling the dry wood whatever money would be received by them, they would utilise the same in the worship of lord Satyanarayana along with their families in an appropriate manner. With this mental resolve, all of them after selling the dry wood, earned four times more the riches, which they delightfully carried to their abodes. Reaching their respective abodes, all of them narrated the incident to their wives individually, which also delighted them. They all performed the worship of the lord. After listening the recitation of the story, all of them completed the worship with devotion. After listening to the recitation, they offered the salutation with devotion and received the prasada, which was also distributed by them among the people of their own castes as well as the other castes. О best of the twice born ones, with the influence of that puja, all the Bhillas making use of the wealth, achieved the best of knowledge and the desired pleasures. The poor yogis achieved the Vaisnavadhama, which is beyond the reach of the people.

## Chapter 96. Glory of the Satya-narayana Vrata

## \|\| 2.96.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha te varṇayiṣyāmi kathāṃ sādhūpacāritām \|*  
*nṛpopadeśataḥ sādhuḥ kṛtārtho'bhūdvaṇigyathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*maṇipūrapatī rājā candracūḍo mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*saha prajābhirānarca satyanārāyaṇaṃ prabhum \|\| 2 \|\|*

*atha ratnapurasthāyī sādhurlakṣapatirvaṇik \|*  
*dhanairāpūrya taraṇīḥ saha gacchannadītaṭe \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dadarśa bahulaṃ lokaṃ nānāgrāmavilāsinam \|*  
*maṇimuktāviracitairvitānaissamalaṃkṛtam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vedavādāṃśca śuśrāva gītavāditrasaṃgatān \|*  
*ramyaṃ sthānaṃ samālokya karṇadhāraṃ samādiśat \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said- I shall now narrate the story of a Vaisya ascetic, who met with success after receiving discourse from the king. Once the immensely glorious king Candracuda of Manipura, together with his people, was once worshipping lord Satyanarayana. In the mean time, a millionaire ascetic of Ratnapura, boarding a boat filled with enormous wealth, moved on witnessing on the way several of the villages and their people. While he was so sailing, he spotted a beautiful place with canopies decorated with the gems and beads. The sound of the reciting of the Vedas accompanied with music was also heard. Finding the pleasant place, he commanded his servants, who were sailing the boat.

## \|\| 2.96.6-14 \|\|

*viśrāmayātra taraṇīriti paśyāmi kautukam \|*  
*bhartrādiṣṭastathā cakre karṇadhāraḥ sabhṛtyakaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*taṭasīmnaḥ samuttīrya mallalīlāvilāsinaḥ \|*  
*karṇadhārā nagā vīrā yuyudhurmallalīlayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*svayamuttīrya sāmātyo lokānpapraccha sādaram \|*  
*yajñasthānaṃ samālokya praśastaṃ samudo yayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kimatra kriyate sabhyā bhavadbhirlokapūjitaiḥ \|*  
*sabhyā ūcuśca te sarve satyanārāyaṇo vibhuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pūjyate baṃdhubhiḥ sārdhaṃ rājñā lokānukaṃpinā \|*  
*prāptaṃ niṣkaṭakaṃ rājyaṃ satyanārāyaṇārcanāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dhanārthī labhate dravyaṃ putrārthī sutamuttamam \|*  
*jñānārthī labhate cakṣurnirbhayaḥ syādbhayāturaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti naraḥ satyasurārca nāt \|*  
*vidhānaṃ tu tataḥ śrutvā cailaṃ baddhvā gale'sakṛt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*daṃḍavatpraṇipatyāha kāmaṃ sabhyānamodayat \|*  
*anapatyo'smi bhagavanvṛthaiśvaryo vṛthodyamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*putraṃ vā yadi vā kanyāṃ labheyaṃ tvatprasādataḥ \|*  
*patākāṃ kāṃcanīṃ kṛtvā pūjayiṣye kṛpānidhim \|\| 14 \|\|*

6-14. “You stop the boat here, because I intend to witness this fun.” Obeying the command of the master, the servants did as was desired by their master. They got down from the boat at the river bank and started displaying their acrobatic proficiency with the sailors, delighting the people there. The ascetic, together with his courtier, descended from the boat and then enquired from the people and knowing the truth about the place, he felt delighted. Finding the place of yajna there, he asked them- “O Gentlemen, what are you doing here?” When so asked by the merchant, the gentlemen replied to him. The king of the place who is always kind to his people, is worshipping Satyanarayana. By the grace of the lord, he achieved the thornless kingdom. With the listening to the same, the one desirous of riches gets the riches, the one desirous of progeny gets a son, the one desirous of knowledge achieves the knowledge and a person in danger is freed from the same. In other words, with the performing of the puja of Satyadeva, all the desires of a human being are fulfilled.” Thereafter, he learnt the method of his worship and tying a cloth around his neck, prostrating on earth again and again, he pleased all the people there. He further said- “O lord, I am childless, therefore, the riches earned by me so far are of no use. But for sake of my own pleasure, in case, even at this stage, if I could get a male or a female child, then I shall worship the lord by offering a gold banner.”

## \|\| 2.96.15-16 \|\|

*śrutvā sabhyā abruvaṃste kāmanāsiddhirastu te \|*  
*hariṃ praṇamya sabhyāśca prasādaṃ bhuktavāṃstadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*jagāma svālayaṃ sādhurmanasā ciṃtayanharim \|*  
*svagṛhe hyāgate tasminnāryo maṃgalapāṇayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. On hearing this, the gentlemen said- “Let your desire be fulfilled.” Thereafter, the vaisya offered his salutation to all of them, started mental adoration of the lord and then returned to his place.

## \|\| 2.96.17-27 \|\|

*maṃgalāni vicitrāṇi yathocitamakārayan \|*  
*viveśāṃtaḥpure sādhurmahākautukamaṃgalaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ṛtusnātā satī līlāvatī paryacaratpatim \|*  
*garbhaṃ dhṛtavatī sādhvī samaye suṣuve tu sā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kanyāṃ kamalalolākṣīṃ bāṃdhavāmodakāriṇīm \|*  
*sādhuḥ parāṃ mudaṃ lebhe vitatāra dhanaṃ bahu \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viprānāhūya vedajñānkārayāmāsa maṃgalam \|*  
*lekhayitvā janmapatrīṃ nāma cakre kalāvatīm \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kalānidhikale vāsau vavṛdhe sā kalāvatī \|*  
*aṣṭavarṣā bhavedgaurī navavarṣā ca rohiṇī \|\| 21 \|\|*

*daśavarṣā bhavetkanyā tataḥ prauḍhā rajasvalā \|*  
*prauḍhāṃ kālena tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vivāhārthamacintayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nagare kāṃcanapure vaṇikchaṃkhapatiḥ śrutaḥ \|*  
*kulīno rūpasaṃpattiśīlaudāryaguṇānvitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*varayāmāsa taṃ sādhurduhituḥ sadṛśaṃ varam \|*  
*śubhe lagne bahuvidhairmaṃgalairagnisannidhau \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vedavāditraninadairdadau kanyāṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*maṇimuktāpravālāni vasanaṃ bhūṣaṇāni ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mahāmodamanāḥ sādhurmaṃgalārthaṃ dadau ca ha \|*  
*premṇā nivāsayāmāsa gṛhe jāmātaraṃ tataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*taṃ mene putravatsādhuḥ sa ca taṃ pitṛvatsudhīḥ \|*  
*atīte bhūyasaḥ kāle satyanārāyaṇārcanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

17-27. At his place, the ladies carrying the welfare material, started performing astonishing activities. In due course of time, the auspicious vaisya together with the performing of playful deeds, entered his city. After sometime, after having the periodical bath, his wife named Lilavati conceived after serving her husband well. In due course of time, she gave birth to a gem like infant girl. She had the wavering eyes resembling the lotus flowers. She delighted the eyes of all the relatives. Finding her daughter, the vaisya was overwhelmed with joy and started distributing enough of riches to the needful people. He summoned the Vedic Brahmanas and got all the welfare ceremonies performed from them. He got the horoscope of the girl child made by the astrologers. She was then given the name of Kalavati. Like the moon who is lord of the rays, Kalavati also kept on growing daily. The girl in the eighth year of her age is known as Gauri; Rohini in the ninth year; Kanya in the tenth year; and thereafter, she is known as the one with menses, with the passage of time. Finding his daughter to have grown up, he selected a youth of Kancanapura city known by the name of Sankhapati for marriage with his daughter. He belonged to a spotless race, possessed enormous beauty, was humble, large-hearted and possessed other virtues as well, besides being suitable for his daughter. Thereafter, during an auspicious time, performing many welfare rites and observing the Vedic rites, he married his daughter to the said vaisya boy. For the sake of her welfare ceremonies, the said Sadhu vaitya gave away enough of gems, beads, corals, costumes and ornaments with utmost delight. Because of his immense love for his daughter, he kept his son-in-law in his own house. The vaisya then started loving him like his own son, while the son-in-law regarded his father-in-law like his own father. After the passage of long time, the vaifya forgot to perform worship of Satyanarayana. Together with his son-in-law, he proceeded to other country for business.

## \|\| 2.96.28-32 \|\|

*vismṛtya saha jāmātrā vāṇijyāya yayau punaḥ \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*atha sādhuḥ samādāya ratnāni vividhāni ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*naukāḥ saṃsthāpya sa yayau deśāddeśāntaraṃ prati \|*  
*nagaraṃ narmadātīre tatra vāsaṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kurvankrayaṃ vikrayaṃ ca ciraṃ tasthau mahāmanāḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā na kṛtaṃ satyasevanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tataḥ karmavipākena tāpamāpācirādvaṇik \|*  
*kasmiṃściddivase rātrau rājño gehe tamovṛteḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*jñātvā nidrāgatānsarvānhṛtaṃ caurairmahādhanam \|*  
*prabhāte vācito rājā sūtamāgadhabaṃdibhiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

28-32. Suta said- Loading various types of gems in his boat, the Sadhu proceeded on voyage to different countries. Reaching over the bank of the river Narmada, he anchored the boat and stayed there. While indulging in the trade of sale and purchase, the noble vaisya, inspite of his stay there for long, by his action, thought and behaviour could not remember the adoration of Satyanarayana. Because of the negligence, he unfortunately had to suffer. Once during the night time in the darkness, the thieves finding all the royal guards to be fast asleep, stole enormous wealth.

## \|\| 2.96.33-40 \|\|

*prātaḥkṛtyaṃ nṛpaḥ kṛtvā sadaḥ saṃprāviśacca saḥ \|*  
*tatastatra samāyātaḥ kiṃkaro rājavallabhaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*uvāca sa tadā vākyaṃ śṛṇuṣva tvaṃ dharā pate \|*  
*muktāmālāśca bahudhā ratnāni vividhāni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*mumuṣuścaurā gatāssarve na jānīmo vayaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*iti vijñāpito rājā puṇyaśloka śikhāmaṇiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*uvāca krodhatāmrākṣo yūyaṃ saṃyāta mā ciram \|*  
*sacauraṃ dravyamādāya matpārśvaṃ tvamupānaya \|\| 36 \|\|*

*no ceddhaniṣye sagaṇāniti dūtānsamādiśat \|*  
*nṛpavākyaṃ samākarṇya prajagmuste ca kiṃkarāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bahuyatnairna saṃśodhya dravyaṃ corasamanvitam \|*  
*ekībhūtvā niśi tadā mahāciṃtāturo'bhavat \|\| 38 \|\|*

*hantā māṃ sagaṇaṃ rājā kiṃ karomi kutaḥ sukham \|*  
*nṛpadaṃḍācca me mṛtyuḥ pretatvāya bhavediha \|\| 39 \|\|*

*narmadāyāṃ ca maraṇaṃ śivalokapradāyakam \|*  
*ityevaṃ saṃmataṃ kṛtvā narmadāyāstaṭaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

33-40. When the vaisya king was woken up by the reciters and singers, he got free form the daily routine. When he entered his court, then the dear servants of the king arrived there and reported- “O lord of the earth, you kindly listen to my words. The thieves have fled away carrying the garlands of gems and beads. О king, we are unaware about the theft.” When the guards so reported to the king, the king who was the best of the noble and auspicious souls, became red in anger and said- “You should all move atonce and present the thieves before me with the stolen property, otherwise you will have to face the death.” Thus the king issued the command. On hearing the words of the king, the servants departed from that place. But inspite of their best efforts, they could find no trace of the thieves as well as the body. All the servants then assembled and became anxious and worried. They thought that “the king would kill them all. Then what should be done to achieve comfort? One of them thought that the punishment of death awarded to me, would make me a goblin. Therefore, I think it is more beneficial to end my life by drowning myself in the waters of the river Narmada.”

## \|\| 2.96.41 \|\|

*videśino'sya vaṇijo dadarśa vipulaṃ dhanam \|*  
*muktāhāraṃ gale tasya luṃṭhitaṃ vaṇijo'sya ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus thinking, he with his other companions, reached the bank of Narmada.

## \|\| 2.96.42-48 \|\|

*cauro'yamiti niścitya tau babaṃdhātmarakṣaṇāt \|*  
*sadhanaṃ saha jāmātrā nṛpāntikamupānayat \|\| 42 \|\|*

*pratikūle harau tasminrājñāpi na vicāritam \|*  
*dhanāgāre dhanaṃ nītvā badhnīta tau sudurmatī \|\| 43 \|\|*

*kārāgāre lohamayaiḥ śṛṃkhalairaṃgapādayoḥ \|*  
*iti rājājñayā dūtāstathā cakrurnibaṃdhanam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*jāmātrā sahitaḥ sādhurvilalāpa bhṛśaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*hā putra tāta tāteti jāmātaḥ kva dhanaṃ gatam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kva sthitā ca sutā bhāryā paśya dhāturviparyayam \|*  
*nimagnau duḥkhajaladhau ko vāṃ pāsyati saṃkaṭāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

*mayā bahutaraṃ dhāturvipriyaṃ hi purākṛtam \|*  
*tatkarmaṇaḥ prabhāvo'yaṃ na jāne kasya vā phalam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*samaṃ śvaśurajāmātrau dvādaśeṣu viṣādinau \|\| 48 \|\|*

42-48. There they found a foreigner vais'ya with enormous wealth, besides the garland of beautiful beads worn by him around his neck. For his own protection, thinking him to be a thief, he put him in bondage. They produced him before the king together with his son-in-law. Because of the adversity of the destiny, the king did not think over the matter deeply and storing the wealth in his treasure, he imprisoned both of them with chains and put them in jail. Thus, at the command of the king, both were bound with iron chains and imprisoned. Sadhu lamented again and again with his son-in-law. He said- “O son, where has my wealth gone? Where are my wife and daughters? Look at the adversity of the destiny, we are presently drowning in the ocean of misery. Who can save us from this calamity? In earlier times, I have antagonised the lord on several occasions. This is the evil result of the same.” Thus, both the father-in-law and the son-in-law suffered miserably for twelve days facing the miseries.

## Chapter 97

## \|\| 2.97.1-8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tāpatrayaharaṃ viṣṇoścaritaṃ tasya te śivam \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃti sudhiyo nityaṃ te vasaṃti hareḥ padam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pratikūle harau tasminyāsyanti nirayānbahūn \|*  
*tatpriyā kamalā devī catvārastasya cātmajāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dharmo yajño nṛpaścauraḥ sarve lakṣmīpriyaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*viprebhyaścātithibhyaśca yaddānaṃ dharma ucyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mātṛbhyo devatābhyaśca svadhā svāheti vai makhaḥ \|*  
*dharmasyaiva makhasyaiva rakṣako nṛpatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dvayorhantā hi coraḥ sa te sarve dharmakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*yatra satyaṃ tato dharmastatra lakṣmīḥ sthirā bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*satyahīnasya tatsādhordhanaṃ yattadgrahe sthitam \|*  
*hṛtavānavanīpālaḥ caurairbhāryātiduḥkhitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vāsolaṃkaraṇādīni vikrīya bubhuje kila \|*  
*nāsti tatpacyate kiṃcittadā kaṣṭamagāhata \|\| 7 \|\|*

*athaikasmindine kanyā bhojanācchādanaṃ vinā \|*  
*gatā vipragṛhe'paśyatsatyanārāyaṇārcanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Sata said- Listening to the life story of lord Visnu, one is relieved of all the three types of sufferings and the same is also beneficial for you. Such of the people with wisdom, who daily listen to the same, they finally achieve the abode of lord Narayana. At the gaining of the adversity of the lord, one achieves several types of hells. The goddess Kamala is the beloved of the lord. Besides Dharma, Yajna, the king and the thief are his four sons. These perform the favourite tasks of the goddess Laksmi. The charities which are given for the sake of Brahmanas and the guests are known as Dharma. The oblations of Svaha and Svadha given for the sake of the gods are known as Yajna. The one who protects dharma and yajna is known as the king and those who destroy them are known as the thieves. Therefore, all of them serve the Dharma. Wherever resides the truth, Laksmi always remains stable there. When one is deprived of the truth, the wealth of the Sadhu which was lying in the boat as well as in the house, was stolen by the thieves and his wife too was tortured, as a result of which she had to save her life by selling away her ornaments and the costumes. But after some time, when both the mother and daughter had no means of livelihood, both of them collected wood from the forest. Thereafter, the girl getting deprived of food and clothes, went to the house of a Brahmana, where the worship of Satyanarayana was going on.

## \|\| 2.97.9-14 \|\|

*prārthayaṃtaṃ jagannāthaṃ dṛṣṭvā sā prārthayaddharim \|*  
*satyanārāyaṇa hare pitā bhartā ca me gṛham \|\| 9 \|\|*

*āgacchatvarcayiṣyāmi bhavaṃtamiti vācaye \|*  
*tathāstu brāhmaṇairuktā tataḥ sā tvāśramaṃ yayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*mātrā nirbhartsiteyaṃtaṃ kālaṃ kutra sthitā śubhe \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa satyanārāyaṇārcane \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kalau pratyakṣa phaladaḥ sarvadā kriyate naraiḥ \|*  
*kartumicchāmyahaṃ mātaranujñātuṃ tvamarhasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*deśamāyātu janakaḥ svāmī ca mama kāmanā \|*  
*rātrau niścitya manasā prabhāte sā kalāvatī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śīlapālasya guptasya gehe prāptā dhanārthinī \|*  
*baṃdho kiṃciddhanaṃ dehi yena satyārcanaṃ bhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. Prayer was being offered there to the lord of the universe. Observing that, she also prayed to the lord- “In case my husband and father return home quite well, then I shall also perform puja for you. I am offering this prayer to you.” The Brahmanas of that place said to her- “It will be so done.” Thereafter, she returned home. But at home, her mother scolded her and said- “0 auspicious one, where had you been for so long?” Then she narrated the event of the recitation of Satyanarayana, which bestows the apparent reward. Therefore, О mother, with your permission, I too would like to perform the same. This is my only desire that both my father and my husband should return safe. With this resolve during the night, the girl named Kalavati went to Silapalagupta and begged for some money, saying- “O brother, give me a little of money for performing the worship of lord Satyanarayana.”

## \|\| 2.97.15-23 \|\|

*iti śrutvā śīlapālaḥ paṃcaniṣkaṃ dhanaṃ dadau \|*  
*tvatpituśca ṛṇaṃ śeṣaṃ mayītyeva kalāvati \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ityuktvā so'nṛṇo bhūtvā gayāśrāddhāya saṃyayau \|*  
*sutāpi tena dravyeṇa kṛtaṃ satyārcanaṃ śubham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*līlāvatī saha tayā bhaktyākārṣītprapūjanam \|*  
*pūjanena viśeṣeṇa tuṣṭo nārāyaṇo'bhavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

*narmadātīranagare nṛpaḥ suṣvāpa maṃdire \|*  
*rātriśeṣe suparyaṃke nidrāṃ kurvati rājani \|*  
*uvāca viprarūpeṇa bodhayañchlakṣṇayā girā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha rājendra tau sādhū parimocaya \|*  
*aparādhaṃ vinā baddhau no cecchaṃ na bhavettava \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ bhūpatiścaiva viprarūpeṇa bodhitaḥ \|*  
*tadā hyantardadhe viṣṇu rvinidro nṛpatistadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vismitaḥ sahasotthāya dadhyau brahma sanātanam \|*  
*sabhāyāṃ maṃtriṇe rājā svapnahetuṃ nyavedayat \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mahāmantrī ca bhūpālaṃ prāha satyena bho dvija \|*  
*mayāpi darśitaṃ svapnaṃ vṛddhavipreṇa bodhitam \|*  
*atastau hi samānīya saṃpṛccha vidhivannṛpa \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ānīya sādhuṃ papraccha satyamālaṃbya bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*kutratyau vāṃ kulaṃ kiṃ vā vasatiḥ kasya vā pure \|\| 23 \|\|*

15-23. On hearing this, Kilapala gave her five gold coins and said- “O Kalavati, I was indebted to your father, for this much of money.” Thus speaking, getting free from the loan, he left for performing sraddha at Gaya. On the other hand, the girl performed the auspicious puja of lord Satyanaryana with her mother. Lord Narayana was immensely delighted with that adoration. The king was sleeping in a temple over the bank of the river Narmada. When only a little part of the night was left and the king was sleeping over his bed, Lord Visnu reached there in the form of a brahmana and said to him- “Get up, О king, free both the ascetics atonce, otherwise you would never meet with welfare.” At these words spoken by the lord in the form of a Brahmana, the king woke up. At the same time, lord Narayana disappeared. The king then expressing the surprise, reached the assembly of the eternal Brahmanas and spoke about the dream to his courtiers. All the people as well as the courtiers said to the king- “This is true. I have also witnessed the same type of a dream, which has been revealed through the Brahmana. The king then summoned both the vaidyas and respectfully asked them- “Where do you live? In which race were you born? In which city do you live?”

## \|\| 2.97.24-28 \|\|

*sādhuruvāca \|*  
*ramye ratnapure vāso vaṇigjātau janirmama \|*  
*vāṇijyārthaṃ mahārāja vāṇijyaṃ jīvikāvayoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*maṇimuktādi vikretuṃ kretuṃ vā tava pattane \|*  
*prāptau dūtaiśca baddhvāvāṃ tvatsamīpamupāgatau \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pratikūle vidhau ko vā daśāṃ nāpnoti vai pumān \|*  
*vināparādhaṃ rājendra maṇicaurānavādayan \|\| 26 \|\|*

*āvāṃ na cauro rājeṃdra tattvatastvaṃ vicāraya \|*  
*śrutvā tanniścayaṃ jñātvā tayorbaṃdhanakāraṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*chedayitvā dṛḍhaṃ pāśaṃ lomaśātimakārayat \|*  
*kārayitvā pariṣkāraṃ bhojayāmāsa tau nṛpaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

24-28. Sadhu said- I live in the pleasant city of Ratnapura. I was born in the family of a vaidya. Trade is our livelihood. We are engaged in the trade of gems and beads and lived in your city. Your servants arrived there, bound us with chains and produced us before you. During the adverse moves of the destiny, what ugly situation is beyond the reach a person? Because of this, without committing any sin, lord Krsna was declared as the thief of the gem. О Rajendra, you can think quite deeply. Both of us are not thieves. Learning about the cause of their bondage and taking their words to be true, the handcuffs as well as the fetters of both of them were removed. Then their (ugly hair) were removed and they were made to take bath and were served with food.

## \|\| 2.97.29-33 \|\|

*nagare pūjayāmāsa vastrābhūṣaṇavāhanaiḥ \|*  
*abravītpūjitaḥ sādhurbhūpatiṃ vinayānvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kārāgāre bahuvidhaṃ prāptaṃ duḥkhamataḥ param \|*  
*ājñāpaya mahārāja deśaṃ gaṃtuṃ kṛpānidhe \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śrutvā sādhuvaco rājā prāha kośādhikāriṇam \|*  
*mudrābhistaraṇīḥ sadyaḥ pūrayāśu madājñayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*jāmātrā sahitaḥ sādhurgītavāditramaṃgalaiḥ \|*  
*svadeśaṃ calito'dyāpi na cakre harisevanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*satyanārāyaṇo devaḥ pratyakṣaphaladaḥ kalau \|*  
*sa eva tāpaso bhūtvā cakre sādhuviḍaṃbanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

29-33. Thereafter, the king provided them with the costumes and ornaments in his own city, besides the vehicles and they were adored as well. Thereafter, Sadhu meekly said to the king- “O lord, we had to suffer immensely in the prison. But presently, I have been placed in another condition. Therefore, О ocean of mercy, with your permission, I would like to return to my country.” On hearing the words of Sadhu, the king said to his treasurer- “At my command, his boat should be filled with the gold coins.” Thereafter, the Vaisya Sadhu together with his son-in-law, departed for his country. But inspite of this, he did not worship the lord. In the age of Kali, Satyanarayanadeva bestows instantaneous reward. Therefore, taking to the form of an ascetic, the lord started behaving like a Sadhu.

## \|\| 2.97.34-39 \|\|

*tāpasa uvāca \|*  
*dharmaḥ kiṃ nauṣu te sādho māmanādṛtya yāsi bhoḥ \|*  
*pratyuttaramadātsādhuḥ kṣipa naukāśca satvaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

*bhoḥ svāminme dhanaṃ nāsti latāpatrādipūritam \|*  
*naubhirgacchāmi svasthānaṃ virodhe nātra kiṃ phalam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ityuktastāpasaḥ prāha tathāstviti vacaḥ kṣaṇāt \|*  
*dhanamaṃtardadhe sādhorlatāpatrāvaśeṣitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dhanaṃ naukāsu nāstīti sādhuściṃtāturo'bhavat \|*  
*kimidaṃ kasya vā hetordhanaṃ kutra gataṃ mama \|\| 37 \|\|*

*vajrapātāhata iva bhṛśaṃ duḥkhitamānasaḥ \|*  
*kva yāsyāmi kva tiṣṭhāmi kiṃ karomi dhanaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*iti mūrchāgataḥ sādhurvilalāpa punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*jāmātrā bodhitaḥ paścāttāpasaṃ taṃ jagāma ha \|\| 39 \|\|*

34-39. The ascetic said- “What has been loaded in your boat, that you are moving disregarding me. Is it the dharma.” In reply to it, Sadhu said- “You kindly release the boat, О great master, there is no wealth in my boat. It has been filled with the leaves and the creepers. I am returning to my home, by means of this boat. What is the use of causing obstruction to the same.” At this, the ascetic said- “Let your words be true at the moment, atonce. Suddenly, the wealth and riches of the vaisya named Sadhu disappeared and the boat was left with leaves and creepers. Then Sadhu was totally upset with the disappearing of the wealth from his boat. Then he thought- “What has happened? What is the cause of it? Where has my wealth gone?” He felt painful as if hit by the fall of vajra. He was at a loss to know as to what was to be done and what should he do? What has happened to my wealth?

## \|\| 2.97.40-41 \|\|

*gale vasanamādāya praṇanāma sa tāpasam \|*  
*ko bhavāniti papraccha devo gaṃdharva īśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*devadevo'thavā ko'pi na jāne tava vikramam \|*  
*ājñāpaya mahābhāga tadviḍambanakāraṇam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Thus getting fainted, the vaisya started lamenting again and again. Soon thereafter, the son-in-law of the vaisya advised him to go to the Tapasa. The vaisya then, putting a scarf around his neck, went to the ascetic and asked him- “Who are you? Are you a god, a Gandharva or Isvara or the god of gods? I am unable to know about your prowess. O excellent one, you kindly tell me the cause of your conducting like this.”

## \|\| 2.97.42-47 \|\|

*tāpasa uvāca \|*  
*ātmā caivātmanaḥ śatrustathātra ca priyo'priyaḥ \|*  
*tyaja mauḍhyamati sādho pravādaṃ mā vṛthā kṛthāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*iti vijñāpitaḥ sādhurna bubodha mahādhanaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ sa tāpasaḥ prāha kṛpayā pūrvakarmataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*caṃdracūḍo yadānarca satyanārāyaṇaṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*anapatyena suciraṃ putrakanyārthinā tvayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*prārthitaṃ na smṛtaṃ hyeva idānīṃ tapyase vṛthā \|*  
*satyanārāyaṇo devo viśvavyāpī phalapradaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tamanādṛtya durbuddhe kutaḥ samyagbhavettava \|*  
*purālabdhavaraṃ smṛtvā sasmāra jagadīśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*satyanārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ tāpasaṃ taṃ dadarśa ha \|*  
*praṇamya bhuvi kāyena parikramya punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva tāpasaṃ tatra sādhurgadgadayā girā \|\| 47 \|\|*

42-47. The ascetic said- Actually, soul of a self (lady) is the enemy of the soul, the same is friendly as well as inimical to a person. Therefore, it is no use indulging in a tall talk. Shed away the foolishness owned by you.” At these words of the Tapasa, the wealthy trader could not realize the factual position. But still, keeping in view his earlier noble deeds, exercising his compassion on the vaisya, the Tapasa said- “When the king Candracuda was performing the worship of Satyanarayana, you being childless had also begged for progeny. But you did not remember it subsequently. Have you not forgotten it? Then why are you suffering now? О evil-minded one, Satyanarayana is omnipresent one and he alone bestows the reward. How can you be happy by disregarding him?” Soon, thereafter, the vaisya was reminded of the earlier boon and got devoted to the lord of the universe. Suddenly, he visualized the ascetic as Satyanarayana. He then prostate on earth again and again and with his choked voice, he tried to please the ascetic.

## \|\| 2.97.48-51 \|\|

*sādhuruvāca \|*  
*satyarūpaṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ satyanārāyaṇaṃ harim \|*  
*yatsatyatvena jagatastaṃ satyaṃ tvāṃ namāmyaham \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tvanmāyāmohitātmāno na paśyaṃtyātmanaḥ śubham \|*  
*duḥkhāṃbhodhau sadā magnā duḥkhe ca sukhamāninaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*mūḍhohaṃ dhanagarveṇa madāṃdhīkṛtalocanaḥ \|*  
*na jāne svātmanaḥ kṣemaṃ kathaṃ paśyāmi mūḍhadhīḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kṣamasva mama daurātmyaṃ tapo dhāmne hare namaḥ \|*  
*ājñāpayātmadāsyaṃ me yena te caraṇau smare \|\| 51 \|\|*

48-51. Sadhu said- Salutation to lord Satyanarayana, who is the form of truth, has the truthful speech, besides being present in the world in the form of truth. Having been influenced with your illusion, a human is unable to visualize his own soul and having been overpowered with your illusion, he forgets about his own welfare. Suffering in the ocean of miseries, he thinks himself to be quite comfortable. I am indeed a fool. Both my eyes have been blinded due to the pride of my riches. Therefore, I am unaware of my own welfare. But how could I do so, being devoid of wisdom? Therefore, О Hari, you kindly forgive me for my foolishness. Salutation to you being the ocean of tapas. You kindly grace me to be your slave, so as to enable me to remember you always.

52-56. Then offering prayer to him in this way, he placed a lakh of gold coins before the ascetic and said- “I shall worship lord Satyanarayana after I reach my home.” At this, Narayana feeling pleased with him, said- “Let all your desires be fulfilled. Living with your sons and grandsons, you enjoy all the pleasures.” Thus speaking, Lord Visnu disappeared from the scene. The vaisya also went to his city. Having been protected by Satyadeva, the vaisya. reached his home after seven days. When he was approaching his own city, he sent his servant in advance to his house, who on reaching his home said to Lilavati - “Sadhu has arrived with his son-inlaw, getting successful. At that point of time, she was engaged in the worship of Satyanarayana with her daughter.

57-62. She entrusted die burden of рuja on her daughter and herself went towards the boat. Kalavati too, who was accompanied with other damsels and was performing the welfare ceremony, hurriedly ended the same and reached the boat. At that point of time in the evening, she intended to see the lotus like face of her husband like a female partridge bird. But because of the disregard of the prasada, boat of Sankhapati with his son-in-law disappeared at the same time. Finding his own son-in-law so submerging in water, the vaisya fainted and started lamenting. Lilavati also got fainted and started lamenting, observing whom Kalavati also fainted and fell down on earth. She started lamenting on regaining consciousness. She started shaking as the banana leaf shakes with the blowing of the wind. She started uttering her master’s name as the beloved of Dharma and the ocean of compassion. The destiny has separated my husband from me all time to come. Half of the body of the husband has already disappeared and the half of it has remained alive.

63-70. Suta then said- Kalavati, who possesses all the arts, whose feet were red like the coral and were soft like the lotus flowers, with tears flowing from her vast eyes which fell over her breasts like the garlands of beads, said- “O Satyanarayana, О ocean of truth, you kindly redeem me from the separation of my husband. I am drowning in the ocean of grief.” On hearing the pathetic words, the lord declared from the sky in an invisible voice- “Kalavati should atonce consume my prasada, which would restore her husband to life. Therefore, don’t grieve. On hearing the divine voice, getting surprised she did so and by the grace of Narayana, Kalavati could meet her husband. At the same time and place, getting immensely pleased, Sadhu adored lord NarAyana offering a lakh of precious coins. Because of the glory of the said vrata, having been filled with delight, getting sons and the grandsons, he then enjoying utmost delight on earth, attained the heaven after death. A person, who would listen to this story with utmost devotion, he would surely attain the heaven. A person who listens to this episode with devotion, he becomes favourite of lord Visnu and all his desires would be fulfilled. Because of this, this excellent vrata of Visnu, which has been emerged out of the face of Brahmana, has been narrated to you.

*viśveśvarīṃ jaganmūrtiṃ saccidānaṃdarūpiṇīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

4-9. Suta said- There was a Brahmana in the age of Kali, who was known by the name of Pitrsarma. He was well-versed in the tattvas of all the Vedas and the related literature. He was always afraid of the abode of Yama. Realizing about the horrible age of Kali which was caused by adharma and the bondage for driving to the abode of Yama, he felt immensely worried. He thought, “which one of the asrama or the caste could be helpful for my achieving welfare? This is because in the age of Kali, the path of a recluse mendicant is deceitful and has been polluted by the cheatings etc. Besides, there is no vanaprastha asrama in the age of Kali. The practice of Brahmacarya is in vogue, only rarely. But the institution of a house-holder has been considered to be the best of all the asramas. Therefore, in this horrible age of Kali, one should search for a wife. In case I could achieve a wife quite suitable to my temperament, then my life could be quite purposeful. Besides I can also achieve welfare.” With this resolve, he started worshipping the goddess Parvati, who is the mother of the universe, bestower of merits, having universal form, blissful and well known in the world. He started worshipping her offering sandalpaste as well as the mental prayer with devotion in order to please her.

*namorajastamomūrtyai durgāyai ca namonamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā stavaṃ devyā prasādaḥ sthāpitastayā \|*

10-17. Pitrsarma prayed thus- “Salutation to the goddess who is herself the form of the universe as well as an absolute one. Salutation to the one who is the form of three gunas, besides being Turiya (or the Divine Being). You are the one who produces the Mahat-tattva (soul or intellect), salutation to you. You are the creator of the pleasure and pain, besides being the mother of Brahman. You are the grandmother, besides being the pride. Salutation to you. О mother, salutation to your formless as well as the spotless form. О mother, you are the form of the three gunas like the sattva, rajas and tamas. Salutation to vidya, pure sattva and the grandmother. О mother, repeated salutation to ignorance or its purified form. О mother Kali, salutation to you again and again possessing sattva and tamogunas. Salutation to you possessing the purified raja and the one who pervades in the entire world. Repeated salutation to rajas and Durga - the form of tamas as well.” Listening to this type of prayer, the goddess showered her compassion on the Brahmana. In due course of time, the daughter of a Brahmana known by the name Visnuyasasvi was married to him. The Brahmana gave the name of Brahmacarini to his wife and started living in Mathura. He started performing dharma with her. After the period’s bath, the Brahmana started bestowing Rtudana to her. As a result of this, they got four sons.

18-33. All the four of them were well-versed in all the four Vedas. Out of those four sons, a son named Vyadi was born to Rgveda, who was well-versed in the field of justice. The boy known by the name of Yajurvedi got a son named Mimamsa. The son of Samavedi was well-versed in the grammar, while Atharvavedi had a son named Vararuci, who was the best and favourite of the royals. All of them reached the court of the king of Magadha. The king welcomed them with great honour and asked them- “Which Brahmacarya is the best one?” Vyadi said- “A person who always remains ready for offering prayer to the gods as per the provision of the scriptures, his Brahmacarya is the best.” Mimamsa said- O king, a person who in the yajna, following the provisions of the karmakanda offers the sandalpaste and gorocana performing homa and oblation for pleasing the Devas, then a person who accepts his prasada he is the best of Brahmacarls.” On hearing this, Panini said- “O king Candragupta, a person who with all the three svaras (tunes) besides the reciting of the sutras in combination with linga, dhatu and ganas perform the yajna of the supreme Brahman, he happens to be the true Brahmacarl and achieves the supreme Brahman.” On hearing this, Vararuci said- “O lord of Magadha, after performing the thread ceremony, a person who while staying in the abode of the preceptor, keeping danda, hair on the body besides the nails, lives on begging while engaged in the study of the Vedas and also obeys the command of his preceptor, he happens to be a Brahmacari in reality.” After listening to the talk of all of them, Pitrsarma said- “A Brahmana, who while living the life of a house-holder, remains engaged in the service of manes, the gods as well as the guests or the beggars and enjoys the union with his wife after the bath of the period, such a person is the true Brahmacar I.” On hearing this, the king said- “O Master, during the terrific age of Kali, your words appear to be the best and deeply religious. Because you arc immensely glorious, besides being well-versed in dharma. I also believe similarly.” Thus speaking, the king who always respected the words of the preceptor, accepted Pitrsarma as his preceptor. He reached the heaven after his demise. Thereafter, mentally adoring lord Damodara. Pitrsarma also reached the Himalaya mountain and entered into the samadhi like the yogins.

2-6. Suta said The son of Samana was known as Panini, who had been defeated by the grand disciple of Kanabhuk Thereafter, feeling disgraced, Panini atonce proceeded onto pilgrimage. Having taken bath and performing oblation at all the places of pilgrimage, he reached the holy place of Kedaranatha. Seeing some light there, he started meditating on Siva. He lived on dry leaves for a week, consumed water alone for ten days and for another ten days, he inhaled the air alone. On the twenty-eighth day, lord Rudra said to him-“You ask for a boon.” Listening to the nectar like voice, he offered prayer to lord Sarvesa, who is the lord of all the lingas besides being the beloved of Girija, offered prayer to him in choked voice.

You kindly bestow all the best of holy places to me. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.99.10-15 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*

10-15. Suta said- On hearing this, lord Mahadva getting pleased, bestowed the sutras to him, which are considered auspicious for all the letters in the form of ... or cakra. In the Manasatirtha, the river of knowledge filled with the water of truth, being free from the blemish of attraction as well as envy and the person who has a dip in such an auspicious water, he achieves the merit of visiting all the holy places. He said- “Panini - the Brahmana, this is the great holy place known by the name of Manasa. This place provides a face to face audience with Brahman, which has been bestowed by me to you. You would become successful by getting the same.” Thus speaking, lord Siva disappeared from that place, while Panini returned to his abode. Then he created Sutrapatha, Dhatupatha, Ganapatha as well as the Lingasutras. Thereafter, he achieved beatitude. Therefore, O best of the Bhargavas, you also serve the Manasatirtha. It is because the auspicious Ganga who bestows all the wolfare and represents all the holy places, had been born of the same. There is no holy place on earth better than Ganga, nor would it ever be on earth in future.

## Chapter 100. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

He went to Vrndavana, which was served by the cowherds and the milkmaids. Reaching there, he started worship of lord Janardana - the leader of the Devas..

Because of the same knowledge, the proficiency of the story of 6rfmad Bhagavata dawned on him, which had been narrated by Sukadeva to the great devotees of Visnu. The narration which is the form of liberation, was recited by him and at the end of which lord Visnu himself appeared on the scene. Thereafter, lord Janardana said-“O intelligent one, you better ask for a boon.”

In the age of Kali, the people who are fearful of the hell, get themselves redeemed with the reciting of your name. The holy book of Srimad Bhagavata which was composed by the sage Vyasa, the same has been entrusted to me by you. In case you have granted a boon to me, then you kindly enlighten me about its glory as well.

8-16. The lord said- Once lord Siva, together with Bhavani, arrived in the city of Kasi at the time when the entire world was overpowered with deceitfulness and cheating and was suffering from the Buddhist rule. Reaching there, he delightfully worshipped the lump of earth. “O fortunate one, you are blissful form of the supreme soul, salutation to you” Listening to him, Parvati asked, who is your chief lord?” He replied- “Mahadeva, a weekly yajna was performed here, therefore, О brightfaced one, this land has become extremely auspicious.” On hearing this, purifying the land, Parvati made that place as their abode. 0 twice bom one, the god of gods, deputed Candisa, Ganesa, Nandi and Skanda for the protection of the place and said- “O goddess, you listen to my pleasant story, which is present here like me.” Thus speaking, he started describing it carefully. On the eighth day, opening his eyes, lord Siva found Parvati fast asleep. He woke her up and said- “For how long have you heard the story?”

17-22. In the hollow of the tree, the parrot chick was listening to the story, which earned him long life. The parrot-chick was being protected by the goddess Parvati herself, who was also meditating on me while living in a Siva temple. At my command, the same parrot is presently lodged in your heart. The glory of Srimad Bhagavata has also been achieved by you from the same parrot. Gandharvasena - the father of the king Vikramaditya, is presently lodged over the bank of the river Narmada. Let him hear also this auspicious story. The giving away of the story of the lord is said to be the best of all. It should be lodged with the fully competent people, who should be devoted to lord Visnu. This charity cannot be compared with the one earned by a person by giving food to a hungry person. After thus speaking, Vopadeva also felt delighted.

But because of the number of the Vedas being four, the recitation of all of them would be impossible. Therefore, I would like to listen to the particular eulogy or stotra by reciting which, one would earn the merit of the Vedas. О proficient one, you please tell me about the stotra which removes the sins.

3-12. Suta said- During the reign of the king Vikramaditya, there lived a Brahmana who lived on hunting. He was actually bom from a Brahmana woman by a hunter. There was a Tripath! Brahmana whose wife was known by the name of Kamini. She was always filled with passion and always had a lust for a union with men. Because of this nature, her eyes were always filled with passion. Once the Tripathi Brahmana went to some other village for the reciting of Durga-Saptasati, where there was the majority of Vaisyas as well as Devalakas. There he lived for a month and could not return home earlier. During the intervening period, the wicked wife of the Brahmana, getting intoxicated with her youthful age, called for the hunter who earned his living by the sale of wood collected from the forest. She paid him five gold coins and enjoyed union with him to her satisfaction. Because of her union with Vyadha, she conceived and in the tenth month, she gave birth to a son. His father performed the name giving ceremony for him. After attaining the age of twelve years, the wicked son could not take to learnings, but always engaged himself in hunting and killing. Because of that, he was given the name of Vyadhakarma. Tripath! ultimately drove out both the mother and the son from his house. Thereafter, observing Brahmacarya, Tripath! started performing recitation of the text of the goddess Candi at Vindhya mountain and as a result of it, he soon became a liberated soul. On the other hand, the mother and the boy, having been driven out of the house of Tripath!, started living with the hunter quite delightfully and while living there, the woman earned enormous amount by evil ways.

*śiṣyatvamagamattatrākṣaramaiśaṃ jajāpa ha \|*  
*bījamaṃtraprabhāveṇa tadaṃgātpāpamulbaṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*niḥsṛtaṃ kṛmirūpeṇa bahuvarṇena tāpitam \|*

*paṭhitvākṣaramālāṃ ca jajāpādicaritrakam \|*  
*dvādaśābdamite kāle kāśyāṃ gatvā sa tu dvijaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*annapūrṇāṃ mahādevīṃ tuṣṭāva parayā mudā \|*  
*rocanādyaiśca saṃpūjyāṃ munidevaniṣevitām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*nityānaṃdakarī parābhayakarī sauṃdaryaratnākarī nirdhūtākhilapāpapāvanakarī kāśīpurādhīśvarī \|*  
*nānālokakarī mahābhayaharī viśvaṃbharī sundarī vidyāṃ dehi kṛpāvalaṃbanakarī mātānnapūrṇeśvarī \|\| 21 \|\|*

13-21. The Vyadhakarma boy became favourite of his parents because of his earning by thefts and violence. Once the wicked boy entered the temple of the goddess, where he stole and usurped the ornaments of the ladies there. Some of the people detected the evil ways of the boy. He also started listening to the noble discourse in the temple by the learned Brahmanas. Because of the listening to the auspicious words of the Brahmanas, a gradual change took place in the conduct of the boy and he became religious-minded. One day, he handed over his wealth to the Brahmana who recited the scripture and received diksa or initiation of Siva-mantra from him, which he started reciting. Because of the effect of the recitation of the mantra, all his burning sins started falling from his body, which started suffering because of the reciting of the mantra. After three years, he was freed from all the sins and became an excellent Brahmana. Then while reciting aksara-mala, he also started reciting the Adi-carita. Thereafter, in the twelfth year, he reached the city of KasT and started adoring the goddess Annapurna there, who was regularly served by the sages as well as the gods. He prayed to the goddess- “O mother Annapurna, bestow knowledge on me. You are always blissful and make others fearless, besides being the treasure of beauty. You are the presiding deity of the city of Kasi. You purify the people, removing all their sins. You create many Iokas, remove the great dangers, besides maintaining the entire universe. You are the prime beauty and bestow compassionate shelter.”

## \|\| 2.101.22-25 \|\|

*sa ityaṣṭottaraṃ japtvā dhyānastimitalocanaḥ \|*

*dattvā tasmai hi ṛgvidyāṃ punaraṃtaradhīyata \|*

*brahmībhūya yathā vipro lebhe siddhimanuttamām \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. Thus reciting the mantra a hundred and eight times and meditating on her, he went to sleep at the same place closing his eyes. The goddess appeared in his dream. She bestowed the knowledge of Rgveda on him and then disappeared. When the learned Brahmana woke up, he had already achieved the Brahmavidya. In due course of time, he became the chief priest of the yajna of the king Vikramaditya. After the conclusion of the yajna, he retired to Himalaya for practicing yoga. O dear one, thus I have narrated to you the auspicious story of the Brahmana, in which the Brahmana boy achieved the supreme success as well as Brahmanhood

*sūta uvāca \|*

1-3. Suta said - O dear one, there once ruled in Ujjayini a king named Bhimavarma, who indulging in all types of violence used to eat meat and drink wine. In order to ill feed his hunger, the wicked king killed even the cocks, pigs and the boars in the forest and ate them. The sinful king also enjoyed the company of prostitutes. Leaving the human flesh, the demon like king used to take all types of meat. In his youth, he met with his end due to the disease of cholera.

## \|\| 2.102.4-12 \|\|

*kāritaścaṃḍikāpāṭhastena duṣṭena bhīruṇā \|*

*tasmai nṛpāya sa munirdattvā madhyacaritrakam \|*

*puṇyakṣetratvamagamanmahāmāyāprasādataḥ \|*

*dvādaśābdāṃtare prāptastadguruḥ śaktitatparaḥ \|*

*tadā prādurabhūddevī jagadaṃbā sanātanī \|*

*mahānandī mahābhāgo bhuktvā bhogaṃ surepsitam \|*  
*ante jagāma paramaṃ lokaṃ devanamaskṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

4-12. He once arranged for the recitation of the Candi-patha and as a result of the merit so earned by him, he was reborn in Magadha in a Ksatriya family. He was known as Mahanandi. Politics was his favourite subject. Because of retaining his earlier memory, he followed the Vedic dharma, he turned as a Mahasakta and became disciple of the sage Katyayana. The great sage bestowed on the king the middle carita of Saptasati together with the seed. Thereafter, reaching the Vindhya mountain, Katyayana started the worship of Sakti. The king also worshipped the eternal goddess offering sandal paste and other material, reciting the Madhyacarita of Durga. Because of the grace of Mahamaya, he achieved the merit of becoming a (highly placed) Ksatriya. Discarding the feeling of his being a Sudra, he worshipped the goddess Sakti for a period of twelve years. Thereafter, his preceptor again returned to him. Then the king, in the company of his preceptor, performed the anusthana of lakh of Candi recitation. At that point of time, getting pleased, the eternal mother of the earth bestowed on the king dharma, artha, kama and moksa. Thus the king known as Mahanandi enjoyed all the comforts like the gods and ultimately, proceeded on to the abode of gods (heaven).

## \|\| 2.102.13-14 \|\|

*iti te kathitā vipra yatproktaṃ yajuṣo gatiḥ \|*

*ityevaṃ varṇitaṃ vipra māhātmyaṃ munivarṇitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. O Brahmana, I have narrated the story of the person performing the puja. By worshipping the goddess by means of Madhyamacarita, the Sudra king achieved the highest position. I am now concluding here the glory of the goddess as narrated by the sages.

## \|\| 2.103.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*

*tatrāvasanmahāprājña upādhyāyaḥ patañjaliḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said- Over the Citrakuta mountain in which are enshrined various types of metals, there lived a teacher who was immensely learned and well-versed in the Vedas and the related literature besides Bhagavadgita. He was a devotee of lord Visnu as well, besides being truthful, having achieved proficiency in commentaries. Once while roaming on pilgrimage, the auspicious soul reached the city of Kasi and started debate with the sage Кatуaуаnа. Getting defeated from the devotee of the goddess, then Patanjali getting ashamed, started worship of the goddess Sarasvati.

5-9. Patanjali said- Salutation to the goddess, salutation to Mahamurti as well as Sarvamurti again and again. Salutation to Siva (the form of welfare), bestower of all the welfare and Visnumaya. You are Sraddha (faith), Buddhi (intelligence), Medha (wisdom), Vidya (knowledge), Katyayanarupa (form of welfare), Santi (peace), as well as speech. Therefore, О Narayani! Salutation to you again and again. When the Brahmana thus adored the goddess, a divine voice from the sky was heard, which declared- “O Brahmana, you recite my excellent glory with a concentrated mind and with the influence of the same, you will achieve the true knowledge. The Rajas-jnana of Katyayana was also received by him in the same manner. He defeated Patanjali because of his devotion towards me.” On hearing the words of the goddess, he went to the temple of Vindhyavasini - the goddess, performed puja and then pleased her with the recitation of the stotra.

## \|\| 2.103.10-16 \|\|

*jñānaṃ prasādajaṃ vipraḥ prāpya viṣṇuparāyaṇam \|*  
*kātyāyanaṃ parājitya parāṃ mudamavāpa ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ūrddhvapuṃḍraṃ ca tilakaṃ tulasīkaṇṭhamālikām \|*  
*kṛṣṇamantraṃ ca śivadaṃ sthāpayitvā gṛhegṛhe \|\| 11 \|\|*

*janejane tathā kṛtvā mahābhāṣya mudairayat \|*  
*ciraṃjīvitvamagamadviṣṇumāyāprasādataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*iti te kathito vipra jāpyānāmuttamo japaḥ \|*  
*kimanyacchrotumicchaṃti śaunakādyā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sarve bhadrāṇi paśyaṃtu mā kaścidduḥkhabhāgbhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*maṃgalaṃ bhagavānviṣṇurmaṃgalaṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*maṃgalaṃ puṃḍarīkākṣo maṃgalā yatano hariḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śuciryo hi naro nityamitihāsasamuccayam \|*  
*śṛṇuyāddharmakāmārthī sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 16 \|\|*

10-16. For the pleasure of the goddess, the Brahmana achieved the excellent knowledge of Visnuparayana. Thereafter, he propagated the importance of urdhva-pundrika, tilakam, wearing a rosary of holy basil round the neck and the reciting of Krsna-mantra, which bestows welfare. Subsequently, he composed Mahabhasya. By the grace of Visnumaya, he attained a long life. О Brahmana, I have thus described the details about the excellent japam. О Saunaka and other Rsis, what else do you want to listen from me? Let all the people enjoy bliss, no one should suffer. Lord Visnu, his Garudadhvaja, Pundarikaksa and Hari forms bestow welfare. A person, who purifying his self, shall listen to this historical treatise, he would surely achieve dharma, artha and kama besides the final beatitude.

## Pratisargaparva Part 3

## Chapter 104. Story of Vikramaditya

## \|\| 2.104.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣayaḥ ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavanvikramākhyānakālo'yaṃ bhavatoditaḥ \|*  
*śatadvādaśamaryādo dvāparasya samo bhuvi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*asminkāle mahābhāga līlā bhagavatā kṛtā \|*  
*tāmetāṃ kathayāsmānvai sarvajño'sti bhavānsadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The Rsis said- О lord, you have narrated the contemporary story of the king Vikramaditya. When twelve hundred years of dvapara were left, lord Krsna displayed his sports over the earth. You are omniscient always. You kindly repeat the same story.

## \|\| 2.104.3-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam \|*

*bhaviṣyākhye mahākalpe prāpte vaivasvatentare \|*

*pāṃḍavairnirjitāḥ sarve kauravāḥ yuddhadurmadāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭādaśe ca divase pāṃḍavānāṃ jayo'bhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dinānte bhaga vānkṛṣṇo jñātvā kālasya durgatim \|*  
*śivaṃ tuṣṭāva manasā yogarūpaṃ sanātanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. Suta said- During the Mahakalpa of Bhisma and at the time of the twenty-eighth dvapara, a terrific war was fought in the land of Kuruksetra. During the war, the proudy arrogant Kauravas were defeated by the Pandavas. The Pandavas gained victory on the eighteenth day. At the end of the day, taking it to be the move of the destiny, Lord Кrsna mentally adored lord Siva - the eternal yogi.

## \|\| 2.104.7-20 \|\|

*kṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*namaḥ śāṃtāya rudrāya bhūte śāya kapardine \|*  
*kālakartre jagadbhartre pāpahartre namonamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pāṃḍavānrakṣa bhagavanmadbhaktānbhūtabhīrukān \|*  
*iti śrutvā stavaṃ rudro naṃdiyānoparisthitaḥ \|*  
*rakṣārthaṃ śibirāṇāṃ ca prāptavāñchūlahastadhṛk \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tadā nṛpājñayā kṛṣṇaḥ sa gato gajasāhvayam \|*  
*pāṃḍavāḥ paṃca nirgatya sarasvatyā staṭe'vasan \|\| 9 \|\|*

*niśīthe drauṇibhojau ca kṛpastatra samāyayuḥ \|*

*aśvatthāmā tu balavāñchivadattamasiṃ tadā \|*  
*gṛhītvā sa jaghānāśu dhṛṣṭadyumnapuraḥsarān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*hatvā yatheṣṭamagamaddrauṇistābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pārṣatasyaiva sūtaśca hataśeṣo bhayāturaḥ \|*  
*pāṃḍavānvarṇayāmāsa yathā jāto janakṣayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*āgaskṛtaṃ śivaṃ jñātvā bhīmādyāḥ krodhamūrcchitāḥ \|*

*astraśastrāṇi teṣāṃ tu śivadehe samāviśan \|*

*punarjanma kalau prāpya bhokṣyate cāparādhakam \|*  
*ityuktvāntardadhe devaḥ pāṃḍavā duḥkhitāstadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*hariṃ śaraṇamājagmuraparādhanivṛttaye \|*  
*tadā kṛṣṇayutāḥ sarve pāṃḍavāḥ śastravarjitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tuṣṭuvurmanasā rudraṃ tadā prādurabhūcchivaḥ \|*

*śastrāṇyastrāṇi yānyeva tvadaṃge kṣapitāni vai \|*  
*pāṃḍavebhyaśca dehi tvaṃ śāpasyānugrahaṃ kuru \|\| 20 \|\|*

7-20. Sri Krsna said- О peaceful Rudra, Bhutesa, wearing the matted locks of hair, salutation to you. You are the creator of the time. You feed the universe, besides being the remover of the sins. О lord, you save the Pandavas. The Pandavas are my devotees and are fearful of the past.” On hearing the prayer, mounted over Nandi and holding a trident, lord Rudra arrived for their protection in the military camp. At that point of time, at the king’s command, Krsna proceeded to Hastinaprua. The Pandavas then made their dwelling place at the bank of the river Sarasvati. At the dead of night, Asvatthama - the son of Dronacarya, Bhoja and Krpacarya reached there. All of them eulogized lord Rudra mentally. Lord Siva, therefore, showed them the way. Holding the sword provided by lord Siva, the valorous Asvatthama killed Dhrstadyumna and others. Thereafter, he left to some other place. Then Suta, who escaped death out of all the servants, apprised the Pandavas of the terrible human massacre, as had happened earlier. Taking Siva to be a culprit at that time, Bhima and other Pandavas getting immensely enraged, wounded lord Siva with their weapons. Their weapons entered the body of lord Siva and were absorbed in the same, which surprised the Pandavas. Thereafter, they attacked Siva with their hands, fists and slaps. At that point of time, lord Siva pronounced a curse on them-“You people are the devotees of lord Krsna, therefore inspite of your having been protected by me, you would face death. You would be reborn in the age of Kali and you shall have to face the reward of your deeds.” Thus speaking, Siva disappeared from the scene. The Pandavas on the other hand took refuge with lord, for the atonement of their sins. Having been deprived of the weapons, the Pandavas with Krsna eulogized mentally and pleased him. Siva then appeared before them and said-“You better ask for a boon.” Hearing this, Sri Krsna said- “Let the weapons which have entered your body be returned and remove the curse pronounced by you on the Pandavas.”

21-30. On hearing this, Siva said- “O Krsnadeva, salutation to you. О lord, I am not at all at fault in this case. I had been overpowered by your Мaуa, which resulted in my pronouncing a curse on the Pandavas. Therefore, the words spoken by me cannot be otherwise. These people shall have to face partial birth. Yudhisthira would be the son of Vatsaraja known by the name of Balakhana or Malakhana and would be the ruler of the city of Sirisa. Because of his speaking the malicious words, he would he bom among the Mlecchas and would be their leader named Virata. The most intelligent Aijuna, my devotee, would be born from his amsa in Parimala family as Brahmananda. The immensely valorous Nakula would be bom in the family of Ratnabhanu and would be known by the name of Laksmana. The immensely intelligent and valorous Sahadeva would be bom as Devasimha - the son of Bhl$masirhha. A king name Prthiviraja would be bom from the amsa of Dhrtarastra at Ajmera. Draupadi would be bom as his daughter and would be known by the name of Vela. Kama would be reborn by the name of Taraka. Raktabija and Rudra would also be reborn on this earth. These Kauravas would be efficient in waging the deceitful wars. The people of the Pandava race would always be valorous and shall fight on the basis of dharma.

## \|\| 2.104.31-34 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā hariḥ prāha vihasya parameśvaram \|*

*mahāvatī purī ramyā māyādevīvinirmitā \|*
