31-34. Suta said- On hearing this, Sri Krsna smiled and said to lord Siva- “I shall help the Pandavas incarnating in the form of Sakti. In the city built by the goddess known by the name of Mahavati, a son would be bom by Desaraja from Devaki's womb who would be known by Udayasimha. A prince named Alha would be bom from my amsa, who would be the destroyer of the rulers of Agnivamsa. Thereafter, Kali would be established. On hearing this, lord Siva disappeared from the scene.

## Chapter 105. The Salivahana era

## \|\| 2.105.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*prātaḥ kāle ca saṃprāpte pāṃḍavāḥ putraśokinaḥ \|*  
*pretakāryāṇi te kṛtvā bhīṣmāntikamupāyayuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*rājadharmānmokṣadharmāndānadharmānvibhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*śrutvāyajannaśvamedhaistribhiruttamakarmabhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṣaṭtriṃśadabdarājyaṃ hi kṛtvā svargapuraṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*janiṣyante tadaṃśā vai kalidharma vivṛddhaye \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said- In the early morning, the grieved Pandavas performed the last rites of the people who had been killed earlier, after which they proceeded on to Bhisma - the grandsire. Reaching before him, they heard from him the facts about the Rajadharma, Moksadharma and Danadharma, with details. Then he performed three Asvamedha sacrifices appropriately, ruled for thirty six years and then proceeded on to the heaven. Thereafter, the people of his race shall be born in the age of Kali, for its expansion.

## \|\| 2.105.4-7 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā sa muniḥ sarvānpunaḥ sūto vadiṣyati \|*  
*gacchadhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve yoganidrāvaśo hyaham \|*  
*cakratīrthe samādhistho dhyāye'haṃ triguṇātparam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu munayo naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ \|*  
*yogasiddhiṃ samāsthāya gamiṣyaṃtyātmanontike \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdaśate kāle'tīte te śaunakādayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*utthāya devakhāte ca snānadhyānādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā sūtāntikaṃ gatvā vadiṣyaṃti punarvacaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Vyasa said- Thus speaking, Suta addressed the Maharsis - “I am presently being overpowered by the yogic sleep. Therefore, all of you should leave the place. I myself, entering into a samadhi, shall meditate on the supreme Brahman, who is beyond the three gunas (sattva, rajas and tamas).” Listening to this, the dwellers of Naimisaranya would also achieve the supreme soul, because of their yogic exercise. Then, after the lapse of twelve hundred years, Sаunака and other Rsis would wake up and after taking a bath in the divine lake, will approach Suta and say.

## \|\| 2.105.8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*vikramākhyānakālo'yaṃ dvāpare ca śivājñayā \|*  
*vinītānbhagavanbhūmau tadā tānnṛpatīnvada \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Rsis said- The command issued by lord Siva during the age of dvapara, that particular time of samvatasara has arrived. Therefore, you kindly mention about the rulers of the earth.

## \|\| 2.105.9-16 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*svargate vikramāditye rājāno bahudhā'bhavan \|*  
*tathāṣṭādaśa rājyāni teṣāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu \|\| 9 \|\|*

*paścime siṃdhunadyaṃte setubandhe hi dakṣiṇe \|*  
*uttare badarīsthāne pūrve ca kapilāntike \|\| 10 \|\|*

*aṣṭādaśaiva rāṣṭrāṇi teṣāṃ madhye babhūvire \|*  
*iṃdraprasthaṃ ca pāṃcālaṃ kuru kṣetraṃ ca kāpilam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*antarvedī vrajathyaivājameraṃ marudhanva ca \|*  
*gaurjjaraṃ ca mahārāṣṭraṃ drāviḍaṃ ca kaliṃgakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*āvaṃtyaṃ coḍupaṃ vaṃgaṃ gauḍaṃ māgadhameva ca \|*  
*kauśalyaṃ ca tathā jñeyaṃ teṣāṃ rājā pṛthakpṛk \|\| 13 \|\|*

*nānābhāṣāḥ sthitāstatra bahudharmapravartakāḥ \|*  
*evamabdaśataṃ jātaṃ tataste vai śakādayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śrutvā dharmavināśaṃ ca bahuvṛṃdaiḥ samanvitāḥ \|*  
*kecittīrtvā siṃdhunadīmāryyadeśaṃ samāgatāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*himaparvatamārgeṇa siṃdhumārgeṇa cāgaman \|*  
*jitvāryyāllāṃṭhayitvā tānsvadeśaṃ punarāyayuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

9-16. Suta said- After the departure of the king Vikramaditya to the heaven, there had been eighteen kings and several kingdoms on earth. I am going to speak out their names, you please listen. There is a Sindhu river in the west; Setubandha in the south; Badarinatha is in the north; while the hennitage of Kapila is located in the east. In the middle of these, there is Indraprastha in the centre, besides Pancala, Kuruksetra, Kapila, Antarvedi, Vrajathya, Marudhanva, Gurjara (Gujarat), Maharastra, Dravida, Kalinga, Avanti, Udupa, Banga (Bengal), Gauda, Magadha and Kausaia. These were the eighteen countries, which were established. All of them had their individual rulers, who spoke different language and followed different faiths. After a lapse of hundred years, learning about the destruction of the dharma there, the Sakas together with their helpers who had already crossed the river Sindhu, reached the Arya country through the Himalayan or the sea voyage. Overpowering the Aryans, they plundered the country (of Aryans) and returned to their own country.

## \|\| 2.105.17-21 \|\|

*gṛhītvā yoṣitasteṣāṃ paraṃ harṣamupāyayuḥ \|*  
*etasminnantare tatra śālivāhanabhūpatiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vikramādityapautraśca pitṛrājyaṃ gṛhītavān \|*  
*jitvā śakāndurādharṣāṃścīnataittirideśajān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bāhlīkānkāmarūpāṃśca romajānkhurajā cchaṭhān \|*  
*teṣāṃ kośāngṛhītvā ca daṃḍayogyānakārayat \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sthāpitā tena maryyādā mlecchāryāṇāṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*siṃdhusthānamiti jñeyaṃ rāṣṭra māryyasya cottamam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*mlecchasthānaṃ paraṃ sindhoḥ kṛtaṃ tena mahātmanā \|*  
*ekadā tu śakādhīśo himatuṃgaṃ samāyayau \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. They also kidnapped their women folks. As a result of this, they enjoyed extreme pleasures by those raids. At that point of time, a king named Salivahana who was said to be the grandson of Vikramaditya, captured back the kingdom of his father. He captured the terrific Sakas from China, Bahlika - born in Jathara country, Kamarupa, Roma and Khurasana and imprisoned their rulers. As a matter of punishment, all their treasures were confiscated. They established the different traditions of Mlecchas and the Aryans. The country of Aryans came to be known as Sindhusthana (which is presently known as Hindustana). The great soul established the country of the Mleccha beyond the river Sindhu. Once the lord of Sakas travelled to a hill of the Himalaya.

## \|\| 2.105.22-34 \|\|

*hūṇadeśasya madhye vai giristhaṃ puruṣaṃ śubham \|*  
*dadarśa balavānrājā gaurāṃgaṃ śvetavastrakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ko bhavāniti taṃ prāha sa hovāca mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*īśaputraṃ ca māṃ viddhi kumārīgarbhasaṃbhavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mlecchadharmasya vaktāraṃ satyavrataparāyaṇam \|*  
*iti śrutvā nṛpaḥ prāha dharmaḥ ko bhavato mataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śrutvovāca mahārāja prāpte satyasya saṃkṣaye \|*  
*nirmaryāde mlecchadeśe masīho'haṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*īśāmasī ca dasyūnāṃ prādurbhūtā bhayaṃkarī \|*  
*tāmahaṃ mlecchataḥ prāpya masīhatvamupāgataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mleccheṣu sthāpito dharmo mayā tacchṛṇu bhūpate \|*  
*mānasaṃ nirmalaṃ kṛtvā malaṃ dehe śubhāśubham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*naigamaṃ japamāsthāya japeta nirmalaṃ param \|*  
*nyāyena satyavacasā manasaikyena mānavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*dhyānena pūjayedīśaṃ sūryamaṃḍalasaṃsthitam \|*  
*acalo'yaṃ prabhuḥ sākṣāttathā sūryocalaḥ sadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tattvānāṃ calabhūtānāṃ karṣaṇaḥ sa samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*iti kṛtyena bhūpāla masīhā vilayaṃ gatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*īśamūrtirhṛdi prāptā nityaśuddhā śivaṃkarī \|*  
*īśāmasīha iti ca mama nāma pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa bhūpālo natvā taṃ mlecchapūjakam \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa ta tatra mlecchasthāne hi dāruṇe \|\| 32 \|\|*

*svarājyaṃ prāptavānrājā hayamedhamacīkarat \|*  
*rājyaṃ kṛtvā sa ṣaṣṭyabdaṃ svargalokamupāyayau \|\| 33 \|\|*

*svargate nṛpatau tasminyathā cāsīttathā śṛṇu \|\| 34 \|\|*

22-34. In the middle of Huna country, he met with a person with auspicious form. He was of fair complexion and was clad in white garments. On being asked as to who he was, the divine person answered- “I am the son of Isa and have been bom from the womb of a virgin. I am the spokesperson of the Mlecchas and am truthful in conduct.” On hearing this, the king said-“What do you feel about dharma?” He replied-“O lord, in this Mleccha country, those who are devoid of truth and traditions, I have arrived as an elegy for them. О king, I have already established the dharma among the Mlecchas. You listen to what I say. The auspicious and inauspicious elements are found in the body, which pollute the mind. Purifying the mind, following the truth and justice, one should be carefill. The Vedic hymns should be recited meditating upon the spotless Paramesvara. As the Paramesa is infallible, similarly the sun is also beyond movement. О king, because of the dragging of the body of five tattvas by the people, Masiha has been destroyed and the image of Isvara lodged in the heart, which is eternal, pure and beneficial, has been fixed. Therefore, I am known as Isamasiha.” Hearing this, the king offered his salutation to Mleccha deity and established the same in a terrific place of Mlecchas. Thereafter, he returned to his country, performed the Asvamedha sacrifice and ruled the country for eight more years. Then he proceeded on to the heaven. After the departure, whatever happened is going out to be related by me. You please listen.

## Chapter 106. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.106.1-6 \|\|

*śrīsūta uvāca \|*  
*śālivāhanavaṃśe ca rājāno daśa cābhavan \|*  
*rājyaṃ paṃcaśatābdaṃ ca kṛtvā lokāntaraṃ yayuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*maryyādā kramato līnā jātā bhūmaṃḍale tadā \|*  
*bhūpatirdaśamo yo vai bhojarāja iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā prakṣīṇamaryyādāṃ balī digvijayaṃ yayau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*senayā daśasāhasryā kālidāsena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tathānyairbrāhmaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ siṃdhupāramupāyayau \|\| 3 \|\|*

*jitvā gāṃdhārajānmlecchānkāśmīrānnāravāñchaṭhān \|*  
*teṣāṃ prāpya mahākośaṃ daṃḍayogyānakārayat \|\| 4 \|\|*

*etasminnantare mleccha ācāryyeṇa samanvitaḥ \|*  
*mahāmada iti khyātaḥ śiṣyaśākhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nṛpaścaiva mahādevaṃ marusthalanivāsinam \|*  
*gaṃgājalaiśca saṃsnāpya paṃcagavyasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*caṃdanādibhirabhyarcya tuṣṭāva manasā haram \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Suta said- In the family of Salivahana, ten kings were born and ruled for five hundred years. They proceeded on to the heaven in due course of time. During the time of their rule, the old traditions gradually declined and ultimately faded out. So much so, that during the time of the last king Bhoja, the traditions faded out completely. Observing the traditions getting disappearing so fast, the valorous king started on the world conquest. He was accompanied by Kalidasa together with the army of ten thousand soldiers. He made other Brahmanas also to accompany him and reached beyond the river Sindhu. He conquered the Mleccahas of Gandhara country, the wicked Naravas of Kasmira. He carried with him their treasures as punishment and proceeded on to his place. At the same time, Mahamada - the preceptor of the Mlecchas, was propagating with his disciples. On the other hand, the king Bhoja also started worshipping Siva in the desert land, with the water of Ganga, pancagavya and the sandal paste. Then he started offering prayers.

## \|\| 2.106.7-8 \|\|

*bhojarāja uvāca \|*  
*namaste girijānātha marusthalanivāsine \|*  
*tripurāsuranāśāya vahumāyāpravarttine \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mlecchairguptāya śuddhāya saccidānandarūpiṇe \|*  
*tvaṃ māṃ hi kiṃkaraṃ viddhi śaraṇārthamupāgatam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Bhojaraja said- “Salutation to the lord Siva, the husband of Girija and the dweller of the desert land. He destroyed the highly illusory Tripurasura. He is of spotless form, protected by the Mlecchas, besides being the form of the Supreme soul. I happen to be your slave and have reached here to take protection with you.”

## \|\| 2.106.9-16 \|\|

*mlecchaissudūṣitā bhūmirvāhīkā nāma viśrutā \|*  
*āryyadharmo hi naivātra vāhīke deśadāruṇe \|\| 10 \|\|*

*babhūvātra mahāmāyī yo'sau dagdho mayā purā \|*  
*tripuro balidaityena preṣitaḥ punarāgataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ayoniḥ sa varo mattaḥ prāptavāndaityavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*mahāmada iti khyātaḥ paiśācakṛtitatparaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nāgantavyaṃ tvayā bhūpa paiśāce deśadhūrtake \|*  
*matprasādena bhūpāla tava śuddhiḥ prajāyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā nṛpaścaiva svadeśānpunarāgamat \|*  
*mahāmadaśca taiḥ sārddhaṃ siṃdhutīramupāyayau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tathā dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayamāgataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

9-16. Suta said- Listening to this prayer of the king Bhoja, lord Siva spoke to the king- “O king Bhoja, you go to the land of Vahanika in the Mahakale^vara region, which is being polluted by the Mlecchas. In the terrific region of Vahanika, the Arуa dharma has disappeared. The daitya Tripurasura has reached there again supported by the king Bali, who had been reduced to ashes by me. He is bom without conjugal contact, is the best of the daityas race and enhances the demon race. He is known by the name of Mahamada, who always practices the Pisaca activities. Therefore, you should not stay in the country of that Рisaса. You would be purified by my grace.” On hearing the words of lord Siva, the king Bhojia returned to his country. On the other hand, Mahamada also reached the bank of the river Sindhu. The deceitful one said to the king in sweet words- “O lord, your gods are my slaves and they live on my left over.” On hearing and observing this, the king was immensely surprised.

## \|\| 2.106.17-22 \|\|

*mlecchadharme matiścāsīttasya bhūpasya dāruṇe \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tacchrutvā kālidāsastu ruṣā prāha mahāmadam \|*  
*māyā te nirmitā dhūrta nṛpamohanahetave \|\| 18 \|\|*

*haniṣyāmi durācāraṃ vāhīkaṃ puruṣādhamam \|*  
*ityuktvā sa dvijaḥ śrīmānnavārṇajapatatparaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*japtvā daśasahasraṃ ca taddaśāṃśaṃ juhāva saḥ \|*  
*bhasma bhūtvā sa māyāvī mlecchadevatvamāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*bhayabhītāstu tacchiṣyā deśaṃ vāhīkamāyayuḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā svagurorbhasma madahīnatvamāgatam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sthāpitaṃ taiśca bhūmadhye tatroṣurmadatatparāḥ \|*  
*madahīnaṃ puraṃ jātaṃ teṣāṃ tīrthaṃ samaṃ smṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

17-22. He also thought of embracing the Mleccha dharma. At the same time, Kalidasa spoke in anger to Mahamada- “O deceitful one, this is only an illusion created by you to confuse the king. Therefore, I shall kill the deceitful person like you.” Thus speaking, the Brahmana Kalidasa recited the Navarna mantra ten thousand times and started pouring offering in the fire. Getting reduced to ashes with the same, he became the god of the Mlecchas. Thereafter, all his disciples getting panic-stricken, returned to Vahnika country. They carried the ashes of their preceptor Mahamada and buried it under the ground and became peaceful. The place was given the name of Madahinapura (or Madina). It now happens to be the place of their pilgrimage.

## \|\| 2.106.23-32 \|\|

*rātrau sa devarūpaśca bahumāyāviśāradaḥ \|*

*āryyadharmo hi te rājansarvadharmottamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*īśājñayā kariṣyāmi paiśācaṃ dharmadāruṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*liṃgacchedī śikhāhīnaḥ śmaśrudhārī sa dūṣakaḥ \|*

*vinā kaulaṃ ca paśavasteṣāṃ bhakṣyā matā mama \|*

*tasmānmusalavanto hi jātayo dharmadūṣakāḥ \|*  
*iti paiśācadharmaśca bhaviṣyati mayā kṛtaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ityuktvā prayayau devaḥ sa rājā gehamāyayau \|*  
*trivarṇe sthāpitā vāṇī sāṃskṛtī svargadāyinī \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śūdreṣu prākṛtī bhāṣā sthāpitā tena dhīmatā \|*  
*paṃcāśadabdakālaṃ tu rājyaṃ kṛtvā divaṃ gataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sthāpitā tena maryyādā sarvadevopamāninī \|*

*āryya varṇāḥ sthitāstatra viṃdhyānte varṇasaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*narā musalavantaśca sthāpitāḥ siṃdhupārajāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*barbare tuṣadeśe ca dvīpe nānāvidhe tathā \|*

23-32. The Рisaса deity then spoke to the king Bhoja- “O king, your Arya-dharma is the best of all the dharmas. I am propagating this dharma because of the compulsion under the command of Isa, which includes the cutting of linga, removing of the tuft and to keep the beard, to talk tall and consuming of everything. This would be practiced by the people of my class. They would eat the animals without kaula-tantra. They would perform all their religious rites with musala instead of kusa grass. Therefore, these Muslims would be called as the polluters of dharma. I shall propagate this type of dharma.” Thus speaking, he left the place. The king also returned to his place. They established the Samskrta language among the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and Vaisyas, while Prakrita was propagated among the Sudras. Then after ruling the country for fifty years, the king proceeded on to the heaven. He established the Aryavrata country comprising of Vindhya mountain, Himalaya, Madhyapradesa - the auspicious land. He also established the traditions of all the deities. The people of Arya race live there. The people of mixed breed live beyond the river Sindhu which was known as the Muslim country. The dharma of Isamasiha was established in the Barbara, Tusa and all other islands.

## Chapter 107. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

*agnihotrasya kartāro gobrāhmaṇahitaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*babhūvurdvāparasamā dharmakṛtyaviśāradāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dvāparākhyasamaḥ kālaḥ sarvatra parivartate \|*  
*gehegehe sthitaṃ dravyaṃ dharmaścaiva janejane \|\| 9 \|\|*

*grāmegrāme sthito devo deśedeśe sthito makhaḥ \|*  
*āryadharmakarā mlecchā babhūvuḥ sarvatomukhāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*iti dṛṣṭvā kalirghoro mlecchayā saha bhīrukaḥ \|*  
*nīlādrau prāpya matimānhariṃ śaraṇamāyayau \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdamite kāle dhyānayogaparo'bhavat \|*  
*dhyānena saccidānaṃdaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ sanātanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tuṣṭāva manasā tatra rādhayā sahitaṃ harim \|*  
*purāṇamajaraṃ nityaṃ vṛṃdāvananivāsinam \|\| 13 \|\|*

1-13. Suta said- After the death of the king Bhoja, in his race there were seven rulers in quick succession one after another. Because of their having short lives, these unfortunate kings could rule for three hundred years, after which the dynasty came to an end within three hundred years. All of them proceeded on to the heaven. Their countries were divided into small principalities. The seventh king of their race was known as Virasimha. Three kings of his race met with their deaths within two hundred years. The tenth king was known as Gangasimha, who enjoyed the rule of his kingdom in Kalpaksetra. In the Antarvedi region of Kanyakubja country, there was a king named Jayacandra, while at Indraprastha a king named Anangapala ruled there. Similarly, there were numerous rulers for the areas comprising of several villages. There was the forceful expansion of Agnivamsa. There was a Kapilasrama in the east; Vahikanta was in the west; China was in the north; while Setubandha was in the south, in which there were sixty lakhs of the village heads. They performed the homos, besides being kind to the cows and the Brahmanas. During the rule of these religious-minded rulers, the dharma was popular, as it was popular during the times of dvapara. All the householders were rich because the people were quite religious-minded. The gods were established in each and every village. The yajnas were performed at all the places. At that point of time, even the Mlecchas also followed the Arya-dharma. Observing this, the Mlecchas of the age of kali reached the Nilacala mountain in panic and took refuge with the intelligent lord. He performed tapas there for twelve years following the dhyana-yoga while in meditation, witnessing the Supreme soul, who is eternal. He mentally adored lord Krsna with Radha and pleased both. He is eternal, beyond destruction and lived in Vridavana forever.

## \|\| 2.107.14-16 \|\|

*kaliruvāca \|*  
*sāṣṭāṃgaṃ daṃḍavatsvāmingṛhāṇa mama ceśvara \|*  
*. pāhi māṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptaṃ caraṇe te kṛpānidhe \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarvapāpaharastvaṃ vai sarvakālakaro hariḥ \|*  
*bhavāngauraḥ satyayuge tretāyāṃ raktarūpakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dvāpare pītarūpaśca kṛṣṇatvaṃ mama diṣṭake \|*  
*matputrāśca smṛtā mlecchā āryyadharmatvamāgatāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Kali said- О lord, you kindly accept the prostration offered by me with devotion. О compassionate one, I have reached here to take refuge at your feet. You kindly protect me. You are destroyer of all the sins and are the supreme lord - the form of Kala. During Satyayuga, you have fair complexion; during Tetayuga, you have red complexion; yellow during Dvapara and fortunately during my time, you are black in colour. My sons are called Mlecchas, and they have started following the Arya-dharma.

## \|\| 2.107.17-28 \|\|

*caturgehaṃ ca me svāmindyūtaṃ madyaṃ suvarṇa kam \|*

*tyaktadehastyaktakulastyaktarāṣṭro janārdana \|*

*ityuktvā bhagavānsākṣāttatraivāntaradhīyata \|*

*etasminnantare vipra yathā jātaṃ śṛṇuṣva tat \|*

*navadurgāvrataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ navavarṣaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*prasannā caṃḍikā prāha varaṃ varaya śobhane \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sāha tāṃ yadi me mātarvaro deyastvayeśvari \|*

17-28. О master, four houses were built for me. One was to be used for gambling; the second for drinking; the third for gold and the fourth for the enjoying of pleasure with ladies. All the four houses were destroyed by the Ksatriyas of Agnivamsa. О Janardana, disowning the body, family and nation, I have now fallen at your lotus like feet.” On hearing this, with a serene smile over his face, lord Кода said- “O Kali, a valorous soul like me shall be bom for your safety. My ams'a reaching on earth shall destroy the powerful rulers and establish the strong Mleccha rulers.” Thus speaking, lord Krsna disappeared from the scene at one and the same time. The Kali along with Mlecchas felt extremely delighted. In the meantime, an incident took place which you please listen. In a village named Vaksara, there lived a milkmaid known by the name of Vratapa, who had worshipped continuously for Durga. Getting pleased with her, the goddess Candika said to her- “O beautiful one, you ask for a boon.” The milkmaid replied- “O goddess, in case you are really pleased with me, then О goddess, let two children as brave as Rama and Krsna be bom in my family.” The goddess granted the desire of the milkmaid and disappeared from the scene. In due course of time, a king named Vasuman was attracted towards her and married her in a religious manner and lodged her in his palace. In due course of time, the said queen gave birth to two sons named- Desaraja and Vatsaraja. Both of them were as strong as hundred elephants. Both of them overpowered the king of Magadha and became the rulers of the place. Satayatta - the ruler of Varanasi, was too cruel. Because of a boon from lord Siva, a son named Virana was bom to him from the amsa of Bhimasena.

## \|\| 2.107.29-31 \|\|

*tālavṛkṣapramāṇena . cordhvavego hi tasya vai \|*  
*tālano nāma vikhyātaḥ śatayattena vai kṛtaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tābhyāṃ nṛpābhyāṃ tadyuddhamabhavallomaharṣaṇam \|*  
*yuddhena hīnatāṃ prāptastālano balavattaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tadā maitrī kṛtā tābhyāṃ tālanena samanvitā \|*  
*jayacaṃdraparīkṣārthe trayaḥ śūrāḥ samāyayuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. During those days, there was a Mleccha, who could jump to the height of the palm tree. Because of this, he was known by the name of Talana. During that time, he had a fight with Satayatta, which was terrific in nature. Talana being immensely strong, was victorious. Thereafter, a compromise was worked out among the three and they went to Jayacandra to measure their strength with him.

## Chapter 108. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.108.1-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iṃdraprasthe'naṃgapālonapatyaśca mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*putrārthaṃ kārayāmāsa śaivaṃ yajñaṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kanyake ca tadā jāte śivabhāgaprasādataḥ \|*  
*caṃdrakāṃtiśca jyeṣṭhā vai dvitīyā kīrtimālinī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kānyakubjādhipāyaiva caṃdrakāntiṃ pitādadat \|*  
*devapālāya śuddhāya rāṣṭrapālānvayāya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*someśvarāya bhūpāya capahānikulāya tu \|*  
*ajamerādhipāyaiva tathā vai kīrtimālinīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

*jayaśarmā dvijaḥ kaścitsamādhistho himālaye \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā bhūpotsavaṃ ramyaṃ rājyārthe svamano'dadhat \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tyaktvā dehaṃ sa śuddhātmā caṃdrakāṃtyāḥ sutobhavat \|*  
*jayacaṃdra iti khyāto bāhuśālī jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*ratnabhānuśca saṃjajñe śūrastasyānujo balī \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Suta said- Once Anangapala - the ruler of Indraprastha, started the performing of Putrista yajna for getting a son. By the grace of lord Siva, he got two daughters named Candrakanti and Kirtimalini. The daughter Candrakanti was married by the father with the ruler of Kanyakubja known by the name of Devapala. who belonged to the auspicious race of Ra§trapala. Similarly, Kirtimalini was married to Somesvara who was bom in Capahani race and became the king of Ajmera. During those times, a Brahmana was performing severe tap as. Observing the royal function of the king, he also developed a desire to be a king. Thereafter, meeting his end, the auspicious soul was reborn from the womb of Candrakanti. He came to be known as Jayacandra, He was quite valorous and exercised self-control. Ratnabhanu was the name of his younger brother, who possessed immense prowess besides being powerful.

## \|\| 2.108.7-13 \|\|

*sa jitvā gauḍavaṃgādīnmarudeśānmadotkaṭān \|*

*pradyotaścaiva vidyotaḥ kṣatriyau cadravaṃśajau \|*

7-13. He became victorious over the arrogant rulers of Gauds, Vanga, desert kingdoms and other countries. He received the punitive taxes and after return to his place, at the command of his brother, accepted his service. Viravati -the sister of Gangasimha, was the chief queen of Ratnabhanu. By the grace of lord Siva, Nakula’s amsa named Laksana was bom from her womb. He was immensely strong and was well-versed in the fight with sword. Just at the age of seven years, he started looking like his own father. Kirtimalini had three sons known by the names of Dhundhukara, Krsnakumara and Prthviraja who was the youngest of all and who after passing the age of twelve years, was bom as a son to his own father Simhakhela. Hearing this, Anangapala gave away his kingdom to him and he himself returned to the Himalaya for practicing yogic exercises. Dhundhukara - the , ruler of Mathura and the king of Ajmera was his younger brother. At the command of his father, both of them occupied the royal throne. Two Ksatriya princes of Candravamda known by the names of Pradyota and Vidyota accepted the position of ministers with Prthviraja. Both of them were quite strong and arrogant.

14-21. Parimala was the name of Pradyota, who himself was quite strong and was the commander of the kings army of a lakh of soldiers. Bhismasimha - the son of Vidyota, was the leader of the elephants army. At the death of the king Anangapala, finding all of them to be inimical to him, the king Prthviraja disowned all of them and drove them out of his country. Then Pradyota and other warriors who were four in number, accompanied with two hundred soldiers, reached the king Jayacandra and said to him- “O king Jayacandra, the son of your mother’s sister is enjoying the rule of the kingdom of your maternal grandparents fearlessly. We people said to that king judiciously that you are entitled to rule half of this country. Then how can you rule the entire country? On hearing this, he drove out all of us from his kingdom. Therefore, we have arrived here to take refuge with you. Now you can do whatever is considered appropriate by you.” Listening to their words, Jayacandra said to all of them-“Both your sons have been made the leaders of my cavalry force. Then he said to Parimala, you both should accept to be my ministers. Bhismaka was the commander of the elephant force.

22-32. For your livelihood, the city of Mahavati has been given, which is the favourite city of the king Mahipati. On hearing this, all of them were overjoyed. On the other hand, inspite of his being quite valorous, the king Mahipati had to desert the city quite painfully and he started living in the city of Puri. He had two sisters known by the names of Agama and Malana. Agama was married to Prthviraja, while Malana was married to Parimala. After the marriage ceremony, Prthviraja got another city built and people of all the four varnas were settled there. The city was then immensely decorated. At the gate of that fort, in an auspicious muhurta, he dug a tunnel upto Indraprastha which was a yojana in width. It was completed after a long time. The king was himself surprised by looking at it. Since that time, it came to be known as Dehali by the command of the king. After three years, the king Jayacandra, together with his sixteen lakhs of army, was decorated and sent a letter there- “Why has Prthviraja usurped the part of my inheritance. Why has it not been given over to me so for? Even now, half of the kingdom of my maternal grandfather is with him. He should immediately left that portion, Otherwise his armed army shall be destroyed by my powerful army.” Finding the letter, Prthviraja, who was also quite arrogant and who had the army of twenty lakhs, communicated to him through a messenger-“O king Jayacandra, you listen to my words carefully.

33-38. The time when the Ksatriyas of the lunar race were driven out from my place, since that time I had started collecting an army of twenty lakhs, which is quite well equipped presently. You have thought of waging war with an army of sixteen lakhs. All the rulers of Bharata pay taxes to me having been punished except you, who do not pay taxes thinking yourself to be quite powerful. But you now pay the tax expeditiously. Otherwise your army is sure to be destroyed with my sharp arrows.” Because of this, both of them developed terrific animosity. Inspite of his being extremely valorous army, Prthviraja was afraid of the strength of Jayacandra. Prthviraja felt panicky because of the strength of Jayacandra. Jayacandra had occupied half of the Aryavarta country, while Prthviraja had occupied the remaining half of it. Because of this, both of them became inimical to each other and because of which the Agnivamsa was destroyed from the roots.

## Chapter 109. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-15. Suta said - Once Ratnabhanu became victorious over the southern part of the kingdom of Prthviraja and plundered his treasure, on hearing which Prthviraja was immensely surprised. The tilakam of Ratnabhanu was quite vast, because of which he was also called as the tilakam of kalyanamurti-viravati. She was the foremost of the twelve queens, besides being the mother of Laksana. The king Jayacandra had sixteen queens, but because of the deeds of the earlier births, none of the queens had any issue. His chief queen known by the name of Vibhavari was the daughter of the Gauda king. The slave girl who had come with her was known by the name of Surabhanavi. She was quite beautiful and youthful and was well-versed in the love sport. At the sight of that slave girl, the king Jayacandra could not control his passion. Therefore, he enjoyed love sport with her excessively. In due course of time, she gave birth to a daughter named Samyogini. At the age of twelve years, that girl appeared quite beautiful and youthful. The kings of all the countries were invited by Jayacandra to participate in her svayamvara. The valorous Prthviraja also could not resist the temptation of having the girl. In order to marry her, he called his courtier and said to him- “O best of the minister, you go to the pleasant city of Kannauja and establish my golden image in the assembly. Whatever be the feelings of the people there, they should be communicated to me. О best of the race of Bhrgus, Candrabhatta, who was the staunch devotee of the goddess, did according to the instructions of the king. He fulfilled the task entrusted to him. In the gathering of the svayamvara, the rulers of many countries had arrived. But discarding all of them and getting attracted towards the image of Prthviraja, Samyogini said to her father- “O king, I shall marry the king whose has been placed in the assembly.” On hearing this, Jayacandra said to Candrabhata- “In case your king with his entire army comes and could win a victory here, then I shall be extremely happy. On hearing the words of Jayacandra, Candrabhatta went to Prthviraja and communicated the factual position to him.

16-25. Prthviraja then asked his army to get ready at once. In that army, there were a lakh of warriors with elephants, seven lakh cavalrymen, five thousand charioteers who were masters of archery, twelve lakhs of foot soldiers, besides three hundred rulers. Accompanied with his two brothers, Prthviraja reached the city of Kanyakubja. In the army of Prthviraja, Dhundhukara was the leader of the elephant army, while the valorous Krsnakumara was the leader of cavalry. The various rulers were made to lead the foot soldiers. They created tumultuous sound, as a result of which the earth appeared to be noiseless. The army camped there in an area of twenty коsas. On hearing the arrival of Prthviraja, Jayacandra ordered his sixteen lakhs of solders to get ready. In the army of Jayacandra, there were a lakh of elephant riders, eight lakh cavalry man, seven lakhs foot soldiers, who were well-versed in all types of war. Besides two hundred rulers were ready to help him. The kings of the lunar race considered Prthviraja to be a culprit and got ready for waging a war from all the sides. The closed litter of Samyogini was lodged over the bank of the river Isa, where the sweet music was being played upon.

26-30. The closed litter of Samyogini was being guarded by the military commanders known by the names of Ratnabhanu of elephant army and Rupanika Laksana. Pradyota and Vidyota were protecting Ratnabhanu, while Bhisma and Parimala were on guards for Laksana. Getting arrogant, the foot soldiers of the king waged a great war and started killing the enemy army. In this war, the cavalry men fought with cavalry men, the elephant riders with the elephant riders and the foot soldiers with the foot soldiers. The rulers of both sides were feeling unconcerned with the war. Till the sun rose in the sky, the war went on.

31-44. Thus the war was fought for five days continuously. Ten thousand elephants of Prthviraja, one lakh of cavalry men, five lakhs of foot soldiers and two hundred kings were killed, besides three hundred chariots. On the other hand, nine thousand elephants, a thousand chariots, three lakhs of foot soldiers and a lakh of cavalry men of Jayacandra were too killed. On the sixth day, feeling extremely painful, Prthviraja mentally adored lord Siva. Feeling pleased with the prayer of Prthviraja, Lord Siva confused the army of Jayacandra. At that point of time, Prthviraja went to Samyogini and was fascinated at her beauty. Samyogini too, almost fainted at the sight of Prthviraja. At that point of time, Prthviraja carried the palanquin of Samyogini and proceeded towards Dehall. When Prthviraja covered a distance of a yojana, the Jayacandra’s soldiers were woken up from the swoon and finding the palanquin together with Samyogini, they followed Prthviraja with great speed. Hearing their tumult, Prthviraja left half of his army there and returned to his abode. Under the leadership of both the brothers, the half of his army got ready for war at the Varaha region. They fought a terrific war with Pradyota and other warriors. The horse riders fought with horse riders, the elephant riders fought with elephant riders, which was quite a terrific and horrified one. By evening, both the armies had to suffer a great loss. At the dead of night, the soldiers of the army of Prthviraja fled toward Dehali.

*kṛṣṇako ratnabhānuśca yuyudhāte parasparam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ubhau samabalau vīrau gajapṛṣṭhasthitau raṇe \|*  
*anyonyanihatau nāgau khaṅgahastau mahī tale \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yuyudhāte bahūnmārgānkṛtavaṃtau sudurjayau \|*  
*praharāntaṃ raṇaṃ kṛtvā maraṇāyopajagmatuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*hate tasminmahāvīrye kānyakubjā bhayāturāḥ \|*  
*mūrchitāṃstrīnsamādāya paṃcalakṣabalairyutāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*raṇaṃ tyaktvā gṛhaṃ jagmurnṛpaśokaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*ratnabhānau ca nihate hatotsāhāśca bhūmipāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*svaṃsvaṃ niveśanaṃ jagmurmahīrājabhayāturāḥ \|*  
*devānārādhayāmāsuryatheṣṭaṃ te gṛhe gṛhe \|\| 59 \|\|*

*mahīrājastu balavānsaptalakṣabalānvitaḥ \|*  
*dhuṃdhukāreṇa sahito vaṃdhukṛtyordhvamācarat \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tathā bhīṣmaḥ parimalo lakṣaṇaḥ pitaraṃ svakam \|*  
*gaṃgākūle samāgamya caurdhvadaihikamācaran \|\| 61 \|\|*

45-61. But Pradyota and other warriors did not stop following them, there even again a terrific war started. In the said battle, Dhundhukara shot an arrow at the heart of Pradyota. Having been hurt with the poisonous arrows of (Dhundhukara), the life of Praydota departed from his body. Witnessing the death of his own brother, the valorous Vidyota drove his elephant forward and attacked Dhundhukara. He attacked with tomara weapon thrice due to which he fell down fainted. Finding his brother Dhundhukara having fallen fainted, Krsnakumara drove forward his elephant and in rage attacked at the valorous warrior, which killed him. At the fall of the commander Vidyota, Ratnabhanu started fighting. At the same time, leading an army of a thousand elephants, Dhundhukara attacked Laksana, who was being supported by Bhisma and Parimala. The king who had achieved a boon from lord Siva, made all the three warriors named Bhisma, Parimala and Laksana senseless. Finding them fainted, Ratnabhanu made Dhundhukara senseless with his Vaisnavastra and started fighting with Krsnakumara. Both of them had equal strength and were riding over the elephants. With the proficiency of their archery, they killed the elephants of each other. Then they started fighting over the ground, making several paths. In the same battlefield, both of them attacking over each other, met with their end. At the death of both of them, the soldiers of Kanyakubja got frightened and therefore they fled away to their homes with five lakhs of army. Getting grief stricken, the king after the death of Ratnabhanu, was further discouraged. Then because of the terror of Prthviraja, all the rulers went back to their respective homes and started adoring their family deities. The valorous Prthviraja with the army of seven lakhs, together with Dhundhukara, performed the last rites of his brother. Thereafter, Bhisma, Parimala and Laksana performed the funeral rites of their father.

## \|\| 2.109.62-63 \|\|

*bhūmirājasya vijayo jayacaṃdayaśo raṇe \|*  
*prasiddhamabhavadbhūmau gehegehe janejane \|\| 62 \|\|*

*jayacaṃdraḥ kānyakubje dehalyāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*utsavaṃ kārayitvā tu paramānandamāyayau \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. In this way, the victory of Prthviraja and the glory of Jayacandra was spread in every house on earth, reaching all the human beings. Jayacandra celebrated the event in Kanyakubja and Prthviraja did so at Dehall, with delight.

## Chapter 110. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.110.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bhīṣmaḥ siṃhasthite gaṃgākūle śakraprapūjakaḥ \|*  
*śakraṃ sūryamayaṃ jñātvā tapasā samatoṣayat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*māsāṃte bhagavāniṃdro jñātvā tadbhaktimuttamām \|*  
*varaṃ varaya ca prāha śrutvā śūrobravīdidam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dehi me vaḍavāṃ divyāṃ yadi tuṣṭo bhavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*iti śrutvā tadā tasmai vaḍavāṃ hariṇīṃ śubhām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dadau sa bhagavāniṃdrastatraivāntarhitobhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tasminkāle parimalaḥ pitṛśokaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*pārthivaiḥ pūjayāmāsa mahādevamumāpatim \|*  
*parīkṣārthaṃ śivaḥ sākṣātsarparogeṇa taṃ grasat \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said- Bhismasimha started worshipping Indra over the bank of Ganga. Thereafter, he performed tapas for Indra in the form of the sun. After a month, getting pleased with him, the valorous Indra said to him-“You ask for a boon.” On hearing that, the valorous monarch said- “In case you are happy with me, then you kindly give me a divine and beautiful deer.” On hearing this, Indra bestowed a deer to him. Thereafter, Indra disappeared from the scene. At the same time, because of the grief of the demise of Parimala’s father, he started worshipping Siva in the form of a Parthiva Sivalinga. In order to test his devotion, lord Siva made him suffer from snake bite.

## \|\| 2.110.6-13 \|\|

*vyatīte paṃcame māse nṛpaḥ śaktivivarjitaḥ \|*  
*na tatyāja mahāpūjāṃ mahākleśasamanvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*maraṇāya yayau kāśīṃ svapatnyā sahito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*uvāsa vaṭamūlāṃte rātrau rogaprapīḍitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*etasminnantare kaścitpannago mūlasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*śabdaṃ cakāra madhuraṃ śrutvā rudrāhirāyayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*rudrāhiṃ pannagaḥ prāha bhavānnirdaya mandadhīḥ \|*  
*śivabhaktaṃ nṛpamimaṃ pīḍayetpratyahaṃ khalaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mūrkho'yaṃ bhūpatiḥ sākṣādāranālaṃ pibennahi \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa rudrāhirāha re pannagādhama \|\| 10 \|\|*

*rājño dehe paraṃ harṣaṃ pratyahaṃ prāptavānaham \|*  
*svagehaṃ duḥkhatastyājyaṃ kathaṃ tyājyaṃ mayā śaṭha \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mūrkhotra bhūpatiryo vai tailoṣṇaṃ yanna dattavān \|*  
*ityuktvāntargato dehe śrutvā sā malanā satī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*cakāra pannagoktaṃ tadgatarogo nṛpo'bhavat \|*  
*tailoṣṇairbilamāpūrya cakhāna ca satī svayam \|\| 13 \|\|*

6-13. By the end of the fifth month, the king became totally deprived of strength, but inspite of his suffering so badly from the disease, he did not perform the worship of lord Siva. Thereafter, the king together with his wife, proceeded towards Kasi in order to meet with his end. Reaching there, because of his suffering badly, they spent the night under a banyan tree. In the meantime, a serpent who lived at the root of that tree created sweet sound, hearing which the serpent which was lodged in the body of the king, came out. The tree originated snake told the other snake that it was quite cruel and foolish. You cause pain to the noble king who is the devotee of lord Siva. The king also is a fool, otherwise he should have consumed aranala by now in order to get rid of the disease.” On hearing this, the Rudra-serpent said to the tree serpent-“O degraded Rudra-serpent, I always enjoy pleasure in the body of the king. Therefore, О wicked one, then how could I discard his body? Anyone leaves his place due to some painful situation only. The king also is a fool, who does not pour hot oil in your snake hole.” Thus speaking, he again entered the body of the king. Thereafter, the noble queen Malana put into practice the method spoken by the serpent, as a result of which the king was freed from the ailment forever. Then after pouring the hot oil in the snake hole, the queen started digging it also.

## \|\| 2.110.14-19 \|\|

*tato jātaṃ svayaṃ liṃgamaṃguṣṭhābhaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*jyotīrūpaṃ cidānaṃdaṃ sarvalakṣmasamanvitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*niśīthe tama udbhūte dikṣu sūryatvamāgatam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sa vismito rājā pūjayāmāsa śaṃkaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

*mahimnastavapāṭhaiśca tuṣṭāva girijāpatim \|*  
*tadā prasanno bhagavānvaraṃ brūhi tamabravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śrutvāha nṛpatirdevaṃ yadi tuṣṭo maheśvara \|*  
*śrīpatirme gṛhaṃ prāpya vasenmatpriyakārakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tathetyuktvā mahādevo liṃgarūpatvamāgataḥ \|*  
*pratyahaṃ bhāramekaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ suṣuve tanoḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadā malastu saṃtuṣṭaḥ prāpto gehaṃ mahāvatīm \|*  
*bhīmasiṃhena sahitaḥ paramānaṃdamāyayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

14-19. As a result of the digging, a Sivalinga of the size of a thumb was found from the snake hole, which was of the form of the eternal sky, the supreme soul, besides possessing all the auspicious symbols. In the dead of the dark night, with the recovery of the Sivalinga, dazzling light like sunshine was spread around everywhere. Observing that, the king started worshipping lord Siva with devotion. He prayed to Siva by reciting the Sivamahimna-strotra, who was lord of Girija, who getting pleased with the king, asked him to seek for a boon. On hearing that, the king said- “O lord Mahesvara, in case you intend to shower your grace on me, then the lord of Sri reside in my house for the fulfilling of my desires.” Thus speaking, the lord of Sri taking to the form of a Sivalinga, started giving a bhara of gold to the king daily. The king Parimala also getting pleased, returned to his abode in the city of Mahavati and started living with comfort with Bhismasimha.

## \|\| 2.110.20-30 \|\|

*tataḥprabhṛti varṣāṃte jayacaṃdrapurīṃ yayau \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā parimalaṃ rājā kṛtakṛtyatvamāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*diṣṭyā te saṃkṣito rogo diṣṭyā te darśitaṃ mukham \|*  
*bhavānnijapurīṃ prāpya sukhī bhavatu mā ciram \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yadā me vighna ābhūyāttadā tvaṃ māṃ samācara \|*  
*iti śrutvā parimalo gatvā sthānamavāsayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tadā tu lakṣaṇo vīro bhagavantamuṣāpatim \|*  
*jagannāthamupāgamya samabhyarccāparo'bhavat \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pakṣamātrāṃtare viṣṇurjagannātha uṣāpatiḥ \|*  
*varaṃ brūhi vacaśceti lakṣaṇaṃ prāha harṣataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ityuktaḥ sa tu taṃ devaṃ natvovāca vinamradhīḥ \|*  
*dehi me vāhanaṃ divyaṃ sarvaśatruvināśanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā jagannāthaḥ śaktimairāvatādgajāt \|*  
*samutpādya dadau tasmai divyāmairāvatīṃ mudā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*āruhyairāvatīṃ rājā lakṣaṇo gehamāyayau \|*  
*sa vai parimalo rājā jagāma ca mahāvatīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare vīrāstālanādyā madotkaṭāḥ \|*  
*mahāvatīṃ purīṃ prāpya dadṛśustaṃ mahīpatim \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tena sārddhaṃ ca mahatīṃ prītiṃ kṛtvā nyavāsayan \|*  
*māsānte ca punaste vai rājāno vinayānvitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ūcustaṃ śṛṇu bhūpāla vayaṃ gacchāmahe purīḥ \|*  
*tadā rājāpi tānprāha sarvānkṣitipatī natha \|*  
*dattvādhikāraṃ putrebhyastadā'yāsyāmi vo'ntikam \|\| 30 \|\|*

20-30. Не went to the king Jayacandra after a year. On meeting Parimala, the king thought himself

to be successful and said- “It is a matter of great fortune that you have recovered fully and I could see your pleasant face today.” You live in your city quite comfortably. I shall call you whenever any obstruction appears. On hearing this, Parimala went to his place and spent his time comfortably. At that point of time, Laks ana was also engaged in the worship of Visnu -the lord of Usa. After the lapse of a fortnight, lord Visnu said to him- “You ask for a boon.” When so asked by the lord, with all the humility, he said, offering salutation to him-“You kindly get me a divine vehicle, which should be able to destroy all the enemies.” On hearing this, extracting strength from Airavata, lord Jagannatha gave him a divine elephant. Then mounting over that elephant, the king Laksana returned to his home. On the return of the king Parimala at Mahavati, Talana and other valorous warriors also reached there and met Parimala. Establishing an intimate friendship with him, he kept on living there lovingly. After the lapse of one month, the king humbly said to him- “O king, now we intend to return to our place and you kindly permit us to leave. When the permission was received from the king, they said to him- “Entrusting all the responsibilities to my son, I shall return here to live with you.”

## \|\| 2.110.31-41 \|\|

*tathetyuktāstu te rājñā svagehaṃ punarāyayuḥ \|*  
*sānujo deśarājastu dvijebhyaḥ svapuraṃ dadau \|\| 31 \|\|*

*putrebhyastālano vīro dadau vārāṇasīṃ purīm \|*  
*alikollāmatiḥ kālaḥ patra puṣpodarī varī \|\| 32 \|\|*

*karīnarī sulalitasteṣāṃ nāmāni vai kramāt \|*  
*dvau dvau putrau smṛtau teṣāṃ pitustulyaparākramau \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sa vai putrājñayā śūrastālano rākṣasapriyaḥ \|*  
*yātudhānamayaṃ devaṃ tuṣṭāva mlecchapūjanaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tathā vasumataḥ putrau bhūpatīdeśavatsajau \|*  
*śakraṃ sūryyaṃ samārādhya kṛtakṛtyau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*siṃhinīnāma vaḍavāṃ yā tu dattā bhayānakā \|*  
*āruhya balavāñchūro gamanāya mano dadhau \|\| 36 \|\|*

*paṃcaśabdaṃ mahānāgamindradattaṃ manoramam \|*  
*deśarājastamāruhya gamanāya mano dadhe \|\| 37 \|\|*

*hayaṃ papīhakaṃ nāma sūryadattaṃ narasvaram \|*  
*vatsarājastamāruhya gamanāya mano dadhe \|\| 38 \|\|*

*trayaḥ śūrāḥ samāgamya nagarīṃ te mahāvatīm \|*  
*ūṣustatra mahātmāno bahumānena satkṛtāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*senā ṣaṣṭisahasraṃ tatteṣāṃ svāmī sa tālanaḥ \|*  
*maṃtriṇau bhrātarau tau ca nṛpateścandravaṃśinaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tairvīrai rakṣito rājā kṛtakṛtyatvamāgataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

31-41. Thus speaking to the king, all of them returned to their abodes, then Desaraja together with his younger brother Vatsaraja entrusted the care of the city to the Brahmanas. The valorous Talana gave away the city of Varanasi to his sons, who were said to be Alikollamati, Kala, Patra, Puspodari, Kan, Nari and Sulalita. All of them had two sons each, who were as strong as their fathers. Talana, who was dear to the Raksasas, at the desire of his son, pleased Raksasadeva by Mlecchapujana. Thereafter, Desaraja and Vatsaraja - the sons of Vasuman, respectively worshipped Indra and Surya. A Raksasa named Yatudhama gave away a mare named Simhini to Talana. The elephant named Pancasabda was given over to Desaraja. The horse named Papiha was given by the Sungod which could speak the human language to Vatsaraja. All the three warriors, mounting over their vehicles, reached the city of Mahavati and they respectfully started living there. Talana was made there the chief commander of the army of sixty thousand soldiers. Parimala - the king of lunar race, was made the minister with his brother. Thus having been well protected by the three warriors, the king Parimala thought himself to be quite successful.

## Chapter 111. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.111.1-8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*jambuko nāma bhūpālo mahīrājo bhayāturaḥ \|*  
*kāliyena yutaḥ prāpto narmadāyāstaṭe śubhe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pārthivaiḥ pūjayāmāsa devadevaṃ pinākinam \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsānte mahādevo jambukaṃ prāha bhūpatim \|\| 2 \|\|*

*varaṃ varaya te'bhīṣṭaṃ bhūpa āha kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*ajitatvaṃ nṛpaiḥ sarvairdehi me karuṇānidhe \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tathetyuktvā mahādevastatraivāntarhitobhavat \|*  
*kāliyasta tsuto labdhvā vīro māheśvaraṃ varam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mohanaṃ sarvasainyānāṃ pituraṃtikamāyayau \|*  
*pitaraṃ prāha namrātmā dehyājñāṃ tāta matpriyām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gamiṣyāmi balaiḥ sārddhaṃ gaṃgāṃ śuddhajalāṃ śubhām \|*  
*tathetyuktvā pitā tasmai yayau tu svaṃ niveśanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pranaṣṭo mulaṃ yuddhaṃ teṣāṃ vīravarakṣayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sāha graiveyakaṃ hāraṃ maṇimuktāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*matpriyaṃ dehi me vīra tathetyuktvā yayau gṛhāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Suta said- Once the king Jambuka getting frightened, together with his son named Kaliya worshipped Siva in parthiva form over the bank of the river Narmada. By the end of the sixth month, lord Mahadeva said to the king Jambuka- “You ask for the boon you desire." At this, the king spoke with folded hands- “O ocean of mercy, you grant me a boon that I should become invincible from all the kings.” Lord Siva granted him the boon and then disappeared from the scene. His son Kaliya also worshipped lord Siva and received Mohanastra from the lord and then humbly said to his father- “O father, kindly permit me to go to Gangasagara in order to have a bath in the holy river there. I shall move with my army.” After giving him the permission, the father retired to his palace. He then said to his sister- “O pleasant sister Vijaya, what is the favourite thing you want? You tell me quickly.” She replied- “O brother, I need a naulakhd garland fully decorated with the gems and beads, which is quite dear to me. Therefore, you surely bring it for me.” The brother accepted the demand of his sister and then left the place.

## \|\| 2.111.9-14 \|\|

*kāliyo lakṣaturagaiḥ saṃyutastvarito'gamat \|*  
*prāpya gaṃgāṃ sāgaragāṃ kṛtvā snānaṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dattvā dānāni viprebhyo jayacandrapurīṃ yayau \|*  
*nirdhanaḥ samabhūdrājā bāhuśālī mahābalaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kānyakubje mahāhārau na prāpto bahumūlyakaḥ \|*  
*tadorvīyādhipenaiva mahīśena prabodhitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yayau mahāvatīṃ ramyāṃ śivadattavaro balī \|*  
*rurodha nagarīṃ sarvāṃ śrutvā rājā bhayāturaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*rudraṃ kapardinaṃ śaṃbhuṃ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau \|*  
*śivājñayā nṛpo dhīmānbalaiḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrakaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sārddhaṃ purādbahiryātastribhiḥ śūraiḥ surakṣitaḥ \|*  
*tasya nāgāḥ sahasraṃ ca deśarājaśca tatpatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. The army comprised of a lakh of cavalry men reached Gangasagara. He took his bath there appropriately and then distributed charities to the Brahmanas. Then he proceeded towards the city of Jayacandra, who was discarded by him like a pauper. When he could not find the great garland in Kanyakubja as well, the king of Urai told him. Thereafter, the said king, getting arrogant because of the boon he had received from lord Siva, reached the pleasant city of Mahavati and surrounded it from all the sides. Finding this, getting frightened, the king of the place took refuge with lord Siva adoring him at the same time. At the command of lord Siva, the king, with sixty thousand army men, getting protected from the three immensely valorous warriors, reached in the battleground at the exterior of the city. In his army, there were a thousand elephants which were led by Desaraja.

## \|\| 2.111.15-22 \|\|

*hayāḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasrā vatsarājastu tatpatiḥ \|*  
*śeṣāḥ padātayastasya tālanenaiva rakṣitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ahorātrapramāṇena mahadghoramavartata \|\| 16 \|\|*

*te hatvā śātravīṃ senāṃ cakrurjayaravānmuhuḥ \|*  
*bhayārtā nārmadeyāśca māhiṣmatinivāsinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dudruvuḥ sarvato vipra dṛṣṭvā tānkāliyo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*āśvāsya prayayau yuddhamarddhasainyasamanvitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*hṛdi kṛtvā mahādevaṃ mohanaṃ bāṇamādadhat \|*  
*siddhamantraprabhāveṇa mohitāste babhūvire \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śeṣāste śatravaḥ sarve ripughātāya saṃyayuḥ \|*  
*alasāṃstānkapāleṣu jaghnuste bhayavarjitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*bhīṣmasiṃhastathā dṛṣṭvā bodhayāmāsa sainikān \|*  
*sūryadattena bāṇena saṃjñākhyānena tatra vai \|\| 21 \|\|*

*bhairavākhyena bhallena śatrudehamatāḍayat \|*  
*mūrcchitaḥ so'patadvīro gajapṛṣṭhe śarārditaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

15-22. The cavalry men were sixteen thousand, who were commanded by Vatsaraja, while the foot soldiers were led by Talana. Both the kings fought a terrific war. Many warriors were killed. The terrific war was being fought during the day and night. The soldiers of Parimala started indicating victory by shouting the slogans of victory. The people of Mahismati city fled away in panic in all the directions. О Brahmana, finding them fleeing, the king Kaliya assured them variously and he reached there for a fight with half of his army. Reciting the name of lord Siva, he used the Mohana arrow. Because of the siddha-mantra, all were overpowered by swoon. The rest of the army started destroying the army of Parimala. Then Bhismasimha freed the soldiers from swoon with the arrow known as Samjna. Thereafter, using Bhallastra of Bhairava, he attacked the body of the enemy. As a result of this, the valorous Kaliya fell down fainted over the elephant.

## \|\| 2.111.23-28 \|\|

*tadā māhiṣmatī senā niryayau sā diśau daśa \|*  
*muhūrtaṃ kaśmalaṃ prāpya punarutthāya kāliyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bhallena tacchiraḥ kāyādapāharata bhūmipaḥ \|*  
*hate tasminmahāvīrye tālanādyā mahā balāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kāliyaṃ te parājitya taṃ śatruṃ pratyaṣedhayan \|*  
*mahākaṣṭānvito bhūpo dhyātvā manasi śaṃkaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mohayitvā ripūnsarvān yayau svaṃ niveśanam \|*  
*arddhasainyena sahitā hataśeṣāstrayastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tadā parimalo rājā dṛṣṭvā śatruparājayam \|*  
*pariṣvajya mahāvīrānsva gehaṃ punarāyayau \|\| 27 \|\|*

*jayacandrastu tacchutvā paraṃ vismayamāgataḥ \|*  
*tālanaṃ ca samāhūya senādhīśamakarāyat \|\| 28 \|\|*

23-28. At that point of time, his entire army was scattered in all the directions and after remaining unconscious for a ghadi (22 minutes), Kaliya got up and making use of his spear, cut off the head of Bhisma. At the death of the valorous Bhisma, Talana and other valorous warriors obstructed the forward march of Kaliya - the enemy. But the king feeling extremely painful, reciting the name of Siva mentally, cast the swoon over the enemy and moved to his abode. On the other hand, all the three of them, Talana and other warriors, collected the remaining half of their army, and entered the city. At that point of time, the king Parimala, learning about the prowess of the enemy, embraced those who had returned and honoured them. Hearing this, Jayacandra felt extremely surprised. Then he summoned Talana and declared him as the chief of the army.

## \|\| 2.111.29-32 \|\|

*bhīṣmasiṃhe gate loke paṃcamāsāntare nṛpe \|*  
*tatpatnī janayāmāsa putraratnaṃ śubhānanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sā tu gurjarabhūpasya tanayākhyā madālasā \|*  
*divyaṃ putraṃ samālokya mumude sagaṇā bhṛśam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śrutvā tajjanma nṛpatirvitatāra dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*āhūya gaṇakānprājñāñjātakarma hyakārayat \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sahadevāṃśa evāsau bhuvi jātaḥ śivājñayā \|*  
*devasiṃhaḥ kṛto nāma gaṇakaiḥ śāstraciṃtakaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. With the departure of Bhismasimha to the heaven, his wife gave birth to a son. She was the daughter of the king of Gujarata and was known by the name of Madalasa. Learning about the birth of a son to her, all the people were surprised. The king performed his name giving ceremony and distributed enormous riches. After the name giving ceremony was performed for the boy by the astrologer, he revealed on an enquiry that, “At the command of lord Siva, the аmsа of Sahadeva has been bom in the form of an infant on earth. The learned people give him the name of Devasimha.”

## Chapter 112

## \|\| 2.112.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kāliyaṃ tau parājitya bhrātarau nṛpasevakau \|*  
*gatau gopālake rāṣṭre bhūpatirdalavāhanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sahasracaṃḍikāhome nānābhūpasamāgame \|*  
*gṛhītau mahiṣau tābhyāṃ bhūpairanyaiśca durjayau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūrvaṃ hi nṛpakanyābhyāṃ pratyahaṃ baṃdhanaṃ gatau \|*  
*tau saṃpūjya vidhānena dadau tābhyāṃ ca kanyake \|\| 3 \|\|*

*devakīṃ deśarājāya brāhmīṃ tasyānujāya vai \|*  
*dadau durgājñayā rājā rūpayauvanaśāli nīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said - Both the king and the courtier combined defeated Kaliya and then proceeded to Gopalaka country ruled by Dalavahana, where a thousand Candi-yajnas were going to start in which many rulers were to join. Both the brothers captured the buffaloes, which were to be sacrificed in the yajna and which could not be captured by any other ruler. Both the daughters of the king had already bound them. Feeling delighted, the king gave away both the girls too both the brothers respectively. Devaki was given over to Desaraja, while Brahmi was given over to Vatsaraja. Then at the command of the goddess Durga, the marriage ceremony of both the girls was performed.

## \|\| 2.112.5-14 \|\|

*lakṣāvṛttiṃ tathā veśyāṃ gītanṛtyaviśāradām \|*  
*kanyayośca sakhīṃ ramyāṃ meghamallārarāgiṇīm \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śataṃ gajānrathānpaṃca hayāṃścaiva sahasrakān \|*  
*catvāriṃśacca śibikāḥ pradadau dalavāhanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bahudravyayutāṃ kanyāṃ dāsadāsīsamanvitām \|*  
*udūhya vedavidhinā prāpatuśca mahāvatīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

*malanā tāṃ vadhūṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyai graiveyakaṃ dadau \|*  
*brāhmyai ṣoḍaśaśṛṃgāraṃ tathā dvādaśabhūṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*rājā ca paramānandī deśarājāya śūriṇe \|*  
*dadau daśapuraṃ ramyaṃ nānājananiṣevitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ūṣatustatra tau vīrau rājamānyau mahābalau \|*  
*etasminnantare jāto devasiṃho harājñayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*jāte tasminkumāre tu devakī garbhamādadhau \|*  
*dāsaśrutā paterdevī suṣuve putramūrjitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*gaurāṃgaṃ kamalākṣaṃ ca dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā \|*  
*tadānaṃdamayo devaḥ śakraḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śaṃkhaśabdaṃ cakāroccairjayaśabdaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*diśaḥ praphullitāścāsangrahāḥ sarve tathā divi \|\| 13 \|\|*

*āyātā bahavo viprā vedaśāstraparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*cakruste jātakarmāsya nāmakarma tathāvidham \|\| 14 \|\|*

5-14. A whore named Laksavrtti, who was well-versed in dance and music and her maids who were proficient in Megha-maladra raga, were also sent with the girls. Besides these, a hundred elephants, five thousand horses and forty palanquins were lovingly given over by the king Dalavahana. Besides these, enormous riches in addition to slaves and slave girls were also given. Both the brothers then proceeded on to the city of Mahavati. After finding the bride, Malana gave away the naulakha garland, while Brahmi was given over the sixteen types of srngaras and twelve ornaments. Feeling extremely blissful, Parimala gave away ten lands to valorous Desaraja, which were inhabited by people of various castes. Both the valorous brothers started living there. When Devasimha was born with the desire of lord Siva, Devaki had also conceived at the same time. In due course of time, the child who was of fair complexion, having lotus like eyes, was born illumined with his own lustre. With the birth of such a son, all the gods along with Indra felt delighted. The conches were sounded repeatedly. The directions looked green. Similarly, the planets in the sky expressed their delight. Many of the Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas and Sastras collected there and performed the name giving ceremony.

## \|\| 2.112.15-17 \|\|

*rāmāṃśaṃ taṃ śiśuṃ jñātvā prasannavadanaṃ śubham \|*  
*bhādrakṛṣṇatithau ṣaṣṭhyāṃ candravāre'ruṇodaye \|\| 15 \|\|*

*saṃjātaḥ kṛttikābhe ca pitṛvaṃśayaśaskaraḥ \|*  
*āhlādanāmnā hyabhavatpraśritaśca mahītale \|\| 16 \|\|*

*māsānte ca sute jāte brāhmī putramajījanat \|*  
*dharmajāṃśaṃ tathā gauraṃ mahābāhuṃ suvakṣasam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The son with smiling face, who was bom on Monday, on the sixth dark fortnight at dawn and in the Krttika constellation, was the one who could make his paternal race glorious. Taking into account that he happened to be the amsa of Rama, he was given the name of Ahlada or delight. The child gained the glory on earth with this name. After a month from the birth of that child, Brahmi also gave birth to a gem like son, who was of fair complexion, having long arms, vast chest and hailed from the family of Yudhisthira.

## \|\| 2.112.18-20 \|\|

*tadā ca brāhmaṇāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā bālaṃ śubhānanam \|*  
*prasannavadanaṃ cāruṃ padmacihnapadasthitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tairdvijaiśca kṛto nāmnā balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*varṣānte vatsaje jātaṃ mūlagaṃḍāntasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*cāmuṇḍo devakisuto nijavaṃśabhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*janitāraṃ tatastyājya ityūcurdvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*na tatyāja sutaṃ rājā bālatve'pi dayāparaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Observing the child at that point of time, having a delightful face, beautiful soles of the feet with lotus marks which were indicative of his being quite powerful, the Brahmanas gave him the name of Balakhana. A year after the birth of the first child, Devaki gave birth to another son, who was given the name of Camunda. He was bom at the end of Mala constellation. He was the destroyer of his race. The Brahmanas therefore desired that the child should be discarded, which would be beneficial for the race. But the king observing that his childhood was filled with compassion, could not disown him.

## \|\| 2.112.21-28 \|\|

*trivarṣāṃte gate tasminbalakhānau sute śubhe \|*  
*śūdryāṃ jātaḥ śikhaṃḍayaṃśo rūpaṇo nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vatsarājo yayau deśe gurjare ca madālasām \|*  
*sa sutāṃ ca samādāya dine tasminsamāgataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*prāpte tasminvatsarāje jambukaḥ svabalairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*saptalakṣaiśca saṃprāpto bāhuśālī yateṃdriyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*rurodha nagarīṃ sarvāṃ rājñaḥ parimalasya vai \|*  
*trilakṣaiśca māhāvatyai sārddhaṃ tau jagmatuḥ purāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

*māhiṣmataiḥ saptalakṣaiḥ sārddhaṃ yuddhamabhūnmahat \|*  
*trirātraṃ dāruṇaṃ ghoraṃ yamarāṣṭravivarddhanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śivasya varadānena bhrātrorjātaḥ parājayaḥ \|*  
*baddhvā tau jambuko rājā luṃṭhayitvā mahāvatīm \|\| 26 \|\|*

*veśyāṃ lakṣāratiṃ tasya taṃ hataṃ tadgajaṃ tathā \|*  
*graiveyakaṃ tathā hāraṃ maṇiratnavibhūṣitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā nagarīṃ sarvāṃ bhasmayitvā gṛhaṃ yayau \|*  
*ye guptā bhūtale śūrāste śeṣāśca tadā'bhavan \|\| 28 \|\|*

21-28. When these children were three years old, a child of the race of Sikhandi was bom from the womb of a Sudri woman who was given the name of Rupana. When Desaraja had gone to the country of Gujarata to get back Madalasa on his return, on the same day the king Vatsaraja was surrounded from all the four sides by the forces of the king Jambuka. When the city of Parimala was so surrounded, both the brothers Desaraja and Vatsaraja, with their army of three lakhs came out of the city of Mahavati. Though the enemy had an army of seven lakhs of soldiers, still the people fought with the enemy army for three nights and most of the opposite army was killed. Unfortunately, both the brothers were conquered by the king Jambuka who had received a boon from lord Siva. He put both of them in bondage and plundered the city. The plunder included the whore named Laksarati, the elephant Pancasabda and Maniratna - the Naulakhd garland. After plundering all, they burnt the entire city from all the sides. At that point of time, only those could escape who hid themselves in the underground chambers.

## \|\| 2.112.29-39 \|\|

*durgeṣu yāni ratnāni tāni prāpya mudā yayau \|*  
*luṃṭhite nagare tasmindevakī garbhamuttamam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ saptamāsyaṃ hi cādadhāddaivatapriyā \|*  
*jñātvā kulādhamaṃ putraṃ cāmuṃḍaṃ devakī satī \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kalpakṣetraṃ samāgamya kāliṃdyāṃ tamapātayat \|*  
*yojanānte gate tasmitmahīrājapurohitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sāmanto nāma taṃ gṛhya śvaśurālayamāyayau \|*  
*jātastu daśamāsānte rātrau ghoratamovṛte \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bhādrakṛṣṇāṣṭamīsaumye brāhmanakṣatrasaṃyute \|*  
*prādurāsījjagannātho devakyāṃ ca mahottamaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śyāmāṃgaḥ sa ca padmākṣa iṃdranīlamaṇidyutiḥ \|*  
*vimānānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ prakāśaḥ samajāyata \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vismitā jananī tatra dṛṣṭvā bālaṃ tamadbhutam \|*  
*nagare ca mahāścaryaṃ jātaṃ sarve samāyayuḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*udayaḥ kimaho jāto devānāṃ sūryarūpakaḥ \|*  
*ityāścaryyajujāṃ teṣāṃ vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśo bhūtale jātaḥ sarvānandapradāyakaḥ \|*  
*sa nāmnodayasiṃho hi sarvaśatruprakāśahā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ityākāśavacaḥ śrutvā te paraṃ harṣa māyayuḥ \|*  
*yasminkāle suto jātastadā ca malanā satī \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śyāmāṃgaṃ sundaraṃ bālaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam \|*  
*suṣuve paramodāraṃ phālgunāṃśaṃ śivājñayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

29-39. Plundering the valuable articles of the fort, he delightfully returned to his country. During those days, Devaki conceived, who was of the amsa of Krsna and had grown seven months old. The auspicious lady Devaki, thinking her son Camunda to be evil for his family, left him at the bed of the river Yamuna. The child was carried away in the current of the water for four kosas. The priest of Prthviraja saw the child, rescued him and carried him to his inlaw’s place. At the end of tenth month, on the eighth day of the black fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada and on Wednesday, in the terrific dark night at the time of Rohini constellation, Jagannatha was born out of the womb of Devaki. He was of dark complexion, had lotus like eyes and had a complexion of sapphire. At that point of time, the light of a thousand planes was visible. Sighting the unique child, his mother Devaki was herself surprised. All the people of the city also collected there. They observed, “Have the gods risen in the form of the sun?” They were thus surprised. When they were so discussing, a divine voice from the sky was heard- “The amsa of Krsna has appeared on earth, who would provide bliss to one and all. He would be known as Udayasimha, who would be victorious over all his enemies.” Listening to the divine voice, all the people were delighted. At the time when the son was born, on the same night, the queen Malana also gave birth to a beautiful boy with dark complexion and all auspicious symbols. He was bountiful with the amsa of Phalguna. He was born with the blessing of lord Siva.

## \|\| 2.112.40-43 \|\|

*tadā tu nagarī sarvā harṣabhūtā babhūva ha \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhāhani sute jāte brahmānandaguṇākare \|\| 40 \|\|*

*brāhmī tu suṣuve putraṃ pārṣadāṃśaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*śyāmāṃgaṃ kamalākṣaṃ ca dṛḍhaskandhaṃ mahābhujam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇāśca tadāgatya jātakarma hyakārayan \|*  
*sukhakhānirdvijairnāmnā kṛtastu gaṇakottamaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*krameṇa varddhitā bālāḥ sarvalokaśivaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ kālī mahacchreṣṭhā pitṛmātṛpriyaṃkarī \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. At that point of time» the capital city was flooded with delight and because of this, the child was given the name of Brahmananda. Six days after the birth of the virtuous child, Brahmi also gave birth to a beautiful boy who was the amsa of a valorous courtier. He was of dark complexion, had lotus like eyes, strong shoulders and long arms. Looking at the child, the astrologers after performing the name giving ceremony, gave him the name of Sukhakhani. The children, who extended welfare to the world, started growing. Kali was quite dear to the parents.

## \|\| 2.112.44-49 \|\|

*tṛtīyābde vayaḥ prāpte kṛṣṇāṃśe balavattare \|*  
*śakrastaddarśanakāṃkṣī hayārūḍho jagāma ha \|\| 44 \|\|*

*krīḍansa candanāraṇye kṛṣṇāṃśo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha \|*  
*nabhasthaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaṃ jahāsa vai \|\| 45 \|\|*

*aśvinī hariṇī divyā uccaiḥśravasamantike \|*  
*gatvā garbhamupādāya svagehaṃ punarāyayau \|\| 46 \|\|*

*varṣāṃtare ca suṣuve kapotaṃ tanayaṃ śubham \|*  
*pañcābdaṃ ca samāyāte vidyādhyanamāsthitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ śivaśarmāṇaṃ sarvavidyāviśāradam \|*  
*svabhaktyā sevanaṃ kṛtvā te cakrurvedapāṭhikām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*aṣṭābde caiva kṛṣṇāṃśo nāmapatrādikāṃ kriyām \|*  
*likhatāṃ bālakānāṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ śreṣṭhatāmagāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

44-49. On reaching the age of three years, the child who was the amsa of Krsna and quite powerful, at that point of time Indra mounted over the horse and arrived there in order to have a look at the child in the forest of sandal wood, where the boy was engaged in childhood sports with other children. Finding Indra in the sky, the child uttered a loud laugh. On the other hand, the mare named Harini reached the divine horse Uccaisrava of Indra and got herself conceived and then returned home. At the end of the year, she gave birth to a son named Kapota. At the start of the fifth year, the children started their studies. The Brahmana Sivasarma, who was well-versed in all the lores, was educating the boys, who served his teacher well. Attaining the age of eight years, Udayasimha became the most brilliant of all other students and he could write letters quite well.

## Chapter 113. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.113.1-8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*navamābdaṃ vayaḥ prāpte kṛṣṇāṃśo balavattaraḥ \|*  
*paṭhitvānvīkṣikīṃ vidyāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭikalāstathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dharmaśāstraṃ tathaivāpi sarvaśreṣṭhaṃ babhūva ha \|*  
*tasminkāle bhṛguśreṣṭha mahīrājo nṛpottamaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*karārthaṃ preṣayāmāsa svasainyaṃ ca mahāvatīm \|*  
*te vai lakṣaṃ mahāśūrāḥ sarvaśastrāstradhāriṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ūcuḥ parimalaṃ bhūpaṃ śṛṇu caṃdrakulodbhava \|*  
*sarve ca bhārate varṣe ye rājāno mahābalāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ṣaḍaṃśaṃ karamādāyāsmadrājāya dadaṃti vai \|*  
*bhavānkare hi tasyaiva yogyo bhavati sāṃpratam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*adyaprabhṛti cedrājñe tasmai dadyātkaraṃ na hi \|*  
*mahīrājasya raudrāstraiḥ kṣayaṃ yāsyati sainikaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ye bhūpā jayacaṃdrasya pakṣagāste hi tadbhayāt \|*  
*dadaṃte bhūmirājāya daṃḍaṃ tanmānasatkṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa nṛpatistasmai rājñe mahātmane \|*  
*karaṃ ṣaḍaṃśamādāya dadau prītisamanvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Suta said- At the start of the ninth year of his age, he was educated impatiently the sixty four kalas (arts) and proficiency in dharmasastras, because of which he became quite popular. О best of the race of Bhrgus, at that point of time, Prthviraja deputed his army to Mahavati for the collection of the land revenue. The immensely valorous soldiers who were a lakh in number said to the valorous king Parimala - “O king born in the lunar race, you kindly listen to our words. The powerful kings of the land of Bharata pay one eighth of the land revenue (or income) of their state to our king (Prthviraja). Now you also be competent enough to pay him the tax. Therefore, from today onwards, you shall have to pay the royal tax, failing which the warriors of Prthviraja would destroy you with their Raudrastras. This is why, all the rulers of the side of Jayacandra, feeling frightened, extend all the honour to Prthviraja.” Hearing this, the king Parimala pleasantly paid one sixth of the revenue of his kingdom to Prthviraja.

## \|\| 2.113.9-16 \|\|

*daśalakṣamitaṃ dravyaṃ gṛhītvā te samāyayuḥ \|*  
*mahīrājaḥ prasannātmā pūrvavairamapāharat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tadā te lakṣaśūrāśca kānyakubjamupāyayuḥ \|*  
*jayacaṃdraṃ tu natvocuḥ śṛṇu lakṣaṇakovida \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pṛthvīrājo mahārājo daṃḍaṃ tvattaḥ samicchati \|*  
*ityuktastairvaiṣṇavāstrī lakṣaṇastānuvāca ha \|\| 11 \|\|*

*maddeśe maṃḍalīkāśca bahavaḥ saṃti sāṃpratam \|*  
*bhūmirājo māṃḍaliko mayi jīvati mā bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ityuktvā vaiṣṇavāstraṃ tānkruddhaḥ sa ca samādadhat \|*  
*tadastrajvālataḥ sarve bhayabhītā pradudruvuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mahīrājastu tacchrutvā mahadbhayamupāgamat \|*  
*daśābdaṃ ca vayaḥ prāpte kṛṣṇāṃśe mallakovide \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nānāmallāḥ samājagmustena rājñaiva satkṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye sa kṛṣṇāṃśo bāhuśālī babhūva ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

*urvīyādhipateḥ putraḥ ṣoḍaśābdavayā balī \|*  
*śatamallaiśca sahitaḥ kadācitsa samāgataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

9-16. Carrying ten lakhs of wealth (gold coins), the soldiers left the place. Getting pleased, Prthviraja also disowned the old enmity. Thereafter, a lakh of soldiers reached the city of Kanyakubja and offering their salutation to the king of the place said to him- “O immensely learned monarch, the king Prthviraja has demanded tax from you.” On hearing these words, the king who possessed the vaisnavastra said to them- “I have several rulers of different mandalas serving me. But during my life time, Prthviraja could not achieve the position of a mandala monarch. Thereafter, in his utter rage, he was about to make use of the vaisnavastra, when the soldiers observing the terrific flame of the weapon, fled away from that place. On hearing this, Prthviraja also felt extremely panicky. At the age of ten years, Udayasimha attained mastery in the wrestling fight. At that point of time, several wrestlers assembled there. The king welcomed them all. With the assembling of the wrestlers there, Udayasimha appeared to be the strongest of all. Among the wrestlers, there was a wrestler of sixteen year’s age who was the son of Prthviraja, with a hundred of other wrestlers who accompanied him.

## \|\| 2.113.17-24 \|\|

*pitṛṣvasṛpatiṃ bhūpaṃ natvā nāmnā'bhayo balī \|*  
*uvāca śṛṇu bhūpāla kṛṣṇo'yaṃ madamattaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tena sārddhaṃ bhavenmallayuddhaṃ mama nṛpottama \|*  
*iti vajrasamaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā rājā bhayāturaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*uvāca śyālajaṃ premṇā bhavānyuddhaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭābdo'yaṃ sutaḥ snigdho mama prāṇasamo bhuvi \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kva bhavānvajrasadṛśaḥ kva suto'yaṃ sukomalaḥ \|*  
*anyairmallairmadīyaiśca sārddhaṃ yogyo bhavānraṇe \|\| 20 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā nṛpaḥ syālo mahīpatiriti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa tamāha ruṣāviṣṭo bālo'yaṃ balavattaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ bhūpa yathā jñāto mayā śiśuḥ \|*  
*āgaskṛtaṃ mahīrājaṃ matvā satilakaḥ sutam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*paṃḍitāṃśca samāhūya muhūrtaṃ pṛṣṭavānmudā \|*  
*gaṇeśo nāma matimāñjyotiśśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇaṃ vacanaṃ prāha mahīrājamanuttamam \|*  
*śivadattavaro rājankubera iva sāṃpratam \|\| 24 \|\|*

17-24. He said to the husband of his father’s sister- "O king, Krsna seems to be quite arrogant. My name too is Abhaya. О best of the humans, there should be a wrestling dual between him and myself. Listening to the vajra like words of the boy, the king said to him- “You are well-versed in the wrestling fight and my son is only eight years old. You are hard like vajra and he is only a tender boy. There are many other wrestlers here with me. You can display your proficiency with anyone else.” On hearing this, he said in anger- “This boy is extremely strong. I am speaking out the way I know this boy. You please listen. The king Tilaka, thinking his son to be a culprit, called for the learned Brahmanas and asked them to speak out a muhurta or auspicious time. At that point of time, Pandita Ganesa, who was an exceedingly learned person, started describing the symbols. He said- “The best of the son of Desaraja is quite suitable for him, who after receiving a boon from lord Siva, looks like Kubera. He is bom from the amsa of Sri Krsna. О king, there is no other person comparable with him on earth. I am repeatedly telling you the truth.”

## \|\| 2.113.25-30 \|\|

*kṛṣṇāṃśastasya yogyo'yaṃ deśarājasuto'varaḥ \|*  
*nānyo'sti bhūtale rājansatyaṃ satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tacchrutvā lakṣaṇo vīraḥ pūrve barhiṣmatīṃ prati \|*  
*kalpakṣetraṃ dakṣiṇe ca bhūmigrāmaṃ tu paścime \|\| 26 \|\|*

*uttare naimiṣāraṇyaṃ svakīyaṃ rāṣṭramādadhat \|*  
*ataḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kumāro'yaṃ kānyakubje mayā śrutaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nāgotsave ca bhūpāla paṃcamyāṃ ca nabhassite \|*  
*dṛśyamātraṃ kumārāṃgaṃ tasmādyogyo hyayaṃ sutaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa kṛṣṇāṃśo vākchareṇa prapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*abhayaṃ bhujayoḥ śīghraṃ gṛhītvā so'yudhadbalī \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kṣaṇamātraṃ raṇaṃ kṛtvā bhūmimadhye tamakṣipat \|*  
*abhayasya bhujo bhagnastatra jāto balena vai \|\| 30 \|\|*

25-30. Listening to him, the valorous Laksana established his kingdom comprising of Barhismati city in the north; Kalpaksetra in the south; Bhumigrama in the west; and upto Naimisaranya in the north. Therefore, I have heard that the prince of Kanyakubja is the best. О king, on the nagapancami day of the month of Sravana, the limbs of the princes become invisible. Therefore, the competent boy should have a fight with me on that particular day. Hearing the arrow like words, the king felt painful. Holding Abhaya by both the hands, he started fighting with him. In a moment, he held him and threw him on the ground. In the fight, the arm of Abhaya was broken.

## \|\| 2.113.31-37 \|\|

*mūrcchitaṃ svasutaṃ jñātvā khaḍgahasto mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*preṣayāmāsa tānmallānkṛṣṇāṃśasya prahāraṇe \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ruṣāviṣṭāṃśca tāñjñātvā kṛṣṇāṃśo balavattaraḥ \|*  
*tānekaikaṃ samākṣipya vijayī sa babhūva ha \|\| 32 \|\|*

*parājite mallabale khaḍgahasto mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*maraṇāya matiṃ cakre kṛṣṇāṃśasya prabhāvataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jñātvā tamīdṛśaṃ bhūpaṃ vārayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*abhayaṃ nīrujaṃ kṛtvā premṇā gehamavāsayat \|\| 34 \|\|*

*navābdāṃge ca kṛṣṇāṃśe cāhlādādyāḥ kumārakāḥ \|*  
*mṛgayārthe dadhuścittaṃ tamūcurbhūpatiṃ priyam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*namaste tāta bhūpāgrya sarvānaṃdapradāyaka \|*  
*asmabhyaṃ tvaṃ hayāndehi matpriyānkaruṇākara \|\| 36 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ tathetyuktvā mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*bhūtale vāsino'śvānvai divyānrāṭ caturo varān \|\| 37 \|\|*

31-37. Finding his son having been fainted, the king sent the wrestlers holding swords in their hands, for the killing of Krsnamsa. Finding the wrestlers in rage, Udayasimha held each one of them with force and threw them on the ground. Thus he became victorious. At the defeat of the wrestling warriors, the king hold a sword in his hand and thought of ending his own life from Udayasimha. When the king found them ready for ending their lives, he freed Abhaya. He along with the king were lovingly kept by him in his place. At the start of the new year, Udayasimha, Ahlada and other princes went to the forest for hunting. At the time of the departure, they said to the king- “O best lord of the earth, you are extremely compassionate and bestow delight to others. Therefore, you give me the loving horses. Accepting his words, four divine horses were given to the princes, which were born out of the womb of the mare named Harini.

## \|\| 2.113.38-39 \|\|

*dadau tebhyo mudā yukto hariṇīgarbhasaṃbhavān \|*  
*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tvanmukhena śrutaṃ sūta hariṇī vaḍavā yathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*bhīṣmasiṃhāya saṃprāptā śakrāddeveśato mune \|*  
*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmaḥ kuto jātāsturaṃgamāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. The Rsis said- The story in which the mare named Harini was received from Indra had been heard by us from you. Presently, we would like to know as to how were the horses given to the princes? These horses were decorated with divine ornaments and could move in the sky.

## \|\| 2.113.40-42 \|\|
