*divyāṃgā bhūṣaṇāpannā nabhassalilagāminaḥ \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*deśarājena bhūpena purā dharmayutena vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sevanaṃ bhāskarasyaiva kṛtaṃ ca dvādaśābdikam \|*  
*sevānte bhagavānsūryo varaṃ brūhi tamabravīt \|\| 41 \|\|*

*prāha deva namastubhyaṃ yadi deyo varastvayā \|*  
*hayaṃ divyamayaṃ dehi nabhasthalajalātigam \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Suta said - The religious-minded king Desaraja had in earlier times performed tapas for the Sungod continuously for twelve years. Then the Sungod, getting pleased with him, said to him- “You ask for a boon.” He replied saying- “O Deva, salutation to you. In case you are pleased with me, you give me a horse, who could move in the water of Akasa-Ganga.”

## \|\| 2.113.43-51 \|\|

*tathetyuktvā raviḥ sākṣāddadau tasmai papihakam \|*  
*lokānpāti papīrjñeyastasyedaṃ nāma cottamam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*ataḥ papīhako nāma lokapālanakarmavān \|*  
*sa hayo madamattaśca hariṇīṃ divyarūpiṇīm \|\| 44 \|\|*

*bubhuje smaravegena tasyāṃ jātāsturaṃgamāḥ \|*  
*manorathaśca pītāṃgaḥ karālaḥ kṛṣṇarūpakaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ekagarbhe samudbhūtau śaibyasugrīvakāṃśakau \|*  
*yasmindine samudbhūtau jiṣṇuviṣṇukalāṃśataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tadā jātau hariṇyāśca meghapuṣpabalāhakau \|*  
*bindulaśca suvarṇāṃgaḥ śvetāṃgo harināgaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*divyāṃgāste hi catvāraḥ pūrvaṃ jātā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*paścādaṃśāvatārāśca jātāsteṣāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra śṛṇu tatra kathāṃ śubhām \|*  
*bhūtale te hayāḥ sarve prāptāścoparibhūmigāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*devasiṃhāya baline dadau cāśvaṃ manoratham \|*  
*āhlādāya karālaṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃśāyaiva bindulam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*brahmānaṃdāya putrāya pradadau harināgaram \|*  
*te catvāro hayārūḍhā mṛgayārthaṃ vanaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

43-51. Accepting his request, the Sungod gave him a horse named Papiha who could fly in the sky. Thereafter, the horse named Papiha became lustful and was unable to control his passion. In that condition, he united with a mare named Harini, out of whose womb two colts of yellow and black colours were born. Both of them were twins. They were known to have been bom out of the amsa of Siva and Sugriva. Thereafter, from the amsas of Jisnu and Visnu and from the womb of the mare Harini, two mare colts known by the names of Meghapuspa and Balahaka were bom. One of them was believed to have gold like limbs and was known by the name of Bindula, while the one with white complexion was known by the name of Harinagara. These were the initial four horses. With the amsas of these horses, several other horses were bom. О Brahmana, thus I have spoken to you the story of their birth. Now you listen to the further story on the arrival of these horses on earth. The strong horse named Manoratha was given over to Devasimha, Ahlada (Alha) got the horse named Karala, Udayasimha got the horse named Bindula, while Brahmananda got the horse Harinagara. All the four princes, riding their own horses, proceeded to the forest for hunting.

## \|\| 2.113.52-55 \|\|

*hariṇīṃ vaḍavāṃ śubhrāṃ balakhāniḥ samāruhat \|*  
*tadanu prayayau vīro vanaṃ siṃhaniṣevitam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*āhlādenaiva śārdūlo hataḥ prāṇibhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*devasiṃhena siṃhaśca sūkaro balakhāninā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*brahmānaṃdena hariṇo hatastatra mahāvane \|*  
*mṛgāḥ śataṃ hatāstaiśca tāngṛhītvā gṛhaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare devī śāradā ca śubhānanā \|*  
*mṛgī svarṇamayī bhūtvā teṣāmagre pradhāvitā \|\| 55 \|\|*

52-55. Riding his own mare, Balkhana followed them. All of them reached the forest of lions. Ahlada hunted a tiger, which was quite dangerous for the life. Similarly, Devasimha hunted a lion, while Balakhana hunted a wild boar. Brahmananda on the other hand, hunted a stag. Thus the princes hunted hundreds of wild animals in the forest and carrying all of them with themselves, moved towards their abodes. At the same time, taking to the form of a golden deer, the goddess Sarada with a pleasant face started galloping before them.

## \|\| 2.113.56-62 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ mohitāḥ sarve svaiḥ svairbāṇairatāḍayan \|*  
*śarāstu saṃkṣayaṃ jagmurmṛgyaṃge balavattarāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*āhlādādyāśca te śūrā vismitāśca babhūvire \|*  
*tasminkāle sa kṛ्ṣṇāṃgo bāṇenaiva hyatāḍayat \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tadā ca pīḍitā devī bhayabhītā yayau vanam \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ krodhatāmrākṣastatpaścātprayayau balī \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vanāṃtaraṃ ca saṃprāpya devī dhṛtvā svakaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*tamuvāca prasannākṣī parīkṣā te mayā kṛtā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yadā te ca bhayaṃ bhūyāttadā tvaṃ māṃ sadā smara \|*  
*sādhayiṣyāmi te kāryaṃ kṛṣṇāṃśo hi bhavānvibhuḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*ityuktvāntarhitā devī śāradā sarvamaṃgalā \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśastu yayau gehaṃ taiśca sārddhaṃ mudā yutaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tadā parākramaṃ teṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā sukho'bhavat \|*  
*gṛhe gṛhe ca sarveṣāṃ lakṣmīrdevī samāviśat \|\| 62 \|\|*

56-62. At the sight of the doe, all the princes shot their arrows at her, but all the terrific arrows got destroyed after entering into the body of the doe. Observing that, Ahlada and other princes were extremely surprised. At the same time, Udayasimha attacked the doe with his arrow. Having been wounded and feeling painful with the wound, the goddess moved to the other forest. Thereafter, Udayasimha also, with his eyes getting red like copper, followed the doe. Reaching the other forest, the doe reverted to her original form. Then displaying a smile over her face, she said to him- “I have put you to test. Therefore, whenever you are in danger, you should always remember me. I shall bestow success on you, because you arc all pervading and have been born of the amsa of Sri Krsna.” Thus speaking, the goddess Sarvamangala disappeared from the scene. Thereafter, Udayasimha reached home with other princes. At that point of time, observing the bravery of the princes, the king felt delighted. The goddess Laksmi also started living in many of the houses in the city.

## Chapter 114. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.114.1-7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*daśābde ca vayaḥ prāpte viṣṇoḥ śaktyavatārake \|*  
*vasaṃtasamaye ramye yayuste pramadāvanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ūṣustatra vratācāre mādhave kṛṣṇavallabhe \|*  
*snātvā ca sāgare prātaḥ pūjayāmāsuraṃbikām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛtukālodbhavaiḥ puṣpairdhūpairdīpairvidhānataḥ \|*  
*japtvā saptaśatīstotraṃ dadhyuḥ sarvakarīṃ śivām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kaṃdamūlaphalāhārā jīvahiṃsāvivarjitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhaktiṃ samālokya māsāṃte jagadaṃbikā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dadau tebhyo varaṃ ramyaṃ tacchṛṇudhvaṃ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*āhlādāya suratvaṃ ca balatvaṃ balakhānaye \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kālajñatvaṃ ca devāya brahmajñatvaṃ nṛpāya ca \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśāyaiva yogatvaṃ dattvā cāṃtardadhe śivā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kṛtakṛtyāstadā te vai svagehaṃ punarāyayuḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ prāpte vare ramye malanā putramūrjitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta said - Udayasimha, who had been the incarnation of the sakti of lord Visnu, at the age of ten years, in the pleasant function of the spring season, feeling delightful, once went to the pleasure garden. Reaching there at the time of the spring season, which was the favourite of Sri Krsna, the people started of performing a vrata. Taking bath in the ocean in the early morning, they collected the seasonal flowers and fruits, besides incense and lamp and then adored the goddess Ambika there. Then all the boys recited the Durga-saptasati and started meditating on the goddess Parvati - the mother of the universe. They took fruits and roots alone in place of the food. Thus performing vrata and other religious rites in the forest, a month passed. During this period, their entire daily life met with a change. They were detached from the killing of animals etc. Getting pleased with their devotion, the mother of the universe bestowed them with a beautiful boon, which is going to be revealed by me. You listen to the same carefully. Ahlada got the divine status; Balakhana gets the enormous strength; Deva attained the far sight or the knowledge of future; Brahmananda got Brahmajhana or the knowledge of Brahman; and Udayasimha became well-versed in the yogic exercise. Thus bestowing all these qualities over the princes, the goddess disappeared from the scene. All the princes considered themselves individually successful and returned to their respective abodes. After receiving of the boons by the pleasant princes, the queen Malana gave birth to an illustrious son.

## \|\| 2.114.8-14 \|\|

*śyāmāṃgaṃ sātyakeraṃśaṃ suṣuve śubhalakṣaṇam \|*  
*sa jñeyo raṇajicchūro rājanyapriyakārakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*āṣāḍhe māsi saṃprāpte kṛṣṇāṃśo hayavāhanaḥ \|*  
*urvīyāṃ nagarīṃ prāpta ekākī nirbhayo valī \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā sa nagarīṃ ramyāṃ caturvarṇaniṣevitām \|*  
*dvijaśālāṃ yayau śūro dvijadhenuprapūjakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dattvā svarṇaṃ dvijātibhyaḥ saṃtarpya dvijadevatāḥ \|*  
*mahīpatigṛhaṃ ramyaṃ jagāma balavattaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*natvā sa mātulaṃ dhīmāṃstathānyāṃśca sabhāsadaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tadā nṛpājñayā śūrā baṃdhanāya samudyatāḥ \|*  
*khaṅgahastāḥ samājagmuryathā siṃhaṃ gajāḥ śaśāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mohitaṃ taṃ nṛpaṃ kṛtvā duṣṭabuddhirmahīpatiḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā lohamayaṃ jālaṃ tasyopari samādadheḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

8-14. Не was of dark complexion and of the amsa of Satyaki. He was brave, well-versed in the warfare, besides being the favourite of the rulers. Once in the month of asadha, riding his horse, Udayasimha reached the city of Urviya alone. Finding the fearless and beautiful city there where the people of all the four castes were living quite happily, he met with the Brahmanas in the home of the twice bom. He happened to be a great devotee of cows as well as the Brahmanas. Finding there the twice bom as Suvarna, pleasing the gods as well as the twice bom, he reached the charming palace of the king Bali. Offering salutation to his own maternal uncle and other courtiers with the permission of the king, all the warriors got ready to capture him. Ail of them holding swords in their hands pounced upon him, like an elephant attacking a lion. The king bringing the boy under the spell of mantras, made a net of wire and he himself was lodged over it.

## \|\| 2.114.15-27 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vīro bodhito devamāyayā \|*  
*āgaskṛtānripūñjñātvā khaṅgahastaḥ samāvadhīt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*hatvā paṃcaśataṃ śūro hayārūḍho mahābalī \|*  
*urvīyāṃ nagarīṃ prāpya jalapāne mano dadhau \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kūpe dṛṣṭvā śubhā nāryo ghaṭapūrtikarīstadā \|*  
*uvāca madhuro vākyaṃ dehi suṃdari me jalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tāḥ suṃdaraṃ rūpaṃ mohanāyopacakrire \|*  
*bhittvā tāsāṃ tu vai kumbhānpāyayitvā hayaṃ jalam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vanaṃ gatvā ripuṃ jitvā baddhvā tamubhayaṃ balī \|*  
*caṇḍikāpārśvamāgamya tadvadhāya mano dadhe \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śrutvā sa karuṇaṃ vākyaṃ tyaktvā svanagaraṃ yayau \|*  
*nṛpāṃtikamupāgamya varṇayāmāsa kāraṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śrutvā parimalo rājā dvijātibhyo dadau dhanam \|*  
*samāghrāya sa kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ kṛtakṛtyo'bhavannṛpaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*saṃprāptaikādaśadābde tu kṛṣṇāṃśe yuddhadurmade \|*  
*mahīpatirnirutsāhaḥ prayayau dehalīṃ prati \|\| 22 \|\|*

*baliṃ yathocitaṃ dattvā bhaginyai bhayakātaraḥ \|*  
*ruroda vahudhā duḥkhaṃ deśarājātmajaprajam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*agamā bhaginī tasya dṛṣṭvā bhrātaramāturam \|*  
*svapatiṃ varṇayāmāsa śrutvā rājābravīdidam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*adyāhaṃ svabalaiḥ sārddhaṃ gatvā tatra mahāvatīm \|*  
*haniṣyāmi mahāduṣṭaṃ deśarājasutaṃ ripum \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ityuktvā dhuṃdhukāraṃ ca samāhūya mahābalam \|*  
*sainyamājñāpayāmāsa saptalakṣaṃ tanutyajam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kecicchūrā hayārūḍhā uṣṭrārūḍhā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*gajārūḍhā rathārūḍhāḥ saṃyayuśca padātayaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

15-27. By about the same time, Devamaya - the goddess Sarada, made the boy conscious and alert him as a result of which the boy holding a sword in his hand, started facing the violent enemies. In a short time, he could destroy five hundred of his enemies alone. Thereafter, riding his own horse, the valorous boy entered the city of Urviya. Reaching there, he desired to have some eatables and drink. He went to a well and said to the beautiful damsels there - "O beautiful damsels, I need a little of water to drink.” All the damsels were attracted at the beauty of the boy and tried to entice him. But, breaking their pitchers, the boy made his horse to drink water. Then he went to the forest and overpowered his enemies. He captured all the enemies and produced them before the goddess Candika. Listening about this happening, the king Prthviraja came from his city to the place of Parimala and he narrated all the causes to him. On hearing that, the king Parimala donated riches to the twice born and then touched the head of Udayasimha and while so doing, he thought himself to be quite successful. At the time of the entry of the great warrior Udayasimha in the eleventh year, getting disgusted the king Prthviraja returned to Dehali. Getting disgusted with his own sister, he gave appropriate Bali (gift) to his sister feeling grieved for Udayasimha, the son of Desaraja cried a lot. Agama was the name of his sister. Finding her brother so upset, she communicated the cause of the same to her husband, who said- “I shall today itself go to Mahavati and kill Udayasimha - the wicked son of Desaraja.” Thus speaking, he commanded the great warrior Dhundhukara-“The seven lakh soldiers of my army always remain ready to sacrifice their lives. You decorate them at once. Some of the warriors were moving on horse backs, some ride over elephants and other on chariots. Besides the foot soldiers were also marching.

## \|\| 2.114.28-30 \|\|

*devasiṃhastu kālajñaḥ śrutvā cāgamanaṃ ripoḥ \|*  
*nṛpapārśvaṃ samāgamya sarvaṃ rājñe nyavedayat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śrutvā parimalo rājā vihvalo'bhūdbhayāturaḥ \|*  
*balakhānistamutthāya harṣayukta ivāha ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*adyāhaṃ ca mahīrājaṃ dhuṃdhukāraṃ sasainyakam \|*  
*jitvā daṃḍyaṃ ca bhavataḥ kariṣyāmi tavājñayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Earlier Devasimha had received the boon of having the farsight. Therefore, he could foresee the arrival of the enemy and going to the king, he narrated the entire situation to him, hearing which the king Parimala became upset and started getting frightened. Finding him so upset, Balakhana Simha, in a fit of delight, lifted him up and delightfully said- “I shall be victorious today over Prthviraja and his army besides Dhundhukara. At your command, I shall receive the royal taxes from them and turn them as your subjects for all times to come.”

## \|\| 2.114.31-35 \|\|

*ityuktvā taṃ namaskṛtya senāpatirabhūnmune \|*  
*tadā tu nirbhayā vīrā dṛṣṭvā rājānamāturam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*caturlakṣabalaiḥ sārddhaṃ te yuddhāya samāyayuḥ \|*  
*śiṃśapākhyaṃ vanaṃ ghoraṃ chedayitvā ripostadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ūṣustatra raṇe mattāḥ sarvaśatrubhayaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*etasminnantare tatra dhuṃdhukārādayo balā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kṛtvā kolāhalaṃ śabdaṃ yuddhāya samupāyayuḥ \|*  
*pūrvāhṇe tu bhṛguśreṣṭha sannaddhāste śataghnipāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śataghnībhistrisāhasraiḥ pañcasāhasrakā yayuḥ \|*  
*dvisahasraśataghnībhiḥ sahitā ścandravaṃśinaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

31-35. О sage, after thus speaking, he accepted to be the chief commander offering his salutation to the king. At the same time, all his valorous followers followed him. But the king still remained anxious. All the warriors who were four lakhs in number, collected and reached the battle ground hurriedly, where they cut off the simsapa (Asoka) trees in the forest of the enemy and started living there. At the same time, Dhundhu and other great warriors reached there creating huge noise. They started the war. О best of the race of Bhrgu, at the time of forenoon, getting ready, the warriors carried three thousand guns, five thousand of them started fighting themselves. Among them were the two thousand warriors of the lunar race, who fought with their guns.

## \|\| 2.114.36-41 \|\|

*sainyaṃ ṣaṣṭisahasraṃ ca svagarlokamupāyayau \|*  
*tadarddhaṃ ca tathā sainyaṃ mahīrājasya saṃkṣitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dudruvurbhīrukāḥ śūrā valakhānerdiśo daśa \|*  
*rathā rathai raṇe hanyurgajāścaiva gajaistathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*hayā hayaistathā uṣṭrā uṣṭrapaiśca samāhanan \|*  
*evaṃ sutumule jāte dāruṇe roma harṣaṇe \|\| 38 \|\|*

*hāhābhūtānsvakīyāṃśca sainyāndṛṣṭvā mahābalān \|*  
*aparāhṇe bhṛguśreṣṭha pañca śūrāḥ samāyayuḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*brahmānaṃdaḥ śaraiḥ śatrūnanayadyamasādanam \|*  
*devasiṃhastathā bhallairāhrādastatra tomaraiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*balakhāniḥ svakhaḍgena kṛṣṇāṃśastu tathaiva ca \|*  
*dvilakṣānkṣatriyāñjaghnuḥ sarvasainyaiḥ samaṃ tataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

36-41. In the terrific war, Parimala - the king of the lunar race, had an army of sixty thousand which arrived there at Dharmapuri. Half of that army was that of Prthviraja. Feeling disturbed, the warriors of Balakhana started fleeing here and there. The chariots fought with chariots, the elephants with elephants and the camels with camels were fighting the terrific war. О best of the race of Bhrgu, finding his own army defeated in the terrific war, the five warriors came together on the next day and entered the enemy army. Brahmananda started sending the enemy army soldiers to the abode of Yama. Similarly, Devasimha used spears, Ahlada used tomaras, Udayasimha and Balakhana used their swords. Similarly, Udayasimha also killed many of the warriors. Those valorous warriors destroyed two lakhs of the enemy army.

## \|\| 2.114.42-49 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā parājitaṃ sainyaṃ dhuṃdhukāro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*āhlādaṃ ca svabhallena gajārūḍhaḥ samāvadhīt \|\| 42 \|\|*

*āhlāde mūrcchite tatra devasiṃho mahābalaḥ \|*  
*bhallena bhrātaraṃ tasya daṃśayāmāsa vegataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sa tīkṣṇavraṇamāsādya gajasthaḥ saṃmumoha vai \|*  
*āgatāḥ śatarājāno nānādeśyā mahābalāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śastrāṇyastrāṇi teṣāṃ tu chittvā khaṅgena vatsajaḥ \|*  
*svakhaḍgena śirāṃsyeṣāṃ pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 45 \|\|*

*hate śatrusamūhe tu taccheṣāstu pradudruvuḥ \|*  
*mahīrājastu balavāndṛṣṭvā bhagnaṃ svasainyakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ājagāma gajārūḍhaḥ śivadattavaro balī \|*  
*raudreṇāstreṇa hṛdaye cāvadhīdvatsajaṃ ripum \|\| 47 \|\|*

*āhlādaṃ ca tathā vīraṃ devaṃ parimalātmajam \|*  
*mūrcchayitvā mahāvīrāñchatrusainyamupāgamat \|\| 48 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā śataghnīśca mahāvadhamakārayat \|*  
*ropaṇastvarito gatvā rājñe sarvamavarṇayat \|\| 49 \|\|*

42-49. At the same time, observing his army getting defeated, the valorous Dhundhukara attacked Ahlada with his spear while seated over the elephant back, which fainted him. When Ahlada was fainted, the valorous Devasimha attacked his brother with his spear with great force. As a result of this attack, a big wound was caused in his body, with the pain of which he fainted over the elephant itself and then fell down on the ground. At that point of time, hundreds of strong rulers who had arrived from various countries, their weapons were cut off by Balakhana quickly. He also cut off their heads which were scattered on the earth and whosoever escaped out of them, they fled away in panic. Finding his army being destroyed, Prthviraja who had received a boon from lord Siva, marched towards the battlefield mounted over an elephant. He wounded the heart of Balakhana with the Raudra weapon, together with Ahlada and the sons of Parimala. Making all these warriors unconscious, Prthviraja reached the enemy army. Worshipping the guns, he destroyed the enemy army there. Observing this sight, Ropana went to the king and apprised him of the factual position.

## \|\| 2.114.50-54 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vīraḥ sukhakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*kapotaṃ hayamāruhya nabhomārgeṇa cāgamat \|\| 50 \|\|*

*mūrcchayitvā mahīrājaṃ svabaṃdhūṃśca savāhanān \|*  
*kṛtvā nṛpāṃtamāgamya baṃdhanāya samudyataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tadotthāya mahīrājo mahādevena bodhitaḥ \|*  
*punastānsvaśarai raudrairmūrcchayāmāsa kopavān \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sukhakhānyādikāñchūrānsaṃbadhya nigaḍairdṛḍhaiḥ \|*  
*nṛpaṃ parimalaṃ prāpya punaryuddhamacīkarat \|\| 53 \|\|*

*hāhābhūtaṃ svasainyaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sa udayo hariḥ \|*  
*nabhomārge hayaṃ kṛtvā tāḥ śatadhnīranāśayat \|\| 54 \|\|*

50-54. In the mean time, mounting over his horse named Kapota, Sukhakhani reached the battle ground through the skyway and made Prthviraja unconscious. Then together with his brothers, he reached before Prthviraja in order to put him in bondage, but Prthviraja got consciousness by the grace of lord Siva and he cast a swoon with the use of his Rudrastra over Sukhakhani and other warriors and bound them with chains and carried them to the king Parimala. The war started again. At that point of time, finding his army crying, Udayasimha mounted over his horse and reached there through the sky way and destroyed the guns and the army totally.

## \|\| 2.114.55-61 \|\|

*mahīrājagajaṃ prāpya baddhvā taṃ nigaḍairbalo \|*  
*āhlādapārśvamāgamya bhrātre bhūpaṃ samarpayat \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tadā tu pṛthivīrājo lajjitastena nirjitaḥ \|*  
*pañcakoṭidhanaṃ dattvā svagehaṃ punarāyayau \|\| 56 \|\|*

*devasiṃhājñayā śūro balakhānirhi vatsajaḥ \|*  
*tairdravyairnagarīṃ ramyāṃ kārayāmāsa sundarīm \|\| 57 \|\|*

*śirīṣākhyaṃ puraṃ nāma tena vīreṇa vai kṛtam \|*  
*sarvavarṇasamāyuktaṃ dvikrośāyāmasaṃmitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tatraiva nyavasadvīro vatsajaḥ svakulaiḥ saha \|*  
*triṃśatkośe kṛtaṃ rāṣṭraṃ tatraiva balakhāninā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*śrutvā parimalo rājā tatrāgatya mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*āghrāya vatsajaṃ śūraṃ deśarājasutaṃ tathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*brahmānaṃdena sahitaḥ svagehaṃ punarāyayau \|\| 61 \|\|*

55-61. Then reaching near the elephant of Prthviraja, the valorous warrior imprisoned him and bound him with chains and fetters and then handed over Prthviraja to Ahlada. At that point of time, Prthviraja felt immensely ashamed at his feet. He then gave away five crores of wealth as present to Ahlada and went back to his abode. At that point of time, with the command of Devasimha, Balakhana - the son of Vatsaraja, established a beautiful city with the wealth so received by him from Prthviraja. The said city was given the name of Siris'a or Sirsa. The people of all the castes were lodged in the same, which was spread into an area of two krosas. While living in the same city with his family, Balakhana spread his kingdom to thirty krosas. On hearing this, the king Parimala was extremely delighted. He arrived there with Udayasimha and smelling his head, returned to his capital city with Brahmananda.

## Chapter 115

## \|\| 2.115.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dvādaśābde hi kṛṣṇāṃśe yathājātaṃ tathā śṛṇu \|*  
*iṣaśukladaśamyāṃ ca rājñāṃ jātaḥ samāgamaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kānyakubje mahāramye nānābhūpāḥ samāyayuḥ \|*  
*śrutvā parājayaṃ rājño mahīrājasya lakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśadarśane vāṃchā tasya cāsīttadā mune \|*  
*pitṛvyaṃ bhūpatiṃ prāha draṣṭuṃ yāsyāmi taṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*jito yena mahīrājaḥ sarvalokaprapūjitaḥ \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya jayacaṃdro mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*bhrātṛjaṃ praṇataṃ prāha śṛṇu śuklayaśaskara \|\| 4 \|\|*

*rājarājapadaṃ te hi kathaṃ saṃhartumicchasi \|*  
*ityuktvā jayacaṃdrastu tadājñāṃ naiva dattavān \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said- Whatever happened in the twelfth year of the age of Udayasimha, the same is being repeated by me. You please listen. Learning about the defeat of Prthviraja, Laksana developed a desire to have a meeting with Udayasimha. In the city of Kenyakubja, on the bright tenth lunar day of the month of Asvina, a large number of rulers assembled at Kanyakubja. Then he said to his uncle Jayacandra - "I would like to go and meet Udayasimha, who had defeated Prthviraja. On hearing this, the king Jayacandra said to the humble nephew Laksana - “You are holding the position of the king of kings. Then why do you intend to destroy that position (by going to meet Udayasimha)?” Thus speaking, he did not permit him to go.

## \|\| 2.115.6-8 \|\|

*rājānaste ca sahitāḥ svasainyaiḥ parivāritāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ draṣṭumicchantaḥ saṃyayuśca mahīpatim \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śirīṣākhyapurasthaṃ ca jñātvā kṛṣṇāṃśamuttamam \|*  
*mahīpatiṃ puraskṛtya samājagmurnṛpāstadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dadṛśustaṃ mahātmānaṃ puṃḍarīkanibhānanam \|*  
*prasannavadanāḥ sarve praśaśaṃsuḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Though all other rulers went to meet him including the lord of Earth. In the city of Sirisapura, under the leadership of Mahipati, they met Udayasimha. The face of Udayasimha appeared beautiful like the blossoming lotus flowers, observing which all the rulers started praising him from all the sides, with delight.

## \|\| 2.115.9-14 \|\|

*tadā mahīpatiḥ kruddho vacanaṃ prāha bhūpatīn \|*  
*yasyeyaṃ ca kṛtā ślāghā yuṣmābhirdūravāsibhiḥ \|*  
*pitarau tasya balinau māhiṣmatyāṃ mṛtiṃ gatau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jambuko nāma bhūpālo nārmadīyaiḥ samanvitaḥ \|*  
*baddhvā tau prayayau gehaṃ luṃṭhayitvā dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*śilāpatre samāropya tayorgātramacūrṇayat \|*  
*śirasī ca tayośchittvā vaṭavṛkṣe samāruhat \|\| 10 \|\|*

*adyāpi tau sthitau vīrau hā putreti prabhāṣiṇau \|*  
*pretadehe ca pitarau yasya prāpto mahābalo \|*  
*tasyodayo vṛthā jñeyo vṛthākīrtiḥ priyaṃkarī \|\| 11 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa kṛṣṇāṃśo bhūpatīnprāha namradhīḥ \|*  
*gatau matpitarau sārddhaṃ gurjare yatra vai raṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mlecchairnarāśanaiḥ sārddhaṃ tannṛpeṇa raṇo'bhavat \|*  
*deśarājo vatsarājo yuddhaṃ kṛtvā bhayaṃkaram \|*  
*mlecchaistaiśca hatau tatra śruteyaṃ viśrutā kathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mātulenādya kathitaṃ navīnaṃ maraṇaṃ tayoḥ \|*  
*cetsatyaṃ vacanaṃ tasya pauruṣaṃ mama paśyata \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. Listening to the praise of Udayasimha, Mahipati said to all the rulers who had assembled there- “Having arrived here from far off places, the person who is being praised by you his father met with his end at Mahismati city. A king named Jambuka of that place together with his warriors, living over the banks of Narmada, arrived there and held him in bondage and plundered all his wealth and proceeded to his place, where his body was pounded in the grinding machine and his head is still hanging in the banyan tree there, still feeling painful. Therefore, his uplift is of no use and his glory will be destroyed.” On hearing this, Udayasimha spoke quite humbly there - “My father had gone to Gurjaradesa, where the war was fought. The war was started by the king of Gujarata with the man-eater Mlecchas. Both Desaraja and Vatsaraja were killed by the Mlecchas while fighting there. This is what has been heard by me. But my maternal uncle has projected new version of the death of my father. In case the words spoken by him are true, then you would witness my strength without delay.”

## \|\| 2.115.15-26 \|\|

*ityuktvā tānsa kṛṣṇāṃśo mātaraṃ prāha satvaram \|*  
*hetuṃ ca varṇayāmāsa bhāṣitaṃ ca mahīpateḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śrutvā vajrasamaṃ vākyaṃ ruroda jananī tadā \|*  
*nottaraṃ pradadau mātā pati duḥkhena duḥkhitā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*jñātvā pitṛvadhaṃ śrutvā jambukaṃ śivakiṃkaram \|*  
*manasā sa ca kṛṣṇāṃśastuṣṭāva parameśvarīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jaya jaya jaya jagadamba bhavāni hyakhilalokasurapitṛmunikhāni \|*  
*tvayā tataṃ sacarācarameva viśvaṃ pātamidaṃ hṛtameva \|\| 18 \|\|*

*iti dhyātvā sa kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ suṣvāpa nijasa dmani \|*  
*tadā bhagavatī tuṣṭā tālanaṃ balavattaram \|*  
*mohayitvāśu tatpārśve preṣayāmāsa sarvagā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*caturlakṣabalaiḥ sārddhaṃ tālanaḥ śīghramāgataḥ \|*  
*svasainyaṃ codayāmāsa caikalakṣaṃ mahābalam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*balakhānistadā prāptaścaikalakṣabalānvitaḥ \|*  
*anujaṃ tatra saṃsthāpya śirīṣākhye mahābalaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sajjībhūtānsamālokya tānudyāne sasainyakān \|*  
*bhītaḥ parimalo rājā kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ prati cāyayau \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vihvalaṃ nṛpamālokya kṛṣṇāṃśo'śvāsayanmudā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*lakṣasainyaṃ tadīyaṃ ca gṛhītvā cādhipo'bhavat \|*  
*śataghnyaḥ paṃcasāhasrā nānāvarṇāḥ suvāhanāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*patākāḥ pañcasāhasrāḥ sāhasraṃ kāṣṭhakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*gajā daśasahasrāśca rathāḥ paṃcasahasrakāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*trilakṣāśca hayāḥ sarve uṣṭrā daśasahasrakāḥ \|*  
*śeṣāḥ padātayo jñeyāsta sminsainye bhayānake \|\| 26 \|\|*

15-26. Thus speaking in the assembly, Udayasimha went to his mother and he wanted her to speak truthfully about the words uttered by Mahipati. But learning the vajra like words of her son, the mother having been filled with the grief of the death of her husband, spoke nothing. Thereafter, Udayasimha came to know the truth about the death of his father and Jambuka being a great devotee of Siva, and he started reciting mentally the name of the goddess Durga. He said- “Victory again and again to Durga - the mother of the universe. You are the creator, sustainer and the destroyer of the mobile and immobile creatures of the world.” Thus mentally adoring her, Udayasimha went to sleep over his bed. At the same time, the goddess getting pleased, confused the valorous Talana and sent him to Udayasimha, who at once reached there with four lakhs of his army. Balakhana also reached there with a lakh of his army, placing the capital city under the guard of his younger brother. Finding the assemblage of the army in his own garden, Parimala got frightened and reached before Udayasimha. Finding him so upset, Udayasimha assured him. He also took over the responsibility to lead a lakh of the warriors of his army. The army which collected there, had five thousand guns, various types of vehicles, five thousand of flags, a thousand of carpenters, ten thousand elephants, five thousand chariots, three lakhs of horses and the rest were the foot soldiers.

## \|\| 2.115.27-33 \|\|

*tālanaśca samāyātaḥ sarvasenādhipo'bhavat \|*  
*devasiṃho rathānāṃ ca sarveṣāmīśvaro'bhavat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*balakhānirhayānāṃ ca sarveṣāmadhipo'bhavat \|*  
*āhlādaśca gajānāṃ ca sarveṣāmadhipo'bhavat \|*  
*pattīnāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ kṛṣṇāṃśaścādhipo'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*natvā te malanāṃ bhūpo dattvā dānānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*samāyayuśca te sarve dakṣiṇāśāṃ balānvitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pakṣamātragataḥ kālo mārge tasminraṇaiṣiṇām \|*  
*chittvā tatra vanaṃ ghoraṃ nānākaṃṭakasaṃyutam \|*  
*senāṃ nivāsayāmāsurnirbhayāste mahābalāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*devasiṃhamatenaiva yoginaste tadābhavan \|*  
*nartakaścaiva kṛṣṇāṃśaścāhlādo ḍamarupriyaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*maḍḍudhārī tadā devo vīṇādhārī ca tālanaḥ \|*  
*vatsajaḥ kāṃsyadhārī ca balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*māturagre sthitāste vai nanṛtuḥ premavihvalāḥ \|*  
*mohitā devakī cāsīnna jñātaṃ tatra kāraṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

27-33. Talana was made to command the entire army. Similarly, Devasimha took over the command of the army of chariots. Besides this, Balakhana was the leader of the cavalry men, Ahlada was the leader of elephants, while the foot soldiers were placed under the charge of Udayasimha. Before departure, all the brothers touched the feet of the queen Malana and also gave enormous riches in charity. All of them marched on towards the southern direction. Desirous of waging a war, the army spent a fortnight in the journey. Thereafter, they reached the desired place and cleared the forest of wild growth and the thorny bushes which were spread there. The army was then made to camp there. Then at the command of Devasimha, all the brothers took to the form of yogis. Udayasimha could dance, damaru was to be played by Ahlada, cymbal by Devasimha, vina by Talana, bronze balls and cymbals by Balakhana - the son of Vatsa. All of them then started dancing with delight before their mother, observing which Devaki was fascinated, but she could not know the reason for the same.

## \|\| 2.115.34-38 \|\|

*mohitāṃ mātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ harṣamupāyayuḥ \|*  
*tadā tāṃ kathayāmāsurvayaṃ te tanayā hi bhoḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*natvā tāṃ prayayuḥ sarve purīṃ māhiṣmatīṃ śubhām \|*  
*nagaraṃ mohayāmāsurvādyagānaviśāradāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dūtyā sārddhaṃ riporgehaṃ yayuste kāryatatparāḥ \|*  
*nṛtyagānasuvādyaiśca rājñaste mohane ratāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*visaṃjñāṃ mahiṣīṃ kṛtvā kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ sarvamohanaḥ \|*  
*prāptavāṃstatra yatrāsau tatsutā vijayaiṣiṇī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā sā suṃdaraṃ rūpaṃ śyāmāṃgaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*mumoha vaśamāpannā maithunārthaṃ samudyatā \|\| 38 \|\|*

34-38. Finding their mother getting fascinated, all of them felt delighted. Then they said to their mother- “O mother, we are all your sons.” Then offering salutation to her, all the princes reached the city of Mahismati and started attracting the people of the town with their dance and music. With the help of a female messenger, all the princes reached the palace of the enemy. All of them fascinated the entire royal court with their dance and music. On the other hand, Udayasimha fascinated the chief queen extremely who lost her consciousness. Thereafter, he reached the place where the princess Vijaya was lodged. She witnessed the dark complexioned and beautiful appearance. The princess was so overpowered with passion that discharging all the shame, she got prepared to have a union with him.

## \|\| 2.115.39-43 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tathā gatāṃ nārīṃ kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ ślakṣṇayā girā \|*  
*śatrorbhedaṃ ca papraccha kāminīṃ madavihvalām \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sāha bho devakīputra yadi pāṇiṃ grahīṣyasi \|*  
*tarhi te kathayiṣyāmi piturbhedaṃ hi dāruṇam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tathetyuktvā sa balavāṃstasyāḥ pāṇiṃ gṛhītavān \|*  
*jñātvā bhedaṃ ripoḥ sarvaṃ tāmāśvāsya yayau mudā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*etasminnantare rājñī bādhitā prāha yoginam \|*  
*deśarājapriyāhāraṃ navalakṣasya mūlyakam \|*  
*tubhyaṃ dāsyāmi saṃtuṣṭā nṛtyagānavimohitā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vatsasutastāṃ praśasya gṛhītavān \|*  
*prayayau baṃdhubhiḥ sārddhaṃ jambūko yatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 43 \|\|*

39-43. Finding that the princess had been so fascinated with his beauty, he asked her to reveal the secret method to defeat the enemy. At this, she said- “O son of Devaki, in case you holding my hand take an oath to own me, then I can reveal the harsh secrets of my father.” Then holding her hand, Udayasimha accepted her condition and learnt all the secrets of the enemy. Then he assured her. Thereafter, he delightfully returned to his place. By about the same time, having been overpowered with love, the queen said to the yogi- “I am extremely happy with your dance, therefore, I am giving the naulakha garland of the queen of Desaraja. On hearing this, Balakhana - the son of Vatsa, immensely praised the queen and accepted the gift quite gracefully. Thereafter, he accompanied with all his associates, reached the palace of the king Jambuka.

## \|\| 2.115.44-51 \|\|

*nanarta tatra kṛṣṇāṃśo balakhāniragāyata \|*  
*āhlādastālano devo dadhmurvādyagatīrmudā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*mohito'bhūnnṛpastatra kāliyaḥ svajanaiḥ saha \|*  
*kāmaṃ varaya kṛṣṇāṃga yacca te hṛdaye sthitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vacaḥ śatrorbalakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*tamāha bho mahīpāla lakṣāvartirvarāṃganā \|*  
*svavidyāṃ darśayenmahyaṃ tadā tṛptiṃ vrajāmyaham \|\| 46 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tathā matvā lakṣāvartiṃ nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*sabhāyāṃ nartayāmāsa deśarājapriyāṃ tathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*sā veśyā sutamāhlādaṃ jñātvā yogitvamāgatam \|*  
*ruroda tatra duḥkhārtā netrādaśrūṇi muṃcatī \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ruditāṃ tāṃ samālokya rudannāhlāda eva saḥ \|*  
*svabhujau tāḍayāmāsa tatpriyārthe mahābalaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśastatra taṃ hāraṃ tasyāḥ kaṃṭhe pradattavān \|*  
*uvāca krodhatāmrākṣastāmāśvāsya punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ahaṃ codayasiṃho'yaṃ piturvairārthamāgataḥ \|*  
*haniṣyāmi ripuṃ bhūpaṃ sātmajaṃ sabalaṃ tathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

44-51. Reaching there, Udayasimha started dancing while Balakhana started singing. The rest played on other musical instruments. With all his relatives, Kaliya was also present there, who said to Udayasimha- “O king, you ask for the thing you desire.” Hearing the words of the enemy, Balakhana said- “O king, in case the whore named Laksavati displays her art, then I shall feel extremely pleased.” On hearing this, the king commanded Laksavati dancer to perform in the court, though she was the beloved of Desaraja. Finding her son Ahlada in the form of a yogi, the stream of tears started flowing from her eyes. She started crying. Finding his mother so crying, Ahlada also started putting his arms. On the other hand, Udayasimha adorned his neck with the valuable garland. Then the enraged Ahlada with his red eyes said- “With Udayasimha I have arrived here in order to take revenge for our father. Therefore, I shall surely kill the enemy king with his family.”

## \|\| 2.115.52-55 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacastasya kāliyo balavattaraḥ \|*  
*piturājñāṃ puraskṛtya śatavyūhasamanvitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ ca baṃdhanāyaiva kapāṭaṃ samaruddha saḥ \|*  
*tāñchatrūnsamanujñāya pāśahastānsaśastragān \|\| 53 \|\|*

*svaṃsvaṃ khaḍgaṃ samākṛṣya kṣatriyāste samāghnata \|*  
*śataśūre hate taiśca kāliyo bhayakātaraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tyaktvā tātaṃ pradudrāva te tu gehādbahiryayuḥ \|*  
*svasainyaṃ śīghramāsādya yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*śibirāṇi kṛtānyeva narmadākūlamāsthitaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

52-55. On hearing these words, the valorous Kaliya, at the command of his father, in order to capture the people of the enemy side, ordered all the gates to be closed. Finding the armed force of the king having reached there in the front, all the K$atriya warriors entered the place and started killing the royal soldiers. With the falling of a hundred strong enemy army, Kaliya got frightened and fled away from that place, leaving his father alone. Ahlada and other Ksatriya warriors also fled away from that palace. They swiftly reorganized their army and got ready for waging the war. They had set up their camps over the banks of the river Narmada.

## \|\| 2.115.56-62 \|\|

*kṛtvā tu narmadāsetuṃ nalvamātraṃ supuṣṭidam \|*  
*svasainyaṃ tārayāmāsa caturaṃgasamanvitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*rurodha nagarīṃ sarvāṃ balakhānirbalairyutaḥ \|*  
*śataghnīragrataḥ kṛtvā mahāśabdakarīstadā \|*  
*māhiṣmatyāśca harmyāṇi pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 57 \|\|*

*narāśca svakulaiḥ sārddhaṃ mukhyadravyasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*viṃdhyādreśca guhāṃ prāpya tatroṣurbhayakātarāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kāliyastu gajānīke paṃcaśabdagaje sthitaḥ \|*  
*hastipā daśasāhasrā yuddhāya samupāyayuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tasyānujaḥ sūryavarmā trilakṣaisturagairyutaḥ \|*  
*tuṃdilaśca rathaiḥ sārddhaṃ rathasthaśca sahasrakaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*raṃkaṇo vaṃkaṇaścobhau caturlakṣapadātibhiḥ \|*  
*jagmatustau mahāmlecchau mlecchabhūpasahasrakaiḥ \|*  
*dākṣiṇātyagrāmapāste tau puraskṛtya saṃyayuḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ubhe sene samāsādya yuddhāya samupasthite \|*  
*tayośca tumulayuddhamabhavallomaharṣaṇam \|\| 62 \|\|*

56-62. Thereafter, making a strong bridge, they carried the army to the other bank of Narmada. The great warriors like Balakhana and others surrounded the town of Mahi$mati from all the sides and started thundering aloud. They razed to the ground the high mansions of the palaces as well as canopies etc. Getting frightened, the people of the town took refuge in the mountain caves together with their valuables. Surrounded by the army of elephants, Kaliya was mounted over the huge elephant named Pancasabda and marched towards the battle ground with ten thousand elephant riders, his younger brother Suryavarma commanding three lakhs of cavalry men, besides Tundila leading a thousand chariots, four lakh soldiers of Mleccha army, besides a thousand of Mleccha rulers and two Mleccha commanders leading the Mleccha army marched towards the battleground. Both the armies started fighting terrific battle in the battleground.

## \|\| 2.115.63-66 \|\|

*triyāme rudhiraisteṣāṃ nadī prāvartata drutam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāsrajāṃ nadīṃ ghorāṃ māṃsakardamavāhinīm \|*  
*balakhānirameyātmā khaṅgapāṇirnaro yayau \|\| 63 \|\|*

*bhallahastastadā devo manorathahaye sthitaḥ \|*  
*biṃdulasthaśca kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ khaṅgenaiva ripūnahan \|\| 64 \|\|*

*āhlādaśca gadāhastaḥ pothayāmāsa vāhinīm \|*  
*rūpaṇo nāma śūdraśca śaktihastonyahanripūn \|*  
*tālano hastanistriṃśo māhiṣmatyāṃ hananyayau \|\| 65 \|\|*

*evaṃ mahābhaye jāte raṇe tasminmahābale \|*  
*dudruvuḥ sarvato vīrāḥ pāhipāhītyathābruvan \|\| 66 \|\|*

63-66. In the war lasting for three praharas, the river of blood started flowing in which the flesh flowed like the mud, observing which Balakhana held a sword in his hand, Devasimha hold a spear riding over the horse. Manoratha was riding over the Bindula horse, Udayasimha held the sword, Ahlada held a club, Rupana held a sakti, while Talana hold a sword. Destroying the enemy army, all of them entered the city of Mahismati. In the terrific war of the great warriors, the valorous soldiers fled away in panic here and there.

## \|\| 2.115.67-73 \|\|

*prabhagnaṃ svabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāliyo balakhānikam \|*  
*gajasthastāḍayāmāsa svabāṇaistaṃ mahābalaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*hariṇī vaḍavā tasya jñātvā svāminamāturam \|*  
*gajopari samāsthāya svapādaistamapātayat \|\| 68 \|\|*

*patite kāliye vīre paṃcaśabdo mahāgajaḥ \|*  
*śṛṃkhalaistāḍayāmāsa śūrāṃstānmadamattakān \|\| 69 \|\|*

*mūrcchite paṃcaśūre tu rūpaṇo bhayakātaraḥ \|*  
*devakīṃ varṇayāmāsa yathājātaṃ gajena vai \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tadā tu duḥkhitā devī dolāmāruhya satvarā \|*  
*taṃ gajaṃ ca samāsādya varṇayāmāsa kāraṇam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*gajarāja namastubhyaṃ śakradatta mahābala \|*  
*ete putrāstu te vīra pālanīyā yathā pituḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā divyagajo devamāyāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*devakīṃ śaraṇaṃ prāpya kṣamasvāgaskṛtaṃ mama \|\| 73 \|\|*

67-73. Finding his army getting shattered, Kaliya while mounted over the elephant, attacked Balakhana with his arrows. Thereafter, his mare named Harini, finding her master getting upset, reached the enemy elephant and hit it with her hand leg making it to fall on the ground. At the fall of the valorous Kaliya, using the iron chain, the elephant named Pancasabda made the five brothers to faint by striking them with the same. At the fainting of all the five warriors, Rupana atonce rushed to Devaki. Getting painful at the hearing of the news, she reached there by a palanquin and explained to the king elephant, the reason for the same in detail—“The elephant king who was quite forceful and given by Saka, salutation to you. You must protect the valorous warriors, like a father.” Hearing this, the divine elephant reached and took refuge with Devaki and started begging forgiveness for his sin.

## \|\| 2.115.74-82 \|\|

*ityukte gajarāje tu kṛṣṇāṃśo balavattaraḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā mūrcchāṃ yayau tatra yatrāhlādaśca mūrcchitaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tamutthāpya karasparśairbalakhānisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*piturgajaṃ mahāmattamāhlādāya pradattavān \|*  
*karāla mandaṃ smitaṃ rūpaṇāya tadā dadau \|\| 75 \|\|*

*mūrcchitaṃ kāliyaṃ śatruṃ baddhvā sa nigaḍairdṛḍhaiḥ \|*  
*senāntaṃ preṣayāmāsa balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*sūryavarmā tadā jñātvā baddhaṃ baṃdhuṃ ca kāliyam \|*  
*prayayau śatrusenāntaṃ krodhena sphuritādharaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tamāyāntaṃ samālokya te vīrā yuddhadurmadāḥ \|*  
*rathasthaṃ maṃḍalīkṛtya svasvamastraṃ samākṣipan \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kuṃṭhite'stre tadā teṣāṃ vismitāste'bhavanmune \|*  
*cintāṃ ca mahatīṃ prāptāḥ kathaṃ vadhyo bhavedayam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tasyāstraiste mahāvīrā vraṇārtibhayapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā yuddhaṃ punargatvā raṇaṃ cakruḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*evaṃ kati dinānyeva babhūva raṇa uttamaḥ \|*  
*āhlādo vatsajo devastālano bhayasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmustena vīreṇa mohitāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇastu taṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā devīṃ viśvavimohinīm \|*  
*tuṣṭāva manasā vīro rātrisūktaṃ paṭhanhṛdi \|\| 82 \|\|*

74-82. At the same time, getting consciousness, the powerful Udayasimha reached before Ahlada and made him regain his consciousness with the touch of his trunk. Thereafter, together with Balakhana, his own father’s elephant was given over to Ahlada. The divine horse named Karala was also given over to Rupana. Thereafter, the fainted enemy Kaliya was put in bondage with handcuffs and was handed over to his army by. Balakhana. When Suryavarma came to know that his brother was in chain, then with the fluttering of his lips, he rapidly entered the enemy army. Finding his entry in the army, the terrific warrior while seated in the chariot, found that he was surrounded from all the sides and he was attacked with all the weapons. But he could not be hurt with any one of the weapons, and therefore finding that their weapons were unfructuous on him, they felt surprised and worried as well thinking about the ways to kill him. On the other hand, they got wounded with the weapons shot by them. Getting wounded, they started fleeing from the battleground, but soon returned and started fighting again. The war continued for many days. Thereafter, Ahlada, Balakhana, Devasimha, Talana and other warriors were frightened and confused. All of them took refuge with Udayasimha. Finding them so upset, Udayasiimha mentally adored the goddess, who confused the universe. He started reciting Ratri-sakta in his mind.

## \|\| 2.115.83-90 \|\|

*tadā tuṣṭā jagaddhātrī durgā durgārtināśinī \|*  
*mohayitvā tu taṃ vīraṃ tatraivāṃtaradhīyataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*nidrayā mohitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāṃśastu mahābalaḥ \|*  
*babaṃdha nigaḍaistaṃ ca devakyante samāgamat \|\| 84 \|\|*

*tuṃdilaśca tathā jñātvā bhātṛśokapariplutaḥ \|*  
*ājagāma hayārūḍhaḥ khaṅgahasto mahābalaḥ \|*  
*ripusainyasya madhye tu bahuśūrānatāḍayat \|\| 85 \|\|*

*māhiṣmatyāśca te śūrā raṃkaṇena samanvitāḥ \|*  
*tatsainyaṃ bhañjayāmāsustālanena prapālitam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*pradrutaṃ svaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā tālanaḥ parighāyudhaḥ \|*  
*śirāṃsi pothayāmāsa mlecchānāṃ ca pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 87 \|\|*

*vaṃkaṇaṃ ca tathā hatvā khaḍgenaiva ca raṃkaṇam \|*  
*tuṃdilaṃ ca tathā baddhvā dinānte śibiraṃ yayau \|\| 88 \|\|*

*kāliye ca ripau baddhe subaddhe sūryavarmaṇi \|*  
*tuṃdile ca tathā baddhe raṃkaṇe vaṃkaṇe hate \|\| 89 \|\|*

*sahasraṃ mleccharājāno hataśeṣā balānvitāḥ \|*  
*pakṣamātramahorātraṃ yuddhaṃ cakruḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

83-90. At that point of time, the goddess Durga who removes all the troubles like a fort, getting pleased, confused Suryavarma and disappeared from the scene. The valorous Udayasimha finding him overpowered with sleep, bound him with handcuffs and fetters, and produced her before Devaki. On receiving this information, Tundila getting upset because of the bondage of his brother, rushed towards the enemy army, holding a sword in his hand. Reaching there, he started killing the enemy warriors. In the meantime, a warrior named Rankana started destroying the army of Talana. At the sight of his fleeing army, Talana severed the heads of Mlecchas with his parigha, felling them over the ground. Thereafter, killing Rankana and Vankana, and putting Tundila in bondage, he reached his camp in the evening time. With the bondage of Kaliya, Suryavarma and Tundila, and the killing of Rankana and Vankana, all the Mlecchas who were thousands in number, kept on fighting throughout the day and night. They were thousands in number and they stayed there with their army for a fortnight, fighting day and night.

## \|\| 2.115.91-101 \|\|

*pratyahaṃ tālano vīraḥ senāpatiramarṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiṃ bhūpāñjaghānāśu śatrusainyabhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*bhayabhītā ripoḥ śūrā hatā bhūpā hataujasaḥ \|*  
*hataśeṣā yayurgehamarddhasainyā bhayāturāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*jambukastu tathā śrutvā duḥkhito gehamāyayau \|*  
*vrataṃ hyanaśanaṃ kṛtvā rātrau śocannaśeta saḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*niśīthe samanuprāpte tatsutā vijayaiṣiṇī \|*  
*pūrṇā tu sā kalā jñeyā rādhāyā vrajavāsinī \|\| 94 \|\|*

*āśvāsya pitaraṃ taṃ ca yayau māyāviśāradā \|*  
*rakṣakāñchivirāṇāṃ ca mohayitvā samāyayau \|\| 95 \|\|*

*bhrātaro tatra gatvāsau yatra sarvānabodhayat \|*  
*kṛtvā sā rākṣasīṃ māyāṃ paṃcavīrānamohayat \|\| 96 \|\|*

*nirastrakavacānbaṃdhūnpratidolāṃ samāruhat \|*  
*pituraṃtikamāsādya tasmai bhrātṛndadau mudā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*prabhāte bodhitāḥ sarve snānadhyānādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā yayū ripoḥ śālāṃ dṛṣṭavanto na tāṃstadā \|\| 98 \|\|*

*babhūburduḥkhitāḥ sarve kimidaṃ kāraṇaṃ katham \|*  
*tānuvāca tadā devaḥ prāptā hyatra ripoḥ sutā \|\| 99 \|\|*

*kṛtvā sā rākṣasīṃ māyāṃ hṛtvā tāngehamāyayau \|*  
*tasmādyūyaṃ mayā sārddhaṃ gatvā yatraiva tadguruḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*viṃdhyopari mahāraṇye nānāsattvaniṣevite \|*  
*kuṭīraṃ tasya tatraiva nāmnaivailavilī hi saḥ ilavilā \|*  
*yogasiddhiyutaḥ kāmī rākṣasebhyo hi nirbhayaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

91-101. In a fit of anger, the valorous army commander known by the name of Talana killed sixty Mleccha rulers in no time. Talana looked like Yama for the enemy army. Whatever the warriors and rulers of Mlecchas had been left out, they fled away with the remaining army to their respective abodes. The king Jambuka felt extremely painful on hearing this news. Then he observing fast, went to sleep in his bed at night. Because of the warriors haunting him, he could not sleep. At the dead of night, his daughter named Vijaya, who was well-versed in all the arts and lores and resembled Radha of Vraja, assured her father and reached the enemy camp and cast her spell over the guards there. Then she, reaching her brothers, cast spell over her five brothers and Alha with her Raksasi lore. She put them all in a palanquin and carried them to her father, to whom she prosecuted them. In the early morning, all the people, finishing their daily bath etc. went to the enemy camp where they had been lodged as prisoners. When they could not find them there, they were taken aback and said- “What is the reason for it?” At that point of time, Devasimha said- “Vijaya - the daughter of the enemy, had arrived here last night and she had kidnapped them with her illusion. Therefore, all of you should go along with me there, where her preceptor lives. Her preceptor is known by the name of Ailavili. He lives in Vindhya Mountain in a cottage in the forest, with several of the wild animals. He has achieved success in the yogic practices. Therefore, he is not at all afraid of the demons.

## \|\| 2.115.102-109 \|\|

*jambukasya sutā tatra pratyahaṃ svajanairyutā \|*  
*ekākinī ca sā rātrau svaṃ guruṃ tamarīramat \|\| 102 \|\|*

*kṛteyaṃ cailavilinā māyā manujamohinī \|*  
*kāryasiddhiṃ gamiṣyāmo gatvā taṃ puruṣādhamam \|*  
*iti śrutvā tu catvāro vināhrādaṃ yayurvanam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*gītanṛtyapravādyaiśca mohayitvā ca ta dine \|*  
*vāsaṃ cakruśca tatraiva dhūrtaṃ māyāviśāradam \|\| 104 \|\|*

*sa tu pūrvabhave daityaścitro nāma mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*bāṇakanyāmuṣāṃ nityamavāñchacchiva pūjakaḥ \|*  
*jāta ailavilī nāma pakṣapūjī sa vegavān \|\| 105 \|\|*

*tayormadhye pramāṇo'yaṃ vivāho me yadā bhavet \|*  
*tadāhaṃ tvāṃ bhajiṣyāmi saṃtyaktvodvāhitaṃ patim \|\| 106 \|\|*

*hate tasminmahādhūrte gatvā saṃgrāmamūrddhani \|*  
*jambukasya yayurdurgaṃ dṛṣṭvā te taṃ samāruhan \|*  
*hatvā tatra sthitānvīrāñchataghnyaḥ parikhākṛtāḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*tadā tu jambuko rājā śivadattavaro balī \|*  
*jitvā pañca mahāvīrānbaddhvā tānnigaḍairdṛḍhaiḥ \|*  
*śaivaṃ yajñaṃ ca kṛtavāṃsteṣāṃ nāmnopabṛṃhitam \|\| 108 \|\|*

*rūpaṇastu tathā jñātvā devakīṃ pratyavarṇayat \|*  
*tadā tu duḥkhitā devī bhavānīṃ bhayahāriṇīm \|*  
*manasā ca jagāmāśu śaraṇyāṃ śaraṇaṃ satī \|\| 109 \|\|*

102-109. But inspite of all this, he is quite lustful. The daughter of the king Jambuka daily goes alone or with her companions and enjoys love sports with him. The same saint Ailavili has imparted the knowledge of confusing humans to her. Reaching the degraded person like him, we people shall be surely successful.” On hearing this, except Ahlada, all the four brothers proceeded towards the forest. Reaching there, these people fascinated the wicked ascetic with their dance and music and they spent the day in his hermitage. The degraded ascetic was a terrific Raksasa in his earlier birth who worshipped lord Siva to win over Usa - the daughter of Banasura. He came to be known as Ailavili during this birth. He forcefully worshipped the Yaksa. Both of them had reached an agreement that after her marriage, she would leave her husband and embrace him forever.” Thereafter, these people, after killing him, reached the battleground and attacked the fort of Jambuka. They surrounded the fort from all the sides and killed the warriors of that place. At that point of time, the king Jambuka had with him the boon of lord Siva. They put them all in bondages and started a yajna for Siva. Thereafter, the incident was narrated by Rupana to Devaki. On hearing that, Devaki was completely upset and she mentally adored goddess Parvati - the remover of dangers.

## \|\| 2.115.110-119 \|\|

*tadā tuṣṭā jagāddhātrī svapnāṃte tāmavarṇayat \|*  
*aho devaki kalyāṇi putraśokaṃ tyajādhunā \|\| 110 \|\|*

*yadā tu jambuko rājā śivadattavaro balī \|*  
*homaṃ kartā sa maṃdātmā teṣāṃ ca balihetave \|\| 111 \|\|*

*mohayitvā tadāhaṃ taṃ mocayitvā ca te sutān \|*  
*vijayaṃ te pradāsyāmi mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā satī devī namaskṛtya maheśvarīm \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa vidhivaddhūpadīpopahārakaiḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare rājā devamāyāvimohitaḥ \|*  
*suṣvāpa tatra homānte te ca jātā hyabaṃdhanāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*tairbaddho jambuko rājā nigaḍairāyasairdṛḍhaiḥ \|*  
*te taṃ baddhvā yayuḥ śīghraṃ devakīṃ prati nirbhayāḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare tatra kāliyādyāstrayaḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*trilakṣaṃ sainyamādāya yuddhāya samupāyayuḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

*punaryuddhamabhūdghoraṃ senayorubhayostadā \|*  
*tālanādyāśca catvāro hatvā tāṃ ripuvāhinīm \|\| 117 \|\|*

*trīñchatrūnkoṣṭhakīkṛtya svaśastrairjaghnurūrjitāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dināni katicittatra jāto mahāraṇaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*kāliyo duḥkhito bhūtvā sasmāra manasā haram \|*

110-119. Getting pleased, the mother of the universe then said to Devaki - “O foremost Devaki, why are you grieving for your sons presently? When Jambuka would get ready to offer them in sacrifice, I shall confuse him at that point of time, free your sons from the bondage and bestow victory on them. Therefore, I would say that you relieve your heart of the grief ” On hearing this, Devaki who was devoted to her husband, offered salutation with devotion to the goddess, besides incense, lamp and other presents with devotion. She completed the worship of Mahesvari variously. At the same time, having been confused by the illusion of the goddess, the king was overpowered by sleep. On the other hand, (the sons of Devaki) were automatically released from the chains. They atonce collected the chains and with those chains, they tightly bound the king Jambuka in chains and then went to their mother Devaki. Hearing this, the three sons, together with three lakhs of warriors, reached the battleground and started war. Both the armies then started the terrific war in the battleground, in which Talana and other warriors destroyed the enemy army. The three brothers who were the main enemies, were surrounded from all the sides and started wounding one another. The battle was thus carried out for many days. Then Kaliya getting upset, started mentally adoring lord Siva. Thereafter, he confused all the enemies with the use of Mohanastra.

120-135. At the same time, the devoted wife Devaki, because of the influence of her devotion to her husband, reached before her sons and addressed the son who was mounted over Pancasabda elephant king. She again pleased the mother of the universe, who confused the entire universe. As a result of it, the son of DevakI regained consciousness and then killed great warriors. Ahlada killed Suryavarma, Udayasimha killed Kaliya, Balakhana killed Jambu - the son of Tundila. O dear one, Kaliya in his earlier birth was Jarasandha and similarly, Suryavarma was the monkey known by the name of Dvivida. Tundila was Trisirasa demon, while Jambuka was Srgala All these rulers were always engaged in jealousy, enmity and quarrel. Thus, at the death of the sons of the enemy, DevakI who was grieving for her husband, cut off the head of Jambuka with a sword. Thereafter, Udayasimha feeling disgusted, having been overpowered with affection, placed both the heads of his father over the heart of Jambuka. At the same time, both the heads smilingly said- “Let you attain long life, О intelligent one, you perform Sraddha for my sake at Gaya.” Hearing these words emerging from the body of a goblin, the goddess Devaki established the enemy Jambuka in the stone grinder and then spoke to her sons with delight- “O my sons, you cut off the body of degraded Jambuka in small pieces and grind it in the oil mill. I shall apply oil so made over my body and then take my bath.” Thus speaking, she started crying. Obeying the command of their mother, the sons like Balakhana and others gathered with other queens and performed the last rites of the father. At the same time, the queen MalanS observed that her husband Parimala was on the verge of facing death. О Brahmana, at the time of his death, the daughter of Jambuka holding a sword in her hand, made Balakhana to faint, besides Talana, Devasimha and Ahlada also attacked the other enemy warriors. She kidnapped them with her illusion. After killing a hundred of his warriors, Balakhana in rage, cut off her head and dropped it in the funeral pyre.

136-139. At the same time, a divine voice from the sky declared- “O Balakhana, you listen to my

## Chapter 116. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.116.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kasminmāsyabhavadyuddhaṃ tayoḥ katidināni ca \|*  
*tatpaścātsva purīṃ prāya tadā kimabhavanmune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rsis said- О sage, for how long the forces of Mahismati and Mahavati kept on fighting with each other? Ultimately, what did the forces of Mahamati did on their return to the capital city?

## \|\| 2.116.2-6 \|\|

2-6. Suta said - The terrific war between the two forces started in the month of Pausa and evenly continued for a hundred days. Thus the warriors of Mahavati, reaching their homes in the month of Jyestha, felt delightful playing on the musical instruments. Hearing his sons becoming victorious, the king Parimala summoned the Brahmanas and gave several types of charities to them. Thereafter, everyone felt comfortable. Learning about the news of victory, offering his salutation, Prthviraja humbly said to Balakhana - “Half a crore of wealth is being given by me to you. Accepting this, you kindly return the kingdom of Mahismati to me. Salutation to you, О lord I shall continue to give this much of amount to you every year.” Accepting that amount, Balakhana returned his kingdom to Prthviraja. Thereafter, he returned to his home.

7-16. When Udayasimha reached the age of thirteen years, I am revealing to you the divine sports played by the lord. On the thirteenth bright moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, together with Udayasimha, Ahlada departed for Gaya for performing pindadana there. He was accompanied with several of the elephants, chariots, horses and enormous wealth. During that journey on pilgrimage, Udayasiriiha was mounted over the horse Bindula, Malakhana over the mare Harini, Devasimha over the horse Papiha and Sukhakhani was mounted over the horse named Karala. Covering the entire journey in two days, all the four of them reached the region of Gaya. They performed sixteen sraddhas from the full moon day to the moonless day. They gave away a hundred elephants, a hundred chariots and a hundred horses decorated with gold ornaments. Besides this, they also gave away cows, gold, gems and several types of costumes. Thereafter, performing the sraddha successfully, they decided to return home. A whore of that place named Laksavarti also went to Badarikasrama. Shedding her life there, she attained the eternal position and became an apsara again. Returning from Gaya, all of them went to Kasi and started living there. On the full moon night, there was a lunar eclipse by Rahn and there was darkness everywhere. The rulers of several countries had assembled there to take their bath in the Ganga at Kasi. Among them, there was a ruler of the Vaghela dynasty known by the name of Netrasimha who hailed from Himalaya and was decorated with several metals. After the death of the valorous Ratnabhanu, the king Netrasimha getting frightened, worshipped Indra at a site known as Netraturiga.

*asya śabdena bhūpāla tvaṃ sainyaṃ jīvayiṣyasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-22. After twelve years, getting pleased with his worship, Indra gave him the nectar in the form of a damaru, which had been originally made by the goddess Parvati for Indra - her devotee. Then giving it to Indra, she said to him- “With the sound of this damaru, your dead army would always come back to life and the great enemy warriors would get destroyed in no time. After receiving the damaru, the valorous Netrasimha built a city which was meant for all the people, which was spread in an area of four krosas, with four gates and was invincible by the enemy. Over the land of Bharatavarsa, it came to be known as the city of Netrasimha. This country was in the region of Kasmira, which was spread with mountain peaks in all the directions. О sage, Netrasimha took care of that city like his son. Because of that, the inaccessible village was known as Netrapala.

23-31. During the journey to Kasi, the valorous king Netrasimha was accompanied with his daughter named Svarpavati, who was born of the amsa of Revati and with the grant of a boon by Kamaksa - the goddess proficient in the activities related to Мaуa or illusion. The beautiful girl had the face of the rising moon and having a look at the charming face, people were taken aback and behaved as if fainting, who had arrived to take a bath at the holy place. Similarly, at the sight of the charming girl decorated with all the ornaments, Ahla becoming lustful got fainted and fell down on the ground. The girl also felt attracted at the sight of Ahla. Both her handmaids put her in palanquin and carried her to the king. After somehow recovering from that great illusion, Ahlada regained consciousness, but he soon lost his consciousness again. Udayasimna felt painful and said - “You are well-versed in the tattva, then why are you getting so much fascinated? You are well aware of the fact that attraction develops from rajoguna, from which emerges confusion and from confusion arrogance is generated. You are always invincible, therefore making use of the sword of consciousness, you destroy the illusion completely.” Listening to the words of his brother, he got himself relieved of his illusion and then proceeded on to his abode, where he recited the Madhyamcarita of the goddess and served delicious food to hundreds of learned Brahmanas. At the end of the same month, the goddess bestowed success on him and made the girl ready for the marriage. The girl met with Ahlada - the son of Devaki, in the dream.

32-41. In the early morning, she kept on thinking about the same, getting enamoured. At that point of time, she meditated upon the Kamaksi Devi, who could grant all the wishes. Then she wrote a letter in the month of pausa and bound it in the neck of a parrot, which was despatched as the carrier of the letter. The parrot then reaching the garden of the city of Mahavati, said to Udayasimha in human voice- “The princess Svarnavati has sent a letter for your brother. You get it and a reply thereof should be tied around my neck.” On hearing that, the valorous Udayasimha took the letter and read it. Knowing about all the matter, he handed it over to Ahlada. It was written therein- “O valorous one, you have killed many valorous kings like Jambuka and others in the battleground. Similarly, after killing the enemy of my father in the battleground, you accept my hand in marriage.” Reading this, Ahlada assured her and wrote a letter in reply and tied it in the neck of the parrot. The parrot was a pannaga in earlier birth and after getting a curse from Pundarika, he became a parrot. After accomplishing the task of Svarnavati, the parrot proceeded on to the heaven.

42-56. After its death, Svarnavati cremated it and distributed charities among the Brahmanas for the satisfaction of the departed soul. On the dark fifth day of the month of magha, with the seven lakh of his army, Ahlada departed from his place. Talana and other warriors were mounted over their respective vehicles and engaged themselves for the protection of Ahlada from all the sides. On the fifteenth day, they reached the capital city crossing the Vanga country and they rapidly reached the Himalaya region. The carrier messenger said to Rupana - “You mount the horse Karala, wearing the coat of arms, equipped with all the five weapons. You reach before the king and inform him about our arrival. Then you carve some battle-sign over your body and return at once.” Accepting the command, Rupana who was from the amsa of Sikhandi, immediately entered the capital city. Reaching there, he witnessed the royal court there, in which several of the warriors from hills, the rulers together with their valorous courtiers were present, adding to the grace of the place. The immensely valorous Netrasimha was addressed by him- “A great and powerful warrior known by the name of Balakhana together with his seven lakh soldiers, have reached in the capital city. Therefore, you get ready to give the hand of your daughter in marriage to Ahlada at once. О king, the reward for this should be given to me in the form of a terrific war.” Hearing these words, the king getting immensely enraged, commanded the chief of the court. In order to capture Rupana, he got the huge gate of the court closed. Under the presidentship of the lord of the city, the security guards were observed by the king, who were a hundred in number and were equipped with nooses and other weapons. Then Ruраnа stood before them holding a sword in his hand for a fight. Thereafter, killing them all in the battleground, he picked up the king’s crown and rushed to Balakhana and gave away the royal crown to him. Obseiving this courage and getting delighted, Balakhana surrounded the capital city of Netrasimha with his seven lakh warriors from all the sides. Together with his mountain rulers, the valorous Netrasimha invited them for a fight in the high peaks of Himalaya. His army comprised of a thousand elephants, a thousand valorous rulers and five lakh foot soldiers.

57-63. Yogasimha - the leader of the elephant army challenged Balakhana, the leader of the cavalry army challenged Udayasimha, the prince Vijayakumara together with other rulers challenged Devasimha, Talana as well as Rupana for a war. The great warriors of both the sides attacked one another and turned the battle quite terrific. The soldiers from the mountain surrounded the enemy army from all the sides and killed two lakhs of their warriors. Observing the total destruction of the army, all the four warriors mounted on their divine horses, killed a large number of the enemy soldiers. But the enemy warriors, at the sound of the damaru causing the nectar, were hurriedly brought back to life and they again rushed for waging the war. О best of the race of Bhrgu, thus by so regaining their lives, the battle continued for seven days and nights and became horrible, in which the great warriors displayed their competence in the war. But the enemy army was brought back to life again and again and destroyed the enemy soldiers. Observing this, Talana and other warriors felt extremely painful, lost all hope of victory and went to Udayasimha and prayed to him.

Offering his salutation to her, he spoke in sweet voice- “I happen to be your servant Udayasimha, I have taken refuge with you like the goddess Кamакsi .” Thereafter, he apprised her of the factual position of the war and also said- “All our soldiers getting tired, have lost all hope for victory.” She said- “O Udayasimha, you atonce move on to the temple of the goddess Kamaksi. On the ninth moon day, I shall arrive there for worship of the goddess.

68-73. One of the slave girl shall also carry this damaru. You can kidnap her with the \<}amaru. On hearing this, Balakhana returned to his army camp. The ruler meet with welfare after worshipping her, otherwise, О graceful one, there is always the danger of obstruction.” Hearing the words of her father and with his permission, she entered the temple of the goddess with the sounding of the damaru.

74-80. At the same time, Udayasimha was present there in the form of the bride of the gardener. He snatched the damaru from the hand of the slave girl and fled away from there. With the loss of the nectar like damaru, Netrasimha getting frightened, commanded the preparation for performing of Aindra-yajna. At the rise of the dawn, they reached the place where the battle was started with Netrasimha. Udayasimha first worshipped the damaru and then created sound from it, hearing which all the dead soldiers were brought back to life.

81-88. Surrounding the city with their arrogant warriors, again all of them started playing on musical instruments. With the sound so produced and finding that the city had been surrounded, feeling frightened, Netrasimha offered himself in the fire altar of the yajna for the pleasure of Indra. Getting pleased with his action, the lord Indra said to the king- “Lord Rama and Krsna in the form of Ahlada and Udayasimha respectively have incarnated on earth. Therefore, your daughter is quite suitable for Ahlada, because that girl is also the amsa of Yogini and Revati. Thus speaking, Devaraja Indra himself snatching away the beloved damaru of Parvati, threw it in the fire altar. Then offering prayer to the goddess Durga, he proceeded on to his loka. After the departure of Indra to heaven, with a desire to compromise with Udayasimha, Netrasimha proceeded towards Urai, which was ruled by Mahipati. Meeting the king and welcoming him, the maternal uncle of Ahlada said to him- “O king, though Ahlada is most powerful as compared to his own brothers, but because of his having been bom in a low family, he could not enter my community.

Thereafter, he invited the six warriors like Talana and others for marriage in the mandapa.

Bhogasimha on the other hand was captured by Balakhani.

101-106. In the third circumambulation, Vijaya when attacked by a warrior, was stopped by Sukhakhani. Tn the fourth circumambulation, the attack of the ruler Purnabala was stopped by Rupana and he fought fiercely. In their fifth circumambulation, the king was stopped by Talana. In the sixth circumambulation, Ahlada himself caught hold of Netrasimha. In the ensuing fight, several warriors were wounded. All these six people, even when they were without weapons, deprived the attackers of their weapons. In the mean time, Devasimha, who had been well-versed in the Kala-tattva, reached there from the sky way and gave away their respective vehicles to all of them. Thereafter, Udayasimha mounted over the horse Bindula; Devasimha over the horse Manoratha; Rupana over the horse named Karala, Ahlada over Papiha horse and Balakhani over the mare Harini, besides Talana mounted over Simhani. All of them got ready for a war.

107-115. All of them destroyed the army of the king during the night itself and put their chief commander prisoner in. Thereafter, the palanquin was carried out of the house and the seven circumambulations were completed. Thereafter, all of them reached their army camp. Reaching there, Netrasimha, who was crying- “save me,” “save me”, was put in bondage and lodged in terrific prison. Thereafter, Harananda - the younger brother of Netrasimha, who was the ruler of the forest named Sundara, learning about the precarious condition of his brother, arrived there with a lakh of army and started a war there. In the mean time, the army of Netrasimha comprising of four lakhs of soldiers, also arrived there. This army of five lakhs of soldiers started fighting with the army of seven lakhs of soldiers. In the terrific war, half of the enemy army was destroyed and the remaining soldiers took to flight. This surprised Harananda immensely. Thereafter he, who was proficient in Rudra illusion, finding the enemy so powerful, started meditating upon Siva. Thereafter he, making use of Sabari illusion, turned the enemy soldiers in stone, freed his elder brother and his son, besides the entire army and then returned to his abode.

*rurodoccaistadā devīṃ dhyāyaṃtī kāmarūpiṇīm \|*  
*tadā tuṣṭā jagaddhātrī mūrcchitāṃstānabodhayat \|\| 118 \|\|*

*te sarve cetanāṃ prāptāḥ prāhuḥ svarṇavatīṃ mudā \|*  
*kvāsthito vaṃdhurāhlādo devi tvaṃ kāraṇaṃ vada \|\| 119 \|\|*

*yathā baddhaḥ svayaṃ svāmī kathayāmāsa sā tathā \|*  
*ahaṃ śukī bhavāmyadya bhavānbiṃdulasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*ityuktvā sā śukī bhūtvā kṛṣṇāṃśena samanvitā \|*  
*yatrāste tatpatirbaddhastatra sā kāminī yayau \|\| 121 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśo'pi hayārūḍho nabhomārgeṇa cāptavān \|*  
*abhīrīṃ mūrtimāsādya svāminaṃ prati sā yayau \|\| 122 \|\|*

*āśvāsya taṃ yathāyogyaṃ kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ pratyavarṇayat \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśastatra balavānhatvā durga nivāsinaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*rakṣakāñchatasāhasrānhatvā bhrātaramāyayau \|*  
*paurṇimāṃ madhuyuktāṃ ca jñātvā sarve tvarānvitāḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

*ayodhyāṃ śīghramāgamya snātvā vai sarayūṃ nadīm \|*  
*holikādāhasamaye śīghraṃ veṇyāṃ samāgatāḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

116-125. At the time of his departure, with the use of his illusion, Netrasimha put unconscious Ahlada in bondages and carried him to his fort. On his reaching home, praising the Brahmanas, he gave them enough of charities. At that point of time, Svarnavati found her husband in bondages, then she cast the spell of Siva on the relatives and soldiers of the king. Getting upset, she cried for some time. Then she started pleasing the Kamarupini Devi quite carefully. The mother of the universe was then pleased and bestowed consciousness on those who had been fainted. After regaining then-senses, they asked Svarnavati- “O goddess, where is the brother Ahlada, you tell us about his condition. She then revealed all the facts about him in detail. She also said to Udayasimha - “You ride the horse and I shall accompany you in the form of a parrot I shall lead you to the place where my husband has been kept in bondage. Udayasimha also reached there with the help of the sky way. Svarnavati then took to the form of milkmaid, reached her husband and assured him variously. Besides she also revealed the sensitive secrets of the place to Udayasimha. The valorous Udayasimha killed the guards of the fort, who lived in thousands. Then he, on the full moon day of the month of caitra, departed with his brother to Ayodhya. Feeling delighted, Svarnavati then took the holy bath there. Thereafter, on the occasion of Holi, all of them reached over the Vent-tala or the bank of the river Veni.

## \|\| 2.116.126-128 \|\|

*snānadhyānādikā niṣṭhāḥ kṛtvā gehamupāyayuḥ \|*  
*sāgarasya taṭaṃ prāpya kṛtvā te ca mahotsavam \|*  
*caitrasya kṛṣṇapañcamyāṃ svagehaṃ punarāyayuḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

*dūtā uṣṭrasamārūḍhāstatkṣemakaraṇotsukāḥ \|*  
*vaiśākhe śuklapaṃcamyāṃ svagehaṃ punarāyayuḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

*malanā bhūpatiścaiva gehegehe mahotsavam \|*  
*kārayitvā vidhānena brāhmaṇebhyo dadau dhanam \|\| 128 \|\|*

126-128. Taking bath and performing meditation there, they reached their home. After some time, they reached their seashore and organized a vast function. After that, on the dark fifth day of the month of Caitra, they returned to their respective homes and started living there with comfort. The messengers who use the camel carts, on the bright fifth day of the month of Phalguna, reached their homes. At that point of time, the joy of Malana and the king Parimala knew no bounds. Festivities were performed in each and every house. The Brahmanas were given enough of riches in charity.

## Chapter 117. Collateral history of the Age of Kali
