*brāhmaṇebhyo dadau svarṇadhenuvṛndaṃ hayāngajān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*indule tanaye jāte dvimāsāṃte mahītale \|*  
*yogasiṃhastadāgatya svarṇavatyai dadau dhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*netrasiṃha sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā malanāsnehasaṃyutā \|*  
*papraccha kuśalapraśnaṃ bhojayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śatavṛndāśca nartakyo nānārāgeṇa saṃyutāḥ \|*  
*tatrāgatyeva nanṛturyatra bhūpasutaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*saptarātramuṣitvā sa yogasiṃho yayau gṛham \|*  
*ṣaṇmāse ca sute jāte devendraḥ snehakātaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*putrasnehena taṃ putraṃ sa jahāra svamāyayā \|*  
*saṃhṛtya bālakaṃ śreṣṭhamindrāṇyai ca samarpayat \|\| 9 \|\|*

1-9. Suta said- Whatever happened in the fourteenth year of the age of Udayasimha is being narrated by me. You please listen. Because of the curse from the goddess Janaki, Jayanta - the son of Indra, entered the womb of the queen Svarnvati, in the age of Kali. On the bright ninth day of the month of Caitra, at noon on Thursday, he was bom as a prince. His face was as bright as the moon and he possessed all the royal symptoms. At the birth of the excellent son, all the gods with Rsis declared- “He has taken birth on earth, being the son of Indra. Therefore, he should be known by the name of Indula. At that point of time, Ahlada delightfully performed his name giving ceremony and also gave to the Brahmanas in charity the gold, cows, many elephants and horses. Two months after the birth of Indula on earth, Yogasimha went to Svarnavati and gave to her enough of gold and wealth. At that time, because of enough of affection, the queen Malana finding Yogasimha - the son of Netrasimha, asked him about his welfare in choked voice. Then she served him food appropriately. Thereafter, she tried to please him with the dance and music of various dancers. Thus staying delightfully for seven nights, he returned home. Upto the age of six months of the prince, Indra became upset while spending his time. He could not help himself. Ultimately, because of his love for his son, he kidnapped his own son with his illusion. Kidnapping the excellent child, he entrusted his care to his own wife Indrani.

## \|\| 2.117.10-11 \|\|

*snehaplutā śacī devī svastanau tamapāyayat \|*  
*devyā dugdhaṃ sa vai pītvā ṣoḍaśābdasamobhavat \|\| 10 \|\|*

*induṃ pīyūṣabhavanaṃ gṛhṇāti vapuṣā svayam \|*  
*ataḥ sa indulo nāma jayantaśca prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*sa bālaḥ svapiturvidyāṃ paṭhitvā śreṣṭhatāmagāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Out of her affection, Indrani made the child suck her breast. With the sucking of the breast milk of Indrani, he then suddenly appeared as the boy of sixteen years. His ordinary body then looked like that of the moon. Because of this, Jayanta is also known as Indula. He gained the knowledge of his father and achieved excellence.

## \|\| 2.117.12-17 \|\|

*vinaṣṭe bālake tasmindevī svarṇavatī tadā \|*  
*rurodoccaistadā dīnā hā putra kva gato'si bhoḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*jñātvāhlādaṃ tathā bhūtaṃ daśagrāme tathāvidhe \|*  
*raudraḥ kolāhalo jāto rudatāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ mune \|\| 13 \|\|*

*āhlādaḥ svakulaiḥ sārddhaṃ nirāhāro yateṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*śāradāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptastrirātraṃ tatra cāvasat \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tadā tuṣṭā svayaṃ devī vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|*  
*he putra svakulaiḥ sārddhaṃ mā śucastvaṃ sutaṃ prati \|\| 15 \|\|*

*indraputro jayantaśca svargalokamupāgataḥ \|*  
*divyavidyāṃ paṭhitvā sa trivarṣāṃte gamiṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yāvattvaṃ bhūtale'vātsīstāvatsa bhūtale vaset \|*  
*tatpaścātsvargatiṃ prāpya jayanto hi bhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

12-17. At the kidnapping of the child and finding him missing, Svarnavati lamented for the child, crying aloud. Learning about this news, Ahlada and the people of his ten villages also started crying. The people of that place were therefore drowned in compassion. Ahlada performed a vrata with all his family members, taking refuge with the goddess Barada and stayed in the place of the goddess for three days and three nights. The goddess was then pleased and declared in divine voice from the sky- “O son, why are you grieving for your child with your family? Shed away all the worries. He actually is Jayanta - the son of Indra, who was given to his father Indra in the heaven. Attaining the divine knowledge there, he would return after three years on earth and shall live with you. Thereafter, reaching the heaven, he would take to the form of Jayanta.”

## \|\| 2.117.18 \|\|

*ityukte vacane devyā niśśokāste tadābhavan \|*  
*daśagrāmapuraṃ prāpya samūṣurjñāna tatparāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Listening to the words of the goddess, Ahlada discarded the grief and went back to the ten villages, where he started spending time like the learned people.

## Chapter 118. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.118.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*indule svargasaṃprāpte te vīrāḥ śokakātarāḥ \|*  
*śāradāṃ pūjayāmāsuḥ sarvalokanivāsinīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

*japtvā saptaśatī stotraṃ trisandhyaṃ premabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*dhyānenānandamāpannāstadā saptaśatehani \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sāmantadvijaputraśca cāmuṇḍo nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*so'ṣṭavarṣavayā bhūtvā pūjayāmāsa caṇḍikām \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said- At the departure of Indula to heaven, the warriors felt painful with grief and worshipped the omnipresent goddess Sarada. Overpowered with love and devotion, they recited the Saptasati stotra thrice a day and enjoyed bliss by meditation. Camunda - the son of a Brahmana courtier, had been reciting the three caritras of the goddess since the age of eight years.

## \|\| 2.118.4-12 \|\|

*dvādaśābde tato jāte tricaritrasya pāṭhataḥ \|*  
*parīkṣārthaṃ tu bhaktānāṃ sākṣānmūrtitvamāgatā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kuṃḍikeyaṃ ca bho bhaktāḥ pūrayāmi ca tāmaham \|*  
*yūyaṃ tu manasopāyaiḥ kurudhvaṃ pūraṇe matim \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sukhakhānistu balavānmadhupuṣpaistathā phalaiḥ \|*  
*kuṇḍikāṃ pūrayā māsa na pūrṇatvamupāgatā \|*  
*balakhānistathā māṃsairmūlaśarmā tu raktakaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*devakī ca tadā havyaiścandanādibhirarcanaiḥ \|*  
*kuṇḍikāṃ pūrayāmāsa na pūrṇatvamupāgatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*āhrādaścaiva sarvāṃgairudayaḥ śirasā svayam \|*  
*kuṇḍikāṃ pūrayāmāsa tadā pūrṇatvamāgatā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*uvāca vacanaṃ devī svabhaktānbhaktavatsalā \|*  
*sukhākhāne bhavānvīro bhaviṣyati surapriyaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*balakhānirmahāvīro dīrghe kāle sa mṛtyubhāk \|*  
*mūlaśarmā tu balavānraktabījo bhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

*devakī ca bhaveddevī cirakālaṃ svalokagā \|*  
*āhlādaścaiva kṛṣṇāṃśastayormadhye dvayaṃ varam \|*  
*ekastu devavatprokto balādhikyo dvitīyakaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*niṣkāmo'yaṃ devasiṃho mṛto mokṣatvamāpnuyāt \|*  
*ityuktvāntardadhe mātā te sarve tṛptimāgatāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

4-12. He had reached the age of twelve years. In order to test the devotion of her devotees, the goddess herself appeared from her own image and said- “O my devotees, I would like to fill up this fire altar. You first mentally think of the means to fill the same.” On hearing this, the valorous Sukhakhani initially tried to fill up the altar with incense, flowers and fruits but inspite of his best efforts, he could not do so. Similarly, Balakhani tried his best to fill the altar with red flowers; Devaki with the sandal flowers, but the same could not be filled. At the same time, Ahlada poured all his limbs into it, while Udayasimha cut off his head and dropped the same into the altar, as a result of which the altar was filled. The goddess getting pleased with this, then said- “O valorous Sukhakhani, you would become the favourite of the gods. The valorous Balakhani would met with his end after a long time. The valorous Mulasarma would be Raktabija. The goddess Devaki shall enter her abode after a long time. I am granting two boons to Ahlada and Udayasimha. One would live like a god and the other one would possess excess of strength. Besides Devasimha, who performs selfless deeds, shall achieve redemption after his death.” Thus speaking, the mother goddess disappeared from the scene and the devotees started living with pleasure.

## Chapter 119

## \|\| 2.119.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*prāpte saptadaśābde ca kṛṣṇāṃśe tatra cābhavat \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ muniśārdūla dṛṣṭaṃ yadyogadarśanāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ratnabhānau mṛte rājñi marudhanvamahīpatiḥ \|*  
*gajasenastadā vipra pṛthvīrājabhayāturaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said- О lion among the sages, I am going to narrate the events, which were witnessed by me during the seventeenth year of the age of Udayasimha. You please listen. 0 Brahman, after the departure of the king Ratnabhanu to the heaven, the king Gajasena of Marudhanva getting frightened from the king Prthviraja, worshipped the fire god with the performing of yajna, with dedication and other means.

## \|\| 2.119.4-16 \|\|

*tadā prasanno bhagavānpāvakīyaṃ hayaṃ śubham \|*

*aṣṭādaśavayobhūtāḥ sarve te munipuṃgava \|*

*tārakādyāśca bhūpālāḥ sarvaśastrāstrasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*rurudhuḥ sarvato vīraṃ te balātkanyakārthinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tathāvidhānnṛpāndṛṣṭvā bhūpānpaṃcaśatānbalī \|*  
*sa śīghraṃ khaṅgamutsṛjya śatabhūpaśirāṃsyahan \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sarvato vadhyamānaṃ taṃ balakhāniṃ sa tārakaḥ \|*  
*tadbhujābhyāṃ dadau khaḍgaṃ sa tadaṃge dvidhābhavat \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mahīrājasuto jyeṣṭho dṛṣṭvā khaḍgaṃ tathā gatam \|*  
*apovāha raṇācchūrastatpaścātte nṛpā yayuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*parājite nṛpabale balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*tāṃ kanyāṃ śibikārūḍhāṃ svagehaṃ so'nayadbalī \|\| 16 \|\|*

4-16. The fire god, getting pleased with him, graced the king with a beautiful horse, two sons and a daughter named Gajamuktika. All the four of them who were bom of the amsa of the fire god, had the complexion of fire. They were extremely valorous and had all the auspicious symbols. All of them took birth over the earth. О best of the sages, at the age of eighteen years, getting pleased, the goddess Durga bestowed a boon to the girl- “O daughter, Balakhana would be your husband. Thereafter, Gajasena - the Vaghela king, performed svayamvara for his daughter, in which several of the princes getting attracted with the beauty of the princess, participated in the svayamvara. On Monday, the eighth bright moon day of the month of the Margasirsa, the girl arrived for selection of a groom, having the face displaying the lustre of the lightning. The king Balakhana was fainted at the sight of the beauty of the princess. The girl Gajamuktika too was filled with passion at the sight of Balakhana. Under such a situation, the auspicious princess placed the garland Vaijayanti around the neck of Balakhana. At this, Taraka and other princes who had arrived there to seek the hand of the girl, surrounded Balakhana from all the sides displaying their force. Finding five hundred rulers attacking him, Balakhana rapidly held the sword in his hand and cut off the heads of a hundred rulers. Then Taraka finding that Balakhana had been surrounded by the rulers from all the sides, held his sword at their hands. But the sword broke into two pieces, when it struck with the body of Balakhana. Taraka - the elder son of Prthviraja, observed this and with the usurping of his horse, all his kings who had accompanied him, fled away from the battleground. After defeating the rulers, Balakhana put the princess in the palanquin and proceeded towards his own house.

## \|\| 2.119.17-23 \|\|

*tāṃ gacchaṃtīṃ sutāṃ dṛṣṭvā gajaseno mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*mahīpatyājñayā prāpto jñātvā taṃ kṣatriyādhamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jaṃbukaghnaṃ mahāvīraṃ māyayā tamamohayat \|*  
*jāte nidrāture vīre durgāyāḥ śāpamohite \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nigaḍaistaṃ babaṃdhāśu dṛḍhairlohamayai ruṣā \|*  
*lohadurgaṃ ca saṃprāpya grāmarūpaṃ mahīpatiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*cāṃḍālāṃśca samāhūya kaṭhināṃstatravāsinaḥ \|*  
*vadhāyājñāpayāmāsa tasya daṃḍairanekaśaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*te raudrāstaṃ samābadhya tāḍayāmāsurūjjitāḥ \|*  
*tattāḍanāttadā nidrā tatraiva vilayaṃ gatā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tatastu caṃḍālānbalakhāniratāḍayat \|*  
*talamuṣṭiprahāreṇa cāṃḍālā maraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mṛte paṃcaśate raudre taccheṣā dudruvurbhayāt \|*  
*kapāṭaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā nṛpāṃtikamupāyayuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

17-23. Observing the departure of his daughter, in consultation with Mahipa - the lord of UrvI and at the advice of the defeated rulers, the king Gajasena confused Balakhana, who was the killer of the degraded Ksatriya ruler Jambuka besides being a great warrior, with his illusion. Subsequently, because of the curse of the goddess Durga, he was confused and was under swoon. He was then sent to the village with an iron fort. The Cabalas of the place were then summoned and commanded to kill him. Receiving such a type of command, the terrific Cayndalas started torturing and beating him with canes. After some time, he regained his senses. Finding that the Candalas were attacking him, Balakhana started attacking the Candalas with his fists and slaps. In this way, five hundred Candalas were killed by him and the rest of them fled away from the place. Thereafter, securely closing the door, Balakhana went to the king in the palace.

## \|\| 2.119.24-29 \|\|

*sa nṛpaḥ kāraṇaṃ jñātvā hastabaddho mahābalī \|*  
*uvāca tatra gatvāsau vacanaṃ kāryatatparaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bhavānmahābalo vīra cāṃḍālairbaṃdhanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*dasyubhirluṃṭhitastatra nidrāvaśyo vanaṃ gataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*matsutā bhavane prāptā diṣṭyā tvaṃ jīvitaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*udvāhya matsutāṃ śīghraṃ svagehaṃ yātumarhasi \|*  
*iti śrutvā priyaṃ vākyaṃ taṃ praśasya tathākarot \|\| 26 \|\|*

*maṃḍape vedakarmāṇi vivāhārthaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*jātāyāṃ maṃḍapārcāyāṃ patramāhlādahetave \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tadājñayā likhitvāsau gajaseno'gnisevakaḥ \|*  
*uṣṭrārūḍhaṃ samāhūya śīghraṃ patramacodayat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*balakhānervivāho'tra bhavānsainyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya yogyadravyāṇi bhuktvā tvaṃ tṛptimāvaha \|\| 29 \|\|*

24-29. Learning about all the causes, the king spoke to him with folded hands- “It is quite a painful situation that you had been captured by the low caste Candalas and the thieves have usurped your wealth. Perhaps you had gone to sleep reaching the forest. My daughter has returned to my palace. It is a matter of great pride and fortune to find you alive. In order to marry my daughter, you hurriedly go back to your home.” On hearing this, Balakhana was pleased and he praised him immensely. The king also issued instructions for making a pavilion for the performing of the marriage. After the preparations for the marriage were made, Gajasena - the devotee of the fire god, sent a messenger to Ahlada through the fast going camel with a letter and said- “Carry this letter at once to Ahlada.” It was written in the letter, “The marriage of Balakhana is going to be celebrated here, you come here with your army and accept my hospitality.”

## \|\| 2.119.30-34 \|\|

*ityukte niśi jātāyāṃ balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*bhojanaṃ kṛtavāṃstatra viṣajuṣṭaṃ nṛpārpitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*garalaṃ tena saṃbhuktaṃ na mamāra varācchubhāt \|*  
*tataḥ kāle ca saṃprāpte dṛṣṭvā mohatvamāgatam \|*  
*punarbabaṃdha nigaḍaistāḍayāmāsa vetasaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*viṣadoṣamasṛkdvārānnissṛtaṃ sarvadehataḥ \|*  
*tadā bubodha balavānbhūpatiṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*rājankimīdṛśaṃ jātaṃ tvatsainyaṃ tāḍane ratam \|*  
*sa āha bho mahāvīra matkule rītirīdṛśī \|*  
*yātanāṃ prathamaṃ prāpya tadanūdvāhito bhavet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ityukte sati bhūpāle gajamuktā samāgatā \|*  
*pitaraṃ prāha vacanaṃ ko'yaṃ tattāḍane gataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

30-34. Subsequently, on the same night, the king made Balakhana to consume poison with food. But inspite of his consuming poison with food, he could not meet with his end, because of the boon he had received earlier. When Balakhana became unconscious, he was again put under chains and was beaten with canes over hands and the soles. At the same time, the poison flowed with the blood from his body and he regained his senses. Then he spoke quite humbly to the king- “O king, what is the. reason for your army to attack me like this?” The king replied- “O valorous one, this happens to be the tradition of my family. The groom is initially tortured and then he is married.” At these words spoken by the king, the princess arrived there and spoke to her father- “Who is being punished with these attacks?”

## \|\| 2.119.35-40 \|\|

*nṛpaḥ prāha sute śīghraṃ yāhi tvaṃ nijamaṃdire \|*  
*kṛṣikaroyamāyāto dravyārthaṃ tāḍane gataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*chittvā tadbaṃdhanaṃ ghoraṃ khaḍgahastaḥ samāyayau \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śūrānpaṃcaśataṃ taṃ ca ruddhvā śastraiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*prajaghnatastu tānsarvānbalakhānirvyanāśayat \|\| 37 \|\|*

*gajasena suto jyeṣṭhaḥ sūryadyutirupāgataḥ \|*  
*baddhvā punastaṃ balinaṃ gartamadhye samākṣipat \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tathā gataṃ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā gajamuktā suduḥkhitā \|*  
*niśi tatra gatā devī dattvā dravyaṃ tu rakṣakān \|\| 39 \|\|*

*patiṃ niṣkāsya rudatī vyajanaṃ pataye dadau \|*

35-40. The king said- “О Daughter, you atonce return to your palace. He is only a farmer -teller of land and is being punished for extracting the tax.” Listening to the insulting words, the valorous Balakhana broke his claims and holding the sword in his hand, he shattered to pieces the five hundred soldiers who guarded him. Thereafter, Suryamani - the son of Gajasena, arrived there and put Balakhana again in chain and threw him in a deep pit. Witnessing the pitiable condition of her husband, Gajamukta felt extremely painful. At dead of night, paying wealth to the soldiers, she reached before her husband in prison. She served food to him properly and then returned. This process was continued for a fortnight.

## \|\| 2.119.41 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare vīraścāhlādaḥ saptalakṣakaiḥ \|*  
*sainyaiḥ sahāyayau śīghraṃ śrutvā tatraiva kāraṇam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thereafter, accompanied with the seven lakhs of his army, Ahlada arrived there.

## \|\| 2.119.42-50 \|\|

*balakhānirgato garte rurodha nagarīṃ tadā \|*  
*gajaiḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasrairgajaseno raṇaṃ yayau \|\| 42 \|\|*

*trilakṣaiśca hayaiḥ sārddhaṃ sūryadyutirupāyayau \|*  
*kāṃtāmalastadā prāptastrilakṣaiśca padātibhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tayoścāsīnmahadyuddhamahorātraṃ hi sainyayoḥ \|*

*dāhayāmāsa tatsainyaṃ tālanādyaiśca pālitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*bhasmībhūtaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā tālanaḥ śatrusammukhe \|*

*mūrchitaṃ nṛpamājñāya sūryadyutirupāyayau \|*  
*pāvakīyaṃ samāruhya dāhayāmāsa tālanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare śūrau devau cāhlādakṛṣṇakau \|*  
*babandhatū ruṣāviṣṭau sūryadyutimariṃdamam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*subaddhaṃ bhrātaraṃ jñātvā hayaṃ kāṃtāmalo'ruhat \|*

*amaratvātsa āhlādastadā tu samajīvayat \|\| 50 \|\|*

42-50. He had heard already that Balakhana had been consigned in a ravine. Therefore, the city of Gajasena was surrounded from all the sides and invited the king for waging a war. Gajasena had an army of sixteen thousand warriors besides three lakhs of horses were with Suryamani, while three lakhs of foot soldiers were with Kantamala - the younger brother of Suryamani. All of them reached in the battleground. They started the continuous war for day and night. Under the leadership of Talana and Gajasena besides others, both the armies fought with great force during the first day of the war. But the immensely valorous Gajasena, finding on the next day that his army was getting shattered, made use of fire power, which reduced the army of Talana to ashes. Observing the destruction of his army, making use of his spear, Talana attacked Gajasena, who got fainted. Thereafter, making use of the fire horse, Suryamani reduced Talana to ashes. In the mean time, both Ahlada and Udayasimha getting enraged, made Suryamani captive. At the sight of his brother getting captive, Kantamala mounted over the horse. Confusing Devasimha, he reached near Udayasimha, who captured him and removed the lustre of his horse as a result of which, his entire army of seven lakhs of soldiers was reduced to ashes at once, except Ahlada who escaped because of his being eternal.

## \|\| 2.119.51-62 \|\|

*gajasenasyārddhasainyaṃ taiśca sarvairvināśitam \|*  
*vijayaṃ nṛpatiḥ prāpya harṣito gehamāyayau \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vahnibhūtaṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ dṛṣṭvāhlādaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*durgāṃ devīṃ sa tuṣṭāva manasā raṇamūrddhani \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdasamaṃ rūpaṃ dhṛtvā vidyāviśāradaḥ \|*

*kecitsaṃnyāsino bhūtvā kecidvai brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*jīvatvaṃ prāptavantaste tathānye saṃkṣayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*baddhvā tāngajasenādīṃstrīñchūrānsa ca tālanaḥ \|*

*balakhāniṃ ca niṣkāsya tālanastadanaṃtaram \|*

*tānvīrāṃstāḍayāmāsa vetasaiḥ staṃbhabaṃdhanaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*gajamuktājñayā vipra senāpatarirudāradhīḥ \|*  
*tālanastānsamutsṛjya vivāhārthaṃ samāyayau \|*  
*balakhānirhayārūḍho gajamuktā ca maṃḍape \|\| 62 \|\|*

51-62. He also destroyed the remaining army of Gajasimha with the cavalry men. Still Gajasimha remained victorious, who returned to his abode. When Udayasirnha was reduced to ashes, Ahlada mentally adored the goddess Durga, who said- “Your son returning from the heaven, shall bring back all the dead soldiers to life.” At these words of the goddess, Indula gained the age of twelve years and arrived on earth mounted over the Amrta horse. From the said horse, there appeared three horses like the clouds. All the three of them appeared like the three gods. They extinguished the fire in the battleground, Thereafter, the main horse finding that the fire was getting extinguished, dropped foam from its mouth, as a result of which all the dead soldiers were brought back to life. Finding that the fire had been extinguished and the seven lakh soldiers of the enemy had regained their lives getting well-equipped, the king Gajasena with his two sons started fleeing on all the sides. They had been left with only a lakh of soldiers, who getting frightened fled away from the battleground disguising themselves. Some of them took to the form of recluses, some as Brahmacarins. Only those could survive, who fled away from the battleground. But those who remained in the form of soldiers were all killed. Thereafter, Talana made captive Gajasena with both his sons and Udayasimha proceeded towards the castle of Indra. Reaching there, they freed Balakhana and others from the bondages in the ravine. Then asked them the cause of their capture. Thereafter, all the three of them (Gajasimha and his sons) were bound with the pillars and they were beaten with the canes. О Brahman, at the same time, Gajamukta arrived there and got his father and brothers freed. Thereafter, the preparations for the marriage started. Balakhana reached the marriage mandapa mounted over a horse, where he seemed quite graceful.

## \|\| 2.119.63-64 \|\|

*gajasenastadā divyairbhojanaistānabhojayat \|*

*lakṣaśūrānsa saṃsthāpya svayaṃ rudrapuraṃ yayau \|\| 63 \|\|*

*te rātrau lohadurgeṣu hyuṣitvā yatnato balāt \|*  
*prabhāte ca kapāṭe na dvāraṃ dṛṣṭvā tadābravīt \|*  
*dvāramudghāṭayāśu tvaṃ no cetprāṇāṃstyajiṣyasi \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. The king Gajasena then welcomed the guests. But this welcome was quite deceitful. On this pretext, all of them were lodged in the iron castle and were securely locked. Gajasimha then secretly put on guard a lakh of soldiers on duty and left the place with his daughter. Finding the doors closed in the morning, the army commander said- “Let the gates of the fort be opened quickly, otherwise you will have to face your death.

## \|\| 2.119.65-74 \|\|

*iti senāpatiḥ śrutvā lakṣaśūrānsamādiśat \|*

*iti śrutvā tu te śūrāḥ śataghnyastaiḥ suropitāḥ \|*  
*ekaikaṃ kramaśo jaghnurvṛṃdaṃ te vairatatparāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*hate daśasahasre tu kṛṣṇāṃśo biṃdulaṃ hayam \|*

*hataśeṣā bhayārtāśca sahayāśītisammitāḥ \|*

*śrutvā bhayāturo rājā svasutābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ \|*

*ṣoḍaśoṣṭrāṇi svarṇāni gṛhītvāhlāda eva saḥ \|*  
*yayau svagehaṃ sahitaḥ putrabhrātṛsamanvitaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*saṃprāpte gehamāhlāde devī svarṇavatī svayam \|*

*mṛtāhaṃ ca tvayā putra punarujjīvitā khalu \|*  
*dhanyāhaṃ kṛtakṛtyāsmi jayanta tava darśanāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

*iti śrutvendulo vīro natvāha jananīṃ mudā \|*  
*anṛṇaṃ nādhigacchāmi tvatto mātaḥ kadācana \|\| 73 \|\|*

*saṃprāpte gehamāhlāde rājā parimalaḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*vādyāni vādayāmāsa viprebhyaśca dadau dhanam \|\| 74 \|\|*

65-74. On hearing these words of the enemy commander, the commander of the army of Gajasimha commanded his soldiers- “You start killing the enemies.” At the command of their leader, the soldiers started making use of their weapons. The warriors of the opposite camp also started fighting destroying the enemy army. When over ten thousand soldiers were killed, Udayasimha mounted over his horse named Bindula and started killing the enemy soldiers with his sword. Getting frightened, the remaining eighty thousand warriors reached the castle of Indra and narrated the tale of the killing of the warriors. At this, the king got frightened and with both his sons, Gajasena went to Ahlada and offered his daughter decorated with the best of costumes and ornaments. This way, he washed the sin committed by Mahita - the lord of Ural. On the other hand, Ahlada accepted sixteen camels loaded with gold (from the king Gajasimha) and returned to his place with his son and other relatives. On the arrival of Ahlada at his place, the goddess Svarnavati took Indula in her lap and cried pathetically saying- “0 son, you have brought back a dead mother like me to life. О Jayanta, with the meeting with you today, I felt quite successful and graceful.” On hearing this, Indula offered salutation to his mother with delight and said-“O mother, I can never be free from your debt, О mother’’. On hearing these words, the king Parimala distributed enough of riches to the Brahmanas, with the sound of music.

## Chapter 120. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.120.1-8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśe'ṣṭādaśābde tu yathājātaṃ tathā śṛṇu \|*  
*mṛte kṛṣṇakumāre tu bhūpatau ratnabhānunā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mahīrājaḥ suduḥkhārto lakṣacaṃḍīmakārayat \|*  
*homānte tu tadā devī vāguvāca nṛpaṃ prati \|\| 2 \|\|*

*varṣevarṣe tu te sapta bhaviṣyaṃtyaṃgasambhavāḥ \|*

*ityukte vacane tasminrājñī garbhamatho dadhau \|*  
*karṇāṃśaśca suto jātastārako balavattaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dvitīyābde tathā jāte duśśāsanaśubhāṃśataḥ \|*  
*nṛhaririti vikhyātastṛtīyābde tu cābhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

*uddharṣāṃśaḥ saradano durmukhāṃśastu mardanaḥ \|*  
*vikarṇāṃśaḥ sūryyakarmā bhīmaścāṃśo viviṃśateḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*varddhanaścitrabāṇāṃśo velā tadanu cābhavat \|*  
*yathā kṛṣṇā tathā saiva rūpaceṣṭāguṇairmune \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhuvi tasyāṃ ca jātāyāṃ bhūkampo dāruṇo'bhavat \|*  
*aṭṭāṭṭahāsamaśivaṃ cāmuṃḍā khe cakāra ha \|*  
*raktavṛṣṭiḥ pure cāsīdasthiśarkarayā yutā \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Suta said- During the eighteenth year of the age of Udayasimha, whatever happened is being narrated by me. You please listen. When Krsnakumara was killed at the hands of Ratnabhanu, Prthviraja felt extremely grieved. In sheer grief, he started a lakh of Candi-yajnas. After the completion of the homa, the goddess informed the king by means of the divine voice from the sky- “From the womb of your queen Agama, a prince would be bom of the amsa of Kauravas as well as Draupadi.” Thereafter, the queen conceived as a result of which Тarака was bom of the amsa of Karim, who was quite a valorous son. During the second year, a son named Nrhari was bom of the amsa of Dussasana. During the third year, a son named Saradana was born of the amsa of Uddhava. During the fourth year, a son named Mardana was born of the amsa of Durmukha. During the fifth year, a son named Suryakarma was born of the amsa of Vikarna. During the sixth year, Bhima was born, while in the seventh year a son named Vardhana was also born. After the seven sons, a daughter was also born who possessed all the qualities, merits, beauty and grace of Draupadi. With the birth of this girl child, there occurred a terrific earthquake. At that point of time, the goddess Camunda uttered a loud laugh in the sky. There was the rain blood mixed with the powder of bones.

## \|\| 2.120.9-16 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāśca samāgatya jātakarmādikāṃ kriyām \|*  
*kṛtvā nāma tathā cakre śṛṇu bhūmipa sākṣaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ilā ca śaśino mātā vikalpenā'bhavadbhuvi \|*  
*tasmādveleti vikhyātā kanyeyaṃ rūpaśālinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dadau dānaṃ mudā yukto vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdavayaḥ prāpte sā sutā varavarṇinī \|*  
*uvāca pitaraṃ namrā śṛṇu tvaṃ pṛthivīpate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*maṃḍape raktadhārābhiryo māṃ saṃsnāpayiṣyati \|*  
*draupadyā bhūṣaṇaṃ dātā sa me bhartā bhaviṣyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*svarṇapatre tadā rājā padyaṃ velāmukhodbhavam \|*  
*likhitvā tārakaṃ prāha tvamanveṣaya tatpatim \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sārddhaṃ lakṣatrayaṃ dravyaṃ gṛhītvā lakṣasainyakaḥ \|*  
*nṛpāntaraṃ yayau śīghraṃ tārakaḥ piturājñayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*siṃdhusthāne cāryadeśe bhūpaṃ bhūpaṃ yayau balī \|*  
*na gṛhītaṃ nṛpaiḥ keścittadvākyaṃ ghoramulbaṇam \|*  
*mahīpatiṃ sa saṃprāpya mātulaṃ tadvaco'bravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

9-16. After the birth of the daughter, the name that was given to her by the Brahmanas is being related by me. You please listen. Ila was the name of the moon, who took her birth on the earth. Therefore, the beautiful girl was given the name of Vela which is the alternative of Ila. At her birth, displaying his delight, her father distributed enough of riches and gifts to the Brahmanas including the costumes and ornaments. At the age of twelve years, the excellent girl said to her father- “You listen to my words. О lord of earth, only such a person, who would make me sleep over the stream of blood in the mandapa of marriage, he would be my husband and the giver of ornaments to me.” Listening to the words spoken by the princess, the father got those words embossed over the gold leaf, which was given by the king to Тarака with the instruction to search for a suitable husband for the girl. Then with the permission of his father, Taraka departed from the city of the king with a lakh of soldiers and three and a half lakhs of wealth. He started the journey from the bank of the river Sindhu, he journeyed through the kingdoms of all the Arya countries, but no ruler accepted this snake poison like passage. Thereafter, roaming about here and there, he reached Mahipati - his maternal uncle and narrated to him the factual position.

## \|\| 2.120.17-22 \|\|

*śrutvā sa āha bho vīra brahmānando mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sa ca vākyaṃ pragṛhṇīyādāhlādādyaiḥ surakṣitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kiṃ tvayā viditaṃ naiva caritaṃ tasya viśrutam \|*  
*bhavānṣaḍbaṃdhusahitaḥ kṛṣṇāṃśādyairvivāhitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*te sarve vaśagāstasya brahmānaṃdasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*nāsti bhūmaṃḍale kaścittadbalena samo nṛpaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā yayau tūrṇaṃ tārakaḥ svabalaiḥ saha \|*  
*tatpadyaṃ kathayitvāgre hastabaddhastadābhavat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśastu gṛhītvāśu padyaṃ vākyamuvāca ha \|*  
*ahaṃ vivāhayiṣyāmi brahmānaṃdaṃ nṛpottamam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tūṣṇīṃ bhūtāstadā sarve tārakaḥ sa dvijaiḥ saha \|*  
*abhiṣekaṃ tadā kṛtvā svagehaṃ punarāyayau \|\| 22 \|\|*

17-22. On hearing this, the maternal uncle said-“0 valorous one, you go to the prince Brahmananda, who himself is extremely powerful, besides being guarded by Ahlada and other warriors. I am confident that he would surely accept your conditions. Are you not aware of his character? It was Udayasimha alone, who had got the marriage of six brothers performed. All those people are under the control of Udayasimha. There is no other ruler as valorous as he on earth. On hearing these words, Taraka reached the desired place with his army and with folded hands offered the letter to Udayasimha. Udayasimha atonce received the letter in his hand and said- “I shall make Brahmananda to receive the hand of the girl in marriage.” There was a complete silence in the assembly at that point of time. Then performing the abhiseka of Brahmananda, Taraka went back to his abode.

## \|\| 2.120.23 \|\|

*māghamāse site pakṣe trayodaśyāṃ suvāsare \|*  
*vivāhalagnaṃ śubhadaṃ varakanyārthayostadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The date of marriage for the bride and groom was fixed on the thirteenth bright moon day of the month of Magha.

*raṇajicca balī bālo dvilakṣabalasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*evaṃ dvādaśalakṣāṇāṃ sainyānāmadhipo balī \|*  
*tālanaḥ siṃhinīsaṃstho vaḍavāṃ prayayau saha \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sainyairdvādaśalakṣaiśca sahitastālano balī \|*  
*āyayau dehalīgrāme mahīrājānupālite \|\| 28 \|\|*

*devo manorathārūḍho viṃdulasthaḥ sa kṛṣṇakaḥ \|*  
*vaḍavāmṛtamāsādya svarṇavatyāḥ suto gataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*rūpaṇaśca karālastha āhlādaśca papīhake \|*  
*balakhāniḥ kapotastho hariṇastho'nujastataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*raṇajinmalanāputraḥ saṃsthito harināgare \|*  
*pañcaśabdagajārūḍho mahāvatyadhipo gataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vimānavaramāruhya dhīvaraiḥ śatavāhikaiḥ \|*  
*maṇimuktāsvarṇamayaṃ sahasrairvādyakairyutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ayutaiśca patākaiśca vetrapāṇisahakrakaiḥ \|*  
*sahasraiḥ śibikābhiśca pañcasāhasrakai rathaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śakaṭairmahiṣoḍhaistu tathā pañcasahasrakaiḥ \|*  
*sarvatopaskṛtaṃ ramyaṃ brahmānaṃdaṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śrutvā kolāhalaṃ teṣāṃ mahīrājo nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*vismitaḥ sa babhūvātra śibirāṇi mudā dadau \|\| 35 \|\|*

24-35. To accompany the marriage party, seven lakhs of soldiers together with Talana reached the city of Mahavati. Ahlada had a lakh of soldiers and was also accompanied with Udayasimha and Sukhakhani. A lakh of soldiers were with Sukhakhani, a lakh of soldiers were also with Balakhana, Netrasimha also had a lakh of warriors, besides Yoga and Bhoga. Bali, who was always victorious in the battleground, also reached there with two lakhs of warriors. With twelve lakhs of army, Talana mounted over his mare named Simhini was leading the same. Then he reached the city of Dehali, where he made his army to rest, which was the capital city of Prthviraja. In the said journey, Devisimha mounted over the horse named Manoratha, Udayasimha over Bindula, Indula - the son of Svarnavati, mounted over he mare named Amrta, Rupana was mounted over the horse Karala, Ahlada over the horse Papiha, Balakhani over the horse Kapota, Sukhakhani over his horse Harina and the victorious Malana’s son Brahmananda mounted over the horse named Harinagara looking quite graceful. The king Parimala of Mahoba was himself seated over the king of elephants named Pancasabda. He also had an excellent plane which was fully decorated with costly pearls and gems and was carried by hundreds of carriers of low castes. Several types of musical instruments were sounded. There were guards numbering ten thousands who guarded it holding cane sticks in their hands. Besides there were a thousand attendants, a thousand palanquins, five thousand chariots, besides five thousand carts driven by male buffaloes that moved on surrounding Brahmananda. The turmoil of the marriage party surprised Prthviraja immensely. Thereafter, getting immensely pleased, he provided excellent camp accommodation for all of them.

## \|\| 2.120.36-44 \|\|

*durgadvāri kriyāṃ ramyāṃ kṛtvā vidhividhānataḥ \|*  
*draupadyā bhūṣaṇaṃ dehi velāyai sa tamabravīt \|\| 36 \|\|*

*indulastu yayau svargaṃ vāsavaṃ prati cābravīt \|*  
*draupadyā bhūṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ dehi mahyaṃ surottama \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kuberātsa samānīya divyamābhūṣaṇaṃ dadau \|*  
*indulaḥ praharānte ca prāptaḥ pitre nyavedayat \|\| 38 \|\|*

*āhlādastu svayaṃ gatvā velāye bhūṣaṇaṃ dadau \|*  
*prāpte brāhme muhūrte tu vivāhastatra cābhavat \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saṃprāpte prathamāvarte tārakaḥ khaḍgamādadau \|*  
*āhlādastaṃ samāsādya yuyudhe bahulīlayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*nṛharistu dvitīye ca kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ prati cārudhat \|*  
*tathā saradanaṃ vīraṃ balakhānirupāyayau \|\| 41 \|\|*

*mardanaṃ sukhakhānistu caturthāvartake'rudhat \|*  
*raṇajitsūryavarmāṇaṃ sa bhīmaṃ rūpaṇo balī \|*  
*devastu vardhanaṃ vīraṃ saptāvarte kramādyayau \|\| 42 \|\|*

*śatabhūpānkhaḍgadharāngajasenādikāṃstadā \|*  
*lakṣaṇādyāḥ samājagmurmaṃḍape bahuvistate \|\| 43 \|\|*

*bhagnabhūtaṃ nṛpabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*mahīrājo yayau rūḍho gajaṃ cāribhayaṃkaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

36-44. After performing the puja at the gate of the castle in an appropriate manner, he said-“Kindly send the ornaments of Draupadi for Vela.” On hearing this, Indula reached the heaven and said to Indra- “O best of the gods, you kindly get me the ornaments of Draupadi well.” Hearing these words, Indra at once sent the ornaments of Draupadi and handed them over to Indula. Receiving those ornaments, Indula at once returned with those ornaments to his father and respectfully handed over the ornaments to him. The Ahlada himself sent those ornaments to Vela for her use. Thereafter, the marriage ceremony started. At the time of the first circumambulation, Taraka attacked Brahmananda with the sword, but suddenly reaching there, Ahlada stopped the attack and fought bravely by his sports. During the second circumambulation, the attack of Nrhari was foiled by Udayasimha. During the third circumambulation, the attack of Saradana was prevented by Balakhana. Similarly, in the fourth circumambulation, the attack of Mardana was repulsed by Sukhakhani. During the fifth attack, Brahmananda himself repulsed the Attack of Suryavarma and Bhima subjugated Rupana. During the seventh circumambulation, Devisimha stopped the attack of Vardhana. At that point of time, in the vast mandapa, together with a hundred other rulers, Laksana started killing the armies of the king. Finding his own army getting shattered, the king Prthviraja getting enraged, mounted over an elephant named Aribhayankara and started fighting a war in the battleground.

## \|\| 2.120.45-55 \|\|

*jitvā tānnetrasiṃhādīñchabdavedhī nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ prayayau śīghraṃ bauddhinīṃ hastinīṃ sthitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*śivaṃ manasi saṃsthāpya jitvā baddhvā ruṣānvitaḥ \|*  
*agamattamupagṛhya darśayāmāsa taṃ nṛpam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śrutvā parimalo rājā kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ bhīruko yayau \|*  
*vṛttāntaṃ kathayāmāsa cāhrādādiparājayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ajitaḥ sa ca kṛṣṇāṃśo nabhomārgeṇa maṃdiram \|*  
*gatvā jagarja balavānyoginyānaṃdadāyakaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tadā sa lakṣaṇo vīrastyaktvā baṃdhanamuttamam \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ manasi saṃsthāpya mahīrājaṃ samāyayau \|\| 49 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā cāgamāṃ dolāṃ svayaṃ śibiramāptavān \|\| 50 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare sarve tyaktvā mūrcchāṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*khaḍgayuddhena tāñjitvā baddhvā tānnigaḍairdṛḍhaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sānvayāñchatabhūpāṃśca hatvā tadrudhirāvahaiḥ \|*  
*draupadīṃ snāpayāmāsurvelārūpāṃ kalottamām \|\| 52 \|\|*

*vivāhānte ca te sarve śibirāṇi samāyayuḥ \|*  
*samutsṛjya sutānsapta subhojyaiste hyabhojayan \|\| 53 \|\|*

*bhuktavatsu suvīreṣu sāhasrāstaiḥ sutaiḥ saha \|*  
*rurudhuḥ sarvato jaghnurastraśastraiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sahasraśūrāṃstānhatvā punarbaddhvā mahābalān \|*  
*śibirāṇi samājagmusteṣāṃ hāsyaviśāradāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

45-55. The best of the kings, who could shoot at the sound defeating Netrasimha and other warriors, reached Laksana who had been fighting seated over the cow elephant named Bauddhini. He fought a terrific war. Mentally devoting his mind towards Siva and getting enraged, Prthviraja became victorious over him and captured him. He bound him in chains and presented him before the king. Observing that, the king Parimala was immensely frightened and said to Udayasimha- “Ahlada and other rulers have been defeated in the fight with Prthviraja.” Then invincible Udayasimha at once went to the king’s palace through the sky way and reaching there, he thundered aloud. With Udayasimha who delighted the Yogini with his terrific roar, Laksana was enraged, broke his bondages and devoting his mind to lord Visnu, he reached the palace of Prthviraja. Carrying the queen Agama in a palanquin, he returned to his army camp. In the meantime, all the soldiers who had fainted regained the consciousness. Then all of them carrying swords in their hands, pounced upon the enemy army and killed the enemy warriors. Then while becoming victorious, they were put under chain and also handcuffed. Draupadi and beautiful Vela took their bath with that blood. After the marriage, all the warriors returned to their respective camps. Reaching there, the king freed his sons from the bondage. Reaching their abodes, they made arrangements for their food, inviting people to take their food. In the secret chambers of the fort, the well-armed soldiers had been hiding there. At the same time, the people of the marriage party from Mahoba arrived there, well equipped for taking food. All the seven sons of the king participated for serving food to the people of the marriage party. At the same time, the soldiers who had been hiding in the fort, started fighting. The people of the marriage party, discarding the food, captured a thousand warriors together with the seven princes and put them under chains. The captives were laughed at and were carried to the individual camps.

46-61. Thereafter, Prthviraja went to the king Parimala with ten lakhs of gold coins and the girl named Vela and prayed to him with folded hands- “O son of Pradyota, О king, the valorous Laksana has kidnapped my wife named Agama with the intention of making her a slave girl.” Hearing this, the king Parimala together with rulers, advised Laksana immensely, but he failed to accept their advice. Thereafter, the chaste Vela started lamenting quite loudly. Listening to her cries, both Udayasimha and Balakhani reassured Vela variously. Then both Udayasimha and Balakhani rushed through the sky way and reached before Laksana and scolded him. Thereafter, they carry Agama with them. Udayasimha lodged Agama in her palace. Then returning to his camp, he freed all the seven sons of Prthviraja. The princess of Prthviraja, after getting freed from the bondages, took an oath not to resort to the cheating again. О sage, in this way, after staying there for ten nights, the king departed for his capital city.

*ityu्ktvā ca vaco rājā sa snehādaṃkamaspṛśat \|*

*bhagnāsthī bhūpatī cobhau pāvakīyaiścikitsakaiḥ \|*  
*sukhavaṃtau gṛhaṃ prāpya kṛtakṛtyatvamāgatau \|\| 66 \|\|*

*malanā svasutaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāptamudvāhitaṃ gṛhe \|*  
*kṛtvotsavaṃ bahuvidhaṃ viprebhyaśca dadau dhanam \|*

*sabhāyāṃ lakṣaṇo vīro yātrākāle tamabravīt \|*

*nabhomārgeṇa saṃprāptau yoginau ca śivājñayā \|\| 68 \|\|*

62-68. At that point of time, with tears flowing from his eyes, Prthviraja uttered before the king, bowing at his feet- “O king, your bride is presently twelve years of age. Because of her being a small girl, she will not be able to bear separation from her parents, therefore, you can go home leaving her here. On her becoming adult, I shall present her to you with army. Thus speaking, the king Prthviraja lovingly met with the king Parimala. But with the meeting of both Prthviraja and Parimala, who had been deprived of limbs, Ahlada felt extremely painful. He caught hold of Prthviraja and broke his limbs. When the bones of both the rulers had been broken, Netrasimha who was. a physician as well, restored the limbs of both the kings and made them healthy. Thereafter, both of them returned to their respective abodes. The queen Malana finding that her son had been married, distributed charities to the Brahmanas with delight. She also performed homa for the goddess appropriately, in order to appease her. Then Laksana narrated the story of his journey in detail. He also told her that he had kidnapped Agama to make her the queen of Jayacandra, but at the command of lord Siva, both the yogi reached before me and snatched her away. Then she was sent back to her abode.

## \|\| 2.120.69 \|\|

*jahatustau ca māṃ jitvā tattīkṣṇabhaya mohitam \|*  
*adyāhaṃ dhāma gacchāmi ciraṃ jīva nṛpottama \|*  
*ityuktavaṃtaṃ taṃ natvā yayurbhūpāḥ svamālayam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Otherwise I had been bent upon as stated above. Thereafter, the king begged permission for his departure- “O best of rulers, let you enjoy long life. You kindly permit me. I intend to move to my place now.” After their departure, all the rulers received permission with all humility and returned to their respective places.

## Chapter 121. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.121.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*viṃśābde caiva kṛṣṇāṃśe yathā jātaṃ tathā śṛṇu \|*  
*sāgarākhyasarastīre kadācidiṃdulo balī \|*  
*japtvā saptaśatīstotraṃ tatra dhyānānvito'bhavat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare haṃsā ākāśādbhū mimāgatāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca rutaśabdaiśca sa dhyānādutthito'bhavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vakṣyamāṇaṃ vacaḥ prāhurdhanyo'yaṃ divyavigrahaḥ \|*  
*parvatānāṃ himagirirvanaṃ vṛṃdāvanaṃ tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mahāvatī purīṇāṃ ca sāgaraḥ sarasāmapi \|*  
*nārīṇāṃ padminī nārī nṛṇāṃ śreṣṭhastvamiṃdulaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bho indula mahāprājña mānase sarasi sthitāḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ śrutvā śriyo vākyaṃ nalinī sāgaraṃ gatāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said- I am now revealing the events of the twentieth year of the age of Udayasimha. You please listen. Once Udayasimha reached over the bank of the lake known by the name of Sagara and performed the recitation of Durga-saptasati. At the same moment, some swans descended there from the sky. Hearing the sound of the swans, the concentration of Udayasimha was disturbed. Soon thereafter, he got up and started hearing the voice of the swans, who spoke- “Graceful are the people who has the divine body. As the Himalaya is the best among the mountains, Vrndavana among the forest, Mahoba the best out of the cities, the ocean out of the reservoirs, similarly PadminI is the best among the ladies, while Indula is the best among the men.” Then addressing Indula, it spoke- “We are the swans, residents of the lake Manasarovara. Obeying the words of the goddess Laksmi, we had gone to Nalinisagara.

## \|\| 2.121.6-8 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tatra śubhāṃ nārīṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām \|*  
*saptālibhiryutāṃ ramyāṃ gītanāṭya viśāradām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā mohatvamāpannā vayaṃ deśāntaraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*vilokitā narāḥ sarve'trāsmābhirjagatītale \|*  
*tvatsamo na hi ko'pyatra padminī sadṛśo varaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ naḥ samāruhya tāṃ devīṃ draṣṭumarhasi \|*  
*tathetyuktvā śakrasuto haṃsarājaṃ samāruhat \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. We found there a beautiful damsel adorned with all the ornaments and had arrived there with her seven handmaids. Finding the damsel engaged in dance and music, we felt attracted towards her. Later we visited the entire world, but found no other woman comparable with PadminI. Therefore, you mount over us and get along with us there. Accepting their request, Indula mounted over the back of one of the swans.

## \|\| 2.121.7-15 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā mohatvamāpannā vayaṃ deśāntaraṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*vilokitā narāḥ sarve'trāsmābhirjagatītale \|*  
*tvatsamo na hi ko'pyatra padminī sadṛśo varaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ naḥ samāruhya tāṃ devīṃ draṣṭumarhasi \|*  
*tathetyuktvā śakrasuto haṃsarājaṃ samāruhat \|\| 8 \|\|*

*siṃhaladvīpake ramye hyāryasiṃho nṛpaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tatsutā padminī nāmnā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|*  
*rāgiṇyaḥ sapta vikhyātāstatsakhyaḥ pramadottamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*nalinīsāgare ramye girijāmaṃdiraṃ śubham \|*  
*tatra sthitāṃ ca tāṃ devīmindulaḥ sa dadarśa ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sāpi taṃ sundaraṃ dṛṣṭvā haṃsadehe samāsthitam \|*  
*saṃmohyāhūya taṃ devaṃ tena sārddhamarīramat \|\| 11 \|\|*

*varṣamekaṃ yayau tatra nānālīlāsu mohitaḥ \|*  
*naktaṃ divaṃ na bubudhe ramamāṇastayā saha \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhaktigarvatvamāpanne cāhlāde jagadaṃbikā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā cāntardadhe devī garvācaraṇakuṃṭhitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasya prāptaṃ mahadduḥkhamāhlādasya jayaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*sa kaiścitpuruṣairvīraḥ kathito'bhūtsva maṃdire \|\| 14 \|\|*

*indulaṃ rūpasampannaṃ laṃkāpuranivāsinaḥ \|*  
*rākṣasāstaṃ samāhṛtya svagehaṃ śīghramāyayuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

7-15. In the pleasant island of Simhala. a king named Aryasimha ruled the country. Padmini happened to be his daughter, who was unique beauty and youthful. All the seven Raginis became her friends in the form of beautiful damsels. In the temple of Parvati located over the bank of Nalinisagara, Padmini was enjoying recreation. Indula also reached there at the same time and had a look at Padmini. The beautiful Padmini also found a young man riding the back of the swan. Getting attracted towards his beauty, she called that man and enjoyed his company. Getting attracted with the various types of her sports, Indula stayed there for a year. In the mean time, Ahlada had become proud of his devotion for the goddess, who resolved to shatter his pride by all means. Subsequently, Ahlada had to face several misfortunes, because some people spoke to him in the same temple. The people of Lanka feeling attracted towards the beauty of Indula, have kidnapped him and have gone back to Lanka.

## \|\| 2.121.16-23 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ sakulo vilalāpa ha \|*  
*hāhāśabdo mahāṃścāsītteṣāṃ tu rudatāṃ mune \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśo ruditaṃ prāhāhlādaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ śṛṇuṣva bhoḥ \|*  
*jitvāhaṃ rākṣasānsarvāṃstālanādyaiḥ samanvitaḥ \|*  
*iṃdulaṃ tvāṃ sameṣyāmi bhavāndhairyaparo bhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*balakhāniśca kṛṣṇāṃśo devasiṃhaśca tālanaḥ \|*  
*saptalakṣabalaiḥ sārddhaṃ lakāṃ prati yayurmudā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mārgaprāptāśca ye bhūpā grāmapā rāṣṭrapāstathā \|*  
*yathāyogya baliṃ ramyaṃ prāpya tasmai nyavedayan \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ye bhūpā madamattāśca jitvā tāṃstālano balī \|*  
*baddhvā taiśca samāgacchatsetubaṃdhaṃ śivasthalam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā ca rāmeśaṃ rāmeṇa sthāpitaṃ śivam \|*  
*siṃhaladvīpamaganṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare tadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nalinīsāgaraṃ prāpya tatra vāsamakārayan \|*  
*patraṃ saṃpreṣayāmāsa balakhānirnṛpāya ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*āryyasiṃha mahābhāga svapotāndehi tīrṇakān \|*  
*bhavāṃśca svabalaiḥ sārddhaṃ laṃkāṃ prati vrajādhunā \|*  
*no cettvāṃ sabalaṃ jitvā rāṣṭrabhaṃgaṃ karomyaham \|\| 23 \|\|*

16-23. On hearing this, Ahlada started lamenting with his family. О sage, while so crying, he uttered pathetic words from his month. At that point of time, Udayasimha, who had been completely upset, spoke with confidence-“Along with Talana and others, I shall defeat all the Raksasas and bring back Indula, but you kindly be patient. Subsequently, Balakhani, Udayasimha, Devasimha and Talana departed towards Lanka with seven lakh soldiers of his army. Whichever rulers met on the way, they all prayed to these people who felt intoxicated with their pride. The valorous Talana defeated them all, captured them all and putting them in chains and handcuffs, made them to accompany them. In this way, they reached the vicinity of the Siva temple at Setubandha, Ramesvaram. All of them worshipped lord Siva there and then proceed on the journey to the island of Simhala. They reached there in six months and camped there over the bank of Nalinisagara. Balakhani then wrote a letter and sent it to the king of Lanka- “O auspicious one, О Aryasimha, send your boats because we intend to visit your city. Or otherwise, you arrive in Lanka, with your army. Otherwise, shattering your army, I shall destroy your kingdom.”

*indulaḥ staṃbhanaṃ maṃtraṃ saṃsthāpya śara uttame \|*  
*staṃbhayāmāsa tatsainyaṃ tālanādyaiḥ surakṣitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*divase sukhaśarmā ca trilakṣaiḥ svadalaiḥ saha \|*

24-29. Reading the letter, the valorous king, who was guarded by Indula - the son of Indra, at once started for waging the war. Indula on the other hand, making use of the stupefying mantra, initiated an arrow and stupefied the entire army of Talana and others. Sukhasarma fought during the day with his soldiers who were three lakhs in number. During the night, Indula accompanied with a hundred princes marched for the waging of the war, He had the steed of green colour, while the princes had disguised themselves as yogins. This small contingent of soldiers killed thousands of soldiers. They lived comfortably in their abodes. Thus both the armies fought continuously for a period of six months in which the vast army of Balakhana was destroyed.

## Chapter 122. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-8. Suta said- Observing the destruction of his army, the valorous Balakhana felt painful at heart and commanded to stop the war. Then he summoned Devasimha, who was well aware of the activities of all the three times, and called all the associates for consultation. Listening to his words, the valorous Devasimha, who had been a great yogi as well, spoke to all of them-“One of the son of Indra who is well-versed in the use of all the weapons, with the help of a divine weapon will make all your weapons infructuous in the morning itself. Thereafter, reaching in the night, he will himself kill all your soldiers. Therefore, with my help, together with Talana and Udayasimha, you gain victory over the son of Indra, otherwise all of you getting destroyed, shall reach the place of Yama.” On haring the words of Devasimha, the valorous Balakana, with the help of his brothers and friends, started making all the efforts. At that point of time, Udayasimha had reached the age of twenty first year. Then Udayasimha, the leader of that war, concealed his army in a ship. At the dead of night, he kept half of the army in the ship and the other half of the same was made to march. They were all cavalry and were also well-versed in the art of war.

9-17. Reaching the city gate, they opened the strong gate and killing the guards there, they started plundering the city. Subsequently, they reached the enemy fort and started killing the enemy soldiers. In the meantime, Udayasimha reached the residential palaces, where they found the queen Padmini with exquisite beauty and was observed with her seven handmaids in singing and dancing. They put her in a palanquin and carried her to their camp, where a terrific battle was fought. The valorous Balakhana on the other hand, with the help of Deva and Talana, destroyed the enemy army which had been fighting under the command of Indula. Thereafter, Satyavarma - the enemy commander was surrounded, defeated and captured. Both the infuriated warriors then killed Satyavarma. Getting immensely enraged, Indula (Jayanta) brought back his own brother-in-law to life with the army and then returned to his palace. Finding the people crying there, he went to the palace of his beloved, but he could not find his beloved there with her handmaids. Then he went to the palace of Aryasimha and came to know of the factual position. Then he came to know that the enemies who were well-versed in the use of weapons, had plundered his abode and had kidnapped his beloved.

18-30. The brave heart then started crying. He lamented- “O my beloved, О passionate one, you show me your face atonce. Your husband is quite anxious to see your face.” Thus lamenting and crying, he picked up his bow and arrow besides the sword which confused the enemy. Getting enraged, he reached the battleground alone. At the same time, the valorous Balakhana, at the sight of the beautiful damsel, started lamenting- “O Indula, the valorous one, О my dear brother, this beautiful damsel is fit to be your wife alone. Where have you disappeared? You appear at once and own this beautiful damsel.” Thus lamenting, he started adoring lord Siva mentally, Balakhana was fainted. In the mean time, the valorous Indula - the son of Indra, destroyed the army fighting under the command of Udayasimha. Thereafter, finding his army getting destroyed, the commander Talana mounted over the mare known by the name of Simhini and uttered a lion’s roar. He declared- “O valorous one, you cannot be victorious simply with the destruction of the army. О Yogi, first of all you kill me and thereafter you kill my soldiers.” On hearing these words, the terrific Indula shot an arrow at the heart of Talana, which was destroyed by the latter with his sword. Thereafter, with the attack of a spear, Indula was fainted. When Indula became unconscious, the mare taking to the divine form reached in the sky, where Indula regained his consciousness. At that point of time, the boy placed the kalastra over his bow, which created terrific sound and by which Talana was dead. At the death of the army commander, Udayasimha reached there by the sky way and started thundering there again and again. At that particular moment, Indula shot a fire arrow at Udayasimha as a result of which fire was spread in the sky. Udayasimha then made use of vayavya weapon.

31-36. Udayasimha then consumed the force of the weapon with his yogic practices and reached at the back of Indula. Indula - the son of Indra, then observing the audacity of the enemy, made use of gandharvastra in order to confuse him, which was destroyed by Udayasimha by his yogic powers. Udayasimha in this way destroyed all the weapons used against himself by Indula again and again making all his efforts infructuous. Indula then getting enraged, got down from the mare and standing over the earth, started fighting with his sword. In the mean time, the rulers like Devasirhha and others had a glance of the terrific war, which surprised them all.

37-45. At the time of dawn, the valorous Balakhana looked at Indula, who looked graceful having been clad in deer hide and the matted locks of hair over the head. The glorious son of Indra appeared as having b een immensely fatigued. Then he took oath of his father, who happened to be the brother of Balakhana- “O son of Krsna (Udayasimha), I shall cut off your head with this sword. In case I fail to do so, you think my mother to be an unchaste lady.” With this firm resolve, having been filled with blemish and holding a sword in his hand, he reached close to Balakhana. Looking at him, with his throat choked, Balakhana threw away his weapon and he reached before his son and said- “O Indula, you are immensely fortunate since you extend glory to your parents. You are mental son of Ahlada and Svarnavati. Therefore, О valorous one, you first kill me, then kill your uncle Udayasimha, Devasimha and the entire family. Thereafter, you can live comfortably in the house of Sukhavarma and enjoy all the pleasures there.” On hearing these words of Balakhana, the boy then thought them to be belonging to the same family, threw away the sword at a distance and atonce placed his head over the feet of his uncle. Then crying aloud, he begged forgiveness, saying- “O my dear respectable uncle, it has been said in the Vedas that the women entice the men, irrespective of their being gods, humans, serpents or danavas. Therefore, they are blemished. The net of womanhood always remains ready to overpower the others.

46-52. I am facing the same today. Inspite of my being the son of Indra known as Jayanta and also of the father Ahlada who is totally purified, I had been born in that race, but falling in the beauty of Padmini, I never thought in this regard. Therefore, you kindly forgive an unfortunate and foolish person like me for my sins.” Thus speaking, the boy overwhelmed with love and affection, again started crying. He further said- “I have brought back to life the entire army as well as the valorous Talana.” Hearing the words of the boy, feeling extremely blissful, Udayasimha took the boy in his lap. Thereafter, he celebrated a huge function in the same area. On hearing this news, Aryasimha also married the girl PadminI, with Indula giving enormous riches in an appropriate manner Besides the girl, several of huge elephants decorated with pearls and gems and ornaments, were given over to the son-in-law. Thereafter, these people, having been overwhelmed with sweet words, returned to their abodes. From there, they returned to their respective countries delightfully.

*daśahārākhyanagaraṃ saṃprāptaḥ svakulaissaha \|*
