53-58. They covered the horrible distance in a month and reached Kirtisagara. They performed celebrations. Getting extremely pleased after meeting his son and the bride, Ahlada invited the Brahmanas and distributed several types of charities among them, pleasing them at the same time. Thereafter, all the people of the Dasahara city collected there with their families and sung the enormous glory of Udayasimha, which had been spread in the far off lands. Even Prthviraja also expressed his surprise on learning about the tale of Jayasimha. PadminI was when cursed by the sage Durvasa, from an Apsara she was bom over the earth as a damsel. She remained graceful on earth upto the age of twelve years. Then she attracted the disease of consumption and again proceeded on to the heaven. She lived in the palace o f Ahlada for nine months only.

## Chapter 123. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.123.1-7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*mune pāṃcāladeśe tu rājāsīdbalavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*tasya patnī viśālākṣī jaladevīti viśrutā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bisenavaṃśabhūpālo vedatattvaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*sastrīkaḥ pūjayāmāsa varuṇaṃ yādasāṃ patim \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasya putrāvubhau jātau kṣatradharmaparāyaṇau \|*  
*laharo jyeṣṭhatanayo mayūradhvaja eva hi \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdavayā bhūtvā mayūradhvaja eva saḥ \|*  
*ājñayā jyeṣṭhabaṃdhośca skaṃdadevamatoṣayat \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yateṃdriyastathā maunī vānaprastha parāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*paṃcābdaṃ tadvratī bhūtvā japadhyānaparobhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavānsenānīragnibhūḥ svayam \|*  
*svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa sarvāścaryasamanvi tam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mayūradhvaja evāpi dṛṣṭvā sarvamayaṃ śiśum \|*  
*devasenāsahāyaṃ ca tuṣṭāva ślakṣṇayā girā \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta said- Once in the Pancala (Punjab) region, a king named Balavardhana ruled there. He had a beautiful queen having vast eyes who was known by the name of Jaladevi. The king was well-versed in the Vedas, worshipped Varuna couple - the lord of waters, as a result of which two sons were bom to him, who were devoted to the K$atriya dharma. The elder one was known as Lahara, while the younger one was known as Mayuradhvaja. At the age of twelve years, Mayuradhvaja, with the permission of his elder brother, started worshipping Skandadeva. Observing strict discipline and maintaining silence, he lived in the forest like a forest dweller for five years. He performed japam in an appropriate manner. Thereafter, Skanda - the army commander as well as the son of the fire god, feeling extremely pleased, graced Mayurahvaja by appearing before him in a wonderful form. Sighting the wonderful god who happened to be his family deity too, he tried his best to please him with his sweet voice.

## \|\| 2.123.8-17 \|\|

*mayūradhvaja uvāca \|*  
*jayati te vapurdivyavigrahaṃ nayati sarvadā devatāgaṇān \|*  
*pibati mātriyaṃ dugdhamuttamaṃ vadhati sarvadā daityadānavān \|\| 8 \|\|*

*namaste devaseneśa mahiṣāsuramardana \|*  
*ṣaḍānana mahābāho tārakaprāṇanāśaka \|\| 9 \|\|*

*prasanno bhava sarvātmanguhaśaktidharāvyaya \|*  
*kiṃkaraṃ pāhi māṃ nityaṃ śaraṇāgatavatsala \|\| 10 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā stutiṃ tasya senānīstamuvāca vai \|*  
*kiṃ te'bhīṣṭaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha mattaḥ sarvamavāpsyasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ityuktastena devena bhūpatiḥ prāha namradhīḥ \|*  
*balaṃ me dehi bhagavansahāyaṃ kuru sarvadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tathetyuktvā tu taṃ skaṃdastatraivāntardadhe punaḥ \|*  
*sa nṛpastu prasannātmā kārayāmāsa vai puram \|\| 13 \|\|*

*nāmnā mayūranagaraṃ naravṛṃdasamanvitam \|*  
*dviyojanāyāmayutaṃ skaṃdadevena rakṣitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*laharo nāmā tadbaṃdhurdvidaśābdaprayatnataḥ \|*  
*varuṇaṃ pūjayāmāsa nadīnadasamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavānvaruṇo yādasāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*varaṃ brūhīti vacanaṃ premṇovāca mahīpatim \|\| 16 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā'mṛtamayaṃ vacanaṃ laharo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva ślakṣṇayā vācā pāśinaṃ payasāṃ patim \|\| 17 \|\|*

8-17. Mayurahvaja said- Victory to this divine body possessed by you, which manages the army of gods, sucks the milk of your mother and kills all the armies of Daityas and Danavas. О lord of the divine army, you are the destroyer of Mahisasura, you have six faces, you have long arms and are the killer of Tarakasura. Salutation to you. You are the soul of whole universe, you possess the Guha-sakti, be pleased with me always. You are graceful on those who take refuge with you. You protect a servant like me. On hearing this, Skanda said- “O best of the rulers, what do you desire to have? You tell me. You can achieve everything from me.” At these words of lord Skanda, the king spoke with humility-“O lord, you kindly bestow your enormous strength on me and always be helpful to me.” Accepting it, lord Skanda disappeared at the same time. The king getting pleased built a city there which was given the name of Mayurnagara. The people of various castes lived there. The city was spread in an area of two yojanas and was guarded by Skandadeva. Lahara - the brother of Mayuradhvaja also performed tapas for twenty years making great efforts over the bank of a river for lord Vanina. At that point of time, lord Varuna spoke to Lahara in sweet voice- “O king, you ask for a boon.” Hearing the nectar like words, the king Lahara spoke in his pleasant voice to Varuna - the lord of waters as well as the carrier of a noose, pleasing him at the same time.

## \|\| 2.123.18-28 \|\|

*lahara uvāca \|*  
*yasya cittaṃ mahajjñeyaṃ tapo balasamanvitam \|*  
*ataḥ pracetāste nāma namastubhyaṃ pracetase \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ruṇaddhi payasāṃ vegaṃ na kenāpyavarodhitaḥ \|*  
*atastvaṃ varuṇo nāma namaste varuṇāya vai \|\| 19 \|\|*

*daityānāṃ baṃdhanārthāya devānāṃ jayahetave \|*  
*divyaḥ pāśastvayānītaḥ pāśine te namonamaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*iti stutastadā devo rājñā tenaiva dhīmatā \|*  
*nagarīṃ kārayāmāsa lāharīmatha cottamām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*triyojanāyāmayutāṃ caturvarṇasamanvitām \|*  
*svayaṃ ca grāmarakṣārthe tatrovāsa jalā dhipaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bhūpastu tatprasādena prāpa rājñīṃ śubhānanām \|*  
*rāvī nāma mahāśreṣṭhā jñeyā devāṃganopamā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa sutānṣo ḍaśasaṃmitān \|*  
*dhārtarāṣṭrāṃśajānmukhyāngajatulyabalānvitān \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tatpaścātkanyakā jātā nāmnā madanamaṃjarī \|*  
*dvādaśābdavayaḥprāpte sutāyāḥ sa tu bhūpatiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*devasiṃhaṃ varaṃ matvā caṃdravaṃśinamuttamam \|*  
*prāhūya jyeṣṭhatanayaṃ preṣayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*raṇadhīrastu tanayo lakṣamudrānvito balī \|*  
*sahasraśabarasahitaḥ prāptavānsa mahāvatīm \|\| 27 \|\|*

*natvā parimalaṃ bhūpaṃ tadīyātkulaśālinaḥ \|*  
*svahetuṃ varṇayāmāsa vivāhārthe svasuḥ svayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

18-28. Lahara said- Because of your having enormous tapas to your credit, you possess a great mind and because of it, you also came to be known as Praceta. I offer my salutation to lord Praceta. You are forceful enough to stop the force of the water without much effort, which cannot be controlled by anyone else. You were therefore given the name of Varuna. I offer my salutation to Varuna. You patronized the weapon pasa (noose) for binding the daityas and for the victory of the gods. Therefore, I offer my salutation again and again to the carrier of pasa. Thus eulogizing lord Varuna, the intelligent king built a city named Lahari which was spread in an area of three yojanas and was graced by the people of all the four varnas. Lord Varuna himself resided there for the protection of that city. In due course of time, the king got a beautiful wife by the grace of lord Varuna, who was known by the name of Kalyanamukhi or Rajni. She possessed enormous beauty like a young damsel. The king produced sixteen sons from the womb of that queen, who were having their amsas from Kauravas - the sons of Dhrtarastra and were as valorous as the king of elephants. Later on, a most beautiful girl named Madanamanjari was also bom. On her attaining the age of twelve years, the king thought of marrying her to the king Devasimha of the lunar dynasty and for that purpose, he sent his elder son to the king Devasimha. Together with a thousand brave warriors and a lakh of gold coins, the son Ranadhira departed towards the city of Mahavati. Reaching there, the prince offered his salutation to the king Parimala and his relatives and revealed to them the cause of his arrival there- “I have arrived here for the sake of the marriage of my sister here.”

## \|\| 2.123.29-33 \|\|

*śrutvā parimalo bhūpo devasiṃhaṃ mahāmatim \|*  
*āhūya vacanaṃ prāha vivāhārthe manaḥ kuru \|\| 29 \|\|*

*devasiṃhastu balavānpitṛvyaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|*  
*vivāhaṃ na kariṣyāmi brahmacaryaṃ vrataṃ mama \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bahudhā prārthitassarvairdvijavṛṃdasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*na tatyāja vrataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ devasiṃho mahāmatiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tadā parimalo bhūpo raṇadhīraṃ vaco'bravīt \|*  
*sukhakhānirayaṃ bālo vivāhārthe vadāmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tatheti matvā sa nṛpo raṇadhīro gṛhaṃ yayau \|*  
*pitaraṃ kathayāmāsa sukhakhānirmahāvrataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

29-33. On hearing these words, the king summoned the intelligent Devasimha and said- “I have a great desire that you accept this marriage proposal.” On hearing this, Devasimha meekly spoke to his uncle- “I have taken the vow for the performing of Brahmacarya, therefore, I am unable to accept the proposal for marriage.” On hearing this, the Brahmanas assembled there and did their best to convince the prince for marriage, but Devasimha declined to accept the proposal for the marriage. He remained firm over his resolve. Thereafter, the king Parimala said to Ranadhira- “For this relationship, I hand over the boy Sukhakhani to you. Therefore, you better fix up the marriage with him.” The king Ranadhira accepted the said proposal with delight and then departed to his abode. Reaching there, he praised the beauty and vrata of Sukhakhani.

## \|\| 2.123.34-46 \|\|

*etasminnantare dhūrto mahīpatiruvāca tam \|*  
*ayogyo'yaṃ vivāho'tra pāvakīye kulottame \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śūdrīyo'tra varo rājanvarṇasaṃkarakārakaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ sainyasahito jetuṃ tāngaṃtumarhasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kārāgāre lohamaye baṃdhanaṃ kuru bhūpateḥ \|*  
*matkīrtiḥ svargagā nityaṃ jagatyaṃte bhaviṣyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

*jitastairjambuko rājā netrasiṃhastu yo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tathā gajapatirbhūpaḥ pṛthvīrājo mahābalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*āryasiṃhastathānye ca jitāste balavattarāḥ \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco ramyaṃ laharo nṛpasattamaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*senāṃ saṃsthāpayāmāsa caturaṃgabalānvitām \|*  
*caturlakṣamitāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ pālitāṃ ṣoḍaśātmajaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*māghaśukladaśamyāṃ ca balakhāniṃ mahābalaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptaḥ svakulaissārddhaṃ caturlakṣabalānvitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*deśe pāṃcālake ramye laharīnagare sthitaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśābde ca kṛṣṇāṃśe tatra vāsamakārayat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nṛpaterājñayā śūrā yuddhāya samupāyayuḥ \|*  
*balakhānistu dharmātmā dṛṣṭvā śūrāṃstathāgatān \|*  
*vīrānājñāpayāmāsa svakīyānsaṃgare punaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tayoryuddhamabhūdghoraṃ senayorlomaharṣaṇam \|*  
*paṃcame'hni divā prāpte balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśenaiva sahito riporvadhamakārayat \|\| 43 \|\|*

*parājitāśca te śūrā hataśeṣā bhayāturāḥ \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā ṣoḍaśasutā rathaṃ svaṃsvaṃ samāsthitāḥ \|*  
*yuddhāyābhimukhaṃ jagmurdhanurbāṇaviśāradāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśastāṃstathā dṛṣṭvā śaravarṣasamanvitān \|*  
*ekākī prayayau śīghraṃ khaḍgacarmadharo balī \|\| 45 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ dhanūṃṣi saṃchidya baddhvā tānyuddhadurmadān \|*  
*āhlādāya dadau vīraḥ kṛṣṇāṃśo raṇakovidaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

34-46. At the command of the king, the army declared a war. In order to become victorious in the battleground, the religious-minded Balakhana, observing the arrival of the warriors, issued a command to his warriors. The battle between both the armies started. On the fifth day, the valorous Balakhana together with Udayasimha destroyed the enemies. Several of the enemy warriors met with their death in the battlefield, while others fled away getting terrified. Finding their army in disarray, the sixteen princes, who were well-versed in the art of archery, mounted over their respective chariots, reached the battleground and started fighting. Finding the princes pouring the rain of arrows, Udayasimha also reached the battleground and carrying a sword and a shield, destroyed their bows alone and captured them. Thereafter, Udayasimha, who was well-versed in war, brought the princes and handed them over to Ahlada.

## \|\| 2.123.47-53 \|\|

*putrāṇāṃ bandhanaṃ śrutvā laharo nṛpasattamaḥ \|*  
*plāvayāmāsa tatsainyaṃ balakhānermahātmanaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*jalībhūte tathā sainye jayanto balavattaraḥ \|*  
*vāyavyāstreṇa samare śuśoṣa sakalaṃ jalam \|*  
*laharasya tataḥ senāmuvāha bahuyojanam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*tadā tu bhagavāndevo varuṇo yādasāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*sutāmudvāhayāmāsa laharasya mahīpateḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*laharo'pi prasannātmā jñātvāṃśaṃ jagatītale \|*  
*bhaktiṃ cakāra śuddhānāmaṃśānāṃ parayā mudā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dattvā ca bahudhā dravyaṃ parikramya punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*svānte niveśayāmāsa māsamātraṃ prasannadhīḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*aṃśāste'pi mahāpūjāṃ gṛhītvā laharapradām \|*  
*dolāmāropya tāṃ devīṃ svagehāya yayurmudā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra kṛṣṇāṃśacaritaṃ śubham \|*  
*sukhakhānervivāhaṃ ca śrutvānaṃdamavāpnuyāt \|\| 53 \|\|*

47-53. Learning about the capture of his sons, the king Lahara made the soldiers of the army of Balakhana to be carried away with the force of the current of water. Then the valorous Jayanta, making use of the windarrow, dried up the water. Besides he drove away the enemy army at a distance of many yojanas. At the same time, lord Vanina - the lord of waters, himself performed the marriage of the daughter of Lahara with the valorous Sukhakhani. Learning about this, the king Lahara was immensely pleased and he became a great devotee of lord Vanina on earth. Thereafter, the valuable belongings of all the dead soldiers were placed over their respective bodies and they were praised repeatedly. They were lodged in the palace delightfully for a month as guests. The warriors also respected their honour. Then they placed the bride in the palanquin and returned delightfully. О Brahmana, I have thus related the story of Udayasimha to you. You would be delighted to know about the marriage of Sukhakhani.

## Chapter 124

## \|\| 2.124.1 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*gṛhaṃ gatvā ca te vīrāḥ kiṃ cakruścaritaṃ śubham \|*  
*tattvaṃ kathaya viprendra sarvajño'si mato hi naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rsis said- O Indra among the Brahmanas, reaching their respective abodes whatever activities were performed by the valorous warriors, you please speak out the same, because you are all knowledgeable among all of us.

## \|\| 2.124.2-9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*gṛhamāgatya te sarve parito bhūpateḥ sabhām \|*  
*gatvā vārtāṃ tathā cakruryathā jāto mahāraṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śrutvā parimalo bhūpo vājivṛṃdaṃ kṣayaṃ gatam \|*  
*āhūya sa ca kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ vacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*siṃdhudeśe ca gaṃtavyaṃ tvayā ca balaśālinā \|*  
*pañcalakṣānhayānkṛtvā punarāgaccha vai gṛham \|\| 4 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu kṛṣṇāṃśo devasiṃhena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*svarṇabhārasahasroṣṭrāngṛhītvā tarasā yayau \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śūraiśca daśasāhasraissārddhaṃ tatra samāgataḥ \|*  
*mayūranagarī yatra caturvarṇasamanvitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prātaḥkāle tu saṃprāpte mālākārasya vai sutā \|*  
*puṣpānāma samāsannā cāraṃbhe kusumārthinī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśastu tadā pūjāṃ kṛtvā devamayo mudā \|*  
*jagāma vipinaṃ ramyaṃ vasaṃte puṣpanālike \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bahvāścaryayutaṃ puṣpa mattabhramaranāditam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā mumoha kṛṣṇāṃśastadarthe svayamudyataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

2-9. Suta said- Reaching their abodes, all the warriors decorated the assembly of the king. Parimala narrated the details of the war fought by them to the king. Listening to the words of the warriors that there had been an excessive loss of the steed in the battle, then he called for Udayasimha and humbly said to him- “You go to the Sindhu valley and purchase five lakhs of horses and return to this place.” On hearing this, together with Devasimha, Udayasimha loaded a lakhs of gold bharas over the camels and departed from that place with ten thousand attendants. Reaching the city named Mayura of that country in the morning which looked quite graceful with the people of all the four castes, they found that the daughter of a gardener was moving with flowers. Udayasimha - the amsa of the gods, in a delightful mood, also reached in the same orchard after finishing his worship. The buds were looking charming there in the spring season, besides the intoxicated black wasps were hovering over the buds. Observing the beauty of that garden, Udayasimha got fascinated.

## \|\| 2.124.10-18 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare puṣpā puṣpārthaṃ samupāgatā \|*  
*dadarśa devasadṛśaṃ ṣoḍaśābdamayaṃ naram \|*  
*prasannavadanaṃ śāntamiṃdranīlamaṇidyutim \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśastu śubhāṃ nārīṃ dṛṣṭvāścaryamupāgataḥ \|*  
*papraccha vacasā tāṃ vai kasyeyaṃ surasuṃdarī \|*  
*svargalokādihāyātā yadi vā pannagī svayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā ca sā prāha mālākārasya vai sutā \|*  
*ahaṃ śūdrī mahābāho puṣpārthaṃ samupāgatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*puṣpeṇānena bhūpāla tulitā bhūpateḥ sutā \|*  
*nāmnā puṣpavatī devī rādheva saguṇāvalī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*devaiśca prārthitā bālā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|*  
*makaraṃdabhayāddevāstasyā yogyā na vai balāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ bhūpa makaraṃdo yathā bhavet \|*  
*mayūradhvajabhūpena saṃprāpto guhato varaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ajeyo'nyaiśca kṛṣṇāṃśādṛte tvaṃ jagatītale \|*  
*tanmitraṃ pṛthivīrājo rājarājaḥ śivapriyaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sa rājyaṃ kārayāmāsa dharmameghaṃ haripriyam \|*  
*tadā prasanno bhagavānyajñeśo yajñamūrtimān \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mithunaṃ janayāmāsa pāvakātsuṃdarānanam \|*  
*makaraṃdaḥ suto jñeyaḥ kanyā puṣpavatī matā \|\| 18 \|\|*

10-18. At the same time, Puspa (the daughter of the gardener) also reached there for the collection of the flowers and she found that the man there in the orchard was as beautiful and sixteen years of age. He had a delightful face. He was quite peaceful in nature and the complexion of his body resembled the lustre of sapphire. Finding that damsel there, Udayasimha also felt surprised. Then he asked her- “Whose beloved is this girl resembling the divine damsel, who has arrived here from the heaven or is she a serpent girl?” On hearing this, the daughter of the gardener said-“O long-armed one, I have been bom in an auspicious race and have arrived here for collecting the flowers. О monarch, by means of the same merit, the princess would be measured. She is known by the name of Puspavati Devi and she had earned fame because of her virtues like Radha. Even the gods aspire to get this beautiful damsel. Being fearful from Makaranda, the gods are unable to use their force against me. О monarch, I am going to reveal the reason for the same. You please listen. The king Mayuradhvaja has received a boon from Skanda that besides Udayasimha, you are invincible from all other rulers or warriors on earth. He has Prthviraja as his friend, who is king of kings, besides being devoted to lord Siva. Once the king, in order to please lord Visnu, performed the Dharmamedha yajna. Getting pleased at that time, lord Yajnesa produced the twin children with the glowing faces resembling the fire. The twins comprised of a son named Makaranda and a daughter named Puspavati.

## \|\| 2.124.19-26 \|\|

*pañcamābdavayā bhūtvā makaraṃdo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva tapasā dharmaṃ vedadharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdavayaḥ prāpte makaraṃde nṛpapriye \|*  
*prasanno bhagavāndharmo dadau tasmai mahāhayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śilāmayaṃ mahāvegaṃ śatrusenākṣayaṃkaram \|*  
*tamaśvaṃ svayamāruhya sarvapūjyo hyabhūtsukhī \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasyedaṃ suṃdaraṃ divyaṃ vipinaṃ surapūjitam \|*  
*bhavānarhati vai śreṣṭhaḥ puṣpavatyāḥ kalevaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ smarapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*dadau bahudhanaṃ tasyai mālinyā gehamāgataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*devasiṃhastu kālajño jñātvā mohatvamāgatam \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ bodhayāmāsa padyaiḥ sāṃkhyasamudbhavaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśastu tatassārddhaṃ devasiṃhena tanmayaḥ \|*  
*siṃdhudeśaṃ samāgatya krītvā sarvahayāṃstadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*māsānte gṛhamāgatya rājñe sarvānnyavedayat \|*  
*puṣpavatyāḥ śubhaṃ rūpaṃ dhyātvā puṣperitaṃ balī \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśo mohamāgatya tuṣṭāva jagadaṃbikām \|\| 26 \|\|*

19-26. At the age of five years, the immensely valorous Makaranda, who was well-versed in the Vedas, pleased lord Dharma with his tapas. At the age of twelve years, lord Dharma getting pleased with him, gave him a divine horse which was stone like and which could move with great speed and could destroy the enemy army. With the owning of that horse, he became comfortable and adorable by all. This beautiful orchard belongs to him, which is divine and is worshipped even by the gods. Thereafter, she also said- “The beauty and charm of Puspavati is meant for you.” On hearing these words, Udayasimha felt attracted towards her and he became passionate as well. Thereafter, giving her enormous riches, he went to her abode. Then Devasimha, who could visualize the future time, finding that Udayasimha had been attracted towards the girl, delivered to him the discourse on Samkhya philosophy and enlightened him. Thereafter, Devasimha together with Udayasimha, reached the Sindhu country, purchased the horses, reached back his home by the month end and handed over the horses to the king. Once recalling the auspicious beauty of Puspavati and feeling fascinated towards her, Udayasimha once adored goddess Jagadamba.

27-33. Udayasimha said- О divine mother, you are always auspicious, having the eternal form. I am suffering immensely because of the cupid or the god of love. You better protect me besides attracting Puspavati towards me. You are the one who confused the daityas Madhu and Kaitabha, besides being the killer of Mahisasura. О goddess, protecting the passionate person like me, you enlighten Puspavati too. You are the one who reduced daitya Dhumralocana to ashes besides being the destroyer of Canda and Munda. О goddess, you drank the blood of Raktabija and frightened all the daityas. О goddess, you are the destroyer of the daityas Sumbha and Nisumbha, you kindly protect me, who is suffering from passion. You kindly attract Puspavati towards me.” Thus, while so adoring the goddess, he sat over his excellent seat. At that point of time, the goddess Sarada appeared before Udayasimha in dream. Similarly, the bestower of the boon continued to appear in his dream during each night and this way, four months of the rainy season were passed. At that stage, Udayasimha had reached the age of twenty three years.

34-41. At the start of the month of Kartika, Udayasimha accompanied with Devasimha, departed towards the city of Mayura protected by Makaranda. Reaching there, they started living in the house of Puspamalini. Once Udayasirnha made a garland of flowers in which gems and beads were studded. It was extremely attractive. Puspa carried it to the palace of Puspavati. Looking at the attractive garland which was quite attractive like Tvastra, Puspavati getting attracted wore it over her breast and then she said- “O handmaid, you speak truthfully before me. Wherefrom have you got this beautiful garland which has attracted my mind?” Hearing these words and having been frightened from Makaranda, holding flowers in her palm Puspa spoke to her- “In case you assure my life, then I shall speak out the truth.” At the assurance of Puspavati, Puspa said- “There is a sister of mine known by the name of Krsna, who is extremely beautiful and attracts the world. She lives in the capital city of Mahavati Presently, she has arrived in my house. This pleasant garland was made by her.”

42-54. On hearing this, Puspavati said to Malini-“Let me meet her atonce. You are aware of the fact that because of the fear of Makaranda, no person can reach me. I am telling you the truth.” Listening to these harsh words and getting frightened, Puspa could speak nothing further, though Puspavati asked her again and again. At this, Puspavati then asked her- “Are you afraid of something.” At this, she said-“My sister is extremely beautiful and in case she comes here and someone getting attracted towards her assaults her physically, then I shall be as good as dead. I have spoken to you because you always follow the family dharma as well as the tradition.” On hearing this, Puspavati, who was the incarnation of dharma, spoke again- “You are well aware of the fact that my father Mayuradhvaja is quite statesman and in case anyone does so as you says, he shall have to proceed to the abode of Yama. Therefore, you bring your sister in a palanquin and after her meeting with me, you can return with her to your home.” Accepting this, the damsel of Sudra caste returned home and apprised Udayasimha of the factual position. О sage, listening to the beautiful words, Udayasimha pricked his nose himself and wore all the ornaments. He turned himself into a beautiful damsel and then proceeded on to the place of Puspavati together with Puspa. At the sight of the beautiful Krsna, Puspavati said to Puspa- “Listen to me О handmaid, the physique possessed by your sister resembles a person, who is daily seen by me in dream and unites with me daily.” On hearing this, Udayasimha said- “I happen to be the close handmaid of the excellent son of Desaraja known by the name of Udayasimha. I make garland daily for his use, accepting which he daily adores the goddess.

55-65. Once he was walking in the orchard slowly and at that point of time, his face had been faded out somewhat. Observing his sadness, I went to him and said to him- “Why do you look so exhausted today? You tell me atonce.” On hearing my words, he said to me-“O friend, I daily see a youthful and beautiful girl in my dream. Because of my separation from her, my mind is fading out.” On hearing this, Puspavati said to the beautiful girl- “O girl with a pleasant face, at the time when I get married with my beloved, at that time I shall load you with enormous and valuable gifts. Therefore, you go to him atonce and convey my message to him.” Hearing this, Puspa getting overwhelmed with love, put Krsna in the palanquin and moved towards her house. At the gate of the fort, when the palanquin reached the valorous Makaranda who was at that time only twelve years of age, he went to the palanquin and had a look at the beautiful girl lodged in it, having the complexion of the blue lotus flower, vast and beautiful eyes, which could attract the mind. The great warrior who had been bom of the digit of Govardhana, attracted him at the first sight Overwhelmed with love, he said- “You accept my words. I would desire you to be my wife getting into my palace.” Hearing this, Krsna with a serene smile over the face, said to the prince- “O valorous warrior, you belong to an auspicious race having been bom of the fire altar. You appear to be of the age of sixteen years. You are also holding the weapons like quiver, sword and spears etc.

At that point of time, generating the pain in the heart of Makaranda, he left the place. Thereafter, he returned his home with Devasimha. On the other hand, on regaining consciousness Makaranda started burning in the fire of lust. Then he went to the house of Рusрa and apprised her of the factual position. Finding that the great warrior Makaranda had been absorbed in the love for Кrsnа, Puspa humbly said to him- “O best of the monarchs, you listen to my words, Krsna house is in the capital of Mahavati. The valorous warrior, who defeating your uncle Lahara, married his daughter with his brother, such a valorous Udayasimha would surely return. Therefore, you should rapidly equip your army.” Hearing these terrific towards, the king Makaranda fixed the guns over the entrance gates and deputed three lakhs of armed soldiers for the protection of the city at the proper places.

77-82. On the arrival of Udayasimha at his home, he apprised Balakhana of the factual position. Hearing his words, the valorous Balakhana collected five lakhs of his warriors, equipped them and marched towards the city of Мауurа. There were five thousand guns in his army, besides ten thousand elephants, a lakh of horses, besides the foot soldiers. Continuing their march for a fortnight, they reached the city of Mayura in the Pancala country. Learning about their arrival, Makaranda himself carried a sword and a shield in his hands and reached the battleground. Thereafter, he commanded his army- “You destroy the valorous enemy warriors.” On hearing this, the soldiers started firing from then guns, as a result of which the enemy army started getting destroyed by the seven thousand warriors on the southern gate. There were a lakh of cavalry men under the command of Balakhana, who were equipped with bhusundis, saktis and swords. All of them were well-versed in the art of war. On the other hand, a lakh of cavalry men of Makaranda fought a terrific war. The cavalry men of both the sides fought a terrific war.

83-93. At the western gate, twenty thousand warriors were fighting with ten thousand warriors of the enemy. Similarly, the army of forty thousand camels was fighting a terrific war with the great warriors like Balakhani and others at the northern gate. Thus, a horrifying war was going on throughout the day and night continuously. Thereafter, the warriors of Balakhani were defeated and started fleeing from the battlefield. At that point of time, Udayasimha riding over the horse named Bindula, Balakhani rode over the horse known as Kapota, Devasimha riding over the horse named Manoratha and Ahlada rode over the elephant and they reached the eastern and other gates and started killing the enemy warriors with their sharp swords. The enemy army being unable to face the horrible attacks of Balakhana and others, deserted the battleground and reached before Makaranda. Finding his warriors fleeing from the battleground, Makaranda mounted over his stone like horse and marched for waging a war with his sword and a spear. On the arrival of Makaranda in the battleground, he was surrounded by Udayasimha and his warriors from all the sides. The valorous Balakhana then attacked him with his sword over his neck. Similarly, Devasimha attacked him with a spear, Ahlada shot an arrow at him in the chest, while Udayasimha attacked him with his sword. Since Makaranda was mounting over the stone horse, all the attacks of the opponents became infructuous. Finding the attack of the enemy becoming infructuous, Makaranda thundered aloud. On the other hand, all the warriors were fainted with the attack of Makaranda with his spear.

*nāgapāśena taṃ baddhvā makaraṃdaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*vivāhaṃ kārayāmāsa kṛṣṇāṃśasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*senāmujjīvayāmāsa svakīyāmiṃdulo balī \|*  
*maṃgalaṃ kārayāmāsa makaraṃdo gṛhegṛhe \|*  
*dadau kanyāṃ vidhānena bahudravyasamanvitām \|\| 104 \|\|*

*mayūradhvajabhūpālo mahāsnehamacīkarat \|*  
*nṛpājñāṃ te puraskṛtya yayuḥ sārddhaṃ mahāvatīm \|\| 105 \|\|*

94-105. The valorous Makaranda then captured the enemy warriors who were in a pitiable condition and produced them before his father. On the other hand, finding the great warriors having been defeated, Rupana atonce rushed to Mahavati and apprised the king of the factual position. Hearing the same, Brahmananda together with Indula and a lakh of warriors marched towards the city of Mayura. Reaching there, a harsh letter was written and sent to the king. The letter said- “I am the husband of the daughter of Prthviraja and my name is Brahmananda. You better give away your daughter named Pu§pavati for Udayasimha, otherwise your entire army would be destroyed by my army. On reading the letter, Mayuradhvaja - the best of the kings marched with Makaranda and two lakhs of army and reached the battleground and started a terrific war with the army. The valorous Brahmananda was fighting with arrows. Having been wounded with the spear of Makaranda, he fell down on earth getting fainted. Then Jayanta -the son of Svarnavati, atonce reached there and displayed before Makaranda the proficiency of his vidya. He reduced to ashes his stone horse with the use of Vaisnava weapon. Then using Brahmastra, he made him fell over the ground. О best of the race of Bhrgu, the valorous Makaranda was bound with the serpent noose. Then his sister was married with Udayasimha and he brought back all the army warriors to life. Thereafter, Makaranda performed welfare ceremonies in all the homes of the city. At that point of time, the king Mayuradhvaja gave away his daughter in marriage to Udayasimha, with enormous riches. The king was overwhelmed with affection. After many days, with the permission of the king, the great warriors returned to Mahavati.

## Chapter 125. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.125.1-7 \|\|

*maṃgalaṃ kṛtavānrājā tadā parimalo balī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*puṣpavatyā tayā sārddhaṃ gītanṛtyaviśāradaḥ \|*

*tena puṇyaprabhāvena sārvabhaumo babhūva ha \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta said- At the arrival of valorous Udayasimha in the city of Mahavati, the king Parimala celebrated the welfare festival. Udayasimha danced with Puspavati, while singing at the same time. He started spending time with her in enjoyments alone. As in the spring season Indra enjoys the company of the apsaras, similarly Udayasimha also indulged in all types of sports with Puspavati. Because of his cleverness, he inspite of enjoying all the sports with her, did not unite with her. Once while dancing, Puspavati herself asked Udayasimha- “what were you in the earlier birth?” On hearing this, Udayasimha said smilingly- “O beloved, in earlier birth, I had been a king named Candrahasa. I had been in miserable condition since my childhood. I daily adored the image of lord Salagrama and with the merit of the same, I became a king.

## \|\| 2.125.8-17 \|\|

*mlecchaiśca darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ vinayādbhaktibhāvataḥ \|*

*iti te kathitaṃ devi yugamaryādamuttamam \|*

8-17. At the time of death, my mind got devoted to lord Salagrama, and because of the pleasure of Brahma, I attained the Sayujya salvation of the lord. In due course of time, Kali offered prayer to Paramesvara Visnu, who happens to be the soul of the time. He reported me from his body and made me take birth on earth. О my beloved, whenever the dharma is on the decline, then in order to establish the tradition of the related yuga, I take birth on earth during those times. During the Satyayuga, the mental worship is performed for the pleasure of the gods. Similarly, during the Tretayuga, the gods are pleased by worshipping Agni, performing homa, besides yajnas and charities. During Dvapara, the images are worshipped to please the gods and in the horrible age of Kali, the worship of Brahman is considered to be the best. О darling, during Satyayuga, I appear as a swan (hamsa), Yajna-purusa in Tretdyuga and Hiranyagarbha in Dvapara age. For the satisfaction of the gods, in the age of Kali, I happen to be Salagrama, for providing comforts to the people. О my darling, by the worship of Salagrama, the ascetics, the gods and the pitrs get delighted. The twice-born of all the three castes should worship Salagrama by offering the sandal paste. The Sudras should worship Salagrama after taking bath with devotion, while the Mlecchas should have an audience with Salagrama with devotion after taking the bath and by so doing, they also earn merits. Salagrama himself is the blissful lord, Brahman, and with the mere sight of the lord, all the sins and blemishes disappear. Thus, I have revealed to you the traditions of each one of the yugas. Now you speak out truthfully, as to whose daughter were you in the earlier birth?”

18-20. Puspavati said - In earlier birth, I had been a whore known by the name of Candrakanti. I had performed dance and music before the gods, with the influence of which I achieved the heaven. In the heaven, attracted towards my youthfulness and beauty, the gods prayed to me, but inspite of my living in the heaven, I preserved my Brahmacarya intact. Because of the same merit, I was bom as Usa - the daughter of Banasura. During that birth, Aniruddha (the grandson of Srikrsna) accepted my hand in marriage.

21-27. Thereafter, for his own selfish end, Kali prayed for my master and with partial incarnation, he was bom with Markandeya, where he displayed his own glory. The tradition of my husband is still preserved in the wood. О master, obeying his command, I was bom as the daughter of the king Jambuka. At that point of time, I had attained my divine form and I was known by the name of Vijayaisini (or Vijaya). There I had been killed by your brother Balakhana. (You are well aware of the fact) that becoming the sister of Makaranda, I have achieved you as my husband. Because of that blemish, your brother himself went to the king Gajapati and has suffered badly.” Thus speaking like the mynah with her husband, she kept quiet. On the arrival of the festival of Holi, the queen Malana once affectionately found her daughter Candravall in a dream. On that particular night, she became quite anxious to meet her daughter. Therefore, she wept for the whole night due to the separation for her. At that point of time, realizing about the truth of her crying, Udayasimha accompanied with ten thousand courtiers, carrying several types of riches, himself departed alien towards the house of Candravali.

28-36. Learning about Udayasimha’s departure, Prthviraja and his arrowed enemy also moved to the same place. Because of him having been bom of the amsa of Duryodhana, he was more selfish. There was a village named Thatha, which was protected by the people of the race of Yadus. A king named Virasena together with the three lakhs of his soldiers, lived there. He had eight sons who were youthful besides being immensely beautiful. They were known by the names of- Kamasena, Prasena, Mahasena, Sukhasena, Rupasena, Visvaksena, Madhuvrata and Madhupa. They were bom of the amsas of Yadavas and were enhancing the glorious traditions of the Yadovas. Reaching there, Udayasimha - the lion among the humans, prostrated before Virasena and then handed over the letter of queen Malana with ten bharas of gold. He then enjoyed food with various delicious dishes with the Yadavas. Then he went to the palace of Candravali and conveyed the welfare of the place. Overwhelmed with affection, she said- “At the time of my marriage, you were only two years old. Today twenty years have passed. My parents have never remembered me. They have totally forgotten me. О valorous one, you have atleast remembered me. Today my life and birth have been successful. How much shall I say, my life has been successful by meeting my brother.

37-43. At that point of time, getting delighted, Udayasimha humbly said to his sister- “When Jambuka had plundered the house, the king felt painful for that incident and getting frightened, the king had been passing his days. When we people came of age, we became victorious over Jambuka. Prthviraja had also surrounded our capital city from all the sides. Defeating him, I married my brother Brahma with his daughter named Vela. Thereafter, we had to go to Simhala island, facing many difficulties for the sake of Indula. The father had to face many such troubles. Because of these difficulties, we could find no time to come to this side. But О sister, we people are quite happy now a days. We would like to serve you now, because we are all your servants.” Thus listening to the soft and pleasant words, Candravali was overwhelmed with love and affection. Feeling extremely delighted, she lodged them in her personal palace. In the mean time, reaching the court of Virasena, after accepting the welcome of the guest and intervening in the talk, the deceitful Mahipati said.

44-53. The king has driven out Ahlada and other wicked people from his place, because these degraded people had committed theft in the royal treasure. At that point of time, these people were living in the village named Sirisa. Udayasimha, who is an opportunist, has arrived in your house. He will carry Candravali in a palanquin. О king, I am speaking the truth to you. These words can never be otherwise.” Hearing these words and considering them to be true, the king summoned Kamasena, who was the husband of Candravali. The king then said to him- “O son, you capture and bind Udayasimha.” On hearing this, Kamasena served the poisonous food to Udayasimha. On hearing this, Candraval at once came to her brother and carrying the vase (with poisonous food), left the place. Kamasena then belaboured his wife badly with canes in great anger. At that point of time, Udayasimha bound both the hands and feet of his sister’s husband. When Virasena came to know about the capture of his son, he asked his other sons to put Udayasimha in bondages. At that point of time, Udayasimha then arrived in his army camp and fought with the soldiers, who were carrying the palanquin. The army of ten thousand warriors was on one side and on the other side were three lakhs of warriors. Both the sides started fierce battle. The terrific war went on for many days and nights.

## \|\| 2.125.54-57 \|\|

*hatā lakṣaṃ mahāśūrā udayena mahābalāḥ \|*

*dṛṣṭvā parājitaṃ sainyaṃ sapta putrā mahābalāḥ \|*

*sa vīro biṃdulārūḍho bhūmau kṛtvā gajāsanān \|*

54-57. A lakh of warriors of the enemy were killed, while a thousand soldiers of Udayasimha were killed. Those who escaped death, they getting frightened by the Yadavas, fled away. At the defeat of his army, the seven sons, mounting over their respective elephants, surrounded Udayasimha from all the sides. The valorous Udayasimha mounting over his horse Bindula, captured all the seven princes killing their elephants and destroying their lion thrones. After shattering their weapons, they were forced to lick the dust. Hearing the news, Virasena - the great devotee of the Sungod, reduced to ashes the enemy army with the weapon he had received from the Sungod. With the use of the same weapon, Udayasimha too got fainted with his horse.

58-64. Then Virasena, putting the opponent soldiers and Udayasimha in bondages and freeing his son’s wife, celebrated festivities in the palace. The remaining courtiers as well as the warriors of Udaisimha fled away here and there. Some of them who were able to escape went to the king Parimala and apprised him of the factual position from beginning to end. Recalling Mahipati or Prthviraja to be an extremely wicked person, he said to Brahmananda- “You at once go there with a lakh of soldiers of the army and free your brother, putting your sister’s husband in bondage.” On hearing this, accompanied with a lakh of warriors, Brahmananda reached there and in anger surrounded the city from all the sides. Thereafter, he captured all the soldiers who had arrived for waging the war and put them in bondage. With the capture of his army, Virasena tried to reduce them to ashes with his solar weapon. But at the same time, Brahmananda made use of Brahmastra which made the weapons of the enemy infructuous and at the same time, displayed his terrific form. Observing this, the king Virasena took refuge with the same Brahmananda. Then becoming fearless, Brahmananda said to him.

## \|\| 2.125.65-68 \|\|

*dhūrtavākyena he bhūpa madbaṃdhurbādhitastvayā \|*

*atastvaṃ bhaginīyuktaṃ svasutaṃ dehi me nṛpa \|\| 65 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā ca nṛpatirvacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|*

*ityuktvā vīrasenaśca sutaṃ caṃdrāvalīṃ tathā \|*  
*dattvā tasmai prasannātmā tatprasthānamakārayat \|\| 67 \|\|*

*brahmānando'pi balavānkṛṣṇāṃśena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*senayāśītisāhasryā yayau sārddhaṃ mahāvatīm \|\| 68 \|\|*

65-68. On the words spoken by a deceitful person, you put my own brother in bondage. The ladies killing is always prohibited, but your son disregarded the tradition and had mercilessly beaten my sister. Therefore, you handover your son Kamasena with your daughter.” On hearing this, the king spoke with all humility- “My daughter is not at home presently, but Kamasena is present here.” Thus speaking, Virasena handed over Kamasena and Candravali to Brahmananda. Subsequently, he delightfully sent them off as well. The valorous Brahmananda departed back for Mahavati with eighty thousand of his soldiers.

## \|\| 2.125.69-70 \|\|

*malanā svasutaṃ dṛṣṭvā premavihvalakaṃpitā \|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra kṛṣṇāṃśacaritaṃ śubham \|*

69-70. On reaching home, the queen Malana was filled with delight at the sight of her son and bathing him with her tears, she made the son take his bath and distributed the riches to the Brahmanas. О Brahmana, thus I have narrated the story of Udayasimha, who was an amsa of Sri Krsna. I am repeating the same story which removes the sins, you please listen.

## Chapter 126. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-7. Suta said- On the bright tenth day of the month of Asvina, the king celebrated a great festival in which the Brahmanas were fully satisfied with enormous daksina. Besides it, the servants of the state were also given the rewards. During the combination of the month of Kartika, the valorous Udayasimha together with Indula and Devasimha departed towards the city of Barhismati with his army, where many of the rulers had already been camping. At the same time, Citralekha also arrived there with her seven handmaids for the worship of Citragupta. She created a beautiful уanа in the Ganga with her illusion as a wonder. A large number of rulers arrived there to have a look at the same. At the same time, Udayasimha accompanied with Indula and Devasimha arrived there with other warriors.

*citrarekhā mahāramyā vāhīkanṛpateḥ sutā \|*

*yena svapnāṃtare ramyaṃ sārddhaṃ bhuktaṃ tayā sukham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8-14. In the watery grove, the beautiful daughter Citrarekha of Vahlika spotted the moon shine, besides being spotless and pleasing. She had enjoyed the pleasure of having united with him in a dream. On the other hand, the daughter of Abhinandana, taking him to be the son of Ahlada, turned him as a parrot and put him in a cage of illusion. By kidnapping him in the svayamvara, she enjoyed the extreme pleasure. Thereafter, winding up her illusion, she returned her home with delight. On waking up, when Udayasimha could not find his son there, he enquired about him from Devasimha by waking him up. He asked-“Where has the boy gone?” Though Devasimha was aware of all the happenings, but he could not know as to where had the boy gone or who had kidnapped him. When he was unable to give any reply and was himself found surprised, Udayasimha started crying aloud. Finding him so crying, the wicked Mahipati, feeling delighted, went to Ahlada. Reaching there and crying aloud, he spoke with humility.

15-28. “Your brother Udayasimha made Indula and Devasimha to consume highly effective intoxications and has made them senseless. Thereafter, killing Indula, he consigned him to the forceful waves of the waters of the Ganga. Whatever was done by him, it was witnessed by me with my own eyes. He also stopped me from revealing the truth by giving me a hundred gold coins. What treatment was extended by him to Devasimha on his regaining consciousness is unknown to me. Making use of his own wisdom, whatever was done by him, no one could know.” Inspite of the words spoken by Mahipati, Ahlada was unable to believe the words so spoken by Mahipati. At the same time, both warriors also reached there while crying. Because of the separation from his nephew (the son of his brother), Udayasimha was about to end his life. Finding him in that condition, Ahlada developed a trust in the words of Mahipati. Getting enraged, he took a cane covered with leather and started beating Udayasimha. Influenced with the illusion of the wicked person Mahipati, the mother, wife and sister of the boy started consoling Ahlada. All of them started advising Alhada variously, but having been overpowered with the illusion, he could understand nothing. At that point of time, finding her husband being beaten by her brother, Puspavati atonce reached there and felt painful because of the suffering of her husband. Udayasimha was denounced without any cause. At the same moment, the learned people well-versed in the Vedas, said to Ahlada- ‘The killing and disowning are both considered to be equal. You think of whatever is suitable.” At these words of the learned people, Ahlada - the auspicious soul, feeling painful because of the grief of his son, called for the Candalas and handed over Udayasimha - the killer of his son, to them and said to them- “You kill him and his wife both. You also show me the eyeballs of both of them after extracting them.” On hearing this, the Candalas went into the deep forest with both of them at the place infested with wild animals. At the same time, Devasimha influenced the Candalas and freed both the condemned persons giving the Candalas enough of money. Both Udayasimha and his wife were taken to the house of Balakhani and were lodged there. Gajamukta - the chaste lady, concealed both of them in her house and took good care of them. The Candalas on their part, brought the eyeballs of the deer and handed them over to Ahlada. Then getting enraged, Devasimha said to Ahlada-“Disgrace to a wicked and evil-minded person. You have got my friend killed.

29-35. I am going to many countries in search of him.” Thus speaking, the valorous Devasimha proceeded towards the town of Sirisa. With the permission of Gajamukta, together with the couple, in the dead of the dark night, he reached the city of Mayura. The valorous Makaranda understood the entire situation there and lodged his sister and Udayasimha in his house. Thereafter, Makaranda indulged in various type of religious activities, performing yajnas at the same time. Feeling pleased, Dharmaraja said to Makaranda- “The daughter of the king Abhinandana is known by the name of Citrarekha. She worships Citragupta. She has a handmaid named Kesarini who is the daughter of Natya and is proficient in magic. Kutuka is the preceptor of Kesarini, who changes his forms by yogic practices. He has spread his illusion upto the area of a hundred yojanas. The related land is beyond the reach of the enemies. The land also turns the enemy into stones. Because of the influence of Citragupta, the king always remains fearless.

*ityuktvāntardadhe devassa rājā vismayānvitaḥ \|*

36-43. The daughter of the same king known by the name of Citrarekha has kidnapped Indula. She keeps him in the human form at night and as a parrot during the day. Under the influence of Citrarekha, Indula is badly suffering there. Therefore, you yourself, along with Devasimha and Suryavarma should go collectively, with the mantra given by me and meet Citrarekha. Influencing the princess by your dance and music, you extract the vidya possessed by the young girl and then return to me. Thereafter, you fight there with your armies.” Thus speaking, Dharmaraja disappeared from the scene. After waking up, the king felt immensely surprised. Thereafter, he revealed all the methods told to him by Dharmaraja to Udayasimha. At the start of the month of Phalguna, all the three of them who were well-versed in the yogic practices, took the form of yogins and reached the court of the king Gajapati in the pleasant city of Indragrha. Devasimha played on cymbals, Makaranda played on lute, while Udayasimha started dancing, which pleased all present there. Displaying the proficiency of their art, all of them made the king of the place spell bound. Getting pleased with his family and the army, the king of the place said- “O yogins, you tell me the desire of your minds.” On hearing this, all of them spoke quite humbly- “You give me your son Suryavarma, since I have to perform a special task.

44-54. I shall return your son soon after my task is finished, because Brahma had prescribed the Rajadharma for the protection of the universe. On hearing this, the king entrusted the care of his son to them and then he retired to his palace. Thereafter, these people started their work. After covering the journey for fifteen days, they reached the city of Bahlika. Making use of the mantra given by Dharmaraja and feeling delightful, they entered the palace, where ail the Ksatriya people had assembled. Those people displayed their proficiency in dance and music there before the audience, which influenced all the Ksatriyas. Then feeling overjoyed, the Tomaras and Kulabhupana Ksatriyas, getting filled with delight, showered enormous riches on them. Thereafter, they went to the palace of the king Abhinanda for performing the dance. In the music party, Makaranda played on lute, Devasimha played on cymbals, Suryavarma played on small cymbals, while Udayasimha performed the dance which enamoured all queens besides the king. 'Hie art of dancing of the party influenced the queens the most. Citrarekha was also present in the group of ladies, who in order to fascinate the people had created several types of illusions which became infructuous at the same time. Getting enumerated, the lady said- “O valorous one, you speak out whatever is known to you?” Then Udayasimha replied to the lady - “0 goddess, you give me the parrot, otherwise I shall pronounce a curse on you.” On hearing this, the worried Citrarekha said to the yogins-“You tell me who are you?

55-63. It is because the illusion by which the gods like Indra and others were influenced in a moment, that all have become infructuous on you. You could not be illusioned. Therefore, you are surely Narayana, Dharmaraja or lord Siva himself.” At these words of Citrarekha, Udayasimha said- “My name is Udayasimha, O goddess. My brother-in-law Makaranda and Devasimha, besides Suryavarma are accompanying me. In separation from Indula, we people have taken to the form of yogins. My elder brother Ahlada has become mad in separation of his son, therefore you give me back Suka or Indula.” Thus speaking, Udayasimha started crying aloud saying- “O Mahabala, О Indula, you atonce appear before me, otherwise I shall end my life here itself in the presence of all.” Hearing this, the beautiful Citrarekha feeling shameful, said- “you kindly accept me also with your son.” Thus speaking, she turned Indula with a beautiful body. Thereafter, the couple, falling at the feet of Udayasimha, started crying aloud. Udayasimha, on the other hand, feeling delighted, assured them variously. Then he made Indula to write a letter, carrying which all of them reached the city of Mayura, by means of a yantra.

*mahīpatiṃ samāhūya vacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ kathaya me bhūpa kṛṣṇāṃśena hatassutaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

64-68. Thereafter, having been honoured from Makaranda, Suryavarma returned to his abode. The valorous Devasimha, carrying that letter and riding the horse named Manoratha, departed for Mahavati. Reaching that place, he met Ahlada, who was behaving like a mad person grieving for his son. He said to Ahlada - “Who are you roaming about like a mad person? He said- “I am Devasimha, who had been searching for your son. You received a letter written by your son himself.” On hearing this, Ahlada felt extremely delighted. He also tried to know the manner in which his son was kidnapped and the reasons for his getting kidnapped.

*sa hovāca śrutaṃ vīra kṛṣṇāṃśena yathā hataḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā tu vihasyāśu kāryasiddhimupāgataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*ahlādaḥ krodhatāmrākṣaḥ keśānā kṛṣya taṃ mudā \|*  
*vetasaistāḍayāmāsa svahastena punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*śrutvā parimalo rājā sapatnīkassamāgataḥ \|*  
*bahudhā modayāmāsa rāmāṃśaṃ bahurūpiṇam \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-81. Thereafter, Mahipati was summoned and he said to him with humility- “You tell me truthfully the way my son was kidnapped by Udayasimha.” He replied- “The way Udayasimha had killed your son was heard by me, which I had conveyed to you.” Thus speaking, he laughed and said- “My job has been done.” On hearing this, both the eyes of Ahlada became red in anger like the copper. Then he picked up a stick of cane and started striking on his body. Hearing it, the king Parimala with his queen reached there and tried to convince Ahlada, who had taken to many forms. In utter rage, Ahlada was telling him- “O wicked and sinful person, you got my brother killed. Therefore, I shall send you also with your family to the place where you have sent my brother. At that point of time, Mahila also getting silent, started taking deep sighs. He was reminded of the sin committed by him, feeling painful. At the same time, Balakhana arrived there and relieved of his maternal uncle of the sin of getting his brother killed. Thereafter, he started preparations for the marriage of his nephew. In making the arrangements for the marriage, Netrasimha participated with a lakh of his soldiers, Тaraка with fifteen hundred warriors. Virasena joined with ninety thousand soldiers, Talana with a lakh of warriors, while Suryavarma joined with the lakh of army. Besides, Brahmananda and Ahlada also joined together with a lakh of armies each. Ahlada was moving on lamenting- “O brother, where have you disappeared leaving me alone ” Saying these words, he fainted sometimes and at times he got back his senses. The valorous Balakhana together with Devasimha and a lakh of soldiers marched towards Vahlika city. Travelling throughout the day and night, all of them reached the city of Vahlika on the fifth black day of the month of Jyestha.

*eko rathaḥ sthito yuddhe tatpaścātsaṃsthitā gajāḥ \|*  
*pañcāśacca kramātteṣāṃ vājinaśca śataṃśatam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ paścātkramājjñeyā pattayo daśa saṃsthitāḥ \|*

*eko ratho gajāssarve śatārddhaṃ tu hayāstu ye \|*

*gajāstu daśasāhasrā madamattāḥ pṛthagyayuḥ \|*  
*yuddhe 'smingaṇitaṃ hyevaṃ śūrāḥ śatruprahāriṇaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*abhinandanabhūpasya mlecchāḥ paiśācadharmiṇaḥ \|*  
*trilakṣāśca hayārūḍhā ekalakṣāḥ śatapripāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*ekalakṣaḥ padacarā bhuśuṇḍīparighāyudhāḥ \|*  
*tomarānvayasaṃyuktāḥ kṣatriyāḥ prayutāni vai \|*  
*gajasthāstatra saṃprāptā yatrāhlādamahā camūḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*tayoścāsīnmahadyuddhaṃ tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam \|*  
*madamattāśca te sarve nirbhayā raṇamāyayuḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*saptāhorātramabhavadyuddhaṃ samaraśāli nām \|*

*ekalakṣaṃ hatāḥ sarve balakhāneśca sainyapaiḥ \|*  
*hāhābhūte śatrusainye bhayabhīte diśo gate \|*  
*harṣitā balakhānyādyā jaya durge vaco'bruvan \|\| 91 \|\|*

82-91. Balakhani resorted to the formation of the vyuha or the army formations. The chariots were in the forefront, followed by elephants, fifty horses and then contingents of ten foot soldiers. I am now speaking out the size of a single army which comprised of chariots, elephants, fifty cavalry men. Five thousand guns were allotted to each contingent of the army. Besides these, there were fifty thousand foot soldiers. Thus Malakhana had sixteen armies which comprised of ten thousand intoxicated elephants positioned separately.” The army which forcefully attacked the enemy army was counted. The army of the king Abhinandana has been described thus. The Mlecchas following the Mlecchas were three lakhs, in which the cavalry men were also included. There were a lakh of guns, one lakh of the foot soldiers who were equipped with bhusundis and parigha weapons. The warriors of Tomara race of Ksatriya vamsa were ten lakhs in number, who were mounted over the elephants and reached in the battlefield close to the army of the Ahlada. Both the armies started a terrific and great war. The intoxicated warriors started blowing the war instrument fearlessly. The war was fought for a week continuously during the day as well as the night. Half of the army of Bahlika and a lakh of army warriors of Balakhana were killed in the war. A terror was created in the army. The terrified people started fleeing here and there. The soldiers of Balakhana uttered the slogans of victory of Durga, feeling delighted.

*mahānandaśca nandaśca parānandopanandakau \|*

*gajasthāste mahāvīrāstomarānvayasaṃbhavāḥ \|*

*dṛṣṭvā sainyaṃ parābhūtaṃ balakhānistadā ruṣā \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tadā kesariṇī nāṭyā aṣṭau baddhvā mahābalān \|*

*bāhlīkaśca prasannātmā baddhvā tānnigaḍairdṛḍhaiḥ \|*

*devyāśca varadānena devasiṃho bhayāturaḥ \|*

*jñātvā svarṇavatī devī sarvavidyāviśāradā \|*

92-105. At the sight of the destruction of their army, the seven princes who hailed from the race of Kauravas arrived in the battlefield. They were known by the names of Mahananda, Nanda, Parananda, Upananda, Sunanda, Surananda and Prananda. They were the ornaments of the Tomara race and were mounted over the elephant. With the shooting of the sharp arrows, they started killing the warriors of Balakhana. Observing the defeat of the soldiers of his army, Balakhana got enraged and then he mounted over his horse named Kapota and marched towards the battle ground. Reaching there, Devasimha fought with Nanda, Tarana with Parananda, Suryavarma with Upananda, Taraka with Sunanda, Netrasimha with Surananda and Makaranda with Prananda. All of them fought a terrific war. Ail the warriors with the desire to kill one another, fought a terrific war till noon in which a large number of soldiers were either killed or wounded. Thereafter, getting terrified from the prince of Bahlika known as Balakhana, some of them fled away from the battleground, terrified from Balakhana. Finding the enemy army getting horrible, the king Abhinandana called for Kutuka and Natya Kesarini and related to them the cause of his own defeat. Hearing this, Kutuka assured the king variously. Then making use of the Sambari illusion, he turned the entire enemy army into stones and senseless. At that point of time, Natya Kesarini captured all the eight valorous warriors and carried them to the king and produced them before him. She herself then returned to her place. Then Abhinandana - the lord of Bahlika, bound all the captures with handcuffs and fetters, got their treasures plundered and added all their riches to his own treasure. Because of the boon received from the goddess, Devasimha escaped the illusion of the goddess. Getting terrified, he reached Mahavati and narrated all what had happened in the battleground to Svarnavati, who was well-versed in all the vidyas. Then Svamavati, taking to the form of an eagle, went to Puspavati.

*ruditvā kathayāmāsa yathā prāptaḥ parājayaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*na dāho dāhamāpanno na bhasmī bhasmavānkhalu \|*

*kutukaṃ ca tathābhūtaṃ hatvā svarṇavatī svayam \|*  
*kārāgāre lohamaye sthitānvīrānamocayat \|\| 116 \|\|*

106-116. Finding the couple in the house of Makaranda, she while crying, spoke out the cause of the defeat of the soldiers of her side. At that point of time, feeling highly painful, Udayasimha said to Makaranda - “You immediately get ready to march with me, because even my preceptor Ahlada has been put in bondage. The learned people of the past have declared that one earn a grave sin at the destruction of the race. О my dear, you rescue me from the ocean of sorrow in which I am drowning.” On hearing this, the brother-in-law together with ten thousand of his soldiers, taking to the form of mendicants and holding swords and shields in their hands marched towards the city of Bahlika. Udayasimha, who was mounted over the horse, was rapidly leading the army. At the same time, Svarpavati, together with Puspavati, taking to the form of eagles, reached the battleground. She destroyed the Sambari illusion and brought her army back to senses. Then those soldiers surrounded the capital city of Abhinandana from all the sides. Finding that the enemy army had regained their senses, Kesarini again tried to cast her spell of Sambari maya's net over the enemy army, but both the damsels (Puspavati and Svarnavati) destroyed the spell caused by Kesarini. Besides they captured both wicked persons. Thereafter, an attempt was made to reduce the capital city to ashes. But because of the power of the king, it could not be burnt. Therefore, the city escaped destruction inspite of the making of an attempt to reduce it to ashes, because the illusion in the city was caused by Citrarekha herself. Finding that the effort of Svarnavati was becoming infructuous, Puspavati getting enraged, killed Kesarini and her flesh was thrown to the jackals and vultures who ate it. On the other hand, Svarnavati killed Kutuka and freed her warriors who were lodged in prison with strong bondages.

*tadā kolāhalaścāsīdrudatāṃ balaśālinām \|*

117-128. Thereafter, Svarnavati together with Puspavati reached before Makaranda where he was lodged with Udayasimha. Finding that the enemy warriors were highly influenced by the goddess, he departed for a war, getting enraged. Thereafter, a terrific war started between the two armies in which Mahananda fought with Balakhana, Nanda with Ahlada, Parmananda with Devasimha, Upananda with Тarakа, Netrasimha with Sunanda, Surananda with Talana, Vlrasena with Prananda and Brahmananda himself fought with the king. All the princes were mounted over the elephants and were fighting ceaselessly with the bows and arrows. The war continued throughout the day and night. At the same time, Citrarekha arrived in the battleground and finding that the warriors of her side were upset, she carefully made a painting of Citragupta. In this illusion, she created a large number of helpers, most of whom appeared to belong to the family of Abhinandana. Looking at them, the warriors of Mahavati getting frightened and confused, started fleeing from the battleground. The grieved and upset soldiers fled from that place and established their abodes at a distance of five yojanas from the battleground. During the evening time, in darkness, feeling disappointed the valorous warriors were crying and lamenting- “O valorous Udayasimha, you protect those who take refuge in you. Citrarekha had kidnapped your prince Indula. Having been confused by her, we have arrived to take refuge with you.” Thus lamenting, they started crying aloud- “Where are you О Intelligent one, where are you?” When the soldiers so cried aloud, a huge turbulence was created? All of them were fainted, denouncing Ahlada and fell down over the ground.

*śṛṇvatāṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ kathayiṣyāmi vai punaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

129-140. Hearing them, Ahlada also felt as if vajra had fallen over him. He then becoming hysterical, started beating his chest. By about the same time, Udayasimha, who had been born of the amsa of Sri Krsna, arrived there in the form of a yogi with ten thousand of his followers besides Makaranda, on Friday - the eighth day of the rise of the moon. They started plundering the army of Balakhana. Conquering all the rulers, they collected enormous wealth. Thereafter, mounting over the elephant Pancasabda, he went before his brother and thundered aloud. Hearing his voice, Balakhana could recognize them all. At that point of time, the valorous warrior was witnessing auspicious symptoms as well. Therefore, he forcefully raised up both his hands, held Udayasimha and made him sit in his lap. Thereafter, overwhelmed with his love, he made him bathe with his tears flowing from his eyes. Then he distributed enough of charities to the Brahmanas and narrated all the sequence of events from beginning to end. Feeling delighted then, Udayasimha also repeated his own story. Then again leading the armies, they departed towards the city of Bahlika. Reaching there, they made use of the vidya possessed by Citrarekha and destroyed her illusion. The king Abhinandana together with his sons and courtiers were put in bondages. Citrarekha was properly married with Indula. At that point of time, the king Abhinandana too, feeling delighted, gave away his daughter Citrarekha with enormous wealth to Indula which included a hundred elephants, a hundred steed, a thousand cows, a hundred slaves and an equal number of slave girls. Balakhana accepted them all gracefully and then proceeded towards Mahavati. During the month of Sravana, reaching Mahavati with his entire paraphernalia, Ahlada gifted suitable prizes to all the warriors as well as the monarchs. Thereafter, accepting the hospitality of the king, they went back to their respective abodes. О Brahmana, I have thus narrated to you the story which destroys the age of Kali. Now I am telling you the story which destroys all the sins. You listen to it carefully.

## Chapter 127. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-8. Suta said- Getting the marriage of Indula performed, Mahipati reached the abode of Udayasimha, where he usually remained uncomfortable. Thereafter, reaching Dehall with Taraka, he narrated the entire story to the king there. Listening to the performance of Udayasimha, the king of Dehall was immensely surprised. In the mean time, the large-hearted and intelligent courtier Candrabhatta said to the king- “O Monarch, I have worshipped the goddess Vaisnavi who is the mother of the universe. After bestowing the boon over me, the goddess who was pleased with my adoration, had enlightened me with the conduct of Udayasimha. Therefore, I am composing his life sketch which is the remover of the sins, in the form of a book.” Thus speaking, he recited the story of Udayasimha in which the glory of the devotees had been recited in presence of all who were present there. Hearing that, the king Prthviraja was immensely surprised. At the same time, Mahipati spoke- “The valorous Udayasimha, who’s life story has been contained in the form of this book, is more proud of his divine horses. He possesses four divine horses, who can move in the water, on earth and in the sky with an equal force. By forcibly snatching those horses, you could become most powerful.”

9-18. On hearing these words, the king called for an attendant, who was quite clever in the practical conversation and briefing on all the matters by sending a messenger. Reaching the city of Mahavati, the messenger started conveying the message of Prthviraja with all humility. He said- “O monarch, you have four divine horses with auspicious bodies. My daughter Vela who is also your daughter-in-law, is quite anxious to have a look at them. Therefore, О Monarch, at her desire, shedding away the surprise, make arrangements for sending those horses urgently, otherwise all the commander will be destroyed in the fire. Listening to this horrible message, the king Parimala summoned Ahlada and others and spoke to them quite humbly- “You accept my words and give away your horses to him (Prthviraja) gladly.” Hearing the words of the king Parimala, Ahlada meditated upon the goddess Parvati - the mother of the universe, and spoke to the king in sweet voice- “O Monarch - the favourite of lord Siva, these horses are dear to me like my life. Therefore, I am unable to part my relationship with these horses. This is the truth and the total truth spoken by me. This cannot be otherwise.” On hearing these words, the valorous king Parimala took a very harsh vow before the great warriors. It is a grave sin by you and the food of this place would be like the flesh of a Brahmana, the water would be like the blood of a cow, the bed would be like your mother and the assembly of this place would be like Brahmahatya. It would be a great sin for you to live in my country.

19-22. Listening to the horrible vow, the goddess Devaki was immensely worried and started crying bitterly. Finding her in this condition, all her relatives also started crying. At that point of time, Udayasimha had just entered the twenty fifth year of his age. On the bright fourteenth day of the month of Bhadrapada, those religious-minded warriors came out with their horses and then proceeded on to the kingdom of Jayacandra at Kanyakubja. In the journey, Svarnavati, Puspavati and Citrarekha with Indula were moving with ten thousand of their warriors with horses. Indula himself was mounting over the horse named Karala, while his father was seated over the Pancasabda elephant. Similarly, Udayasimha mounted over the horse Bindula following the goddess Devaki, and marched on.

23-30. Leaving the rich village of the great monarch, they continued their journey for three days. Thereafter, they spotted the capital city of Jayacandra. Reaching there, they apprised the king of the factual position, offering their salutation to him. Then they worshipped the goddess Candika. While staying there, when Devasimha apprised the king Jayacandra about the cause of their exile, Jayacandra refuged to give them any help because it had not been approved by Parimala. Then Devasimha getting disappointed, went to Udayasimha, who riding on his horse Bindula plundered the city which was guarded by Laksana. Observing this, Laksana mounted over his elephant and shot an arrow at the heart of Udayasimha, but the arrow became infructuous with the influence of Visnu-mantra. Observing this, Laksana descended from the elephant and stood over the ground. Then he offered his salutation at the feet of Udayasimha which had been decorated with his servants. Then he offered prayer to him in a choked voice.

31-32. Laksana said- “O lord, I am a devotee of lord Visnu and worship lord Visnu daily. О valorous one, I know you very well. You have incarnated by the strength of lord Krsna, because there is none else in the world except you, to make my arrow shot infructuous. Therefore, О master, you kindly forgive me for my audacity, because I have done it under the influence of your illusion.”

33-45. Thus speaking and accompanied with them, Laksana reached before Jayacandra and repeated before him the story of his defeat appropriately. Thereafter, the king, in order to test them, who had been influenced with the shadow, sent them to the place of the goddess Sitala’s courtyard. At that point of time, Ahlada and Udayasimha playfully held the elephant from the tail and pulled it like a sheath, as a result of which the elephant named Kuvalayapidha was killed. At the death of the huge elephant, the king was frightened and he gave them the village Rajagrha. Then at the start of the bright fortnight of Asvina, the valorous Laksana, with the permission of the monarch, started for the world conquest. In the journey, seven lakhs of soldiers together with Talana were marching. Reaching Varanasi, they surrounded the capital city of the king of Gauda family which was known as Varanasi and ruled by the king Rudravarma. The army of Laksana surrounded the city from all the sides. The monarch Rudravarma with his fifty thousand warriors started fighting, but within a prahara’s time, he became victorious and received the tax for sixteen years, which amounted a crore of gold coins. It was sent to Jayacandra. Thereafter, they attacked the king of Magadha. They were also victorious over Magadha and they collected the tax for twenty years from the king of Magadha, which also amounted to a crore of gold coins and which too were sent to their king. From there, they reached the country of Vanga (Bengal) which was ruled by Kalivarma. Reaching there, Laksana started fighting with a lakh of warriors. Fighting the war continuously during the day and night, they became victorious and they collected the tax for twenty years, which was in the form of a crore of gold coins and which was also presented to ' the king Jayacandra.

46-60. Advancing from that place, they reached the Ustra country which was ruled by Dhoyikavi, who fought with a lakh of his army of soldiers, who getting permission of lord Jagannatha and playing on the war buggle, became ready for waging the war. Both the armies fought a terrific war. In a day and night, Udayasimha became victorious over that king. He collected the tax in the form of a crore of gold coins from that king and sent it to Jayacandra - the king of Kannauja. Thereafter, the valorous Laksana journeyed for the Pundra country, which was ruled by the king Nagapati having an army of fifty thousand soldiers. Fighting a battle there and before sunset, he became victorious and received a crore of gold coins from him. Thereafter, reaching the Mahendra mountain, they offered their salutation to the sage Bhargava and then reached the kingdom of Netrapala ruled by Yogasimha. He also paid a crore of gold and invited Udayasimha to stay with him (the sage) with his army for a week. Thereafter, the intoxicated warriors reached the city of Vlrasimha, which was lodged over the peak of Himalaya. The city of Virasimha was surrounded from all the sides, This city had been guarded by the great Yogi Gorakhanatha, as the king had been devoted to the sage. Pravira - the younger brother of the king, together with his ten thousand warriors, started a terrific war with the army led by Laksana. The valorous Pravira daily destroyed one thousand warriors of the enemy and in the evening he used to go to the yogi and offered his salutation to him. Having been pleased with the devotion of Pravira, the yogi used to bring the soldiers of the king back to life daily infusing strength in each one of them like an elephant. Thereafter, the yogi again used to absorb in his yogic practices or sam adhi. In this way, the war of the warriors continued for a month and a half. At that point of time, feeling disappointed, Udayasimha with the warriors, said to Devasimha- “Why are we people not becoming victorious? You kindly speak out to me the reason for the same.” On hearing this, Devasimha said to Udayasimha-“You listen to my words. In case you defeat the yogi Gorakhanatha with your dance, you would surely be victorious thereafter.” Hearing these words, all the warriors with Udayasimha disguised themselves as yogis and went to the temple of the yogi the next morning.

61-73. On the other hand, in the battle field, the army was being looked after by Laksana. Reaching the temple, Udayasimha, who was proficient in the playing on flute, started dancing while Devasimha was playing on cymbals, Talana played on vina, while Ahlada played on small cymbal, singing over the lines of Sanatani Gita. Feeling delighted at their performance, the saint Gorakhanatha, who was well-versed in yoga, said to those people-“You ask for a boon.” Hearing this, they said-“All of us offer our salutation to you. In case you intend to bestow a boon on us, then you kindly bestow the Sanjivani-vidya to Ahlada.” On hearing this, Gorakhanatha was absorbed in meditation for a while and then delightfully said- “This Sanjivani-vidya will be fruitful with you for a full one year. Thereafter, it becoming fruitless with you, shall return to me. Therefore, discarding this world today, I am proceeding on to my disciple Bhartrhari and shall sleep there.” Thus speaking, the great yogi Gorakhanatha disappeared from the scene. At the same time, reaching the battlefield, the warriors gained victory over Pravira, besides Virasimha. Then they plundered their army of ten thousand and made the king their servant. Thereafter, Laksana delightfully reached Kausala and defeated the king Suryadhara, who fought with his army of ten thousand soldiers and collected the tax for sixteen years, which worked out to a crore of gold coins. Then they started to Naimisaranya for taking a holy bath there. At that point of time, the festival of Holi was being celebrated there. Therefore, Laksana distributed enormous riches to the Brahmanas, celebrating the festival. Reaching Naimisaranya, they took bath at all the holy places and pleased the gods as well as the Brahmanas. Thereafter, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Caitra, they started their journey for Kannauja. О Brahmana, I have thus related to you the events of their victory march. Now, I am telling you the story which highlights the death of Balakhana. You please listen.
