74-90. The valorous and unfearful Prthviraja spoke to the courtier who had been sent by Mahipati on the black eighth day of the moon in the month of Margasirsa- “I have heard that your son, because of the boon he had received from the goddess Sarada, had become proudy or Raktabija means blood had become favourite to him because it is in his seed. Therefore, you kindly give him to me.” At these words of the king, the courtier who had been honoured by the king called for his son and said to him- "O son, you are a lover of war. You please be ready for the performing of the task of the king.” On hearing the words of the king, the son said- “O king, you give me a command. You will surely be victorious shortly.” Hearing this, the king said-“Clearing the forest of Sirisa, the valorous Balakhana has usurped the part of my country. The valorous and brave warrior is fearlessly living there. In case you becoming victorious over Balakhana hand him over to me or kill him, the entire country shall then belong to you.” Thus speaking, he put his army of seven lakhs of soldiers under his command. He also delightfully marched on with that army. Spending three days in the journey, he reached Sirisa and surrounded the glorious city of Balakhana from all the four sides. The valorous Balakhana, on learning about the arrival of Camunda, worshipped the goddess Mahamaya and distributed the huge charities. Then accompanied with a lakh of army soldiers, he marched towards the battle ground. He was accompanied by his younger brother Sukhakhani. Sukhakhani mounted over the horse named Harini, while Balakhana was riding over the horse named Kapota. Both of them started killing the soldiers of the enemy army. Then they delightfully reached before Camunda. A fierce battle was then started from both the sides in which the soldiers of both the sides started falling rapidly. The battle continued throughout the day and night in which a large number of warriors were killed. On the next morning, getting free from bath, both the warriors reached the battleground. Balakhana was mounted over a chariot, while Camunda was mounted over an elephant. Both of them started waging a terrific war. Both of them were devoted to the goddess and they cut off the arrows shot by each other. Thereafter, destroying the vehicles of each other, they started destroying the soldiers with the swords held by both of them in their hands. With the fall of the drops of blood of Raktabija over the earth, the same number of valorous warriors emerged out of them.

91-106. О best of the race of Bhrgu, in this way, both the arrogant warriors when surrounded Balakhana from all the four sides, Balakhana took refuge with the goddess Sarada. His valorous younger brother Sukhakhani reached there and reduced Raktabija to ashes with his fire arrow. In earlier times, Sukhakhani had worshipped the Firegod for five years with the offering of payasam in fire. Getting pleased with the same, the Firegod himself appeared before Sukhakhani and handed over his fire arrow to him, which surely kills the enemy. Using the same arrow, he became victorious. Observing this, Balakhana made Camunda captive and brought him in his house. For fear of brahmahatya, he could not kill him. But he was attired in woman’s clothes, placed in a palanquin and was sent to his enemy Prthviraja. Thereafter, the remaining five lakhs of soldiers returned to Dehali and narrated the factual events of the war. Finding Camunda in the dress of a woman, Prthviraja getting enraged, said to Mahipati to move in a deceitful way. Brahmi is the mother of both the warriors, who has been called as yuddha-pativrata or chaste in war. Through a female messenger, you can know about the means of their death. The war should be started thereafter again. On hearing these words, Prthviraja deputed female messengers who were well-versed in deceitful ways in the house of Balakhana. The female messengers took to the form of the Brahmanas and departed towards the abode of Balakhana. Reaching there, praising the king with his daughter, they spoke in an extremely humble voice- “It is a matter of great pride and fortune that both your sons are so strong that they can destroy the enemy merely on their arrival in the battleground. Let them enjoy the life of a hundred years, but can they meet with death some time? On hearing this, Brahmi said- “The foot of Balakhana ensures life to him. On knowing these secrets, the female messengers returned to DehalT and repeated the factual position before the king. The king rewarded them with wealth after which they returned to their abodes. After hearing the words of the female messengers, the king started the worship of parthivalinga of Siva for a thousand days.

1-15. Suta said- O sage, at the time of the start of the age of twenty six years, the deeds performed by Udayasimha are being related by me, which you please listen. In the southern country, there is a lake known as Bindusara at the bank of which a fort is located which is known as Bindugadha. It is spread in the area of a yojana and is decorated with the teachers of the varna-dharma. The lord of the capital city is known by the name of Saradanandana, who belongs to the family of Visvakasena. While performing parayana of Brahmadhyana, he was engaged in the looking after of his people. By the influence of Brahmacarya, he had lodged the semen in the head and because of which he was known as Kamapala of the earth. Once, while performing a yajna, he adored the four-faced Brahma - the best of the gods. A part of the yajna was given to the queen, consuming which she conceived. On the tenth month, she gave birth to a beautiful daughter named Padmini. She was the mine of all the virtues besides being the image of the entire beauty on earth. On her entering the age of twelfth year, the girl possessing the best complexion became due for a svayamvara. Looking at her, her brother known by the name of Padmakara and who was the follower of Prthviraja, with the permission of his father, invited all the rulers and then organized the svayamvara which was attended by the rulers of all the countries. Together with his four warriors including Ahlada and with the permission of their father, the monarch Laksana also joined the svayamvara in Bindugadha. The valorous Prthviraja finding Laksana also present there, for the protection of all the rulers present there, made his army to take their positions. In the mean time, the princess PadminI together with her handmaids, reached the place of svayamvara. She reached before Laksana, who was of dark complexion, youthful and possessed all the auspicious symbols. He was of the age of forty to fifty years, having vast chest, strong shoulders, besides being quite healthy like a god. Finding Laksana quite suitable for herself and guarded by Ahlada and others, the princess placed the garland of victory around the neck of Laksana. Laksana also, holding her soft hands, placed her in his chariot and delightfully started from that place, which was filled with the kings.

16-30. Prthviraja on his part surrounded Laksana with other rulers of his side from all the sides. Then Talana, who was mounted over the mare named Simhini and was bom of the amsa of Bhimasena, started fighting with the warriors making use of his parigha. Ahlada, who was mounting over the elephant Pancasabda and belonged to the amsa of Balabhadra, started killing the opponent soldiers making use of tomaras. At that point of time, Udayasimha who was mounting over the horse Bindula, killed and shattered many of the rulers. Devasimha was mounting over the horse Manoratha. He thundered aloud and killed many of the enemy warriors with his spear. Laksana on his part placed the vaisnava arrows over his bow and was killing the army of Prthviraja. Both the armies fought bitterly for a prahara. Thereafter, deserting the battleground, Prthviraja returned to Dehali. Then, Saradanandana erected an auspicious mandapa and completing all the formalities of the marriage, gave away the girl to Laksana. At the same time, Mahipati arrived there and said to the prince Padmakara, who was present there with a lakh of his army soldiers- “O my friend, what had happened to your wisdom. It is surprising that having taken birth in a high Ksatriya family, you have developed your relationship with Laksana who is of mixed caste and are giving away your sister to him. Ahlada and others were born of the womb of a milkmaid and because of this, the religious-minded people discarded them.” On hearing this, Padmakara who was part master in creating the illusion, making use of his Sambari illusion, captured the invincible warriors and put them in prison. Because of the boon of the goddess, Devasimha regained consciousness at the same dead of night and returned to Kannauja. Reaching there, he narrated the entire sequence of events to Indula. On hearing this, Indula with Devasimha at once departed for Bindugadha. Learning about their arrival and in order to confuse them like the sun being covered by the clouds, Padmakara made use of his Sambari lore.

31-38. But Indula placing the arrow over his bow, reduced his entire illusion to ashes. Thereafter, using the kamastra, the valorous warriors regained consciousness and broke their bondages as well as the iron doors. Thereafter, they come out and started destroying the enemy. They despatched five thousand ksatriya warriors to the abode of Yama. Then the king Saradananda arrived there with all humility and gracefully handed over his daughter to Laksana. He also distributed various types of food items, clothes and ornaments to others. Thereafter, overwhelmed with love, the king sent off his daughter with Laksana. On the dark eighth day of the month of Magha, she safely reached his home. After their return, the king Jayacandra, having been overwhelmed with love, gave away a hundred villages each to Talana and others as the pride. The cows, garments, costumes were also distributed to the Brahmanas in the related festivities.

## \|\| 2.128.39-45 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*mahīrājo varaṃ prāptaḥ śaṃkarātpārthivārcanāt \|*  
*saṃyojya phālgune māsi senāṃ śatrubhayaṃkarām \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saptalakṣaiśca sahitaḥ śirīṣākhyapuraṃ yayau \|*  
*nṛpājñayā ca cāṃmuḍo rurodha nagaraṃ punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sukhakhānistadā kruddho lakṣasainyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*nagarādbahirāgatya mahāvadhamakārayat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*pāvakāstreṇa balavānhatvā daśasahasrakam \|*  
*mahīrājamupāgamya vacanaṃ prāha nirbhayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*adya tvāṃ ca haniṣyāmi tvaṃ vā hantā raṇe mama \|*  
*svavidyāṃ kuru bhūpa tvaṃ no cedyāsyasi vaiśasam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā mahīrājo raudrāstraṃ cāpa ādadhe \|*  
*tadastrācca mahāvahniḥ prādurbhūto bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sukhakhānistadāgneyaṃ saṃdadhau tasya śāṃtaye \|*  
*raudrāgninā ca saśaraḥ sukhakhānirlayaṃ gataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

39-45. Suta said- On the other hand, gaining a boon after worshipping the parthivalinga of Siva and leading a vast army of a lakh of soldiers, Prthviraja marched towards the city of Sirisa. At the command of the king, Camunda again getting enraged, together with a lakh of his soldiers, came out of the city and started fighting with the army of Sukhakhani. Making use of his fire-weapon, he killed the soldiers. Thereafter, he reached before the king Prthviraja and becoming fearless, said to him - “I shall surely kill him or alternatively you will be my killer. Therefore, О monarch, you first make use of your lore, otherwise you will have to prepare for going to the hell.” On hearing these words, Prthviraja placed the terrific arrow over his bow, as a result of which the terrific fire flames emerged out of it. In order to subside the same, Sukhakhani shot his fire arrow, but with the terrific weapon of Prthviraja, Sukhakhani was reduced to ashes.

46-61. After doing its assigned task, the weapon of Siva re-entered the quiver. Hearing the news about the event, Balakhana was frightened, reached the battleground, reminded of the enmity of his brother and started destroying the enemy army. At the same time, reciting the name of Sarada in his mind, Prthviraja also reached there. He was impressed with the strength of Balakhana and said to him- “You better listen to me. I have made deep pits within an area of a krosa and twelve warriors who are well-versed in waging the war, have been entrusted to guard them. Becoming victorious over my soldiers, in case you cross all the twelve pits, then I shall give you half of my kingdom.” The valorous Balakhana, taking the words of the king to be true, mounted over his horse named Kapota and holding a sword in his hand, started towards the pointed place. Observing the pits there, the valorous warrior killed the brave warriors in hundreds. Then the great and valorous warrior reached the twelfth pit, where he was surrounded by Camunda with his ten thousand warriors. The fighting was started. Balakhana destroyed the army of the deceitful Brahmana, he reached close to Camunda and started thundering aloud. They had also dug up a thirteenth pit, which was simply covered with hay and sand by name only. Underneath the same, the poisonous spear had been fixed and buried. As a move of destiny, Balakhana fell into that pit which was quite dark, besides being horrible spreading in an area of one krosa. Balakhana - the son of Vatsa, had his feet torn out in that pit. At that point of time, his horse came out of the pit with great difficulty and started killing the enemies with its hoofs. Camunda reached there at the same time, cut off the head of Balakhana and destroying his army at the same time. Hearing the news, Gajamukta got the pyre made and then she ended her life with her husband. Learning about this incident, Brahmananda arrived there with his wife and cremated the body of Sukhakhani. Thereafter, Prthviraja destroyed the capital city which was deprived of the soldiers and held celebrations in Dehali.

## Chapter 129. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-15. Suta said- Once in the month of Sravana, on the occasion of Nagapancami, the quarrelsome Mahipati proceeded to Dehali. In the Pancami festival there, where dance and music was usually arranged in a big way, there reaching before Prthviraja and offering his salutation to him, he spoke to him quite humbly- “O king, in the city of Mahipati, Vamana festival is celebrated with great pomp and show. Therefore, I have a desire that you should attend the festival.” On hearing this, Prthviraja asked Dhundhakara and Camunda with a lakh of soldiers that they should reach the forest of Sirisa and establish their army camp there. In the mean time, Mahipati at once reached the king Parimala of the solar race and after offering his salutation to him, the illusory wicked person, turning a serious face, said to him-“O king, in order to fight with you, Prthviraja is arriving here. After adoring the divine linga there, they shall kidnap your daughter Candravati by force. Therefore, О intelligent one, you get along with me with your army and making use of deceitful tricks, defeat him and then live comfortably in your capital city.” On hearing this, the divine king Parimala, accompanied with his army of four lakh soldiers, attacked the enemy army at dead of night and killed five lakhs of his warriors. Thereafter, he started using the guns, as a result of which in one single attempt a large number of warriors were killed. At the same time, the king Prthviraja got up and became ready for fighting the war. Taking him to be a strong enemy, he fought a terrific war. When armies of both the sides were at war, for the welfare and safety of her son the queen Malana went to the temple and worshipped the goddess farads with great devotion. She prayed to her- “O great goddess, you remove all the miseries. You remove all my obstructions and enlighten Udayasimha about it. After reciting the mantra of the goddess ten thousand times with oblations etc., she slept in the temple for the whole night. The goddess Sarada appeared in her dream and said to her- “O goddess Malana, don’t be grieved. The great obstruction with you shall stand removed shortly.” Then she also appeared in the dream of Udayasimha and said to him- “O son, your birth place is in trouble because of your enemy king. You go at once and redeem it at once, otherwise it would get destroyed.”

16-26. Listening to the words of the goddess and feeling surprised, he went to Devasimha and told him everything. Listening to him there, the chaste Svarnavati who was engaged in the performing of tapas and was suffering from the mental agony, cried for long. At the same time, feeling painful Udayasimha said to Devasimha- “What is my duty at the moment, you tell me.” Listening to his words, Devasimha with Laksana and Udayasimha started for Mahivati. Talana, who was an amsa of Bhima, was moving with his seven lakhs of army soldiers. Only Ahlada was absent from the army. Reaching the kalpaksetra, all of them disguised themselves as yogins. Then Udayasimha with Talana, Devasimha and valorous Laksana collected the instruments for dance and music and departed for the battle ground. Both the armies fought a horrible war there for a week. On the seventh day, all the great warriors also reached there. The king Parimala finding that his army was getting defeated and finding himself having been caught in the net of miseries, he went to Prthviraja who was mounted over his chariot. Yedava - the husband of Candravati, who was mounted over the elephant, instigated Dhundhukara and started fighting with bow and arrows.

27-35. At the same time, Brahmananda, who was riding the horse named Harinagara, challenged his enemy known by the name of Taraka. Both of them started shooting arrows at each other. Similarly, Ranajit started shooting arrows at his enemy the prince Mardana who felt upset with that attack, killing his son at the same time. Rupana was riding over the horse and was fighting with Madana who was born of the womb of a milkmaid, being the amsa of Samkha and was engaged in the terrific fight with Nrhari. When all the warriors were engaged in the fight, as per the advice of Mahipati and together with ten thousand soldiers Camunda entered the city of Mahipati, which was extremely charming, inhabited by the people of all the four castes and was filled with all the cereals and riches. Reaching the gate, the sinful Mahipati, together with Camunda alone, entered the royal palace. Meeting her brother, Malana feeling grieved, said to him- “Today is the eighth dark day of the month of Bhadrapada. The yavavrhi which has been sown in the house, has to be consigned in the Kirtisagara’s lake waters. But it could not be done. The sinful Prthviraja has also arrived on the occasion of the Vamana festival. In the absence of Ahlada and Udayasimha, I feel extremely painful.” On hearing this, the wicked Mahipati said- “A Brahmana named Devidata - a messenger of Udayasimha, has reached here from Kannauja. He shall perform all your tasks.”.

36-55. Hearing this, the goddess Candravali, adorned with all the ornaments and looking at the passionate Brahmana named Camunda, spoke to the mother fearlessly- “O mother, this Brahmana is a wicked cheat. He will kidnap me I am not aware as to who is he? Therefore, being a chaste woman, how can I go with him?” On hearing this, Mahipati felt extremely ashamed and left the place with Camunda. In the meantime, Brahmananda and other three lakhs of warriors, getting defeated, tightly closed the gates of the fort and were feeling extremely worried. On the other hand, according to the words of Mahiraja, together with six lakhs of warriors Prthviraja had surrounded the Pramadavana from all the sides. On reaching Sirisapura and finding the city having been deserted, Talana and other warriors were extremely surprised. Wandering in the deserted city here and there, they had an encounter with a sage named Mada. They offered their salutation to him. Then feeling worried, they asked the sage- “O sage, where has Balakhana gone? Where have the people of the city gone?” On hearing these words, the yogi Mada said- “Everything has been destroyed by Prthviraja. He has also deceitfully killed Balakhana. This beautiful pyre belongs to him.” Hearing the horrible words, feeling extremely grieved, Udayasimha started lamenting- “O brother, you belonged to the amsa of Dharmaputra. Where have you gone? It is extremely difficult for me to live on this earth without you. You appear before me at once, otherwise I shall put an end to my life.” In this way, he lamented for long. Then suddenly Balakhani, who was in pretayoni, appeared with his wife and narrated while crying, the way in which he met with his end. Thereafter, mounting over a divine plane he proceeded towards the heaven. His kala or the digit merged in Yudhi$thira. Then feeling grieved, Udayasimha offered oblation to his brother and reached the royal palace of Mahipati where playing on flute, he impressed the audience with his dance. Disguised as yogins, Talana played on vina, Devasimha played on cymbals and Laksana played on small drums. Listening to the sweet tune of music, the king became pleased. Then the queen Malana who was observing the celebrations of Vamana festival, spoke with choked voice- “I am so unlucky to have lost my lord and all his valorous brothers who were all amsas of Krsna. This city of Mahiraja has been deserted after their departure.”

## \|\| 2.129.56-70 \|\|

*ityuktāṃ malanāṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ sneha kātaraḥ \|*

56-70. Thus lamenting, Malana was spotted by Devasimha. Then Udayasimha spoke to her with humility- “O goddess, you please accept my words. О queen, we the yogins, are well-versed in the waging of war. Therefore, after accomplishing your task, we shall go to Naimisaranya. Therefore, whatever be the number of the barley spots carried by the ladies to the lake of Kirtisagara, we as the yogi warriors, shall protect you all.” Hearing this, her chaste daughter Candravati said to her mother- “The one who performs the dance is none else than Udayasimha, because both his eyes resemble the lotus flowers and his limbs are quite pleasant. Here on earth, who else except Udayasimha can be competent enough to protect us? It is because Prthviraja is invincible from all others.” On hearing this, overwhelmed with affection, the queen Malana together with other damsels, carrying the barley growth in their hands, started from that place with their palanquin and while walking, all of them were talking about the performance of Udayasimha. On the other hand, quickly organizing his warriors who had disguised themselves as yogins and were marching under the command of Talana, Laksana reached Kirtisagara and they all surrounded the damsels from all the sides and provided protection to them. They allowed them to finish their performance independently and freely. At that point of time, realizing about the arrival of Udayasimha, the quarrelsome Mahipati went with his son to Parimala of the solar race and spoke to him while crying- “O king, the yogins have plundered all the ladies, besides kidnapping Malana and Candravati. They arrived here disguised as yogins, but were the soldiers of Prthviraja and they have handed over Candravati, Taraka and my sister Malana to Prthviraja.” Listening to these horrible words, getting immensely enraged the valorous Brahmananda, leading an army of a lakh of soldiers, marched towards the place where a thousand soldiers of Prthviraja were present. Their soldiers were being carefully protected by Ranajit and Kamasena. In that battlefield, both the armies fought a terrific war. At that point of time, disguised as the yogins, Talana, Brahmananda, Laksana as well as the immensely valorous Abhayasimha and Devasimha themselves reached Mahipati and started helping him. In the mean time, becoming victorious over the enemies, they put them in bondages. At the same time, Kamasena arrived there.

71-90. Looking at him, Laksana bound Kamasena and Devasimha bound Ranajitsimha after defeating both of them and they remained there. At the same time, the valorous Brahmananda bound Talana and reached before Laksana and started fighting shooting the arrows. When the bow was destroyed, Laksana was also captured, while Devasimha got fainted. At this, the army, of the yogins started crying and they fled away from the battleground here and there. Observing the misfortune, he said to the ladies arriving there- “Brahmananda is destroying my army. Therefore, all of you should get along with me quickly.” Thus speaking, he accompanied with the ladies, as soon as Udayasimha reached before Brahmananda, then a terrific war started between Nara and Narayana. The valorous Udayasimha reached his chariot by the sky way and made him senseless with the use of his sword. When he was fainted, he freed Talana and others from the bondages. Thereafter, he departed from the battlefield disguised as yogi After the defeat of the yogi soldiers, the valorous Brahmananda, accompanied with all the ladies, departed towards their abodes. At the same time, with the support of Mahipati, the valorous Prthviraja, who had received a boon from lord Siva, surrounded all the damsels from all the sides. When the war started, Nrhari fought with Abhaya, Mardana with Rupana, Saradana with Madana, Taraka with Brahmananda and Camunda fought with Kamasena, making use of archery. Thereafter, valorous Abhaya, creating sound from the bow, broke the bow of Nrhari. Then he started fighting with sword. But when the sword was broken, Nrhari discarded the fight. Abhaya said in great anger- “You are the son of Prthviraja and my cousin brother, then why are you fleeing from the battleground discarding the dharma of a ksatriya?” On hearing these words, Nrhari getting immensely enraged, shot a horrible parigha over the hand of Abhaya as a result of which he died instantaneously and reached the heaven. He was bom of the amsa of Krtavarma, therefore he was absorbed in the same Krtavarma. Similarly, the valorous Sardana, after killing Madana - the son of a cowherd, shattered the enemy army and shouted the slogan victory aloud. Madana was bom of the amsa of Uttara, therefore he merged in the same race. At the same time, Rupana reached before the fainted Madana and started fighting Saradana with his sword. On the other hand, getting enraged Brahmananda put Taraka in bondage and reaching before Prthviraja, started fighting with him. Ranajit, who was desirous of victory, making use of a spear, cut off the head of Nrhari - the son of Prthviraja

*mṛte'sminmardane vīre tadā saradano balī \|*

*mahatkaṣṭamupāgamya raṇajinmalanodbhavaḥ \|*

*mahīrājastu balavānputraśokena duḥkhitaḥ \|*

*śirīṣākhyapuraṃ ramyaṃ yathā śūnyaṃ mayā kṛtam \|*  
*tathā mahāvatī sarvā brahmānaṃdādibhissaha \|*

*ityuktvā dhuṃdhukāraṃ vai cāhvayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ \|*

*iti śrutvā dhuṃdhukāro gatvā śīghraṃ ca dehalīm \|*  
*uṣitvā sapta divasānyuddhabhūmimupāgamat \|\| 105 \|\|*

*tadāṣṭalakṣasahito mahīrājo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*tārakeṇa ca saṃyukto yuddhāya samupāyayau \|\| 106 \|\|*

91-106. Nrhari was bom of the amfa of Dussasana. Therefore, after his death, his amsa was merged with the same. After the death of Nrhari, Mardana getting enraged, shot arrows one after the other over Ranajit, who was bom of the Stvika amsa. Thereafter, Ranajit - the son of Parimala, shattered his arrows. Then making use of his spear, he removed the head of Mardana from his body. At the death of Mardana, the valorous Saradana, making use of his spear, attacked Ranajit at his chest. Having been hurt with that weapon, feeling extremely painful, Ranajit severed the head of the enemy with his sword. At the death of his brother, Taraka getting extremely enraged, shot arrows at Ranajit who was mounted over a chariot. Ranajita on his part, destroyed the arrows and the bow of the enemy, and again shot three terrific arrows at the heart of the enemy. Like the serpent having been hurt with the rod, similarly getting enraged Taraka uttered the name of Siva in his heart and shot a poisonous arrow, which cut off the neck of the enemy. Thus he was killed and reached the heaven. At the death of the valorous warrior, Brahmananda felt extremely painful. Subsequently, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Bhadrapada, Brahmananda returned with the ladies to his abode guarded by sixty thousand soldiers. But because of the fear of Prthviraja, the doors of the main gate were securely closed and he went to take refuge with the goddess Sarada. The valorous Prthviraja, getting grieved of the death of his son, took a vow in presence of all the rulers that as he had ruined Srngapura, similarly I shall destroy Mahivati together with Brahmananda of the lunar family with my arrows. Thus speaking, the king called for Dhundhukara and said- “O dear, leading five lakhs of soldiers, you reach here at once.” On hearing this, Dhundhukura went to Dehall and returned to the battleground in a week. Thereafter, Prthviraja again made preparations for war with Taraka and eight lakhs of soldiers.

## Chapter 130. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

*sūta uvāca \|*

*bhādrakṛṣṇadaśamyāṃ ca malanā śokakātarā \|*  
*jananāyakamāhūya vacanaṃ prāha duḥkhitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aye kacchapadeśīya gotamānvayasaṃbhava \|*  
*harināgaramāruhya kānyakubjaṃ vrajādhunā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*putramāhlādamāhūya sānujaṃ matpriyaṃkaram \|*  
*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ hṛdi saṃciṃtya trai punaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*malanāṃ duḥkhitāṃ prāha na tvāyāsyati sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*rājñaḥ parimalasyaiva vākyaṃ matvā suduḥkhadam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ ruroda malanā satī \|*  
*punarmūrcchāṃ gatā bhūmau jīvanaṃ tyaktumudyatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*hā rāmāṃśa mahābāho vatsa kṛṣṇāṃśa sundara \|*  
*kva gatau saha devakyā tyaktvā māṃ maṃdabhāginīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tadā parimalāputro dṛṣṭvā rājñīṃ tathā gatām \|*  
*bahudhāśvāsya balavānkānyakubjapuraṃ yayau \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta said- At the start of the age of twenty seventh year of Udayasimha - the image of welfare, on the dark tenth day of the month of Bhadrapada, the queen Malana was extremely worried. She summoned the leader of the people and said to him- “O pride of her race, О dweller of Kacchapa country, you mount the horse Harinagara just now and go to Kanyakubja and bring here my son Ahlada with his younger brother, who are my beloved children.” On hearing this and taking the words spoken by her quite seriously, he offered his salutation to the depressed queen Malana and departed from that place. But getting reminded of the painful words of the king Parimala, she started crying and fainted. On regaining consciousness, she spoke getting ready to meet her end- “O Ahlada - the amsa of Sri Rama and beautiful dear Udayasimha -the amsa of Sri Krsna, where have you gone leaving an unfortunate person like me, together with DevakI?” At that point of time, Jananayaka - the son of Parimala reassured the queen variously. Thereafter, he departed for Kannauja.

## \|\| 2.130.8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*tvayā parimalāputrassaṃprokto jananāyakaḥ \|*  
*romaharṣaṇa no brūhi so'yaṃ kastena kiṃ kṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Rsis said- O Romaharsana, you have described Jananayaka as the son of Parimala. Therefore, we are desirous of knowing about him and what did he do? You kindly tell us.

## \|\| 2.130.9-14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iṃdraprasthapurevātsītpradyotaḥ kathito mayā \|*  
*pitā parimalasyaivāmātyo'naṃgamahīpateḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasya kanyā samājātā nāmnā parimalā mune \|*  
*duḥśalāṃśasamudbhūtā raṃbheva sukumārikā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tadvivāhārthamudyogaḥ kṛtaḥ pitrā svayaṃvaraḥ \|*  
*putraḥ kacchapabhūpasya sa nāmnā kamalāpatiḥ \|*  
*tāmudvāhma vidhānena svagehāya yayau mudā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tayossamāgamo jātaḥ putro'yaṃ jananāyakaḥ \|*  
*śatruvidyāparaḥ śūraḥ khaḍgayuddhaviśāradaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*jitvā bhūpānbalādvīraḥ siṃdhutīralanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍaṃśakaramādāya pitṛrājyamupasthitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ekadā tu mahīrājaḥ svasainyaparivāritaḥ \|*  
*kacchadeśamupāgamya karārthaṃ samupasthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. Suta said- Pradyota was the name of the father of Parimala, who was the dweller of Indraprastha, besides being the minister of the king Anangadeva. This has been told by me already. О sage, he had a daughter named Parimala, who was bom of the amsa of Duhsala. She had the body as soft as that of Rambha. Her father arranged a svayamvara for her marriage. During that svayamvara, Kamalapati - the son of the lord of the Kacchapa country, married the girl in an appropriate manner. Thereafter, both of them departed for their home. With the union of both of them, the son named Jananayaka was bom. He was well-versed in the battleground, valorous and had proficiency in the use of sword in the war. He was gaining victory over the rulers living over the banks of the river Sindhi and recovered one sixth of the produce as tax from them.

*no cettvāṃ vai sanagaraṃ kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ kṣapayiṣyati \|*  
*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ vāmano gauravaṃśajaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhayabhīto viniścitya pradadau harināgaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

15-30. Once the king Prthviraja, in order to collect tax from him, marched towards the Kacchapa country. Reaching there, both the armies fought a terrific battle. The rulers of Kacchapa belonging to the solar race were defeated by Prthviraja. Thereafter, leaving that country, he migrated to the country of Mahavati. At that point of time, the king Parimala granted some village to him. While living there, he became famous by this name. Thus at the command of Parimala, Jananayaka of Kacchapa country was going to Kannauja. After his undertaking of the journey and with the support of Mahila, Prthviraja ordered Camunda to capture Jananayaka with a lakh of soldiers. Obeying the command, Camunda reached the bank of river Vetravati and stopped the forward movement of of the solar race. Thereafter, with the use of his sword, the valorous warrior Jananayaka cut off the heads of a hundred soldiers, flew through the sky way and hold in his hand the crown of Camunda - the commander, in his hands. At that point of time, Camunda humbly spoke to him- “You belong to the race of Ksatriyas, while others are givers of the charity to the Brahmanas. Therefore, O valorous one, you kindly return my crown to me and enjoy long life.” Hearing these words, Jananayaka returned the crown to Camunda. Thereafter, reaching the city of Kuthara, protected by the king YAmana, he fearlessly slept under the shade of a banyan tree getting tired. At the comfortable place where that valorous person rested, Vamana came to know the cause of his arrival there through his spies. Then concealing himself, he appeared in ordinary costumes and stole the horse known by the name of Harinagara. When the divine horse was stolen and finding the horse missing, Jananayaka cried for long. Thereafter, following the footprints of the horse, he reached Yamana and spoke to him fearlessly-“You are the ornament of the race of Gauras, but have made the Ksatriyas race as laughable on earth for all time to come. I pray to you that you are a politician. You return the horse to me and live comfortably on earth, otherwise Udayasimha shall surely destroy you with this city.” Hearing this, Yamana of Gaura race was panic stricken and with a firm resolve in his mind, he returned the horse Harinagara.

31-64. But out of his greed, he failed to return the whip which was studded with gems of various types and took false oath. Feeling hurt with the false oath, Jananayaka - the son of Parimala said- “O monarch, the lust for this whip shall surely destroy your fort.” Thus speaking, the excellent warrior reached the excellent town of Kannauja. Out of arrogance, Laksana said there- “Who are you riding fearlessly over the horse?” He said- ‘Parimala - the great king of lunar race, has sent me. О monarch, you are kind to those who take refuge in you. I have come to you alone. With the support of Mahila and using the terrific arrows, Prthviraja has decided to destroy the lunar race. Therefore, along with Ahlada and your army, you kindly come along with me. О lord, by moving now, you will kindly bestow life to those who are almost dead.” At the words thus spoken by him (Jananayaka), Laksana offered his salutation to Jayacandra and also told him the news about Prthviraja’s attack over Mahavati. On hearing this, Jayacandra called for Jananayaka and said to him- “The king Parimala is extremely cruel, because he had deserted his relationship with me who had been his master and he had established relationship with Prthviraja - the ruler of Indraprastha. Taking him to be his own, he deserted the people, who in fact were guarding him. Therefore, one has to reap the reward for whatever he does. (What can I do in this case)?” On hearing this, Udayasimha spoke quite humbly- “O lord, Parimala is impure but at the advice of Mahila, deserting you he joined Prthviraja. Therefore, I pray that you are well aware of all the adharmas. You kindly forgive him for that fault on his part. With your permission, we would like to live with him alone.” On hearing these words, Jayacandra said- “O Udayasimha, you pay the price for staying with me and you can go back with your family atonce. Failing which, it would be impossible for you to go.” On hearing this, Udayasimha, who could impress all, spoke smilingly- “I have performed victory march on all the sides. You kindly pay me the tax for the same. Thereafter, you can deduct the rent for our stay here.” At these words of Udayasimha, feeling ashamed Jayacandra allowed seven lakhs of his soldiers to accompany him. Virasimha, together with his family and Laksana, went to the king and offering his salutation to him, departed from that place. While travelling on the way, they surrounded the fort of the city of Kuthara. Learning about their arrival, the king Vamana happily returned the whip to them. The valorous Vamana was commanded by Laksana to follow him and he himself proceeded hurriedly towards the bank of river Yamuna. Drinking the water of Yamuna, the valorous Laksana together with the army of sixty thousand soldiers, ordered Gangasimha to march in advance and he himself started in order to reach the pleasant bank of the river Vetravati. Reaching there with his army which was well-equipped, the valorous Ksatriyas camped there. In the mean time, with a lakh of his army soldiers and thundering aloud, Camunda started the war with the terrific guns. Both the armies fought the gun battle for a prahara. Then observing the defeat of his army, Raktabija quickly reached in the battleground, riding over an elephant and started shooting arrows at the soldiers of the army of Talana. Having been engaged in the war, some of the warriors of the army of Talana were killed, while a number of them fled away here and there. They were all attacked by Camunda. Observing that his army soldiers were getting shattered, Talana made use of a parigha and made Camunda to fall on earth with his elephant. But making use of his sword, the valorous Camunda defeated Talana who was fighting with parigha and tried to advance further.” At the same time, Laksana -the leader of the enemy army, arrived with the spears. At that point of time, the Raktabija appeared in thousands, who were holding saktis and other weapons. They challenged the Ksatriyas in the war. Finding the several forms of Raktabija, Ahlada and other brave warriors, getting frightful, reached the valorous Brahmananda. Looking at them, Brahmananda went to his father and heard about the arrival of Laksana. Hearing the news of the arrival of Laksana, the king Parimala overwhelmed with love, reached before Ahlada and in utmost anxiety started crying in choked voice. At that point of time, Devaki - the goddess of welfare and overwhelmed with affection, said to the king- “We are quite miserable before you and are ready to serve you as earlier. It is you who had disowned us as a result of which we were compelled to take refuge with the other king. But this was ail the result of the sins of the earlier birth. You kindly forgive us.” On hearing this, the king Paramananda made Ahlada a minister and the command of the army was entrusted to Udayasimha.

65-68. On the fifth day, Prthviraja who was much more proud of the strength of Camunda, reached there and surrounded the city from all the sides. Both of them fought a terrific war for a month. At the auspicious time of the sunrise, Udayasimha, who was leading the army of a lakh of soldiers, reached before Camunda and cut off the heads of his different forms, one by one, which were a thousand in number. After Camunda’s heads were cut off, the warriors appeared in lakhs. The entire army was upset with the killing of Camunda. At that point of time, Udayasimha also getting frightened, started offering prayer to Sarada -the goddess of welfare.

69-79. Udayasimha said- “О goddess, you are dweller of Brahmaloka, salutation to you. O goddess Sarada, you with your sound have expanded this entire universe. I offer my salutation to the goddess who in order to kill Raktabija, took to the form of Camunda. O goddess, I take refuge with you. You kindly protect me.” On hearing this prayer, the goddess Bhagavati - the bestower of the boons and who can do everything, was lodged in the sword of Udayasimha and reduced all the forms of Raktabija to ashes. When a lakh of forms of the enemy were reduced to ashes, only Camunda could be seen present on earth. At that point of time, Udayasimha made Camunda captive and putting him in bondage, sent him to Brahmananda. Hearing this, Prthviraja got immensely frightened. He rushed to the king Parimala who was the image of compassion and love, and said to him- ‘‘You kindly forgive me for my fault. Influenced with the words spoken by Mahipati, I have committed this blunder and because of that, I feel immensely frightened. O valorous one, today my quarrel with you has turned into love and affection. From today onwards, you are my closest relative and I happen to be yours.” On hearing these words, the king Parimala said to him- O son of Ratnabhanu, you go to the one who is famous by the name of Laksana and who is good at those who take refuge with him. He is the devotee of Visnu and is quite compassionate as well.” On hearing these words, Prthviraja took to the form of a Brahmana, went to Laksana and prostrated before him on the ground. At that point of time, the valorous Laksana also expressed excessive love and attachment for Prthviraja. Thereafter, along with seven lakhs of his soldiers, he marched towards Kannauja. Then on the occasion of the month of Phalguna, all the people returned to their respective abodes. At the start of the month of Caitra, they performed sraddha at Gaya. Then during the bright fortnight, he returned to his abode and served food to a thousand Vedic Brahmanas.

1-13. Suta said- At the start of twenty eight years of his age, during the month of Kartika, on Monday, in Krttika constellation and during Vyatipata-yoga, leading his army of ten thousand soldiers together with Svarnavati, Udayasimha started for the bank of the river Ganga in order to drink the Ganga water and finding the marriage crown, where the forest of lotus flowers is found. In the same forest of lotus flowers, the sage Valmiki resides. That particular site, because of its being the form of Brahman over the bank of river Ganga, is said to be pinned like iron. Reaching there, the auspicious soul Udayasimha took his bath with Puspavati and then delightfully gave away a thousand cows in charity to the Brahmanas. At the same time, a beautiful whore known by the name of Sobha arrived there. She was born in a Mleccha family, but was quite pleasant. At the sight of the extremely beautiful Udayasimha - the best of humans, she was filled with lust for him and fainted. Finding her so fainted, Udayasimha, who could attract all, went to his abode and calling the Brahmanas asked them- “O Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas and Sastras, you tell me who is the composer of the eighteen Puranas? What is the reward one achieve by listening to them.” Listening to these excellent words, the learned Brahmanas well-versed in the Sastras, answered to Udayasimha, who was himself well-versed in the ancient literature, in beautiful voice- “Visnu Purana was composed by the sage Parasara, while Skanda Purana was composed by lord Siva. Brahma composed Padma Purana, Bhagavata was composed by Sukadeva. Brahma Purana was composed by Brahma and lord Visnu composed Garuda Purana. These are the six Puranas which are said to be the Satvikas. The sage Vyasa composed the Matsya Purana, Kurma Purana, Nrsimha Purana, Vamana Purana, Siva Purana and Vayu Purana. These six Puranas are said to be Rajasika and relate to the science of rituals. The sage Markandeya composed Markandeya Purana as well as the Varaha Purana.

*tāmasāḥ ṣaṭ smṛtāḥ prājñaiḥ śaktidharmaparāyaṇāḥ \|*

14-26. The excellent Agni Purana was composed by sage Angira, while Tapdl composed the Linga Purana as well as the Вrahmananda Purana. On the other hand, lord Mahadeva composed the Bhavisya Purana. These six Puranas are devoted to Sakti and are known as the Tamasa Puranas. Bhagavata Purana has been treated to be the best of all the Puranas. When the ruler of terrific Kali prevails on earth, the king Vikramaditya travelled from Kailasa on earth and summoned all the sages. At that point of time, the great Rsis dwelling at Naimisaranya had conceived the number of the Puranas as eighteen. The religious-minded Udayasimha when learnt about the same, he organized the recitation of Bhagavata Purana and after listening to it with devotion, he distributed gold to the Brahmanas on the seventh day. He also gave away food to a thousand Vedic Brahmanas. At that point of time, the arrogant Shobha, taking to the form of a Bhiksuki, reached before Udayasimha and started displaying her illusion. She created an illusion by which, with the help of the ganas of Siva and arrogant Pisacas, could turn the people into stones. Observing the same, the goddess Svarnavati who was the wife of Ahlada, destroyed the illusion of Sobha and returned to her abode. The said whore, getting enraged, then stole the precious ornaments of Svarnavati, which were of the value of a lakh of gold coins. Thereafter, she proceeded to the Bahlika country. Reaching Kalpaksetra, Svarnavati - the sister of Netrasimha learnt that the whore had stolen her ornaments. Then feeling painful, she said to Udayasimha- “The whore has stolen all my ornaments. О valorous one, you go at once and come back with my ornaments. This is a pill made by me. In case you keep it in your mouth, the wicked illusion of the whore will have no effect on you. I have made it for your welfare.”

27-42. On hearing this, Udayasirmha, who could impress all, received the pill (and keeping it in his mouth) he departed from that place. While travelling, he reached Varahaksetra, where he spotted the whore. She also sighted Udayasimha, who was as beautiful as the god of love. She reached before Udayasimha by creating an illusion. But her illusion became infructuous as a result of which she started sobbing. Finding her th-e , the compassionate Udayasimha felt delightful and went to her and got the ornaments back from her and then said to her- “O excellent one, why are you crying. You tell me the truth. Don’t delay.” She said-“My brother is known by the name of Sahara. He is as dear to me as my life, but he has met with death with five hundreds of dancers. Therefore, I am crying before you.” Thus speaking, with her illusion she produced bodies of the degraded people. Thereafter, the whore, who was always successful in her efforts, started crying again before Udayasimha and even pretended to end her life. Then the compassionate Udayasimha, at the sight of her pitiable condition, said to her- “O graceful lady, how could your brothers be brought back to life, you tell me?” At this, she replied- “O valorous one, they can regain their lives with the pill which is kept by you in your mouth. Therefore, you plcase give it to me.” When she so desired, Udayasimha gave away the pill to her. Thereafter, the wicked woman, becoming lustful, delightfully made him a parrot and lodged the same in a cage. Then she departed to her city of Bahlika. Reaching her abode, she turned Udayasimha as a human and embraced Udayasimha who was a deeply religious person. Observing the whore in such a pitiable condition, Udayasimha mentally recited the Devi-sukta for the goddess Jagadamba. Then she turning herself to be like a bird parched in the tamarind tree, again turned Udayasimha as a parrot. In the mean time, making use of the illusion of lord Visnu in order to know the secret, Svaranvati turned herself into the form of an eagle and reached there. She found the yogi having been turned as a parrot. At the same time, the whore turning Udayasimha back to human form, said to him quite humbly.

43-64. “О my bIeloved lord, I am badly suffering from lust, therefore you embrace me immediately. You are well aware of the dharma. Therefore, you kindly save me by uniting with me.” At these words of the whore, Udayasimha said—“O beautiful one, you listen to my words. Being a believer of the Arya dharma, I strictly follow the Vedic-dharma. Accordingly, a person who does not unite with his wife during the menstrual period, he is termed as sinful and after spending time in the hell, he takes to the form of a bird. Therefore, to unite with the wives of others one has to fall in the hell. There is no doubt about it.” On hearing these words, she said- “O excellent one, the sages like Visvamitra and Srnga had united with the whores in earlier times, but they never went to the hell. Therefore, you better embrace the passionate women like me.” On hearing this, Udayasimha replied again- “Both of them were the great ascetics and they did so on the strength of their tapas. But presently, I am unable to do so. Woman is said to be half of the body of a man, particularly for the sexual intercourse. I am an Arya Purusa and you happen to be a whore, who is used by many people. Therefore, the sexual intercourse of both of us is impossible. Because from the eastern face initially the word Ri emerged, by which Sanatana became popular. Similarly, from the southern face there emerged the word Yoga/Yajuh. From the western face the word Samaja emerged. Therefore, all the Vedic words based on the meters, are all dear to the Brahmanas. Only the letters emerged from the Atharvan. Therefore, the words which emerged from the five faces are known as the worldly ones, which are Prakrta and have four lakhs divisions. Therefore, the auspicious soul who recites all the four Vedas, he by crossing the worldly forest of birth and death, ultimately attains moksa. When the breath reaches upto the neck, one should not make use of the Yavani language and one should not out go to a Jain temple, even when trampled under the feet of an elephant. These are the words usually heard by the people and spoken by the sages. Therefore, how could I disown my dharma, which bestows comforts to all.” On hearing these words, the whore who was bom in a Mleccha family, feeling immensely enraged, belaboured Udayasimha with canes. Then again she turned him as a parrot and gave him no food. The entire performance of the whore was witnessed by the goddess Svarpavati, who then taking to the form of a woman, turned Udayasimha as a mosquito. She stealthily disappeared from that place and again took to the form of an eagle, after which she departed to her country. She made Udayasimha to sit over her back and reached the city of Mayura.

65-80. On meeting her, Makaranda recognized her to be Svarnavati - the daughter of Netrasimha, as also Udayasimha. He gracefully touched her feet and lodged her in his own palace. On the other hand, when the whore Sobhana went to the cage and found it empty, she fainted and fell down on the ground. On regaining consciousness, she started crying- “what should I do without Udayasimha? Where should I go?” She thus started lamenting variously. Thereafter, she went to Madalinapura. There was an evil person named Mahamedha, who was well-versed in illusion and indulged in satanic practices. After worshipping him, the whore got ready to end her life there. Finding her there, Mahamedha delightfully reached the temple of Marosthala Mahadeva and started worshipping him in Sanskrit language. Feeling pleased with him, Siva said to his attendant - “The valorous Udayasimha - the follower of Arya-dharma has been kidnapped by Svarnavati, therefore to have an audience with her, you come along with me to Mayuranagara.” At these words spoken by him, the illusory one, accompanied by five thousand dancers and Sobha - the whore as well as Sahara started from that place on knowing about this secret from the goddess Visnumayi Indula, Ahlada and Devasimha arrived at Mayuranagara with three lakhs of his warriors and met Makaranda. At the same time, Sobhana and Sahara reached there with their followers and spread their terrific illusion there, which was horrible for the enemy. They started making the formations. The storms started blowing with huge clouds. The star brands started falling. The dust storms started blowing. Because of the terrific illusion, there was darkness on all the sides. Observing this, the valorous Makaranda, seated over a chariot, reached there from where the illusion was being operated. The valorous warrior destroyed the entire illusion with the weapon known Sanibhalla. Then he captured the wicked Sahara and reached his abode. At that point of time, the whore Sobha created Kama-maya in which a number of whore well-versed in dance and music had collected there. They were dancing and singing to attract all the people. Observing the dance, except Devasimha and Udayasimha, all felt attracted towards the same, becoming inactive at the same time. At that point of time, getting devoted to Kamaksa goddess, Svamavati brought them back to consciousness and they stood up. Thereafter, they captured Sobhana and brining her to Mayuradhvaja, bound her with iron chains. When Mahamada came to know of this, he devoting his mind to lord Siva, spread his Sambari lore, in which a large number of creatures were visible including tigers, lions, boars, monkeys, mosquitoes, bugs, serpents, vultures as well as the crows in flocks and were devouring the lions. The warriors were in the state consternation and they started fleeing here and there. But ultimately, the wicked Sobhana had to accept the position of a slave girl of Svamavati. On the other hand, Ahlada reduced to dust Sahara and all other dancers. Thereafter, the pitchers filled with their blood were buried in the ground. Thus the war was carried on there for four months. Then at the start of the month of Vaisakha, all the warriors left for their respective abodes. О Brahmanas, I have narrated the story to you. Now what more do you want to know about?

1\. The Rsis said- О great sage, you had mentioned earlier about a girl named Kinnari. Where was she bom? You kindly tell us about her in detail.

*patirme bhava he nātha śaraṇāgatavatsala \|\| 6 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tathā kṛtvā tayā saha \|*  
*sa reme muniśārdūlaḥ śuko vijñānakovidaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tayossakāśātsaṃjajñe munirnāma suto'nayoḥ \|*  
*tapaścakāra balavāndvādaśābdaṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tasmai dadau tadā patnīṃ svarṇadevasya vai sutām \|*  
*kubero rudrasahitaḥ sa munistu mudānvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tayā reme prasannātmā tayorjātā sutottamā \|*  
*kinnarī nāma vikhyātā himatuṃge samudbhavā \|*  
*tapaścacāra sā devī rūpayauvana śālinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavāñchaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*makaraṃdāya dhīrāya dadau tāṃ rucirānanām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*munistu śaṃkaraṃ prāha devadeva namo'stu te \|*  
*matsutāyai varaṃ dehi rāṣṭravardhanamuttamam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā śivaḥ prāha guruṃḍānte ca bhūtale \|*  
*madhyadeśe ca te rāṣṭraṃ bhaviṣyati sukhapradam \|*  
*triṃśadabdapramāṇena tatpaścātkṣayameṣyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu sa munirhimatuṃganivāsakaḥ \|*  
*makaraṃdena sahitastatra vāsamakārayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

2-14. Suta said- Once upon a time, in the land of Caitraratha, people of various castes lived there. On the arrival of the spring season, the gods used to enjoy sports there. Once an apsara of the heaven known by the name of Manjughosa went to the place of Sukadeva -the best of the Munis. She found him in the form of a beautiful child and tried to attract him. The lustful whore danced and sang over the tune of the music, displaying loveable dancing postures. Thereafter, with folded hands, she offered her prayer to him. The sage Sukadeva at that point of time, listening to her lotus like prayer, delightfully asked her to seek for a boon. Hearing the loveable words of the sage, she prayed to him- “O master, you protect those who take refuge with you. You kindly accept to be my husband.” After accepting her prayer, the sage then united with her. With the union of both of them, a son was born to them, who performed tapas for twelve years continuously and getting pleased by which Rudra with Kubera gave him the daughter of Svarnadeva as his wife. Both of them united and gave birth to a daughter, who came to be known by the name of Kinnari. The girl who possessed enormous beauty and youthfulness, started performing tapas. For the welfare of the world, Lord Siva entrusted the care of that girl to the king Makaranda. In the mean time, the sage prayed to lord Siva saying- “O lord of gods, salutation to you. You kindly give me a husband for my daughter and give me a kingdom of the ocean.” On hearing this, lord Siva said- “After the end of the rule of Gurundas on earth, you will rule the country of Madhyadesa. But after three hundred years, it would be on the decline.” On hearing these words, the dweller of the Utuhga peak of the Himalaya together with Makaranda, started living there.

## \|\| 2.132.15-27 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ śubhām \|*  
*ūnatriṃśābdakaṃ prāpte kṛṣṇāṃśe raṇakāraṇam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*netrapālasya nagaraṃ nānādhātuvicitritam \|*  
*matvā nyūnapatirbauddho rurodha nagaraṃ śubham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*saptalakṣayuto rājā bauddhasiṃho mahābalaḥ \|*  
*trilakṣabalasaṃyuktaissārddhaṃ yuddhamacīkarat \|\| 17 \|\|*

*saptāhorātramabhavatsenāyuddhaṃ bhayānakam \|*  
*yogasiṃho bhogasiṃho vijayaśca mahābalaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*jaghāna śātravīṃ senāṃ bauddhasiṃhena pālitām \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare prāptāḥ śyāmajāpakadeśagāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bauddhā māyāvinassarve lokamānyaprapūjakāḥ \|*  
*punarjātaṃ mahadyuddhaṃ māsamekaṃ tayostadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*netrapālājñayā sarve kṛṣṇāṃśādyāḥ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśo biṃdulārūḍho devaḥ svahayasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*iṃdulaśca karālāśve maṃḍalīko gaje sthitaḥ \|*  
*gautamaśca samāyāto harināgarasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tālanaśca samāyātaḥ siṃhinyupari saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*dhānyapālastailyakāro yuyutsoraṃśasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*lallasiṃhaśca balavānkuṃtibhojāṃśasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*tāmbūlīyakajātīyo lakṣaṇānujñayā yayau \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tadā tu netrasiṃhaśca saptalakṣabalairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*pālitaścāṣṭabhirvīraisteṣāṃ nāśāya cāyayau \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhayabhītāśca te bauddhāstyaktvā deśaṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*cīnadeśamupāgamya yuddhabhūmimakārayan \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tadanuprayayuste vai hūhānadamupasthitāḥ \|*  
*māghamāse tu saṃprāpte punaryuddhamavartata \|\| 27 \|\|*

15-27. Thus narrating, I am going to tell you another auspicious story. When Udayasimha reached the age of twenty nine years, the capital city of Netrapala was surrounded by the Bauddhas from all the four sides, which was built with various metals and was of astonishing type for the simple reason that the ruler of that city was considered to be quite weak by them. With the army of seven lakhs soldiers of king, Bauddha Singh fought a terrific battle with his army of three lakhs soldiers. The battle went on for seven days. The warriors of both the sides continuously fought for a week in which Yogasimha, Bhogasimha and valorous Vijaya fighting with the enemy army led by Bauddha Singh, totally destroyed the enemy army. At the same time, the Bauddhas from Syama and Japaka countries also arrived there, who were adorable by all the Iokas. With the arrival of the foreign armies, the battle continued for another month. With the inspiration of the king Netrapala, Udayasimha and other warriors also reached there, in which Udayasimha was mounted over Bindula, Devasimha over Indula, Mandalika over the horse Karala, Ahlada over the king of elephants, Gautama over Harinagara and Talana joined the war over his mare named Simhini Dhanyapala, Taili who was from the family of Lallasimha and with the command of Laksana, the betel leaves seller also arrived there. At that point of time, the king Netrasimha with seven lakhs of his soldiers who were led by his close associates, were quite secure. They all marched on for the destruction of the Bauddhas, who getting terrified deserted that country and fled towards China and reaching there, they also declared the war. These people also following the Bauddhas, tried to reach the bank of the river Huha. During the month of Magha, both the armies again fought there.

## \|\| 2.132.28-38 \|\|

*śyāmadeśodbhavā lakṣaṃ tathā lakṣaṃ ca jāpakāḥ \|*  
*daśa lakṣāścīnadeśyā yuddhāya samupasthitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśo lakṣasenāḍhyo devo lakṣasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*netrapālaśca lakṣāḍhayo yogabhogasamanvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*maṃḍalīkaścendulena lakṣasainyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*dhyānapālo lallasiṃho lakṣasainyānvitaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*jananāyaka evāpi lakṣasainyayutaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tālano lakṣasenāḍhyo yuddhāya samupāgataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatra yuddhamabhūdghoraṃ bauddhānāmāryakaissaha \|*  
*pakṣamātraṃ muniśreṣṭha yamalokavivarddhanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sapta lakṣaṃ hatā bauddhā dvilakṣaṃ cāryadeśajāḥ \|*  
*tataste bhayabhītāśca tyaktvā yuddhaṃ gṛhaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kṛtvā dārumayīṃ senāṃ kalayaṃtraprabhāvataḥ \|*  
*gajāśca daśasāhasrā saśūrāḥ kāṣṭhanirmitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ekalakṣaṃ hayārūḍhā dārupāśca raṇonmukhāḥ \|*  
*sahasraṃ mahiṣārūḍhāssahasraṃ kolapṛṣṭhagāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*siṃhārūḍhāssahasraṃ ca sahasraṃ haṃsavāhanāḥ \|*  
*kaṃkagomāyugṛdhrāṇāṃ śyāmārūḍhāḥ pṛthaktathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*uṣṭrāḥ saptasahasrāṇi saśūrāśca raṇonmukhāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sapādalakṣaiśca kāṣṭhasainyaiśca mānuṣāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dvilakṣāṇi kṣayaṃ jagmuḥ kṛṣṇāṃśādyaiḥ surakṣitāḥ \|*  
*tato hāhākṛtaṃ sainyaṃ cāryyāṇāṃ ca nanāśa tat \|\| 38 \|\|*

28-38. Bauddha Singh had with him a lakh of the soldiers from Syama, besides ten lakhs of the Chinese Buddhist soldiers. Similarly, the king Netrapala had Udayasimha, Yogasimha, Bhogasimha. Palasimha, Indula, Mandalika, Dhanapala, Lallanasimha, Jananayaka and Laksana. All of them had a lakh of soldiers with each one of the commanders, who had arrived to wage a war. The Aryan’s as well as the Bauddha’s war continued for a fortnight, increasing at the same time the population of Yamaloka. In the battlefield, the Bauddhas lost seven lakhs of their soldiers, while the Aryans lost about two lakhs of their warriors. But they raised the army of wood by mechanism and attacked the Aryans again. In this war, the soldiers of wood, ten thousand elephants, a lakh of steed, a thousand he-buffalos, a thousand kolas, a thousand lions, a thousand swans, eagles and jackals, vultures and seven thousand camel riders were killed in the battlefield. In this war, the Bauddhas lost a lakh of wooden soldiers, while Udayasimha lost a lakh of soldiers. Observing this, there was a great panic in the army of the Aryans.

## \|\| 2.132.39-49 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tatkautukaṃ ramyaṃ jayanto yuddhakovidaḥ \|*  
*āgneyaṃ śaramādāya kāṣṭhasainyeṣu cākṣipat \|\| 39 \|\|*

*bhasmībhūtāśca te sarve tatraiva vilayaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*trilakṣaṃ kṣatriyāḥ śeṣā jayaṃtaṃ raṇakovidam \|*  
*cakrurjayaravaṃ tatra tuṣṭuvuśca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tadā tu cīnajā bauddhāḥ kṛtvā viṃśatsahasrakān \|*  
*hayārūḍhāṃllohamayānpreṣayāmāsurūrjitān \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yogasiṃho gajārūḍho dhanurbāṇadharo valī \|*  
*kaṃṭheṣu lohajānvīrāṃstāḍayāmāsa vai tadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mṛtāste paṃcasāhasrā yogasiṃhaśarārditāḥ \|*  
*bauddhasiṃhastadā śūro dṛṣṭvā tasya parākramam \|*  
*kṛtvā lohamayaṃ siṃhaṃ yogasiṃhamapeṣayat \|\| 43 \|\|*

*pātena tasya siṃhasya sa vīro maraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*tadā tu bhogasiṃhaśca hayārūḍho jagāma ha \|*  
*svabhallena ca taṃ siṃhaṃ hatvā tatra jagarja vai \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tadā tu bauddhasiṃhena śārdūlastatra coditaḥ \|*  
*sahayo bhogasiṃhaśca tenaiva maraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*mātulau mṛtyuvaśagau dṛṣṭvā svarṇavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*karālaṃ hayamā ruhya bauddhasiṃhamupāyayau \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śaramādāya vai śīghraṃ nāmnā saṃmohanaṃ śubham \|*  
*mohayitvā ripubalaṃ bauddhasiṃhasamanvitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*baddhvā tānbauddhasiṃhādīnnṛpāndaśasahasrakam \|*

*tadā te harṣitāssarve prapeṣya nagaraṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*tadveśma yojanāyāmaṃ sarvasaṃpatsamanvitam \|*  
*luṇṭhayitvā balātsarve nṛpadurgamupāyayuḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

39-49. Looking at this battle scene, making use of his fire arrows, Indula reduced to ashes the wooden soldiers with their vehicles. But the remaining three lakhs of the Ksatriya soldiers pleased Indula who was well-versed in the battlefield by shouting the slogans of victory. At that point of time, the Bauddhas from China created twenty thousand soldiers in iron and sent them once again for war in their vehicles. Finding their arrival, Yogasimha shooting his arrows, shattered all the Chinese warriors. As a result of getting wounded with the arrows of Yogasimha, the five thousand iron warriors were killed. Observing the power of Yogasimha, Bauddhasimha made a lion of iron and sent to him. With the attack of the lion, Yogasimha was killed. Observing the fall of Yogasimha, Bhogasimha killed the lion with his spear and then thundered aloud. At the same time, with the shooting of an instrument by Bauddhasimha, Bhogasimha was also killed with his horse. At that point of time, Indula - the son of Svarnavati, finding that both her maternal uncles had met with death, mounted over his horse named Karala and reached before Bauddhasimha. Then he at once overpowered Bauddhasimha and thousand of his follower kings and put them in bondage. He destroyed all the yantras completely and became successful in reaching before Udayasimha. On their arrival, getting pleased, they proceeded towards the city of Prapesya. The houses of that city were filled with all types of riches with which the dwellers of that place enjoyed all the comforts. After plundering and destroying all the houses, the soldiers reached the fort of the king.

## \|\| 2.132.50-52 \|\|

*bauddhasiṃhastadāgatya jayantena vimocitaḥ \|*  
*sutāṃ svāṃ padmajāṃ nāmnā jayantāya dadau mudā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*daśakoṭīḥ suvarṇasya cāhlādāya tadā dhanam \|*  
*sarvaiśca bauddhavṛndaiśca tatraiva śapathaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*āryadeśaṃ na yāsyāmaḥ kadācidrāṣṭrahetave \|*  
*ityuktvā tānpraṇamyāśu saṃprasthānamakārayan \|*  
*trilakṣaiśca yutāste vai netrapālagṛhaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. When Bauddhasimha was released by Indula, he married his daughter known by the name of Padmaja to Indula. Then Ahlada was given ten crores of gold coins. Thereafter, the Bauddhas took an oath before them that- “Because of the lust of the kingdom, we shall never go over to the Arya country.” Thereafter, offering their salutations the Bauddhas departed from that place. Netrapala on the other hand, returned to his abode together with three lakhs of his warriors.

## \|\| 2.132.53 \|\|

*ṛṣayaḥ ūcuḥ \|*  
*indulena kathaṃ sūta tatra prāṇīkṛtā na hi \|*  
*supriyā yogasiṃhādyāstanno vada vicakṣaṇa \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Rsis said- Why did Indula fail to bring back to life the valorous warriors like Yogasimha and others?

## \|\| 2.132.54-59 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āgatā yamalokādvai katicitprāṇino bhuvi \|*  
*tadā tu duḥkhito devo maheṃdrāntamupāyayau \|\| 54 \|\|*

*devarāja namastubhyaṃ sarvadevapriyaṃkara \|*
