*ato vai lokamaryādā viruddhā dṛśyate bhuvi \|\| 55 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ mahendro devamāyayā \|*  
*vaḍavāmṛtamāhṛtya tathā vai svargagāṃ gatim \|*  
*jayaṃtasya svaputrasya mumoda sa suraiḥ saha \|\| 56 \|\|*

*indulaśca tadā duḥkhī śāradāṃ sarvamaṃgalām \|*  
*pūjayitvā vidhānena yogadhyāna paro'bhavat \|\| 57 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ śubhām \|*  
*netrapālaśca balavānbahuputraḥ śucānvitaḥ \|*  
*daśakoṭimitaṃ svarṇaṃ tebhyo dattvā samaṃ samam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*prasthānaṃ kārayāmāsa cāṣṭānāṃ balaśālinām \|*  
*te vai dvilakṣasainyāḍhyāḥ svagehāya yayurmudā \|\| 59 \|\|*

54-59. Suta said- Some people from the place of Yama reached the earth and observing the situation there, returned again to Indra and prayed to him- “O lord of all the gods, salutation to you. О lord, reaching the earth, Jayanta (Indula) himself is bringing back the people to life. Therefore, the tradition of this world is being misused on earth.” On hearing this, Indra - the lord of the gods, making use of Devamaya, usurped the power of Jayanta for freely moving to the heaven as well the nectar. At that point of time, feeling painful, Indula properly adored the goddess Sarada and then he started dhyana-yoga. Speaking this, I am now telling you another story. The valorous Netrapala, grieving for his son, distributed ten crores of gold coins equally among the rest of the sons. Thereafter, the strong army of two lakhs of soldiers of the rest of the sons departed towards their abodes.

## Chapter 133. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.133.1-9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*yadā te cīnadeśasthāstadāhūto nṛpeṇa vai \|*  
*kāmapālena bho vipra lakṣaṇo nakulāṃśakaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*jayacaṃdra mahābhāga sāvadhānaṃ vacaḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*vaiśākhaśukla saptamyāṃ muhūrto'yaṃ dināgame \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ato vai lakṣaṇo vīraścaikākī māṃ samāpnuyāt \|*  
*gṛhītvā matsutāṃ dolāṃ gamiṣyati tavāṃtikam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*senānvitaṃ ca taṃ jñātvā mahīrājo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*grahīṣyati parājitya tasmādyogyaṃ vaco mama \|\| 4 \|\|*

*iti tatratyavacanaṃ matvā rājā prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ hastinīsaṃsthaṃ śataśūrasamanvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*āhūya preṣayāmāsa kāmapālāya dhīmate \|*  
*mārge paṃcadinaṃ vīra uṣitvā tadgṛhaṃ yayau \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tadā padmākaraḥ śyālo jñātvā lakṣaṇamāgatam \|*  
*bhūmirājaṃ samāhūya tena yuddhamacīkarat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇo nakulāṃśaśca dṛṣṭvā śatrumupasthitam \|*  
*svaśaraistarpayāmāsa rājarājaṃ mahābalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*mūrcchayitvā mahīrājaṃ hatvā paṃcaśataṃ balī \|*  
*kāmapālaṃ samāgamya natvā vāsamakārayat \|\| 9 \|\|*

1-9. Suta said- At the time when Udayasimha and other great warriors had gone to China, at that point of time, the king Kamapаla invited Laksana who had been bom of the amsa of Nakula. He wrote in the letter of invitation - “O excellent one, О Jayacandra, you listen to my words quite carefully. On the bright seventh day of the month of Vaisakha, the auspicious time for the ceremony of taking the bride to her husband’s house after marriage has been fixed. Therefore, the valorous Laksana should kindly arrive here at my place alone. Thereafter, he can return to his abode with my daughter. Because in case you come with your soldiers, Prthviraja would come to know about your arrival and defeating you, would abduct the bride with the palanquin. Therefore, my proposal seems to be the best. Hearing this, the king Jayacandra delightfully made Laksana to mount over a cow elephant and sent him to the monarch Kamapala, accompanied with a hundred warriors. The journey was covered in five days, after which he reached the place of king Kamapala. At the same time, the brother-in-law Padmakara came to know of the arrival of Laksana and he immediately invited Prthviraja and started a war with Laksana - the amsa of Nakula. Finding his avowed enemy, Prthviraja started shooting arrows there. As a result of this, Prthviraja was fainted and five hundred of his soldiers were killed, after which Laksana went to the king Kamapaala and offered his salutation to him. Thereafter, the king lodged Laksana in his own place.

## \|\| 2.133.10-15 \|\|

*utthitaśca mahīrājo gatvā padmākaraṃ prati \|*  
*vacanaṃ prāha kāryārthī śṛṇu mitra vaco mama \|\| 10 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇo me mahāñchatrussa ca tvadgehamāgataḥ \|*  
*yadi dāsyasi taṃ baddhvā tvāṃ madaṃgaṃ karomyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa lobhātmā dattvā hālāhalaṃ viṣam \|*  
*baddhvā taṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vīraṃ mahīrājāya cārpayat \|*  
*hatvā tāñchataśūrāṃśca guptavārtāmakārayan \|\| 12 \|\|*

*jñātvā tatpadminī nārī duḥkhitālapya vai bhṛśam \|*  
*caṃḍikāṃ pūjayāmāsa patimaṃgalahetave \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tadā prasannā sā devī varadā sarvamaṃgalā \|*  
*āśvāsya padminīṃ nārīṃ lakṣaṇāṃtamupāyayau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*svapne tamāha sā devī hrīṃ phaṭ gheghe japaṃ kuru \|*  
*asya maṃtraprabhāvācca sarvavighnaḥ praṇaśyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

10-15. After regaining consciousness, the king Prthviraja, who had been quite active, went to the place of Padmakara and said to him- “O dear, you please listen to my words. Laksana happens to be my enemy, who is presently lodged in your house. In case you put him in bondage and give him to me, then I shall declare you as my representative. Padmakara, who was filled with greed by this allurement, administered the terrific poison to Laksana. When Laksana got fainted with the effect of poison, he was bound in chains and then handed over to Prthviraja. Prthviraja on his part killed a hundred warriors who had accompanied Laksana, who was then lodged in a secret chamber. When the queen Padmini came to know of this secret, she felt extremely painful and started lamenting. Thereafter, she adored the goddess Candika for the welfare of her husband. At that point of time, the goddess Sarvamangala getting pleased, assured PadminT, who moved towards Laksana. On reaching there, the goddess said to her in the dream- “You recite the mantra- “hrm phat gheghe”. With the reciting of this mantra, all your obstructions would be removed.

## \|\| 2.133.16-30 \|\|

*sa buddhvā lakṣaṇo vīrastaṃ maṃtraṃ ca jajāpa ha \|*  
*āṣāḍhe māsi saṃprāpte kṛṣṇāṃśādyā gṛhaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tālanaśca yutastābhyāṃ kalyakubjamupāyayau \|*  
*na dṛṣṭo lakṣaṇo vīro jayacaṃdrapriyaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*jñātvā tatkāraṇaṃ taiśca kṛtaṃ yogamayaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhānyapālaḥ kāṃsyadhārī vīṇādhārī ca tālanaḥ \|*  
*lallasiṃho mṛdaṃgāṃko yayuste vai mahāvatīm \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sabhāṃ parimalasyaiva gatvā te yogarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*cakrurgānaṃ mudā yuktāḥ sarve te mohamāgatāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*prasannaśca tadā rājā muktāmālāṃ svakaṇṭhagām \|*  
*tālanāya dadau prītyā tābhyāṃ svarṇāṃgulīyake \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tadā te harṣitāḥ sarve kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ prati cāyayuḥ \|*  
*jñātvā kṛṣṇāṃśa evāpi dhṛtvā yogamayaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*yayau biṃdugaḍhaṃ vīrastālanādyaissamanvitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*haṭṭamadhye samāgamya kṛtvā rāsotsavaṃ śubham \|*  
*gehaṃ padmākarasyaiva gatvā te nanṛturmudā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare sarvā yoṣitastatra cāgatāḥ \|*  
*veṇuvādyavṛtaṃvīraṃ kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ dadṛśurmuhuḥ \|*  
*mohitāstasya gānena jaḍībhūtā dhanaṃ daduḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tadā tu padminī nārī sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutā \|*  
*jñātvā kṛṣṇāṃśamevāpi ruroda ciramāturā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*uvāca ca vilapyāśu matpatirla kṣaṇo balī \|*  
*mahīrājena śūreṇa kārāgāre balātkṛtaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ yoṣā bhavānyogī kathaṃ kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu sa nṛpo bhujamutthāpya satvaram \|*  
*āśvāsya padminīṃ nārīṃ yayuste dehalīṃ prati \|*  
*rājadvāramupāgamya kṛṣṇāṃśassa nanarta ha \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahīrājastu balavānprasannastasyalīlayā \|*  
*vāṃchitaṃ brūhi kṛṣṇāṃśa sarvaṃ yogindadāmyaham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā bhūpavaco vihasyovāca taṃ prati \|*  
*kārāgāraṃ lohamayaṃ nṛpayogyaṃ ca me nṛpa \|*  
*darśayāśu svakīyaṃ vai bhavānbhūpaśiromaṇiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa nṛpatirmohitaḥ kṛṣṇalīlayā \|*  
*darśayitvā ca vai śīpraṃ punastebhyo dadau dhanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tataste yoginassarve saṃprāpya ca mahāvatīm \|*  
*natvā parimalaṃ bhūpaṃ gaditvā sarvakāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

16-30. On regaining consciousness, Laksana too recited the same mantra. At the beginning of the month of Asadha, Udayasimha and other warriors returned to their respective abodes. Talana with Udayasimha proceeded on to Kannauja, where Jayacandra found his beloved nephew Laksana absent. Then he found out the reason for the same. Thereafter, all of them took to the form of yogins in which Dhanyapala played on cymbals, Talana played on a vina, while Lallanasimha played on the double drums. All of them reached the court of the king of Mahavati, where they started dancing and playing on music. Observing the dance and music, all the courtiers felt impressed. The king on his part, removing the garland of beads, gave it to Talana and the other two were given the gold rings. Getting pleased with that honour, they reached before Udayasimha. Finding people to be extremely efficient, the valorous Udayasimha proceeded to Bindugadha, disguised as ascetics with Talana and others. Reaching there, they first of all displayed Rasalila dance in the market place of the city. Thereafter, they went to the house of Padmakara and danced there with delight. At the same time, all the ladies also reached there, who were attracted towards Udayasimha playing on flute. Observing their dance and music, the ladies were immensely impressed and stood there like images. Then the queen PadminI recognized Udayasimha, who was playing on flute. Having thus resolved in her mind, she while sobbing, uttered these pathetic words- “The valorous Laksana happens to be my husband, who has been imprisoned by Prthviraja with the use of his force. I am a lady and you are a yogi Therefore, I feel worried that how could he be freed?” On hearing these words, Udayasimha raised both his hands and assured the queen Padmavati. Thereafter, he departed for Dehali. Reaching there, he danced in the king’s court. The king Prthviraja was highly impressed with the dance and he said to him- “O yogi, you tell me whatever is needed by you? I am prepared to give you everything.” On hearing these words of the king, Udayasimha spoke smilingly- “O king, for keeping the enemy kings, there is an iron prison with you. You are the king of kings. This is what has been heard by me. I desire to have a look at it.” On hearing these words, the king who had been highly impressed with the performance of Udayasimha, showed the place to him and also gave him enough of money. Thereafter, all the yogins returned to Mahavati. Reaching there, they narrated the entire story to the king Parimala.

## \|\| 2.133.31-40 \|\|

*svasenāṃ sajjayāmāsa cāhlādaśca nṛpājñayā \|*  
*pañcalakṣaṃ mahāvatyā hayārūḍhāssamāsthitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tālanassapta lakṣāṇi sainyānyāhūya cāgataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dvādaśalakṣāṇi kṣatriyā raṇadurmadāḥ \|*  
*dehalīṃ ca samājagmussarvaśastrasamanvitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare mantrī cadrabhaṭṭo viśāradaḥ \|*  
*sarvaśāstrārthakuśalo vaiṣṇavīśaktipūjakaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mahīrājaṃ samāgamya vacaḥ prāha śṛṇuṣva bhoḥ \|*  
*mayā vai ca rahaḥ krīḍā dṛṣṭā devīprasādataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tatrodayaśca kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ pūrṇabrahmāṇamāgamat \|*  
*vacaḥ prāha prasannātmā śṛṇu tvaṃ sattvavigraha \|\| 35 \|\|*

*agnivaṃśavināśāya cādya yāsyāmi dehalīm \|*  
*hatvāhaṃ kauravāṃśāṃśca sthāpayitvā kaliṃ bhuvi \|\| 36 \|\|*

*punastavāntikaṃ prāpya rahaḥ krīḍāṃ karomyaham \|*  
*ityuktvā biṃdulārūḍhaḥ sa vīrastvāmupa sthitaḥ \|*  
*ityahaṃ dṛṣṭavānbhūpa kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ yoganidrayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sa bhūpo vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*bhayabhītaḥ sahasrāṇi śūrānāhūya satvaram \|*  
*tebhyaśca lakṣaṇaṃ dattvā vacanaṃ prāha tānprati \|\| 38 \|\|*

*padmākarāya bhūpāya gatvā dattvāśu lakṣaṇam \|*  
*mamāntikamupāgamya kāraṇaṃ vadatāśu tat \|\| 39 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu te sarve vahnivaṃśyā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*gatvā tatra tathā kṛtvā mahīrājamupāgaman \|\| 40 \|\|*

31-40. At the command of the king, Ahlada ordered his army stationed at Mahavati to march on, which was five lakhs in number and always remained there. Similarly, with seven lakhs of his soldiers, Talana too joined him. Thus a total anny of twelve lakhs of soldiers comprising of the terrified ksatriyas marched towards Indraprastha. In the meantime, Candrabhatta - an excellent courtier, who was well-versed in all the Sastras and was devoted to the Vaisnava Sakti, reached before the king Prthviraja and said to him- “In order to please the goddess, I have displayed the lonely sport, in which Udayasimha - the amsa of Krsna appeared as Brahman. Feeling pleased, he said to me- “O Jiva with human body, in order to totally kill the Ksatriyas of Agnivamsa, I am proceeding to Dehali. Completely destroying the Ksatriyas born of the Kaurava race, I shall establish the age of Kali on this earth. Then I shall again reach before you and sport lonely.” Thus speaking, the valorous person mounted over the horse named Bindula and started from that place to reach here. О king, I had learnt all about these facts through the goddess Yoganidra from Udayasimha, who belongs to the amsa of Sri Krsna. On hearing this, even Prthviraja felt extremely surprised. Getting frightened, he summoned a thousand warriors and entrusted the care of Laksana to them, saying- “You take him and hand him over to Padmakara. Thereafter, you convey the entire situation of the place to me.” On hearing these words, the Ksatriyas of the Agnivamsa went there and after doing the job, returned to Prthviraja and said to him.

## \|\| 2.133.41-56 \|\|

*bhagadaṃtaśca teṣāṃ tu sahasrāṇāṃ ca nāyakaḥ \|*  
*mahīrājaṃ vacaḥ prāha śṛṇu tannṛpabhāṣitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*padminī me svasā rājan guptavidyāviśāradā \|*  
*tayā yajñapatirdevaḥ samyagārādhitaḥ purā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dattastena varo ramyo hyantardhānamayaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*sā tu taṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kāṃtamaṃtardhānaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa nṛpatiḥ paramānandamāptavān \|\| 43 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare prāptāḥ kṛṣṇāṃśādyā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*rurudhurdehalīṃ sarvāṃ mahīrājena pālitām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sa tadā pṛthivīrājo gṛhītvā bahubhūṣaṇam \|*  
*sarvebhyaśca dadau premṇā vacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇo nāma te rājā kārāgāre na vai mama \|*  
*yadi mannagare cāsti tarhi te roṣa īdṛśaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ityuktvā taṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ darśayāmāsa vai gṛham \|*  
*mahādevasya śapathaṃ kṛtavānbhūpatirbhayāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tadodayo bhūpavacaḥ satyaṃ matvā suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*svakīyaiḥ saha saṃprāpto grāmaṃ biṃdugaḍhaṃ śubham \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kāmapālastu tacchrutvā kṛṣṇāṃśāgamanaṃ balī \|*  
*baliṃ bahuṃ gṛhītvāśu kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau \|*  
*prāṃjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā vacanaṃ prāha bhīrukaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*sutā me padminī nārī lakṣaṇena samanvitā \|*  
*na jñātvā kva gatā'smābhissatyaṃ satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|\| 50 \|\|*

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ svabalaissaha \|*  
*kānyakubjaṃ samāgatya jayacandramuvāca ha \|\| 51 \|\|*

*bhrātṛjastava bhūpāla padminyā lakṣaṇo'nvitaḥ \|*  
*kāmapālagṛhe nāsti niścito bahudhā mayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*na jāne kva gato rājā mama prāṇasamo bhuvi \|*  
*yadi bhūpa na paśyāmi satyaṃ prāṇāṃstyajāmyaham \|\| 53 \|\|*

*hā ratnabhānutanaya viṣṇubhakta śubhaṃkara \|*  
*svamitraṃ māṃ parityajya kāṃ diśaṃ gatavānbhavān \|*  
*ityuktvā mūrchitaścāsītkṛṣṇāṃśo vaiṣṇavapriyaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tadā svarṇavatī devī svadāsyā śobhayā saha \|*  
*dhṛtvā śukamayaṃ rūpaṃ tatrāgatya svamūrtigā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tayā saṃpreṣitā śobhā mlecchamāyāviśāradā \|*  
*jayacaṃdramupāgamya dhṛtvā divyamayaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

41-56. Bhagadanta, who had been the leader of the thousand strong Ksatriyas, said to Prthviraja- “Whatever the king of the place has told us, is being repeated before you. You kindly listen to the same with utmost attention. He has said- “O king, my sister Padmini who is quite proficient in the secret lore, had in earlier times, worshipped the lord of the yajnas very well. From him, she has learnt to disappear from sight, as a boon. Because of that she would conceal Laksana - her husband.” On hearing this, Prthviraja was immensely delighted. In the mean time, the extremely powerful Udayasimha, with other of his great warriors, surrounded Dehali - the capital city of Prthviraja. At that point of time, Prthviraja approached those people and offering ornaments as gifts, lovingly told them with humility- “The king Laksana is not lodged in my prison. Had he been in my city, then he would have displayed his anger here.” Thus speaking, Prthviraja showed Udayasimha the prison (in which he could have been imprisoned.) Thereafter, getting frightened, Prthviraja took oath of Siva. At that point of time, considering the words of Prthviraja to be true, feeling painful at heart Udayasimha departed for Bindugadha with his soldiers. On their arrival there, the king Kamapala offered many presents to them and with folded hands, said to them- “Where has my daughter Padmini gone with Laksana? We are not aware or the same. I am speaking the total truth.” Hearing these words, Udayasimha with all his warriors, went to Kanyakubja and said to the king Jayacandra- “Your nephew Laksana along with Padmini could not be found in the house of Kamapala. I have confirmed it through various sources. My king, who was like my life, I do not know where he has disappeared on earth. О king, in case I do not find him, I shall surely end my life. О son of Ratnabhanu, you are the great devotee of lord Visnu, where have you gone leaving a friend like me.” Thus speaking, Udayasimha, who had been a devotee of Visnu, fainted. At that point of time, the goddess with her slave girl Sobha arrived there in the form of parrots. Svarnavati then sent the Mleccha girl Sobha to the king Jayacandra.

## \|\| 2.133.57-66 \|\|

*uvāca vacanaṃ tatra śṛṇu bhūpaśiromaṇe \|*  
*māyāvinī ca māṃ viddhi śobhanāṃ nāma viśrutām \|\| 57 \|\|*

*daṃpatī tava bhūpāla saṃhṛtau yena yatra vai \|*  
*tatrāhaṃ ca gamiṣyāmi mahāmadasamanvitā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*āhlādaścendulo vīro devo vai tālano balī \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśapālitāssarve yāsyāmo bhūpate vayam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*ityuktvā śobhanā veśyā kṛtvā yogamayaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*mahāmadaṃ samāruhya paiśācaṃ rudrakiṃkaram \|*  
*prayayau tānpuraskṛtya yogiveṣānmahāba lān \|\| 60 \|\|*

*āhlādo gajasaṃstho vai karālārūḍha indulaḥ \|*  
*tālanaḥ siṃhinīsaṃstho devasiṃho manorathe \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśo bindulārūḍho nartayāmāsa taṃ hayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*kāmarūpamayaṃ deśaṃ śatayojanagāminaḥ \|*  
*balavaṃtaśca saṃprāptā gehegehe janejane \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ śodhayāmāsurna prāptāstatra taṃ nṛpam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*punarmayūranagaraṃ śobhanā taiḥ samanvitā \|*  
*cinvatī taṃ manuṣyeṣu na prāptā tatra vai nṛpam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*punarinnagaḍhagrāmaṃ śobhanā ca janejane \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ mṛgayāmāsa na prāpa tatra lakṣaṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*gatvā bāhlīkanagaraṃ śobhanā taissamanvitā \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ ca nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ nāpaśyattatra duḥkhitā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*punaḥ svadeśamāgamya bāhlīkaṃ mlecchavāsinam \|*  
*markaṭeśvaramīśānaṃ tatrāha vanavāsinam \|*  
*pūjayitvā ca sā veśyā gānanṛtyaparābhavat \|\| 66 \|\|*

57-66. Taking to a divine form, she reached before Jayacandra and said to him- “O foremost of the rulers, you kindly listen to my words. I am a well known woman, who has mastery in illusion. I am going with Mahamada to the person who has kidnapped your son as well as the bride. I, Ahlada, Indula, Devasimha, valorous Talana and Udayasimha will go there with their armies.” Thus speaking, taking to a yogic body, she mounted over Mahamada - the attendant of Siva and making the valorous warriors disguised as yogins, departed from that place. In that journey, Ahlada mounted over an elephant, Indula mounted over the horse named Karala, Talana was mounted over the mare known by the name of Simhini, Devasimha was over his horse named Manoratha, while Udayasimha was mounted over his horse named Bindula, making it to dance while galloping. Starting from that place (Kannauja), they undertook the journey of a hundred yojanas and reached the country of Kamarupa. Reaching there, all of them enquired about Laksana from all the people there, but they could not find him there. Then Sobhana asked about Laksana from every person there and reached the city of Mayura town. She also could not find him there. In this way, the illusory woman called Sobhana went to Innagadha and Bahlika cities and searched the houses of all the people there, but Laksana could not be found. Again she returned to the city of Bahllka and worshipped lord Siva of the desert region, known by the name of Markatesvara Mahadeva. They danced before the lord there.

## \|\| 2.133.67-82 \|\|

*sa devo bhūmimadhyāt samāgamya mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ praṇato bhūtvā'bravīnmlecchaprapūjitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*ahaṃ kālāgnirudreṇa bhūmigarte suropitaḥ \|*  
*asamarthaṃ ca māṃ viddhi gaccha vīra yathāsukham \|\| 68 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā ca sā śobhā nirāśābhūttadā svayam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*punaḥ svarṇavatīṃ prāpya sarvamevā dito'bravīt \|*  
*triṃśadabdaiśca kṛṣṇāṃśe caitraśukla samāgate \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tānāśvāsya suvarṇāṃgī pūjayāmāsa caṃḍikām \|*  
*navarātraṃ gataṃ tasyā bhojanācchādanaṃ vinā \|*  
*niśīthānte tamaḥprāpte gatvāha jagadambikā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*padminī nāma yā nārī maṇidevasya vai priyā \|*  
*jātā sā kāmapālasya gṛhe yajñāvamānitā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*senāpatiḥ kuberasya maṇidevo hi sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pūrvaṃ hi bhīmasenena yakṣayuddheṣu ghātitaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tadā tatpadminī nārī devadevamumāpatim \|*  
*tuṣṭāva ca nirāhārā matpatiṃ dehi śaṃkara \|\| 74 \|\|*

*śatavarṣāṃtare devo mahādeva uvāca tām \|*  
*kalau vikramakāle hi śatadvādaśake'ntike \|\| 75 \|\|*

*nakulāṃśaṃ ca saṃprāpya bhuktvā tena mahatsukham \|*  
*tadviyogena saṃtyajya dehaṃ padmānuvāsitam \|*  
*svapatiṃ ca tadā prāpya kailāsaṃ punareṣyasi \|\| 76 \|\|*

*mahāvatīṃ purīṃ ramyāṃ rāṣṭrapālāya śāradā \|*  
*kariṣyati tadā devī maṇidevastu tvatpatiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tayā viracito bhūmau grāmarakṣārthamudyataḥ \|*  
*prāptastvāṃ padminīṃ nārīṃ kailāsaṃ punareṣyati \|\| 78 \|\|*

*ataḥ svarṇavati tvaṃ vai kailāsaṃ guhyakālayam \|*  
*gatvāśu padminīṃ tatra bodhayāśu vacaḥ kuru \|\| 79 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā svarṇavatī padminīṃ prati cāgamat \|*  
*vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayitvāgre padminīṃ tu dayāturā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*kāmapālagṛhaṃ prāpya tatra vāsamakārayat \|*  
*svarṇavatyapi saṃprāptā tadā śīghraṃ mahāvatīm \|\| 81 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ gatāyāṃ gehe vai padminyā likhitaṃ śubham \|*  
*patraṃ parimalo rājā vartayāmāsa harṣitaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

67-82. Thereafter, the lord, who was adored by the Mlecchas, came out of the earth and said to Udayasimha meekly- “O valorous one, Kalagni Rudra has lodged in this pit. Therefore, I am unable to bestow success on you. Do not take useless trouble here.” Hearing these words, Sobhana getting disappointed, returned again to Svarnavati and narrated to him the entire story. When Udayasimha was passing the thirtieth year of his life, on the occasion of the Navaratras of the month of Caitra, the goddess with golden face assured her devotees variously. Thereafter, they started worshipping Candika appropriately. Then on the last dark night, at the dead of night, the goddess Bhagavati said to Svarnavati- “The lady named Padmini, who is being searched by you with Laksana, is the beloved of Yaksa Manideva. Having been insulted in a yajna, she was born in the house of Kamapala. The said Manideva is the commander of the army of Kubera, who had been killed by Bhimasena, defeating him in the battleground. At that point of time, Padmini, fasting without food, prayed again and again to Siva - the lord of Uma. She said-“O lord, give me back my husband.” After her performing tapas for a hundred years, lord Mahadeva said- “During the age of Kali, at the end of the twelfth century of the Vikrama era, you will enjoy the company of Laksana - the amsa of Nakula, as your husband. Then enjoying all the pleasures with him, on separation from him, you having the fragrant body, would reach Kailasa with your husband. Building the beautiful city of Mahavati for Rastrapala, the goddess Sarada would bestow Manideva as your husband. Having been born on earth by the grace of the goddess, he would be deputed as a king for the protection of a village. Then he would get you as his wife known as Padmini, and shall again move to Kailasa. Therefore, О goddess Svarnavati, you accept my words. You take on journey to Kailasa - the place of the Yaksas and enlighten Padmini of all these facts. Listening to all these words, Sarvangi reached there and narrated all the facts to her. Having been influenced with these words, Padmini agreed to stay in the house of Kamapala. At that point of time, the queen Sona reaching Mahavati, handed over the letter written by Padmini to the king Parimala, in which she had expressed all, including her stay with her father.

## \|\| 2.133.83-93 \|\|

*āgaccha senayā sārddhaṃ kṛṣṇāṃśa balavattara \|*  
*jitvā padmākaraṃ baṃdhuṃ matpatiṃ mocayāśu vai \|*  
*bhūtale lakṣaṇo rājā sthitaḥ padmākarārtigaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*iti jñātvā ca kṛṣṇāṃśo lakṣadvādaśasenayā \|*  
*rurodha nagarīṃ sarvāṃ kāmapālena rakṣitām \|\| 84 \|\|*

*kāmapālastu balavāṃstrilakṣabalasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sutājñayā yayau yuddhaṃ sārddhaṃ padmākareṇa vai \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tayoścāsīnmahadyuddhaṃ senayorubhayostadā \|*  
*ahorātrapramāṇena bhūpasenā parājitā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*padminīṃ śaraṇaṃ prāpya tadā bhrātā pitā sthitaḥ \|*

*divyadṛṣṭistato jātaḥ saṃprāpya tamayudhyata \|*

*baddhvā tatra mudāviṣṭo lakṣaṇaṃ prāpya nirbhayaḥ \|*

*jayacaṃdro'pi balavāndṛṣṭvā gehe svadaṃpatī \|*

*jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe kṛṣṇāṃśo gehamāgataḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

83-93. It was also mentioned therein that the valorous Udayasimha should arrive with his army and defeat her brother Padmakara and get her husband freed. The king Laksana was alive on earth, but was being tortured by her brother. Knowing about this, Udayasimha leading his army of twelve lakhs of soldiers, reached there and surrounded the capital city of the king Kamapala. At the command of all other sons, the king Kamapala reached the battleground with three lakhs of his army soldiers and started the war. The terrific war was fought by both the armies which went on uninterrupted. When the army of Kamapala was defeated, Kamapala with his sons went to Padmini and begged for victory. For the victory of her father and brothers, she handed over die secret letter to them. At that point of time, both of them hiding themselves, killed ten thousand enemy warriors. Observing this, Talana and other warriors were immensely surprised. As a result of this, deserting the battleground, they reached before Udayasimha to take refuge with him. Hearing them and feeling painful, Udayasimha adored the omnipresent Parvati to attain the divine sight, as a result of which he while remaining in the sky, spotted both of them who were engaged in war. Thereafter, he becoming fearless, captured them both and reached before Laksana. Then placing Padmini in a palanquin, they departed for their home. Reaching there, they handed over the couple Laksana and Padmini to the king Jayacandra and felt themselves immensely successful. The king Jayacandra finding the presence of his son and the bride in the house, felt overjoyed and distributed riches to the Brahmanas. He also freed many of the rulers from the prison. Thus, at the start of the month of Jyestha, Udayasimha returned to his place.

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra kṛṣṇāṃśacaritaṃ śubham \|*  
*punaste kathayiṣyāmi dṛṣṭaṃ yogabalena vai \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Brahmanas, I have spoken about the life story of Udayasimha. Now, whatever has been witnessed by me about him due to the yogic practices, I am trying to repeat the same.”

## Chapter 134. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-6. Suta said- О excellent Brahmanas, you listen to what I say. Once when the king Prthviraja was seated over his lion throne, Candrabhatta arrived in his court. On his arrival, the king feeling worried, said to him-“O best of the courtiers, you listen to my words. My entire city is feeling panicky because of the great warriors like Udayasimha. Therefore, when are these enemies of mine going to be killed?” At these words spoken by the king, Bhatta - the auspicious soul of Siva spoke- “O foremost of the rulers, kindly listen attentively to whatever is going to be spoken by me. Brahmananda - the dweller of the city of Mahavati has been born of the amsa of Visnu, who is always victorious. Udayasimha is the amsa of Sri Krsna and happens to be his initiate friend. He always acts in a way which is liked by his friend. Therefore, Brahmananda - the son of Malana, whenever shall move out of this place, then in an unattached manner and at the same time all those people who have been bom of the amsas of the gods, would also leave this place.

7-15. Mahipati then spoke to other courtier who spoke the above words as well as to the king in a humble voice- “I have well thought of a remedy and have decided that the valorous Brahmananda - the best of the king, should be invited alone on the pretext of his taking home the bride and then he should be killed in a deceitful manner, so that you can be successful.” When Mahipati thus spoke, the king getting pleased, said- “O friend, you listen to my words. You at once go to Mahavati, meet the queen Malang there and talk to her in a convincing manner. Thereafter, you return and inform me accordingly by which you could be able to lead a comfortable life for long.” О best of the sages, on hearing this, Mahipati offered his salutation to the king and started for the journey. In the deep darkness, during the dead of night, he met the queen Malana and fearlessly said to her- “Your bride known by the name of Vela has attained beauty and youthfulness, because of which the auspicious damsel has become suitable for her husband. But Prthviraja has heard that Udayasimha was bom in a low caste. Because of that, he does not consider it appropriate to send his daughter to your son. Therefore, you should become ready to act as I want you to do, because it is for your benefit. Your valorous son Brahmananda should proceed with me alone to Urvi - my capital city and go with my army.

16-29. By so doing, he would be able to bring his wife here. There is no doubt about it. Otherwise, disowning her husband, Vela would end her life.” Hearing these words and influenced with devamaya (divine-illusion), the queen went to her husband and narrated the entire situation to him. On hearing this, the king said- “Mahipati is an extremely wicked person. He is always engaged in the efforts for our destruction. Therefore, his proposal does not appeal me at all, because he is playing a trick.” On hearing this, the queen Malana spoke in anger—“As are the brothers, so am I. You take his words as my words and kindly accept the same. The king perforce entrusted the care of Brahmananda to Mahipati. Brahmananda also honouring the command of her mother, accompanied with his maternal uncle, reached the city of Urvi. Thereafter, early in the morning, mounting over his horse Harinagara and under the influence of devamaya, he started for Delhi alone. At the evening time, he reached the palace and met the queen Agama possessing the divine body. Agama also felt delighted on meeting him. Thereafter, on the bright eighth day of the month of Magha, the fearless Brahmananda met all the seven queens of his seven brothers-in-law. Out of them, three were widows and four had their husbands alive. The widows, getting delighted with the arrival of Brahmananda, started narrating their respective tales of sufferings. They said- “O virtuous Brahmananda, you kindly listen to my words with a firm mind. Your wife Vela, who is dark-complexioned and an image of quarrelsomeness, got our husbands killed and made our lives miserable. Therefore, О attraction of our minds, we pray to you with folded hands that you become husband of the woman, who have no husbands, because you are most suitable for us.” On hearing these words, the valorous Brahmananda spoke sweet and appropriate words- “Earlier in Satyayuga, the ladies had been quite chaste and devoted to their husbands. During Tretayuga, they were mediocre types, degraded during Dvapara-yuga and of lowest type in the age of Kali, who enjoyed the company of the other people. Therefore, in their treatises, Devala and Asita have supported the marriage of widows during the age of Kali.

30-41. These Rsis were of the opinion that in Satya-yuga, the women led a chaste life. During Treta-yuga, they burnt themselves with their husbands. During Dvapara-yuga, leading a chaste life they observed Brahmacarya's last line. But in the age of Kali, there is no provision for performing the Sati-vrata. Therefore, all of you keeping contact with me, enjoy the best of pleasure. Listening to his words, they decorated themselves wearing all the ornaments. Then they reached before Brahmananda and desired to embrace him. At this, Brahmananda - the son of Malana spoke fearlessly- “Your husbands have made use of you, who were killed by our brothers in the battlefield. Therefore, I cannot own you. This is the total truth which is being spoken by me.” On hearing such harsh words, those women said to the king, while crying-‘The wicked husband of Vela is forcing us to fall from dharma, therefore this wicked person should be punished by you, otherwise we people are ready to lay down our lives.” On hearing the words of the ladies, Brahmananda was summoned by the ruler who told him-“You appear to have been born in the race of the low castes, because the one who enjoys the wives of others, he has to proceed to the abode of Yama. Therefore, О husband of my daughter, I atonce imprison you.” On hearing these harsh words, Brahmananda rushed towards taking out the sword form the sheath. But getting frightened, the king rushed towards Camunda and closed the door tightly, which served him as a prison.

43-53. Suta said- О best of the sages, there was a king named Mayavarma in Angadesa. He worshipped Tamasi-sakti which could influence all, as a result of which an excellent kavaca was procured by him, which could frighten all. Receving that kavaca, the king wandered on earth. Thereafter, his queen named Pramada produced ten sons after a gap of one year each and they were from the amsas of Kauravas. О excellent one, they were known by the names of Matta, Pramatta, Unmatta, Sumatta, Durmada, Durmukha, Bahu, Suratha and Viratha. Thereafter, a sister was also born, who came to be known by the name of Madireksana. A daitya named Kitava felt attracted at the beauty of that girl. Thereafter, he went to Mayavarma and prayed to him quite meekly- “In case you give away your daughter to a passionate person like me, then I shall perform all your jobs. There is no doubt about it.” On hearing this, the king entrusted her daughter to the daitya. Thereafter, the lustful daitya - the dweller of the caves, becoming lustful, started coming in the king’s palace during the darkness of night and - joyed the company of the girl. In the early morning, he used to retire to his cave. In this way, the time passed on. Then the king gave a lakh of gold coins to his priest and the son Taraka was selected for the girl. The valorous one, together with sixteen lakhs of his army besides a hundred rulers, travelling for a month, informed the king of their arrival. At that point of time, Udayasimha was fifteen years of age. On the occasion of the marriage of Taraka, a large number of rulers assembled there.

*kitavo nāma medhāvī daityavaṃśayaśaskaraḥ \|*  
*tena me pīḍitā bālā rātrau ghoratamovṛte \|\| 55 \|\|*

*bhakṣitāstena daityena saṃyayuste yamālayam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ ca bahudhā dravyaṃ luṃṭhayitvā madāturaḥ \|*  
*matsutāyai dadau sarvaṃ tasmāttvaṃ ditijaṃ jahi \|\| 57 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā mahīrājassarvasainyasamanvitaḥ \|*

*kitavassa tu māyāvī jitvā sarvānmahābalān \|*

*tārakaśca tadā duḥkhī dhyātvā śaṃkaramuttamam \|*  
*pāṣāṇabhūto hyagamanmahādevaprasādataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

54-60. At that point of time, Mayavarma spoke to the king who was in the company of Taraka-“O valorous king of kings, you kindly listen to my humble request. There is a valorous and intelligent daitya named Kitava, who trouble my daughter in the dark nights. Many princes had arrived for marrying that girl, but this daitya killed them and ate them up sending them to the abode of Yama. He plundered all the riches of those princes and gave them to my daughter. I therefore request you to kindly kill that daitya” On hearing these words, with his entire army, he reached the battleground called for Kitava and fought a terrific battle with him. Thereafter, defeating all the warriors, the illusory daitya abducted Taraka and carried him to his cave. At that point of time, Taraka feeling miserable, meditated for lord Siva who getting pleased with him, turned him into the image of stone.

## \|\| 2.134.61-70 \|\|

*tārakaḥ kitavenaiva saṃhṛto ditijena vai \|*  
*yadi tvaṃ me sutaṃ dehi koṭisvarṇaṃ dadāmi tat \|\| 63 \|\|*

*ahorātramabhūdyuddhaṃ teṣāṃ tena samanvitam \|*  
*kitavastu ruṣāviṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ devasiṃhakam \|*  
*balakhāniṃ mohayitvā jagarja ca punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*sukhakhānistadā śūraḥ kitavaṃ balavattaram \|*  
*svakhaḍgena śirastasya chittvā rājānamāgamat \|\| 66 \|\|*

*trayaste sukhino bhūtvā sukhakhāniṃ praśasya ca \|*  
*mahīrājāya ca dadau tārakaṃ kaitavaṃ śiraḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tadā bhūpasutā devī sukhakhāniṃ samāvṛṇot \|*  
*mahīpatistadāgatya tatsutāṃ madirekṣaṇām \|\| 68 \|\|*

*saṃbodhya vividhairvākyairbhūmirājāṃtamāgamat \|*  
*tārakasya tayā sārddhaṃ vivāho mudito'bhavat \|\| 69 \|\|*

*koṭisvarṇaṃ nṛpātprāpya balakhānirmahābalaḥ \|*  
*prayayau baṃdhubhissārddhaṃ śirīṣākhyapuraṃ śubham \|\| 70 \|\|*

61-70. In the mean time, the Ksatriyas of Mahavati reached there. They were ten thousand in number and were led by Udayasimha and other warriors. On seeing them, Mahiraja, who was overpowered with the grief of his son, said to Balakhana-“Taraka has been abducted by Kitava - the son of Diti. In case you bring back my son, then I shall give you a crore of gold coins.” On hearing this, Udayasimha accompanied by Devasimha, Balakhani and Sukhakhani, forcibly surrounded Kitava from all the sides. All of them fought with the daitya continuously during the days and nights. Thereafter, Kitava getting enraged, made Udayasimha, Devasimha and Balakhana senseless and uttered a lion’s roar. In the mean time, Sukhakhani separated the head of Kitava from his body and produced it before the king. At that point of time, the princess desired Sukhakhani to be her husband. But Mahapati arrived there and advised Madireksana variously and dissuaded her. Then he produced her to the king. Thereafter, she was married to Taraka, while Balakhana received a crores of gold coins, after which he returned to the city of Siri§a with his brother.

## \|\| 2.134.71-77 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*gurjare nṛpatiścāsīnmūlavarmā mahābalaḥ \|*  
*prabhāvatī tasya sutā daśaputrānujābhavat \|\| 71 \|\|*

*balaśca prabalaścaiva subalo balavānbalī \|*  
*sumūlaśca mahābhūlo durgo bhīmo bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*karabho nāma vai yakṣo lallarājasya sevakaḥ \|*  
*prabhāvatīṃ samālokya mumoha madavihvalaḥ \|*  
*pañcavarṣāṃtare jāte tena bhuktā kumārikā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*mūlavarmā mahīrājaṃ samāhūya sasainyakam \|*  
*vacanaṃ prāha namrātmā rājarāja vacaḥ kuru \|\| 74 \|\|*

*prabhāvatīṃ śubhāṃ kanyāṃ nṛharāya dadāmyaham \|*  
*ityuktvā nṛharaṃ putraṃ samāhūya svamaṃdire \|*  
*dadau vedavidhānena sutāṃ ca nṛharāya vai \|\| 75 \|\|*

*pakṣamātrāṃtare yakṣaḥ karabhastatra cāgataḥ \|*  
*daṃpatī pīḍayāmāsa jitvā sarvamahīpatīn \|\| 76 \|\|*

*mahīrājastadā duḥkhī vatsajau balavattarau \|*  
*samāhūya kathitvāgre ruroda balavānbalī \|\| 77 \|\|*

71-77. Suta said- There was a valorous king named Mdlavarma in the region of Gujarata. The name of his younger daughter was Prabhavati, besides ten other sons, who were known by the names of Bala, Prabala, Subala, Balavan, Bali, Sumula, Mahamula, Durga, Bhima and Bhayankara. There was a Yaksa known by the name of Karabha who was an attendant of Lallaraja and was attracted at the sight of Prabhavati. The passionate Yaksa, within five years, started uniting with the princess. When Mulavarma came to know about the same, he called for and prayed him humbly- “O king of kings, I intend to many my daughter Prabhavati with your son Nrhara. Thus speaking, he called his son Nrhara in palace and appropriately performed his marriage with her. After the lapse of a fortnight, the daitya defeated all the rulers and started disturbing newly wedded couple variously. Then feeling miserable, he called for Balakhani and Sukhakhani - the sons of Vatsaraja and expressed his pitiable condition.

## \|\| 2.134.78-80 \|\|

*dayālū vatsajau vīrau karabhāṃtamupeyatuḥ \|*  
*karabhastau samālokya tatraivāṃtardhimāgamat \|*  
*nāgapāśena tau baddhvā pīḍayāmāsa daṃpatī \|\| 78 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ karabhaṃ yakṣakiṃkaram \|*  
*baddhvā yogabalenaiva mocayāmāsa dampatī \|\| 79 \|\|*

*bhrātarau tau samāgamya nāgapāśaṃ tu cāsinā \|*  
*chittvā mumoda balavānkoṭisvarṇaṃ gṛhītavān \|*  
*bhūmirājaḥ prasannātmā dehalīṃ mudito'gamat \|\| 80 \|\|*

78-80. Both the compassionate sons reached before Karabha. But the Yaksa disappeared on seeing both of them and caught them in the bondage of serpents and again started troubling the newly weds. On hearing this, Udayasimha reached before Karabha. He bound him with his yogic powers and relieved the couple from mental and physical agony. Thereafter, he reached before his brother and cut off the serpent bondage with his own sword. Thereafter, receiving a crore of gold coins, all of them returned to their homes delightfully. Then, they started on journey to Dehall with his son and his bride.

## \|\| 2.134.81-90 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kāśmīre ca nṛpaścāsītkaikayo nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*daśa putrāśca tasyaiva kanyā ca madanāvatī \|\| 81 \|\|*

*kāmaḥ prakāmaḥ sakāmo niṣkāmo nirapatrapaḥ \|*  
*jayaśca vijayaścaiva jayanto jayavāñjayaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*sa bhūpo bhūmirājaṃ ca samāhūya vaco'bravīt \|*  
*putraste vai saradano matkanyāṃ prāptumarhati \|\| 83 \|\|*

*gaṃdharvassukalo nāma matkanyāṃ ca śubhānanām \|*  
*jyotsnāyāṃ niśi saṃhṛtya tayā sārdraṃ hi dīvyati \|\| 84 \|\|*

*pūrṇimāyāṃ ca saṃprāptaḥ sa vai citrarathapriyaḥ \|*  
*vaiśākhasyāsite pakṣe cāṣṭamī cādya maṃgalā \|*  
*vadhaṃ kuru nṛpaśreṣṭha dehalīṃ gaṃtumarhasi \|\| 85 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā mahīrājo lakṣasainyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā daṃpatī śīghraṃ dehalīnagaraṃ yayau \|\| 86 \|\|*

*vaiśākhyāṃ sukhajātāyāṃ sukalonāma vīryavān \|*  
*gaṃdharvo daśa sāhasrai rurodha nagaraṃ ruṣā \|\| 87 \|\|*

*nagarācca bahirjātā ye śūrā madavihvalāḥ \|*  
*hatvā tānsukalaḥ śīghraṃ rājñe duḥkhaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 88 \|\|*

*bhayabhīto mahīrājo dhyātvā sarvamayīṃ śivām \|*  
*suṣvāpa niśi śuddhātmā tuṣṭābhūjjagadaṃbikā \|\| 89 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśādīnbodhayitvā taiśca sārdhaṃ samāgamat \|*  
*teṣāṃ cāsīnmahadyuddhaṃ gaṃdharveṇa tadāhnikam \|\| 90 \|\|*

81-90. Suta said- Once a king named Kaikaya ruled in Kasmira. He had ten sons and a daughter Madanavati. The sons were known by the names of Kama, Prakama, Sankama, Niskama, Nirapatrapa, Jaya, Vijaya, Jayanta, Jayavan and Jaya. The king called Prthviraja and requested him that he intended his daughter to marry his son named Saradana, but a Gandharva named Sukala during the moonlight kidnaps my daughter and enjoys sports with her. The Gandharva had arrived here on full moon day of the month of Caitra. Today is the dark eighth day of the month of Vaisakha. What I would desire is that you better think of leaving for Dehali only after killing him. On hearing this, Prthviraja, securing the safety of his son and daughter-inlaw, departed for Dehali. When the full moon day of the month of Vaisakha was over, the Gandharva known by the name of Sukala, getting enraged, surrounded Dehali with ten thousand of his warriors. Whenever someone went out of the city, the Gandharva named Sukala used to devour him. In this way, in a very short period, he troubled Prthviraja immensely. The noble soul Prthviraja also getting frightened from him, adored the goddess Siva with devotion, who was immensely pleased with his worship. She therefore enlightened Udayasimha and others about the situation. Then she taking them with herself, departed from the place of the battlefield, where the war was going on throughout the day and night.

## \|\| 2.134.91-96 \|\|

*balakhāniśca balavāñchatagaṃdharvamuttamam \|*  
*tridināṃte ca saṃhatya sukhakhānistathaiva ca \|\| 91 \|\|*

*sukalaśca tadā kruddho gāṃdharvīṃ ca sasarja ha \|*  
*bahudhā te hi gaṃdharvāstaiśca sārddhaṃ samārudhan \|\| 92 \|\|*

*bhayabhītāstadā sarve rāmāṃśaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*āhlādaśca prasannātmā śāradāṃ sarvamaṃgalām \|\| 93 \|\|*

*divāsūktena tuṣṭāva tadā prādurabhūcchivā \|*  
*gaṃdharvānmohayitvāśu drāvayāmāsa śāradā \|\| 94 \|\|*

*parājite ca gaṃdharve kṛṣṇāṃśo janamohanaḥ \|*  
*mahīrājamupāgamya koṭisvarṇaṃ gṛhītavān \|\| 95 \|\|*

*ṣoḍaśābde ca kṛṣṇāṃśe saṃprāpte devipūjake \|*  
*mārgamāsaṃ tu saṃprāpte mardanaśca vivāhitaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

91-96. In that war, the valorous Balakhani killed a hundred Gandharvas in three days. Sukhakhani also performed similarly. Thereafter, Sukala created the Gandharva illusion. In the net of that illusion, the Gandharvas surrounded all the warriors of Mahavati. At that point of time, the warriors getting frightened from them, took refuge with Ahlada. The delightful Ahlada, at once started adoring goddess Sarada also known as goddess Sarvamangala. Getting delighted, the goddess appeared before him and making the Gandharvas senseless, the goddess Sarada forced the Gandharvas to flee from that place. After defeating the Gandharvas, Udayasimha, who impressed all, reached before Prthviraja and received a crore of gold coins from the king. Udayasimha was devoted to the goddess and was running in the age of sixteen years at that time. During those days, in the month of Margasirsa, the marriage of Mardana - the son of Prthviraja, was performed. The related story is like this.

## \|\| 2.134.97-111 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*puṃḍradeśe mahārājo nāgavarmā mahābalaḥ \|*  
*babhūva takṣakaparo dharmavāñjagatītale \|\| 97 \|\|*

*patnī nāgavatī tasya takṣakasya sutā śubhā \|*  
*pituḥ śāpena sañjātā kaliṃgādhipateḥ sutā \|\| 98 \|\|*

*daśaiva tanayāścāsankanyā tasya śubhānanā \|*  
*suvelā nāma vikhyātā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|\| 99 \|\|*

*purohitaṃ samāhūya mahīrājāya praiṣayat \|*  
*sa gatvā kathayitvāgre mardano vīrato mayā \|\| 100 \|\|*

*mahīrājastu tacchrutvā trilakṣabalasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*maṃgalaṃ kārayāmāsa gatvā nāgapure śubhe \|\| 101 \|\|*

*suvelā pitaraṃ prāha dehi me nāgabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*vivāhaṃ hi kariṣyāmi nocetprāṇāṃstyajāmyaham \|\| 102 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā nāgavarmā mahīrājāntamāyayau \|*  
*suvelāyā abhiprāyaṃ varṇayāmāsa vistarāt \|\| 103 \|\|*

*ityuktaḥ sa mahīrājo vismitobhūtsuduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*preṣayāmāsa vai patraṃ yatrāhlādādayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*iti jñātvā tadā'hlādaḥ śūrapaṃcaśatāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśavatsajaissārddhaṃ dināṃte ca samāgamat \|\| 105 \|\|*

*śatayojanagāminyo vājinyaśca dviyāmake \|*  
*sahasrayojanaṃ vīryaṃ tāsāṃ caiva dine niśi \|\| 106 \|\|*

*kalāṃśādudbhavā aśvā vājinā ca hareḥ svayam \|*  
*ratnāśvasya kalāṃśaśca kapoto haraṇībhavaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*gāyatro yobhavadvājī kālacakrapravartakaḥ \|*  
*tatkalāṃśātsamudbhūto ravidattaḥ papīhakaḥ \|*  
*hariṇī nāma tacchaktiḥ kalāṃśādbhūmimāgatā \|\| 108 \|\|*

*sukhakhāniḥ papīhastho balakhāniḥ kapotagaḥ \|*  
*āhlādaśca karālastho biṃdulastho hareḥ kalā \|\| 109 \|\|*

*gatvā te tu mahīrājaṃ natvā tuṃgāsanāṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*prasannaḥ sa mahīrājo vacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*mama putrāśca yuṣmābhistrayaḥ śūrā vivāhitāḥ \|*  
*tathaiva mardanaṃ vīraṃ samudvāhya sukhī bhava \|\| 111 \|\|*

97-111. Suta said- The lord of Pundra country was known as the valorous Nagavarma. He was an extremely religious person, who was always engaged in the worship of the serpent Taksaka. Nagavati was known to be his wife, who was the daughter of Taksaka and who because of the curse from her father, was bom as the daughter of the king of Kalinga. That king sent a message through his priest that he had selected his son named Mardana as a match for his daughter. Hearing that, Prthviraja with his lakhs of soldiers, went to Nagapura and performed the welfare ceremony. At that point of time, Suvela said to her father- “you kindly get me Nagabhusana (serpent ornament). I shall get married only after receipt of the same, otherwise I shall end my life.” On hearing this, Nagavarma reached before Prthviraja and expressed to him in detail the desire of his daughter Suvela. On hearing this, Prthviraja was not only surprised but also felt uncomfortable. Soon thereafter, he sent a letter to Ahlada and others with a request. Accepting that, Ahlada, accompanied with Udai Singh, Balakhana, Sukhakhani and others tried to reach there in a day. All of them mounted the horses, who could cover a distance of a hundred yojanas during the noon time. In this way, the powerful steed covered a distance of a thousand yojanas in a day and night. Reaching there, they informed (the concerned people). Those horses were bom of the horse of Indra. Harm! was bom of the amsa of Ilasva from the mare Harini. The horse named Kalacakra was bom of the amsa of Gayatri. Papila was given by the Sungod, while Harini was bom of the amsa of Sakti. The horse named Papiha was used for riding by Balakhana, Ahlada mounted over Karala and Udayasimha rode over Bindula. Reaching before Prthviraja, all of them offered their salutation to him. Getting delighted, Prthviraja spoke to them pleasantly - “The way all of you have earlier performed the marriages of my sons, similarly you arrange for the marriage of Mardana and enjoy all the comforts.”

## \|\| 2.134.112-120 \|\|

*iti śrutvā sa āhlādo gatvā bhūtalamuttamam \|*  
*rasātalaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ nāginīṃ prāha nirbhayaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*supto hi tava bhartā ca puṃḍarīkaḥ śubhānanaḥ \|*  
*bodhayāśu mahārājñi nāgānāṃ no dayāṃ kuru \|\| 113 \|\|*

*ityuktā sāha taṃ vīraṃ puṃḍarīkaśca matpatiḥ \|*  
*ruṣāviṣṭaśca balavāndāhayecca vapustava \|\| 114 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vihasyāha tava bharturna no bhayam \|*  
*ityevaṃ vacanaṃ kṛtvā padbhyāṃ pucchamatāḍayat \|\| 115 \|\|*

*prabuddhaśca tadā rājā nāgānāṃ ca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*jvālāmālāṃ svadehācca janayāmāsa vīryavān \|\| 116 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tadviṣamujjvālaṃ sa dhyātvā sarvamaṃgalām \|*  
*śamayāmāsa balavāndevīpūjanatatparaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*puṃḍarīkaḥ prasannātmā nāgabhūṣaṇamuttamam \|*  
*āhlādāya dadau śīghraṃ sarvaśṛṅgārasaṃyutam \|\| 118 \|\|*

*āhlādastu hayārūḍho mahīrājāya dattavān \|*  
*vivāhaṃ kārayāmāsa vaivāhikavidhānataḥ \|*  
*koṭisvarṇaṃ nṛpātprāptaṃ gṛhītvā śīghramāyayau \|\| 119 \|\|*

*hayavidyāsamārūḍhāste hayā gehamāgatāḥ \|*  
*jñeyāḥ paṃcaśataṃ sarve saśūrā gṛhamāyayuḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

112-120. On hearing this, Ahlada went to the well known netherworld and fearlessly said to queen serpent- “O queen, your husband Pundarika is sleeping at the moment. You better inform him of my arrival. Don’t be compassionate on the Nagas at the moment.” On hearing this, the queen said- “My husband Pundarika when wakes up, he getting antagonized with his warriors, would reduce your body to ashes in anger.” Ahlada spoke smilingly - “I am not at all afraid of your husband.” Thus speaking, Ahlada himself pressed the tail of the serpent with his foot. The valorous king of the serpent then started throwing poison out of his body. Observing the flames of the poison, the valorous Ahlada who was the devotee of the goddess Sarvamangala, subsided the poisonous flames. At that point of time, Pundarika getting delighted, handed over the ornament of adornment to him. Thereafter, the marriage of the girl was properly celebrated and receiving a crore of gold coins, all of them went back to their own abodes. The steed who were well versed in the asva-vidya, carried them all to their respective abodes together with five hundreds of their warriors.

## \|\| 2.134.121-135 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*madradeśeṣu yaścāsīnmadrakeśo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*pañcābdaṃ pūjayāmāsa svargavaidyau surottamau \|\| 121 \|\|*

*tayośca varadānena daśa putrā babhūvire \|*  
*sutā kāntimatī jātā rūpayauvanaśālinī \|\| 122 \|\|*

*sa mahīrājamāhūya trilakṣabalasaṃyutam \|*  
*dadau kanyāṃ vidhānena madreśaḥ sūryavarmaṇe \|\| 123 \|\|*

*navoḍhāṃ tu tadā patnīṃ sūryavarmā gṛhītavān \|*  
*svagehāya yayau śīghraṃ mahīrājo balaissaha \|\| 124 \|\|*

*karburonāma māyāvī vibhīṣaṇasuto balī \|*  
*rākṣasastatra saṃprāpto dṛṣṭvā kāṃtimatīṃ śubhām \|\| 125 \|\|*

*madrakeśasya tanayāṃ divyaśobhāsamanvi tām \|*  
*jahāra paśyatāṃ teṣāṃ sahyādrigirimāyayau \|\| 126 \|\|*

*mahīrājastadā duḥkhī vilalāpa bhṛśaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*dehalīgehamāgamya dūtamāhūya satva ram \|\| 127 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṃśaṃ preṣayāmāsa sa gatvā samavarṇayat \|*  
*jñātvā te tu hayārūḍhāḥ śūrāḥ paṃcaśatāvṛtāḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*sahyādrigirimāgamya kṛṣṇāṃ śaḥ karburaṃ prati \|*  
*nirbhayo vacanaṃ prāha śṛṇu rākṣasasattama \|\| 129 \|\|*

*vibhīṣaṇo bhaktarājastasya tvaṃ dayitaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvayā na kartavyaṃ pāpaṃ vaṃśa vināśanam \|*  
*rāvaṇena purā sītā saṃhṛtā viditaṃ tava \|\| 130 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa hovāca pureyaṃ dayitā priyā \|*  
*mama gaṃdharvatanayā muniśāpānmahīṃ gatā \|\| 131 \|\|*

*ato'haṃ tadviyogena tyaktvā laṃkāṃ mahāpurīm \|*  
*madrakeśamahaṃ prāpya madrakeśabhayādaham \|*  
*na jahāra priyāṃ ramyāṃ tatroṣitvā dinaṃ bahu \|\| 132 \|\|*

*adya me vaśagā sābhūnnāmnā kāṃtimatī śubhā \|*  
*jitvā māṃ ca gṛhāṇāśu samarthāśca vayaṃ sadā \|\| 133 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa kṛṣṇāṃśaḥ khaḍgayuddhamacīkarat \|*  
*saptarātreṇa taṃ jitvā labdhvā kāṃtimatīṃ śubhām \|*  
*tadā ca dehalīṃ prāpya mahīrājāntamāyayau \|\| 134 \|\|*

*koṭisvarṇaṃ dadau rājā kṛṣṇāṃśāya mahātmane \|*  
*sa vīro baṃdhubhiḥ sārdhaṃ pramadāvanamāyayau \|\| 135 \|\|*

121-135. Suta said- Once in the Madradesa country, a valorous king named Madrakesa ruled. He worshipped Asvinikumara - the best of the gods, for five years. Getting pleased with his worship, he bestowed the king ten sons and a daughter known by the name of Kantimati. When the girl attained the beauty and the youthful age, the king of Madra country invited the king Prthviraja and married his daughter with Suryavarma. After his marriage, Suryavarma went to his city along with his bride. In the mean time, a demon named Karbura, who was quite an illusory one and said to be the son of Vibhisana, had a look at Kantimati who was adorned with all the ornaments. He kidnapped her and departed towards the Sahyadri mountain. At that point of time, Prthviraja was repeatedly lamenting. Somehow he reached Dehall and sent a messenger to Udayasimha, who narrated the factual position to Udayasimha and all others there. Thereafter, all of them riding over their respective horses and accompanied with five hundred valorous samantas, proceeded towards the Sahyadri mountain. Reaching there, Udayasimha fearlessly said to the demon Karbura- “O best of Raksasas, you listen to my words. You are the son of Vibhisana - the great devotee (of Rama). Therefore, you should not commit this sin which destroy the race, because in earlier time Havana had kidnapped JanakI, which is not unknown to you.” On hearing these words, the demon said- “She is my beloved wife of earlier times, who had been bom in a Gandharva race. She has been bom on earth because of the curse of a sage. In separation from her, I had been living in Madradesa leaving Lanka. But I could not kidnap her from that place because of the fear of the king of that place. I have got Kantimati after many days. In case you want to have her, you will have to fight with me and we people are always competent.” Hearing these words, Udyasimha started fighting with the demon with his sword. After seven days’ fight, the demon was defeated. Then taking the auspicious Kantimati with them, they handed her over to Prthviraja. At that point of time, the king Prthviraja gave away a crore of gold coins to Udayasimha, who then left the place with his brothers.

## \|\| 2.134.136-154 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*paṭṭanākhyapure rājā nāmnā pūrṇāmalo balī \|*  
*vasūnārādhāyāmāsa paṃcavarṣāntare mudā \|*  
*tadā prasannāste devā dadustasmai varaṃ śubham \|\| 136 \|\|*

*varadānācca sañjātā daśa putrā mahīpateḥ \|*

*māṃ śabdavedhinaṃ viddhi cauryadeśadhuraṃdharam \|\| 143 \|\|*

*tadā prasannaḥ kṛṣṇāṃśo vacanaṃ prāha nirbhayaḥ \|*

*tatpaścādbhūmimāgatya yathāyogyaṃ kuruṣva bhoḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sahodo nīlasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*paiśācaṃ deśamagamatpunaḥ prāpto rasātalam \|\| 153 \|\|*

*bhūmirājaḥ prasannātmā koṭisvarṇaṃ dadau tadā \|*  
*gajārūḍhāśca te paṃca saṃyayuśca mahāvatīm \|\| 154 \|\|*

136-154. Suta said - Purnamala was the lord of the city of Patna who had delightfully adored Vasus continuously for five years, who getting pleased with his worship bestowed on him an auspicious boon by which the king got ten sons and a daughter named Vidyunmala. When the girl became youthful, the king respectfully invited Prthviraja at his place with seven lakhs of his soldiers and married his daughter with his son Bhimasena. Thereafter, Bhimasena returned with his newly wedded wife and started spending time delightfully with his wife at Dehall. In the mean time, Sahoda - the king of Paisaca country, together with ten thousand of his Mleccha warriors, started making arrangements for kidnapping of Vidyunmala - the wife of Bhimasena. With the permission of the valorous daityas, he reached the auspicious place of Kuruksetra and camped there with his army. Initially, he broke all the images of the gods and desecrated the holy place with the blood of cows. The strong ruler then sent a messenger with a letter to the religious-minded king Prthviraja. Hearing that letter, the king said to the Yavana king in reply- “You becoming the lord of Mlecchas, have arrived here for the sake of Vidyunmala. I am also the leader of Caurya country and proficient in shoot at the sound.” Thus speaking, together with his three lakhs of warriors, he reached the battle ground of Kuruksetra, where a terrific battle was fought between the two of them. At the dead of night of the dark night of the month of Jyestha, the valorous daitya emerging from the netherworld with his ten thousand warriors arrived and started killing the warriors of Prthviraja, besides eating them at the same time. Getting frightened at that time, Prthviraja took refuge with the goddess Sarada. At the same time, Udayasimha and others also arrived there in a moment by the grace of the goddess Bhagavati. After killing a thousand of daityas, the valorous Udayasimha and both the sons of Vatsaraja started attacking the enemy with their swords. Getting pleased with their waging of the war, the king of the daityas was pleased and asked them to seek for a boon. On hearing these words, these people said- “In case you are pleased with us then you give us a promise, not to invade this Arya country in future and going to Mleecha, you eat only the Mlecchas.” Listening to their terrific words, the king Bali himself went to Udayasimha and realizing his importance, he himself prayed to him. Thereafter, Udayasimha delightfully said- “Till such time I live in this world, you better stay in your homes. Thereafter, you can come to this country and behave properly.” On hearing these words, Sahodadhi with all his Pisacas went back to the netherworld and Prthviraja also delightfully paid a crore of gold coins to them. Thereafter, all the five of them, mounting over the elephant, returned to their country of Mahavati

*pūrṇo babhūva kanakai rājarājaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

155-168. Suta said- Prthviraja’s son named Varddhana, who was the best of all his sons, had started adoring lord Visnu at the age of five years. The lord getting pleased with his devotion, showered all the riches on him and as a result of which, with the influence of the lord of Gandharvas, the entire treasure of Prthviraja was filled to the capacity within a year. Thereafter, Kubera also delightfully gave the daughter named Kinnari to Mankana - the son of the king. О sage, thus I have narrated the stories related to the marriage of the sons of Prthviraja. Thereafter, valorous Dhundhukara with a lakh of his warriors, challenged Brahmananda for a war reaching there. At that point of time, the valorous Udayasimha had just entered in the twenty first year of his age. Finding the enemy army before him, Brahmananda - the son of Malana, destroyed half of the enemy army using his Brahmastra. The remaining fifty thousand soldiers fled away here and there in fright. Thereafter, Dhundhukara also deserting the battlefield, returned to Prthviraja, hearing which Prthviraja feeling painful, summoned Mahipati and Candrabhatta and told them-“You tell me how could I be victorious? You think over it quickly and tell me.” At that point of time, Mahipati said- “O best of the kings, I am expressing my opinion. You kindly listen. The valorous Camunda should be disguised as a woman and his palanquin should be given over to Brahmananda. Dhundhukara with his four sons should be present there and attack him with their weapons.” On hearing this, Prthviraja was delighted. In the evening of the bright eighth day of the month of Magha, moving on the same lines, the palanquin being guarded by the four warriors, he sent the palanquin to Brahmananda. Reaching before Brahmananda, Camunda in the guise of Vela forcefully attacked over his chest with ai trident, as a result of which the strong warrior cried with pain. In the mean time, all the five warriors also reached there. Taraka, who was one of them, shot an arrow at his heart. Silryavarma attacked him with a tomara, Bhima attacked him with a club, Varddhana attacked him with a sword and Dhundhu attacked him with a spear over his head, at one and the same time.

*kaniṣṭhāmṛtabhāvena velāyā balavāṃstadā \|*

*velā nāma mahībhartuḥ sutāhaṃ tvāmupasthitā \|*  
*matpatiśca bhavāndhīraśchadmanā vaṃcakairhataḥ \|*

*harināgaramāruhya mayā sārddhaṃ śubhānane \|*  
*gatvā tīrthāni ramyāṇi saṃtyajāmi kalevaram \|\| 179 \|\|*

169-179. With the simultaneous attacks of all of them, the valorous Brahmananda was fainted and fell down on the ground. But inspite of his body having been so badly wounded, he held his sword and separated the heads of Bhima and Varddhana from their bodies. Then he reached before Suryavarma and made him roll over the ground. At that point of time, leaving Brahmananda, Taraka, Dhundhukara and Camunda reached before Prthviraja. After killing of all his three sons, Prthviraja reached before Vela and cried pathetically. On hearing this, Vela at once mounted the palanquin, quickly reached before Brahmananda and found him in fainted condition. Thereafter, she started crying, finding her brothers lying dead. At that point of time, Brahmananda opened his eyes. Finding Vela crying there, he asked her- “In case you have come to me in this war, whose daughter are you? Whose beloved are you? О excellent one, in case you want to do good to me, then give me water for drinking.” On hearing these words, the chaste Vela at once gave him water to drink and said to him during the same night - “O son of Malana, I would like to say something to you. You kindly listen to me. I am the daughter of Prthviraja known by the name of Vela. You are , my valorous husband. Therefore, I have arrived here. O Rajendra, though these dishonest people have fraudulently attacked you with the intention of killing you, still I request you that you should save your life and kindly enjoy all the pleasures with me.” On hearing these words, Brahmananda said to her—“In this age of Kali, it would be better to die instead of remaining alive. Therefore, you accept my words and riding over my horse Harinagara, get along with me. I would like to put an end to my life at some holy place."

## \|\| 2.134.180-186 \|\|

*itpuktvā tau samāruhya pūrve ca kapilāntikam \|*

*velāmuvāca vacanaṃ bhādraśuklāṣṭamīdine \|*  
*dehaṃ tyajāmi bho rājñi tārakaṃ jahi bhūtale \|\| 183 \|\|*

*kurukṣetraṃ mayā sārddhaṃ bhavānvai gaṃtumarhati \|\| 184 \|\|*

*sthitvā tatra samasvānto bhaja tvaṃ sarvamaṃgalām \|*  
*ahaṃ mahāvatīṃ prāpya punarvai dehalīṃ prati \|\| 185 \|\|*

*tārakaṃ ca tathā hatvā tvatsamīpaṃ vrajāmyaham \|*  
*ityuktaḥ sa tathetyuktvā brahmadhyānaparo'bhavat \|\| 186 \|\|*

180-186. After this conversation, both of them rode over Harinagara horse and initially moved towards the eastern direction, reached the Kapila-asrama (Ganga-sagara) and took their bath and gave away charities. Thereafter, they also travelled further and visited other holy places, where they took sacred baths and gave away charities, feeling immensely satisfied. Thus they visited Kapilasrama in the east, Setubandha in the south, Dvaraka in the west and Badarikasrama in the north where they took their baths. Thereafter, reaching Gandhamadana mountain, the valorous Brahmananda said to Vela- “O my queen, today is the eighth bright day of the month of Bhadrapada and I want to face the end of my life here. You remaining on earth, must kill Taraka.” On hearing these words, she humbly spoke- “O master, you kindly accept my words. You better come along with me at Kuruksetra and pray for your welfare there and I visiting Mahavati from there, shall again return to Dehali after killing Taraka there. Then, I shall return to you.” Accordingly, he accepted the words of Vela and reaching Kuruksetra, he started meditating on Brahma.

## Chapter 135. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-10. Suta said- (At the time of the above incident), Udayasimha was passing through the age of thirty second year. At the same time, the queen Vela taking to the form of yogini, riding over the Harinagara horse, departed for the city of Mahavati. Reaching there, she reached the court of the king Parimala. She offered her salutation to him and then started speaking. At that point of time, Udayasimha and other great warriors were also present there. She said- “You consider Mahipati to be your beloved and well wisher, while Udayasimha is considered to be a rebellion. As a result of this, with the help of valorous Taraka and your other sons, you got my valorous husband Brahmananda killed. Dhundhukara made Camunda a woman and took her to my husband. All the people collectively and deceitfully destroyed my husband. Presently, my husband is lying at Kuruksetra in an unconscious condition. Therefore, all of you should make preparations for going with me to reach there.” Hearing these extremely harsh words, Udayasimha and other valorous warriors, denouncing the king Parimala and his queen Malana, declared-“Both of you have gott. my friend badly injured.” Thus speaking, all of them started crying aloud. Thereafter, sending the sons to all the four directions, they summoned them to get armed and proceed to Dehali. At the same time, she sent a poison like bitter letter to Prthviraja at Dehall and herself went to the palace of Malana. The king Prthviraja listened to that letter carefully and learning about it, his comfortable sleep atonce disappeared. He also summoned the rulers who were dependent on him and started preparations for war.

*dussaho duśśalaścaiva jalasaṃdhaḥ samaḥ sahaḥ \|*  
*viṃdastathānuviṃdaśca subāhurduṣpradharṣaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*durmarṣaṇaśca duṣkarṇaḥ somakīrtiranūdaraḥ \|*

*tomarānvayabhūpālo bāhlīkapatirāgataḥ \|*

*citropacitrau citrākṣaścāruścitraḥ śarāsanaḥ \|*

*teṣāmaṃśāḥ kramājjātā abhinaṃdanadehajāḥ \|*  
*mahānaṃdaśca naṃdaśca parānaṃdopanaṃdakau \|*  
*sunaṃdaśca surānandaḥ pranaṃdaḥ kauravāṃśakaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

11-21. Prthviraja, who was the amsa of Duryodhana, leading the army of twenty four lakhs off soldiers, marched towards Kuruksetra. The king Parimala also, with Udayasimha and other warriors, leading an army of sixteen lakhs soldiers besides Vela and other family members, reached Kuruksetra. Reaching there, they found that Brahmananda was engaged in meditation at the holy place of Syamanta-Pancaka. He set up his camps. The rulers of Dehall who were the amsa of Kauravas, getting desirous of victory, also started setting up their camp. On the full moon day of the month of Kdrtika, taking the bath and after distributing charities, then on the dark second day of the month of Margasirsa, the terrific war started in which king Lahara of the Visvakasena had arrived with his sixteen sons, who were born of the amsas of Kauravas. They were known by the same names as they had in earlier birth, such as Dussaha, Dussala, Jalasandha, Samahsahah, Vinda, Anuvinda, Subahu, Duspradharsana, Durmarsana, Duskarna, Somakrti, Anudara, Sala, Sattva and Vivitsu. These were the names of his warriors. Tomara - the lord of Bahlika, known by the name of Kulabhusana, arrived with his army of three lakhs of soldiers. He had also brought with him his seven sons known by the names of Mahananda, Nanda, Parananda, Upananda, Sunanda, Surananda and Prananda, who in earlier births were born in the Kaurava-vamsa as Citra, Upacitra, Citraksa, Carucitra, Sarasana, Sulocana and Suvarna.

*nṛpaḥ pariharavaṃśīyo māyāvarmā mahābalī \|*  
*lakṣa sainyayutaḥ prāpto daśaputrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*durmado durvigāhaśca naṃdaśca vikaṭānanaḥ \|*

*durmukho durdaro vāyuḥ suratho virathaḥ kramāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

*lakṣasainyaiśca balavāndaśaputrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-44. The king Mayavarma of Parihara-vamsa who belonged to Angadesa arrived there with the army of ten lakhs of soldiers. Besides, Durmada, Durvigaha, Nanda, Vikajanana, Citravarma, Suvarma, Sudurmocana, Unjabha, Sunabha and Upananda were the rulers of amsas of Kauravas. In addition to this, the rulers of Kauravas family included Matta, Pramatta, Unmatta, Sumatta, Durmada, Durmukha, Durddhara, Vayu, Suratha and Viratha had arrived with ten sons. The king Malavarma of Sukla-vamsa was accompanied with a lakh of his soldiers, besides his ten sons known by the names of Bala, Prabala, Subala, Balavan, Bali, Sumula, Mahamula, Durga, Bhima and Bhayankara, who were in earlier birth known as Ayobahu, Mahabahu, Citrariga, Citrakundala, Citrayudha, Nisangi, Pasi, Vrndaraka, Drdhavarma and Drdhaksatra who were all the amsas of Kauravas. Kaikeya - the king of the lunar race, arrived with a lakh of his soldiers, besides his ten sons, at Kuruksetra, which was a terrific battleground. The names of his sons were- Kama, Prakama, Sankama, Niskama, Nirpatrapa, Jaya, Vijaya, Jayanta, Jayavan and Jaya. Their names in the earlier birth respectively were - Bhimavega, Bhiabala, Balaki, Balavarddhana, Ugrayudha, Dandadhara, Drdhasandha, Mahidhara, Jarasandha and they belonged to the race of Kauravas. Similarly, the Nagavamsiya king of Pundra country known by the name of Nagapala arrived there with a lakh of soldiers and ten sons, who were known in their earlier birth as Ugrasrava, Ugrasena, Senani, Dusparayana, Aparajita, Kundasayi, Visalaksa, Duradhara, Drdhahasta, Suhasta and belonged to the Kaurava race. The king Madrakesa of Tomara family arrived there with a lakh of his soldiers and ten sons, who in their earlier births were known by the names of Vatavega, Suvarca, Nagadanta, Agrayajaka, Ketu, Vaksi, Kavaci, Kratha, Kundala and Kundadhira. All of them were bom earlier in the Kaurava race. The king of Magadha belonging to the Sardula race arrived with a lakh of his warriors and his ten sons were present there. The sons were known by the names of Virabahu, Bhimastha, Dhanurdhara, Raudrakarma, Drdharatha, Alolupa, Abhaya, Anadhrsta and Kundabhedi who also were the amsas of Kauravas. They were known by the same names (in the present birth as well). Mankana - who was the lord of Rupadesa and was a kinnara himself, also reached there. This Rupadesa has been identified by the learned people as having been lodged beyond China, which is the place of dwelling of the beautiful kinnaras.

*jagannāyaka evāpi śūrāyutasamanvitaḥ \|*

45-55. In the battlefield of the royal races, the people of Mankana’s race also reached with ten kinnaras and the eight sons who were known by the names of Viravi, Pramathi, Dirgharomaka, Dirghabahu, Mahabahu, Vyudho and Kanakadhvaja. All of them were bom of the kinnaras and were known by the same names on earth. The king Netrasimha also arrived with a lakh of his soldiers, who were the amsas of Salya and were bom in the Sardula-vamsa. The king Gajapati of the race of Sakuni entrusting the care of his kingdom to his sons, arrived there with a lakh of his soldiers. Mayuradhvaja - the amsa of Virata entrusting his kingdom to Makaranda, had arrived there with a lakh of his warriors. Similarly, Virasena of the amsa of Ugrasena, accompanied with Kamasena and an army of a lakh of warriors, reached there. The king Laksana leaving PadminI with great difficulty, leading an army of seven lakh soldiers, also reached there. Talana, Dhanyapala, Lallasimha, Udayasimha and Indula, accompanied with an army of a lakh of soldiers, were also present. Bhima, Yuyutsa and from the family of Kuntibhoja were bom Talana, Dhanyapala and Lallasimha. Together with Udayasimha and Indula, they arrived with an army of a lakh of soldiers. Ahlada was from the amsa of Bhagadatta. Besides Gautama, Kulabhusana and Jananayaka arrived there with the army of ten thousand soldiers.

56-75. Similarly, several of the intoxicated rulers of small kingdoms in thousands, together with their respective armies, arrived at the battlefield of Kuruksetra. Together with his son and a lakh of his soldiers, Mulavarma reached before the king Parimala and informed him of his arrival. At the same time, the son of the king Kaikeya arrived there with a lakh of his army. The valorous kings Netrasimha, Mayuradhvaja and Virasena, together with their sons and a lakh of soldiers, also arrived there. Besides Laksana with a lakh of his soldiers and Alhada with an equal number of soldiers arrived there for the help of the king Parimala, who had his own army of three lakhs. In this way, the king Parimala made preparations in the battlefield with an army of sixteen lakhs of soldiers. Similarly, for Prthviraja’s help, Lahara - the best of the kings, Mayavarma, Nagavarma, king of Madradesa, Purnamala with his sons had arrived there with an army of a lakh of soldiers each. The kinnara named Mankana with his sons and a lakh of soldiers, Gajaraja with an army of a lakh of soldiers, Dhundhukara with five lakhs of soldiers and Bhagadatta - son of Krsnakumara arrived with three lakhs of his soldiers to help Prthviraja. The son of Dalavahana, Angada - a dweller of the Desagopala country and dear to Devaki, besides rulers of Kalinga, Trikona, Sripati, Sritara, Mukunda, Suketu, Ruhila, Guhila, Induvara and valorous Jayanta were present there. Each one of them had an army of ten thousand soldiers each. Besides a thousand small rulers were also there to assist Prthviraja, who had their respective armies of a thousand warriors each. Out of these armies, two hundred of the rulers were entrusted with the protection of the kingdom of Dehali. Thus Prthviraja - the lord of Dehali, reached the battlefield with twenty four lakhs of his army. The terrific war ended after eighteen days, after the destruction of the Ksatriyas. О son of the race of Bhrgu, I am now describing the war in details. You listen attentively. On the black second day of Margasirsa, the immensely strong Prthviraja becoming fearless, summoned the king Lahara and said to him- “O excellent one, together with your son and Camunda guarded by Dhundhukara, you get ready to march towards the battlefield. Hearing these words, all of them reached the battlefield.

76-95. At that point of time, the king Parimala called for Mayuradhvaja and said to him- “O best of monarchs, getting guarded by Udayasimha and Jayanta (Indula) besides Devasimha together with a lakh of warriors, you should reach the battleground.” On hearing this, leading the army of a lakh of warriors, Mayuradhvaja reached the battleground and fought with the king Lahara. Both the rulers fought vigorously in the battleground. A lakh of army soldiers in that war were distributed like this- A chariot, five hundred elephants, five thousand horses and ten times of that number were the foot soldiers. After informing you about the distribution of the warriors, I am giving details of the army commanders. You listen to me carefully. There was a master for the ten soldiers who was known as Pattipa. Similarly, five cavalry men were commanded by a leader named Gulmapa. The leader of five elephants was known as Gajadhipa. In the terrific war of the age of Kali, there was a charioteer who led these people. In those army formations, forty camel riders served as messengers. In these armies, there were a thousand guns positioned separately at suitable places. Thirty six foot soldiers worked for the same, details of which are like this. You please listen. Ten soldiers were to supply the gun fodder. Ten soldiers were there to operate them. Ten soldiers were there for making them wet. Three of them were there to ignite fire in the guns and remaining three were to keep watch over them. Thus, for the battle which lasted for three praharas, the details have been discussed. The Sudras also attended the army formations to help the soldiers. In this way, the distribution of a lakh of soldiers has been provided, who were fighting the religious war in the battlefield. Starting from the early morning, the war continued upto noon from both the sides of the soldiers. Thereafter, all the army commanders assembled there for the purpose of waging the war. Then after the fight between the warriors of Mayuradhvaja and Lahara in the battleground, the valorous and famous Dhundhukara and other warriors appeared for the war for a prahara. Camunda fought with Udayasimha, Dhundhukara fought with Indula and Bhagadatta fought a terrific war with Devasimha, in which by the evening time, soldiers of lower ranks were killed. In this war, Udayasimha killed all the sixteen sons of the king Lahara in a ghadi (22 minutes). Then blowing his victory conch, he marched towards the king Laksana. On the other hand, Camunda, Dhundhukara and Bhagadatta together with their hundred warriors, reached before the king Prthviraja and comfortably slept during the night. On the other hand, leading the remaining thousand soldiers, Indula and Devasimha reached the king Parimala and delightfully spent the night there. In the early morning of the third day, the king Prthviraja summoned the monarch Gajapati and said to him- “Getting guarded by three warriors, together with a lakh of warriors, you get ready to reach the battlefield. At the same time, the king Parimala too commanded Netrasimha saying- “Under the command of the great warriors like Udayasimha, you march forward for the start of the war.”

## \|\| 2.135.96-117 \|\|

*tayoścāsīnmahayuddhaṃ senayorubhayoḥ kramāt \|*  
*hayā hayaiḥ kṣayaṃ jagmurgajāścaiva tathā gajaiḥ \|*  
*paccarāḥ paccaraiḥ sārddhaṃ śataghnyaśca śataghnibhiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*aparāhne muniśreṣṭha netrasiṃho mahābalaḥ \|*  
*mahāgajaṃ gajapatiṃ gatvā yuddhamacīkarat \|\| 97 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ ca virathau saṃchinnadhanuṣau tadā \|*  
*khaḍgahastau mahīṃ prāpya cakratū raṇamulbaṇam \|*  
*anyonyena vadhaṃ kṛtvā svargalokamupāgatau \|\| 98 \|\|*

*indulastaṃ tu cāmuṃḍaṃ devo vai dhuṃdhukaṃ tathā \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśo bhagadattaṃ ca jitvā rājānamāyayuḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*śeṣaiḥ paṃcaśataiḥ śūraistaiḥ sārddhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ prati \|*

*prātaḥkāle tu saṃprāpte mahīrājo mahābalaḥ \|*

*bhavāndaśasutairvīrairlakṣasainyaiśca saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sarvaśatruvināśāya gaṃtumarhati sattama \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa nṛpatirvādyānsaṃvādya cāyayau \|\| 102 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā parimalo bhūpo māyāvarmāṇamāgatam \|*  
*jagannāyakamāhūya vacanaṃ prāha nirbhayaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*bhavāndaśasahasraiśca sārddhaṃ taistribhiranvitaḥ \|*

*gatvā sabhāyāṃ nṛpatiṃ praṇamya vākyaṃ samūcuḥ śṛṇu caṃdravaṃśin \|*
