96-117. On that particular day, both the armies fought a terrific battle in the battlefield in which cavalrymen fought with cavalrymen, elephant riders with elephant riders, while the foot soldiers fought with the foot soldiers and the riflemen fought with riflemen. The gunners fought with the gunners, forcefully killing one another. О best of the sages, in the said battle, during the noon time, the king Netrasimha started fighting with Gajapati. While fighting, both of them initially discarded their chariots, cutting the bows and arrows of each other and then making use of their respective swords, fought a terrific war. Thereafter, while waging the war, both of them met with their end. On the other hand, Indula attacked Camunda, Devasimha attacked Dhandhu and Udayasimha defeated Bhagadatta and then they proceeded towards the king, followed by five hundred valorous warriors. Even after the defeat, Bhagadatta had with him thousands of warriors on the third day. Prthviraja summoned Mayavarma in the early morning and said to him- “O excellent one, you reach in the battlefield with a lakh of your soldiers and your ten sons for the destruction of the enemies.” On hearing these words, the monarch indicated his arrival in the battlefield with the sounding of the war band. Observing them, the king Parimala too commanded the fearless leader Jaganayaka-“Accompanied with the ten thousand of your army and three warriors, you get ready to deal with these warriors in the battleground and work for my victory there.” On hearing this, all of them reached there in the battleground. О best of the sages, both the armies fought the terrific war for a prahara. But inspite of having been guarded by Udayasimha and others, the ten thousand warriors were killed in the battleground. Thereafter, the warriors of Anga country, blowing their own conches, declared victory for themselves. At that point of time, Udayasimha and other warriors reaching there within a prahara, killed a lakh of the enemy soldiers. In the afternoon, Mayavarma with his sons, Udayasimha and Devasimha besides Jaganayaka reached the battlefield. Then Udayasimha fought with Mayavarma of Angadesa riding over a horse. He kept on churning the enemy army. He was bom of the amsa of Madhusudana, subsequently, the lord of the Angadesa shot three arrows at back of Udayasimha's head. At that time, Udayasimha got enraged like a serpent, when hurt with a rod. He made his horse to fly in the air and when it reached over the chariot of the king of Anga, made the horse to kick the king of Angadesa with its hind legs, who fell down on the ground. Thereafter, the king took out his sword and attacked over the body of the horse and said to Udayasimha, “You had been victorious over many powerful kings, but I shall feel comfortable by completely destroying your unsteady illusion. Thereafter, my glory would spread in all the directions.” When the king was thus speaking, Udayasimha took out this sword and cut off the head of the king of Angadesa. With the severing of the head of the king of Anga country, his ten sons surrounded him and tried to create disturbance, but in the mean time, Indula killed five of his sons then and there. Two of his sons were killed by Devasimha with the attack of a spear. The eldest son was killed by Jaganayaka and the remaining two sons were killed by Udayasimha himself. Then in the evening time, blowing the conch, the warriors departed towards their camps. Because of their getting tired, they had a sound sleep at night and getting free from the essential routine in the morning, they reached the court of the king and said- “O ruler of the lunar race, who would be the chief commander for the day? You kindly tell us.”

## \|\| 2.135.118-126 \|\|

*śrutvāha bhūpodya tu vīrasenaḥ sakāmasenaḥ svabalaiḥ sametaḥ \|*  
*raṇaṃ kariṣyatyacireṇa vīrāstasmātsurakṣadhvamaribhya eva \|\| 118 \|\|*

*sa vīraseno nṛpatiṃ praṇamya lakṣaiḥ svasainyairyudhi saṃjagāma \|*  
*tadā mahīrājanṛpaḥ pratāpī sa nāgavarmāṇamuvāca tāpī \|\| 119 \|\|*

*raṇāya gacchāśu sutaiḥ sameto lakṣaiḥ svasainyairuta bhūpavarya \|*  
*hatvā ripuṃ ghoratamaṃ hi vīraṃ patiṃ mahāntaṃ yudhi vīrasenam \|\| 120 \|\|*

*ityuktavaṃtaṃ nṛpatiṃ praṇamya suvādayāmāsa tadā hi vīraḥ \|*  
*tayorbabhūvāśu raṇo mahānvai susenayoḥ saṃkulayuddhakartroḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

*triyāmamātreṇa hatāśca sarve vimānamāruhya yayuśca nākam \|*  
*hateṣu sarveṣu ca nāgavarmā suteṣu vai yādavabhūpamāha \|\| 122 \|\|*

*bhavānvisainyaśca tathaiva cāhaṃ bhavānsaputraśca tathāhameva \|*  
*saṃsmṛtya dharmaṃ kuru yuddhamāśu tato rathasthaḥ sudhanurgṛhītvā \|\| 123 \|\|*

*bāṇaiśca bāṇānbhuvi tau ca chittvā babhūvastustau virathau nṛpāgryau \|*  
*khaḍgena khaḍgaṃ ca tathaiva chittvā vimānamāruhya gatau hi nākam \|\| 124 \|\|*

*sa kāmasenaḥ svaripośca putrāñjaghāna bāṇaiśca tadāṣṭasaṃkhyān \|*

*ripoḥ śiro jahraturugravegī sa kāmasenaśca kabaṃdha eva \|*  
*hatvā ripū tau ca tadā militvā svargaṃ yayuste ca vimānarūḍhāḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

118-126. Hearing these words, the king said-“Virasena shall reach the battleground with Kamasena and other warriors today. Therefore, all of you should be careful in guarding him. When Virasena was offering his salutation to the king Parimala, at the same time the king Prthviraja called for the monarch Nagavarma and said to him- “O best of the rulers, you yourself, together with your sons and a lakh of soldiers, quickly reach the battleground and defeat the terrific enemy and attain victory over him.” On hearing these words, offering his salutation to the king, the king Virasimha made preparation for marching towards the battleground. Reaching there, both the armies fought a terrific war in which, within three praharas all the soldiers were killed and reached the heaven boarding a vimana or plane. After killing of all the soldiers, Nagavarma said to Virasena of Yaduvamsa- “Like you, I have also arrived here with my sons, getting deprived of the chariot. Therefore, for the sake of equality and dharma, you kindly start the war. Thereafter, both the warriors, using the bows and arrows, started shooting arrows at each other. After destroying the bow and arrows, they fought with swords and killed each other and then proceeded to the heaven, mounting over a plane.

*manorathastho jaganāyakaśca sa tālano vai vaḍavāṃ vigṛhya \|*  
*karālasaṃsthaśca tadā jayanto vigṛhya cāpaṃ tarasā jagāma \|\| 133 \|\|*

*papīhakasthaśca sa rūpaṇo vai jagāma kṛṣṇāṃśasamanvitaśca \|*

*samaṃtataḥ kinnarasainyaghoraṃ vināśayāmāsurupāṃśukhaḍgaiḥ \|*  
*vinaśyamāne trisahasrasainye sa kinnareśastarasā jagāma \|\| 135 \|\|*

*dhyātvā kuberaṃ ca gṛhītacāpo nabhogatastatra babhūva sūkṣmaḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

127-136. Thereafter, Kamasena killed eight of his sons with these arrows. Then the elder and younger brothers of the sons reached there and with the attack of their swords, cut off the head of Kamasena from his body. With the fall of the head of Kamasena on the ground, his headless trunk killed both of his enemies. In this way, all of them collectively boarding over a beautiful plane, left for the heaven. After the killing of all of them, Camu^a and his warriors surrounded Jananayaka from all the sides and started injuring his horse Harinagara. Thereafter, the divine horse, spreading its wings, flew in the sky killing the elephant of Dhundhukara as well as Camunda, and reduced to pieces the chariot of Bhagadatta. At that point of time, Jananayaka blowed the conch of victory. Then he went to Udayasimha who had narrated to him the whole story. At the end of the night, getting free from the daily routine, the warriors like Jananayaka and others marched towards the battlefield. At that point of time, Prthviraja summoned Mankana - the kinnar and said-“O kinnara king, you quickly reach the battlefield for the killing of my enemies. Today, the gods will fight with the humans, thought it has never been done earlier.” At these words spoken by him, together with his sons and the kinnara soldiers, the king Mankana went to the battlefield. Observing their arrival in the battlefield, the king Parimala commanded his warriors-“Jaganayaka should ride over the horse Manoratha, Talana should ride over the mare Simhini, Jayanta should ride over the horse Karala and march on without delay. Rupana should ride over the horse Papiha, Udayasimha should ride the elephant and Lallasimha over the horse. Dhanyapala and other soldiers were marching towards the battleground with their warriors. All these warriors reaching there, surrounded the kinnara warriors form all the sides and started wounding them. When three thousand of there soldiers were destroyed, Mankapa - the lord of kinnaras, hid himself in the sky and wounded the enemy warriors from the sky. With his horrible thunder and hard attack, all the enemy soldiers getting hurt, started crying. At the same time, the valorous Indula reached before the enemy.

## \|\| 2.135.137-154 \|\|

*adṛśyamānaḥ svaśaraiḥ kaṭhorairvinardya sarvānhi nanarda ghoram \|*  
*vilapyamāne ca samastaśūre jayanta evāśu jagāma śatruma \|\| 137 \|\|*

*dhyātvā maheṃdraṃ kaṇakaṃ ca baddhvā kṛṣṇāṃśamāgamya padau nanāma \|*  
*tadā tu te śatrusahasrasainye niśamya baddhaṃ kaṇakaṃ nijeṃdram \|\| 138 \|\|*

*vinargha ghoraṃ rurudhuśca sarvānmāyā vino guhyakamastramūhuḥ \|*  
*dineṣu sapteṣu tathā niśāsu babhūva yuddhaṃ ca samaṃtatastaiḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*śramānvitāḥ sapta mahāpravīrā hateṣu sarveṣu suṣupuśca vai yadā \|*  
*tadā kuberaṃ kaṇakaśca dhyātvā labdhvā varaṃ baṃdhanamāśu chittvā \|\| 140 \|\|*

*suptānsamutthāya ca sapta śūrānniśīthakāle sa cakāra yuddham \|*  
*jitvā ca tānṣaṭ sa varaprabhāvāttadeṃdulenaiva raṇaṃ cakāra \|\| 141 \|\|*

*gṛhītakhaḍgau raṇaghoramattau hatvā tato vai bhuvi ceyatuśca \|*  
*prajagmaturnākamupāntadevau saṃstūyamānau surasattamaiśca \|\| 142 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale vijāte ruroda rāmāṃśa utālalāpa \|*  
*pāpaiḥ kalāpaiḥ parīpīḍyamānaḥ kulānvitaḥ sarva yuto munīṃdra \|\| 143 \|\|*

*sa paṃcaśabdaṃ gajamāruroha trilakṣasainyaistarasā jagāma \|*  
*tadā mahīrāja utāha śṛṇvangacchadhvamadyaiva mayā sametāḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

*svapaṃcalakṣaiḥ prabalaiśca śūraiḥ sārddhaṃ rurodhāśu ripośca senām \|*  
*tayorbabhūvāśu raṇaḥ praghoro vinardatoryudanimittamāśu \|\| 145 \|\|*

*triyāma mātreṇa hatāśca sarve dvayośca pakṣā balaśālinaśca \|*  
*tadā mahīrāja utāyayau vai samaṃḍalīkaśca dhanurvigṛhya \|\| 146 \|\|*

*sa dhuṃdhukāraśca tadājagāma ratha sthitaṃ lakṣaṇamugravīram \|*  
*tadodayo vai bhagadattameva cāmuṃḍakaṃ bhīṣmakarājasūnuḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

*sa paṃcaśabdaṃ gajamāsthito vai gataḥ sa evāśu jagāma bhūpam \|*  
*dhanurvigṛhyāśugamulbaṇaṃ ca nṛpasthitaścātha bhayaṃkaraṃ ca \|\| 148 \|\|*

*gajaṃ pramattaṃ śivadattamugramāhlādahantāramuvāca vākyam \|*  
*aye pramattāgragajeṃdra śūra jayaṃ ca me dehi śivapradatta \|\| 149 \|\|*

*sa maṃḍalīko raṇadurmadaśca rāmāṃśa āhlāda iti prasiddhaḥ \|*  
*tasmācca māṃ rakṣa javena hastinmahābalātkāla rasācca vīrāt \|\| 150 \|\|*

*ityevamukto nṛpatiṃ sa hastī vacastamāhāśu śṛṇuṣva rājan \|*  
*yāvadahaṃ vai tanujīvadhārī tāvadbhavāñchatrubhayaṃkaraśca \|\| 151 \|\|*

*ityuktavaṃtaṃ ca gajaṃ pramattaṃ sa paṃcaśabdaśca tadā svadaṃtaiḥ \|*  
*mukhaṃ caturbhiśca vidārya śatrornanarda ghoraṃ sa maheṃdradattaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*sa rudradattaśca gajaḥ pramatto ruṣānvadhāvattarasā gajeṃdram \|*  
*ripuṃ svapadbhyāṃ ca cakhāna kuṃbhaiḥ svatuṃḍadaṃḍena tudaṃ prakurvan \|\| 153 \|\|*

*avāpa mūrchāṃ ca sa paṃcaśabdastadāśu bhūpaṃ prati maṃḍalīkaḥ \|*  
*svatomareṇāṃgavraṇaṃ pradāya khaḍgena hatvā gajarājamugram \|*  
*jagāma padbhyāṃ sa ripupramāthī yatra sthitaścendula ugradhanvā \|\| 154 \|\|*

137-154. Devoting his mind at Indra, he captured Mankana, who was sent to Udayasimha and then touched his feet. The kinnara warriors, finding their lord in bondage, made use of their secret weapons. As a result of this, the war continued unabated for a week with the distraction of the warriors in the battlefield. When the soldiers were getting upset after the killing of the seven great warriors, Mankana mentally adored Kubera and got a boon from him and then shattered his own bondages. At the dead of night, when all the warriors were asleep, the enemy soldiers started fighting with them. After defeating the most influential warriors, Mankana started fighting with Indula with sword. Getting intoxicated, both of them attacked each other with swords, as a result of which both of them were getting eulogized by others. О best of the sages, in the early morning, when the news of the death of Indula reached Ahlada, he cried aloud. Thereafter, leading an army of three lakhs of soldiers, he mounted over the elephant Pancasabda and rushed to the battlefield. Prthviraja on the other hand, commanded his valorous warriors to march with him towards the battleground.” At the command of the great king, he accompanied with five lakhs of his soldiers, arrived in the battleground and surrounded the enemy army from all the sides. Thundering aloud, both the great warriors were fighting themselves. In the three praharas of the war, the warriors of both the sides were killed and wounded. At that point of time, holding their own bows and arrows, Prthviraja and Ahlada arrived in the battleground. In this war, the king Laksana fought with Dhundhukara, Udayasimha fought with Bhagadatta and Devasimha with Camunda. Seated over Pancasabda elephant, he commanded Mattagajendra - “O Gajendra gifted by lord Siva, I should be victorious in the battlefield. You should protect me from the horrible enemy known by the name of Ahlada. О great elephant, he is the death for me.” At these words of the king, the elephant replied to him- “O king, you must accept my words. Till such time I remain alive in this body, you would be terrorsome for your enemies.” When these words were spoken by that elephant, then the enemy elephant that had been given by Mahendra, was tom out with his four tusks by the Pancasabda elephant. Thereafter, the elephant which had been given by lord Rudra, with the attacks of his trunk crushed it under his feet and made the enemy elephant senseless. When the enemy elephant was fainted, then making use of his weapon tomara Ahlada wounded the body of Prthviraja, besides attacking the elephant with his sword. Thereafter, Ahlada - the killer of the enemies, marched on foot from that place and reached the place where the body of his son Indula was lying.

## \|\| 2.135.155-172 \|\|

*utthāpya putraṃ ca vilapyamānāṃ patnīṃ svakīyāṃ prati cājagāma \|*  
*tadā pramattau ca gajau samūrchāṃ tyaktvā punaścakratureva yuddham \|\| 155 \|\|*

*sa lakṣaṇaḥ khaḍgavareṇa bāṇānripośca chittvā nijavaiṣṇavāstram \|*  
*dadhāra cāpe ca sumaṃtrayitvā sadhuṃdhukāraṃ ca gajaṃ dadāha \|\| 156 \|\|*

*hate ca tasminnijamukhyabaṃdhau sabhūmirājaśca gṛhītacāpaḥ \|*  
*śareṇa raudreṇa ca lakṣaṇaṃ taṃ jaghāna tatrādibhayaṃkarasthaḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

*sa mūrchitaḥ śukla kuleṣu sūryastadodayo vai bhagadattameva \|*  
*sumūrchayitvā ca jagāma śīghraṃ yatra sthito lakṣaṇa ekavīraḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

*bhayānvitastaṃ ca vilokya rājā javena dudrāva ca raktabījam \|*  
*tadā sudevaṃ ca sa raktabījo jitvā tu kṛṣṇāṃśayutaṃ jagāma \|\| 159 \|\|*

*bāṇena śīghraṃ sa ca mūrcchayitvā punaśca devaṃ ca sa mūrchayitvā \|*  
*tadbaṃdhanāyodyata āśukārī sa lakṣaṇastatra tadā jagāma \|\| 160 \|\|*

*pradhāya cāpe ca sa vaiṣṇavāstraṃ pracodayāmāsa ca raktabīje \|*  
*tadā sa sāmantasuto balīyānraṇaṃ vihāyāśu vilokya saṃdhyām \|*  
*bhayānvitaḥ svaiśca yuto yayau vai yatra sthitā bhūpatayaḥ sakopāḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*vilokya śatruṃ ca sa ratnabhānoḥ suto yayau vai śibirāṇi yuktaḥ \|*  
*niśāmya bhūpaḥ sa ca caṃdravaṃśī jayaṃ svakīyaṃ suṣupustu te vai \|*  
*prātaśca kāle sa ca caṃdravaṃśī vilokya śuklānvayamāha bhūpam \|\| 162 \|\|*

*aye gu्rjaradeśīya mūlavarmansutaiḥ saha \|*  
*lakṣasainyānvito bhūtvā gantumarhatu vai bhavān \|\| 163 \|\|*

*ityuktaḥ sa tu bhūpālo yuddhabhūmimupāyayau \|*  
*mahīrājājñayā prāpto nāmnā pūrṇāmalo balī \|\| 164 \|\|*

*daśaputrānvito yuddhe sainya lakṣeṇa saṃyutḥ \|*  
*tayoścāsīnmahadyuddhaṃ yāmadvayamupasthitam \|\| 165 \|\|*

*hateṣu teṣu sarveṣu tau nṛpau sasutairbalau \|*  
*anonyena raṇaṃ kṛtvā yamaloka mupāgatau \|\| 166 \|\|*

*mārgakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ prabhāte vimale ravau \|*  
*kaikayo lakṣasenāḍhyo dayāputrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*lakṣaṇānujñayā prāptastasminyudhi bhayānake \|\| 167 \|\|*

*madrakeśastadā rājā daśaputrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*lakṣasainyānvitastatra yatra yuddhaṃ samanvabhūt \|*  
*parasparaṃ hatāḥ sarve dinānte kṣatriyā raṇe \|\| 168 \|\|*

*punaḥ prabhāte vimale bhagadatto mahābalī \|*  
*trilakṣabalasaṃyukto jagarjja raṇamūrddhani \|\| 169 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ lakṣaṇo vīrastrilakṣabalasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*cakāra tumulaṃ ghoraṃ senayā ca svakīyayā \|\| 170 \|\|*

*aparāhṇe hatāḥ sarve sainikā nṛpayostadā \|*  
*bhagadattaḥ svayaṃ kruddho rathastho lakṣaṇaṃ yayau \|\| 171 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇo rathamāruhya svapituḥ śatrujaṃ nṛpam \|*  
*tribhirbāṇaiśca saṃtodya bhallena samatāḍayat \|\| 172 \|\|*

155-172. Reaching there, he lifted up his body and bitterly lamented. Thereafter, he carried his body and reached his wife who was waiting with grief. On the other hand, when the intoxicated elephants regained their senses, the war was started again. At that point of time, the arrogant Laksana, making use of the best of the swords, burnt out Dhundhukara with his elephant. On the other hand, at the death of the close relative, Prthviraja mounted over the immensely terrific elephant and shooting his terrific arrow, attacked Laksana by which the son of the lunar race was fainted. Then Udayasimha made Bhagadatta senseless and tried his best to reach Laksana, who was lying there alone. Finding their arrival, the king Prthviraja was panic stricken and rushed towards Raktabija. At that point of time, Raktabija had defeated Devasimha and reached before Udayasimha and made him senseless. Devasimha was also brought back to senses. Finding him there, Laksana who was well-versed in waging of war, reached there and placing the vaisnavastra over the bow, challenged Raktabija. At that point of time, Raktabija - the son of a Samanta, observing the arrival of evening time and getting frightened, fled away from the battleground and he hid himself among the other rulers, who had collected there in great anger. Finding that the enemy was fleeing, Laksana - the son of Bhanu, returned to his camp. At that point of time, the king Parimala of lunar race felt delighted at his victory. Then his people went to sleep. In the early morning, after finishing the daily routine, Parimala of the lunar race said to king of his own race-“Mulavarma is the lord of Gujarata country. With his sons and a lakh of his army, he should march towards the battleground.” At this command of the king, the king marched on to the battleground. On the other hand, the king Prthviraja commanded the valorous Purnamala that together with a lakh of his army soldiers and ten sons, he should reach the battleground. Both the warriors fought a terrific war upto the noon time, in which a large number of warriors of both the sides were killed. After the killing of the warriors, both the kings attacked each other with their sons and departed for the heaven. On the fourteenth dark day of the month of Margasisa, on the rising of the spotless sun in the morning, the king Kaikeya with a lakh of his army and the sons, reached the battleground. At that point of time, the king Madrakesa also, together with his ten sons and a lakh of soldiers, marched on for fighting the war. In the battleground, a terrific battle was fought between both the armies. By the evening time, a large number of Ksatriyas of both the sides attacking one another, were killed and proceeded on to the heaven. On the next day, the valorous Bhagadatta with three lakh of his army soldiers, reached in the battleground. Finding that, the valorous Laksana too, with his own warriors, reached there and started the war.

*sārddhaṃ jagāma yuddhāya tathā vyūhyāyudhadripūn \|\| 179 \|\|*

*tatonujaḥ pravīraśca śrīpatiṃ so'yutaissaha \|*  
*nṛpaḥ sūryo dharo vīro'yutāḍhayo balavānraṇe \|*  
*śrītāraṃ nṛpamāsādya mahadyuddhamacīkarat \|\| 182 \|\|*

*vāmanoyutasaṃyukto mukuṃdaṃ prati so'gamat \|*  
*gaṃgāsiṃhaśca balavānmahilaṃ prati sāyutaḥ \|\| 183 \|\|*

*lallasiṃhoyutaissārddhaṃ guhilaṃ prati so'gamat \|*  
*triśatāni tato bhūpāḥ sahasrāḍhyāḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 184 \|\|*

*kṣudrabhūpāḥ kṣudrabhūpāṃstriśatāni samāyayuḥ \|*  
*anyonyena hatāḥ sarve kṛtvā yuddhaṃ bhayānakam \|\| 185 \|\|*

172-185. In the afternoon, the soldiers of both the sides had been killed, fighting with one another. Thereafter, mounting over a chariot, Bhagadatta reached before the chariot of Laksana. Laksana also found his ancestral enemy, attacked him with arrows as well the spears. On other hand, getting enraged, Bhagadatta deprived the opponent of his chariot. Finding him enraged and robber like enemy, Laksana killed his horses and the charioteer and faced Bhagadatta himself. On the other hand, using his sword, Balakhana destroyed the kavaca - shield of the son of Bhagadatta, cut off his body into three parts. When the enemy was killed during the evening, then riding over the elephant, Laks ana returned to his camp. At the death of Bhagadatta, Prthviraja getting extremely enraged, sent all the rulers together with Camunda to the battlefield. On the bright first day of the month of Margasirsa, a great war was fought by the great rulers who has assembled in the battlefield, in which from the side of Prthviraja, Angada, Kalinga’s ruler, Trikona, Sripati, Sritara, Mukunda, Ruhila, Guhila, Suketu and ninety thousand soldiers, besides nine kings assembled there. The military bands were being played upon on the occasion of the war festival. Observing that, the valorous Laksana also, with his rulers, reached the battleground and made the army formations surrounding the enemies. In this battle, the king Rudravarma, together with his ten thousand warriors, was fighting with the king Angada. Similarly, accompanied with ten thousand soldiers Kalivarma fought with Kalinga. Then Virasimha fought with Trikona with an equal number of soldiers, his younger brother known as Pravira fought with Sripati and the valorous king Suryadhara leading an army of ten thousand soldiers fought a horrible war with Sritara. Mukunda fought with Vamana, Mahila fought with Gangasimha and Guhila fought with Lallasimha. Each one of them had ten thousand soldiers with them. Among them were six hundred small rulers as well, who fighting furiously, got destroyed there.

## \|\| 2.135.186-205 \|\|

*cāmuṃḍastu tadā dṛṣṭvā mṛtakānsarvabhūpatīn \|*  
*lakṣaṇāntamupāgamya mahadyuddhaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 186 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇo raktabījaṃ taṃ jñātvā brāhmaṇasaṃmatam \|*  
*vaiṣṇavāstraṃ tadā tasmai na dadau tena pīḍita \|\| 187 \|\|*

*sāyaṃkāle tu saṃprāpte lakṣaṇo hastinīsthitaḥ \|*  
*ekākī śiviraṃ prāptaścāmuṃḍaṃ nṛpamāyayau \|\| 188 \|\|*

*dvitīyāyāṃ prabhāte ca kṛṣṇāṃśo devasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*śūrairdaśasahasraiśca yuddhabhūmimupāyayau \|\| 189 \|\|*

*tārakaśca sacāmuṃḍo dvilakṣabalasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*dviśataiśca tathā bhūpaiḥ sārddhaṃ yuddhamupasthitau \|\| 190 \|\|*

*puraskṛtya nṛpānsarvānsasainyau balavattarau \|*  
*teṣāmanu sthitau yuddhe tatra jāto mahāraṇaḥ \|\| 191 \|\|*

*yāmamātreṇa tau vīrau hatvā sarvamahīpatīn \|*

*tābhyāṃ śramānvitābhyāṃ ca cakratustau samaṃ raṇam \|\| 193 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ triyāmamātreṇa saṃbabhūva mahānraṇaḥ \|*  
*sāyaṃkāle tu saṃprāpte kṛṣṇāṃśaśca nirāyudhaḥ \|*  
*talaprahāreṇa ripuṃ mūrcchayāmāsa vīryavān \|\| 194 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare vīrastārako devasiṃhakam \|*  
*hayaṃ manorathaṃ hatvā śaṃkhaśabdamathākarot \|\| 195 \|\|*

*tacchabdātsa ca cāmuṃḍastyaktvā mūrchāṃ mahābalaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃśasya śiraḥ kāyādapahṛtya ca vegavān \|*  
*tayorgṛhītvā śirasī mahīrājamupāyayau \|\| 196 \|\|*

*mahīrājastu te dṛṣṭvā paramānaṃdanirbharaḥ \|*  
*dattvā dānaṃ dvijātibhyo mahotsavamakārayat \|\| 197 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇasya tadā sainye hāhāśabdo mahānabhūt \|*  
*śrutvā kolāhalaṃ teṣāṃ jñātvā tau ca hatau nṛpaḥ \|*  
*brahmānaṃdastadā mūrcchāṃ tyaktvā velāmuvāca ha \|\| 198 \|\|*

*priye gaccha raṇaṃ śīghraṃ harināgaramāsthitā \|*  
*mama veṣaṃ śubhaṃ kṛtvā tārakaṃ jahi mā ciram \|\| 199 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu sā velā rāmāṃśena samanvitā \|*  
*sahasraśūrasahitā yuddhabhūmimupāyayau \|\| 200 \|\|*

*śrutvā sa lakṣaṇo vīrastālanena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*sainyaiśca daśasāhasrairmahīrājamupāyayau \|\| 201 \|\|*

*tṛtīyāyāṃ prabhāte ca tārako balavattaraḥ \|*  
*brahmānaṃdaṃ ca taṃ matvā mahadyuddhamacī karat \|\| 202 \|\|*

*raktabījaśca cāmuṃḍo rāmāṃśo balavattaraḥ \|*  
*cakāra dāruṇaṃ yuddhaṃ tasminvīrasamāgame \|\| 203 \|\|*

*yāmamātreṇa rāmāṃśo hatvā tasya mahāgajam \|*  
*tacchastrāṇi tathā cchitvā mallayuddhamacīkarat \|\| 204 \|\|*

*triyāmamātreṇa tadā sāyaṃkāle samāgate \|*  
*mamaṃtha bhrātṛhantāraṃ sa ca vīro mamāra ha \|\| 205 \|\|*

186-205. Observing the death of these rulers, Camunda reached before Laksana and fought a horrible war with him. Even after having been injured badly by him. Laksana did not use his vaisnava weapon on him, since he happened to be a Brahmana. During the evening time, Laksana mounted over a cow-elephant and returned to his camp alone, while Camunda reached in the camp of Prthviraja. On the second day of the moon, in the early morning, together with Devasimha, Udayasirnha leading an army of ten thousand soldiers, he reached the battleground. On the other hand, Taraka and Camunda also, with two lakhs of their army, reached there. Making other rulers to march forward, the prominent warriors of both the sides, with their soldiers following them, fought a horrible war on that particular day in which within a prahara, Udayasimha and Devasimha destroyed all those rulers and also a lakh of their soldiers. Thereafter, getting tired, they started resting. Then the wicked Taraka, accompanied with Camunda, started fighting with the tired soldiers. Both the sides fought a pitched battle for three praharas. At the evening time, Udayasimha was left with no weapon. But even in that condition, he hit the enemy with hand, who fell down unconscious. In the meantime, Taraka killed Devasimha with his horse named Manoratha, and he blew his conch thereafter, hearing which the valorous Camunda regained his consciousness and in anger, cut off the head of Udayasimha from his body. Thereafter, carrying the heads of both of them, both of them reached before Prthviraja, who felt delighted at the sight. Then he gave away the desired charities to the Brahmanas and arranged festivities. When Laksana came to know about the death of both the warriors, his army became panicky and tumultuous noise was created. Listening to the tumultuous sound, Brahmananda regained his senses and spoke to Vela - “O dear, riding over the horse named Harinagara, you at once reach the battleground. Taking to my form, you go and at once kill Taraka. Don’t delay.” Hearing these words, Vela accompanied with Ahlada and a thousand soldiers, reached the battlefield. Hearing the news, Laksana and Talana with ten thousand warriors, reached before Prthviraja. On the third day of the moon, Taraka taking Vela to be Brahmananda, fought a terrific war with him. Raktabija-Camunda also fought with Ahlada who was the amsa of Rama. Within a prahara, Ahlada killed his elephant and also destroyed all his weapons. Thereafter, both of them were engaged in a wrestling fight which continued for three praharas. In the evening time, churning Camunda - the killer of his brother, Ahlada killed him.

*mahīrājamupāgamya mahadyuddhamakārayat \|\| 210 \|\|*

*dhānyapālaḥ śataṃ bhūpāṃllakṣaṇaśca tathā śatam \|*  
*tālanaśca śataṃ bhūpānhatvā rājānamāyayau \|\| 212 \|\|*

*mahīrājastadā duḥkhī dhyātvā rudraṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*niśīthe samanuprāpte hataśeṣaissamāgataḥ \|*

*lakṣaṇāntamupāgamya mahadyuddhamacīkarat \|\| 214 \|\|*

*tadā tu lakṣaṇo vīro vaiṣṇavāstraṃ samādadhe \|*  
*tenāstreṇa kṣayaṃ jāto mahīrājasya sāyakaḥ \|*  
*tenāstratejasā rājā mahāsaṃtāpamāptavān \|\| 216 \|\|*

*dhyātvā rudraṃ mahādevaṃ tyaktvā vidyāṃ ca vaiṣṇavīm \|*  
*svabhallena śiraḥ kāyādapāharata bhūmipaḥ \|\| 217 \|\|*

*hastinī ca tadā ruṣṭā gajamādibhayaṃkaram \|*  
*gatvā yuddhaṃ muhūrtena kṛtvā svargamupāyayau \|\| 218 \|\|*

*uṣaḥkāle ca saṃprāpte malanā patimuttamam \|*  
*taccitāyāṃ samāropya dadāha svaṃ kalevaram \|\| 219 \|\|*

*tadā tu devakī śuddhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ balavattaram \|*  
*tālanādīṃstathā hutvā dadāha svaṃ kalevaram \|\| 220 \|\|*

*prabhāte vimale jāte caturthe bhaumavāsare \|*  
*tathā hutvā svarṇavatī kṛtvā teṣāṃ tilāṃjalim \|*  
*dhyātvā sarvamayīṃ devīṃ sthirībhūya svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 221 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare tatra kalirbhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*vāṃchitaṃ phalamāgamya tuṣṭāva ślakṣṇayā girā \|\| 222 \|\|*

206-222. Then Vela destroyed all the weapons of Taraka. She took up her sword and cut off the head of Taraka. Thereafter, the daughter of Drupada, with the permission of her fatherin-law, entered the funeral pyre of her husband. Then narrating the story of her living with her husband for seven births, she was reduced to ashes with her husband. At the same time, the wife of Indula also ended her life with her husband. During the same night, getting grieved, the king Parimala reached before Prthviraja with Laksana and fought with him a terrific war. At that point of time, they were left with only a lakh and twenty five thousand warriors. The king Parimala had three lakhs of soldiers. Dhanyapala, Laksana and Talana killed a hundred rulers each and went to the king Prthviraja. Then the king Prthviraja, feeling painful and grieved, at the dead of night, devoting his mind to lord Mahesvara, together with the rest of his soldiers, mounted the elephant alone and started fighting. With the arrows that he had received from lord Siva, he killed Dhanapala and Talana reached before Laksana. Reaching there, he fought a terrific battle. With the use of Raudrastra, several of the rulers were killed. Thereafter, in order to attack over Laksana, Prthviraja took up the Raudrastra, while Laksana took up his Vcii§nava weapon by which the weapon of Prthviraja became infructuous and the king had to face unbearable heat of the same. Thereafter, Prthviraja meditated upon Rudra and using the Bhallastra, he severed his head from the body. At that point of time, the cowelephant of Laksana getting enraged, defeated Gaja and others in a muhurta itself and departed for the heaven. Thereafter, at dawn, the queen Malana entered the funeral pyre with her husband reducing her own body to ashes. At the same time, Devaki also placed the bodies of Laksana and Talana in the same pyre and reduced her body too to ashes. On the fourth day of Tuesday, Ahlada put the body of his dead wife in the same pyre and offering oblation for the dead, meditating upon the all pervading goddess, he sat in mediation. At the same time, Kali with his wife arrived there and for the success of his desire, started offering prayer to her in a humble voice.

*nama āhlāda mahate sarvānaṃdapradāyine \|*  
*yogeśvarāya śuddhāya mahāvatīnivāsine \|\| 223 \|\|*

*kalaikayā samāgamya bhuvo bhārastvayā hṛtaḥ \|\| 224 \|\|*

*rājānaḥ pāvakīyāśca tapobalasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*hatvā tānpañcasāhasrānkṣudrabhūpānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*yogamadhye samāsīno namastasmai mahātmane \|\| 225 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ sainyāḥ ṣaṣṭilakṣāḥ kramādvīra tvayā hatāḥ \|*

*tasya netre mayā śuddhe kartavye nīlarūpake \|\| 228 \|\|*

*tava priyaḥ sadā nīlastathaiva ca mama priyaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ duḥkhado deva daityānāṃ harṣavarddhanaḥ \|\| 229 \|\|*

*ityuktvā sa tu rāmāṃśo gajamāruhya vegataḥ \|*  
*mahīrājamupāgamya mahadyuddhaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 230 \|\|*

*rudradatto gajastūrṇaṃ paṃcaśabdamupasthitaḥ \|*

*keśeṣu ca mahīrājaṃ gṛhītvā tarasā balī \|*  
*kalidattaṃ mahānīlaṃ netrayostena tatkṛtam \|\| 234 \|\|*

*nirāhāro yatirbhūtvā mṛtaḥ svargapuraṃ yayau \|*

*tadā mlecchassahoḍḍīno nirbaṃdhanamathākarot \|*

*kṣurapreṇa ca bāṇena hatvā vahnau dadāha vai \|\| 246 \|\|*

*vidyunmālāṃ sa ca mleccho gṛhītvā ca dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*tatrāsthāpya svadāsaṃ ca kutukoḍḍīnamāgataḥ \|\| 247 \|\|*

223-247. Kali said- “Being blissful, you bestow all the bliss. Salutation to you, O great Ahlada. You had been a Yogesvara and lives in Mahavati in an auspicious manner. O long armed one, you have incarnated on earth as the amsa of Sri Rama and are bent upon bringing me up. You have reduced the weight of the earth by killing five thousand rulers of Agnivamsa. Thereafter, you have absorbed yourself in yogic meditation or yoga-dhyana. I am offering my salutation to a great personality like you. O excellent one, after displaying your astonishing prowess, you have destroyed sixty lakhs of the enemy army. Therefore, you beg for a desired boon.” On hearing these words, Ahlada said fearlessly-“O Deva, you be kind enough to spread my glory to all the people. I shall again try to fulfil all the tasks entrusted by you to me, but you kindly listen to my words. O Deva, the king Prthviraja is a religious-minded king besides being the devotee of Siva and Sakti. Therefore, I want to bestow him the blue eyes, since he is your favourite. He has caused pain to me and delighted the daityas,” Thus speaking, Ahlada - the amsa of Rama, mounting over his elephant, rushed to fight with Prthviraja, with great force. Reaching there, he started fighting with Prthviraja. At the same time, the elephant named Rudradatta placed the weight of both his front legs over the tusks of Gajendra known as Pancasabda and fought with it forcefully. After both of them were killed by Ahlada, they proceeded on to the heaven. The king Prthviraja, getting panic stricken at that time, fled with great speed from the battlefield. But Ahlada rushed after and caught him. Then making use of the blue powder given to him by Kali, he turned the eyes of Prthviraja as blue. At the same time, taking him to be inauspicious, lord Siva left left for Kailasa - the dwelling place of the Guhyakas. Together with Kali, Ahlada also went to the Kadalivana or the Banana forest and started the yogic meditation. Finding him engaged in yogic practices, the delighted Kali went to Bali and narrated to him the entire sequence of events. At that point of time, Bali - the lord of daityas, together with his ten thousand warriors, went to another country and said to Sahoddina- “I shall keep on guarding you. You come with me tonight itself, defeat Prthviraja and abduct Vidyunmala” On hearing this, together with a lakh and five thousand soldiers, he started for Kuruksetra. Sixteen days were spent in journey, then he became victorious over Prthviraja and his sons. Thereafter, he went to Mahavati. There, in association with Mahipati, he plundered the riches of the place. The king Lingartha did his best in Kirtisagara, but he could not be successful. Per force he returned his home and performed the Laksacandi homa and fell delighted. Hearing that, Jayacandra feeling grieved for the death of his son, started fasting taking to the form of a mendicant. As a result of this, he had to proceed to heaven in a short time. On the other hand, Prthviraja fought a terrific war with Sahoddina who was captured on the seventh day. He tried his best to kill him, but was unable to do so. In the meantime, under compulsion, Sahoddina freed him from the bondage. Then at the command of the king Prthviraja, Candrabhatta produced the sacred flame there and shooting him with a sharp arrow, cremated him in the same fire. Thereafter, the king of Mlecchas, plundering enough of wealth from his country and kidnapping Vidyunmala, entrusted the care of the kingdom to one of his soldiers named Kutubuddina and himself returned to his country.

## Pratisargaparva Part 4

## Chapter 136. Description of Pramara Vamsa

## \|\| 2.136.1-10 \|\|

1-10. Vedavyasa said- “At the time of the end of Dvapara and at the start of Kali, the way in which the kings of the solar and lunar races were described, the same has been narrated by me. The way in which Suta, going to the city of Visala, would recite collateral history of the country, the same auspicious history has also been narrated to you. At the invitation of king Vikramaditya, the eighteen Puranas which would again be narrated by the sage Suta, would be popular in the age of Kali. The gist of the eighteen Upa-Puranas history has been contained in twelve chapters. The same as well as the details about the incarnation of the lord who would appear on earth in a partial manner, would be known as the partial incarnations of the sakti of Radhakrsna. Lord Suta would reach in the Naimisaranya and shall narrate the relevant stories to eighty eight thousand Rsis. The same auspicious stories have also been repeated before you. Saunaka and other great Rsis of the Naimisarnya, getting relieved of the routine of daily bath etc., shall go to sage Suta and then pray to him. Whatever reply would be given to them by Suta, the same is going to be repeated by me.”

## \|\| 2.136.11-12 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ kṛṣṇasya caritaṃ bhagavanbhavatoditam \|*  
*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi rājñāṃ teṣāṃ kramātkulam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*caturṇāṃ vahnijātānāṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ \|*  
*sa haristriyugī proktaḥ kathaṃ jātaḥ kalau yuge \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The Rsis said- “We have very well heard the life story of the rising lord Krsna. Presently, we would like to listen to the life story of the rulers of the Agnivamsa or fire race. Besides the lord, who is known as of three yugas, how did he incarnate on earth in the age of Kali?”

*sūta uvāca \|*

*tatra gopāndasyugaṇānvaśīkṛtya mahābalī \|*

13-20. Suta said - О best of the sages, you have put up an excellent question. I shall surely give the answer to you. Besides I shall exhaustively narrate the story of the rulers of fire race. The king Pramara lived in an auspicious and divine city, which had been built by the goddess Ambika. The king who had been the follower of Samaveda, had a son after the completion of his rule for six years, who was known as Mahamara. After three years of his rule, a son named Devapi was bom to him. He ruled the country for the same period as his father ruled. О sage, he had a son named Devaduta. He also ruled the country for the same period as his father did. I am speaking out the cause for the same. You please listen. After the death of the valorous king Asoka, Kali adored the Sungod. On the fifth year of his tapasya, the Sungod getting pleased with him, bestowed a son to him, who came to be known as Saka. At that point of time, Kali feeling delighted, built a city named Taittira for noble Saka. While living there, the valorous Saka subjugated the cowherds and the robbers and repeatedly tried to subjugate the Arya country. As a result of this, the large numbers of the Aryana rulers were killed. Therefore, they are said to have been short lived.

*gaṃdharvasenaśca nṛpo devadūtātmajo balī \|*

*tataḥ kṣudhāturo rājā śvaviṣṭhādhānyagarhitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*saṃskṛtya maṃdire rājā śālagrāmāya cārpayat \|*

*kṛtvā dadau varaṃ tasmai śṛṇu tanmunisattama \|*

21-30. Baliraja’s Gandharvasena - the son of Devaduta, after occupying the throne for fifty years, left for the performing of tapas. When lord Siva was pleased with him, he was blessed with a son named Vikram", who ruled his country for a hundred years. He got a son named Devabhakta, who ruled the country for ten years and was subsequently killed by the Sakas. The said Devabhakta had a son named Salivahana, who ruled for sixty years and subjugated Sakas. Thereafter, he proceeded on to the heaven. He had a son named Salihotra, who proceeded to the heaven after ruling for a period of fifty years. He had a son named Salivardhana who had a son named Sakahanta. Sakahanta had a son named Suhotra, while Havirhotra was the son of Suhotra. Havirhotra had a son named Indrapala, who built a city named Indravati and ruled over it. During the rule of this king, there were no rains for four years. During that period, suffering from hunger, the king made food items from the cereals produced out of the refuse and offered the same to lord Saligrama, as a result of which the lord getting pleased, granted him a boon by means of the voice originating from the sky. I am going to tell you about the same, you please listen. The divine voice said- “O best of the rulers, till such time the rulers of your race shall occupy the throne, upto that time there would never be any loss of rains in your excellent country.” Thereafter, by the grace of lord Siva, he got a son named Sambhudatta.

31-44. He had a son named Bhaumaraja. Bhaumaraja had a son named Vatsaraja, while Vatsaraja had a son named Bhojaraja. Bhojaraja had a son named Sambhudatta, who ruled the country for a period lesser than his father. Sambhudatta had a son named Bindupala, who established a country named Bindukhanda. He ruled the country comfortably for the same period as ruled by his father. O sage, Bindupala had a son named Rajapala. Mahinara was the son of Rajapala, while Somavarma was the son of Mahinara. Kamavarma was the son of Somavarma. A son named Bhumipala was born to Kamavarma, who dug up a lake on earth and made a beautiful city as well. He had a son named Rangapala or Bhumipala. He become victorious over many rulers, because of which he came to be known as Virasimha. In due course of time, he established his son over his throne and himself proceeded on to the forest for the performing of tapas, where because of the pleasure of the great lord, he attained the heaven. The excellent king Rangapala had a son named Kalpasimha. The period of rule of all these rulers was the same as their ancestors. Kalpasimha was issueless, but he ruled the country for the same period as his father did. Once feeling delighted, they went on pilgrimage to have a bath in the holy river of Ganga. He took his bath there and distributed charities to the Brihmanas and then proceeded on to Kalpaksetra. Finding the sacred land barren there, he built a beautiful city there, which was known by the name of the city of Kalapa. While ruling there, he got a son who became popular by the name of Gangasimha and who inspite of his being childless, ruled for a period of ninety years. Thereafter, he went to Kuruksetra and fighting there in the war, achieved the heaven. Thus the auspicious race of the Pramaras came to an end.

45-46. Thereafter, the ladies of their race developed contact with other Ksatriyas as a result of which the mixed generation was bom. The generation of the mixed breed following the Vaisyas living with Mlecchas spent their lives. О Brahmanas, thus I have narrated the vamsas of the southern rulers.

## Chapter 137. Pramara Vamsa described

*sūta uvāca \|*

*iṃdraprasthaṃ dadau tasmai prasanno nagaraṃ śivaḥ \|*

*tomarāvarajaścaiva cayahānisutaḥ śubhaḥ \|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ vīrasiṃhastato'bhavat \|*  
*śatārddhābdaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tato biṃdusuro'bhavat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*piturarddhaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ madhyadeśe mahātmanā \|*

*vikramāya dadau vīrāṃ pitā vedavidhānataḥ \|*  
*svaputrāya svakaṃ rājyaṃ madhyadeśāntaraṃ mudā \|\| 9 \|\|*

1-9. Suta said- The king Vayahani who had been the ruler of the region of Madhyadesa, on his occupying the throne, made Ajmera as his capital city, which was built by Brahma. Ajanma and his mother Laksmi who had the cooperation of Rama, had well arrived there and the city was built. Because of the same, it came to be known as Ajmera. After ruling for a period of ten years, he got a son named Tomara, who worshipped lord Mahesvara in the form of clay figure. Getting pleased with his worship, lord Siva granted him the city named Indraprastha. Since that time, the future generation of his race came to be known as Tomaras. The son of Cayahani who was the son of the younger brother of Tomara, became popular by the name of Samala on earth. After ruling for seven years, he got a son named Mahadeva. Mahadeva had a son named Ajaya who had a son named Vlrasimha, who ruled on earth for half a century. The remaining rulers ruled on earth for the same period as the fathers did. The noble king Bindusara, who was the son of Virasimha, continued to rule the country for half the period for which his father ruled. He got twins comprising of a son named Vira and a daughter named Vira. The father of the daughter married her as per Vedic rites. Thereafter, getting delighted, he established his son in his place who ruled the country for the same period as his father did. The noble king Bindusara, who was the son of Virasimha, ruled the country of Madhyadesa for half the period for which his father ruled.

10-16. The king thereafter had a son named Manikya, who ruled the country for a period of fifty years. Thereafter, he got a son named Mahasimha and Candragupta was bom as son of Mahasimha, who ruled for half the period for which his father ruled. All the rest of the aforesaid rulers ruled for the same period as their fathers did so. Candragupta had a son named Pratapa and Pratapa had a son named Mohana, who could rule only for three years. The rest of the rulers ruled the country like their ancestors. Thereafter, he got a son named Svetaraya, who had a osn named Nagavahana. Lohadhara was the son of Nagavahana, while Virasimha was bom to Lohadhara. Virasimha had a son named Vibudha, who ruled the country for a period of fifty years. The rest of the rulers ruled for the same period, as was done by their forefathers. Again, Vibudha had a son named Candraraya, while Harihara was bom as son to Candraraya. Vasanta was bom to Harihara, while Balanga was bom to Vasanta.

Jayasimha was bom to Mantradeva, who ruled the country for a period of fifty years and conquered the entire Arya country. By collecting the enormous riches, he performed a great yajna.

21-28. Thereafter, he got a son named Anandadeva. The valorous Somesvara was born as a son to Anandadeva, who married the eldest daughter of Anangapala known by the name of Kirtimalini, who produced three sons. The eldest son was known by the name of Dhundhukara who was the king of Mathura. The middle son was known by the name of Kumara, who inherited the throne of his father. The youngest son was known by the name of Prthviraja, who after establishing himself as the king of Dehali, ended his life after having been defeated by the Mleccha king Sahoddina. He caused the total destruction of Cayahani dynasty. The Mleccha king enjoyed the wives of the remaining rulers as a result of which mixed generation was produced. Some of the Ksatriyas of that time who had been wandering here and there, were not included in the Mleccha or Jaffa castes or Mehanas, because they had all been mixed. At that point of time, only Mehanas, Mlecchas and Jattas were believed to be the Aryans.

## Chapter 138. Pramara Vamsa described

## \|\| 2.138.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śuklavaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu vipravarāditaḥ \|*  
*yadā kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ brahma tyaktvā bhūmiṃ svakaṃ padam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*divyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ prayayau bhūtale tadā \|*  
*kalerāgamanaṃ jñātvā mlecchapā dvīpamadhyage \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sthitā dvīpeṣu vai nānā manujā vedatatparāḥ \|*  
*kalinā mitradharmeṇa dūṣitāste babhūvire \|\| 3 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭisahasrāṇāṃ varṣāṇāṃ munisattama \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti vai jātaḥ kālaḥ kalisamāgame \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said - О excellent Brahmana, I am now going to describe the genesis of the Sukla-vamsa, which you please listen. When lord Krsna leaving his abode Vrndavana, proceeded on to his divine abode, at that point of time the followers of Vedic dharma refused to accept the slavery of the Mleccha rulers and started living in small islands. Even there, they were polluted by the followers of Kali desecrating their religious worship. О best of the sages, Kali had arrived on earth sixty eight thousand years back.

## \|\| 2.138.5-12 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi dvīparājyamacīkarat \|*

*tatpaścādbhārate varṣe mlecchayā kalirāyayau \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tadbhārataṃ varṣaṃ lokapālaiśca pālitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bhayabhītastvarāviṣṭo gandharvāṇāṃ yaśaskaraḥ \|*  
*sa kaliḥ sūryamārādhya samādhistho babhūva ha \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tato varṣaśatābdāṃte saṃtuṣṭo ravirāgataḥ \|*  
*soṃśubhirlokamātapya mahāvṛṣṭimakārayat \|\| 8 \|\|*

*caturvarṣasahasrāṇi caturvarṣaśatāni ca \|*

*saṃpannaṃ bhārataṃ varṣaṃ tadā jātaṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*

*sahasrābdakalau prāpte mahendro devarāṭ svayam \|*

*daśaputrānsamutpādya sa dvijo miśramāgamat \|\| 12 \|\|*

5-12. Не ruled in the islands for sixty thousand years. Thereafter, he worshipped the Sungod with Mlecchas. Thereafter, Kali arrived in Bharata with the Mlecchas. Finding the land of Bharata having been guarded by the Lokapalas, he was extremely frightened, but Kali, who was glorious among the Gandharvas, started meditating upon the Sungod. After the lapse of a hundred years, the Sungod getting pleased with his devotion, after scorching the earth with its rays dropped excessive rains on earth. О best of the sages, all this happened four thousand years ago. Thereafter, Bharatavarsa became self sufficient, because at that point of time, the earth was made self sufficient by Nyuha Yavana. After the lapse of a thousand years of Kali, Mahendra - the king of the gods, departed Каsуара to Brahmavarta. Holding in marriage the hand of Devasakti, he produced ten sons from her and then proceeded on to the country named Misra.

## \|\| 2.138.13-21 \|\|

*miśradeśodbhavānmlecchānvaśīkṛtyāyutaṃ mudā \|*

*naṣṭāyāṃ saptapuryāṃ ca brahmāvartaṃ mahottamam \|*

*svaputraṃ śuklamāhūya dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ tapodhanam \|*  
*ājñāya raivataṃ śṛṃgaṃ tapase tu punaḥ svayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*navaputrāṃstathā śiṣyānmanudharmaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*śrāvayāmāsa dharmātmā sa rājā manudharmagaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vāsudevaṃ jagannāthaṃ tapasā samatoṣayat \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavāndvāra kānāyako balī \|*

*dvārakāṃ kārayāmāsa hareśca kṛpayā hi saḥ \|*  
*tatroṣya mudito rājā kṛṣṇadhyānaparobhavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

13-21. Winning over ten thousand Mlecchas of that country, he returned to his own country and took them as his disciples. Subsequently, when all the seven priests had been destroyed in the auspicious land of Brahmavarta, which was located in between the Sarasvati and Drsadvati rivers, he commanded them to stay there. Thereafter, he commanded his son named Sukla - the best of Brahmanas as well as a great ascetic, to perform tapas over the Raivata mountain peak. The rest of his sons were made the householders. Following the dharma of Manu, he delivered to them the discourse of the dharma of Manu. On the other hand, reaching the Raivata mountain, Sukla pleased lord Vasudeva - Jagannatha. Then getting pleased with him, the valorous lord Jagannatha who was the form of Sat, Cit and Ananda, became pleased with his tap as. Getting pleased with him, the valorous Dverakadhisa, holding the hand of that Brahmana, entered the ocean and made him to have a look at the town of Dvaraka. О best of the race of Bhrgus, after the lapse of two thousand years, Sukla reached the Arbuda mountain by the way of fire. He overpowered his three brothers and the Bauddhas and by the grace of the lord, the city of Dvaraka was established. Subsequently, while staying there, they started meditating on lord Krsna.

22-35. By the grace of the lord, he occupied the throne of the western country and got a son named Visvaksena. After ruling for twenty years, he got a son named Jayasena who himself ruled the country for thirty years. He got a son named Visena. After ruling for fifty years, twin children were bom to him, who were given the names of Pramodasimha and Modasimha. The king Visena got the marriage of his son performed with the daughter of Vikrama and then gave away his kingdom to his son. He ruled the country for the same period as his father did and then he got a son named Sindhuvarma, who disowning the kingdom of his father, established his own kingdom, which came to be known on earth as Sindhudesa. Thereafter, the king Sindhuvarma had a son named Sindhudvipa, who became the lord of Sindhudvipa and who made Kacchapi - the daughter of Gautama race as his wife and received the country of Kacchadesa. He overpowered the Pulindas as well as the Yavanas and gained glory. He had a son named Bhujavarma, who defeated the Sabara-bhillas and then established his kingdom there. Because of this, the land came to be known as Bhuja country. Bhujavarma had a son named Ranavarma and Citravarma was the son of Ranavarma. He established the Citranagari in the forest. Citravarma's son was known as Dharmavarma who had a son named Krsnavarma. Krsnavarma had a son named Udaya, who established a city named Udaipura in the mid of forest. Udaya had a son named Vapyavarma, who constructed step-wells, wells, tanks mid several palaces, besides a city for religious motives.

36-48. In the meantime, a king named Balada who getting intoxicated, leading an army of a lakh of soldiers, marched from his country and started waging the war. The king Vapyavarma defeated the Mleccha king and celebrated great activities in honour of lord Krsna. Thereafter, he got a son named Guhila who had a son named Kalabhoja. Rastrapala was the name of the son of Kalabhoja, who disowning the position of his father, adored goddess Vaisnavi for performing great tapas. The goddess getting pleased at that time, built for him a beautiful city of Mahavati, which was always protected by Manideva. All the aforesaid rulers ruled for the same period for which their fathers ruled. The intelligent king Rastrapala, after ruling his city for ten years, got two gem like sons named Vijaya and Prajaya. Out of them, Prajaya discarding the position of his father, meditated upon the goddess farads for a period of twelve years. The goddess then taking to the form of a girl, playing on a vina and riding over a horse, appeared before the king and said to him- “O prince, what for are you worshipping the goddess Parvati? I am prepared to bestow on you the related reward.” On hearing these words, the king said - “O sweet-tongued goddess Kumari (maiden), you built up a new city for me. I offer my salutation to you.” On hearing these words, the goddess presented the auspicious horse to the king and proceeded towards the southern direction leading him. Closing both his eyes, the king followed her. Thereafter, the king arrived at a region in the western direction.

*tadā tu saptakanyāśca śilābhūtā gṛhe sthitāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

49-59. From there, he again turned toward the eastern direction, which was the dwelling place of the bird known as Markana. Reaching there, he was terrified and opened his eyes. Suddenly, he found a beautiful city built by the girl. The Ganga flowed to the north of the city. Pandura was towards the south and Isa was on the east where there lived the bird Markana. The city was lodged over an uneven ground, because of which it was given the name of Kanyakubja. He (the king) occupied the lion throne of that country for ten years, then a son named Venu was born to him, who was more interested in playing on flute. The king married a beautiful girl named Kanyavati, making her his own wife. The queen produced seven girls, who appeared as the auspicious form of her mother. They were known by the names of Sitala, Parvati, Kanya, Puspavati, Govardhani, Sindura and Kali, who respectively represented Brahmi, Mahesvari, Kaumari, Vaisnavi, Varahi, Indrani and Camunda and became popular accordingly. Once the queen tied a cotton rope to the neck of an earthen pitcher, went to the well and hung down the pitcher. Some other ladies also arrived there, who were clad in beautiful costumes and adorned with several types of ornaments. Finding them so charmingly decorated and she herself clad in a single sari, she felt disgusted and could not draw the pitcher from the well. Finding the women engaged in the mutual talk, the goddess Kanyavati returned to her abode without the pitcher. On reaching home, she found her daughters having been turned into stones.

## \|\| 2.138.60-71 \|\|

*śrutvā veṇustadāgatya bhartsayitvā svakāṃ priyām \|*  
*brahmacaryavrataṃ tyaktvā ramayāmāsa yoṣitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*nṛpādvai vīravatyāṃ ca yaśovigraha ātmajaḥ \|*  
*babhūva balavāndharmī cāryadeśapatiḥ svayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*viṃśadvarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tena rājñā mahītale \|*  
*mahīcaṃdrastasya sutaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*caṃdradevastasya suto rājyaṃ tena pituḥ samam \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tasmātsuto jāto maṃdapālo mahīpatiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tasya bhūpasya samaye sarve bhūpāḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā taṃ maṃdapālaṃ ca taddatte saṃsthitā gṛhe \|\| 64 \|\|*

*piturarddhaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ kumbhapālastato 'bhavat \|*  
*rājanīyā ca nagarī piśācaviṣaye sthitā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tatpatiśca mahāmodo mlecchapaiśācadharmagaḥ \|*  
*sa jitvā bahudhā deśāṃlluṃṭhayitvā dhanaṃ bahu \|\| 66 \|\|*

*mlecchadharmakaraḥ prāptaḥ kumbhapālo yataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*kumbhapālastu taṃ dṛṣṭvā kalinā nirmitaṃ nṛpa \|\| 67 \|\|*

*mahāmodaṃ samāgamya praṇanāma sa buddhimān \|*  
*tadā mlecchapatiḥ śūro dattvā tasmai dhanaṃ bahu \|\| 68 \|\|*

*rājanīyāṃ ca nagarīṃ prāptavānmūrtikhaṃḍakam \|*  
*viṃśadabdaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ kuṃbhapālena dhīmatā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tatputro devapālaścānaṃgabhūpasya kanyakām \|*  
*samudvāhya vidhānena caṃdrakāṃtiṃ tayā saha \|\| 70 \|\|*

*kānyakubjagṛhaṃ prāpya jitvā bhūpānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasyobhau tanayau smṛtau \|\| 71 \|\|*

60-71. Hearing the news, the king Vena returned to his abode and scolded his wife very much. Thereafter, discarding Brahmacarya, he united with his wife as a result of which a son was bom to her, who was the incarnation of glory. He was quite valorous, auspicious-minded and became the king of Arya country. The said king ruled over the country for a period of twenty years. Thereafter, he got a son named Mahicandra who had a son named Candradeva. He had a son named Mandapala, during whose rule all the rulers had lived in the houses built by Mandapala in a compassionate manner. He ruled the country for half the period for which his father had ruled, while the other rulers ruled their countries for as long as their fathers did so. The king Mandapala had a son named Kumbhapala, who made Mahamoda to retreat by his wisdom. Once the Mleccha king Mahamoda - the lord of the city of Rajaniya which was surrounded by the Pisacas, defeated rulers of several countries and plundered their riches. He also reached the capital city of Kumbhapala. О king, observing Mahamoda -the Mleccha king who happened to be an incarnation of Kali, the king Kumbhapala thought carefully. Thereafter, the intelligent king went to him and delightfully offered his salutation to him. The idol breaker Mleccha king was immensely pleased with him and giving him enormous riches, he returned to his city named Rajaniya. After ruling for twenty years, a son named Devapala was bom to Kumbhapala who married the daughter named Candrakirti of the king Anangapala. He returned to Kanyakubja with the bride and enjoyed a comfortable life. While ruling there, he became victorious over many of the rulers. He ruled his kingdom for the same period for which his father did so.

## \|\| 2.138.72-79 \|\|

*jayacaṃdro ratnabhānurdiśaṃ pūrvāṃ tathottarām \|*  
*āryadeśasya vai jitvā vaiṣṇavo rājyamāptavān \|\| 72 \|\|*

*ratnabhānośca tanayo lakṣaṇo nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*kurukṣetre raṇaṃ prāpya tyaktvā prāṇāndivaṃ gataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*samāptimagamadvaṃśo vaiśyapālasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*kuṃbhapālasya śauklasya vaiśyānāṃ rakṣakasya ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

*viṣvaksenānvaye jātā viṣvaksenā nṛpāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*visenasya kule jātā visenāḥ kṣatriyāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*guhilasya kule jātā gauhilāḥ kṣatriyā hi te \|*  
*rāṣṭrapālānvaye jātā rāṣṭrapālā nṛpāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*vaiśyapālasya vai vaṃśe kuṃbhapālasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*vaiśyapālāśca rājanyā babhūburbahudhā hi te \|\| 77 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇe maraṇaṃ prāpte śukla vaṃśadhuraṃdhure \|*  
*sarve te kṣatriyā mukhyāḥ kurukṣetre layaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*śeṣāstu kṣudrabhūpālā varṇasaṃkarasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*mlecchaiśca dūṣitā jātā mleccharājye bhayānake \|\| 79 \|\|*

72-79. In due course of time, he got two sons named Jayacandra and Ratnabhanu, who conquering the northern and eastern Arya countries, established the Vaisnava state. The famous Laksana was the son of Ratnabhanu, who died while fighting a terrific war at the land of Kuruksetra. With the departure of the intelligent Vaisyapala who was the protector of the Vaisyas, Kumbhapala's race got concluded. The rulers of the race of Visvaksena, those born in Visena race, the race of Guhila and the Ksatriyas bom in the race of Rastrapala were known as Rastrapalas. The descendants of Vaisyapala and the intelligent Kumbhapala’s race created many differences and have been known to be of many types. Laksana was the terrific ruler of the lunar race and after his death, many of the Ksatriyas were destroyed at Kuruksetra. At that point of time, only small kings were left out whose wives were forcibly enjoyed by the Yavanas/Mlecchas and produced terrific mixed breed.

## Chapter 139. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.139.1-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bhṛguvarya śṛṇu tvaṃ vai vaṃśaṃ pariharasya ca \|*  
*jitvā bauddhānpariharo'tharvavedaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śaktiṃ sarvamayīṃ nityāṃ dhyātvā premaparo'bhavat \|*  
*prasannā sā tadā devī sārdhayojanamāyatam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nagaraṃ citrakūṭādrau cakāra kalinirjaram \|*  
*kaliryatra bhavedbaddho nagare'sminsurapriye \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ataḥ kaliṃjaro nāmnā prasiddho'bhūnmahītale \|*  
*dvādaśābdaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tena pūrvapradeśake \|\| 4 \|\|*

*gauravarmā tasya sutaḥ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ pituḥ samam \|*  
*svānujaṃ ghoravarmāṇaṃ tatrāsthāpya mudānvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gauḍadeśaṃ samāgamya tatra rājyamakārayat \|*  
*suparṇo nāma nṛpatistato'bhūdgauravarmaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Suta said- O excellent seer of the race of Bhrgu, I would narrate the story of Parihara race. You please listen. The Pariharas, who are devoted to the Atharvaveda, getting victorious over the Bauddhas, then started the worship of the goddess, who is all powerful. The goddess getting pleased, built up a city of Kalinirjara near Citrakuta which was spread in an area of a yojana and a half. In that divine city, Kali has been imprisoned. Because of the negitivating of his existence, it came to be known on earth as Kalinjara. The pleasant city is lodged in the eastern region. After ruling the city for twelve years, the king got a son named Gauravarma. He established his younger brother over the throne of his father, who established his kingdom in the Gauda region, where the king Gauravarma produced a son named Suparna.

## \|\| 2.139.7-19 \|\|

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ rūpaṇastatsuto'bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ kāravarmā suto'bhavat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śako nāma tato rājā mahālakṣmīṃ sanātanīm \|*  
*trivarṣāṃte ca sā devī kāmākṣīrūpadhāriṇī \|\| 8 \|\|*

*svabhaktapālanā caiva tatra vāsamakārayat \|*  
*śatārddhābdaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tena vai kāmavarmaṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mithunaṃ janayāmāsa bhogo bhogavatī hi sā \|*  
*vikramāyaiva nṛpatiḥ sutāṃ bhogavatīṃ dadau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*svarājyaṃ ca svaputrāya pradadau bhogavarmaṇe \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ kālivarmā suto'vat \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mahotsavaṃ mahākālyāḥ kṛtavānsa ca bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*tasmai prasannā varadā kālī bhūtvā svayaṃ sthitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kalikā bahupuṣpāṇāṃ sā cakāra svaharṣataḥ \|*  
*tābhirbhavaṃ ca nagaraṃ saṃjātaṃ ca manoharam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kalikātā purī nāmnā prasiddhābhūnmahītale \|*  
*kauśikastasya tanayaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kātyāyanastasya sutaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*tasya putro hemavataḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śivavarmā ca tatputraḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|*  
*bhavavarmā ca tatputraḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*rudravarmā ca tatputraḥ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ pituḥ samam \|*  
*bhojavarmā ca tatputrastyaktvā vai paitṛkaṃ padam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhojarāṣṭraṃ vanoddeśe kārayāmāsa vīryavān \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ gavavarmā nṛpobhavat \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ viṃdhyavarmā nṛpo'bhavat \|*  
*svānujāya svakaṃ rājyaṃ dattvā vaṃgamupāyayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

7-19. Subsequently, Suparna gave birth to Rupana and Kamavarma was bom as a son to Rupana, who changed his name as Saka. He worshipped the Sanatani or ancient goddess Mahalaksmi. After worshipping her for three years, the goddess who takes to the form of Kamaksi, resided there itself for the protection of her devotee. After ruling the country for fifty years, Kamavarma got a son named Bhoga and a daughter named Bhogavati were bom as twins. The king married his daughter Bhogavati to Vikrama and gave away his kingdom to his son Bhogavarma. In due course of time, Bhogavarma had a son named Kalivarma, who celebrated great festival for Mahakali. The goddess who bestows blessings, getting pleased with him, established herself there as Kali and because of her delight, an numerable buds were grown over the flowering plants. Thereafter, she was also instrumental in building up a beautiful city there, which came to be known by the name of Kalikata. Thereafter, the king had a son named Kausika. Katyayana was bom as a son to Kausika. Hemavata was bom as son to Katyayana. Hemavata had a son named Sivavarma. Bhavavarma was the son of Sivavarma. Rudravarma was the son of Bhavavarma and Bhojavarma was the son of Rudravarma, who established the country of Bhoja. Bhojavarma had a son named Gavavarma and Gavavarma had a son named Vidhyavarma, who gave over his kingdom to his younger brother and himself went to Vangadesa.

## \|\| 2.139.20-27 \|\|

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ sukhasenastato'bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ balākastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*daśavarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ lakṣmaṇastatsuto'bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ mādhavastatsuto'bhavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ veśavastatsuto' bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ surasenastato'bhavat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tato nārāyaṇo'bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ śāṃtivarmā sutobhavat \|\| 23 \|\|*

*gaṃgākūle śāṃtipuraṃ racitaṃ tena dhīmatā \|*  
*nivāsaṃ kṛtavānbhūpaḥ pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ padam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nadīvarmā tasya suto gaṃgādattavaro balī \|*  
*cakāra nagarīṃ ramyāṃ nadīhāṃ gauḍarāṣṭragām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gaṃgayā ca tadāhūtobhijño vidyādharaḥ svayam \|*  
*tenaiva rakṣitā cāsītpurī vedaparāyaṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*viṃśadvarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tena rājñā mahātmanā \|*  
*gaṃgāvaṃśastato jāto viśruto'bhūnmahītale \|\| 27 \|\|*

20-27. Again, he had a son named Sukhasena and Balaka was the son of Sukhasena, who ruled only for six years and the rest of the aforesaid rulers ruled for the same period for which their respective fathers ruled. Balaka had a son named Laksmana, who had a son named Madhava, who had a son named Kesava. Surasena was the son of Kesava and Narayana was the son of Surasena. Santivarma was bom as a son to Narayana, who built a city over the bank of the river Ganga. Santivarma had a son named Nandivarma and Gangadatta was bom to Nandivarma. He was quite a valorous monarch, who built the city of Nadiha in the country of Gauda. The monarch known as Gangadatta adored a Vidyadhara and pleased him with his devotion. He guarded well the city established by him. The said noble monarch ruled the country for twenty years and the glory of the Ganga dynasty was spread over the earth. All the aforesaid rulers ruled the earth for the same period for which there father’s did so.

## \|\| 2.139.28-40 \|\|

*śārṅgadevastasya suto balavānharipūjakaḥ \|*  
*gauḍadeśamupāgamya haridhyānaparobhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*daśavarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ gaṃgādevastu tatsutaḥ \|*  
*viṃśadvarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ cānaṃgastasya bhūpatiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tanayo balavāṃścāsīdgauḍadeśamahīpatiḥ \|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ kalivarmā suto'bhavat \|\| 31 \|\|*

*rāṣṭradeśamupāgamya jitvā tasya nṛpaṃ balī \|*

*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ dhṛtivarmā suto'bhavat \|*  
*pitustulyaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tasya putro mahīpatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jayacaṃdrājñayā bhūpa urvīmāyāmiti smṛtām \|*

*viṃśadvarṣaṃ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ sahoddīnena vai tataḥ \|*

*tadanvaye ca ye bhūpāḥ śārdūlīyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*bhūpānāṃ bahudhā rāṣṭraṃ śārdūlānvayasaṃbhavam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*babhūva sarvato bhūmau mahāmāyāprasādataḥ \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ vipra pāvakīyamahībhujām \|\| 39 \|\|*
