28-40. A son named Sarngadeva was born to Gangadatta, who was quite valorous and devoted to lord Visnu. He always meditated the lord in the Gauda country. After his ruling the country for ten years, he got a son named Gangadeva who occupied the royal throne for twenty years. Subsequently, he got a son named Ananga who was quite valorous and became the ruler of the Gauda country. The king Ananga had a son named Rajesvara who had a son named Nrsimha. Kalivarma was the son of Nrsimha who defeated the king of Rastra country. Thereafter, he spent a comfortable life in the city of Mahavati. Then he got a son named Dhrtivarma and Mahipati was the son of Dhrtivarma, who with the permission of Jayacandra built a town named UrvI and lived therein. When all the rulers of the lunar race were killed in the battlefield of Kuruksetra, Mahila became the ruler of Mahavati. He ruled for twenty years, after which in the same Kuruksetra, he - the amsa of Suyodhana was killed at the hands of Sahoddina. The rest of the rulers ruled the countries for the same period for which their fathers did so. Ghoravarma - the descendant of the Parihara family, while ruling Kalinjara, produced a son named Sardula. The rulers of the Sardula family expanded their kingdom variously from all the sides. Thus the auspicious races of the solar and lunar dynasties have been described. Now I shall describe the manner in which the lord incarnated on earth.

## Chapter 140. Collateral history of the Age of Kali

## \|\| 2.140.1-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*madhyāhnakāle saṃprāpte brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*cākṣuṣāṃtaramevāpi mahāvāyurbabhūva ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatprabhāvena hemādriḥ kaṃpamānaḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*yathā vṛkṣastathaivāsau tatkaṃpādeva maṃḍalaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nabhaso bhūtale prāptastadā bhūmiḥ prakaṃpitā \|*  
*babhūva muniśārdūla sarvalokavināśinī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*saptadvīpāḥ samudrāśca jalabhūtā babhūvire \|*  
*lokālokastadā śeṣo'bhavatsottaraparvataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śeṣā bhūmirlayaṃ prāptā manvaṃtare laye \|*  
*sahasrābdāṃtare bhūmirbabhūva jalamadhyagā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tadā sa bhagavānviṣṇurbhavena vidhinā saha \|*  
*śaiśumāraṃ śubhaṃ cakraṃ cakāra nabhasi sthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Suta said- During the noon time of Brahma of invisible birth, the force of the wind appeared as a result of which the Himalaya mountain started shaking repeatedly like a tree. With the shaking of the Himalaya, the wind force arrived from the sky on the earth and the earthquake started on earth. О lion among the sages, all the lokas were destroyed with the earthquake and there was a overflow of water from the ocean. At that point of time, the Lokaloka mountain escaped destruction. With the land having been faced with the deluge, the period of Manvantra was also absorbed (in time). After the lapse of a thousand years, the earth was totally submerged in water.

## \|\| 2.140.7-19 \|\|

*gṛhītvā sakalāstārā grahānsarvānyathāvidhi \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa bhagavānyathāyogyaṃ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*punarvai jyotiṣāṃ cakraiḥ śoṣitā sakalā mahī \|*  
*sthalībhūyāyutābdānte dṛśyamānā babhūva ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tadā sa bhagavānbrahmā mukhātsomaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*dvijarājaṃ mahāprājñaṃ sarvavedaviśāradam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhujābhyāṃ bhagavānbrahmā kṣatrarājaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*sūryaṃ ca janayāmāsa rājanītiparāyaṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ūrubhyāṃ vaiśyarājaṃ ca samudraṃ saritāṃ patim \|*  
*ratnākaraṃ ca kṛtavānparameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*padbhyāṃ ca janayāmāsa viśvakarmāṇamuttamam \|*  
*dakṣaṃ nāma kalābhijñaṃ śūdrarājaṃ sukṛtyakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*somādvai brāhmaṇā jātāḥ sūryādrājanyavaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*samudrātsakalā vaiśyā dakṣācchūdrā babhūvire \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sūryamaṃḍalato jāto manurvaivasvataḥ svayam \|*  
*tasya rājyamabhūtsarvaṃ prāṇināṃ lokavāsinām \|\| 14 \|\|*

*divyānāṃ ca yugānāṃ ca tajjñeyaṃ caikasaptatiḥ \|*  
*tadā sa bhagavānviṣṇurviśvarūpā'vatārakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*viṣṇuḥ pūrvārddhato jātaḥ parārddhādvāmanaḥ svayam \|*  
*bālaḥ satyayuge devo viśvarūpaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*catuśśatāni varṣāṇi paramāyurnṛṇāṃ tadā \|*  
*tretāyāṃ yauvanaṃ prāptaḥ pūrvārddhātsaṃbhavo hareḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*varṣāṇāṃ triśatānāṃ ca nṛṇāmāyuḥ prakīrtitam \|*  
*dvāpare vārddhiko devo nṛṇāmāyuḥ śatadvayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kalau tu maraṇaṃ prāpto viśvarūpo hariḥ svayam \|*  
*nṛṇāmāyuḥ śatābdaṃ ca keṣāṃciddharmaśālinām \|\| 19 \|\|*

7-19. At that point of time, lord Visnu with Brahma and Siva, established the auspicious wheel of time in the sky. After that, Lord Brahma established whole of the stars and planets at appropriate places accordingly. They again started drying up the earth with the Jyotisacakra and as a result of this, the earth after making efforts for ten thousand years, appeared in the form of dry land. At that point of time, lord Brahma generated the nectar from his mouth. Because of this, Brahma is known as the lord of Brahmanas who are extremely intelligent and well-versed in all the Vedas. Again, lord Brahma created the Sungod, the lord of regions from his arms, who is enormously valorous besides being specialist in polity. Similarly, Uru created the ocean who happens to be the lord of Vaisyas. The ocean is also called the hasp of the rivers and the treasure of gems or pearls. Thereafter, the intelligent Brahma created Visvakarma Daksa, who is a specialist in all the arts, the lord of Sudras and the performer of the noble deeds. Thereafter, Brahma - the lord of the twice-born ones known as Soma, created Brahmanas, Surya created the Ksatriyas, while Vaisyas originated from the ocean. Thereafter, Vaivasvata was created by the solar disc, who solely rules over the universe. After the seventy one time expiry of the divine yugas, lord Visnu incarnates in the universal form. During the first half of the yuga, lord Visnu incarnates while in the second half incarnates Vamana. During the Satyayuga, the eternal lord of universal form appears as a child. At that point of time, the average age of the humans is four hundred years. The lord who is bom in the first half of the yuga, becomes youthful in the Tretayuga when the average age of humans is three hundred years. During Dvapara, Visnu appears in old age when the average life of humans is two hundred years. During the age of Kali, the universal lord Visnu himself meets with his end. During this yuga, the age of some of the religious-minded people becomes hundred years.

## \|\| 2.140.20-31 \|\|

*parārddhādvāmano devo mahendrāvarajo hariḥ \|*  
*caturbhujo mahāśyāmo garuḍopari saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*viśvarūpahitārthāya triyugī saṃbabhūva ha \|*  
*vāmanārddhācca triyugī jāto nārāyaṇaḥ svayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śvetarūpo hariḥ satye haṃsākhyo bhagavānsvayam \|*  
*tretāyāṃ raktarūpaśca yajñākhyo bhagavānsvayam \|*  
*dvāpare pītarūpaśca svarṇagarbho hariḥ svayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kalikāle tu saṃprāpte saṃdhyāyāṃ dvāpare yuge \|*  
*kalā tu sakalā viṣṇorvāmanasya tathā kalā \|*  
*ekībhūtā ca devakyāṃ jāto viṣṇustadā svayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vasudevagṛhe ramye mathurāyāṃ ca devatāḥ \|*  
*brahmādyāstuṣṭuvurdevaṃ paraṃ brahma sanātanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavāndevānāha śubhaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ ca hitārthāya daityānāṃ nidhanāya ca \|*  
*ahaṃ kalau ca bahudhā bhavāmi surasattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*divyaṃ vṛṃdāvanaṃ ramyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ bhūtalasaṃsthitam \|*  
*tatrāhaṃ ca rahaḥkrīḍāṃ kariṣyāmi kalau yuge \|\| 26 \|\|*

*sarve vedāḥ kalau ghore gopībhūtāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*raṃsyante hi mayā sārddhaṃ tyaktvā bhūmaṃḍalaṃ tadā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rādhayā prārthito'haṃ vai yadā kaliyugāṃtake \|*  
*samāpya ca rahaḥkrīḍāṃ kalkī ca bhavitāsmyaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yugāṃtapralayaṃ kṛtvā punarbhūtvā dvidhātanuḥ \|*  
*satyadharmaṃ kariṣyāmi satye prāpte surottamāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu te devāstatraivāntarlayaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ yugeyuge krīḍā hareradbhutakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ye tu vai viṣṇubhaktāśca te hi jānaṃti viśvagam \|*  
*yathaiva nṛpaterdāsāḥ svarājñaḥ kāryagauravam \|*  
*jānaṃti nāpare vipra tathā dāsā hareḥ svayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

20-31. Getting incarnated in the later half period, the lord incarnating on earth as Vamana, is known as the younger brother of Indra. He has four arms and dark complexion. He rides on Garuda, becomes Triyugi in his universal form. From Triyugi Vamana, lord Narayana is him self bom. During the Satyayuga, having a. bright complexion, he is know n by the name of Hamsa (swan). Similarly, in the Tretayuga, he is known as Yajna and has red complexion. During Dvapara, he is of golden complexion or yellow-coloured. During the closing time of Dvapara, at the arrival of the age of Kali, all the digits of Visnu and a digit of Vamana get merged and he incarnated in the house of Vasudeva from the womb of Devaki as an incarnation of lord Visnu. At that point of time, all the gods offered prayer to the eternal Brahman. The lord then getting pleased with the gods and for their welfare besides the destruction of the daityas, would incarnate in many forms. He shall remain on earth in a subtle form and shall sport in the secluded forest of Vrndavana. At that point of time, taking it to be the terrific period of Kali, all the Vedas disowning the earth in a detached manner, would appear as milkmaids and would sport with me. Then again at the end of the age of Kali, at the prayer of Radhika, I shall discard the lonely sport and shall appear in the form of Kalki. O best of gods, again after the end of the yuga, I shall divide my own body of the same yuga in two parts and perform Satyadharma,” On hearing these words, all the gods were absorbed in the same.

## \|\| 2.140.32-34 \|\|

*viṣṇuvāṃchānusāreṇa viṣṇumāyā sanātanī \|*  
*racitvā vividhāṃllokānmahākālī babhūva ha \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kṛtvā kālamayaṃ sarvaṃ jagadeccarācaram \|*  
*paścāttu bhakṣayitvā tānmahāgaurī bhaviṣyati \|\| 33 \|\|*

*namastasyai mahākālyai viṣṇumāye namonamaḥ \|*  
*mahāgauri namastubhyamasmānpāhi bhayānvitān \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Similarly, in each and every yuga, the astonishing types of sports of the lord are performed. But the leader of the entire universe is known only to be the devotee of Visnu and none else can know him. O Brahmana, as the glory of the performance of a monarch is well known to his attendant alone and none else, similarly the activities of the lord cannot be known by anyone other than his devotee alone. Then taking to the form of Mahakali as per his own will, he as a destroyer, consumes the entire universe. Therefore, salutation to the illusion of lord Visnu. Salutation to Mahakali again and again. Salutation to Mahagauri who protects the panic-stricken people like us.

## Chapter 141. The Pravara Dynasty

## \|\| 2.141.1 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca \|*  
*mahīrājānmuniśreṣṭha ke rājāno babhūvire \|*  
*tānno vada mahābhāga sarvajño'sti bhavānsadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rsis said- O best of the sages (after Prthviraja) who were the kings who ruled the country? You kindly speak out about them because you happen to know everything.

## \|\| 2.141.2-10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*paiśācaḥ kutukoddīno dehalīrājyamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*valīgaḍhaṃ mahāramyaṃ yādavai rakṣitaṃ puram \|*  
*yayau tatra sa paiśācaḥ śūrāyutasamanvitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vīrasenasya vai pautraṃ bhūpasenaṃ nṛpottamam \|*  
*sa jitvā kutukoddīno dehalīgrāmasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare bhūpā nānādeśyāḥ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*jitvā sa kutukoddīnaḥ svadeśāttairnirākṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sahoddīnastu tacchrutvā punarāgatya dehalīm \|*  
*jitvā bhūpāndaityavaro mūrtikhaṃḍamathākarot \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatpaścādbahudhā mlecchā ihāgatya samantataḥ \|*  
*paṃcaṣaṭsaptavarṣāṇi kṛtvā rājyaṃ layaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*adyaprabhṛti deśe'smiñchatavarṣāntare hi te \|*  
*bhūtvā cālpāyuṣo mandā devatīrthavināśakāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mlecchabhūpā muniśreṣṭhāstasmādyūyaṃ mayā saha \|*  
*gaṃtumarhatha vai śīghraṃ viśālāṃ nagarīṃ śubhām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ duḥkhātsaṃtyajya naimiṣam \|*  
*yayuḥ sarve viśālāyāṃ himādrau girisattame \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tatra sarve samādhisthā dhyātvā sarvamayaṃ harim \|*  
*śatavarṣāntare sarve dhyānādbrahmagṛhaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

2-10. Suta said- The Yavana king arrived in the country with ten thousand of the Yavana soldiers and defeated Bhupasena - the grave son of Prthviraja. He returned again to DehalT and started living a comforatble life. In the meantime, the rulers of several states collected and fought a fierce battle with him and drove Kutubuddina out of the country. Hearing this news, Sahoddina again arrived in Dehali and getting victorious over the local rulers, he indulged in the destruction of the sculptures. Thereafter, several of the Mleccha rulers arrived in the country of Bharata and ruled here for five hundred years. In due course of time, they were merged (in the society). Therefore, within a hundred years from today, those Yavana rulers who desecrate the images as well as the holy places, shall get destroyed enjoying shot span of lives. Therefore, all of you should get ready to come along with me to the town of Visala. On hearing these words, somehow discarding the holy place of Naimisaranya, they started towards the city of Visala. Reaching there, all of them started meditating on the lord. In due course of time, all the Rsis performing the meditation, reached the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.141.11 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ sakalaṃ bhāvyaṃ yogābhyāsavaśāddrutam \|*  
*varṇitaṃ ca mayā tubhyaṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Vyasa said- We have heard the stories which could be known with the application of the yogic practices. Now what more do you want to listen from me?

## \|\| 2.141.12-16 \|\|

*manuruvāca \|*  
*bhagavanvedatattvajña sarvalokaśivaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ māyābhavo jāto bhavānvedabhavo bhuvi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*avidyayā ca sakalaṃ mama jñānaṃ samāhṛtam \|*  
*ato'haṃ vividhā yonīrgṛhītvā lokamāgataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*paraṃ brahmaiva kṛpayā dṛṣṭvā māṃ maṃdabhāginam \|*  
*vyāsarūpaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā samuddhartumupāgataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*namastasmai munīṃdrāya vedavyāsāya sākṣiṇe \|*  
*avidyāmohabhāvebhyo rakṣaṇāya namonamaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*punaranyacca me brūhi sūtādyaiḥ kiṃ kṛtaṃ mune \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā svāminvaktumarhasi sāṃpratam \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. Manu said - О lord, you are quite learned about the Vedas and bestow welfare on all the Iokas. You are infact an incarnation of the Vedas on earth. With ignorance, all my knowledge has faded out and because of that, wandering in seal births, I have ultimately reached in this world. It was because of the immense grace of the Supreme Being, that by coming across an ignorant person like me and for the sake of my redemption, you have appeared before me. Therefore, I offer my salutation to the great sage Vedavyasa, who happens to be the witness of the deeds and relives me of ignorance. Salutation to you again and again, О sage, thereafter, what did Suta and other sages did? О master, you kindly tell me the whole of the story.

## \|\| 2.141.17-21 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*brahmāṃḍe ye sthitā lokāste sarvesminkalevare \|*  
*ahaṃkāro hi jīvātmā sarvaḥ syātkoṭihīnakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*purāṇo'ṇoraṇīyāṃśca ṣoḍaśātmā sanātanaḥ \|*  
*indriyāṇi manaścaiva pañca cendriyagocarāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*jñeyo jīvaḥ śarīre'sminsa īśaguṇabaṃdhitaḥ \|*  
*īśo hyaṣṭādaśātmā vai śaṃkaro jīvaśaṃkaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*buddhirmanaśca viṣayā iṃdriyāṇi tathaiva ca \|*  
*ahaṃkārasya ceśo vai mahādevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*jīvo nārāyaṇassākṣācchaṃkareṇa vimohitaḥ \|*  
*sa baddhastriguṇaiḥ pāśairekaśca bahudhābhavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. Vyasa said- The arrogance in the entire world as well as in this body is known as the Jivatma which is deficient. Because of the differences of ancient, subtle and more subtle, the eternal supreme should be known as the soul. There are five organs of knowledge (viz., ear, eyes, nose, tongue and skin). There are the five organs of activity (tongue, hands, feet, wind and lap). These happen to be the rulers of the body. Making use of three gunas (sattva, rajas and tamos) it is bound with them. The supreme soul is also known as Astadasatma besides being Sankara, who bestows welfare on the jiva. The intelligence, mind and sense organs happen to be the subjects. The arrogance of Jivatma is known as Isa, Mahadeva and Sanatana. But inspite of his being the Jivatma, he is the form of Brahman and getting confused by lord Siva, it is bound with noose of the three gunas. It then transforms itself from one to many. He is also called as Kala (time), BhagavSn, Isa besides having the form of Mahakalpa.

## \|\| 2.141.22-34 \|\|

*kālātmā bhagavānīśo mahākalpasvarūpakaḥ \|*  
*śivakalpo brahmakalpo viṣṇukalpastṛtīyakaḥ \|*  
*īśanetrāṇi tānyeva bandhakalpaścaturthakaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vāyukalpo vahnikalpo brahmāṃḍo liṃgakalpakaḥ \|*  
*īśavaktrāṇi pañcaiva tattvajñaiḥ kathitāni vai \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyakalpaśca tathā tathā garuḍaka lpakaḥ \|*  
*kalpo bhāgavataścaiva mārkaṇḍeyaśca kalpakaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vāmanaśca nṛsiṃhaśca varāho matsyakūrmakau \|*  
*jñānātmano maheśasya jñeyā daśa bhujā budhaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aṣṭādaśadineṣveva brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*kalpāścāṣṭādaśāssarve budhairjñeyā vilomataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kūrmakalpaśca tatrādyo matsyakalpo dvitīyakaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyaḥ śvetavārāhaḥ kalpo jñeyaḥ purātanaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dvidhā ca bhagavānbrahmā sūkṣmaḥ sthūlo'guṇo guṇī \|*  
*saguṇaḥ sa virāṇnāmnā viṣṇu nābhisamudbhavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nirguṇovyayarūpaścāvyaktajanmā svabhūḥ svayam \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ saguṇasyaiva śatāyuḥ kālanirmitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ūnaviṃśasahasrāṇi lakṣaiko mānuṣābdakaiḥ \|*  
*ebhirvarṣairdinaṃ jñeyaṃ virājo brahmaṇaḥ svayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nirguṇo'vyaktajanmā ca kālātsarveśvaraḥ paraḥ \|*  
*avyaktaṃ prakṛtirjñeyā dvādaśāṃgāni vai tataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*indriyāṇi mano buddhiravyaktasya smṛtāni vai \|*  
*avyaktācca paraṃ brahma sūkṣmajyotistadavyayam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yadā vyakte svayaṃ prāpto'vyaktajanmā hi saṃsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*śatavarṣasamādhistho yastiṣṭhecca niraṃtaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sūkṣmo manonilo bhūtvā gacchedvai brahmaṇaḥ padam \|*  
*satya lokamiti jñeyaṃ yogagamyaṃ sanātanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

22-34. The three eyes of the Isa are said to be Sivakalpa, Brahmakalpa and Visnukalpa. The same are also interpreted as the fourth kalpa of Isa. The five kalpas like Bandhakalpa, Vayukalpa, Vahnikalpa, Brahmandakalpa and Lingakalpa are the five heads of Isa as conceived by those well versed in tattvas. The ten arms of Mahesvara are known to represent Bhavisyakalpa, Garudakalpa, Bhagavatkalpa, Markandeyakalpa, besides Vamana, Nrsimha, Varaha, Matsya and Kurma. The eighteen kalpas of the invisible Brahman are made in eighteen days, for the counting of which the learned people have conceived it to be of the reverse order. The first one is the Kurmakalpa, the second one is the Matsyakalpa and the third is the Sveta-varaha kalpa and to know about the reality of the same, the Rsis had tried in the ancient times. Lord Brahma divided himself into two parts and then popularized himself into subtle, gross, nirguna, saguna and the universal form. Brahma is said to have emerged out of the navel of lord Visnu. The same Brahma who is said to be nirgurta, vyaya-ruра of invisible birth or the self bom, has the age of a hundred years. The eighty thousand human years form a single day of Brahma. Brahma, who is devoid of gunas, of invisible birth, is the lord of all and has greeted us with the Kala (time). It is believed that the said Paramesvara is of invisible Prakrti and has twelve limbs including five organs of knowledge, five limbs of activity, besides intelligence and the mind. The supreme Brahman emerges out of the invisible force, the subtle flame of which is imperishable. In his invisible state, he reaches himself. Because of this, he is known as the invisible birth. Attaining the saguna form, He enters into the samadhi for a hundred years. The subtle mind in the form of the wind makes constant efforts and when he achieves the place of Brahma, it is called sanatana or an eternal one, the same is known as Satyaloka.

## \|\| 2.141.35-42 \|\|

*tatra sthāne tu munayo gatāḥ sarve samādhinā \|*  
*tatroṣitvā ca lakṣābdaṃ bhūrlokātkṣaṇamātrakam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*saccidānaṃdaghanakaṃ tataḥ prāptāḥ kalevare \|*  
*netrāṇi ca samunmīlya saṃprāpte dvitayāhnike \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dadṛśurmanujānsarvānpaśutulyānhi sūkṣmakān \|*  
*ṣaṣṭyabdāyuryutānghorānsārddhakiṣkudvayonnatān \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kvacitkvacitsthitā varṇā varṇasaṃkarasannibhāḥ \|*  
*sarve mlecchāśca pāṣaṃḍā bahurūpamato sthitāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tīrthāni sakalā vedāstyaktvā bhūmaṃḍalaṃ tadā \|*  
*gopyo bhūtvā ca hariṇā sārddhaṃ cakrurmahotsavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pāṣaṃḍā bahujātīyā nānāmārgapradarśakāḥ \|*  
*kalinā nirmitānvarṇānvaṃcayitvā sthitā bhuvi \|\| 40 \|\|*

*iti dṛṣṭvā tu munayo romaharṣaṇamaṃtike \|*  
*gatvā tatra bhaviṣyaṃti tataḥ prāṃjalayo hi te \|\| 41 \|\|*

*taiśca tatra stutaḥ sūto yoganidrāṃ sanātanīm \|*  
*kathayiṣyati saṃtyajya kalpākhyānaṃ munīnprati \|*  
*tacchṛṇuṣva nṛpaśreṣṭha yathā sūtena varṇitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

35-42. By reaching that place, the Rsis entering into samadhi in which state they continue for a lakh of years, in a moment enter the body of the eternal one. Thereafter, on the next day, when he opens his eyes, he found all the people as animals in subtle form. Each one of them had the age of sixty years and of two spans, occasionally some castes like the mixed breed were also visible. But all of them were deceitful, Mlecchas having many forms. At that point of time, all the holy places and the four Vedas, deserting the earth and taking to the forms of milkmaids, had joined the festivities with the lord. The age of Kali had made the people deceitful, dividing them into several castes, several faiths and their leaders, depriving them of religious activities, but he himself became firm. Observing such a situation, the sages would try to reach the sage Romaharsana (Suta). Reaching before him, they would offer their salutation to him with folded hands. When so eulogized by the sages, Suta discarding his eternal yogic sleep, shall recite the stories of the kalpa. Now I am going to repeat the stories narrated by Suta. You please listen.

## \|\| 2.141.43-50 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*kalpākhyānaṃ pravakṣyāmi yaddṛṣṭaṃ yoganidrayā \|*  
*tacchṛṇudhvaṃ muniśreṣṭhā lakṣābdāṃte yathābhavat \|\| 43 \|\|*

*mukulānvayasaṃbhūto mlecchabhūpaḥ piśācakaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā timiraliṃgaśca madhyadeśamupāyayau \|\| 44 \|\|*

*āryānmlecchāṃstadā bhūpāñjitvā kālasvarūpakaḥ \|*  
*dehalīnagarīmadhye mahāvadhamakārayat \|\| 45 \|\|*

*āhūya sakalānviprānāryadeśanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmānyūyaṃ mūrtiprapūjakāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*nirmitā yena vā mūrtistasya putrīsamā smṛtā \|*  
*tasyāḥ kiṃ pūjanaṃ śuddhaṃ śālagrāmaśilāmayam \|*  
*viṣṇudevaśca yuṣmābhiḥ proktaḥ sa tu na vai hariḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ato vaḥ sakalā vedāḥ śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*vṛthā kṛtāni munibhirlokavañcanahetave \|*  
*ityuktvā tānbalādgṛhya jvaladagnau samākṣipat \|\| 48 \|\|*

*śālagrāmaśilāḥ sarvā balātteṣāṃ supūjyakāḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā coṣṭrapṛṣṭheṣu samāropya gṛhaṃ yayau \|\| 49 \|\|*

*taittiraṃ deśamāgamya durgaṃ tatra cakāra saḥ \|*  
*śālagrāmaśilānāṃ ca svāsanārohaṇaṃ kṛtam \|\| 50 \|\|*

43-50. Suta said - О best of the sages, after the lapse of a lakh of years, whatever had happened, with the use of my yogic sleep, I had foreseen all that happened and have narrated to you. There had been a Mleccha king named Timiralinga, who was bom in Mukula dynasty. He was the follower of Pisaca faith. He went to the Madhyadesa and became victorious over the Aryans as well as the Mleccha rulers. Then reaching the city of Dehall, he started terrific massacre. He called for all the Brahmanas of the Arya country and told them- “You are the idol worshippers. Those who made the images are like his sons. Therefore, the worship of the idols could be proper. You have equated Saligrama with Visnu. Therefore, having been termed as Saligrama, he could never be equated with Visnu. Therefore, I would say that the Vedas and the Sdstras have been composed just to cheat the people. Thus speaking, he threw all the Brahmanas in the burning fire flames. Thereafter, the slab of Saligrama and the related priests were forcibly imprisoned and putting over the camel backs, he took them with him and returned to his country. Reaching there, he built a fort in Taittira country and started living there. He made Saligrama slap as the step for his bed.

## \|\| 2.141.51-59 \|\|

*tadā tu sakalā devā duḥkhitā vāsavaṃ prabhum \|*  
*samūcurbahudhālapya devadevaṃ śacīpatim \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vayaṃ tu bhagavansarve śālagrāmaśilāsthitāḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā mūrtīśca sakalāḥ kṛṣṇāṃśena prabodhitāḥ \|*  
*śālagrāmaśilāmadhye vasāmo muditā vayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*śilāssarvāśca no deva śāladeśasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*tāśca vai mleccharājena svapadārohaṇīkṛtāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ devānāṃ bhagavānsvarāṭ \|*  
*jñātvā balikṛtaṃ sarvaṃ devapūjānirākṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*cukopa bhagavānindro daityānpratyabhravāhanaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā vajramatulaṃ svāyudhaṃ daityanāśanam \|*  
*taittire preṣayāmāsa deśe mlecchanivāsake \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tasya śabdena sakalā deśāśca bahubhinnakāḥ \|*  
*sa mleccho maraṇaṃ prāptastadā sarvasabhājanaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*śālagrāmaśilāḥ sarvā gṛhītvā vibudhāstadā \|*  
*gaṃḍakyāṃ ca samākṣipya svargalokamupāyayuḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*mahendrastu suraiḥ sārddhaṃ devapūjyamuvāca ha \|*  
*mahītale kalau prāpte bhagavandānavottamāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vedadharmaṃ samullaṃghya mama nāśanatatparāḥ \|*  
*ato māṃ rakṣa bhagavandevaiḥ sārddhaṃ kalau yuge \|\| 59 \|\|*

51-59. At that point of time, all the gods feeling painful, went to their lord and apprised him of the factual position, saying- “Having been enlightened by Krsna’s amsa, discarding all the images, we dwell in the Saligrama slabs. O lord, these stone slabs come form Sala country. But Mleccha ruler has made steps out of it for riding over his bed like the footsteps.” On hearing this, Indra thought the worship of the gods as humiliation by the daityas and became enraged over the demonic forms. Then Indra - the carrier of the clouds, picked up the weapon vajra and threw it towards the Mleccha country. With the thunder of the vajra, the entire country of the Mlecchas was tom into several parts and then was destroyed. The Mleccha king was also destroyed with all his kiths and kins. The gods then recovered the Saligrama slab and dropped it in the river Gandaki and then returned to the heaven. Reaching there, Mahendra approached Brhaspati with all the gods and said to him-“O lord, with the arrival of Kali on earth, the Danavas, desecrating the Vedic faith, would work for my destruction. Therefore, you protect me and the gods in the age of Kali.”

## \|\| 2.141.60-65 \|\|

*jīva uvāca \|*  
*mahendra tava yā patnī śacī nāmnā mahottamā \|*  
*dadau tasyai varaṃ viṣṇurbhavitāsmi sutaḥ kalau \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tvadājñayā ca sā devī purīṃ śāṃtimayīṃ śubhām \|*  
*gauḍadeśe ca gaṃgāyāḥ kūle lokanivāsinīm \|\| 61 \|\|*

*pratyāgatya dvijo bhūtvā kāryasiddhiṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*bhavānvai brāhmaṇo bhūtvā devakāryaṃ prasādhaya \|\| 62 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ rudrairekādaśaiḥ saha \|*  
*aṣṭabhirvasubhiḥ sārdhamaśvibhyāṃ sa ca vāsavaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tīrtharājamupāgamya prayāgaṃ ca ravipriyam \|*  
*māghe tu makare sūrye sūryadevamatoṣayat \|\| 64 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatistadāgatya sūryamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*indrādīnkathayāmāsa dvādaśādhyāyamāpaṭhan \|\| 65 \|\|*

60-65. Brhaspati said- О Mahendra, Visnu has bestowed a boon to your wife Saci that during the time of Kali, I will be your son, who obeying your command, shall be born in a Brahmana family and try to help in the establishing of the task of the gods.” On hearing the words of the divine preceptor, on the Makara day of the month of Magha, Indra together with eleven Rudras, eight Vasus and Asvinikumaras went to Prayaga - the place which is the favourite of the Sungod. All of them worshipped the Sungod. At that point of time, Brhaspati also reached there and narrated the glory of the Sungod, which was composed by him in twelve chapters.

## Chapter 142. Birth of Ramananda and Nimbarka

## \|\| 2.142.1-4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspatistu bhagavānmunirdevānsamāsthitān \|*  
*kiṃ provāca ca māhātmyaṃ maṃḍalasthasya vai raveḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā brahmanbrūhi nastatsamutsukān \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ sūto vacanamabravīt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatiṃ samāsīnaṃ jīvarūpaṃ guṇālayam \|*  
*prayāgastho mahendraśca suraiḥ sārddhamuvāca ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kathayasva mahābhāga sūryamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*yacchrutena raviḥ sākṣātprasannodya bhavetprabhuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. The Rsis said- О Brahman, what type of the glory of the Sungod was narrated by Brhaspati in the gathering of the gods and the Rsis? All of us are anxious to listen to the same. Therefore, you kindly narrate the same. On hearing the words of the Rsis, Suta said-“Finding Brhaspati seated over a graceful seat at Prayaga, Indra with all the gods said- “O excellent one, you kindly narrate the glory of the Sungod, hearing which the Sungod would be pleased.”

## \|\| 2.142.5-12 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*dhātṛśarmā dvijaḥ kaścidapatyārthe prajāpatim \|*  
*tapasā toṣayāmāsa barhiṣmatipure sthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*paṃcamābde tu bhagavānsaṃtuṣṭaśca prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*sutaṃ kanyāṃ punaḥ putraṃ trīṇyapatyāni saṃdadau \|\| 6 \|\|*

*varṣāṃtare janayitvā tryapatya sa dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*dhātṛśarmā paraṃ harṣamāptavānputralālanaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vivāhāśca kathaṃ teṣāṃ bhavitavyā mahottamāḥ \|*  
*iti cintānvito vipro gaṃdharveśaṃ ca tumburum \|\| 8 \|\|*

*havanaistoṣayāmāsa varṣamātravidhānataḥ \|*  
*tumburuśca tadāgatya taṃ cakāra manoratham \|\| 9 \|\|*

*prasannastu tadā vipro vadhūrjāmātaraṃ mudā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ vihāraṃ ca punaściṃtāṃ cakāra ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

*bhūṣaṇāni ca vāsāṃsi dhanāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ kathaṃ bhaviṣyaṃti nirdhanānāṃ mamāśuca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭivarṣamayo bhūtvā caṃdanādyairdhanādhipam \|*  
*vidhivatpūjayāmāsa varṣamātraṃ tu tatparaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

5-12. Brhaspati said- A Brahmana living in the city of Barhismati known by the name of Dhatrsarma, performed tapas for Prajapati with the desire of getting a son. On the fifth year, the lord Prajapati getting pleased, bestowed him two sons and a daughter within a year. As a result of this, Dhatrsarma getting extremely pleased, started bringing up the sons and the daughter. Soon the Brahmana got worried about the marriage of his children and after performing homa for a year, he worshipped tumburu - the leader of the Gandharvas. In due course of time, the Gandharva getting pleased, fulfilled the desire of the Brahmana for which the Brahmana was immensely delighted. He again got worried for the means for their usages. He thought- “I am poor and am now sixty years of age. Therefore, how could the children be provided with costumes and ornaments? Thus thinking, he worshipped Kubera - the god of wealth, with sandalpaste etc. in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 2.142.13-19 \|\|

*tadā prasanno bhagavāndadau tasmai dhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*vidyāṃ yakṣamayīṃ ramyāṃ paṃcasvarṇapradāṃ mudā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sahasrajāpī saṃpūjya havanaṃ taddaśāṃśakam \|*  
*tarpaṇaṃ mārjanaṃ caiva kṛtvā vāṃchāmavāptavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ vartamānasya gataḥ kālo mahānsvayam \|*  
*mṛtyorāgamanaṃ tasya jātaṃ rogasamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pīḍitastu rujā vipraḥ śaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|*  
*stutibhiḥ śrutirūpābhistuṣṭāva balavarjitaḥ \|*  
*māsamātreṇa bhagavāndadau jñānaṃ svayaṃ haraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dhātṛśarmā tu tatprāpya bhāskaraṃ mohanāśanam \|*  
*sūryavāravrataistatra toṣayāmāsa namradhīḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*paṃcābde bhagavānsūryo bhaktibhāvena vatsalaḥ \|*  
*caitryāṃ tamāha vacanaṃ varaṃ brūhi punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dhātṛśarmā tu tacchrutvā bhāskaraṃ mohanāśanam \|*  
*praśrayāvanato bhūtvā tuṣṭāva parayā girā \|\| 19 \|\|*

13-19. At that point of time, Kubera - the lord of riches, getting pleased gave him enormous wealth, besides the Yaksa-vidya which yielded five gold coins daily. The Brahmana used to recite the mantra a thousand times. Then spending one tenth of the wealth, he performed oblation, homa etc. and had his desire fulfilled. In this way, the greater period of his comfortable life was spent. When the time of death arrived, he became ill. Then suffering from the ailment, he performed Vedic stuti in honour of lord Siva. After the lapse of a month, lord Siva getting pleased, bestowed divine knowledge on him, with the use of which the humble Dhatrsarma, performing vratas on Sundays, started adoring the Sungod. After the lapse of five years, the Sungod who is gracious over his devotees, was pleased with his devotion and on the full moon day of the month of Caitra, inspired him to seek for a desired boon. On hearing the words of lord Bhaskara -the Sungod who is remover of the illusion, the Brahmana offered a prayer to him.

## \|\| 2.142.20-22 \|\|

*dhātṛśarmovāca \|*  
*pravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca manasosya tanau priyā \|*  
*rātrirūpā pravṛttiśca nivṛttirdinarūpiṇī \|*  
*bhavatastejasā jāte lokabaṃdhanahetave \|\| 20 \|\|*

*avyakte tu sthitaṃ tejo bhavato divyasūkṣmakam \|*  
*tridhābhūtaṃ tu viśvāya tasmai tejātmane namaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*rājasī yā smṛtā buddhistatpatirbhagavānvidhiḥ \|*  
*bhavatastejasā jātastasmai te vidhaye namaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Dhatrsarma said- There are two beloved in this body known as Pravrtti and Nivrtti (inclination of mind and retirement). Out of these, Pravrtti is the form of night and Nivrtti is the form of the day. Because of the worldly bondages, both the Pravrtti as well as the Nivrtti emerge out of your lustre, which is divine as well as invisible and is divided in three parts for the sake of the world. Therefore, О soul of the form of lustre, I offer my salutation to you. The Rajasi wisdom, having Brahma as her spouse, is born of your lustre. Therefore, salutation to Brahma - the lord of fate, again and again.

## \|\| 2.142.23-24 \|\|

*sāttvikī yā tanau buddhistatpatirbhagavānhariḥ \|*  
*bhavatā nirmitassattvāttasmai te haraye namaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tāmasī mohanā buddhistatpatiśca svayaṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*tamobhūtena bhavatā jātastasmai namonamaḥ \|*  
*dehi me bhagavanmokṣaṃ saṃjñākāṃta namonamaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The Sattviki wisdom which is in our body having lord Hari as its spouse, is born of you. Therefore, salutation to you lord Hari. The preservation of the body is the responsibility of lord Visnu. Therefore, salutation to you as the form of Hari. Similarly, Siva is the lord of Tamasika wisdom or illusion has emerged out of you, since you are the form of darkness. Therefore, salutation to you as the form of tamas. О lord of consciousness, I offer my salutation to you repeatedly. You kindly bestow moksa on me.

## \|\| 2.142.25-29 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*ityevaṃ saṃstutastena bhagavāndhātṛśarmaṇā \|*  
*mahendravacanaṃ prāha taṃ dvijaṃ jñānakovidam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mokṣaścaturvidho vipra sālokyaṃ tapasodbhavam \|*  
*sāmīpyaṃ bhaktito jātaṃ sārūpyaṃ dhyānasaṃbhavam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*sāyujyaṃ jñānato jñeyaṃ teṣāṃ svāmī paraḥ pumān \|*  
*saguṇo viguṇo jñeya ānando mokṣiṇāṃ kramāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*devānāṃ caiva deheṣu ye mokṣāḥ punarāgatāḥ \|*  
*yadgatvā na nivartaṃte tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yatprasannena viprendra sāyujyaṃ me bhavettava \|*  
*manumātraśca yaḥ kālastāvatte mokṣa āsthitaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtardadhe devastena mokṣīkṛto dvijaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

25-29. Brhaspati said- О Mahendra, when the Brahmana Dhatrsarma thus offered his prayer, lord Surya spoke to the Brahmana possessing the enormous wisdom- “O Brahmana, moksa is of four types. Salokya is achieved with the performing of the tapas. Samipya is achieved with the devotion, Sarupya is achieved by meditation and Sayujya is achieved with the achieving of the divine knowledge. The supreme soul is the lord of all these types of moksa (salvation). The bliss of moksa is said to increase gradually to double. The same moksa reaching the body of the gods, is reestablished. Therefore, after reaching there, no return is possible. It is the same, as is called the paramapada of lord Visnu. О foremost of the Brahmanas with the pleasure of whom you have achieved my Sayujya moksa, this would remain in vogue during the time of the life of Manu.” Thus speaking, Sungod disappeared, while the Brahmana achieved the moksa.

## \|\| 2.142.30-35 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktavaṃtaṃ vāgīśaṃ caitramāse divākaraḥ \|*  
*svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śṛṇudhvaṃ sakalā devā yannimitāḥ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*vaṃgīye svāṃśamutpādya devakāryaṃ karomyaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ityuktvā svamukhāttejaḥ samutpādya divākaraḥ \|*  
*svabhaktāyai sukanyāyai dvijapatnyai dadau hi tat \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dhātṛśarmā dvijo yo vai sūrye mokṣamupāgataḥ \|*  
*sa vai tattejasā jātaḥ kāvyakārasya maṃdire \|\| 33 \|\|*

*īśvaro nāma vikhyātaḥ purīśadvānta ātmavān \|*  
*jitvā viprānvedaparānmahatīṃ kīrtimāptavān \|\| 34 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā jīvanabhāṣitam \|*  
*punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ ramyāṃ devabhyo jīvanirmitām \|\| 35 \|\|*

30-35. Suta said- Thus when the glory of the devotion was so spoken out on the occasion of the full moon day of the month of Caitra, the Sungod displayed his true form before Brhaspati. Thereafter, the eternal Sungod, who is also the god of gods, said to the gathering- “O gods, the purpose for which you have assembled at this place, I am going to speak out the same. All of you should please listen. Having been born out of the amsa of my body, I shall accomplish all your divine tasks.” Thus speaking, the Sungod took the ball of lustre out of his mouth and gave it to the Brahmana, who gave it to both his wives. Then the Brahmana named Dhatrsarma achieved the Sayujya moksa of the Sungod and felt quite comfortable. He was reborn in the house of a poet. He was well-versed in all the scriptures and was known by the name of Kesava. He became victorious over many of the Brahmanas in discussion over the Vedic literature and became famous. О Brahmana, thus I have narrated to you the glory as revealed by Brhaspati, but the story which was narrated by Brhaspati to the gods is being spoken by me, you please listen.

## \|\| 2.142.36-52 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*māyāvatyāṃ dvijaḥ kaścinmitraśarmeti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*kāvyavidyāparo nityaṃ rasikaḥ kāminīpriyaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kuṃbharāśiṃ mayi prāpte gaṃgādvāre mahotsavaḥ \|*  
*babhūva bahu lairbhūpeḥ kāritastīrthatatparaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tatrotsave narā nāryyo bahubhūṣaṇabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*samāyayurdarśanārthe paramānandanirbharāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mitraśarmā tu sa prāpya kāmasenasya vai sutām \|*  
*kāvyakelikalāyuktāṃ dvādaśābdamayīṃ śubhām \|\| 39 \|\|*

*dākṣiṇātyasya bhūpasya tanayāṃ madhurānanām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ tadvaśitvamupāgataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sā tu taṃ citriṇī nāmnā mitraśarmāṇamuttamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tu mūrcchitā cāsīdvipramūrtirhadi sthitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*svagehaṃ punarāgatya citriṇī bhāskaraṃ prabhum \|*  
*pratyahaṃ pūjayāmāsa bahumānapurassarā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mitraśarmā tu tatsthāne gaṃgākūle manohare \|*  
*prātaḥ snātvā śucirbhūtvā vaiśākhe jalamadhyagaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*stotramādityahṛdayamajapatsūryatatparaḥ \|*  
*pratyahaṃ dvādaśāvartaistoṣayāmāsa bhāskaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

*māsānte bhagavānsūryo dadau tasmai hi taṃ varam \|*  
*sa tu labdhavaro vipraḥ svagehaṃ punarāgataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*citriṇī tu varaṃ prāptā vāṃchitaṃ lokabhāskarāt \|*  
*punastau pitarau svapne bhāskareṇa prabodhitau \|\| 46 \|\|*

*mitraśarmāṇamāhūya varayāmāsatuḥ sutām \|*  
*svānte nivāsayāmāsa kāmasenaśca daṃpatī \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tau tu cakraṃ mudāviṣṭau pratyahaṃ sūryadevatam \|*  
*tāmrapātre ca tadyaṃtraṃ lekhayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ījatū raktakusumairvrataṃ kṛtvā ravipriyam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*śatābdavapuṣau cobhau nirjarau śramavarjitau \|*  
*ārogyau maraṇaṃ prāpya sāmīpyaṃ ca ravergatau \|\| 50 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā ravergāthāṃ vaiśākhyāṃ devarāṭ svayam \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ bhāskaraṃ devaṃ dadarśa sahitaṃ suraiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*bhaktinamrānsurāndṛṣṭvā bhagavāṃstimirāpahaḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ ramyaṃ devakāryaparaṃ śubham \|*  
*mamāṃśāttanayo bhūmau bhaviṣyati surottama \|\| 52 \|\|*

36-52. Brhaspati said- In the town of Mayavati, once there lived a Brahmana named Mitrasarma, who always remained busy in composing of poetry. He was the lover of a damsel. When the sun was in the sign of Aquarius, great festivities were organized at Haridvara in which the rulers of many countries participated. The festivities were attended by the lovers of supreme bliss besides the men and the women adorned with all the ornaments comprising of the great community. Mitrasarma also reached there to attend the festivities and felt attracted towards the daughter of the king Kamasena from south. She was of twelve years age and was well-versed in poetry, besides being an auspicious figure with beautiful face, had vast eyes resembling those of a doe. Looking at her, Mitrasarma fell for her beauty and became anxious. The girl, who was known by the name of Citrini, looking at the Brahmana, established his figure in her heart and was fainted. Returning home, the girl named Citrini started worshipping the Sungod with great devotion. On the other hand, Mitrasarma, while staying over the bank of the river Ganga, starting from the month of Vaisakha, getting free from his daily mediation in the morning, started reciting the Adityahrdaya stotra of the Sungod twelve times a day on each day. By so doing, the Brahmana boy was trying to please the Sungod. At the end of the month, the Sungod was pleased with him and granted a boon to him. After getting a boon, the Brahmana boy returned to his place. Citrini too received the desire boon from the Sungod. The Sungod then introduced them to the parents of both of them in dream. Thereafter, the king Kamasena called for Mitras'arma and married his daughter Citrini with him. After marriage, both of them were made to live with the king. Passing their time delightfully, both of them started worshipping the Sungod. The Surya-mantra was got written over the copper plate and both of them offered the red flowers to the same. They also pleased the Sungod by performing the vratas on every Sunday. By so doing, both of them remaining young like the gods, started leading a comfortable life. At the time of their death, they achieved moksa, disowning their bodies. Listening to the glory of the month of Vaisakha, the lord Mahendra has face to face meeting with the Sungod. Finding the gods having been filled with utmost devotion, Sungod - the remover of darkness, said to them- “O best of the gods, a part of mine would appear on earth for the establishment of the task of the gods.

## \|\| 2.142.53-56 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā svasya biṃbasya tejorāśiṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*samutpādya kṛtaḥ kāśyāṃ rāmānaṃdastatobhavat \|\| 53 \|\|*

*devalasya ca viprasya kānyakubjasya vai sutaḥ \|*  
*bālyātprabhṛti sa jñānī rāmanāmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*pitrā mātrā parityakto rāghavaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tadā tu bhagavānsākṣāccaturdaśakalo hariḥ \|*  
*sītāpatistaddhṛdaye nivāsaṃ kṛtavānmudā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra mitradevāṃśato yathā \|*  
*rāmānaṃdastu balavānharibhakteśca saṃbhavaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

53-56. Suta said- Thus speaking, the Sungod, taking out a portion from the solar disc, dropped it in the city of Kasi from which Ramananda was born of a Brahmana who was a temple priest. He was quite learned ever since his childhood and was also devoted to Sri Rama. When he was disowned by his parents, he took refuge with the lord. Lord Rama - the husband of Sita, possessing fourteen digits besides being the form of Visnu, getting pleased with him, dwelt in his heart. О Brahmana, thus I have narrated to you the story of Ramananda who was the amsa of the Sungod and turned out to be a great devotee of Sri Rama.

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*

57-67. Brhaspati said- I am narrating to you a pleasant story of the Sungod, for the month of Jye$tha. Earlier during the time of Satyayuga, there once lived a Brahmana named Aryama, who was well-versed in the Vedas and the post-Vedic literature. There was also a king named Sraddha-yajna. His daughter named Pitrmati was married to the Brahmana. The Вrahmana named Aryama produced seven sons and a chaste daughter who was devoted to her husband. His sons were quite intelligent, well-versed in the Dharmasastras. Once the Brahmana, deeply thinking in his mind, adored the Sungod for achieving the riches. He worshipped the Sungod variously. He offered white flowers and white sandalpaste in the morning, while the red flowers and red sandalpaste was offered by him in the noon. During the evening time, he offered the yellow flowers and the yellow sandalpaste. He performed the worship of the Sungod for a period of one month and at the end of the month of Jyestha, the Sungod presented him with an auspicious gem which yields a sera (95 kgs) of gold daily. With the wealth thus made available, the Brahmana spent enough of it in the religious functions. He built on earth several of the wells, step-wells, tanks and beautiful temples. Subsequently, for the delight of the Sungod, after the completion of these activities, he spent a youthful and healthy life for a thousand years. Thereafter, disowning his body, he achieved the Suryaloka and dwelt there for a lakh of years, and after which he achieved the form of the Sun. Thus, I have narrated to you the glory of the Sungod. Therefore, О Indra, you should worship the Sungod in the form of the solar disc.” On hearing these words, the gods then started adoring the Sungod by reciting the stories of the solar race in prose. The Sungod then getting pleased with them, appeared before them in the month of Jyestha and addressed the gods thus- “O gods, during the terrific age of Kaliу lord Krsna would be bom as Nimbaditya and shall perform the task of the gods, gloriously with fame, besides stopping the decline of the dharma.

68-85. Suta said- Now you listen to the story of the birth of Nimbarka, who had been commanded by lord Visnu to perform according to the instructions of the lord. To the south of the Meru mountain over the auspicious banks of the river, there is a Tailanga country which is served by the great Rsis. All of you should incarnate there and have an audience with the gods. Then patronising the noble dharma as revealed by Narada, in an unattached manner, you should live on earth. Making your hermitages at Haridvara, Mathura, Naimisaranya etc. you should live there besides making my Sudarsana hermitage. Tailanga country should be inhabited by great sages and the hermiatge of Sudarsana will be resided by a sage of Bhrgu vamsa named Aruna who will be the master of all Vedas and Vedangas. He will be possessing the shine of Visnucakra along with his wife Jayanti. Jayanti achieved her great husband by adoring the goddess Manasa with the splendour of Moongod. She was shining with all auspicious gunas as moon shines on the day of Purnima in the month of Karttika. Till such time the sun shines in the sky, you should take your food during the day only. On hearing these words, all of them accepted it and after getting the food prepared, all of them were made to be seated for taking the food. In the mean time, the sun was set. But he again initiated the Sungod, as a result of which all the sages could witness the Sungod resembling the lemon tree. The sages present there praised him immensely and uttered- “Well done”, “Well done.” Form that time onwards, the boy was called by the name of Nimbaditya on earth.

## Chapter 143. Birth of Madhvacarya, Sridharacarya, Visnusvami, Vanibhusana, Bhattojidiksita and Acarya Varahamihira

*aṣṭavarṣasahasrāṇi divyāni padamuttamam \|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ mahendraḥ surasaṃyutaḥ \|*

*āṣāḍhapūrṇimāyāṃ ca sa devo jagatītale \|*

*vṛndāvane mahāramye janayiṣye kalau bhaye \|*

1-10. Brhaspati said- О Indra, in the early Tretdyuga, a Brahmana named Sakrasarma lived in the city of Ayodhya. He was an auspicious soul and spent his time in worship of the gods. The Brahmana delightfully worshipped individually Asvinlkumaras, the eleven Rudras, eight Vasus and the Sungod, making use of the hymns of Yajurveda. Thereafter, he pleased then with delicious items of food. Getting pleased with his devotion, the petty gods besides the thirty three deities made his inaccessible desire a success. He remaihed young upto ten thousand years and spent a comfortable life. At the time of death, he was absorbed in the Sungod, where he lived in the solar disc for a lakh of years and by the grace of the gods, he reached Bahmaloka, where he lived for a period of eight thousand divine years. He was lodged in the same solar disc in which the Sungod himself lived. Hearing this, in the month of Asadha, the gods with Suresa -Indra humbly adored the Sungod. On the full moon day of the month of Asadha, he appeared on earth and said to the gods- “At the terrific time of Kali, in the pleasant orchard of Vrndavana, the Sungod in the form of a Brahmana, shall establish the task of the gods. He would be bom as a son in the abode of a Brahmana named Madhava and would be known by the name of Madhu. He would be a great preacher of Mahayoga and the Vedic dharma.

## \|\| 2.143.11-12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavānsūryo devakāryārthamudyataḥ \|*  
*svāṃgāttu teja utpādya vṛṃdāvanamapre ṣayat \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vimukhānmadhurālāpairvaśīkṛtya samantataḥ \|*  
*tebhyaśca vaiṣṇavīṃ śaktiṃ pradadau bhuktimuktidām \|*  
*madhvācārya iti khyātaḥ prasiddho'bhūnmahītale \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Suta said- Thus speaking, the Sungod, getting ready for the performing of the task of the gods, taking out a part of lustre out of his body, sent it to Vridavana. Having been bom there, the child overpowered his opponents and bestowed the Vaisnavi sakti, which bestows devotion as well as the salvation and took them as their disciples. Since that date, he came to be known as Madhvacarya on earth.

*śantanustu tadā rājā sūryavrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*

*yaṃ yaṃ kareṇa spṛśati vṛddho bhavati vai yuvā \|*

*sa vai paṃcaśatāyuśca nirjaro nirupadravaḥ \|*

*ityevaṃvādinaṃ jīvaṃ parjanyo bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa prayāgaṃ prati cāgataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*murā nāha prasannātmā mleccharājye kalau yuge \|*  
*vṛndāvane samāgamya devakāryaṃ karomyaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

13-28. Brhaspati said- There had been a Brahmana who lived in Dvaparayuga and was known by the name of Meghasarma. He had been quite learned, full of wisdom, religious minded, besides being the preacher of the Vedic dharma. He was a true devotee and whatever he produced by farming, he used one tenth of the income for the religious purpose. Once during the time of the king Santanu’s rule, the rains failed. But the clouds poured rain in the fields of Meghasarma which were spread in an area of a krosa. At that point of time, the cereals could be procured from the shops by making payment of a drona coin. Meghasarma alone had enough of wealth as well as the cereals. The rest of the people, after suffering from the failure of rains, went and took refuge with the king Santanu. The king felt disturbed at the sufferings of the people. He called for Meghasarma and said to him- “O best of the Brahmanas, salutation to you. You kindly be my preceptor as a result of which there should be no failure of rain in this kingdom. You issue a command accordingly.” At these words of the king, Meghasarma said to him- “With the start of the month of Sravana, you call for twelve Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas and make them recite the Surya mantra for a lakh of times. Later, on the full moon day, you yourself performing the vrata, should pour one tenth of the number of offerings in the fire when it is in flames. Thereafter, the oblation and the sprinkling of the water should be done appropriately. After achieving success, you will become comfortable.” Accepting the words of the Brahmana, the king performed the japam, after which he served food to the Brahmanas. The Sungod getting pleased, made the clouds to pour the rain. At that point of time, after performing the parayana, the king Santanu gained glory and came to be known as the noble soul. To whomsoever the king touched with his hand, he inspite of his being old became youthful. With the influence of the Sungod, the same quality was gained by Meghasarma. The said Meghasarma led the youthful life for a period of five hundred years and after his death, he attained the Suryaloka. Spending a lakh of years there, he would achieve Brahmaloka. The Sungod getting pleased with Brhaspati, appeared before him at Prayaga and then said to the other gods-“During the age of Kali, Mleccharaja, after incarnating in Vrndavana, has decided to perform the task of the gods.”

## \|\| 2.143.29-30 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavānsūryo gatvā vṛndāvanaṃ śubham \|*  
*śrīdharo nāma vikhyātaḥ putrobhūdvedaśarmaṇaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ samālokya viśāradaḥ \|*  
*cakāra viduṣāmarthe pradīptaṃ śrīdharaḥ śubham \|*  
*śrīmadbhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ purāṇopari tatkṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Suta said- Thus speaking, the Sungod departed for Vrndavana. Reaching there, he was bom as the son of Vedasarma and was known by the name of Sridhara and attained enormous glory. This learned person, taking Srimadbhagavata Purana to be quite mysterious, wrote a beautiful commentary on it for the benefit of the learned people. The commentary by 6ridhara on the Srimadbhagavata Purana is held in high esteem by the people of wisdom.

*satyavādī mahāsādhuḥ steyahiṃsāvivarjitaḥ \|*

*ekadā pathi bhikṣārthaṃ gacchatastasya bhūpateḥ \|*

*babhūva vāṭikāṃ kṛtvā kalirdānamanoharām \|*  
*tamuvāca dvijo bhūtvā prāṃśuśarmanvacaḥ śṛṇu \|\| 34 \|\|*

*mameyaṃ vāṭikā ramyā tatra gaccha sukhī bhava \|*  
*iti vipravacaḥ śrutvā vāṭikāṃ tāṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kalistu vāṭikāmadhye gatvā ramyaphalāni ca \|*  
*troṭayitvā dadau tasmai bhojanārthaṃ mahākhalaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*prāṃjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā prāṃśuśarmāṇamabravīt \|*  
*bhuṃkṣva vipra mayā sārddhaṃ kaliṃdasya phalaṃ śubham \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ityuktaḥ sa tu taṃ prāha vihasya madhura svaram \|*  
*vṛkṣe bibhītake caiva kaliṃdasya phale tathā \|*  
*kaliḥ prāptaḥ smṛtaḥ prājñaistasmādgṛhṇāmyahaṃ na hi \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yadi dattaṃ phalaṃ bhaktyā tvayādya dvijasevinā \|*  
*śālagrāmāya vai dattvā prasādaṃ tadbhajāmyaham \|*  
*śālagrāmaḥ svayaṃ brahma saccidānandavigrahaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

31-39. Brhaspati said- Earlier during the time of the start of the age of Kali, there lived a Brahmana by the name of Pransu, who always remained engaged in the study of the Vedas as well the Sastras. He adored the gods and the guests, was truthful, extremely noble, besides being free from the blemishes of theft and violence. He brought up his wife and son by means of begging. О king, once when he was going for begging, he had an encounter with an illusory cheat. The cheat falsely creating an orchard and taking to the form of a Brahmana, said to him- “0 Pransusarman, you listen to my words. This is my beautiful orchard. You better walk into my orchard for a while.” On hearing these words, Pransusarma went into the orchard and had some rest there. After sometime, the wicked Kali plucked some ripe fruits from the orchard and gave them to Pransu for eating and then said to the Brahmana- “You kindly eat the watermelon fruit with me.” On hearing these words, the noble Brahmana spoke with sweet voice- “The learned people believe that the Kali resides in the fruits of watermelon and myrobalan, therefore I cannot accept it. In case, you have offered it to me as a Brahmana, then I would offer it to lord Saligrama first and then consume it as his prasada, because Saligrama himself is the form of Brahman and is also known as blissful. It is because of his grace only, the prohibited stuff also becomes eatables.” On hearing this, Kali was extremely disappointed and felt ashamed as well.

## \|\| 2.143.40-52 \|\|

*darśanāttasya cābhakṣyo bhakṣyo bhavati niścitaḥ \|*

*iti śrutvā prāṃśuśarmā tatphalaṃ vatsamuṃḍavat \|*

*tadā tu sa kalirbhūpastaṃ vipraṃ tāḍya vetasaiḥ \|*  
*kārāgāre lohamaye kṛtavānnyāyamitrakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*prātaḥkāle ravau prāpte prāṃśuśarmā suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva bhāskaraṃ devaṃ stotrairṛgvedasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavānraviḥ sākṣātsanātanaḥ \|*  
*viprasya karṇayorvākyamuvāca nabhaseritam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*śṛṇu vipra mahābhāga kālarūpo hariḥ svayam \|*  
*caturyugaṃ tena kṛtaṃ viśvapālādihetave \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kalirviśvasamūhānāṃ mṛtyave racitastathā \|*  
*ato ghore kalau prāpte viṣṇumāyāvinirmitam \|*  
*kaliñjaraṃ ca nagaraṃ tatroṣya mudito bhava \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ityuktvā rakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tasya viprasya bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*kaliñjare ca nagare preṣayāmāsa taṃ dvijam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sapādaśatavarṣaṃ ca dvijastatra vasanravim \|*  
*ārādhya putrapatnīko ravilokamupāyayau \|\| 49 \|\|*

*sa vai bhādrapade māsi sūryo bhūtvāyutābdakam \|*  
*paścādbrahmapuraṃ prāpya paramānandamāptavān \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā jīvastamabravīt \|\| 50 \|\|*

*āgatya bhāskaro devaḥ pūrṇimāyāṃ tu bhādrake \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśe kalau prāpte svayaṃ jātaḥ kaliñjare \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śivadattasya tanayo viṣṇuśarmeti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*vedaśāstrakalābhijño vaiṣṇavo deva pūjakaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

40-52. The Brahmana then carried the fruit and proceeded to his place in the village. On his arrival there, the king came to the Brahmana and asked him- “What had been brought by you? I would like to have a look at it” On hearing this, Pransusarma handed over the fruit to the king. When he looked at the fruit, at that time he felt totally surprised. Then the Kali king, using a cane-stick, started beating the Brahmana. Thereafter, he put him in iron chains and imprisoned. The next morning when the sun rose, Pransusarma reciting the hymns from the Rgveda, adored the Sungod. At that point of time, the Sungod getting pleased, poured the words into the ears of Pransu- “Lord Visnu himself is the form of death. He has created four yugas on earth and out of them Kali has been created for the destruction of the entire universe. Therefore, during the horrific time of Kali, you go to Kalinjara and lead a comfortable life there. The Sungod then protecting the Brahmana, safely transported him to the fort of the Kalinjara. The Brahmana, while his stay at that place, spent comfortable time for a hundred and twenty five years with his wife and the son. Then in the month of Bhadrapada, he turned himself as the sun and lived in Suryaloka for a thousand years and then he reached Brahmaloka, where he achieved the supreme bliss. О Brahmana, thus I have narrated to you the entire story which had been told by Brhaspati to me. On the full moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, during the time of twenty eighth Kaliyuga, Bhaskara himself arrived in the city of Kalinjara and was born in the house of Sivadatta. He became popular by the name of Visnusarma. He was well-versed in ail the Vedas and the Sastras and was devoted to Visnu.

## \|\| 2.143.53-57 \|\|

*caturvarṇānnarānvipra samāhūya harergṛhe \|*  
*vacanaṃ prāha dharmātmā viṣṇuḥ sarveśvaro hariḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ śiṣya viśvakāraṇa kārakaḥ \|*  
*bhagavānsaccidānandaścaturviśatitattvavān \|*  
*devānsasarja lokārthe tasmātsarveśvaro'bhavat \|\| 54 \|\|*

*pūrvaṃ hi sakalāndevānpūjayitvā naraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*paścācca pūjayedviṣṇuṃ yathā bhṛtyā nṛpaṃ punaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu te sarve praśasya bahudhā hi tam \|*  
*viṣṇusvāmīti taṃ nāmnā kathāṃ cakruśca harṣitāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra viṣṇusvāmī yathābhavat \|*  
*punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ ramyāṃ bṛhaspatimukheritām \|\| 57 \|\|*

53-57. He invited people of all the castes in the temple of the lord and said- “The divine soul lord Visnu is supreme. О disciple, I am going to speak out the cause for the same. Because of his creating the universe, he has become the creator of all. You please listen. The blissful lord getting divided in twenty four tattvas, produce the gods for the welfare of the lokas. Therefore, he is treated to be the lord of all. Because of this, as the attendant is adored first and then the master, similarly, before worshipping all the gods, lord Visnu should be worshipped first of all.” On hearing this, all the people present there praised him immensely. He therefore attained the glory by the name of Visnusvaml and felt immensely delighted. Thus, I have narrated to you the story of the presence of Visnusvami. Now, I am narrating another beautiful story which was spoken by Brhaspati in earlier times. You please listen.

## \|\| 2.143.58-64 \|\|

*jīva uvāca \|*  
*purā caitrarathe deśe bhagaśarmā dvijo'bhavat \|*  
*svarveśyā maṃjughoṣāyāṃ munimedhāvinā bhuvi \|\| 58 \|\|*

*pitṛmātṛparityaktaḥ sa bālaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*sūryamārādhayāmāsa tapasā śatavārṣikam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sūryamaṇḍalamadhyasthā sāvitrī nāma devatā \|*  
*sarvasūryasya jananī kanyā tanmaṇḍalasya vai \|\| 60 \|\|*

*prasannā tapasā tasya prādurbhūtā sanātanī \|*  
*āśvine māsi rājānaṃ dvijaṃ cakre ca maṇḍale \|\| 61 \|\|*

*lakṣavarṣasahasrāṇi māsi māsi tathāśvine \|*  
*prakāśaṃ kṛtavānvipraḥ pūjito lokavāsibhiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tvaṃ sūryaṃ bhaja devendra sa te kāryaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*iti śrutvāśvine māsi sa ravirdevapūjanāt \|\| 63 \|\|*

*pratyakṣamagamattatra vacaḥ prāha surānprati \|*  
*kānyakubje śubhe deśe vāṇībhūṣaṇa ityaham \|*  
*bhavāmi satyadevasya viprasya tanayaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

58-64. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, in the Caitraratha country,, the sage Medhavi produced a child named Bhagasarma from the womb of an apsara named Manjughosa. The child after having been abandoned by the parents, got devoted to the Sungod and started worshipping him. After performing tapas for a hundred years, the goddess Savitrl who is lodged in the middle of the Sun disc and is the mother of the Sungod besides being the daughter of the mandala, delightfully appeared before the Brahmana and made him the ruler of the month of Asvina. The people of that country adored the Brahmana, who bestowed the month of Asvina for a thousand lakh of years. Therefore, О Devendra, you should adore the same Sungod, who would bestow success on you. On hearing this, he adored the Sungod of the month of Asvina, who feeling pleased appeared before them and said to them- “I shall incarnate in the house of a Pransu named Satyadeva in the town of Kanyakubja. I shall be then known by the name of Vanibhusana.

## \|\| 2.143.65-69 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavānsūryo jātaḥ kānyapure śubhe \|*  
*jitvā pākhaṃḍino viprānmāṃsabhakṣaṇatatparān \|*  
*chaṃdograṃthaṃ svanāmnā vai kṛtavāndaivatapriyaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*matsyamāṃsāśanā viprā mṛgameṣājakāśanāḥ \|*  
*ekībhūya samāgamya cakruḥ śāstrārthamulbaṇam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*kalinā'dharmamitreṇa rakṣitāste dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dvijaṃ ca parājitya matsyaketuṃ ca tadgṛhe \|\| 67 \|\|*

*balācca staṃbhanaṃ cakrustadā viṣṇupriyo dvijaḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavīṃ śaktimāgamya svamukhānmīnakhāditān \|\| 68 \|\|*

*saṃjīvya darśayāmāsa te dṛṣṭvā vismitāstadā \|*  
*śiṣyabhūtāśca te tasya vaiṣṇavaṃ matamā gaman \|\| 69 \|\|*

65-69. Suta said- Saying this, the Sungod was bom in the city of Kanyakubja and became victorious over the heretical Brahmanas who were non-vegetarians. Then the Sungod, on the basis of his name, composed a book in meters. At that point of time, the Brahmanas who consumed fish, meat of deer, sheep, goat etc. collected and started violent debate with him. Having been protected by Kali - the friend of Adharma, the Brahmanas defeated them and hoisted the flag of fish in their houses. Then the Brahmana Visnupriya invoked the Vais navi sakti and vomited out the fish which had been taken by him, alive form his mouth and displayed it before them, which surprised them all. Thereafter, taking the Vai§nava faith to be supreme, all of them became his followers.

## \|\| 2.143.70-77 \|\|

*jīva uvāca \|*  
*kadācitsarayūtīre devayājī dvijo'bhavat \|*  
*sarvadevaparo nityaṃ vedapāṭhaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tatsutastu mṛtiṃ prāpto janmamātre hi dāruṇe \|*  
*tadā tu sa dvijaḥ śrutvā sūryadevamatoṣayat \|\| 71 \|\|*

*jijīva tatprasādena vivasvānnāma cābhavat \|*  
*ṣoḍaśābda vapurbhūtvā sarvavidyāviśāradaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*apatyavāndharmaparaḥ sūryavataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*śivarātridine prāpte tatpatnī bhūṣaṇapriyā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*suśīlā nāma vikhyātā patisevārthamāgatā \|*  
*sa vratī rudradevasya dṛṣṭvā tāṃ madhurānanām \|\| 74 \|\|*

*balādgṛhītvā tu niśi bubhuje smaravihvalaḥ \|*  
*maithunasyaiva doṣeṇa tasya kuṣṭho mahānabhūt \|\| 75 \|\|*

*liṃgedriyaṃ ca patitaṃ gudabhraṣṭo mahāṃgaruk \|*  
*kena cidupadeśena ravivārasya vai vratam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*sa cakre dvādaśaṃ premṇā nirāhāro yatendriyaḥ \|*  
*tena vrataprabhāveṇa sarvapīḍā layaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

70-77. Brhaspati said- Once upon a time, there lived a Brahmana named Devayaji over the bank of the river Sarayu, who was devoted to all the gods and was the reciter of the Vedas. His son met with the death soon after his birth. On hearing that, the Brahmana pleased the Sungod and at the same time, by the grace of whom the infant got back his life and was known by the name of Vivasvan. On attaining the age of sixteen years, the boy had achieved proficiency in all the lores. He was quite religious-minded and performed the vratas for the Sungod. Once on the occasion of Sivaratri, his wife named Susikla, adorned with all the ornaments, went to her husband in order to serve him. The Brahmana boy, inspite of his performing the vrata for Siva, was overpowered by lust at the sight of the charming face of his wife and united with her forcibly. As a result of this, he attracted the disease of leprosy. His phallus fell on the ground and the rectum was shattered. His entire body attracted terrific disease which was incurable. At the advice of someone, he observed fast for twelve Sundays, controlling all his sense organs. With the influence of the vrata, all his pains were removed.

## \|\| 2.143.78-81 \|\|

*tadā śraddhā ravau prāptā pratyahaṃ sa dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*āditya hṛdayaṃ japtvā kāmarūpo dvijo'bhavat \|\| 78 \|\|*

*nārībhirbhartsitaḥ pūrvaṃ sotha kāminīyācitaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryavrataṃ kṛtvā brahmadhyānaparo'bhavat \|\| 79 \|\|*

*śatāyurbrāhmaṇo bhūtvā jñānavānrogavarjitaḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā prāṇānravirbhūtvā sūryamaṇḍalamadhyagāt \|\| 80 \|\|*

*kārtike māsi lakṣābdaṃ prakāśaṃ kṛtavānnabhaḥ \|*  
*taṃ ca sūryaṃ mahendrastvaṃ pūjayāśu suraiḥ saha \|\| 81 \|\|*

78-81. Since that time, he developed a great faith in the Sungod and soon thereafter, he started reciting the Adityahrdaya stotra daily and attained the excellent beauty. The one who was denounced by the ladies, with the attaining of his beauty again, all of them became desirous of him. But he kept up the vow of celibacy and always meditated upon Brahma. The said Brahmana in this way lived upto nine hundred years. He remained free from ailments, learned and after leading a comfortable life, met with his end and was lodged in the solar disc. He illuminated the earth for a lakh of years. Therefore, O Mahendra, you should worship the Sungod with all the gods.

## \|\| 2.143.82-98 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā mahendrastu māsamātraṃ hi bhāskaram \|*  
*pūjayitvā vidhānena pūrṇimāyāṃ dadarśa ha \|\| 82 \|\|*

*uvāca śakraṃ sa ravirdevakāryaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*bhaṭṭairvidyāmayairdhūrtaiḥ sūtrapāṭhaśca khaṃḍitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*dhātupāṭho nyapaṭhito bhraṃśārthaḥ svaravarṇakaḥ \|*  
*jitvā tānbhaṭṭapāṣaṃḍānvedamuddhārayāmi bhoḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*ityuktvā sa gataḥ kāśyāṃ gehe vai vedaśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*dīkṣitānvayabhūtasya nāmnā kāryaguṇo'bhavat \|\| 85 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdavapurbhūtvā sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*śivamārādhayāmāsa viśvanāthaṃ śivāpriyam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*trivarṣānte ca bhagavāṃstasmai jñānaṃ mahaddadau \|*  
*tasya jñānaprabhāveṇa vyaktamavyaktamuttamam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*jñātaṃ kāryaguṇenaiva dīkṣitena tadā hṛdi \|*  
*avyakte yadā buddhiḥ sā vidyā dvādaśāṃginī \|\| 88 \|\|*

*vyakte'haṃkārabhūte ca buddhirjñeyā budhairajā \|*  
*avidyā nāma vikhyātā ṣoḍaśāṃgasvarūpiṇī \|\| 89 \|\|*

*avyaktaṃ tu paraṃ brahma vyaktaṃ śabdamayaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*ahaṃkāro lokakaro hi vyakto'ṣṭadaśāṃgakaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*vṛṣarūpadharo mukhyo nandiyānaḥ smṛto budhaiḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgāṇi tasya catvāri tripādo dviśirā vṛṣaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*saptahastastridhā baddho nityaśuddho mukhe sthitaḥ \|*  
*suvantaśca tiṅantaśca kṛdaṃtaścāvyayastathā \|\| 92 \|\|*

*dvaudvau śṛṃgau ca śirasornaṃdiyānasya vai smṛtau \|*  
*bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavaccaiva trayaḥ pādā hi tasya vai \|\| 93 \|\|*

*rūḍhiśca yogarūḍhiśca śabdau tasya śirodvayam \|*  
*kartā karma ca karaṇaṃ saṃpradānaṃ vibhāgataḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*saṃvaṃdhaścādhikāraśca bhujāstasya vṛṣasya vai \|*  
*vākyaṃ svarānvitaṃ jñeyaṃ vibhattyaṃtaṃ padaṃ smṛtam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tābhyāṃ baddhaśca sa vṛṣo nandiyānātha te namaḥ \|*  
*tasyoparisthitaṃ nityamavyaktaṃ liṃgarūpi yat \|\| 96 \|\|*

*jātaśca vṛṣaliṃgābhyāṃ so'haṃkāro hariḥ svayam \|*  
*nārāyaṇaḥ ṣoḍaśātmā bahumūrtiramūrtikaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*iti jñānaṃ hṛdi prāpya tadā siddhāntakaumudīm \|*  
*jitvā bhaṭṭāṃścakārāśu bhaṭṭojiḥ praśruto'bhavat \|\| 98 \|\|*

82-98. Suta said- On hearing this, Mahendra worshipped the Sungod for a month in an appropriate manner. On full moon day, the Sungod was pleased and appeared before him. He said- “I am prepared to perform your task. The wicked and the deceitful Bhatta Panditas, who had desecrated the Sutra-patha, Dhatu-patha and other recitations, besides the vocal recitations as well, I shall defeat them and redeem the Vedas"' Thus speaking, the Sungod proceeded onto KasI and incarnated in the house of Vedasarma Diksita and became famous by the name of Diksita. By reaching the age of twelve years, he had achieved proficiency in all the Sastras and started worshipping lord Siva - the spouse of the goddess Parvati. After the lapse of three years, lord Siva got pleased with him. lord Siva turned him as an extremely learned person, as result of which he attained the complete knowledge of visible and invisible form of the Almighty. When the mind was fixed in the invisible one, he was known as Dvadasanga. With mind having been stabilized by pride, the learned people called him Ajanma or (unborn). Similarly Avidya (ignorance) is described to be of sixteen forms. Invisible or Avyakta is the name of the supreme Brahman, while the visible one is known as Nida or the sound. The visible one which is the form of Ahamkara (pride) besides being the creator of the universe, is of eighteen forms. The learned people have described Nandi in the form of a bull as having four horns, three feet, two heads and seven arms. Getting bound in two ways, the auspicious soul is lodged in the mouth. This bull has the four horns over the head which are known by the names of Subanta, Tinganta, Krdanta and Avyaya. The three feet represent the past, present and future. The two heads as known as Rudhi (production) and Yogarudhi (yogic philosophy). The seven arms represent Karta (the performer), Karma (the deed), Karana (motive), Sampradana (initiation), Apadana (separation), Sambandha (link), Adhikarana (support), and the words with sound and the pada at the end of the division are connected with both of them. Therefore, salutation to the form of Nandi - the invisible holder of Avyakta (invisible). Brahman is lodged over Nandi. With the holding of Linga and the Nandi, arrogance is created who happens to be Hari himself or Narayana of sixteen souls as well as many other forms. Thus enshrining the enormous knowledge in his mind, Diksita defeated the deceitful and wicked Bhatta. Thereafter, he composed Siddhanta-Kaumudi, as a resuit of which he became famous by the name of Bhattoji Diksita.

## \|\| 2.143.99-116 \|\|

*jīva uvāca \|*  
*purā kāṃcīpure ramye gaṇako brāhmaṇottamaḥ \|*  
*purodhāḥ satyadattasya rājño vedaparasya vai \|\| 99 \|\|*

*ekadā gaṇako dhīmānsatyadattamuvāca ha \|*  
*muhūrto'bhijidākhyoyaṃ puṣyanakṣatrasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*hāṭaṃ kuru mahārāja sāṃprataṃ bahuvṛttidam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tathā kṛtvā ḍiṃḍimadhvaninā pure \|*  
*narānājñāpayāmāsa tacchṛṇuṣva surottama \|\| 101 \|\|*

*akrītaṃ yasya vai vastu hāṭe'sminvaiśyakovidaiḥ \|*  
*mayā krītaṃ ca tajjñeyaṃ satyametadvaco mama \|\| 102 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā śūdrajanāścakrurnānāvidhaṃ vasu \|*  
*vaiśyaissarvaṃ tadā krītaṃ mahānhāṭo hi so'bhavat \|\| 103 \|\|*

*ekadā lohakāraśca dāridraṃ loharūpiṇam \|*  
*kṛtvā hāṭamupāgamya śatamudrāmayācata \|\| 104 \|\|*

*akrītaṃ puruṣaṃ rājā jñātvā lohadaridrakam \|*  
*krītaṃ taṃ śatamudrābhirgṛhītvā gehamāgamat \|*  
*kośāgāre tadā rājñā sthāpitobhūddaridrakaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

*niśīthe tama udbhūte karma dharmaśca mā tathā \|*  
*bhūpagehātsamāgatya paśyatastasya nirgatāḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*tatpaścātsatyapuruṣo rājānamidamabravīt \|*  
*daridro yatra bhūpāla tatra karmaparo na hi \|*  
*karmaṇā rahito dharmo bhūtale na sthiro bhavet \|\| 107 \|\|*

*dharmeṇa rahitā lakṣmīrna śobheta kadācana \|*  
*ahaṃ lakṣmyā vihīnaśca na tiṣṭhāmi kadācana \|\| 108 \|\|*

*ityuktvā gantumicchaṃtaṃ gṛhītvā karayornṛpaḥ \|*  
*namrībhūto vacaḥ prāha śṛṇu satyaṃ mama priyam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*na tyājyo hi mayā deva bhavānkiṅgantumarhati \|*  
*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ satyadevo gṛhegamat \|\| 110 \|\|*

*tatpaścācca svayaṃ lakṣmīstadgehe gaṃtumudyatā \|*  
*tāmāha bhūpatirdhīro devi tvaṃ caṃcalā sadā \|\| 111 \|\|*

*acalā bhava bho mātastarhi manmadiraṃ vraja \|*  
*iti śrutvā varaṃ dattvā nṛpagehaṃ yayau tadā \|\| 112 \|\|*

*purodhasaṃ taṃ gaṇakaṃ samāhūya nṛpottamaḥ \|*  
*lakṣasvarṇaṃ dadau tasmai kathitvā sarvakāraṇam \|\| 113 \|\|*

*putrajanmani kāle tu saṃprāptaṃ tena vai dhanam \|*  
*vyayaṃ kṛtvā dhanaṃ sarvaṃ poṣayāmāsa bālakam \|\| 114 \|\|*

*pūṣā nāma tato jātaṃ mārgaśīrṣe śubhe dine \|*  
*sa tu sūryaṃ samārādhya jyotiḥśāstraparaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*sūrye tu mokṣamagamaddevadevaprasādataḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ mārgamāse vai raviṃ devendra pūjaya \|\| 116 \|\|*

99-116. Brhaspati (Jiva) said- In earlier times, there lived a Brahmana named Ganaka at Kancipuri. The king of the place was the follower of the Vedic dharma known by the name of Satyadeva. The said Brahmana happened to be the priest of the king. Once the intelligent Ganaka Brahmana said to the king Satyadeva- “O king, in the Pusya constellation, the auspicious time known as Abhijit is arriving. You better start organizing a bazaar (market) which would yield you great dividends.” On hearing this, the king made an announcement with the beating of the drum, collected all the people there and said to them-“I am going to tell you whatever the king told to his people. You please listen.” He issued a command- “In case no one purchases the commodity of a trader in this bazaar, the same would be purchased by the king himself. This is my truthful resolve ” On hearing these words, the Sudras also made various things and started bringing them in the bazaar for sale. Once a blacksmith made the figure of a pauper and brought it for sale in the bazaar and fixed its price at hundred rupees. The king observed that no one was prepared to purchase that figure. Therefore, he purchased the same and bringing it at home, deposited it in the treasury. On the same day, at the dead of night in complete darkness, the Karma (deeds), Dharma and Laksmi left the place in his full view. Thereafter, the noble person also said to the king- “O king, the abode in which the poverty dwells, such a person is unable to perform his duty. When he becomes actionless, his dharma also does not remain on earth. Having been deprived of the dharma, such a person’s home is never graced by the goddess Laksmi. In a house which is devoid of Laksmi, I also do not stay there.” Thus speaking, Satyadeva was also desirous of leaving the place, when the king addressed them in a humble voice- “O Satyadeva, you listen to my words. О Deva, you are extremely dear to me. Therefore, I can never disown you. Would you like to leave me even now?” On hearing these words, Satyadeva returned to the abode of the king. Thereafter, Lak$ml also became anxious to return to the abode of the king. Finding her desirous of returning, the king said- “O goddess, you are always unstable, but О mother, now you go to my place and live there permanently.” On hearing this, Laksmi bestowed a boon on the king, besides her permanent stay in the palace. Thereafter, the king called for his Ganaka priest and narrated the entire sequence of events to him, giving him a lakh of gold coins at the same time. At the same time, a son was bom in the house of the priest. Making use of the riches, he brought up the child very well. The boy was bom on the auspicious day of Margasirsa and came to be known as Pusa, who worshipping the Sungod, achieved proficiency in the science of astrology. After his death, with the grace of the Sungod, he was absorbed in the solar disc. Therefore, adoring the Sungod in the month of Margasirsa is highly benefecial.

117-125. Suta said- After worshipping Indra, at that point of time, Surya appeared there in the form of Рusа before the gods and spoke in sweet voice- “In the town of Ujjayini, in the house of Rudrapasu, I shall be born by the name of Mihiracarya and shall became famous by this name. Then I shall compose the treatise on astrology.” Thus speaking, lord Рusа was born in the house of a Brahmana. During the Мulа-Naksatra and auspicious Abhijityoga, the boy was born and due to the same, his parents put him in a wooden box and consigned the child in a river at the dead of night. The river carried the boy to the ocean of Lanka. Living there, he attained mastery in the astrological science. He specialized in Jataka, Phalita and Mukaprasna (basic question). Thereafter, Vibhisana - the lord of the Raksasas, went to him and said- “O great devotee and beloved of Hari, salutation to you. I have been kidnapped by the demonesses. I take refuge in you.” On hearing this, the best of the Brahmanas, sent him back to his birth place. Reaching there, the astrological treatise which is the part of the Vedas and which had been destroyed by the Mlecchas and had been divided in three parts, was redeemed by him.

## Chapter 144. Birth of Dhanvantari, Susruta and Jayadeva

1-10. Suta said- In the holy place of Prayaga, lord Brhaspati narrated the excellent glory of the Sungod again and said- “O best of the gods, earlier in the Tretayuga with the order of Lord Siva, the Sungod was bom at Pratisthanapura. I am going to talk about the same. You please listen. At the end of the Tretayuga, Pariksita was the king of Simhala island, who followed the Vedic dharma and always adored the gods and the guests. His daughter named Bhanumati always performed the vrata of the Sungod. Getting pleased of her devotion, the Sungod daily visited her house at noon and consumed the food offered by her. Once on Sunday, the maid having lotus like soft limbs, started going out for taking a bath. On reaching the place, Narada also reached there. Finding the lonely lady bathing in water, he picked up her costumes and spoke fearlessly- “O excellent beauty, I have been upset with your side glance. Therefore, you hold my hand.” At these words o f Narada, the maid lowering her head, said to the sage- ”0 divine R$i, you kindly listen to my words, I am a maid and you are the bestower of the son. The damsels adore you remaining in the sky. Because of which they are known like Menaka, Rambha etc. and I am myself known as a human being. The bad smell always remains in the human body with nine gates, which can never be found in the divine damsels.”

## \|\| 2.144.11-13 \|\|

*iti śrutvā vacastasyā lajjito nāradastadā \|*

*kuṣṭhībhūtaṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|*
