11-13. On hearing this, Narada felt extremely ashamed. Subsequently, he went to lord Mahadeva and narrated to him the entire story. Lord Siva, who bestows welfare to the universe, finding Narada suffering from leprosy, adored the Sungod who appeared in person at that point of time, relieved Narada of the disease and then addressed lord Siva- “O Mahadeva, you kindly give me the command to enable me to grant you your desire.”

14-16. At these words of the Sungod, lord Siva said - “Taking to the form of a Brahmana, you accept that girl.” Subsequently, the Sungod did so. The Sungod then married Bhanumati and started performing tap as, as a result of which he regained the Suryaloka. It is he who provides light in the month of Раusа. Therefore, О Mahendra you perform the task of the gods, by adoring the Sungod.”

## \|\| 2.144.16-23 \|\|

16-23. Suta said- Listening to the words of the preceptor, Suresa (Indra) with other gods, adored the Sungod in the month of Pausa, after which Sungod getting pleased, said to the gods with his noble voice- “I shall be born at Kasi by the name of Dhanvantari and living there, I shall relieve the people of their ailments with which the people suffer during the age of Kali. In this way, the task of the Devas would be established.” Thus speaking, the lord Bhaskara arrived in the city of Kasi and was born as a son in the house of Kalpadatta Brahmana. Getting delighted, he accepted the royal prince Susruta besides the old Brahmana as his disciples. After that, he composed the Kalpaveda, by which the ailing human body is rejuvenated. All the secrets of that kalpa are enshrined in this tantra. At that point of time, that particular form of the Sungod came to be known on earth as Dhanvantari, with the very look of whom, one is relieved of all the ailments. Susruta studied a hundred chapters of the Kalpaveda composed by Dhanvantari and composed Sausruta-tantra.

24-31. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, in the pleasant city of Pampapura, there lived a Brahmana known by the name of Heli, who was proficient in all the sixty four kalas (arts). He adored the Sungod daily. Discarding the practice of receiving the charities, he patronized the display of art, which included art in costumes, art in iron, paintings and making of images in metals. Thus he practiced all types of arts, as a result of which he earned five thousand gold coins. Within a month, he created a fruit. With the wealth earned by him, he performed a yajna, which pleased the Sungod. Because of this, the Sungod illuminates the world in each one of the months of Magha. Hie same Brahmana known by the name of Hell, performed many yajnas which pleased the Sungod. As a result of this, he also built a pillar in the Pampa lake. The Sungod himself reached the Pampa lake at noon, perched over the top of the pillar and accepted the eatables offered to him by the Brahmana. In this way, the Sungod accepted the eatables in every month and lived in a pleasant mood. Then the Brahmana after living on earth for a thousand years, met with the end of his life. After death, he reached the solar disc and again pleased the Sungod in the month of Magha. Therefore, О Devendra, you must worship the same Sungod, who would surely establish your task.

32-46. Suta said—Listening to these words of Brhaspati, together with all other gods, Indra worshipped Sungod in the form of Visvakarma. At that point of time, the Sungod getting pleased, pleased the gods in the form of Tvasta. He said to the gods with sweet voice- “O best of the gods, you listen to my words. In a village named Bilva in Vanga country, I shall be bom as Vedic scholar, popularly known by the name of Jayadeva, who would be the foremost of all the poets.” Thus speaking, reaching the Vanga country, the Sungod was bom in the house of a Kanduki Brahmana. He served his parents continuously from the age of five to twelve years. After the death of his parents, he pleased the departed souls by performing their last rites. Performing their sraddha, he made them dwell in the heaven. After the ceremony of yajnopavita for Jayadeva was performed, he took to renunciation and started living there in a close by forest. At that point of time, he was twenty three years old. By about the same time, a Brahmana offered his daughter to the lord Jagannatha. After the puja had been performed, the eternal Aniruddha, who was present in wood there, said to the Brahmana-“O Satyadeva, you listen to my words. The body of Jayadeva is my body. Therefore, at my command, you offer your daughter Padmavati to Jayadeva. At these words of the lord, the Brahmana at once went to the place of recluse Jayadeva. He left his daughter there and returned to his home with delight. The girl Padmavati took him as her beautiful husband and served him for many years. Jayadeva then taking to a samadhi, composed Nirukta based on the Vedas, which was variously interpreted by the learned people. He composed Nirukta of five types.

*vismito dharmapālaśca jayadevamuvāca ha \|*

47-57. The Sudras of Naga dynasty had desecrated the Prakrta language. They were fools and favourites of Kali and were defeated. For the sake of the gods, they created the Panini treatise. Once the wicked Kali, entering the hearts of the thieves, made them steal the wealth of Jayadeva, which had been given to him by the king. However, they left Padmavati taking her to be a chaste woman, but Jayadeva’s hands and feet were cut off and he fell into a deep pit, while crying. The crying husband was rescued by the wife from the pit somehow. At the same time, the king was moving for hunting and on his way, he found Jayadeva without the hands and feet and asked him- “Who has put you in such a miserable condition?” He replied- “O lord, I have achieved this position because of my own deeds. Nobody is at fault in this case.” On hearing this, the king Dharmapala put him into a palanquin and with the help of his queen, proceeded towards his palace. Reaching the palace, the king received diksa from him. Thereafter, a dharmasala was built. Once the thieves, who had been inspired by the Kali, taking to the form of the Vaisnavas, reached the place of the king and said- “We are the people well-versed in the Sastras and have presently arrived here. The food prepared by us is delightfully consumed by lord Visnu. You can witness the same today yourself. I shall display the same before you.” Thus speaking, the fake Vaisnavas who were devoted to Kali, making use of their illusion, displayed lord Visnu consuming the food, before the king. Feeling surprised, the king Dharmapala said to Jayadeva - “O preceptor, the devotees of Visnu have arrived here in my house, who display the lord before us. Therefore, you also move to that place quickly.”

*śūlāttaṃ hi samuttārya hastau pādau nṛpo'cchinat \|\| 61 \|\|*

*asmākaṃ śiṣyabhūto hi rājāsmābhiḥ prabodhitaḥ \|*  
*ityuktamātre vacane duḥkhitābhūcca dāritā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*caurāṃstānsā hi pātāle cakāra surarakṣitān \|*  
*jayadevastathā bhūtāndṛṣṭvā caurānruroda ha \|\| 63 \|\|*

*kraṃdamāne dvije tasminhastāṃghrī prakṛtiṃ gatau \|*  
*vismitaṃ nṛpatiṃ tatra sarvaṃ hetumavarṇayat \|\| 64 \|\|*

*śrutvā rājā prasannātmā jayadevamukhodbhavam \|*  
*gītagoviṃdamevāśu paṭhitvā mokṣamāgamat \|\| 65 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra jayadevo yathābhavat \|*  
*kṛṣṇacaitanyacaritaṃ yathā jātaṃ śṛṇuśva tat \|\| 66 \|\|*

58-66. On hearing this, Jayadeva also reached there. The king however was immensely surprised when the wicked cheats found Jayadeva smiling. Therefore, they said to the king- ‘This Brahmana was a cook with the king of the Gauda country. Once the wicked Brahmana in greed for wealth, served poisoned food to the king. But when the king came to know about the reality, he intended to crucify him. Then we reached there and pleaded before the king that it would be sinful to kill a Brahmana, and thus saved his life. But the king in anger cut off his hands and feet, because the king happened to be our disciple. We had spoken accordingly. When they so spoke, they felt extremely painful and their hearts were about to burst out. Thereafter, the king lodged them in the netherworld, who were guarding the lord of gods. Observing this, Jayadeva cried. When he cried pathetically, his hands and feet were restored as before. The king felt extremely surprised at this. At that point of time, Jayadeva explained all the causes there, which delighted the king the most. Therefore, the songs in the form of Gita-govinda were sung by the king and he achieved moksa. Thus I have narrated the story of Jayadeva. Now I shall narrate the story of Kjsna Caitanya.

## Chapter 145. Birth of Krsna Caitanya and Sahkaracarya

1-8. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, there was a Brahmana named Visnusarma, who was well-versed in the Vedas. With a delightful heart, he always adored lord Visnu, who is the form of all the gods. Because of his adoring the lord and getting honoured even by all the gods, he lived on begging alms. He had a wife, but had no children. Once an ascetic arrived at the house of the Brahmana. Observing that the wife of the Brahmana was quite devoted and humble, but suffering from poverty, he said-“this is the philosopher’s stone which is quite compassionate and with its very touch, even the iron turns gold. You keep it with you for three days and make as much gold as you like. By that time, I shall return after taking my bath in the river Sarayh.” Thus speaking, the Brahmana went for taking his bath. The Brahmana lady then made as much gold as she could. At the same time, Visnusarma also arrived back to his place after begging. Finding his wife having been decorated with gold, he said- “O intoxicated beauty, you can go to a passionate lover and live with him, because I happen to be the devotee of lord Visnu. I am a poor Brahmana who is afraid of stealing. You are beautiful and getting intoxicated because of your beauty. Therefore, how can I accept you?” On hearing these harsh words and getting afraid of her husband, she placed the philosopher’s stone as well as the gold before her husband and started serving him.

9-18. The Brahmana then carried the gold as well as the touch stone and dropped them in the river Gharghara. After the end of three days, the ascetic returned and said to the humble Brahmana lady- “Have you not made gold from the touch stone?” She replied- “My husband is an auspicious soul. He has dropped the gold as well as the stone in the river Gharghara. Because till such time the touch stone was in the house, he did not permit me to cook the food. О preceptor, the touch stone is not available with us at the moment.” On hearing these words, the ascetic was immensely surprised. On the return of the Brahmana, he started scolding him- “You have been confused by the destiny and have become a pauper. In case you do not need the auspicious stone, you better return the same to me, otherwise I am going to end my life.” At these words of the ascetic, Visnusarma said-“You go to the bank of the river Gharghara, you will find the stone there itself.” Thus speaking, the Brahmana went with the ascetic to the river bank and showed him several of the pebbles resembling the philosopher’s stone. At the same time, the ascetic humbly offered his salutation to the Brahmana- “I worshipped lord Siva for twelve years continuously and achieved the auspicious stone, but with a mere meeting with the greedy person like me, you have received numerous auspicious stones.” Thus speaking, the ascetic not only received the divine knowledge, but also the moksa. The Brahmana Visnusarma lived on earth for a thousand years, adored the Sungod variously and then achieved moksa from Visnu. The same Brahmana possessing the Vaisnava lustre, illuminated the entire universe in each one of the Phalguna month as a result of which the divine cause was established.

19-26. Suta said - Thus speaking, the lord Brhaspati again addressed Indra —the lord of Saci and spoke to him- “In the month of Phalguna, you should enjoy all the comforts. At these words of the preceptor Brhaspati, Indra appropriately adored Sungod who is the god of gods in the form of Visnu. At that point of time, the Sungod getting pleased, emerged out of the solar disc with four arms, red complexion and resembled the lord of yajnas. Then in the presence of all the gods, he entered into the body of the Indra. At that point of time, Indra absorbed his own body into the present body and took to the form of Brahmana, who was never bom of a human body. His wife Indrani also did so. Thereafter, both of them, suffering from the Vaisnava fire, roamed about in a forest over the bank of the river Ganga for a year. Indrani had taken to the form of a Brahmapa damsel, who became pregnant. On the Thursday of the bright twelfth day of month of Bhadrapada, at the time of Brahma-mandala, lord Visnu himself incarnated in her womb who possessed all the arts. He had four arms, red complexion. He possessed the lustre of sun in Aquarius zodiac symbol. At that point of time, the Rudras, Vasus, Visvedevas, Marudganas, Sadhyas, Bhaskara and the Siddhas were present there eulogizing the lord.

*devā ūcuḥ \|*

27-29. The gods said- О Master, we offer our salutation to you with Siva, your feet are decorated with the symbols of vajra, flag, club and ankusa or goad. You roam about with the sages and remove the danger of the world. You hold sankha, cakra, gada and lotus. You destroy the strong bodies of the enemies of the gods. You also preserve the mobile and immobile creatures of the world. Your fickleness becomes the cause of destruction of the enemy and establishes the cause of the gods. I offer my salutation to the son of Saci, who bestows bliss, who removes terrific sins, sufferings and harsh words. You destroy the enemies of the gods quickly and establishing peace in the world, redeem crores of sinners being the attendant of the Iokas.

*bhaktāṃbhodharadhāriṇī vijayinī niṣkaṃpasaptāvalī devo naḥ kuladevataṃ vijayate caitanyakṛṣṇo hariḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-34. You taking to the form of a swan, observing the truth, have protected the Vedas. Because of the form of yajna, you are the preserver of the Iokas. Becoming the son of Indra from Saci, you have incarnated on earth in the form of yajna and have protected all the Vedas. Let the son of Saci always remain in our hearts. He is the one who has incarnated for showing mercy on all, fully illuminated the universe and bestowing his devotion in the age of Kali is decorated with the ugly lustre of Siva. О great lord, you are Krsna Caitanya and the son of Saci. It is you who give birth to the humans on earth and out of compassion bring them up and for bestowing your supreme position over them, have also incarnated on earth. In this terrific age of Kali, we the gods are suffering from the sons of Diti. Therefore, you kindly protect us. Let Krsna Caitanya, our family deity, be always successful. The one who is fragrant with the beautiful fragrant limbs, has the forests of golden lotuses, is Himalaya of love, who is spring of the compassion, who have the goddess with clouds of devotion and who is always victorious. We are offering our salutation to the lord who is adored by all and who is omnipresent. In the terrific age of Kali, he makes the earth, tortured by the enemy of the gods, to sprout and incarnates in the universe. He is the one, by listening to whose name, the enemies of the gods, squeezing their bodies in the form of seeds, incarnate on earth. By listening to whose name, the enemies of the gods get trampled upon and reach the nether world. Besides, the indigenous Mlecchas always suffer.

37-49. Brhaspati said- О best of the gods, I am going to tell you. You please listen. In earlier time, there was a Brahmana known by the name of Mrgavyadha, who lived on the hunting of the deer. Holding a bow and an arrow in his hand, he always used to kill the Brahmanas who moved in the forest on their journey. The immensely foolish Brahmana for his fun, also collected their sacred threads. Thus that wicked person acted deplorably. He was also aware of the fact that the wealth of Brahmana is nectar like, that of the Ksatriya is sweet, the wealth of a Vaisya is like the cereals and the wealth of the Madras is like the blood. But still, he had mostly killed the Brahmanas, beside the three varnas. When the Brahmanas were so abundantly killed by the wicked person, the gods went to Brahma and apprised him of the factual position. On hearing the same, Brahma felt extremely painful. Brahma then summoned the seven Rsis and said to them- “You please go there and redeem him.” On hearing these words, Vasistha and other Rsis beside Marici went there and stood there obstructing the path of Mrgavyadha. Finding the seven Rsis present there, the powerful Mrgavyadha holding the bow, spoke in a thundering voice- “I shall kill all of you today.” Then Marici and other Rsis, smilingly said- “O valorous one, you are making efforts to kill us for your own selfish purpose or for the sake of your family?” At this, the wicked Brahmana said- “I shall kill you all for myself as well as my family. For this purpose, I kill the rich Brahmanas alone.” At this, the Maharsis said- “O great archer, come on, we are ready for the same. But you tell us one thing, that who would own the sin of Brahmahatya?' On hearing this, the terrific Brahmana, who in the view of the Maharsis was getting purified, went to his people and said to them- “I have committed a terrible sin.

*yathā pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti tathā mājñātumarhatha \|*  
*ityuktāstena te prāhuḥ śṛṇu tvaṃ maṃtramuttamam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*rāma nāma hi tajjñeyaṃ sarvāghaughavināśanam \|*  
*yāvattvatpārśvamāyāmastāvattvaṃ japa cottamam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ityuktvā te gatā viprāstīrthāttīrthāntaraṃ prati \|*  
*marāmarāmaretyevaṃ sahasrābdaṃ jajāpa ha \|\| 53 \|\|*

*japaprabhāvādabhavadvanamutpalasaṃkulam \|*  
*tatsthānamutpalāraṇyaṃ prasiddhamabhavadbhuvi \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tataḥ saptarṣayaḥ prāptā valmīkāttaṃ nirākṛtam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā śuddhaṃ tadā vipramūcuste vismayānvitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*valmīkānnissṛto yasmāttasmādvālmīkiruttamam \|*  
*tava nāma bhavedvipra trikālajña mahāmate \|\| 56 \|\|*

50-56. Since you share the wealth with me, therefore you also share a portion of my sins.” On hearing these words, the people of the household said- “We shall never share your sins at any rate. The earth and the Sungod, who are the witness for all, are witness for this as well.” On hearing these words, Mrgavyadha spoke to the seven Rsis with folded hands-“You kindly tell me some way out to get me relieved of my sins.” When Mrgavyadha so spoke with his humble tone, the Maharsis said- “We tell you an excellent mantra. You please listen. The name of Rama is the remover of all the sins and should be recited by you, till our return to you.” Thus speaking, the Maharsis proceeded on to pilgrimage from one holy place to another. The Mrgavyadha on the other hand, started uttering the word Mara, Mara and Mara, which with the uttering of three words continuously, takes to the form of Rama. He continued doing so for a thousand years. By the glory of the reciting of the mantra, a lotus forest was grown there and because of which that place on earth came to be known as Utpalaranya. The seven Rsis again visited that place after a long time and removed the sound of white ants around the Brahmana and found him in a purified form. They said to him- “O dear one, you are aware of the happenings of present, past and future. О intelligent one, because of your having emerged out of the sound of white anthill, you would attain glory as Valmiki.

## \|\| 2.145.57-66 \|\|

*kalpāṣṭādaśayuktaṃ hi śatakoṭipravistaram \|\| 57 \|\|*

*cakāra nirmalaṃ padyaiḥ sarvāghaughavināśanam \|*  
*tatpaścātsa śivo bhūtvā tatra vāsamakārayat \|\| 58 \|\|*

*adyāpi saṃsthitaḥ svāmī mṛgavyādhaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*

*vaivasvate'ntare prāpte cādye satyayuge śubhe \|*

*tadā sarasvatī devī nadī bhūtvā samāgatā \|*  
*taddarśanātsvayaṃ brahmā mukhato brāhmaṇaṃ śubham \|\| 61 \|\|*

*bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyaṃ caiva corubhyāṃ vaiśyamuttamam \|*  
*padbhyāṃ śūdraṃ śubhācāraṃ janayāmāsa vīryavān \|\| 62 \|\|*

*dvijarājastathā somaścaṃdramā nāmato dvijaḥ \|*  
*loke sarvātapaḥ sūryaḥ kaśyaṃ vīryaṃ hi pāti yaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*kaśyapo hi dvitīyo'sau marīcistu tato'bhavat \|*

*lokāndakṣati yaḥ kṛtyaiḥ sa tu dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇoṃgācca te jātāstasmādvai brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

57-66. Thus speaking, those Rsis proceeded on to the heaven. Subsequently, the sage Valmiki composed the epic of Ramayana with eighteen kalpas, which has a hundred crores of verses and which is a poetic excellence. It removes all the sins. The sage then lived there as Siva. The Mrgavyadha Svami is still lodged there. О gods, I am going to recite his story, you listen to it carefully. At the start of Satyayuga, during the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Brahma went to the same Utpalaranya and performed a great yajna there. At that point of time, Sarasvati appeared there in the form of river, looking at whom Brahma produced Brahmanas form his mouth, Ksatriyas from his arms, Vaisyas from his thighs and Rudras from his feet. Besides these, Brahma also produced Dvijaraja Soma, who is also known as the moon. The sun was created as a Ksatriya, who protects the strength of all in the world. Therefore, he is called as Kasyapa as well as Marici. The ocean was known as Ratnakara because it happens to be the storehouse of gems and pearls. Because of its being the support of all the dravyas, it is called Dharma. Because of its being deep beyond measure and having unprecedented treasure, it is also called the husband of rivers. One who, by performing his own deeds makes the world efficient, he is called Daksa Prajapati. He has also been called as Brahman, because of his having been bom of limbs of Brahma.

## \|\| 2.145.67-71 \|\|

*varṇadharmeṇa te sarve varṇātmānaśca vai kramāt \|*  
*dakṣasya manaso jātāḥ kanyāḥ paṃcaśataṃ tataḥ \|*  
*viṣṇu māyāprabhāvena kalābhūtāḥ sthitā bhuvi \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tadā tu bhagavānbrahmā somāyāśvinimaṇḍalam \|*  
*saptaviṃśadgaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dadau lokavivṛddhaye \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kaśyapāyāditigaṇaṃ kṣatrarūpaṃ trayodaśam \|*  
*dharmāya kīrtiprabhṛtīrdadau sa ca mahāmuniḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*nānāvidhāni sṛṣṭāni cāsanvaivasvate'ntare \|*  
*teṣāṃ patistvayaṃ dakṣo'bhūdvidherājñayā bhuvi \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tatra vāsaṃ svayaṃ dakṣaḥ kṛtavānyajñatatparaḥ \|*  
*sarve devagaṇā dakṣaṃ namaskṛtya caraṃti hi \|\| 71 \|\|*

67-71. Those who own all the varnas are known as the followers of Varna-dharma. Thereafter, from the mind of Daksa Prajapati, five hundred girls were bom, who having been overpowered with the illusion of Visnu, are spread in the universe in the forms of art. At that point of time, lord Brahma also produced the moon, Asvini and other constellations that are twenty seven in number. Besides it, Aditi and Kirti were given over to Dharma. With the distribution of his daughters like this by the great sage, during the period of Vaivasvata Manvantara, several types of creations were made in the lokas. Subsequently, at the command of Brahma, Daksa Prajapati, while living there, organized a huge yajna there. In the function of the yajna, all the gods participated. They offered their salutation to Daksa Prajapati and then started roaming about here and there. But lord Mahadeva did not offer his salutation to him, which enraged Dak§a and he refused to share the part of yajna to Siva. At that point of time, Mrgavyadha Siva could not tolerate the insult. Therefore, he took to the form of Virabhadra having three eyes, three heads and three legs. Then he appeared there in this form, because of which all the gods, sages and pitrs started suffering badly. The yajna-purusa then took to the form of a deer and fled away on all the sides. But taking the form of a hunter or Vyadha, the Vyadha Siva shattered the limbs of the body of yajna-purusa. At the same time, lord Brahma speaking in sweet and humble voice, praised him (Siva). The Mrgavyadha was pleased with the same and got the yajna completed. When the Sungod was in the Libra zodiac sign, in the lunar disc of the moon, Rudra was himself established and proceeded to his place. Then Rudra in the form of moon, established his superiority over all the seven lokas. On hearing this, Virbhadra was immensely pleased and he extracting his amsa form his body, sent to the house of a Brahmana known as Bhairavadatta, who incarnating in his house as his son during the terrific period of Kali, appeared on earth in the name of Sankaracarya. The boy who was virtuous, quite knowledgeable and Brahmacarl, composed Sankara-bhasya and led the path of Saivism, which patronize Tripunda, sandal paste, rosary of Rudrak§a and the five syllable mantra. These symbols bestow welfare on the followers of Saivism.

## Chapter 146. Birth of Anandagiri, Vanasarma and Purisarma

## \|\| 2.146.1-3 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*purā tu naimiṣāraṇye vipraścājagaro'bhavat \|*  
*vedāntaśāstranipuṇo jñānavāñchambhupūjakaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dvādaśābdāntare rudrastuṣṭo'bhūtpārthivārcanāt \|*  
*tadāgatya dadau jñānaṃ jīvanmokṣatvamāgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*saṅkarṣaṇaṃ samārādhya tajjñānena dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva puṣkalābhiśca stutibhiḥ parameśvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, in the holy land of Naimisaranya, a Brahmana who had been cursed to be a python, lived there. He was well-versed in the Vedanta, quite learned besides being a great devotee of Siva. After the lapse of twelve years, lord Rudra was pleased with his devotion and he bestowed to the python the knowledge for his redemption. As a result of this, the Brahmana achieved the vicinity of lord Siva and tried to further please with his excellent prayers.

## \|\| 2.146.4-6 \|\|

*ajagara uvāca \|*  
*sadaivyaṃ pradhānaṃ paraṃ jyotirūpaṃ nirākāramavyaktamānandanityam \|*  
*tridhā tattu jātaṃ triliṅgaikyabhinnaṃ pumānsattvarūpo rajorūpanārī \|*  
*tayoryattu śeṣaṃ tamorūpameva tataśśeṣanāmne namastenamaste \|\| 4 \|\|*

*rajaścādibhūto guṇasyaiva māyā tathā madhyabhūto narassattvarūpam \|*  
*tathaivāntabhūto napuṃskaṃ tamovatsadaivādya nāgeśa tubhyaṃ namaste \|\| 5 \|\|*

*narādhārarūpo bhavānkālakartā narākarṣaṇastvaṃ hi saṅkarṣaṇaśca \|*  
*ramante munīśāstvayi brahmadhāmni namastenamaste punaste namo'stu \|*  
*narāṅgeṣu cādhārabhūtā śivā yā smṛtā yoganidrā hi śaktistvadīyā \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. The python said - I offer my salutation again and again to the divine lord, the form of extreme lustre, the invisible and formless one, blissful, who appeared in three forms and is beyond the three lingas. The same lord is Purusa in the form of sattva, Nari in the form of rajas, besides being different from tamoguna. In the form of a human, you are a creator of time. You are known as Sankarsana because you attract the humans. You are the lustre of Brahmana, in which the sages roam about. Your strength is displayed in the human form. The same Sakti is known in the world as Siva or Yoganidra. Therefore, salutation to you again and again.

*phaṇāsahasrasahito gaurāṅgo gauravigrahaḥ \|*

*taṃ sarpākhyaṃ mahārudraṃ pratyāgatyātmabhūḥ svayam \|*  
*karkarāśisthite sūrye candre bhagaṇamaṇḍale \|\| 9 \|\|*

*taṃ rudraṃ sthāpayāmāsa candramāḥ sa tu cābhavat \|*

*vacanaṃ sa prasannātmā teja utpādya vai mukhāt \|*  
*vindhyādrau janayāmāsa devadattadvijālaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

*giriśarmā sa vai vipro vijitya viduṣāṃ gaṇān \|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā rudro babhūva ha \|*

7-13. Brhaspati said- When lord Siva was so eulogized by the python, the former in order to bestow the Sayujya moksa to the python, himself took to the form of a serpent, with a thousand snake hoods, with white complexion of the body, dwelling in the ocean of milk besides being the treasure of virtues. Thereafter, Brahma arrived before Siva in the form of a serpent and established him as the leader in the group of constellations when the sun was in Cancer sign of zodiac. By so doing, lord Siva in the form of the moon, took out the lustre from his mouth and sent it to the house of the Brahmana named Devadutta, who dwelt in the Vindhya mountain. Having been born there, he was known as Girisanna, who defeating all the contemporary Brahmanas, travelled to Kasi. Reaching there, he accepted to serve Sankaracarya and became famous by the name of Anandagiri. Thus, I have narrated the story of the incarnation of Rudra. Now I am repeating the story as told by Brhaspati, you please listen.

*jīva uvāca \|*  
*prayāge ca purā hyāsīdbrāhmaṇo harisevakaḥ \|*

14-19. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, there lived a Brahmana, who inspite of his being a devotee of the lord, was a pauper facing misfortune. He was known by the name of Nairrti. He lived on begging alms and somehow managed to maintain his wife and the son. His condition was going from bad to worse. Once the divine sage Narada arrived in his house. The Brahmana served the sage Narada as per his means. Thereafter, Narada returned to Visnuloka. Reaching there, he offered his repeated salutations to lord Narayana and then humbly spoke to the lord-“O lord, the devotees who always get devoted to you have enough of wealth and cereals, but on earth, I have also met with your devotees, who are suffering badly from poverty. О lord Janardana, I am therefore unable to come to a conclusion about the cause of their sufferings. I offer my salutation to you again and again. You kindly enlighten me on this subject.”

20-32. At these words of Narada, lord Narayana -the favourite of his devotees, spoke to him in beautiful words- “O best of the gods, I am speaking out the truth to you. My devotee lord Brahma, finding the people devoted to Narayana, puts them under his control and perform the deeds. He has indeed created Dharma and Adharma, in which Dharma has been equated with the Vedas. The intelligent one built seven Iokas of Dharma, which are known by the names of Bhuloka, Bhuvarloka, Svaraloka, Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapaloka and Satyaloka. He tries to provide more and more comforts to the people there. Similarly, the absence of the Vedas has been termed as adharma which creates adverse works on earth. By patronizing such works in speech, the people achieve the same types of Iokas. Having been deprived of the Vedas, the related adharma enhances the sinful daityas always. The adharma is also spread in seven Iokas, which are lodged below the ground and which were created by Brahma. They cause comforts to the people living there. They are known by the names of Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Talatala, Mahatala, Rasatala and Patala. The Devas followed their dharma as well as they practiced dharma. Therefore, the Devas of the side of Dharma, and Daityas of the Adharma side have been marked out. The sinful and blemished path of the Devas and the Daityas is known as the irreligious one. The people living therein have to suffer always. Brahma has created twenty one types of evil or painful places which are known as Tamisra, Ardhatamsira, Kumbhipaka, Raurava, Maharaurava, Murtiraya, Iksu-yantra, Salmala and Asi (forest of trees with sword like leaves on trees). These are the hells created by Brahma. The whole of these is known as the globe or the universe, in which my supreme position is quite intact. The dwellers of the universe who are devoted to me, can reach this position, but the devotees of the gods achieve these seven Iokas. Besides the Tamasi people also achieve these seven Iokas which are lodged below the earth, like Patala etc.

33-54. Adhaloka is lodged at a distance of a lakh of yojanas from Patala, which is visited by the sinful people. Because of this, my devotees are relieved from all the positions by Brahma and they become paupers. But such of my devotees who adore me and the gods, they possess Laksmi, besides achieving my devotion and the salvation. Leaving aside all other gods, the Brahmana of Prayaga known by the name of Nairrti adores me with utmost devotion, which is the cause of his poverty. О Narada, all the things granted by the Devas are consumed by the people always, but the thing I give to my devotee is not found in the universe. Therefore, at my command, you grant him the auspicious boon.” At these words of the lord - the creator of the universe, Narada went to the abode of the Brahmana and said to his wife- “O chaste lady, you better ask for a desired boon.” On hearing these words, the lady said- “O master, I intend to become the queen of a king.” At the mere speaking of these words, she atonce was turned into a royal queen and the king arrived there at the same time and took her home. When the Brahmana returned in the evening at his home, Narada informed him - “O Brahmana, the beloved of the lord, you better listen to my words. By receiving a boon, your wife has become a queen. Now you also enjoy all the pleasures by getting a boon from me.” On hearing these words, the Brahmana, as a move of the destiny, getting enraged said- “You kindly give me a boon that my wife becomes a she-jackal.” With the uttering of these words, the wife of the Brahmana was turned into a she-jackal. At the same time, the classmate of the Brahmana who was devoted to his preceptor, arrived there and learned the cause of his friend’s misery and said to Narada- “Let my mother regain her earlier position. Thus all the three of them having been overpowered by Devamaya, even after receiving the boon, were deprived of their desires. At that point of time, Narada feeling painful, said to Nairrta- “O Brahmana because of your being akin to the gods, lord Mahesvara is the lord of the universe. Therefore, you should adore him. He would surely make you succeed.” At the advice of Narada, the Brahmana Nairrta adored lord Siva. After the lapse of one year, lord Mahesa delightfully bestowed enormous wealth on him, which was comparable with the riches of Kubera and because of which, the Brahmana came to be known as Devamurti Kubera. Thus, because of his worship of lord Siva, he achieved the undisturbed wealth and led a comfortable life for a thousand divine years. Finally, he attained the heaven. When the sun is lodged in the zodiac symbol of Taurus, he became loveable and popular like like Soma - the king of Candra. О best of the race of Bhrgu, when Brhaspati so spoke to the gods, the son of Nairrti from his own amsa took his birth who was the performer of the Sankhya yoga at Gimara mountain. Because the child was always devoted to the Veda and other scriptures, he came to be known as Vanasarma. At the age of twelve years, he defeated the contemporary learned people. Vanasarma went to Kasi and served Sankaracarya as his disciple.

55-69. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, in the city of Mahismati, there lived a Brahmana known by the name of Vasusarma. He worshipped lord Asutosa Siva for getting a son, performing vrata at the same time. He continued his tapas for a period of twenty four years continuously, but could not gain the grace of lord Siva. Thereafter, the Brahmana getting disgusted, dropped all the limbs of his body in the fire flames in order to please lord Siva. But the lord was still not pleased. Ultimately, the Brahmana getting purified, created an excellent sheep and entered in the fire with the same. At the same time, lord Siva arrived there with his attendants in his divine form. Then he said to Vasusarma- “You ask for a boon you desire.” Getting delighted, the Brahmana with his choked voice, offered his salutation to the beloved of Parvati and spoke to lord Siva quite humbly- “O master, you are the beloved of those who take refuge with you. You kindly bestow a son to me.” At these words of the Brahmana, Siva said smilingly-“It is Brahma, who can bestow a son to you. He is the supreme lord of destiny. Since he has not given a son to you during the hundred births, therefore, I am giving you a son from my own ams a ”Thus speaking, lord Siva took out a part of his lustre form his mouth and gave it to his wife which was divided into two parts. The first part turned into having a goat like feet in the tenth month and the other was born in human form. He came to be known as Ajaikapada in the world. After leading a comfortable life for four hundred years, the god of death appeared before the Brahmana with his attendants. But at the same time, the gods started a terrific war. Thereafter, the strong warrior defeated all the enemies in a year. He gained the glory on earth by the name of Mrtunjaya. The god of death then feeling upset, having been thus defeated by the Brahmana, went to Brahma and apprised him of the factual position. Lord Brahma then reached there with all the gods and established the Brahmana over a royal seat in the lunar disc.

*purīśarmeti vikhyāto yatidattasya vai sutaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā mṛtyuñjayobhavat \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. Hearing about the Ajaikapada, Mahadeva who had taken to the form of a Brahmana and who is the purifier of Kali, went to the city of Mahismati and gained glory their as Purisarma. By the age of sixteen, he defeated all the learned people and served Sankaracarya as his disciple. Thus, I have narrated to you the story of the birth of Mrtunjaya.

## Chapter 147. Birth of Bharatisa, Ksetrasarma and Dhundhiraja

## \|\| 2.147.1-11 \|\|

*nikuṃbhānvayasaṃbhūtaḥ śakratulyaparākramaḥ \|*

*ityuktassa tathetyuktvā brahma lokamupāyayau \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dānavassa \|*  
*tu raudrātmā jitvā svarganivāsinaḥ \|*  
*āhūya dānavāndaityānvivarebhyaḥ prasannadhīḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*svarge nivāsayāmāsa te devā bhūtalīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*lakṣābdaṃ ca surāssarve bubhujuḥ paramāpadaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ekadā nārado dhīmāndṛṣṭvā devāṃstathāgatān \|*

*sa devaśca mahādevo brahmāṇḍeśo vipattihā \|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavānmaheśo lokaśaṃkaraḥ \|*

1-11. Suta said - I am repeating the story told by Brhaspati in earlier times. You please listen. Once there had been a danava named Hirbu, who had been a thorn for each and every living being and caused pain to others. He was bom of the race of Kumbha and became as valorous as Indra himself. He performed tapas for a thousand years as a result of which the gods started suffering due to the heat emerging out of his body. At that point of time, Brahma -the creator of the universe, for the protection of the universe, reached before the daitya and told the Danesvara to seek for a boon. He offered his salutation to Brahma and spoke to him with all humility- “O master, being the creator of the universe and in case you are anxious to bestow a boon on me, then no mobile or immobile being of the world should be able to kill me in future.” The boon was granted by Brahma, after which he retired to Brahmaloka. But the evil-minded daitya defeated the gods dwelling in the heaven, called the daityas from Patala and established his dominance in the heaven. He misused the gods for a lakh of years. Once Narada noticed the pitiable condition of the gods and said to them- “All of you should worship the lord Siva, because he is the lord of the universe and remover of the miseries of the people.” On hearing these words, the surprised gods worshipped lord Siva in Parthiva form for eleven years, after which Mahadeva was pleased with them. Lord Siva then took to the form of a Jyotirlinga and reduced the three lokas to ashes.

*ye tu vai devabhaktāśca śeṣāścāsanmahābhaye \|*

*etasminnantare brahmā viṣṇunā saha harṣitaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva sa mahārudraṃ stotraissāmasamudbhavaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mithunasthe divānāthe śaśimaṇḍalabhūpatim \|*

*patirūpaḥ kalābhijño bhāratīśa iti śrutaḥ \|*

*śaṃkarācāryamāgamya śiṣyo'bhūttena nirjitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. At that point of time, only the devotees of the gods could escape death. The rest of the people together with the Danavas were reduced to ashes in the huge fire flames. At the same time, Brahma feeling delightful, arrived there with Visnu and eulogized the lord reciting the Samaveda and pleased Maharudra. Subsequently, for the benefit of the gods, when the sun was in the Gemini zodiac sign, Hirbughna Maharudra was established in the lunar disc. On hearing this, in order to make the task of the gods a success, Hirbughna was bom in the house of Sadyakarma in Himalaya, who was in the form of a Yati and was well-versed in all types of arts. He came to be known ultimately as Bharatisa. He defeated many of the learned people and reached the town of Kasi. Reaching there, he was defeated by Sankaracarya and became his disciple.

## \|\| 2.147.17-19 \|\|

*bṛhaspati ruvāca \|*  
*mayaputraḥ smṛto māyī tapo ghoraṃ cakāra ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*padaikena sthitaḥ sūrye sahasrābdaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*sa lokāṃstāpayāmāsa tapasā lokavāsinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavānparameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*trayo grāmāstatpriyārthe kramādvai tena nirmitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Brhaspati said- Looking at the Sungod, Mayi - the son of Maya, performed hard tapas, standing on one leg for a thousand years, As a result of this, the lustre that emerged out of his body, made the people to suffer immensely. At that point of time, the grandsire Brahma, feeling pleased with him, created three lokas and gave them to him.

## \|\| 2.147.20-25 \|\|

*sauvarṇaṃ svargasadṛśaṃ puraṃ ṣoḍaśayojanam \|*  
*tadadho yojanānte ca rājataṃ ca bhuvarmayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tadadho yojanānte ca bhūrlokamiva cāyasam \|*  
*evaṃ puranivāsinyo daityānāṃ yoṣito mudā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śatakoṭimitā daityā dharmātmāno nivāsinaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā yajñabhāgaṃ ca devatulyā babhūvire \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tadā nirbalino devāḥ kṣudhayā pīḍitāḥ prabhum \|*  
*bhagavantaṃ mahāviṣṇuṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ parayā girā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*caturyugasamūhānāṃ varṣāṇāṃ bhagavanprabho \|*  
*adhikāravihīnāśca vartaṃte svargamaṇḍale \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tāmasāṃtaramevāpi ṣoḍaśaiva caturyugam \|*  
*vyatītāni mahāviṣṇo māyināṃ duḥkhaṃ bhuṃjatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

20-25. These included the city made of gold, which was spread in an area of sixteen yojanas with golden palaces in that city. A yojana below it like Bhuvarloka, a second city was made in silver and still downwards was the city of iron spread in an equivalent area. Thus the Daityas started living delightfully in the cities which were built by Brahma, together with their ladies besides a hundred crores of other Daityas. By living there, the Daityas started accepting the part of yajnas from the Devas. As a result of this, the gods started suffering from hunger. Then they went to their master Visnu and offered prayers to him. They said- ‘‘O lord, having been deprived of our rights, many yugas have passed. O great Visnu, now in the present age of Kali, even by living on earth in miserable condition, all the four yugas have lapsed sixteen times.”

*sajyaṃ jātaṃ ca rudreṇa puṣṭibhūtaṃ mahaddhanuḥ \|*

*pinākinaṃ mahārudraṃ mīnarāśisthite ravau \|*

*svādhikārāṃstadā devā avāpustāmasāntare \|\| 43 \|\|*

26-43. Then listening to their pathetic tale of sufferings and finding that the religious-minded Daityas had gained proficiency in Sanskrit language, in the terrific age of Kali, he himself took to the form of Buddha, when he was born as the son of the Brahmana named Ajina. The lord then confused the Daityas following the Vedic-dharma with his illusion, made them comfortable but also inactive at the same time. In this way, after their getting the age of sixteen years and getting influenced from them, the people of all the castes stopped the performing of homa. At that point of time, Daityas, who were the dwellers of Tripura, getting enraged, finding that the people were neglecting the study of the Vedas as well as the performing of the yajnas, started causing trouble to them. As a result of this, by the end of kalpa, they were eaten up by the Daityas and all the people were destroyed. Then, at the start of the age of Satyayuga, all the gods went over the Kailasa mountain and worshipped lord Siva there. Getting pleased with their devotions, lord Siva took to the form of a Jyotirlinga. At that point of time, the gods getting pleased, extracted the nectar from the earth and built surprising type of chariot in which the wheels were made of the essence of the sun and the moon, the axle was made of the essence of Sumeru mountain. The people thus made the astonishing type of the chariot and presented it to lord Siva. At the same time, Brahma arrived there and took to the form of a charioteer. The Vedas took the position of its horses. Lord Siva - the gods of all the gods, was lodged there holding a bow of Lokaloka mountain’s essence and made a bow from the same. It was a terrific bow and was known by the name of Ajagava, which had been made quite hard by lord Satyadeva, but finding the same bow broken at the hands of Siva, another bow was made with the essence of lord Visnu. With the essence of heaven, a divine bow was made. When lord Rudra strung the cord of that bow, then the Brahmarsis feeling delighted, offered prayer to the same. Lord Mahesvara came to be known as Pinakina (carrier of a bow). The cord was in the form of the serpent Sesa and the arrow represented Indra, while the wings of the arrow were in the form of the Windgod. Lord Siva killed crores of the daityas in the sky, besides putting Tripura to ashes. When all the three cities were reduced to ashes, Brahma - the leader of the universe, then bestowed to lord Siva the suzerainty of the lunar disc in the Mina sign of zodiac symbol. The gods also subsequently regained their rights.

*sūta uvāca \|*

*samutpādya haradvāre hima sānau cakāra ha \|*  
*macchando nāma tatraiva yogī śaṃbhuparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*gorakhasya gururyo vai tanmukhe teja āviśat \|*  
*raṃbhā nāmnaiva tatraiva svarveśyā kāmarūpiṇī \|\| 46 \|\|*

*macchandaṃ ca vaśīkṛtya bubhuje smaravihvalā \|*  
*tayossakāśādvai jātassa putro rucirānanaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*nāthaśarmeti vikhyāto vidvāñcchreṣṭhataro'bhavat \|*  
*sa jitvā paṃḍitānbhūmau purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*śaṃkarācāryavijitastasya śiṣyo babhūva ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

44-48. Suta said- On hearing this story, lord Pinakina Siva took out his amsa from his body and sent it to Haridvara near Himalaya, which earned the glory as the Macchanda yogi and became the great devotee of lord Siva. He was also the preceptor of Gorakhanatha, in whose mother the lustre of Siva got absorbed. An apsara named Rambha who had taken to a beautiful form, was filled with passion and got her lust satisfied uniting with the yogi Macchanda. With the union of both of them, a sweet natured child was born to them who was known by the name of Nathasarma or Gorakhanatha, besides being a deeply learned person. He defeated many of the top class learned people and then went to the city of Kasi. Reaching there, he was defeated by Sankaracarya - the king of the yogins and he accepted the Acarya as his preceptor.

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*

*babhujurbalavaṃtaste daityapakṣā mahādhamāḥ \|*

*himatuṃge samāgamya tadgarbhaṃ munisaṃbhavam \|*  
*śatavarṣaṃ dadau devī tapasā jñānarūpiṇī \|\| 52 \|\|*

*māturūrū suto bhittvā tato jāto mahītale \|*  
*tejasā tasya putrasya bhasmībhūtamabhūjjagat \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tadā tu sakalā devāḥ puraskṛtya prajāpatim \|*  
*vajrasthitaśca vai tālāssamājagmu rbhayāturāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*pitṛbhidaivatairbālassamājñāto himācale \|*

*jaladevī ca vaḍavā bhūtvā tatteja uttamam \|*

*meṣage dyumaṇau prāpte śaśimaṇḍalagaṃ prabhum \|*

*ūrujātātsmṛto vorvo dahano lokadāhataḥ \|*  
*vaḍavāmukhato jāto vāḍavo nāma sa prabhuḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

49-59. Brhaspati said - In the age of Dvapara during the Caksusa Manvantara, a Ksatriya named Talajangha lived. At the place of Kuruksetra, after the destruction of the Brahmanas, the degraded Daityas looted their riches and made use of the same. At the same time, the wife of a Rsi in pregnant condition, feeling immensely frightened, tried to reach the peak of the Himalaya mountain. Reaching there, the sage’s wife who was the form of the divine knowledge, retained pregnancy for a hundred years and produced a child by tearing out her thigh, who was quite illustrious. When the child was so born on earth, the entire universe was reduced to ashes with his lustre. The gods getting terrified, making Brahma to lead them together with Vaitala and carrying vajra, tried to reach the spot. Reaching there, they accepted the commands of manes and the gods dropped the lustre into the oceanic water which had destroyed the universe. At that point of time, the goddess of the water taking to the form of a mare, drank the lustre with the water. But she started suffering from the lustre of Rudra and ultimately vomited it out. At that point of time, Brahma himself went there and established the lustre at the base of Trikuta mountain in a lake. When sun was in the zodiac Mesa, Brahma established him in the lunar disc. He came to be known as Vorvo Dahana as well as Vadava.

## \|\| 2.147.60-62 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā tu dahano guruvākyaṃ manoharam \|*  
*svamukhātteja utpādya kurukṣetraṃ cakāra ha \|\| 60 \|\|*

*sārasvatasya viprasya gṛhe jātassa vai śivaḥ \|*  
*kṣetraśarmeti vikhyāto vidvacchreṣṭho babhūva ha \|\| 61 \|\|*

*śaṃkarācāryamāgamya śiṣyo bhūtvā parājitaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryavratī kāśyāṃ tasthau śaṃbhuparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. Suta said- The illustrious child Dahana, listening to the beautiful words of Brhaspati, extracted lustre out of his mouth and sent it to Kuruksetra which was born in the house of a Sarasvata Brahmana as his son and came to be known as Ksetrasarma. He was immensely learned. Reaching Kasi, he became the I disciple of Svami Sankaracarya and observed Brahmacarya. He also served lord Visvanatha at Kasi.

## \|\| 2.147.63-74 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*ekārṇave purā jāte naṣṭe sthāvara jaṃgame \|*  
*śatābde brahmaṇaḥ prāpte'vyaktajanmani lokage \|\| 63 \|\|*

*avyaktaṃ prakṛtirmāyā pītvā sarvajalaṃ mudā \|*  
*mahākālī svayaṃ mūrtiraṃdhakārasvarū piṇī \|\| 64 \|\|*

*ekā babhūva tatraiva prākṛte kalpadāruṇe \|*  
*caturyugānāṃ koṭīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ dāruṇe laye \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭilakṣayutānāṃ ca kālastatra vyatī tavān \|*  
*tadā sā prakṛtirdevī nityaśuddhā sanātanī \|\| 66 \|\|*

*svecchayā ca svarūpaṃ svaṃ mahāgauramanuttamam \|*  
*paṃcavaktraṃ daśabhujaṃ trinetraṃ ca dadhau śivā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*bhālanetreṇa sā mātā sūkṣmatejo dadarśa ha \|*  
*śūnyabhūtaṃ paraṃ nityamavikāri niraṃjanam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tadā dikṣu gataṃ brahma svabhujaiḥ prakṛtiḥ purā \|*  
*grahītumicchatī tatra na samarthā babhūva vai \|\| 69 \|\|*

*vismitā prakṛtirmātā paṃcavaktraiḥ sanātanam \|*  
*tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā cirakālātparātparam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*dhātuśabdaiḥ prāṅmukhajaiḥ pratyayairyāmyavaktrajaiḥ \|*  
*suvibhaktimayaiḥ śabdairmukhapaścimajaiḥ sthirā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tiṅvibhaktimayairnityā mukhottaramayai rmudā \|*  
*nabhovaktramayaiḥ śabdairvarṇamātrairniraṃjanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*saccidānaṃdaghanakaṃ pūrṇabrahma sanātanam \|*  
*tutoṣa tattu sarvajñaṃ pacavaktreṣu cāgamat \|\| 73 \|\|*

*puruṣatvamabhūdbrahma svayaṃbhūrnāma cābhavat \|*  
*avyaktātprakṛterjāto'vyaktajanmā hi sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

63-74. Brhaspati said- At the time of dissolution, when the mobile and immobile world got absorbed, then after a hundred years, Brahma consuming the invisible water, generated a definite form of Mahakali - the form of darkness. At the time of the terrific Prakrtakalpa, she was born alone and spent the period of sixty lakh crores of yugas. Thereafter, the goddess Prakriti, who is known as spotless and eternal, made her form by her own sweet will and became quite glorious. The goddess Siva then bestowed her the five faces, ten arms and three eyes. The subtle lustre was projected in her forehead, which is eternal, indestructible and spotless. Observing the same, the goddess Prakrti, spreading her arms, desired to have Brahma who was spread in all the directions, but she failed in her efforts. Then getting surprised, the mother Prakrti adored him with devotion for a long time with all his five mouths. From eastern face, she recited dhatu (primary substance); from the southern face pratyaya; sabda from the western face, vibhakti from the northern five faces. She worshipped the spotless one, who is blissful, cloud like, complete and is eternal Brahman. Thereafter, the omniscient one entered into all her five faces and took to a human form, by which he came to be known by the name of self born in the world. Since he was born from invisible Prakrti, he has been known as the one who was invisibly born.

## \|\| 2.147.75-89 \|\|

*tasya hetoḥ svayaṃ devī varadā lokarūpiṇī \|*  
*mahālakṣmīśca pūrvārddhājjātā ṣoḍaśalokinī \|\| 75 \|\|*

*aṣṭādaśabhujāstasyā lokarakṣaṇatatparāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tadadbhutaṃ rūpaṃ svayaṃbhūrvismayānvitaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*praviśya bahudhā bhūtvā nāntaṃ tasyā jagāma ha \|*  
*bṛhatvādbahurūpatvādbrahmā nāmeti viśrutaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*śramito bhagavānbrahmā satyalokamupa sthitaḥ \|*  
*mukhebhya udbhavairdevo vedaistuṣṭāva śaṃkaram \|\| 78 \|\|*

*ciraṃ kālaṃ tadaṃgādvai nadīnadasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*ekārṇavaṃ tadā jātaṃ śete tatra svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sahasrayugaparyaṃtamuṣitvā'vyaktabhūḥ svayam \|*  
*satyalokamupāgamya punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ cakāra ha \|\| 80 \|\|*

*anantāḥ sṛṣṭayaścāsangaṇarūpāḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*tābhirvyaktamabhūtsarvaṃ mahālakṣmīmayaṃ jagat \|\| 81 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā bahutvaṃ sṛṣṭīnāṃ mahālakṣmīḥ sanātanī \|*  
*vismitābhūcca sarveśaṃ bhagavantamupāyayau \|\| 82 \|\|*

*natvovāca vaco ramyaṃ kṛṣṇamavyaktamaṃgalam \|*  
*bhagavannityaśuddhātmannarāścāsanmahattarāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*kathaṃ teṣāṃ ca gaṇanā kartavyā ca mayā sadā \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasyā dvidhābhūtaśca so'vyayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*pūrvārddhātsa tu raktāṅgaḥ parārddhādgaurarūpavān \|*  
*caturbhujassa raktāṃgo gauravarṇaścatu rbhujaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*sarvasṛṣṭigaṇānāṃ ca sa īśo bhagavānbhavaḥ \|*  
*gaṇeśo nāma vikhyātaśceśvarassa tu viśrutaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*paraścaturbhujo yo vai yogidhyeyo niraṃ janaḥ \|*  
*ekadā vidhito jātaḥ śivaḥ pārvativallabhaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*gaṇeśaṃ pūjayāmāsa sahasrābdaṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*tadā prasanno bhagavāngaṇeśaḥ śarvapūjakaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*varaṃ varaya taṃ prāha pārvatīsahitaṃ haram \|*  
*prasannātmā bhavaḥ sākṣāttuṣṭāva ca vinamradhīḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

75-89. Thereafter, for that Purusa, the universal goddess and the bestower of the boon, took to the form of Mahalaksmi. The same leader of the universe, with her eighteen arms, protected the world. Observing the astonishing type of form, Brahma - the self bom one, was immensely surprised. Thereafter, Brahma entered that form of the goddess and tried to understand about her with many of his forms, but was unable to do so. Since that time, because of his being gigantic and innumerable, he came to be known as Brahma. Thereafter, getting tired, lord Brahma returned to Satyaloka and delighted lord Siva with the reciting of the Vedas from his five faces. After a long time, the rivulets and rivers flowing out of the limbs of Brahma, turned into a deep ocean. While sleeping in the same oceanic water, Brahma spent a thousand yugas. Reaching Satyaloka, he again started creating the universe again. With the same creation which was intoxicated, having separate ganas, the entire universe looked as Mahalaksmi. At that point of time, the eternal Mahalaksmi, observing the crowding and multiplicity of the creation, got surprised and went to lord Sarvesa and humbly spoke to invisible lord Krsna who bestows grace “O lord, you are always having the auspicious soul, a large number of the humans have been created. How shall I be able to keep a count of the same?” On hearing these words, the imperishable one divided himself into two forms. The upper half was of red complexion with four arms and the lower part was of fair complexion with four arms. In the form having red complexion and four arms, the ganas of the universe took to the form of Isa, who came to be known as lord Bhava Ganesa. The other form of fair complexion is the spotless one, which was always adored by the yogins. Once Siva, having been born of Brahma, performed vrata with Parvati and worshipped lord Ganesa for a thousand years. At that point of time, getting pleased with the worship of lord Siva, Ganesa said to him- “You better ask for a boon.” Then he humbly offered prayer to Ganesa.

## \|\| 2.147.90-100 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*namo viṣṇusvarūpāya gaṇeśāya parātmane \|*  
*caturbhujāya raktāya yajñapūrṇakarāya ca \|\| 90 \|\|*

*vighnahaṃtre jagadbhartre sarvānandapradāyine \|*  
*siddhīnāṃ pataye tubhyaṃ nidhīnāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*prasanno bhava deveśa putro bhava mama priyaḥ \|*  
*iti śrutvādipūjyastu gaṇeśo bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*pārvatyāḥ sarvadehāttu tejobhūtātsamu dbhavaḥ \|*  
*tadā kailāsaśikhare sarve devāssavāsavāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*maṃgalārthamupājagmurdevadevasya mandire \|*  
*mahotsavaśca tatrāsītsarvalokasukhāvahaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare tatra sūryaputraḥ śaniḥ svayam \|*  
*krūradṛṣṭiḥ samāyātaḥ kālātmā devamaṇḍape \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tasya darśanamātreṇa sa bālo viśirā hyabhūt \|*  
*hāhākāro mahāṃścāsītkailāse guhyakālaye \|\| 96 \|\|*

*tacchiraścaṃdraloke vai tulāsaṃsthe divākare \|*  
*saptaviṃśaddinānyeva prakāśayati bhūtale \|\| 97 \|\|*

*niṃdito daivataistatra śanirjanabhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*gajasya mastakaṃ chittvā dantaikaṃ rāgarūpi yat \|\| 98 \|\|*

*tacchiśoḥ kaṃdhare rakte'ropayatsūryasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*gaja yonyā stuto brahmā karkaṭasya tadā śiraḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*samāropya tu tadyoniḥ karkaṭo viśirīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ gajānano jāto gaṇeśaśceśvaraḥ svayam \|\| 100 \|\|*

90-100. Lord Siva said- “Salutation to the form of Visnu. Ganesa has four arms, being yajna-murti, besides having the red complexion. He removes obstacles. He feeds the universe. He bestows delight to all beings. He is the lord of Rddhi and Siddhi, salutation to him. Getting delighted, you kindly agree to be my son.” On hearing these words, Ganesa, who is the favourite of the devotees and who is beginningless, then emerging out of the limbs of Parvati, took to the form of a child. At that point of time, Indra and other gods assembled for celebrating an auspicious festival at Kailasa. This festival was quite pleasant for each and every living being. At the same time, Sani - the son of the Sungod, also arrived there. He is known to have an evil eye. At the mere glance of Sani, the head of the child was cut off. Observing which there was a disturbance at Kailasa. When the sun was in Libra zodiac, the head illuminated the world for twenty seven days. At that point of time, all the gods were denounced. Then the Saturn cut off the head of an elephant and placed it over the trunk of the child. Thereafter, Brahma removed the head of the elephant and placed the head of a crab in its place. The birth of Gajanana has been thus described, who is known as Ganesa and Isvara himself.

## \|\| 2.147.101-104 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā gaṇeśastu gurorvacanamuttamam \|*  
*svamukhātskaṃdhamutpādya kāśyāṃ jātaḥ sa ceśvaraḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*daivajñasya dvijasyaiva putro bhūtvā śubhānanaḥ \|*  
*ḍhuṃḍhirājastato nāmnā prasiddho'bhūnmahītale \|\| 102 \|\|*

*jātakābharaṇaṃ nāma jyotiḥśāstraṃ phalātmakam \|*  
*kṛtvā sa vedarakṣārthe śaṃkarācāryamāgamat \|\| 103 \|\|*

*śiṣyo bhūtvā prasannātmā gurusevāparo'bhavat \|*  
*iti te kathitaṃ vipra ḍhuṃḍhirājo yathābhavat \|\| 104 \|\|*

101-104. Suta said- Hearing this, Ganesa taking out his shoulders form his mouth was reborn at Kasi in a Brahmana family, who came to be known as Dhundhiraja. He composed an astrological treatise under the title of Jatakabharanam relating to Phalita Jyotisa for the safety of all the gods. After this, he became the disciple of Svami Sankaracarya. O Brahmana, I have thus narrated the story of the birth of Dhundhiraja.

## Chapter 148. Birth of Aghorapatha Bhairava, Rudra Mahatamya and Balasarma

## \|\| 2.148.1-11 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*ṣoḍaśābde ca samprāpte brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*sa uṣitvā ca kamale sthitaḥ sṛṣṭyarthamudyataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*etasminnantare vaktrātsamudbhūtā ca śāradā \|*  
*dvivyāṅgaṃ sundaraṃ tasyā dṛṣṭvā brahmā smarāturaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*balād gṛhītvā tāṃ kanyāmuvāca smarapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*ratiṃ dehi madāghūrṇe rakṣa māṃ kāmavihvalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu sā mātā ruṣā prāha pitāmaham \|*  
*pañcavaktro'yamaśubho na yogyastava kandhare \|\| 4 \|\|*

*caturvaktro vedamayo yogyassarveśvare tvayi \|*  
*ityuktvāntardadhe mātā brahmā krodhānvito'bhavat \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasya kopāgninā toyaṃ śuṣkabhūtamabhūdbhuvi \|*  
*śāntibhūte ca tatkope rudro jāto bhayaṅkaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bhairavo nāma vikhyātaḥ kālātmā saptavāhanaḥ \|*  
*svanakhaiśca nṛsiṃhābhaiḥ kṣiptvā tatpañcamaṃ śiraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*jagarja balavānrudraḥ śaṅkaro lokaśaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*bhayabhītastadā brahmā bhairavaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nātha naḥ pāpabhūtānāṃ dhiyo yo'sau pracodayāt \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa bhagavānbhairavo lokaviśrutaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*brahmabhūtamahaṃ svāminvareṇyaṃ tvāmupāgataḥ \|*  
*savitustadvareṇyaṃ yadbhargo devasya dhīmahi \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gāḍhamuccai rurodāśu khātpetuścāśrubindavaḥ \|*  
*tato vṛkṣāssamudbhūtā rudrākṣāṇāṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 11 \|\|*

1-11. Brhaspati said- Brahma with invisible birth, was lodged in a lotus for sixteen years. Then he again tried to start the creation. At the same time, goddess Sarada emerged out of his mouth observing whose divine and beautiful limbs, Brahma became lustful, caught her forcibly and expressed his attraction for her. He said- “O passionate one, you protect me by uniting with me. On hearing this, the mother getting enraged, said to Brahma - the grandsire- “Your fifth head being inauspicious, is not fit to remain over your shoulder. You are the lord of all. Therefore, only the four divine heads are fit enough to remain over your shoulders.” Thus speaking, the mother Barada disappeared from the scene, which enraged Brahma immensely. Because of his anger’s fire, the entire water on the earth dried up. Subsequently, when Brahma’s rage was subsided, there emerged a terrific Rudra, who was known аs Bhairava, Kalatma and Saptavahana. He making use of his nails resembling Narasimha, removed his fifth head. Thereafter, lord Siva, who bestows welfare on the people, in the form of the same Rudra, thundered aloud, as a result of which in panic, Brahma went to take refuge with Bhairava. He said to him- “O master, you bestow noble wisdom over an evil minded person like me.” On hearing these words, lord Bhairava, who is quite well known in the world, said to him-“O master, О form of Brahman, I am also present before the illustrious person like you, which happens to be the lustre of Savita’s adorable form. Thereafter, he cried aloud, as a result of which the tears dropped from the sky continuously, which contributed to the growth of the Rudraksa trees.

## \|\| 2.148.12-17 \|\|

*śivo brahmavadhādbhītastatkapālaṃ gṛhītavān \|*  
*kapālī nāma vikhyātaṃ bhairavasya tadā hyabhūt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarvalokeṣu pūtāni yāni cāyatanāni ca \|*  
*tāni tānyeva gatvāśu śuddho nābhūcchivaṅkaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ekadā teṣu vṛkṣeṣu saṃsthito bhagavānharaḥ \|*  
*tadā brahmavadhe doṣaṃ tyaktvā dūramupāgataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhṛti vai śambhurdhṛtvā rudrākṣamuttamam \|*  
*purīṃ kāśīṃ samāyātaḥ kapālastena mocitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kapālamocanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ jātamaghāpaham \|*  
*etasminnantare brahmā sarvadevasamanvitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*samāgatya mahādevaṃ tuṣṭāva stutijaistavaiḥ \|*  
*makarasthe divānāthe śaśinaśceśvaraṃ śubham \|*  
*kapālinaṃ mahārudraṃ cakāra bhagavānvidhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

12-17. On the other hand, getting frightened from the killing of Brahma, Siva carried his head with him, as a result of which the Bhairava form of Siva came to be known as Kapali. At that point of time, Siva too proceeded on for pilgrimage to all the sacred places, but he could not be relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya. Once lord Siva, while roaming about in the universe, started living under the Rudraksa tree, where he was relieved of Brahmahatya. At the same time, Siva wore Rudraksa over his body. Thereafter, reaching Kasi, he consigned the skull of Brahma and the place came to be known as Kapalamocana. In the meantime, Brahma with all the gods arrived there and adored Siva eulogizing him. Thereafter, when Surya was in the Capricomus zodiac symbol, he established Mahadeva as a leader in the lunar disc.

## \|\| 2.148.18-20 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ kapālī bhairavaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*svamukhātsvāṃśamutpādya kāśyāṃ jāto hyayonijaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kapālamocanātkuṇḍātsamāgamya mahītale \|*  
*yatirūpo vedanidhirbhairavo nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*aghoraṃ kaṭhinaṃ mārgaṃ svaśiṣyānsamacodaya \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śaṅkarācāryamāgamya śiṣyobhūtvā sa bhairavaḥ \|*  
*ḍāmaraṃ nāma vai tantraṃ mantrabhūtaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*kīlitā ye tu vai mantrāstena cotkīlitīkṛtāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Suta said- Listening to the words of Brhaspati, Kapali Bhairava took out his own amsa from his own mouth and took birth at Kasi without human contact. While coming out of the Kapalamocana-kunda, he reached the earth and was known as Vedaniddhi ascetic an earth, who preaching Aghora mantra to his disciples, accepted Svami Sankaracarya as his preceptor. He composed a treatise on yantras and mantras in which the contemporary problem was explained. Thereafter, he accepted to serve Svami Sankaracarya.

## \|\| 2.148.21-33 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*mandodarī mayasutā tripurādhipateḥ svasā \|*  
*tripure tu tadā naṣṭe mahāviṣṇuṃ sanātanam \|*  
*bhaktyā tuṣṭāva sā devī pratyahaṃ guptabhāvinī \|\| 21 \|\|*

*bhaktibhāvāttato yogaṃ harau prāpya mahottamam \|*  
*vindhyādrikandhare ghore tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

*caturyugaṃ ca dviśataṃ tasyā jātaṃ samādhitaḥ \|*  
*vaivasvate'ntare prāpte dvādaśe caiva kṛdyuge \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pulastyo brahmaṇaḥ putro viśravā roṣato'bhavat \|*  
*śatābdaṃ ca tapastaptvā viśravā nāma yo muniḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sumālino'tha daityasya sutāṃ vai kaikasīṃ mudā \|*  
*samudvāhya vidhānena pulastyassa ca viśravāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kadalīvipine ramye gandhamādanaparvate \|*  
*sa reme ca tayā sārddhaṃ viśravā bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*rāvaṇaḥ kumbhakarṇaśca tayorjāto hi rākṣasau \|*  
*rāvaṇo mātṛbhaktaśca pitṛbhaktastato'nujaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sahasrābdaṃ tapo ghoraṃ cakratustau varārthinau \|*  
*tadā prasanno bhagavānparameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*dadau tābhyāṃ varaṃ ramyamajeyaṃ devadānavaiḥ \|*  
*tau tu labdhavarau kruddhau puṣpakaṃ yānamuttamam \|*  
*gṛhītvā ca balādvīrau yuyudhāte parasparam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tābhyāṃ vinirjitā devāstyaktvā svargaṃ sukhapradam \|*  
*pārthivaiḥ pūjayāmāsuḥ śivaṃ kailāsasaṃsthitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ekādaśābdamārādhya te devā girijāpatim \|*  
*śaṅkarācca varaṃ prāptā nirbhayāśca tadābhavan \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śivo'pi ca svapūrvārddhājjāto vai mānasottare \|*  
*girau yatra sthitā devī gautamasya tanūdbhavā \|*  
*añjanā nāma vikhyātā kīśakesaribhoginī \|\| 32 \|\|*

*raudraṃ tejastadā ghoraṃ mukhe kesariṇo yayau \|*  
*smarāturaḥ kapīndrastu bubhuje tāṃ śubhānanām \|\| 33 \|\|*

21-33. Brhaspati said- Mandodari - the daughter of the danava Maya, was the sister of Tripuradhisvara. After the destruction of Tripura, lord Visnu was adored by her continuously with her devoted mind. The lord then observing her devotion, bestowed yoga to her. As a result of this, she disappeared over the mountain peak of the Vindhya mountain taking to a deep samadhi. Subsequently, with the passing of all the four yugas two hundred times and at the time of the twelfth Krtayuga of Vaivasvata Manvantara, by the anger of Pulastya - the son of Brahma, Visrava was bom. Thereafter, Vistava - the son of Pulastya, married the daughter named Kaikasi of daitya Sumali. He enjoyed conjugal pleasure with her over the pleasant banana forest of the mountain Gandhamadana. Subsequently, Raksasa named Ravana and Kumbhakarna were bom to the couple. Ravana was devoted to his mother, while Kumbhakarna was a great devotee of his father. With an intention of achieving a boon, both of them performed sincere tapas for a thousand years. Getting pleased with their tapas, the Grandsire appeared before both of them and granted them the boon to become invincible from the gods and the danavas. Subsequently, both of them, with the use of force, usurped the puspaka plane, fought a fierce battle to desert the heaven and adored lord Siva for eleven years over the Kailasa mountain. Subsequently, by receiving a boon from lord Siva, they became fearless. On the other hand, lord Siva also, by his upper half part, was bom in the hermitage of ascetic Gautama from the womb of Anjana who was the wife of the great monkey Kesari. Out of the Raudra lustre which entered in her mouth, thereafter the great monkey united with her.

34-49. At the same time, the Wind-god entered the body of Kesari, united forcibly with Anjana. The couple enjoyed the conjugal pleasure and thus twelve years were passed. Thereafter, the beautiful damsel retained the pregnancy for a year and lord Rudra was bom as a red monkey as their son. Because of the child being ugly, the mother dropped the child at the mountain base. But inspite of that, the valorous son still reached the top of the mountain and captured the Sungod, who was present there. When the Sungod was so tortured by Rudradeva, Devendra reached there and attacked Rudra with vajra, but still he did not free the Sungod. The gods then getting terrified, cried for the rescue of the Sungod. On hearing the cries of the gods, Ravana, who was troublesome for the universe, caught hold of the tail of the monkey and started fighting him with fists. At that point of time, the son of Kesari, freeing the Sungod, fought with him for a year. Thereafter, Rudra in the form of a monkey, immensely frightened Ravana, who fled to all the four directions. At the same time, the great sage Visrava reached there and adored Rudra with the Vedic stotras. Lord Rudra then getting pleased, built his abode near Pampa lake of Ravana. He was the benefactor of the universe having a detached mind. Since he lived there permanently, he came to be known as Sthanu. Ravana was envious of the lokas and the gods, who was beaten with fists by the people. The Rudra in the form of a monkey came to be known by the name of Hanuman. Thereafter, Brahma getting pleased with his tapas, went to that place and said- “O Ocean of tapas, you please listen to my words. At the same time of Vaivasvata Manvantara in the first part of the twenty eight Tretayuga, Sri Rama will incarnate on earth. At that point of time, gaining his devotion, you would feel beholden and successful.” Thus speaking, he made him the leader of the moon of the month of Bhadrapada. At the same time, Mandodari was given over to Ravana. Ravana then becoming the leader of the south-west direction, met with the end of his life at the hands of Sri Rama.

50-53. Suta said- On hearing this, taking to a definite form of a human, Hanuman came to be known on earth as Balasarma and he entered into a debate with Sankaracarya for a month. Subsequently, getting defeated from the great saint, he accepted to be his disciple. While serving his preceptor, he composed a literary work on the story of all the castes, which was based on tantras and mantras.

## Chapter 149. Glory of Rudra

1-9. Brhaspati said- When the sight of the world with sat and asat is consigned in the great dissolution, it becomes invisible. At that point of time, aksara or indestructible only remains in the form of his lustre, which is all pervading and beyond comprehension. The lustre does not become hard, subtle, cool, or hot, besides being free from the beginning, middle and end. It is formless. It is everlasting, desolate, devoid besides being excellent, and which becomes visible only to the people well-versed in yogic exercises. The same also appears in the line of Prakrti. Below the same, like the auspicious mark over the sole of the feet, there remains the position of the glorious rajas, sattva and tamas. Оmkarа is the very base of all of them, who happens to be the supreme Brahman and achieving which one is never reborn. Thus, while being carried in the water of the time of dissolution, long time passed. The supreme Brahman then again desired to be reborn and with the same ahamkdra (pride), produced panca-tanmatras (the subtle form of matter). The Jnana-Vijnana and Pancabhutas (five elements) were bom. Then the Prakrti which was inactive, lord Vibhu by his own will, divided the globe into two parts with twenty two tattvas. The part with virtues created the jiva with buddhi or intelligence. Both of them bestow consciousness to the universe. As a result of this, the eternal jiva is known as Virad. Out of the navel of the same Virad, there emerges a lotus flower of the size of a hundred yojanas.

10-16. The lotus-seated Brahma is born out of the same lotus. He has two arms, four heads, besides two feet. He possesses twenty seven limbs. Such a lord Brahma, soon after his birth, got immensely worried. He thought-“Who am I? What is the source of my birth? Who are my parents?” When he was so thinking, with a huge sound in his heart, the supreme Brahman said- “The performance of tapas is essential.” On hearing these words, the Vidhati performed tapas for lord Visnu for a thousand years. Lord Visnu had four arms in his yogic form. He is absolute, having enormous virtues. The lotus-seated lord Brahma then started meditation in a samadhi. Visnu then took to the form of a child with dark complexion, valorous, adorned with all the weapons and the ornaments. Brahma was then lodged in the lap of Visnu, as a child occupies the lap of his father.

17-33. Then becoming conscious, on looking at the child and getting overpowered with confusion, Brahma started calling him- “My child, my child.” On hearing these words, the lord delightfully said to him - “O Brahman, I am Visnu, your father.” But Brahma failed to accept the words of Visnu. When the controversy between the two arose, then the lord - the form of darkness, appeared on the scene, in the form of a Jyotirlinga or a linga of resplendence. It was quite vast and frightening, besides having been spread in infinite yojanas. At that point of time, Brahma took to the form of a swan, while Visnu took to the form of a Varaha or a boar. Brahma went upwards and Visnu went below the earth. They made all the efforts for a hundred years in order to know the end of the Jyotirlinga. Since both of them were unable to know about the truth, they were ashamed. Both of them worshipped the Jyotirlinga for long. Listening to the prayers of both of them, lord Siva was pleased and he appeared before them in the form of Bhava. Thereafter, he made Kailasa as his abode and started performing tapas there, which continued for five years. Then Тarаkа -the best of the danavas, performed hard tapas for a thousand years and earned boon from Brahma, who also warned him (Tarakasura) that he would meet with his end at the hands of the son of Siva.” On hearing these words, he attacked the gods, overpowered Indra and usurped the kingdom of heaven. The gods then went to Kailasa and worshipped Siva. Getting pleased, lord Rudra asked them to seek a boon. On hearing these words, the gods spoke quite humbly- “O lord, Brahma has granted a boon to Taraka that he would meet with his end from the son born of the semen of Siva. Therefore, O lord, you kindly marry for the sake of our protection. During the Svayambhuva Manvantara, there had been a Prajapati named Daksa. Out of his sixty daughters, Sati is the best who had worshipped for a year. Getting pleased, you had accepted her as your wife, but his ignorant father Daksa denounced you, as a result of which because of the fault of her father, Sati ended her life. Thereafter, the divine lustre of Sati reached the Himalaya mountain. Feeling painful, the lord of mountain Himalaya started feeling lustful and he adored Aryama - the lord of Pitrs. Aryama then delightfully gave away his daughter named Mena who had been auspicious, beautiful and pleasant. Observing her, he took to the human form resembling the gods and enjoyed conjugal sports with her in the forest for long.

34-50. In due course of time, she gave birth to an extremely beautiful girl, who was fair-complexioned. Soon after her birth, she became nine years old. She worshipped lord Siva for a long time. For a hundred years, she stood in water; for a hundred years, she stood in fire flames or five types of fire; for a hundred years, she inhaled air only; for a hundred years she remained in the sky; for a hundred years, she remained in the lunar disc, for a hundred years in the solar disc; for a hundred years in a cave and for a hundred years, with her yogabala she was lodged in the Mahat-tattva and had an auspicious audience with the lord. For the last three hundred years, she is lodged at one and the same place. Therefore, О lord Mahadeva, getting pleased, you kindly marry Siva also known as Parvati. Salutation to you, О lord Mahadeva.” Listening to these beautiful words, lord Siva said to the gods- “The words spoken by Brahma are not appropriate because the Rudras who are senior to me are still unmarried. Having been bom of a flame, Mrgavyadha and others remain unmarried. I am younger to them and I am known as the lord of the yogins. It would be inappropriate for me to accept an auspicious lady who is the form of Мaуa and creator of the universe. Because the goddess Bhagavati is a damsel who has expanded the globe, she is the form of a mother for the yogins living on earth. Then being г yogi, how could I accept a woman who is the form of a mother. Therefore, for the sake of your task, I shall take out my semen and drop it into the fire and in that way, your task would be done.” Thus speaking, lord Siva gave away his semen to the Firegod and again started his tapas. Thereafter, Indra and other gods carried (the semen of Siva) and went to Satyaloka with the Firegod. Reaching there, they narrated the sequence of events to Brahma. On hearing their story, Brahma meditated on Кrsnа and offering salutation to him, said- “Reaching the supreme stage of dhyana-marga, all the matter narrated by Brahma was narrated to Sri Krsna and hearing which the lord took out some lustre from his mouth, which was quite beautiful human. All the beauty of the world was reflected in his body. The same person came to be known in the world as Pradyumna. Brahma then absorbed him in his own body. Then he gave away Pradyumna who tortured Sambarasura.
