51-66. After his birth, the people of the entire universe became extremely lustful. So much so, that even the trees becoming passionate, uniting with the creepers as well as the rivers, desired to subside their passion. At that point of time, Siva — the form of Kala, who is Rudra and who produced flame from his third eye, neutralized their passion. Then Pradyumna -the son of Krsna, for the sake of Mahadeva, placed the five arrows of Kama over his bow. Siva - the protector of Iokas, moved with the Uccatana arrows. With the Vasikarana arrow, he was overpowered by the female; with the Stambhana arrow, he stood before Parvati; with the Akarsana he became desirous of Siva; and with Marana arrow, he was fainted. Then finding Siva, having been fainted, Parvati disappeared. Regaining senses, Siva got up and started lamenting- “O dear, having the moon like face, О beloved, having the pitcher like breast, О beautiful one, you protect me because I am suffering from passion. You appear before me. I am your servant at present.” When Siva was so lamenting, Yogini Siva reached there and offering her salutation to him, she said- ‘ О Deva, I am a girl who moves as per the wish of her parents. Therefore, you should accept my hand with their approval. Having been injured with the arrow of Pradyumna, Siva accepted the words of Parvati and sent the seven Rsis to the place of Himalaya, who reaching there narrated the specific information to Parvati’s father and got his consent for the marriage. All the gods joined in the marriage of Siva with delight, because it was quite essential for them to join the marriage of the leader of the globe. At the time of the marriage, Himalaya felt disturbed with the presence of such a large number of gods at the time of the marriage. Thereafter, the lord of the mountains went to Girija and apprised her of the factual position. On hearing the words of her father, Girija, who have many forms and who is eternal, created crores of the images of Rddhis and Siddhis and put all of them to serve his father. Observing them, Brahma, with all the gods, felt surprised. They also adored Parvati who happened to be the gem of the ladies.

67-85. The Gods said- In your name Uma, U stands for reasoning and Ma stands for Laksmi because you appear in various forms. All of us offer salutation to you in the name of Uma repeatedly. Salutation to Gauri, Kali because of your black complexion, and because of your having fair complexion you are known Haimavati. Salutation to you. Because of you being the wife of Siva and living with Rudra, you are known as Bhavani. Since you are beyond the reach of the yogins, you are known as Durga, salutation to you. We are unable to conceive your glorious form. Being the form of Candika and mother goddess, you are known as Amba. Salutation to you.” Listening to the prayer of the gods, the goddess Sarvamangala - the bestower of boons, said- “I shall remove your danger from the daityas, because getting delighted from the three worlds, I shall incarnate on earth.” Thus speaking, Parvati reaching Kailasa with Siva, entered his cave, where she enjoyed all the bliss for a thousand years. At the same time, the gods getting apprehensive of the destruction of the earth, became panicky and adored lord Siva with Brahma, who was leading them. At that point of time, both of them getting ashamed while repenting also got enraged, which frightened the gods and they fled away from that place. But the valorous Pradyumna stood there like an immovable bull and was reduced to ashes in the fire of anger of Rudra. He was deprived of his solid human body as a result of which he got the subtle form, earning him the title of Ananga or formless. Inspite of his being without a form, Kamadeva is still powerful as he was earlier. Thereafter, Rati adored lord Siva for a year who is known as the beloved of Siva. Getting pleased with her tapas, the eternal Siva bestowed boons to Rati thus- “O goddess Rati, I am speaking to you, which you listen. You would remain present in the hearts of men. By the means of the body of the men, you would have union with your husband as Pradyumna, who is bom of Кrsnа and my devotion. After the passing of the Svarocisa Manvantara and during the Vaivasvata Manvantara, at the end of the twenty-eighth Dvapara, the lord would incarnate on earth. At that point of time, he would be bom as the son of Кrsnа and you would enjoy his company for long over the Meru mountain. In the Dvapara and other yugas, he getting absorbed in gold, would remain present on earth, like Sri Krsna himself. In this way, during the period between afternoon and the evening in each one of the kalpas, lord Visnu would himself appear on earth and cany on the activities for the benefit of the people.” Thus speaking, lord Siva disappeared from the place. Thereafter, Rudra - the beloved of Girija, was established over the position of Bhavaraja.

86-100. Suta said- On hearing this, Bhava took out an amsa form his own mouth and dropped it in the river Godavari, which was born in the house of Acaryasarma and became the younger brother of Ramasarma. He came to be known as Ramanuja. Once Ramasarma, becoming the follower of Patanjali, planned a pilgrimage of all the holy places and reached Kasi, which had been the favourite place of Siva. While at Kasi, he had an audience with Haripriya - the disciple of Sankaracarya, but Ramasarma was defeated there. Feeling shameful at his defeat from the disciple of Sankaracarya, he returned home. Learning of this episode, Ramanuja, who was well-versed in all the scriptures, went to Kasi with his brother and his disciples. Reaching there, they started discussion on the subject of Veddnta. Sankaracarya spoke on Siva, while Ramanuja spoke on Krsna Both the sides continued the discussion for a month, Ramanuja produced lord Visnu before the audience, who is also known as Vasudeva. Vasudeva name appeared with the division of Sacchidananda. He is said to be of the vamsa of Vasus and because of this, Vasudeva became Brahma and his essence was Vasudeva. The one who is known as the eternal Visnu and is adorable by Siva. Thereafter, getting ashamed, Sankara entered the discussion. As a result of this, an aspect of Siva-sutras conceives Siva as Vasudeva. But Ramanuja displayed the image of lord Visnu in these creations as well who is known as Govinda. The name by reciting which the goddess Sarada could be achieved, the same is called Govinda. Therefore, this is the changed name of the lord. But Girisa cannot be called Govinda, because he happens to be the lord of the mountains. Since Rudra has the bull as his vehicle, therefore, he cannot be conceived as Gopaia. Though Siva is called Pasupati as well, but he has not been known as Gopati or the lord of cows. Feeling disturbed by this argument, Sankaracarya felt ashamed and took refuge with Mimamsa. Both of them continued discussion for ten days in the related Sastras, in which Ramanuja supported the yajna-Purusa.

101-111. But Sankaracarya refuted it in this way that though Dharma emerging form conduct has been arranged by yajna, but in the yajna of Daksa Prajapati, the rules of conduct were so demoralized. On hearing these words, Ramanuja humbly said- “The yajna was created for the performing of the activities, for the maintenance of the universe, which emerged out of Aksara-brahman. The same Aksara is the form of Siva which is enshrined in the word Sabda-brahman. The same imperishable performer is also known as Purana-purusa. Therefore, as compared to Aksara, the supreme soul is better. During the performing of yajna, the performer Aksara could not be satisfied. Therefore, he came to be known as yajna-Purusa in the Vedas and the world. At that point of time, lord Siva observing the uplifting of his great grandson, supported him in the form of yajna with his divine voice. But the competent yajna-Purusa, taking Siva to be like the preceptor, fled from the place and by so doing, he established a great dharma. Hearing these words, Sankaracarya feeling humiliated, took refuge in the logic and said - Bhava is called Mrda, because of his birth and satisfaction, besides Bhava by the one who feels the person is known as the performer as well as the lustre. Similarly, the one who steals away the sins, he is called Rudra - the remover of the sins. Accordingly, Siva alone is the creator himself, the feeder himself as well as the remover (of the sins) himself. The same Siva produces Visnu on earth and Brahma with lotus seat, emerges out of Visnu.” On hearing this, Ramanuja said- “Graceful is lord Siva, who possesses the enormous glory. It is truth and unshakable truth that the creator as well as the cause of creation is Siva himself. But I have a great doubt that the glorious Siva always on the name of Rama, why does he recite the name of Hari? The one who has created the universe out of his lustre, besides other creations. He is beyond measure even by Sesa. The yogins also roam about in him, he is the personified lord of my lord. On hearing this, Sankaracarya feeling somewhat ashamed, then started discussion on yogic treatises in which he also established the worship of lord Krsna also. Since he is Kalatma, besides lord Sri Krsna, leader of yoga and the follower of yoga. Thereafter, while discussing over the Samkhya philosophy, Ramanuja established the superiority of Kapila. The one who consumes semen is called Kapi and the one who emerges out of him is known as Kapila. In this way, Kapi or monkey was identified with Rudra. Besides Kapila is the form of Visnu, who is omniscient and is the form of all or has the universal form. On hearing these words, Sankaracarya humbly became the disciple of Ramanuja, clad himself in white clothes and started reciting the spotless name of Govinda in his heart. Thus, I have narrated the glory of Rudra with reference to context, hearing which a person is adorned with wealth, sons and truthful speech.

2-15. Brhaspati said - During the early period of Satyayuga and during the time of Vaivasvata Manvantara, the tamasi Ilvala, beloved of the sage Visrava, worshipped Lord Siva. At the same time, an immensely wicked person known by the name of Yaksasarmi adored a Yaksini and pleased her. Subsequently, the great sinner united even with the daughter-inlaw of his friend, by which he attracted the diseases of leprosy. Finding the Brihmana suffering from leprosy, the Yaksini disowned him and travelled to Kailasa secretly. Once on the day of the Sivaratri vrata, inspite of his suffering from hunger, Yaksasarma was not given the food. On the other hand, he was forced to observe the performance of the puja of lord Siva. The next morning the Brahmana broke his fast. Subsequently, he met with his death in the same temple. With the influence of the same, he became the king of Karanataka country who is known as Rajaraja - king of the mandala. The valorous Rajaraja commanded his people to perform the worship of lord Siva through the Brahmanas daily making all the arrangements. With the influence of the same merit, he ruled perfectly well for a hundred years, enjoying all the comforts. Thereafter, the king who was a noble soul, entrusted the kingship to his son and went on pilgrimage to Kasi and started worshiping Siva, reaching there. After three years, Mahadeva appeared before him in the form of Jyotirlinga and came to be known as Rajesvara. Then getting purified by him, the king reached the womb of Ilvala and was bom as her son with all the auspicious symbols. Because of his birth in the dark and inauspicious time, the infant came to be known by the name of Kubera in the world. He pleased Brahma with his tapas, who getting pleased with him, gave away the city named Lanka built in gold to Kubera. For the processing of the worldly activities, three crores of Yaksas were created. Their master is known by the name of Yaksarad.

16-30. Kinnaras of various forms, who always obey the orders, make the offerings to him. Kubera - the lord of Guhyakas, who decorate their heads with the locks of hair, is said to be self-born. For the benefit of the people, he collected the gems from the people and distributed them among the people, the humans and Raksasas in their homes. All the religious people and the followers of the Vedas are decorated by Kubera — the form of Dharma. Similarly, the wicked rich people and their king are also supplied riches by Kubera. He is the lord of Raksasas and the Raksasas tear out the flesh from the bodies of the humans which are burnt in fire flames. Possessing the supernatural powers when observed by Ravana, he removed them from Lanka and himself occupied the throne (of Lanka). At that point of time, Kubera took refuge with lord Siva, who removes the miseries of the people. Lord Siva became friend of Kubera and got the city of Alakapuri built and made Kubera - the lord of the same. The city of Alaka always bestowed grace on the noble people. By living in that city, Kubera started leading a most comfortable life. Listening to that, Ravana who always live out the world, went to Alakapuri over Kailasa and spotted the beloved of Nalakubara. Ravana, who belonged to the race of Pulastya, becoming anxious forcibly united with the damsel Suprabha, who getting enraged said to Ravana - “O Ravana - the creator of miseries for the people, О Sinful one, I am like your daughter-in-law. Because of this sin, you would attract leprosy. The plane of Kubera, which had been stolen by you like the wealth stolen from the house of thieves, would desert your place and go to its owner.” Having been inflicted with the curse, Ravana felt painful and staying at Kailasa, worshipped lord Siva. He adored Siva for twelve years, but still Siva did not grace him.

31-45. Thus feeling disgusted, Ravana started dropping his heads in the burning fire flames in the homa. In this way, he offered the entire solid part of his body for lord Rudra. Only the ashes were left, But because of the boon granted by Brahma, he could not die. At the same time, he achieved another pleasant body out of the fire, which was also offered by the valorous one to lord Siva. At that point of time, the Pisacas taking to the form of the wind, consumed the body of Ravana. But he still remain alive because of the boon of Brahma. Half of the body in the form of the wind was again offered by Ravana to lord Siva, which was consumed by the terrific Matrganas, but Ravana still remained alive because of the boon of Brahma. Subsequently, the non-existing body, when received by Ravana was again offered by him to lord Siva, at that point of time, Siva - the lord of arrogance, was pleased with Ravana and developed friendship with Ravana like Kubera. Then Ravana, instead of single head, got crores of heads. Because of the pleasure of the god of gods, his body became as hard as vajra. In this way, by means of the harsh boons, Ravana was filled with pride and started roaming about in the universe with the young damsels of Devas, Daityas, humans as well as the serpents in the universe. In this way, Ravana completely uprooted the eternal dharma of chastity and devotion to husband by the wives. Because of his satisfying lord Siva, he never felt hungry or thirsty. Because of the discontinuing of the performing of yajnas, even the gods felt hungry and lived in discomfort. Thus suffering, the gods went to Brahma in the ocean of milk and started adoring lord Paramesvara. At that point of time, lord Brahma feeling pleased with the devotion of the gods, said to the gods- “In the Svetavaraha kalpa, no danava comparable with the troublesome Ravana, has bom. In the earlier Мarkandеуа kalpa, there had been the daityas named Kumbha and Nisumbha. Kumbhakarpa and Ravana are comparable with them, being quite terrific.

46-57. Besides, there had been many Ravanas in the past, but none of them is comparable with the present one. The Prakrti from which I have been bom as Brahma, the same Maya Prakrti has the capacity to create crores of universe and when the gods are facing grave misfortune, Devarat himself is competent enough to relieve them of the miseries. When Indra - the god of gods, faces obstruction or when lord 6iva or Rudra face terrific misfortune, I always remain ready to remove the same. Similarly, for the removal of my misfortunes, lord Hari is always there to remove my calamities. When Brahma is faced with great danger, the supreme Prakrti removes the same. In earlier times, Madhu and Kaitabha were bom as the two great daityas. For his protection, Brahma adored Ambika. Then achieving strength from Ambika, I killed the demons Madhu and Kaitabha. Therefore, at my command, all of you should adore Visnu-maya, who provides protection to all. You should lake refuge with her and worship her.” On hearing these words, the gods adored the supreme Sakti. At that point of time, the goddess who is also known Brahmajyoti Siva, divided herself in two parts, in the form of Sita-Rama who are known as the supreme force, incarnated on earth. Sita also divided herself into two parts and created Rama and Laksmana, who represented Sabda and Artha. Out of them, Rama was the combination of sabda and Laksmana represented the artha or meaning. His semen resembled vajra and his Brahmacarya had been quite strong. The other monkeys were effeminate. Sita bestowed welfare to both of them, being the form of the supreme Sakti and was bom of earth without human contact.

58-63. A person, who has recited the name of Rama a hundred times, his merit is equal to that of the reciting of the name of Sita. During the period of deficiency, the Prakrti, who is beyond destruction is complete, getting herself divided into three parts, makes Rama to appear from the earlier part, Laksmana from the middle and from the eastern part the eternal Yoganidra emerged and is also lodged there. In other kalpas, lord Rama sleeps in the ocean of milk and Laksmana is in the form of Rudra, while Laksmi is in the form of Sita - the daughter of Janaka who appeared on earth. Similarly, many weapons like Sudarsana from Bharata, Sankha as Satrughna on earth, Paratpara Brahman known as Rama appeared in the Vardha kalpa, besides Pradyumna appeared as Laksmana, Aniruddha as Bharata, and kill the Raksasas known as Ravana and others. In the form of Svayambhu Rama, he incarnated on earth and established his auspicious glory in the universe and then returned the puspaka plane to Kubera. He ruled the earth for eleven thousand years and ultimately achieved the final beatitude.

64-73. Suta said- On hearing this, the first Vasudevata known as Kubera, took out a part of himself from his mouth and sent it to the house of Dharmadatta Vaisya which was born there as a son and became famous on earth by the name of Trilocana of Mathura Puri. Spending all his resources, he went on pilgrimage to the holy places. Reaching there, he became the disciple of Ramananda Vaisnava. Subsequently, returning home, with the command of his preceptor, Trilocana devoted himself to Sri Rama and started serving the saints. Getting pleased with his devotion, in the thirteenth month, Rama himself started living in his house as a slave, and started distributing to the Brahmanas several of the gems, gold, various types of costumes and several types of eatables, to their satisfaction. At that point of time, the Vaisnavas and the Yogins were given the things of their likings. Thus, by serving the people for many years, lord Rama - the killer of Ravana, once said to Vaisya Trilocana- “I am Rama (the lord) and not your human slave. Having been attracted with your devotion, while living in your house, I did whatever pleased you and worked for your welfare. But from today onwards, I shall live in your heart as a servant. Thus speaking, lord Rama disappeared from the place. The Vaisya then developed detachment. He left his wife and son, and started meditating on Sri Rama over the bank of the river Sarayu.

## Chapter 151. Birth of Rankana Vaisya

1-15. Brhaspati said- During the period of Svayambhuva Pracinabarhis, the king of Dhruva dynasty started performing a yajna. At the advice of Narada, discarding the violent yajnas, he followed the path of Vaisnavism and produced ten sons. These sons were of the same shape and were known as Practeas. All the sons accepting the command of their father, started performing tapas in the deep water of the ocean. Feeling delighted with their tapas in the deep water of the ocean, lord Brahma, who is four-faced and is known as the self-born, appointed seven of the sons of Praceta as the leaders of the seven oceans. The eighth son was declared as Ratnakara. The ninth was made the leader of Uttaradesa of Manasa. The tenth one was established in a branch of Meru delightfully. The first son was known as Apava because of the flowing of the water in the world. The second son, because of his being the lord of Yadavas, was known as Varuna. At the same time, Brahma reached there and presented him with a noose. Since that date, Varuna came to be known as the holder of pdtfa or noose. In earlier birth, he had worshipped the goddess Brahmasakti. He always consumed Varum (wine) and always remained under its influence. Because of his being the loving devotee of Bhadrakall, he collected several types of red flowers and red flower garlands and worhsipped the same goddess daily, reciting the mantras. After completing the puja of the goddess, he also recited the Navarna-mantra. Thus he daily offered incense, eatables, betel and fruit of the season to the eternal goddess known as Mahakali, Bhadrakali and Mahalaksmi with devotion. Subsequently, he made offerings in the fire flame of sugar, sesamum and honey. He pleased the goddess Jagadamba daily. For the sake of Visnu, he recited the Madhyacarita (of Durga-Saptasati). Then Navarna-mantra was recited appropriately. This was the daily routine of the Brahmana. This process continued for a period of three years, after which the goddess Sarvamangala was pleased with him and asked him to beg for a boon. On hearing the affectionate words, Apava — the best of the Brahmanas, humbly prostrated before her and started offering prayer to the eternal goddess Bhadrakali

*vināśito namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

16-29. Apava said- During Visnukalpa, there lived a danava named Mahisasura who had crores of chariots, horses and elephants. At that point of time, the danava had conquered all the three lokas and established himself over the seat of Mahendra and started ruling the world. While thus ruling the universe, Svarocisa Manvantara was passed. Thereafter, lord Visnu taking out his own lustre as also of all other gods, collected the same in the form of a huge flame. At that point of time, the goddess Bhagavati of her own accord, appeared in the form of Jyotirlinga and killed Mahisasura. I offer my salutation to her repeatedly. Earlier in the Rudrakalpa, a thousand-headed Raksasa emerged out of the mouth of lord Siva, who came to be known as Ravana. He was strong and a terrific demon. He made his abode under the Ioka mountain and ate up the gods, daityas as well as the humans. In this way, in the period of the sixth Manvantara, he conquered the entire globe and established his own reign over it. Thereafter, during the Vaivasvata Manvantar a period and in the twenty eighth Tretayuga, Sankarsana Rama himself incarnated. At the age of sixteen years, he went to Janakapura and broke the bow named Ajagava. At that point of time, Brahma and other gods arrived there and taking him to be eternal Rama, said to him- “The thousand-faced Ravana has terrific people in the world.” Hearing these words, Rama with Sita, boarding over plane driven by swans, went to Lokaloka mountain and fought a terrific war with Ravana. At that point of time, Hanuman had been perched over the flag of the plane driven by the swans. The Vedas served as the horses of the plane and Brahma was the charioteer of the plane. The war continued for a divine year. Thereafter, the Raksasa getting enraged, making use of his two thousand arms, made Rama and Laksmana senseless and then thundered aloud. At the same time, Brahma offered prayer to the Brahmarupini goddess of the water and pleased her. The eternal and peaceful goddess destroyed the demon in the form of Sita. Therefore, salutation to the goddess again and again.

## \|\| 2.151.30-33 \|\|

*brahmakalpe purā cāsīttālajaṃghānvayodbhavaḥ \|*  
*muro nāma mahādaityo brahmaṇo baladarpitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*brahmāṇḍeśaṃ mahārudraṃ mahendrādisamanvitam \|*  
*sa babhūva parājityādhikārī raudra āsane \|\| 31 \|\|*

*devaissārddhaṃ mahādevo mādhavaṃ kṣīraśāyinam \|*  
*gatvā nivedayāmāsa sa viṣṇuḥ krodhasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*jagāma garuḍārūḍho yatra daityo muraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tena sārddhamabhūdyuddhaṃ tasya devasya dāruṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. Earlier in the Brahmakalpa, there lived a daitya named Mura in the dynasty of Lalajangha, who receiving the boons from Brahma, became immensely intoxicated. He defeated Mahendra besides all the gods including lord Mahadeva - the leader of the universe. Then he occupied the seat of Rudra. Thereafter, accompanied with all other gods, Mahadeva went to lord Narayana sleeping in the ocean of milk and apprised him of the factual position. On hearing the words of the gods, lord Visnu getting enraged, mounted over Garuda and departed to the abode of the daitya for the purpose of fighting with him. Reaching there, a terrific battle was fought between both of them.

*sahasrābdamato jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmā bhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*parāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ nityāṃ tuṣṭāva ślakṣṇayā girā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*prasannā sā tadā devī kumārī saptahāyinī \|*  
*caturbhujāstrasahitā bhūtvā daityamuvāca ha \|\| 35 \|\|*

*parājito'yaṃ bhagavāndaityarājena vai tvayā \|*  
*vijayā nāma me ramyā kaiścinnāhaṃ parājitā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*unmīlinī viñculī ca trispṛśā pakṣavarddhinī \|*  
*jayā jayantī vijayā varṣevarṣe kramādaham \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-48. Both of them kept on fighting for a thousand years. Then Brahma, feeling panicky, eulogized the goddess Prakrti. The goddess then getting pleased, took to the form of a seven years old maiden girl, having four arms and holding weapons in her hands. She said to the daitya Mura- “O lord of daityas, the lord has been defeated by you, but I have never faced a defeat from anyone till now. Therefore, I am known by the name of Vijaya. In every year, I take to the alternate forms of Unmllini, Vinjuli, Trisprga, Patravarddhini, Jaya, Jayanti and Vijaya. Vaispava and other eleven gods are my sons. Therefore, I am also known by the name of Ekadasi and by the same name, I remain present in the Vedas. Therefore, you becoming valorous and gaining victory in the battle, accept the hand of Visnu’s mother and be adorable by all.” On hearing these words, the daitya Mura, falling for the beauty of the damsel, started fighting with the goddess, but he could not stand in the battle even for half of a second. The goddess shattered him completely. Subsequent to the death of daitya Mura, his younger brother Narakasura creatd a Maya, who was the destroyer of the gods. She was terrific. But the goddess Ekadasi - the mother of the universe, destroyed her just with the uttering of a humkara, along with Narakasura. After this, she uttered a loud roar. At the same time, the lustre of both the daityas assembled in the eatables. With the desecration of the eatables, the humans attracted several types of diseases. Observing all this, the goddess spoke to the Sungod as well Sukra- “Both of you are well known in the world, therefore, you purify these eatables.” Then both of them obeying the command of the goddess, were adored by her. Therefore, the mother established everything. Salutation to her again and again. Thus hearing the divine stotra, the goddess Bhadrakali said to the Brahmana named Apava- “At the time of the dissolution of the mobile and immobile world and at the time of deluge in the ocean, even then you would lead a comfortable life due to my grace. Reciting this stotra, myself getting pleased, I shall always bestow boons on the people in future.” Thus speaking, the goddess disappeared from the scene and the Brahmana was changed into the form of Vаrunа.

*ābrahmastambaparyantaṃ sarvaṃ viṣṇumayaṃ jagat \|*  
*jñātvā dṛṣṭvā gataḥ kāśyāṃ rāmānandaṃ haripriyam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*natvā tacchiṣyatāṃ prāpya tatra vāsamakārayat \|*

*daśaviprānpañca nṛpānpañca vaiśyāñchataṃ gavām \|*  
*punarujjīvayāmāsa śavabhūtānsa yogavān \|\| 56 \|\|*

49-56. Suta said- Listening to the words of Brhaspati, lord Varuna, who is said to be the second Vasu, took out some lustre form his mouth and threw it over the ground, which fell in the city of Dehall in the house of Dharmabhakta and entered into the womb of his widow daughter. The lord himself established his own amsa in the womb of the girl who would incarnate as a son. This delighted Dharmabhakta immensely. Soon after the birth of the son, he was given the name of Namadeva, who became well-versed in Samkhya-yoga philosophy and achieved sagacious knowledge. Considering the entire world as the form of Visnu, he then travelled to the holy city of Kasi. Reaching there, he became the disciple of Ramanandacarya and started living there. At that point, Sikandara. after accepting the throne of DehalT, summoned Namadeva and put him to test. Getting pleased with him, the Kalipriya Mleccha presented Namadeva half a crore of gold coins. Making use of the wealth so given by the Dehall Ruler, Namadeva built stone steps over the bank of the Ganga for the bathing of the pilgrims there. The same yogi, with use of his yogic strength, brought back to life ten Brahmanas, five kings, five Vai£yas and a hundred cows.

## \|\| 2.151.57-65 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*

*samāgatya vacaḥ prāha varaṃ brūhi dvijottama \|\| 58 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa hovāca bhagavaṃste namo namaḥ \|*  
*prakṛteśca paraḥ putro bhūyānmama varāttava \|\| 59 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tadā brahmā vismitaḥ prāha taṃ dvijam \|*  
*ekā vai prakṛtirmāyā triliṅgajananī svayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tayā dṛśyaṃ jagatsarvaṃ samutpāditamātmanā \|*  
*prakṛteśca paro yo vai paramātmā sa cāvyayaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*abuddhirbodhanirato hyaśrutiśca śṛṇoti vai \|*  
*adehaḥ sa spṛśatyetadacakṣuḥ paśyati svayam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*ajihvonnaṃ sa gṛhṇāti sa jighrati na sā vinā \|*  
*amukho vedavaktā ca karmakāraḥ karaṃ vinā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*apado gacchati hyetadaliṅgo nāribhogavān \|*  
*aguhyo hi karotyetāṃ satattvāṃ guhyabhūtinīm \|\| 64 \|\|*

*śabdabrahma sparśamayaṃ rūpabrahma rasātmakam \|*  
*gandhabrahma paraṃ jñeya tasmai tadbrahmaṇe namaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

57-65. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, there lived a Brahmana named Visvanara. Being childless, he started adoration of Brahma by various means. After the lapse of a year, Brahma getting pleased with the Brahmana’s worship, appeared before him and asked him to seek for a boon. Hearing the words of Brahma, the Brahmana said- “Salutation to you, О lord. You give me a boon that I should get a son, who should be the supreme Brahman and beyond Prakrti ” Brahma felt surprised at the request of the Brahmana and said to him- “The same Maya Prakrti who herself is the producer of Trilinga, has created by herself the visible universe. Paramatma lives beyond that Prakrti and is known us Avyaya. Inspite of his being devoid of wisdom, he is wise, he hears without the ears, touches without the body and look at everything without the eyes. He consumes food without a tongue, smells without the nose, recites the Vedas without the mouth, indulges in all the activities without the hands and walks without the feet. He enjoys the woman without the linga. Without private parts, he has the rectum of nature. The same is Sabda-Brahman, (sparsa) touch, (rupa) beauty, (rasa) essence and (gandha) fragrance. Therefore, I offer my salutation to Brahman.

## \|\| 2.151.66-77 \|\|

*prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādi ubhāvapi \|*  
*vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisambhavān \|\| 66 \|\|*

*ekārthau tau ca śabdaikau rūpaikau nityavigrahau \|*

*puṃstrīnapuṃskajananī jñeyā sā prakṛtiḥ parā \|*

*ajanmā janma cāpnoti mayā jātaḥ sa janmavān \|*  
*kathaṃ sa puruṣo nityastava putro bhaviṣyati \|\| 69 \|\|*

*ato viśvānara mune māyābhūto hariḥ svayam \|*  
*tava putratvamāpnoti varānmama janārdanaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*ityuktvāntardadhe devaḥ pāvakastadvarādabhūt \|*  
*aṣṭānāṃ ca vasūnāṃ ca pāvako hi patistvayam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vaiśvānara iti khyāto'bhavatsvāhāpatiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sa tu pūrvabhave devaḥ purā kalpe'nalobhavat \|\| 72 \|\|*

*naiṣadho brāhmaṇo dhīmānyathā rājā nalastathā \|*  
*saṃkaṭāyāṃ gate bhūpe damayantī pativratā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*svapiturgehamāsādyānveṣayāmāsa bhūpatim \|*  
*tadā nalo dvijaṃ prāpto damayaṃtīpatiḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ mohamāpannā damayaṃtī śubhānanā \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare tatra vāguvācāśarīriṇī \|\| 75 \|\|*

*nāyaṃ nalastava patirbrāhmaṇoyaṃ sumohitaḥ \|*  
*analo nāma vikhyāto devavākyātsa cābhavat \|\| 76 \|\|*

*mahāsarasvatīṃ devīṃ tuṣṭāva sa tu mohitaḥ \|*  
*tasya puṇyaprabhāvena viśvānarasuto'bhavat \|\| 77 \|\|*

66-77. Similarly, both the Prakrti and Purusa are without beginning and have all the blemishes or virtues as are found in Prakrti. Therefore, both have the same meanings, the same words, the same form or beauty and the eternal body which is beyond the beginning, middle or end besides being eternal, auspicious and everlasting. It is the Parasakti, which produces man, woman and eunuch. She is Prakrti beyond comprehension, besides being Purusa, Kavi, subtle, imperishable, knowledgeable, supreme and as such is without both. Then inspite of possessing the above virtues, he is bom of me, then how could he be your son? Therefore, О Visvanara, the lord possessing Maya also known as Janardana, shall incarnate in your place through me.” Thus speaking, Brahma disappeared from the scene. Thereafter, Pavaka or fire emerged who happens to be the lord of eight Vasus. The same Pavaka (fire) - the lord of Svaha, came to be known as Vaisvanara. In the initial kalpa, he was bom in the race of Analasa Brahmana, who lived in the Naisadha country during the time of the king Nala. When the king Nala was facing distress or misfortune, at that point of time, the chaste Damayanti spent her time in the house of her parents while searching for the king Nala. At that point of time, looking at a Brahmana named Anala, Damayanti fell for his beauty and decided to have him as her husband. But at the same time, there had been an announcement in the sky that he is not her husband Nala, but is Anala. After worshipping Brahma, he has achieved this form. He is Anala and not Nala. He has also adored the goddess Sarasvati and with the boon granted by her, he has been bom in the house of Visvanara.

## \|\| 2.151.78-81 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ pāvako bhagavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*svamukhātsvāṃśamutpādya saṃjātastu tato vasuḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*raṃkaṇo nāma vikhyāto lakṣmīdattasya vai sutaḥ \|*  
*nagare kāṃcanapure vaiśyajātisamudbhavaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*yaṃkaṇā nāma tatpatnī babhūva ca pativratā \|*  
*sarvadravyavyayaṃ kṛtvā dharmakāryeṣu daṃpatī \|\| 80 \|\|*

*kāṣṭhamānīya vikrīya bubhujāte parasparam \|*  
*rāmānaṃdastasya gurū raṃkaṇasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

78-81. Suta said- Listening to the narration of Brhaspati, lord Pavaka took out his lustre from his mouth and sent it on earth, which was born as a son to the best of Vaisyas known as Laksmidatta, living at Kancanapura and came to be known as Rankana. The name of his chaste wife was Yankana. The couple spent all their riches for the religious purposes and spent their lives selling the wood. They had got this advice from their preceptor Ramananda.

*aṃguṣṭhamātro bhagavānmahendro vajrasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*kukṣimadhye samāgamya cakre garbhaṃ sa saptadhā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*jīvabhūtānatibalāndṛṣṭvā sapta mahāripūn \|*  
*ekaikaḥ saptadhā tena mahendreṇa tadā kṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*namrībhūtaśca tāndṛṣṭvā mahendrastaiḥ samanvitaḥ \|*  
*yoni dvāreṇa cāgamya praṇanāma tadā ditim \|\| 14 \|\|*

*prasannā sā ditirdevānmahendrāya ca tāndadau \|*  
*marudgaṇāśca te sarve vikhyātāḥ śakrasevakāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

1-15. Brhaspati said- When the terrific and immensely strong sons of Diti were killed at the hands of Visnu, she again tried to appease Kasyapa. After twelve years, her master Kasyapa getting pleased, said to his wife - “O beautiful one, you ask for a boon.” On hearing these words, she replied with delight “The co-wife Aditi has twelve sons, while I had only two of them. Their younger brother Visnu always protects the gods and has killed both my sons. Therefore. I feel extremely painful. O master, you get me such a son, who would be the destroyer of the twelve Adityas.” Hearing these terrific words, the sage Kasyapa said to his wife- “Brahma has created Dharma and Adharma in this world. Still those who follow the dharma, are the favourites of Brahma and those who are averse to it, are the enemies of the humans. Therefore, both of your sons who were the followers of adharma, have been killed. O religious-minded one, you listen to what I have to tell you. First of all, you follow dharma purifying your mind and by so doing, you should be getting a strong son. He would be intelligent, having long life.” On hearing these words, Diti was conceived by Kasyapa and thereafter, she started performing vrata, following auspicious conduct. Indra, on the other hand, realizing that she had a child in her womb, getting frightened, he lived in the house of Diti like a servant and started serving her as one does serve his preceptor. When the pregnancy reached the seventh month, influenced with the illusion of Indra, Diti once slept in her house in an inauspicious manner. At the same time, Indra taking to subtle form, entered the womb of Diti, holding the vajra in his hand and her pregnancy was cut by him in seven pieces. When he found that the seven parts were still alive, after having been cut into seven pieces, he further cut off each one of the seven pieces in further seven pieces. Thereafter, becoming humble, Indra came out with all of them and through the vaginal passage, offered his salutation to Diti. At that point of time, Diti delightfully handed over all her sons to Indra. By so doing, all of them remained with Indra like the servants and came to be known as Marudganas.

## \|\| 2.152.16-30 \|\|

*sa tu pūrvabhave jāto brāhmaṇo lokaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*ilo nāma sa vedajño yathelo nṛpatistadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ekadā balavānrājā manuputra ilaḥ svayam \|*  
*ekākī hayamāruhya merorvipinamāyayau \|\| 17 \|\|*

*meroradhaḥ sthitaḥ khaṇḍaḥ svarṇagarbho haripriyaḥ \|*  
*nivāsaṃ kṛtavāṃstatra kṛtvā rāṣṭraṃ mahottamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ilenāvṛtamevāpi kṛtaṃ tatra sthale surāḥ \|*  
*ilāvṛtamiti khyātaḥ khaṇḍo'bhūdvibudhapriyaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bhārate ye sthitā lokā ilāvṛtamupāgatāḥ \|*  
*merurgirirvṛkṣamayo vidhātrā nirmito hi saḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ārohaṇaṃ naraistasmitkṛtaṃ svarṇamayaṃ śubham \|*  
*tamāruhya kramāllokaḥ svargalokamupāgataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tāndṛṣṭvā manujānprāptānsadehānsvargamaṇḍale \|*  
*vismitāśca surāssarve maheśaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*jñātvā sa bhagavānrudro bhavānyā saha śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*ilāvṛtavane ramye sa reme ca tayā saha \|\| 23 \|\|*

*etasminnantare prāpto vaivasvatasuto mahān \|*  
*ilonāma mahāprājño mṛgayārthī sadāśivam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nagnabhūtaṃ samālokya netre saṃmīlya saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*lajjitāṃ girijāṃ dṛṣṭvā śaśāpa bhaga vānharaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*asminkhaṇḍe sadā nāryo bhaviṣyaṃti ca māṃ vinā \|*  
*ityuktā vacanaṃ tasminnāryassarvā babhūvire \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ilā babhūva nṛpate kanyā janamanoharā \|*  
*bahukālaṃ meruśṛṃge mahattapamacīkarat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ilāsamādhibhūtāyāḥ saptaviṃśaccaturyugam \|*  
*jātaṃ tata ilā kanyā tretāmadhye tu candrajam \|*  
*budhaṃ devaṃ patiṃ kṛtvā caṃdravaṃśamajījanat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ayodhyādhipatiḥ śrīmānyadelāvṛtamāgataḥ \|*  
*tasya rājñī madavatī nāmnā tuṣṭāva pārvatīm \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tadā prāpta ilo viprastasyā rūpeṇa mohitaḥ \|*  
*pasparśa tāṃ madavatīṃ rājñīṃ kāmavimohitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

16-30. The jiva in the womb, like the king Ila of the earlier times, was known as a famous Brahmana by the name of Ila. Once the valorous king Ila —the son of Manu, riding over a horse, travelled alone to the thick forest of the Meru mountain. Reaching there, the king turned the region known as Haripriya below the Meru mountain as an excellent country and started living there, establishing his own country there. With the establishing of the suzerainty there, the gods also started living there. Because of that, the region came to be known as Ilavrta. Subsequently, the people from Bharata also reached there. Brahma had created the Meru mountain like a tree and for climbing up there, people erected the golden step to reach there. By climbing those steps, the people started reaching even the heaven. At that stage, the gods observed that the humans were arriving in the heaven with human bodies. They felt surprised at this and went to Mahesa and apprised him of the reality. On hearing this, lord Siva together with Bhavani and all the mountains went to the same forest and started roaming about there. At the same time, Ila - the son of Vaivasvata, arrived in the same forest for the purpose of hunting. Reaching the same spot, the king found lord Siva was too roaming there in naked condition. He closed his eyes and stood there. At that point of time, lord 6iva finding that Girija was feeling ashamed, pronounced a curse—“Whosoever would come in the region of my country, all of them would become women except myself.” At the words so spoken by lord Siva, all the people present there were turned as females. The king Ila also was turned into a beautiful damsel. The female Ila, while living over the mountain peak, performed severe tapas. After the lapse of the four yugas twenty seven times, Ila accepted Budha - the son of Indra, as her husband and created the lunar dynasty. At the time, when Ila - the monarch of Ayodhya established his suzerainty over the mountain Ilavrta, at that point of time, his queen named Madavati, pleased Parvati with drink. After some time, a Brahmana named Ila, who was as beautiful as the king himself, felt attracted at the beauty of the queen, became lustful and touched the queen Madavati.

## \|\| 2.152.31-36 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare tatra vāguvā cāśarīriṇī \|*  
*ilo nāyaṃ dvijaścāyaṃ tava rūpavimohitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*anilo nāma tatraiva vikhyāto'bhūddvijasya vai \|*  
*kāmāgnipīḍito viprassa tuṣṭāva ca pāvakam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*chittvāchittvā śiro ramyaṃ tasmai jātaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*dattvā tuṣṭāva taṃ devaṃ prasanno'bhūddhanaṃjayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*prāha tvamūnapaṃcā śadvibhedāñjanayiṣyasi \|*  
*tathāhaṃ mitravānbhūtvā tatsaṃkhyastava kāmadaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yathā kubero bhagavānṣaḍviṃśadvaruṇapriyaḥ \|*  
*tathāhamūnapaṃcāśadvibhedastava vai sakhā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ityukte vacane tasminditikukṣau dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vāyurnāma sa vai jātaḥ pāvakasya priyassakhā \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. At the same time, the divine voice from the sky declared- “He is not the king Ila, but is a Brahmana known by the name of Ila, who has fallen for your beauty. Then the Brahmana became popular by the name of Anila. Thereafter, the Brahmana burning with lust, adored Agnideva, offering his head to the fire god again and again in the fire, which reemerged with excellent beauty. Getting pleased with him, Dhanafijaya said- “You shall produce yourself in forty nine forms and I shall be your helper always. As lord Kubera is the helper of the twenty six Varunas, similarly, I shall be the favourite of all the forty nine of you. At these words so spoken by Dhananjaya, the excellent Brahmana entered the womb of Diti and was bom as Vayu, who happens to be the close friend of Pavaka

## \|\| 2.152.37-41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*dhānyapālasya vai gehe mṛlagaṃḍāntajaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*pitṛmātṛparityaktaḥ kāśyāṃ viṃdhyavane tadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*aliko nāma vai mlecchastatra sthāne samāgataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*anapatyo vastrakārī sutaṃ prāpya gṛhaṃ yayau \|*  
*kabīra iti vikhyātaḥ sa putro madhurānanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sa saptābdavapurbhūtvā godugdhapānatatparaḥ \|*  
*rāmānaṃdaṃ guruṃ matvā rāmadhyānaparo'bhavat \|\| 40 \|\|*

*svahastenaiva saṃskṛtya bhojanaṃ haraye'paryat \|*  
*tatpriyārthaṃ harissākṣātsarvakāmaprado'bhavat \|\| 41 \|\|*

37-41. Suta said- At the words so spoken by Brhaspati, he was bom as the son of Vaisya Dhanyapala in Kasi. Since he was bom at an evil time, his parents carried him and left him in the Vindhya forest. A Mleccha named Alika arrived there at the same time. He was a weaver and without a son. He carried the infant from that place and took him to his home. The beautiful infant was subsequently known as Kabira. Upto the age of seven years, the child was fed on cow’s milk alone. Since his childhood, he took Ramananda as his preceptor and stated adoring Rama. 3rl Rama also appeared before him and granted him all his desires.

## \|\| 2.152.42-50 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*uttānapādatanayo dhuvobhūtkṣatriyaḥ purā \|*  
*pitṛmātṛparityaktaḥ sa bālaḥ paṃcahāyanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*govarddhanagirau prāpya nāradasyopadeśataḥ \|*  
*sa cakre bhagavaddhyānaṃ māsānṣaṭ ca mahāvratī \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavānviṣṇurnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*khamaṃḍale padaṃ tasmai dadau prītyā nabhomayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tadvadanaṃ ramyaṃ māyāśaktyā diśo daśa \|*  
*svāminaṃ ca dhruvaṃ matvā bhaktinamrā babhūvire \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dhuvo'pi bhagavānsākṣātsarvapūjyo babhūva ha \|*  
*dikpatiḥ sa tu vijñeyo bhagaṇānāṃ patiḥ svayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*nabhaḥpatiḥ kālakaraḥ śiśumārapatissa vai \|*  
*paṃcatattvā hi vai māyā prakṛtistatpatiḥ svayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasmāddharāyāṃ saṃbhūto bhaumo nāma mahāgrahaḥ \|*  
*jaladevyāstato jātaḥ śukro nāma mahāgrahaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vahnidevyā tato jātaścāhaṃ tatra mahāgrahaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevyāṃ dhruvājjātaḥ keturnāma mahāgrahaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*grahabhūtaḥ sthitastatra nabhodevyāṃ tadudbhavaḥ \|*  
*rāhurnāma tathā ghoro mahāgraha upagrahaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

42-50. Brhaspati said- In earlier times, Dhruva had been the son of the king Uttanapada, who was abandoned by his parents at the tender age of five years. Thereafter, at the advice of Narada, Dhruva went on pilgrimage of Govardhana. He was a great performer of vratas and while reaching there, he meditated upon the lord for six months and getting pleased with him, lord Visnu established him in the sky region as a star. Looking at his beautiful face, Mayasakti, who pervades in all the directions, accepted Dhruva as her lord and offered herself to him with devotion and humility. In due course of time, lord Dhruva was adored by me and all. He happens to be the master of all the directions, constellations, besides the sky. He is the creator of time, lord of porpoises, besides being the spouse of Mayuprakrti of five tattvas. Similarly, Bhauma (Mars) emerged from the womb of the goddess earth, Venus from the womb of the goddess of water, Brhaspati from the womb of the spouse Svaha of Agni, Ketu from the womb of Vasudevi and the great planet Rahu emerged out of the womb of Nabhodevi, who has been described to be terrific as well as an asteroid or a minor planet. All of them were produced from the same planet Dhruva.

## \|\| 2.152.51-61 \|\|

*pūrvasyāṃ diśi vai tasmājjātaścairāvato gajaḥ \|*  
*āgneyyāṃ diśi vai tasmātpuṃḍarīko gajo'bhavat\[1\] \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vāmanaḥ kumudaścaiva puṣpadaṃtaḥ kramādgajāḥ \|*  
*sārvabhaumaḥ supratīko nabhodikṣu tu tatsutāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*abhramuḥ kapilā caiva piṃgalākhyā imāḥ kramāt \|*  
*tāmrakarṇī śubhradaṃtī cāṃganā cāṃjanāvatī \|\| 53 \|\|*

*bhūmidikṣu kariṇyaśca jātāstasmāttu tatpriyāḥ \|*  
*bhaginī ca tathā mātā sutā caiva snuṣā tathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*paśuyonyudbhavānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ tā yoṣitassadā \|*  
*devayonyudbhavānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ patnī smṛtā svasā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*manuvaṃśodbhavānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ cānyodbhavāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*iti dharmo vidhātrokto mayā proktaḥ surā hi vaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*dvidhā dhuvassa vijñeyo bhūmerūrddhvamadhastathā \|*  
*sadguṇaḥ sa divārūpo rātrirūpastamoguṇaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*adhodhruve sadā rātrirnārakāstatra vai sthitāḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvadhruve divā nityaṃ tapomadhye niśā divā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*maho janastapassatyaṃ teṣu nityaṃ dinaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*rauravaścāṃdhakūpaśca tāmisraṃ ca tamomayam \|*  
*teṣu nityaṃ smṛtā rātriḥ kalpamānaṃ ca kovidaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sa tu pūrvabhave cāsīdbrāhmaṇo mādhavapriyaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭyabdaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu prātaḥsnānaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tīrtha puṇyātsa vai vipro mādhavo mādhavapriyaḥ \|*  
*sunītyāṃ garbhamāsādya dhruvo bhūtvā rarāja ha \|*  
*ṣaṭtriṃśacca sahasrābdaṃ rājyaṃ kṛtvā dhruvo'bhavat \|\| 61 \|\|*

51-61. From them, the elephant named Airavata emerged from the eastern direction, the elephant Pundarika emerged from south-east direction, besides Vamana, Kumuda and Puspadanta elephants were bom. Sarvabhauma and Supratika elephants were bom from the same Gajendras. They are the lords of the sky as well as the directions. They had the cowelephants known by the names of Abhramu, Kapila, Pingala, Tamrakarni, Subhradanti, Angana, Anjanavati and others were also born of them. They live in the directions of the earth. Similarly, their sister, mother, daughter, daughter-in-law (were also born of them). They were bom as animals and had always remained wives of Nara-pasus. Their sisters were born in the family of gods. The wives of the humans bom in the race of Manu were the wives born of others. О gods, Brahma had himself described Dharma, which has been repeated by me to you. Now Dhruva (Pole star), getting divided into two parts, is lodged in the Iokas above and below the earth. By Sattvaguna, it is the day and by Tamoguna, it is the night and it is always lodged under the earth as the night and that is the place for the dwellers of the hell. With the presence of Dhruva above the earth, the Iokas of above region always have the day and the middle part has both the day and the night. Besides in the Maharloka, Janaloka and Tapoloka, there is the night always. In earlier birth, there was a Brahmana known by name of Madhava who was immensely devoted to the worship of the lord. Upto the age of sixty years, he travelled to all the places of pilgrimage. He used to take his bath in the early morning. With the influence of that merit, he was quite favourite of the lord. Thereafter, he was bom of the womb of the queen Suniti and was crowned as the king by the name of Dhruva. While ruling the earth for thirty six thousand years, he finally achieved the unshakable position of Dhruva.

## \|\| 2.152.62-66 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ sa dhruvaḥ paṃcamo vasuḥ \|*  
*gurjare deśa āgamya vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*naraśrīrnāma vikhyāto guṇavaiśyasya vai sutaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*kusīdaguṇaguptaśca naraśrīḥ putravatsalaḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā prāṇānyayau svargaṃ sa vaiśyatanayo dhruvaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*pratyahaṃ sa hareḥ krīḍāṃ vṛndāvanamahottame \|*  
*śivaprasādātpratyakṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣamavāptavān \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yasya putravivāhe ca bhagavānbhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*yādavaissaha saṃprāptastasya vāṃchitadāyakaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgamya naraśrībharktarāṭ svayam \|*  
*rāmānandasya śiṣyo'bhūdviṣṇudharma viśāradaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

62-66. Suta said- Thus listening to the speech of Brhaspati, Dhruva - the fifth Vasu, took out his lustre and threw it on earth, by which in the house of a Vaisya named Guna who was the foremost of the Vaisyas, the same was bom as a son and was known by the name of Narasri. He spent his life by giving the wealth on interest. Thus the Guna Vaisya loved his son very much. But Dhruva - the son of the Vaisya, met with the end of his life and proceeded on to the heaven. By the grace of siva, he used to witness the divine sports of Hari in Vrndavan, which delighted him the most. In the marriage of the son of the great devotee, lord Krsna participated with all the Yadavas, fulfilling his desire. Subsequently. Narasri, who was the devotee of Visnu, went to the city of Kasi and accepted Ramananda as his preceptor.

## \|\| 2.152.67-73 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*kadācidbhagavānatrirgaṃgākūle'nasūyayā \|*  
*sārddhaṃ tapo mahatkurvanbrahmadhyānaparo'bhavat \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tadā brahmā hariśśaṃbhuḥ svasvavāhanamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*varaṃ brūhīti vacanaṃ tamāhuste sanātanāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vaca steṣāṃ svayaṃbhūtanayo muniḥ \|*  
*naiva kiñcidvacaḥ prāha saṃsthitaḥ paramātmani \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tasya bhāvaṃ samālokya trayo devāḥ sanātanāḥ \|*  
*anasūyāṃ tasya patnīṃ samāgamya vaco'bruvan \|\| 70 \|\|*

*liṃgahastaḥ svayaṃ rudro viṣṇustadrasavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*brahmā kāmabrahmalopaḥ sthitastasyā vaśaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ratiṃ dehi madāghūrṇe no cetprāṇāṃstyajāmyaham \|\| 71 \|\|*

*pativratā'nasūyā ca śrutvā teṣāṃ vaco'śubham \|*  
*naiva kiṃcidvacaḥ prāha kopa bhītā surānprati \|\| 72 \|\|*

*mohitāstatra te devā gṛhītvā tāṃ balāttadā \|*  
*maithunāya samudyogaṃ cakrurmāyāvimohitāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

67-73. Brhaspati said- Once the sage Atri together with his wife Anasuya were engaged in Brahmadhyana, while performing the great tapas. At that point of time, Brahma, Visnu and Siva, mounted over their respective vehicles, tried to reach there. Reaching there, they asked Atri - the son of Brahma, to seek for a boon. But Atri felt their words to be of no consequence, kept on meditating as before. Reading his feelings, all the three of them then went to Anasuya - the wife of Atri and then spoke to her. At that point of time, having been overpowered by Anusuya. - the wife of Atri, Rudra was holding his linga in his own hand. Visnu was adding essence to the same and Brahma was engaged in making all the efforts to control his passion. All of them were praying her again and again- “O beloved with passionate glance, grant us a physical union, otherwise our lives are coming to an end in your very presence.” Listening to their inauspicious words and getting afraid of their rage, Anasuya kept silent and spoke nothing in reply. But the three gods, who had been utterly confused, forcibly caught hold of her and tried to have a union with her.

## \|\| 2.152.74-82 \|\|

*tadā kruddhā satī sā vai tāñchaśāpa munipriyā \|*  
*mama putrā bhaviṣyaṃti yūyaṃ kāmavimohitāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*mahādevasya vai liṃgaṃ brahmaṇo'sya mahāśiraḥ \|*  
*caraṇau vāsudevasya pūjanīyā naraissadā \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃti suraśreṣṭhā upahāso'yamuttamaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ namaskṛtya munipriyām \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurbhaktinamrāśca devapāṭhaiśca ṛṅmayaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*anasūyā tadā prāha bhavanto mama putrakāḥ \|*  
*bhūtvā śāpaṃ madīyaṃ ca tyaktvā tṛptimavāpsyatha \|\| 77 \|\|*

*ityukte vacane brahmā caṃdramāśca tadā hyabhūt \|*  
*dattātreyo hariḥ sākṣāddurvāsā bhagavānharaḥ \|*  
*tatpāpaparihārārthaṃ yogavanto babhūvire \|\| 78 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare devī prakṛtissarva dharmiṇī \|*  
*vidhiṃ viṣṇuṃ haraṃ cānyaṃ cakre sā guṇarūpiṇī \|\| 79 \|\|*

*manvaṃtaramato jātaṃ teṣāṃ yogaṃ prakurvatām \|*  
*hṛṣitāśca trayo devāssamāgamya ca tānprati \|\| 80 \|\|*

*uvāca vacanaṃ ramyaṃ teṣāṃ maṃgalahetave \|*  
*candramāśca bhavetsomo vasuḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ surapriyaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*rudrāṃśaścaiva durvāsāḥ pratyūṣaḥ saptamo vasuḥ \|*  
*dattātreyamayo yogī prabhāsaścāṣṭamo vasuḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ vākyaṃ samākarṇya vasavaste trayo'bhavan \|\| 82 \|\|*

74-82. At that point of time, getting enraged, the chaste wife of Atri pronounced a curse on them- “Because of your having been confused by lust, you would be my sons. О best of gods, the worship of Sivalinga and the feet of Visnu as performed by the people, would become the matter of joy.” On hearing these harsh words, offering their salutation to her, they became humble with devotion and reciting the Vedic hymns, adored the wife of the sage. Thereafter, Anasuya said- “All of you would be free of my curse only after becoming my sons and be delightful.” At these words of the spouse of the Rsi and in order to relieve themselves of the curse, Brahma took the form of Candrama, Visnu turned himself as Dattatreya and Rudra as Durvasa and they started performing the yogic practices. At the same time, the goddess Prakrti - the holder of dharma and possessing the three gunas (sattva, rajas and lamas), created another set of Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa and she engaged herself in other routine activities. While engaged in the yogic practices, the period of that particular Manvantara was passed. Thereafter, all the gods went to the yogi who speaking the welfare words, addressed them- “The god named Soma would be the sixth Vasu - the Moon. The seventh Vasu named Pratytisa would be Durvasa - the amsa of Rudra. The eighth Vasu named Prabhasa would be Dattatreya, who will be well-versed in yoga. Thus listening to the words, the three of them became the Vasus.

## \|\| 2.152.83-88 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ vasavo harṣitāstrayaḥ \|*  
*svāṃśena bhūtalaṃ jagmuḥ kaliśuddhāya dāruṇe \|*  
*dākṣiṇātye rājagṛhe vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*pīpā nāma sutaḥ somaḥ sudevasya tadā hyabhūt \|*  
*kṛtaṃ rājyapadaṃ tena yathā bhūpena tatpure \|\| 84 \|\|*

*rāmānandasya śiṣyo'bhūddvārakāṃ sa samāgataḥ \|*  
*harermudrāṃ svarṇamayīṃ prāpya kṛṣṇātsa vai nṛpaḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavebhyo dadau tatra pretatattvavināśinīm \|\| 85 \|\|*

*pratyūṣaścaiva pāṃcāle vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*mārgapālasya tanayo nānako nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*rāmānandaṃ samāgamya śiṣyo bhūtvā sa nānakaḥ \|*  
*sa vai mlecchānvaśīkṛtya sūkṣmamārgamadarśayat \|\| 87 \|\|*

*prabhāso vai śāṃtipure brahmajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*śukladattasya tanayo nityānaṃda iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*iti te vasumāhātmyaṃ mayā śaunaka varṇitam \|\| 88 \|\|*

83-88. Suta said- Listening to the words of Brhaspati, for the purification of Kali, all the three Vasus established their respective amsas. One of them was bom in the southern country in the royal house of the best of Vaisya named Sudeva. He was bom as a son of Sudeva. This Pipa in due course of time, was established over throne and he enjoyed the kingdom. Thereafter, becoming the disciple of Ramananda, he went on pilgrimage to Dvaraka. While living there, he made it a rule to distribute the gold coins earned by him to the Vaisnavas. Similarly, Pratyusa also was born in Pancala country as a son to the Vaisya named Margapala. He became popular by the name of Nanaka, who accepting Ramananda as his preceptor, enlightened the Mlecchas about the subtle path. Prabhasa on the other hand, was born as a son to an excellent Brahmana Sukladatta and became famous by the name of Nityananda. Thus, O Saunaka, I have narrated the glory of Vasus.

## Chapter 153. Birth of Raidasa

## \|\| 2.153.1-14 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā tānsurāndevo bhagavānbṛhatāṃpatiḥ \|*  
*aśvinau ca samālokya tayorgāthāmavarṇayat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vaivasvate'ntare pūrvaṃ viśvakarmā vicitrakṛt \|*  
*citraguptaśriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā citralekhāvinirmitām \|*  
*sparddhābhūto mahāmāyāṃ tuṣṭāva bahupūjanaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*prasannā sā tadā devī citrāyāṃ tasya yoṣiti \|*

*yakṣādhīśāśca ṣaḍviṃśatkuberādyāssamāgatāḥ \|*

*pāvakā ūnapaṃcāśadvāyavaśca tathā smṛtāḥ \|*  
*dhruvau dvau ca svayaṃ prāptau somāstatraiva ṣoḍaśa \|\| 6 \|\|*

*trayodaśa ca pratyūṣāḥ prāptā viśvaprarakṣakāḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭyuttaraṃ ca triśataṃ prabhāsā dinarakṣakāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhavādyāśca tadāḥ rudrāḥ śaśimaṇḍalarakṣakāḥ \|*  
*ādityāśca sthitāssarve saṃjñāyāśca svayaṃvare \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dānavā vipracittyādyāścaturāśītirāyayuḥ \|*  
*prahlādādyāstadā daityā vāsukyādyāśca pannagāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śeṣādyāśca tadā nāgāstārkṣyādyā garuḍāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*sarve svayaṃvare prāptā mahākolāhalohyabhūt \|\| 10 \|\|*

*etasminnaṃtare devī devakanyāsamanvitā \|*  
*saṃjñā devānprati tadā pratyakṣamabhavaddivi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tāṃ samālokya balavānbaliḥ kāmavimohitaḥ \|*

*tadā krodhāturā devā rurudhurdaityasattamam \|*

*dānavāśca tadā daityā nānāvāhanasaṃsthitāḥ \|*

1-14. Suta said— Lord Brhaspati then spoke about several tales and then started the tales relating to Asvinikumaras. During the early time of Vaivasvata Manvantara, Visvakarma, who had been an astonishing type of artisan, observed the figure of Citragupta made by Citralekha. Expressing his jealousy for the same, he started adoring Mahamaya by several means. Thereafter, getting pleased, the goddess Mahamaya who is the bestow er of all the knowledge, showered her amsa in his wife named Citra and took birth as her daughter named Samjna. When Samjna reached the age of sixteen years, her excellent father arranged for her svayamvara at the Meru mountain peak. The svayamvara was attended by Kubera - the lord of Yaksas, Varuna with other Yadavas, the Pavakas, forty-nine winds, both the Dhruvas, sixteen Somas, thirteen Pratyasas - the defenders of the day, three hundred and sixty Prabhasas, Bhava and other Rudras - the guards of the lunar region, besides all the Adityas. Similarly, eighty-four Garudas were also present there. At that point of time, huge noise was created in the svayamvara. At the same moment, the goddess Samjna appeared before the gods in the sky. Spotting her, the strong Bali holding her by his hand, in full view of all those present there, kidnapped her. The gods at that point of time, getting enraged, tried to stop the daitya Bali. They attacked him with various types of weapons and started a fierce battle. All the daityas and danavas used various types of vehicles with them and fought a terrific war with the gods.

*pakṣamātra mabhūdyuddhaṃ divyaṃ dānavadevayoḥ \|*

*viśvakarmā mayaścaiva kālanemirhariḥ svayam \|*

*vivasvāṃśca tadā saṃjñāṃ gṛhītvā rathasaṃsthitām \|*

*vivasvaṃtaṃ suraśreṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjñā vaco'bravīt \|*  
*matpatiśca bhavāndevo bhavetkāryakarassadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tvayā jitāhaṃ bhagavanbalervipriyakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*bhrātṛjāgrahaṇe doṣo na bhavetsa kadācana \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vīrabhuktā sadā nārī strīratnaṃ munibhiḥ smṛtam \|*  
*caturddhā prakṛtirdevī guṇabhinnā guṇaikikā \|*  
*ekā sā prakṛtirmātā guṇasāmyātsanātanī \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sattvabhūtā ca bhagi nī rajobhūtā ca gehinī \|*

*bahavaḥ puruṣā ye vai nirguṇāścaikarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*caitanyā'jñānavaṃtaśca loke prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aloke pāpajāssarve devabrahmasamudbhavāḥ \|*

*ko'pi putraḥ pitā bhrātā sa ca tasyāḥ patirbhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

*svakīyāṃ ca sutāṃ brahmā viṣṇudevaḥ svamātaram \|*  
*bhaginīṃ bhagavāñchaṃbhurgṛhītvā śreṣṭhatāmagāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vedamayaṃ vākyaṃ cāditisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*vivasvānbhrātṛjāṃ saṃjñāṃ gṛhītvā śreṣṭhavānabhūt \|\| 28 \|\|*

15-28. In that battle, a large number of daityas and the gods were destroyed. The battle continued for a fortnight, in which the earth of Ilavrta was covered with the dead bodies. In that war, Pancajanya-Data, Hayagriva-Mitraka, Aghasura-Aryama, Bala-Indra, Bakasura-Varuna, Sakata-Pransu, Vatsasura-Bhaga Vivasvan-Bali, Pralamba-Pusa, Gardabha-Savita, Visvakarma-Maya, besides Kalanemi and Visnu fought with each other trying to conquer the enemies. The daitya then getting defeated, fled away. At that point of time, Vivasvan made Samjna to mount his chariot and drove to Visvakarma, to whom she was handed over. Finding Vivasvan in a pleasant mood, Samjna said to him with delight- “Becoming my husband, you should always do my job. О lord, it is you, who defeating the powerful daitya Bali, have achieved me. There would be no blemish by getting the daughter of a brother, because such a relationship has been accepted by the sages saying that “The woman is to be enjoyed by a powerful warrior. The gem like lady as goddess Prakrti, because of her virtues, is divided into four forms. With one part, she is the eternal mother, in the other form she is the sister, representing sattva-guna. In the form of rajoguna, she is the wife and in the form of tamoguna, she is a girl. Therefore, salutation to the goddess. The absolute has been divided into various forms, viz., Caitanya (conscious), ignorant and bom of Prakrti etc. The people dwelling over Aloka (mountain) are bom of Brahma and other gods by sinful means. The conscious woman accepts such a persofi, then he can become her husband. Therefore, who could be the son, father, brother or husband of a woman? Brahma accepted his own daughter as his spouse, Visnu his own mother and Siva his sister as the spouse and ultimately gained glory.” Thereafter, on hearing the Veda like words, Vivasvan accepted the daughter of his brother as his spouse and attained glory.

*yamaśca yamunā caiva divyatejobhiranvitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kurukhaṃḍe mahāramye tapaṃtī tapa ulbaṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*gatvā dadarśa bhagavānsajñāṃ saṃbodhakāriṇīm \|*

*paṃcavarṣāntare saṃjñā garbhaṃ tasmāddadhau svayam \|*  
*tanayau ca samudbhūtau divya rūpaparākramau \|\| 39 \|\|*

*piturduḥkhaṃ samālokya jagmatū ravimaṇḍalam \|*  
*jitvā baṃdhū durācārau krūradṛṣṭyā tadā svayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*baddhvā tau svapituḥ pārśvama saṃprāptau vaḍavāsutau \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā vivasvānbhagavānvairiṇau samupāgatau \|\| 41 \|\|*

*saṃpīḍya tāḍayāmāsa lohadaṃḍairbhayānakaiḥ \|*  
*paṃgubhūtau punastyaktvā chāyāputrau divākaraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

29-42. Subsequently, with the union of both of them, Yama and Yamuna were bom as the son and daughter respectively. At that point of time, considering her husband to be the heap of lustre, Samjna kept her shadow in her place and herself proceeded for the performance of tapas. Thereafter, Vivasvan produced Savarni-Manu, Saturn and Tapati out of his terrific vision from the womb of Chaya - the shadow. But because of the difference in sons, Vivasvan taking her to be his own wife, getting enraged, reduced the Maya to ashes. Subsequently, both Saturn and Savarni finding Vivasvan enraged, fought between themselves. After some time, getting frightened from Vivasvan, both of them went to Himalaya and started performing tapas. After three years, the goddess Mahakali to whom the devotees are her favourites, bestowed boons on both of them. Both of them returned and started fighting with Vivasvan. But Vivasvan, getting frightened, fled from the battleground and travelled to the Kuru country, where his beloved was performing severe tapas taking to the form of a mare. Reaching there, lord Vivasvan spotted his wife Samjna. He was then filled with passion and taking to the form of a horse, he united with her. After enjoying conjugal pleasure with Vivasvan (in the form of a horse), she was conceived as a result of which she gave birth to two powerful and divine sons. Both the sons, finding their father in gloom, reached the solar disc and captured the wicked brothers, made them captive and produced them before their father. When the sons of the mare produced the enemies before Vivasvan, lord Vivasvan beat them with a strong iron rod so that both the sons of Chaya became lame.

## \|\| 2.153.43-48 \|\|

*āśvineyau samālokya vacanaṃ prāha tau mudā \|*

*somaśaktiriḍādevī jyeṣṭhapatnī bhaviṣyati \|*  
*piṃgalā sūryaśaktiśca laghupatnī bhaviṣyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

*iḍāpatissa vai nāma dvitīyaḥ piṃgalāpatiḥ \|*  
*dvādaśassa nṛṇāṃ rāśeḥ krūradṛṣṭiḥ śanaiścaraḥ \|*  
*tasya śāntikaro jyeṣṭho bhaviṣyati mahītale \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dvitīyaśca nṛṇāṃ rāśeḥ sāvarṇirbhramakārakaḥ \|*  
*tasya śāntikaro bhūmau bhavitā piṃgalāpatiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*janmarāśisthitā devī tapatī tā pakāriṇī \|*  
*iḍā ca piṃgalā tasyāḥ śāntikartryau bhaviṣyataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vacastasya suravaidyau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*sāvarṇiśca śanī rāhuḥ ketuḥ svargapratāpanaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu parihārārthau dasrau cāśvinisaṃbhavau \|\| 48 \|\|*

43-48. Thereafter, the Sungod, looking at the daughter of Vadava, delightfully spoke- “As the Jiva and Isa (supreme soul) are one like Nara and Narayana have one and the same colour and are inseparable friends, similarly, both of you would be known by the name of Nasatya and shall always remain delightful. Ida - the sakti of Soma and Pingala - the sakti of Surya would be the wives of elder as well as the younger one respectively. Thereafter, the first son would be known by the name of Idapati and the second son would be known by the name of Pingalapati. The cruel sight of the Saturn in the twelfth zodiac on earth shall be subsided by the elder son. Similarly, by reaching the second house, Savarni and Rahu besides Ketu would lead to travelling. Their effect could be subsided by the husband of Pingala. Similarly, by staying in the zodiac symbol of birth, the goddess Tapati would make the person to suffer. The related ill effects could be subsided by Durga and Pingala.” On hearing these words, the physicians Asvinikumaras and Savarni, Sani, Rahu and Ketu who create heat even in the heaven, felt affected. In order to subside the ill effects of this planet, Asvinikumaras were born.

## \|\| 2.153.49-56 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*

*sadhano nāma vikhyātaḥ pitṛmātṛparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śāligrāmaśilātulyaṃ chāgamāṃsaṃ vicikriye \|*

*sa tu satyanidhiḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇastapa āsthitaḥ \|*  
*bhayabhītāṃ ca gāṃ tatra cāṇḍālāya hyadarśayat \|*  
*rājagehe karastasmātsadhanasya layaṃ gataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*carmakāragṛhe jāto dvitīyaḥ piṃgalāpatiḥ \|*  
*mānadā sasya tanayo raidāsa iti viśrutaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgamya kabīraṃ rāmatatparam \|*  
*jitvā matavivādena śaṃkarācāryamāgataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tayorvivādo sabhavadahorātraṃ matāntare \|*

*rāmānandamupāgamya tasya śiṣyatvamāgataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*iti te kathitaṃ vipra surāṃśāśca yathābhavan \|*
