49-56. Suta said- Listening to the words of the preceptor, both the best of the gods were born on earth in the Sudra race. Out of them, Idapati, killing a goat, was born in the house of a Candala and came to be known by the name of Sadhana. He was immensely devoted to his parents and sold the goat’s meat like the stone of Saligrama. Thereafter, reaching the place of Kabira, he became his disciple. He was a tapasvl Brahmana named Satyanidhi in his earlier birth. Once he gave over a frightened cow to a butcher, as a result of which he received tax from the royal place. Thereafter, he was destroyed with his wealth. The second son Pingalapati was born as a son of Manadasa cobbler and came to be known as Raidasa. Tn the city of Kasi, he was defeated by Kabira in a discussion and became the disciple of Ramananda. О Brahmanas, thus I have narrated to you the life stories of the amsas of gods. The words of these pupil show the right path to the people in the age of Kali.

## Chapter 154. Birth of Visnusvami, Madhvacarya

## \|\| 2.154.1-7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavāñjīvo devamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*svamukhātsvāṃśamutpādya brahmayonau babhūva ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*iṣṭikā nagarī ramyā gurudattasya vai sutaḥ \|*  
*ropaṇo nāma vikhyāto brahmamārgapradarśakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sūtragranthamayīṃ mālāṃ tilakaṃ jalanirmitam \|*  
*vāsudeveti tanmantre kalau kṛtvā janejane \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya kambalaṃ ca tadājñayā \|*  
*gṛhītvā svapurīṃ prāpya kṛṣṇadhyānaparobhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ataḥ paraṃ śṛṇu mune caritraṃ ca harermudā \|*  
*yacchrutvā ca kalau ghore jano naiva bhayaṃ vrajet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pañcābde kṛṣṇacaitanye yajñāṃśe yajñakāriṇi \|*  
*vaṅgadeśabhavo vipra īśvaraḥ śāradāpriyaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prāptaḥ śāntipure grāme vāgdevīvaradarpitaḥ \|*  
*satāṃ digvijayaṃ kṛtvā sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta said- Thus narrating the glory of the gods, lord Brhaspati took out his lustre from his mouth and inspired it to be born in Brahmayoni, who was born in pleasant city of Istika in the house of Gurudatta as a son and was known by the name of Ropana. He was the follower of the Brahmamarga. Ropana popularized rosary of the cotton thread with knots, tilakam of water and Vasudeva mantra among the people. Thereafter, he reached Krsna Caitanya and accepting his command, he put on a blanket. Returning again to his city, he started meditating on Krsna. О sage, hereafter, I am narrating the story of lord. You please listen to the same, hearing which the change of Kali’s age gets removed. Just at the age of five years, Krsnacaitanya came to be known as the performer of the yajnas. Once a Brahmana named Kesava came to him, who belonged to the place in Kasmira and was devoted to the goddess Sarada. The learned Brahamana, who was well-versed in the scriptures, had became victorious in the religious debate and became arrogant with the boons received by him. He then travelled to Santipura.

## \|\| 2.154.8-13 \|\|

*gaṅgākūle stavaṃ divyaṃ racitvā 1 so'paṭhaddvijaḥ \|*  
*etasminnantare tatra yajñāṃśassamupāgataḥ \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ ramyamīśvaraṃ stutikāriṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sukṛtaṃ pūrtamarṇaṃ ca śrutīnāṃ sārameva hi \|*  
*ityuktaṃ bhavatā stotre dūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ vada \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tathāha ceśvaro dhīmāndūṣaṇaṃ naiva dṛśyate \|*  
*ityuktyā prāha bhagavānbhūṣaṇaṃ naiva dṛśyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sukṛtaṃ ca smṛtaṃ dharmaḥ pūrtaṃ caitanyamucyate \|*  
*arṇaṃ vīryamiti jñeyaṃ śrutisāramatastrayam \|*  
*gaṅgājale dūṣaṇo'yaṃ bhūṣaṇo'yaṃ kalevare \|\| 11 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa vai bhikṣurvismito'bhūcca gīḥ priyaḥ \|*  
*lajjitaṃ svajanaṃ dṛṣṭvā śāradā sarvamaṅgalā \|*  
*vihasyeśvaramityāha kṛṣṇaścaitanyasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu tacchiṣyaḥ kṛṣṇamantraupāsakaḥ \|*  
*babhūva vaiṣṇavaśreṣṭhaḥ kṛṣṇacaitanyasevakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

8-13. Reaching the bank of the river Ganga, the Brahmana was adoring and reciting the stotra which had been composed by him, himself. At the same time, Yajnamsdeva arrived there and spoke to the Brahmana named Kesava in sweet voice- “The essence of Srutis have been said to be Sukrta, Purta and Arna which appear like blemish in your stotra being recited by you. Who is the ornament in it, you kindly tell me?” On hearing these words, Kesava said-“There appears to be no fault in this stotra, because Sukrta stands for dharma, POrta stands for consciousness and Arna stands for the seed. Accordingly, all the three of them are said to be the tattvas of the Srutis. As whatever is the blemish found in the sacred Ganga water, it is known as the bhusana of the body.” On hearing these words, the Brahmana who loved Sarasvati, stared at him with surprise. At that point of time, the goddess Sarvamangala, finding her son feeling shy, spoke to Kesava smilingly- “The lord himself is the form of yajna.” On hearing these words, the Brahmana accepted him to be his disciple and started reciting the Krsna-mantra, who subsequently turned out to be the best Vaisnava devotee.

## \|\| 2.154.14-20 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śrīdharo nāma vikhyāto brāhmaṇaḥ śivapūjakaḥ \|*  
*pattane nagare ramye tasya saptāhamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*rājñā bhāgavataṃ tatra kāritaṃ sadhanaṃ bahu \|*  
*gṛhītvā śrīdharo vipro jagāma śvaśurālaye \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatroṣya māsamātraṃ ca svapatnyā saha vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*svagehamagamanmārge caurāḥ sapta tu taṃ prati \|*  
*śapathaṃ rāmadevasya kṛtvā sārddhamupāyayuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*samāpte vipine ramye hatvā te śrīdharaṃ dvijam \|*  
*gorathaṃ sadhanaṃ tatra sabhāryaṃ jagṛhustadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*etasminnantare rāmaḥ saccidānandavigrahaḥ \|*  
*sapta tāṃśca śarairhatvā punarujjīvya taṃ dvijam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*preṣayāmāsa bhagavāṃstadā vṛndāvane prabhuḥ \|*  
*tadā prabhṛti vai vipraḥ śrīdharo vaiṣṇavo'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

*saptābde caiva yajñāṃśe gatvā śāntipurīṃ śubhām \|*  
*brahmajñānamupāgamya yajñāṃśācchiṣyatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*ṭīkā bhāgavatasyaiva kṛtā tena mahātmanā \|\| 20 \|\|*

14-20. Suta said- There was a famous Brahmana known by the name of Sridhara, who always worshipped lord Siva. Once the lord of Pattana invited him respectfully and ananged for the recitation of Srimadbhagavata purana for a week. He got enough of the riches for so doing. Receiving the riches, Sridhara went to his father-in-law. After staying there for a month, he proceeded on to his home with his wife. At the time of the journey, seven thieves proved their nobility, taking an oath in the name of Sri Rama and accompanied them. At the end of the forest, the thieves killed the Brahmana and after so doing, they intended to decamp with the wealth, the bullock cart as well as his wife, but at the same time, lord Rama himself killed all the thieves with his arrows and brought Sridhara back to life and sent him home. Recalling the performance of Sri Rama, Sridhara atonce went to Vrndavana and started living as a Vaisnava and then went to the auspicious place of Santipura. At that point of time, the age of Yajnamsadeva was seven years only. Reaching there, he achieved Brahmajnana from Yajnamsadeva and accepted to be his disciple. While staying there, he composed the commentary on Srimad Bhagavat.

## \|\| 2.154.21-32 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*rāmaśarmā sthitaḥ kāśyāṃ śaṅkarārcanatatparaḥ \|*  
*śivarātre dvijo dhīmānavimukteśvarasthale \|*  
*ekākī jāgarandhyānī japtvā pañcākṣaraṃ śubham \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tadā prasanno bhagavāñchaṅkaro lokaśaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*varaṃ brūhīti vacanaṃ tamāha dvijasattamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*rāmaśarmā śivaṃ natvā vacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ \|*  
*bhavānyasya samādhistho dhyāne yasya paro bhavān \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sa devo hṛdaye mahyaṃ vasettava varātprabho \|*  
*ityuktavacane tasminvihasyāha maheśvaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ekā vai prakṛtirmāyā tridhā brahmasvarūpiṇī \|*  
*śūnyabhūtāvyavasyaiva puruṣasyārddhataijasam \|*  
*gṛhītvā lokajananī puṃklībau suṣuve sutau \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pumānnārāyaṇaḥ sākṣādgauraścāṣṭabhujairyutaḥ \|*  
*tridhā babhūva bhagavānsvecchayā viśvarakṣakaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ardhatejāssa vai viṣṇurvanamālī caturbhujaḥ \|*  
*kṣīraśāyī sa ādityaḥ svayaṃ sadguṇadevatā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ardhatejā dvidhā saiva naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī \|*  
*jiṣṇurviṣṇuḥ sa vai jñeyo parvate gandhamādane \|\| 28 \|\|*

*klībaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ sākṣādbrahmarūpaṃ tridhābhavat \|*  
*pūrvārddhādgauraśeṣaśca parārdhādrāmalakṣmaṇau \|\| 29 \|\|*

*gauraśeṣo dvāparānte balabhadraḥ sa vai svayam \|*  
*rāmalakṣmaṇayordhyānaṃ balabhadrasya pūjanam \|*  
*sadā mayā ca kartavyaṃ tatprāpya tvaṃ sukhī bhava \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ityuktvāntardadhe devo rāmānandasya cābhavat \|*  
*kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya dvādaśābdavayovṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śiṣyo bhūtvā sthitastatra kṛṣṇacaitanyapūjakaḥ \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tadājñayā tenādhyātmarāmāyaṇaṃ śubham \|\| 32 \|\|*

21-32. Suta said- On the day of Sivaratri in the city of Kasi, Ramasarma was worshipping lord Siva. At that point of time, he alone was reciting the five letter mantra of Siva in the Vimuktesvara region of lord Siva. Finding him so meditating, lord Siva, who always works for the benefit of the people, feeling pleased, desired the excellent Brahmana to seek for a boon. At that point of time, Ramasarma spoke to Siva in a humble voice- “The one for whom you mediate upon and always remain devoted to him, let him dwell in my heart. This is the boon I desire from you.” At these words spoken by the Brahmana, Mahesvara said with a smile-“The Prakrti Maya who is also the form of Brahman, besides being the creator of the universe, accepts half the lustre of the indestructible Purusa and gets it divided into three parts. Then two sons, a man and a eunuch were born of the same. The Purusa or man is lord Narayana himself. He is of fair complexion and has eight hands. The lord who guards the universe, of his own desire, got himself divided into three parts. From half of his lustre, there appeared lord Visnu also known as a Vanamali, who is four-armed. He appears as Ksirasayi and Aditya. From the remaining half, he incarnated on earth in the form of Narayana. He lives over the Gandhamadana mountain as Jisnu or Visnu. Lord Sankarsana himself got divided into three parts. From the first part, he had fair complexion and from the lower half, he appears as Rama and Laksmana. The same fair complexion appeared by about the end of dvapara as Balabhadra Balarama. Therefore, I always worship Rama, Laksmana and Balabhadra. By getting them, you would be feeling exceedingly comfortable.” Thus speaking, lord Siva disappeared from the scene. The Deva then, having been bom in the house of Ramananda and reaching the age of twelve years, went to the abode of Krsnacaitanya and became his priest. Subsequently, at the command of Krsnacaitanya, he composed the epic of Adhyatma Ramsyana.

## \|\| 2.154.33-39 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*jīvānandassa vai vipro rūpānandasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*śrutvā caitanyacaritaṃ purīṃ śāntimayīṃ gataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*caitanye ṣoḍaśābde ca natvā taṃ tau samāsthitau \|*  
*ūcatuḥ kṛṣṇacaitanyaṃ bhavatā kiṃ mataṃ smṛtam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vihasyāha sa caitanyaḥ śākto'haṃ śaktipūjakaḥ \|*  
*śaivo'haṃ vai dvijau 1 nityaṃ lokārthe śaṅkaravratī \|*  
*vaiṣṇavo'haṃ dhyānaparo devadevasya bhaktimān \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ahaṃ bhaktimadaṃ pītvā pāpapuṃso baliṃ śubham \|*  
*śaktyai samarpya homānte jñānāgnau yajñatatparaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā dvijau tau tu tasya śiṣyatvamāgatau \|*  
*ācāramārgamāgamya sarvapūjyau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tadājñayā ṣaṭsandarbhaṃ jīvānandaścakāra vai \|*  
*uvāsa tatra matimānkṛṣṇacaitanyasevakaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*rūpānando gurorājñāṃ puraskṛtya mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇakhaṇḍaṃ purāṇāṅgaṃ cakre daśasahasrakam \|*  
*tatroṣya gurusevāḍhyo rādhākṛṣṇa prapūjakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

33-39. Suta said- Thus listening to the life story of Yajnamsadeva, a Brahmapa named Rupananda went on pilgrimage to Santipura with Ramanuja. Reaching there, both of them offering their salutation to Yajnamsadeva, took their seats before him. Then they questioned Krsnacaitanya- “Which one is the faith followed by you?” At that point of time, lord Yajnesa was sixteen years of age. He smiled and said- “O Brahmanadeva, patronizing the peaceful means, I believe in Sakti-manta. I worship Sakti. For the welfare of the people, I also perform the vratas of lord Siva following Saivism. Besides being devoted to lord Visnu, I am a Vaisnava as well, I consume the arrogance of devotion, make the offerings of the sinful persons in favour of the goddess Sakti. Then performing homa in the flames of fire, I complete the уajna." On hearing these words, both of them agreed to be his disciples and became adorable by all. While living there, the intelligent Ramanuja composed Acara-Bhasya and kept on adoring Krsnacaitanya alone. Rupananda also, honouring the command of the preceptor, composed the Krsnakhanda of Dasasahasra-nama, which is an appendix to a purana. Thereafter, worshipping Radha-Krsna, he always served the preceptor, while spending his life.

## \|\| 2.154.40-47 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*viṣṇusvāmī sa vai vipro gataḥ śāntipurīṃ śubhām \|*  
*yajñāṃśa ūnaviṃśābde natvā taṃ prāha sa dvijaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ko devaḥ sarvadevānāṃ pūjyo brahmāṇḍagocare \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa bhagavānuvāca dvijasattamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sarvapūjyo mahādevo bhaktānugrahakārakaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇvīśvaraśca rudreśo brahmeśo bhagavānharaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vinā tatpūjakenaiva padārthā niṣphalā hi te \|*  
*ye tu vai viṣṇubhaktāśca śaṅkarārcanatatparāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śivaprasādātsulabhā vaiṣṇavī bhaktiruttamā \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaḥ puruṣo bhūtvā śaṅkaraṃ lokaśaṅkaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

*karmabhūmyāṃ samāgamya na pūjayati nārakaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇusvāmīti tacchrutvā śiṣyo bhūtvā ca tadguṇaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇamantramupāsitvā 1 sa babhūva śivārcakaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vaiṣṇavī saṃhitā tena nirmitā ca tadājñayā \|*  
*tatroṣya viṣṇubhaktaśca kṛṣṇacaitanyapūjakaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

40-47. Suta said- The excellent Brahmana Visnusvami, while reaching Santipuri, offered his salutation to Yajnamsadeva and said to him- “Who is the god adorable by all the gods in the world?" At that point of time, Yajnamsadeva had reached the age of nineteen years. Listening his words, lord Yajnamsadeva replied- “Lord Mahadeva, who is worshipped by all (is the lord of all), he alone showers his grace over his devotees. Lord Siva alone is the Isvara of all the gods including Visnu, Rudra and Brahma. All the activities become fruitful with the adoration of lord Siva. Such of the devotees of Visnu who worship Siva always, they because of the grace of lord Siva, achieve the excellent devotion of lord Visnu. A person, who having been bom in this karmabhumi and inspite of his being a Vaisnava, do not worship lord Siva, then he belong to hell.” On hearing these words, Visnuavami was impressed by his virtues and became his disciple. While living there, though he was the devotee of Visnu, he worshipped Siva by reciting Krsna-mantra during his life time. Accepting the command of Krsnacaitanya, he composed a treatise known as Vaisnavi Samhita.

## \|\| 2.154.48-61 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*madhvācāryaḥ kṛṣṇaparo jñātvā yajñāṃśamuttamam \|*  
*gatvā śāntipurīṃ ramyāṃ natvā taṃ prāha sa dvijaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇo'yaṃ bhagavānsākṣāttadanye viśvakārakāḥ \|*  
*devā dhātrādayo jñeyāstarhi tatpūjanena kim \|\| 49 \|\|*

*śaktimārgaparā viprā vṛthā hiṃsāmayairmakhaiḥ \|*  
*aśvamedhādibhirdevānpūjayanti mahītale \|\| 50 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vihasyāha yajñāṃśaśca śacīsutaḥ \|*  
*na kṛṣṇo bhagavānsākṣāttāmaso'yaṃ ca śaktijaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*cauro'yaṃ sarvabhogī ca hiṃsako māṃsabhakṣakaḥ \|*  
*parastriyaṃ bhajedyo vai sa gacchedyamamandiram \|\| 52 \|\|*

*cauro yamālayaṃ gacchejjīvahantā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ebhiśca lakṣaṇairhīno bhagavānprakṛteḥ paraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*yasya buddhiḥ sa vai brahmā'haṅkāro yasya vai śivaḥ \|*  
*śabdamātrā gaṇeśaśca sparśamātrā yamaḥ svayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*rūpamātrā kumāro vai rasamātrā ca yakṣarāṭ \|*  
*gandhamātrā viśvakarmā śravaṇaṃ bhagavāñchaniḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yasya tvaksa budho jñeyaścakṣussūryaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*yajjitvā bhagavāñchukro ghrāṇastasyāśvinīsutau \|\| 56 \|\|*

*yanmukhaṃ bhagavāñjīvo yasya hastastu devarāṭ \|*  
*kṛṣṇo'yaṃ tasya caraṇau liṅgaṃ dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*gudaṃ tadbhagavānmṛtyustasmai bhagavate namaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*hiṃsāyajñaiśca bhagavānsa ca tṛptimavāpnuyāt \|*  
*sa ca yajñapaśurvahnau brahmabhūyāya kalpate \|*  
*tasya mokṣaprabhāvena mahatpuṇyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vidhihīno naraḥ pāpī hiṃsāyajñaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*andhatāmisranarakaṃ taddoṣeṇa vasecciram \|\| 59 \|\|*

*mahatpuṇyaṃ mahatpāpaṃ hiṃsāyajñeṣu vartate \|*  
*atastu bhagavānkṛṣṇo hiṃsāyajñaṃ kalau yuge \|\| 60 \|\|*

*samāpya kārtike māsi pratipacchuklapakṣake \|*  
*annakūṭamayaṃ yajñaṃ sthāpayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 61 \|\|*

48-61. Suta said - Madhvacarya - the devotee of lord Krsna, learning about the incarnation of Yajnamsa, went on pilgrimage to Santipuri. Reaching there and offering his salutation to Yajnamsa, he said to him- “Lord Куда is adorable by all, being the lord of all. All other gods including Brahma are the creators of the world. Therefore, there is no use adoring them. By patronizing the Saktimarga, when a Brahmana committing violence, performs Asvamedha or other yajnas and adore other gods, his such performance is of no use.” On hearing these words, Yajnamsadeva - the son of Indrani, spoke smilingly- “Krsna is not the lord incarnate, but because of his birth from the Tamasasakti, is Tamasa (or malignant). Besides, a thief, omnivorous, a killer, consumer of meat, one who enjoys the wives of others and a killer of all the jivas, has to go to the place of Yama. The lord is beyond these symptoms as well as prakrti. His wisdom is arrogant Siva, Ganesa is Sabda-matra for him, Sparsa-matra (touch) is Yama, Rupa-matra (beauty) is Kumara, Rasa-matra is Kubera, Gandha-matra is Visvakarma, Sravana (hearing) is Saturn, Tvak or skin is Mercury, the eyes are the eternal Sun, tongue is Venus and selling is Asvini, salutation to such a lord. Such a lord gets pleased only with the performing of the valiant yajnas and the animal which enters in the flames, achieves the supreme position. So when it achieves moksa, the performer achieves great merit. A sinful person, who does not perform the Himsa-yajna in an appropriate manner, his that fault drives him to Andha-tamisra hell, where he has to stay for a long time. Therefore, with the performing of the Himsa-yajna, one achieves great merit as well the grave sin. Therefore, during the age of Kali, lord Krsna apprised the performing of Himsa-yajna and established the performing of the Annakuta yajna on the bright first day of the month of Kartika.

## \|\| 2.154.62-66 \|\|

*devarājastadā kruddho hyanujaṃ prati duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*vajraṃ saplāvayāmāsa tadā kṛṣṇaḥ sanātanīm \|*  
*prakṛtiṃ sa ca tuṣṭāva lokamaṅgalahetave \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tadā sā prakṛtirmātā svapūrvāddivyavigraham \|*  
*rādhārūpaṃ mahatkṛtvā hadi kṛṣṇasya cāgatā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tacchaktyā bhagavānkṛṣṇo dhṛtvā govardhanaṃ girim \|*  
*nāmnā giridharo devaḥ sarvapūjyo babhūva ha \|\| 64 \|\|*

*rādhākṛṣṇassa bhagavānpūrṇabrahma sanātanaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ kṛṣṇo na bhagavānrādhākṛṣṇaḥ paraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vacastasya madhvācāryo haripriyaḥ \|*  
*śiṣyo bhūtvā sthitastatra kṛṣṇacaitanyapūjakaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

62-66. At that point of time, getting enraged and feeling pity for his younger brother, lord Indra tried to drown the whole of Vraja. But lord Krsna at the same time, for the welfare of the world, worshipped the eternal goddess. Getting pleased, the mother Prakrti took to the form of Radha and dwelt in the heart of Krsna. With the strength of the same, Krsna lifted up the mount Govardhana earning him the title of Giridhara. He then became adorable by all. The sound Radha-Krsna happens to be the complete Brahman. Because of this, it is not the Krsna alone, but both Radha and Krsna are taken to be the divine beings. Both of them are the lord of all, besides being the Supreme. On hearing these words, Madhavacarya accepted Krsnacaitanya as his preceptor and adored him always.

## Chapter 155. Glory of Jagannatha

## \|\| 2.155.1-10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*bhaṭṭojissa ca śuddhātmā śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya namaskṛtya vaco'bravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mahādevo guruḥ sa vai śiva ātmā śarīriṇām \|*  
*viṣṇurbrahmā ca taddāsau tarhi tatpūjanena kim \|\| 2 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa yajñāṃśo viṃśadabdavayovṛtaḥ \|*  
*vihasyāha sa bhaṭṭojiṃ nāyaṃ śambhurmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*samartho bhagavāñchambhuḥ kartā kinna śarīriṇām \|*  
*na bhartā ca vinā viṣṇuṃ saṃhartāyaṃ sadā śivaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ekamūrtistridhā jātā brahmā viṣṇurmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*śāktamārgeṇa bhagavānbrahmā mokṣapradāyakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*viṣṇurvaiṣṇavamārgeṇa jīvānāṃ mokṣadāyakaḥ \|*  
*śambhurvai śaivamārgeṇa mokṣadātā śarīriṇām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śāktaḥ sadāśramo gehī yajñabhukpitṛdevagaḥ \|*  
*vānaprasthāśramī yo vai vaiṣṇavaḥ kandamūlabhuk \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yatyāśramaḥ sadā raudrau nirguṇaḥ śuddhavigrahaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryāśramasteṣāmanugāmī mahāśramaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ śiṣyo bhūtvā sa vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyāṅgaṃ ca vedānāṃ vyācakhyau pāṇinikṛtam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tadājñayā ca siddhāntakaumudyāssa cakāra ha \|*  
*tatroṣya dīkṣito dhīmānkṛṣṇacaitanyasevakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

1-10. Suta said- Once the auspicious soul Bhattoji, a devotee of Siva, went to Krsnacaitanya, offered his salutation to the great saint and said to him- “Mahadeva happens to be the preceptor of all the living beings. Siva himself is the soul of all and the gods like Brahma and Visnu happen to be his slaves. Therefore, what would be the use of worshipping the other two (except Siva)? At that point of time, Yajnamsadeva was of the age of twenty years. He smiled and said to Bhattoji- “Sambhu is not Mahesvara without Visnu. Sadasiva would not be able to function as a karta (creator), bharta (feeder) and even samharta (destroyer). One and the same image is divided into three parts. Because of that, Brahma, Visnu and Siva appeared in the universe. With the following of the Sakta-marga, Brahma bestows moksa to the living being making use of Vaisnava and Saiva paths. With the following of the Vaisnava-marga, Visnu bestows moksa to the living being. Similarly, with the following of the Saiva-marga, Siva bestows moksa to the living being. Sakta is the form of a householder, in which the gods and the pitrs enjoy the share of yajna. Similarly, Vaisnava path has been termed as the Vanaprastha-asrama, in which by consuming the wild roots and fruits, one has to spend his life. The Sannyasa-asrama has always the Raudra form, besides being absolute and auspicious. In this way, Mahesvara represents the Brahmacarya-asrama, which is quite difficult one.” On hearing these words of the lord, he accepted to be his disciple. Thereafter, obeying his command, he wrote a commentary over the grammar of Panini, which is considered to be the third anga of the Vedas, and which came to be known as Siddhanta-Kaumadi. While living there, Bhattojidiksita met with the end of his life.

## \|\| 2.155.11-21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*varāhamihiro dhīmānsa ca sūryaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*dvāviṃśābde ca yajñāṃśe tamāgatya vaco'bravīt \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sūryo'yaṃ bhagavātsākṣāttrayo devā yato'bhavan \|*  
*prātarbrahmā ca madhyāhne viṣṇuḥ sāyaṃ sadāśivaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ato raveḥ śubhā pūjā tridevayajanena kim \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa yajñāṃśo vihasyāha śubhaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*dvidhā babhūva prakṛtiraparā ca parā tathā \|*  
*nāmamātrā tathā puṣpamātrā tanmātrikā tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śabdamātrā sparśamātrā rūpamātrā rasā tathā \|*  
*gaṃdhamātrā tathā jñeyā parā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*aparāyāṃ jīvabhūtā nityaśuddhā jaganmayī \|*  
*bhūmirāpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ manobuddhireva ca \|*  
*ahaṅkāra iti jñeyā prakṛtiścāparāṣṭadhā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*viṣṇurbrahmā mahādevo gaṇeśo yamarāḍ guhaḥ \|*  
*kubero viśvakarmā ca parā prakṛtidevatā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sumerurvaruṇo vahnirvāyuścaiva dhruvastathā \|*  
*somo ravistathā śeṣo'parā prakṛtidevatā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ataḥ somapatī rudro raviḥ svāmī vidhiḥ svayam \|*  
*śeṣasvāmī hariḥ sākṣānnamastebhyo namo namaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tadā vipraḥ śiṣyo bhūtvā ca tadguroḥ \|*  
*tadājñayā caturthāṅgaṃ jyotiḥśāstraṃ cakāra ha \|\| 20 \|\|*

*varāhasaṃhitā nāma bṛhajjātakameva hi \|*  
*kṣudratantrāṃstathānyānvai kṛtvā tatra sa cāvasat \|\| 21 \|\|*

11-21. Suta said- Varahamihira, who was immensely intelligent besides being the worshipper of the Sungod, tried to reach Yajnamsa. At that point of time, Yajnamsa had reached the age of twenty two years. Reaching there, he said to Yajnamsa- “Surya is the apparent lord, because the three other prominent god have emerged out of him. The Sun represents Brahma in the morning, Visnu in the noon and Siva in the evening. Therefore, it is the Sungod alone who should be worshipped and it is of no use to worship the other three gods.” On hearing this argument, Yajnamsa spoke in a sweet voice to him- “The goddess Prakrti appeared in two forms of Para and Apara and created this globe. The Para-gakti is divided into eight forms viz., Namamatra, Puspamatra, Tanmatra, Sabdamatra, Sparsamatra, Rupamatra, Rasamatra and Gandhamatra. Similarly, the Apara-sakti which is always auspicious, besides being universal, stands divided into eight parts of the earth, water, fire, wind, sky, mind, wisdom and arrogance. Visnu, Brahma, Mahadeva, Ganesa, Yamaraja, Guha, Kubera and Visvakarma are the gods related to Para-Prakrti. The gods of the Apara-Prakrti include Sumeru, Varuna, Vahni, Vayu, Dhruva, Soma, Ravi and Sesa. Therefore, Somapati Rudra is Brahma and Sesa besides Hari, salutation to them again and again.” Listening to the words so spoken by him, Mihiracarya accepted to be his disciple. Thereafter, he composed the treatise on astrology which is known by the title of Brhajjataka or Varaha Samhita. While living there, he also composed the other Tantra-literature.

## \|\| 2.155.22-29 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vāṇībhūṣaṇa evāpi śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya vacaḥ prāha vinamradhīḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*viṣṇumāyā jagaddhātrī saikā prakṛtirutkṛtā \|*  
*tayā jātamidaṃ viśvaṃ viśvāddevasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*viśvedevassa puruṣaśśaktijo bahudhābhavat \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇurharaścaiva devāḥ prakṛtisambhavāḥ \|*  
*ato bhagavatī pūjyā tarhi tatpūjanena kim \|\| 24 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā sa yajñāṃśo vihasyāha dvijottamam \|*  
*na vai bhagavatī śreṣṭhā jaḍarūpā guṇātmikā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ekā sā prakṛtirmāyā raciturjagatāṃ kṣamā \|*  
*puruṣasya sahāyena yoṣiteva narasya ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

*devībhāgavate śāstre prasiddheyaṃ kathā dvija \|*  
*kadācitprakṛtirdevī svecchayedaṃ jagatkhalu \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nirmitaṃ jaḍabhūtaṃ tadbahudhā bodhitaṃ tadā \|*  
*na caitanyamabhūdviprā vismitā prakṛtistadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śūnyabhūtaṃ ca puruṣaṃ caitanyaṃ samatoṣayat \|*  
*praviṣṭo bhagavāndevīmāyājanitagolake \|\| 29 \|\|*

22-29. Suta said- Vanibhusana - the devotee of Siva, also reached before Krsnacaitanya and spoke to him quite humbly- “It is the illusion of Visnu which maintains the universe. Therefore, the Prakrti, which is the best of all, the same is responsible for the creation of the universe. The universe had been created with the Devas of the world as well as the Visvedevas. Therefore, the same Bhagavati should be adored and not any other deity.” Hearing these words, Yajnamsa smiled and said to the excellent Brahmana - “The goddess being the form of ignorance as well as virtues, cannot be claimed to be the excellent one. The story in the Devibhagavat is quite popular according to which, the goddess Prakrti once created the universe according to her own sweet will. But О Brahmana, inspite of her best efforts, the universe could not attain consciousness, observing which the Prakrti was extremely surprised. At the same time, she worshipped the Sunyabhuta Purusa in his conscious form, who getting pleased entered the globe so created by the goddess.

## \|\| 2.155.30-35 \|\|

*svapnavadvā svayaṃ jātaścaitanyamabhavajjagat \|*  
*ataḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sa bhagavānpuruṣo nirguṇaḥ paraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*prakṛtyāṃ svecchayā jāto liṅgarūpastadā'bhavat \|*  
*puṃlliṅgaprakṛtau jātaḥ puṃlliṅgo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*strīlliṅgaprakṛtau jātaḥ strīlliṅgo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*napuṃskaprakṛtau jātaḥ klībarūpaḥ sa vai prabhuḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*avyayaprakṛtau jātau nirguṇo'yamadhokṣajaḥ \|*  
*namastasmai bhagavate śūnyarūpāya sākṣiṇe \|\| 33 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu tadvākyaṃ śiṣyo bhūtvā sa vai dvijaḥ \|*  
*triviṃśābde ca yajñāṃśe tatra vāsamakārayat \|\| 34 \|\|*

*chandogranthaṃ tu vedāṅgaṃ svanāmnā tena nirmitam \|*  
*rādhākṛṣṇaparaṃ nāma japtvā harṣamavāptavān \|\| 35 \|\|*

30-35. The entire universe became conscious as if waking up from sleep. Therefore, the same lord is the best, who is Purusa, absolute and supreme. He became the form of linga, because of his emerging out of Prakrti. And because of his birth from the masculine Prakrti, he became eternally masculine. By the birth from feminine Prakrti, he appeared in feminine gender and by his birth in neutral gender, he was known as neutral. Having his birth from indestructible Prakrti, he is known as the one who has controlled the sense organs. Therefore, salutation to the lord, who is the form of Sunya, besides being the witness.” On hearing these words, the Brahmana accepted Krsnacaitanya as his preceptor and started living in his asrama. At that point of time, Yajnamsa had reached the age of twenty three years. While staying there, Vanibhusana composed a treatise on the Vedic meters in his own name. Accordingly, reciting excellent names of Radha and Krsna, he spent his life with delight.

## \|\| 2.155.36-41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dhanvantarirdvijo nāma brahmabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya natvā vacanamabravīt \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bhavāṃstu puruṣaḥ śreṣṭho nityaśuddhassanātanaḥ \|*  
*jaḍabhūtā ca tanmāyā samartho bhagavānsvayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nityo'vyaktaḥ paraḥ sūkṣmastasmātprakṛtirudbhavaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ pūjyassa bhagavānprakṛtyāḥ pūjanena kim \|\| 38 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vihasyāha yajñāṃśassarvaśāstragaḥ \|*  
*nāyaṃ śreṣṭhassa puruṣo na kṣamaḥ prakṛtiṃ vinā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*purāṇe caiva vārāhe prasiddheyaṃ kathā śubhā \|*  
*kadācitpuruṣo nityo nāmamātraḥ svakecchayā \|*  
*babhūva bahudhā tatra yathā pretastathā svayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*asamartho viracituṃ jaganti puruṣaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva prakṛtiṃ devīṃ cirakālaṃ sanātanīm \|\| 41 \|\|*

36-41. Suta said- Dhanvantri, who always kept himself absorbed in the devotion of Brahman, once arrived to Krsnacaitanaya. He offered his salutation to him and said- “You are best of the people, always auspicious besides being eternal. Your maya is form of jada. Because of his being eternal, everlasting, supreme and subtle, the lord is the best and Prakrti emerges out of him only. Therefore, the lord, who is the best of all, should be adored and not of Prakrti.” On hearing these words, Yajnamsadeva. who was well-versed in all the scriptures, smiled and said- “Purusa only cannot be claimed to be the best, because he remains inactive in the absence of Prakrti. There is a story in the Varaha Purana, which is quite well known. According to that story, the eternal Purusa once, who is for his name sake only, of his own sweet will, took to many forms like a goblin, but the Nitya Purusa was unable to create anything. Thereafter, he worshipped the eternal goddess Prakrti for long.

## \|\| 2.155.42-45 \|\|

*tadā devī ca taṃ prāpya mahattatvaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*so'haṅkāraśca mahato jātastanmātrikāstataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mahābhūtānyato'pyāsaṃstaiḥ sañjātamidaṃ jagat \|\| 43 \|\|*

*atassanātanau cobhau puruṣātprakṛtiḥ parā \|*  
*prakṛteḥ puruṣaścaiva tasmāttābhyāṃ namo namaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*iti dhanvantariḥ śrutvā śiṣyo bhūtvā ca tadguroḥ \|*  
*tatroṣya caiva vedāṅgaṃ kalpavedaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*suśrutādapare cāpi śiṣyā dhanvantareḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

42-45. Getting pleased, the goddess went to him and created Mahattatva. From Mahattatva, arrogance was created and from arrogance was created Tanmatra (or the subtle form of matter). From Tanmatra was created the five elements. From those five elements including the sky, the universe was created. Therefore, out of the eternal Purusa and Prakrti, the latter is better, while Purusa is better than Prakrti. Therefore, salutation to both of them.” On hearing these words, Dhanvantari accepted to be his disciple and started living there in the same asrama. While living there, he composed the Kcdpaveda which is a part of the Vedic literature. Dhanvantari had two other disciples besides Susruta.

## \|\| 2.155.46-52 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*jayadevassa vai vipro bauddhamārgaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya pañcaviṃśavayovṛtam \|*  
*natvovāca vaco ramyaṃ sa ca śreṣṭha uṣāpatiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yasya nābherabhūtpadmaṃ brahmaṇā saha nirgatam \|*  
*atassa brahmasūrnāma sāmavedeṣu gīyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

*viśvo nārāyaṇassākṣādyasya ketau samāsthitaḥ \|*  
*viśva keturato nāma na niruddho'niruddhakaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*brahmavelā ca tatpatnī nityā coṣā mahottamā \|*  
*sa vai lokahitārthāya svayamarcāvatārakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā vihasyāha yajñāṃśastaṃ dvijottamam \|*  
*vedo nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣātpūjanīyo naraḥ sadā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tataḥ kālastataḥ karma tato dharmaḥ pravartate \|*  
*dharmātmakāmaḥ samudbhūtaḥ kāmapatnī ratiḥ svayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ratyāṃ kāmātsamudbhūto'niruddho nāmadevatā \|*  
*uṣā sā tasya bhaginī tena sārddhaṃ samudbhavā \|\| 52 \|\|*

46-52. Suta said- Jayadeva, the follower of the Buddhist faith, once went to Krsnacaitanya when he was twenty five years old. Offering his salutation to him, he spoke with a beautiful voice to him- “The lord of Usa is the best of the gods, because Brahma with lotus emerged out of his navel, and therefore, Samaveda describes him as the self-born one. Lord Narayana is lodged over his flag. Therefore, he is called a Niruddha and not Aniruddha. His spouse is known to be his wife. Therefore, the same lord of Usa incarnates on earth for the welfare of the people.” On hearing these words, Yajnamsadeva smiled and said to the excellent Brahmana “Veda alone is the personified form of Narayana and a person should always worship the same. It is because from the Vedas emerges the Kala (time), from Kala emerges the activity, from activity emerges Dharma, from Dharma emerges Kama (desire) and from Kama or desire emerges the conjugal love of the wife. With die combination of the Kama and Rati (conjugal pleasure), the god known as Aniruddha was bom. His sister Usa was also bom with him as a twin.

## \|\| 2.155.53-65 \|\|

*kālo nāma sa vai kṛṣṇo rādhā tasya sahodarā \|*  
*karmarūpaḥ sa vai brahmā niyatistatsahodarā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*dharmarūpo mahādevaḥ śraddhā tasya sahodarā \|*  
*aniruddhaḥ kathaṃ ceśo bhavatoktaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tridhā sṛṣṭiśca brahmāṇḍe sthūlā sūkṣmā ca kāraṇā \|*  
*sthūlasṛṣṭyai samudbhūto devo nārāyaṇaḥ svayam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇī ca tacchaktistayorjalasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*jalājjātassa vai śeṣastasyopari samāsthitau \|\| 56 \|\|*

*supte nārāyaṇe deve nābheḥ paṅkajamuttamam \|*  
*anantayojanāyāmamudabhūcca tato vidhiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*vidheḥ sthūlamayī sṛṣṭirdevatiryyaṅnarādikā \|*  
*sūkṣmasṛṣṭyai samudbhūtaḥ so'niruddha uṣāpatiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tato vīryamayaṃ toyaṃ jātaṃ brahmāṇḍamastake \|*  
*vīryājjātassa vai śeṣastasyopari sa cāsthitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tasya nābhessamudbhūto brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmasṛṣṭistato jātā yathā svapne'pi dṛśyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

*hetusṛṣṭyai samudbhūto vedā nārāyaṇaḥ svayam \|*  
*vedātkālastataḥ karma tato dharmādayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tvadguruśca jagannātha uḍradeśanivāsakaḥ \|*  
*mayā tatraiva gantavyaṃ saśiṣyeṇādya bho dvijāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ kṛṣṇacaitanyakiṅkarāḥ \|*  
*svānsvāñchiṣyānsamāhūya tatpaścātprayayuśca te \|\| 63 \|\|*

*śāṅkarā dvādaśagaṇā rāmānujamupāyayuḥ \|*  
*nāmadevādayastatra gaṇāssapta samāgatāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*rāmānandaṃ namaskṛtya saṃsthitāstasya sevakā \|*  
*ropaṇaśca tadāgatya svaśiṣyairbahubhirvṛtaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

53-65. Krsna is also known by the name of Kala and Radha is his sister. Brahma is the form of karma or activity. Similarly, Mahadeva is the form of dharma and sraddha or devotion is his sister. Therefore, how could Aniruddha be the eternal Isa? In the entire globe, creation had been of three types in which the gross element was created by lord Narayana himself. Narayani happens to be his 3akti. The water had been created out of both of them. Besides Sesa also emerged out of the water, or by which both Narayana and his Sakti look graceful. When lord Narayana went to sleep, then a lotus emerged out of his navel which was a number of yojanas vast. Brahma was then bom out of the same lotus. The same Brahma was responsible for the creation of gods, animals, birds, humans and others, besides the gross creations. For the creation of the subtle world, Aniruddha - the husband of Usa was born. Subsequently, from his forehead, the semen like water emerged and 6esa was bom out of the same, over which the earth is lodged out of the navel of Brahma. The grandsire Brahma emerged, by whom the subtle universe was created like a dream. Similarly, for the Karana Srsti or the creation with cause, Veda Narayana himself appeared. Subsequently, Kala was created by the Veda, Kala created activity and activity created Dharma, О Brahmana, your preceptor Jagannatha belongs to the Udra country. Along With my own disciples, I am proceeding to the same place.” On hearing these words, his followers called for their respective disciples and all of them departed for the sacred city of Jagannatha Puri. Ramanuja with his twelve followers of same faith, Namadeva with his seven followers, besides Ramananda who offered his salutation from a distance, accompanied him. Accompanied with many of their disciples, they reached the place of Krsnacaitanya at Ropana. They offered their salutation to him, after which they engaged themselves to serve him variously.

## \|\| 2.155.66-78 \|\|

*kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya namaskṛtya sthitaḥ svayam \|*  
*jagannāthapurīṃ te vai prayayurbhaktitatparāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*nidhayaḥ siddhayastatra teṣāṃ sevārthamāgatāḥ \|*  
*sarve ca daśasāhasrā vaiṣṇavāḥ śaivaśāktakaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*yajñāṃśaṃ ca puraskṛtya jagannāthapurīṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*arcāvatāro bhagavānaniruddha uṣāpatiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tadāgamanamālokya dvijarūpadharo muniḥ \|*  
*jagannāthaḥ svayaṃ prāpto yatra yajñāṃśakādayaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*yajñāṃśastaṃ samālokya natvā vacanamabravīt \|*  
*kiṃ mataṃ bhavatā jñātaṃ kalau prāpte bhayānake \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā brūhi śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ \|*  
*iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ jagannātho hariḥ svayam \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ ramyaṃ lokamaṅgalahetave \|\| 71 \|\|*

*miśradeśodbhavā mlecchāḥ kāśyapenaiva śāsitāḥ \|*  
*saṃskṛtā śūdravarṇena brahmavarṇamupāgatāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*śikhāsūtraṃ samādhāya paṭhitvā vedamuttamam \|*  
*yajñaiśca pūjayāmāsurdevadevaṃ śacīpatim \|\| 73 \|\|*

*duḥkhito bhagavānindraḥ śvetadvīpamupāgataḥ \|*  
*stutyā māṃ bodhayāmāsa devamaṅgalahetave \|\| 74 \|\|*

*prabuddhaṃ māṃ vacaḥ prāha śṛṇu deva dayānidhe \|*  
*śūdrasaṃskṛtamannaṃ ca khādituṃ na dvijo'rhati \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tathā ca śūdrajanitairyajñaistṛptiṃ na cāpnuyām \|*  
*kāśyape svargate prāpte māgadhe rājñi śāsati \|\| 76 \|\|*

*mama śatrurbalirdaityaḥ kalipakṣamupāgataḥ \|*  
*nistejāśca yathā'haṃ syāṃ tathā vai kartumudyataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*miśradeśodbhave mlecche sāṃskṛtī tena saṃskṛtā \|*  
*bhāṣā devavināśāya daityānāṃ varddhanāya ca \|\| 78 \|\|*

66-78. All of them reached the place of Jagannatha Puri. They were being served by the goddesses named Rddhi and Siddhi. In the crowd of those devotees, besides the Saiva and Saktis, ten thousand Vaisnavas were also present there. All of them making Yajnamsadeva to lead them, with great respect, were proceeding towards the city of Jagannatha. On their arrival there, lord Aniruddha - the spouse of Usa, learning about the arrival of lord Yajnamsa.. took to the form of a Brahmana and himself reached the place where Yajnamsa had been staying. On spotting lord Jagannatha, offering his salutation to him, Yajnamsadeva said to him- “During the horrible time of Kali, which one of the theory has been propounded by you? You tell me specifically. I would like to know about it together with the related tattva.” On hearing these words, lord Jagannatha, who himself is the form of Visnu, for the welfare of the Iokas, started speaking with the charming speech-“The dweller of Misra country, who are Mlecchas people and who are governed by Kasyapa, whose samskaras are of Sudra type, disguising as the Brahmanas, patronizing the tuft as well as the sacred thread, carrying on studies of the Vedas, adored Indra. Feeling painful, he left for svetadvipa. Reaching there, for the welfare of the gods, he adored me with prayers. On my becoming conscious, he said-“O ocean of compassion, you kindly listen to my tale of sufferings. How can a Brahmana take the food prepared by a Sudra? Similarly, how could feel content with yajnas performed by the Sudras. After proceeding of Kasyapa to heaven, during the rule of the king of Magadha, Bali daitya, who is my enemy, has supported Kali. He is making all the efforts to deprive me of the glory. It is he, who has patronized the language of Mlecchas for the destruction of the gods, for supporting Mlecchas for the increase of their strength and given it the form of Sanskrit. Besides, they have popularized the Prakrit language among the Aryans.

79-91. Therefore, I have taken refuge with you. You kindly save me.'’ On hearing these words, I spoke to Devaraja Indra thus- “You ask all the twelve Adityas to incarnate on earth. I also, during the terrible time of Kali, shall also Incarnate on earth myself, In the form of Pravina, Nipuna, Abhijna, Kusala, Krti, Sukhi, Nisnata,, Siksita, Sarvajna, Sugata, Prabhuddha and Buddha would take the forms of Dhata, Mitra, Aryama, Sаkrа, Megha, Pramsu, Bhaga, Vivasvan, Pusa, Savita, Tvastra and Visnu respectively on earth in the Kikata country. All of them denouncing the Vedas, composed the Bauddha literature. Those people handed over the Vedas to the Munis. Because of their denouncing the Vedas, such of the gods who had incarnated on earth, attracted the disease of leprosy. Then they reached before Visnu and offered prayer to him. Getting pleased with their prayer, the lord with his yogic powers, relieved them of the disease of leprosy. But because of the blemish, the Bauddhas, inspite of their being illustrious, became humble. In the first half, there was Neminatha and from the lower half, the Bauddhas emerged. For the destruction of the Bauddhas and for the welfare of the people, the king Indradyumna arrived from the heaven in the Indus valley. He built a temple (at Puri) where the lord lives in the form of a woodstone. Because of the stay of Yajnamsa at that place, its glory was increased. He established Dharma there which grants moksa. With the increase of the glory of the place, there was no distinction among the different varnas between Vedic dharma and the vratas, nor was there any special arrangement for achieving moksa. Lord Jagannatha stays there at Puri for the purification of those, who had practiced the language of Yavanas or had an audience with the Bauddhas or used the language of Yavanas. In the age of Kali, the people get purified by an audience with me,”

## Chapter 156. Krsnacaitanya described

1-2. Suta said- Listening to the words of immensely intelligent Jagannatha, Krsnacaitanya said- “O lord, whatever has been spoken by you for the welfare of the living beings, you speak on the same, besides the story of the birth of Bauddha in detail.

3-11. Jagannatha said- After the lapse of a thousand years of Kali, Kanva - the son of Kasyapa arrived on earth. The divine girl Aryavati was the beloved wife of the sage Kanva. With the permission of Indra, both of them reached the bank of the river Sarada. Reaching there, Kanva most humbly recited the stotras of goddess Sarasvati - the dweller of Kuruksetra, from the Vedas, who lives there in the form of earth. Getting pleased with Kanva, the goddess Sarasvati, within a year, bestowed a boon to him for the expansion of the land of Aryans. Thereafter, the noble couple gave birth to ten sons possessing the Arya wisdom. They were known by the names of Upadhyaya, Diksita, Pathaka, Sukla, Misra, Agnihotri, Dvivedi, Trivedi, Pandeya and Caturvedi. All of them had the qualities according to their names. At the age of twelve years, all of them adored the goddess Sarasvati. Getting pleased with their tapas, the goddess Sarada created the girls with her sakti, who were given over to them and who were known by the names of Upadhyayi, Diksita, Pathaki, Suklika, Misrani, Agnihotrini, Dvivedini, Trivedini, Pandayani and Caturvedini.

12-20. Those girls produced sixteen sons each by serving their respective husbands, who propagated the their gotra (yamsa). Those sons came to be known by the names of Kasyapa, Bharadvaja, Visvamitra, Gautama, Jamadagni, Vasistha, Vatsa, Gautama, Parasara, Garga, Atri, Bhrgu, Angira, Srngi, Katyayana and Yajnavalkya respectively. Subsequently, at the command of the goddess Sarasvati, Kanva went to the Misra country. Reaching there, he subjugated ten thousand Mlecchas by teaching them the Sanskrit language. Thereafter, together with the Mlecchas, he entered the Brahmavarta country. Arriving here, all of them adored the goddess Sarasvati with devotion. The goddess Sarasvati was pleased with their devotion. After five years, she converted them as Sudras with their wives. Thereafter, the Mlecchas having a number of sons, started the profession of artisans for their livelihood. Out of them, two thousand of the Mlecchas became the Vaisyas, the best of whom was the Асarуа Prthu, who was the servant of Kasyapa. He performed tapas for twelve years. At that point of time, the lord Kanva granted him a boon and made him a king of a city named Rajaputra. Subsequently, his queen named Rajanya produced a son named Magadha, who was made the ruler of the town named Magadha.

21-35. Thereafter, Kanva - the son of Kasyapa left for the heavenly abode. On his departure for the heaven, Mlecchas of Sudra varna adored Indra - the lord of Saci by performing a yajna. Getting disturbed with the same, together with his relatives, Indra was born in the Brahmana race and made efforts to usurp the Vedas, under the name of Jina and his wife was known by the name of Jayani. Both of them were born in the Kikata country by the union of Kasyapa and Aditi, beside the Adityas for the welfare of the world. At Bodhagaya located over the bank of the river Karmanasa, they had a discussion with the people well-versed in the Bauddha dharma. They snatched away the Vedas from the Sudras and went to the city of Visala. Then awakening the sages there who had been undergoing samadhi, handed over the Vedas to them. Thereafter, all the gods departed from the earth and went to the heaven. Subsequently, the Mlecchas as well as their followers, who had been reciting the Vedas, were converted to Buddhists. By the influence of Sarasvati, the Aryans were in majority there who had performed havya and kavya for the sake of the gods and the pitrs, by which the gods felt extremely satisfied. After the lapse of two thousand and seven hundred years of the age of Kali, with the inspiration of the daitya king Bali, who was master in illusion as well as the preceptor of Sakyasimha, he became famous by the name of Gautama who was always inclined towards the expansion of the side of the daityas. He went to all the holy places and established his yantras there. Any one of the Bauddha who reached under him, he was deprived of the tuft as well as the sacred thread and embraced the position of the mixed breed. Such type of Aryans were ten crores in number, who were converted to the Buddhist faith. The remaining five lakhs of the Aryans migrated to the mountain peaks. On the other hand, with the influence of the Vedas, the forty princes of Agnivamsa who were the great warriors, drove out the Buddhists from their kingdom. They had forced the Aryans to live beyond the Vindhyas who fortified the system of varnasrama. In the auspicious land of the Aryans, the number of Aryans who dwelt there was five lakhs.

36-48. Suta said- On hearing this speech, Yajnamsadeva, who was Narayana incarnate on earth and the disciple of lord Jagannatha, started propagating the Vedic faith. Nityananda - the best of the Brahmanas, accepted to be the disciple of Jagannatha, offering his salutation to him. At that point of time, Aniruddha getting pleased, applied an auspicious tilakam over the foreheads of both of them, which became famous in the world. The preceptor and his brother, getting pleased, spoke to their disciples- “Usapati and Padmanabha, having looked at the body of lord Jagannatha shall achieve the heaven and such of the people who would gracefully accept their prasada, he would recite the Vedas for crores of years and possess enormous riches during that period. The sage Markandeya sighted lord Krsna under the banyan tree and after taking bath in the ocean, one who takes bath in the Indradyumna tank, he is never reborn. A person who listens to this story with faith and devotion, he earns the merit of performing the pilgrimage of Jagannathapuri. Accordingly, such of the Vaisnavas, who had thus listened to the speeches of Yajnamsa and had accepted the same, they had proceeded on to the heaven. О Brahmana, in the meantime, at the prayer offered by Kali, the daitya Bali becoming remorseful, said to Maya-danava- “The Mleccha Sukandara, who always tries his best for my progress, should be made my helper urgently." On hearing these words of Bali, Maya, who had been quite a learned one, accompanied with a hundred of his daityas, arrived here over the land of activity. I Reaching here, he summoned the wicked people of Mleccha race and made them read the geometry twenty one times.

*mukhe sādhavamantraśca babhūva hitadāyakaḥ \|*

49-61. Thereafter, being well-versed in art of yantra (machine), the Mlecchas fixed the machines in all the seven purls, which increased the strength of the Mlecchas. Whosoever reached under the machine, he got converted as Mleccha. О hearing about this process, the Aryans created a huge pathetic sound. On hearing that sound, the Vaisnava disciples of Krsnacaitanya and his servants as well, started to recite the divine mantra of their preceptor and travelled to those cities. Both the disciples of Ramananda, on reaching Ayodhya, by reciting it in the opposite manner, changed the form of the Vaisnava mantra. The symbol of a trident was drawn over the forehead in white and red colour. The neck was adored with the rosary of holy basil. Their tongue was dubbed in the name of Rama. With the influence of Ramananda, the Mleccha Vaisnavas of Ayodhya were changed into Mleccha Samyogi Vaisnavas. The intelligent Nimbaditya together with his disciples made a pilgrimage to Kancipuram. On the royal road, he spotted the Mleccha-yantra. Then with the reverse reciting of the mantra given to him by his preceptor, he made it popular among the people. At his advice, the people of the place made the leaves of bamboo tree over their foreheads in the form of a line and wore a rosary around the neck, reciting the mantra of Gopi-vallabha. Whosoever reached under their shade was turned as Vaisnava. In this way, the Mleccha ascetics became the purified Vaisnavas. Then Visnusvami, together with his disciples, went on pilgrimage to Haridvara. Reaching there and making use of the adverse mantra, the yantra was purified. The people who reached under the same, were turned as pure Vaisnavas. In their form, there were the sectarian marks on the forehead in the form of two lines, with a red spot in the centre. The neck was adorned with the rosary of holy basil, besides reciting of the Madhava mantra always. The Haripriya Madhavacarya went on pilgrimage to Mathura.

## \|\| 2.156.62-64 \|\|

*rājamārge sthitaṃ yantraṃ vilomaṃ sa cakāra ha \|*  
*tadadho ye gatā lokā vaiṣṇavāstasya pakṣagāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*karavīrapatrasadṛśaṃ lalāṭe tilakaṃ śubham \|*

62-64. Finding the yantra over the Rajapatha, it was put on the reverse side, as a result of which the people reaching under him, were turned as Vaisnavas. The Vaisnavas required the leaf of oleander to be drawn over the forehead as tilakam which was painted upto the tip of the nose. The neck was decorated with the rosary of holy basil and the auspicious name of Radhakrsna was recited from the mouth. At the command of Ramanuja, Sankaracarya together with his disciples, went to the city of Kasi.

*viśvanāthetitanmantraṃ teṣāṃ tatra babhūva ha \|\| 72 \|\|*

65-72. Reaching there, he turned the yantra in a reverse position and propagated the Saiva faith. All the people who collected under it, were converted as Saivas. Their foreheads were decorated with Tripundra and the neck was decorated with the rosary of Rudraksa beads, while the name of Govinda was always recited from the mouth. Then the comfortable Ramanuja proceeded to Totadari. In this form, there were two upward lines over the forehead, with a thin line of yellow colour was always drawn. The neck as usual was decorated with the rosary of holy basil. The virtuous Varahamihira went to Ujjayini and made the yantra infructuous and propagated the Saiva dharma among the people of the place. In that form, the forehead has to be plastered with ashes of the funereal pyre and the neck is to be decorated with the rosary of Rudraksa beads, while the auspicious name of Siva is to be recited from the mouth always. Vanibhusana himself went to Kanyakubja and propagated the Sakta faith. In this form, the crescent is to be curved over the forehead. The rosary of red sandal is to be worn around the neck and the auspicious name of the goddess has to be recited from the mouth. Dhanvantari on the other hand reached Prayaga and the yantra was made ineffective by the reverse method. Among the people who had collected there, the crescent with a red spot was painted over the forehead. A rosary of red sandal was to be worn around the neck and this method was propagated among the people. The intelligent Bhattojidiksita went to Utpalaranya and propagated the use of tripundra of red sandal paste. Besides the neck was to be decorated with rosary of Rudraksa beads. Then auspicious name of Visvanatha was to be recited.

73-80. Ropana went to Istika, metalized the yantra and propagated the Brahmamarga among the people. Similarly, Jayadeva, the great devotee of Visnu, went to Dvaraka and made the yantra infructuous. He propagated among the people to decorate the forehead with a red line and decorate the neck with the rosary of casaia (padmaksa), reciting the name of Govinda. Thus the followers of Vaisnava, Saiva and Sakta faiths were immensely increased. The learned people have conceived Sakti as absolute and Vaisnavas as possessing attributes. The one who is the combination of both, have been termed as Saivas. Thereafter, the thirty three gods, entering into mediation, purified the earth. At Santipura, Nityananda took his samadhi, Hari at Nadiha, Kabira in Magadha country, Raidasa at Kalinjara and Sadhana did so at Naimisaranya and purified the relevant regions. Because of the performance of these people, even today, the great Vaisnavas living on the earth, are performing yajnas at a place known as Merumurddha and expanding the yajnas. Accordingly, I have narrated the life story of Yajnamsadeva, by listening to which the men and women earn great merits. Thereafter, Maya and other demons fled from their abodes and reaching before the daityaraja, said to him.

## Chapter 157. Description of the collateral history of the Age of Kali

1-14. Suta said- Bali - the lord of the daityas, listening to the great victory of the gods, summoned a daitya named Rosana and said to him- “You, together with the son named Sarusa of Timirlinga, go to the same place and perform the great task of the daityas.” On hearing these words, the said daitya, while living in Dehall and getting enraged in his heart, started destroying the people who followed the Devamarga. After ruling for five years, he got a son named Babara, who ruled the country for twenty years. Subsequently, he got a son named Humayu, who getting intoxicated, humiliated even the gods and drove them out. Feeling painful at heart, all the gods assembled in the orchard of Nadiha and adored lord Krsnacaitanya variously. Hearing it, lord Visnu himself getting enraged, created terrific disturbances in his country. The people of the country who had been working in the army as soldiers, defeated Humayun and drove him out. At that point of time, Maharastra Sesasaka reached Dehali and became victorious over the Mleccha king of Dehali. He remained the king of Dehali for five years and increased the religious activities there. At the same time, Mukundasa Brahmacan, who had his birth in the race of Sankaracarya, together with his twenty disciples, performed tapas at Prayaga. The said Brahmacan, listening to the desecration of the wicked Mleccha king Babara, immolated himself in the burning fire flames. His body was reduced to ashes. His disciples also reduced themselves to ashes, with the intention of the destruction of the king. Once the sage Mukunda drank his own hair of the body with milk of the cow, and because of that blemish, he had to be born in the Mleccha family. At that point of time, Humayu was living in Kasmira. Brahmacan Mukunda was born to Humayu as his son. At that time of the birth of the son, a divine voice from the sky declared- “This son would be the best of all and fortunate at the same time. This type of son has never been born with the Pisacas till now, nor would he be born in future. Therefore, the son of Humayu would be known as Akbara.

15-28. The ascetic who had the disciples like Sridhara, Sripati, Sambhu, Varenya, Madhuvrati, Vimala, Devavan, Soma, Varddhana, Vartaka, Ruci, Mandhata, Manakan, Kesava, Madhava, Madhu, Devapi, Somapa, Sura and Madana, the same Mukunda Brahmana has been born as your son.” Listening to the divine voice, Humayun, getting pleased, gave away charities to the hungry people and he brought up that son with enormous love and affection. When the son was ten years old, he went to Dehali and defeated Sesasanka and occupied the throne of Dehali. After occupying the throne for a year by his father, Akbara became the king of Dehali. With the crowning of Akbara as the king, the seven people who were his disciples in the earlier birth, reached in his court and occupied the positions which were appropriate to the status of each one of them. Kesava, Ganasena, Vaijavaka and Madhava had been born in the Mleccha families while Haridasa and Madhu were born in the race of Madhvacarya and became the Vaisnava singers. Devapi of earlier birth became Birabala, who having been born in a Brahmana family, achieved a boon from the goddess Sarasvati and became a reputed minister. Somapa and Manasimha, having been born in the Gautama family, became the army commander of Arya king. On the other hand, having been born in a Brahmana family, Sura became a competent Pandita, who was the great friend of the king and came to be known by the Bilvamangala. He was well aware of the performance of a heroine as well as those of the prostitutes. Madana who was born in the eastern country, became an excellent dancer and became famous by the name of Candana who was well-versed in the sports of seclusion. His thirteen disciples were also born in other countries. Sridhara, who was well aware of the enemy activities, was born as a son of Anapa and was known as Tulasisarma. He was a competent poet of the Puranas. He was educated by a woman. He went to Raghavananda of Kasi and became his disciple.

29-37. Не followed the path of Ramananda. Sripati became blind and followed the ideology of Madhavacarya. He subsequently came to be known as Suradasa. He was the best poet of Krsnalila or the sports of Krsna. Haripriya Sambhu was born in the family of Candrabhatta and followed Ramananda. He used to sing the glory of the devotees of the gods with devotion. Varenya became popular by the name of Sograbhuk and followed the path of Ramananda, who inspite of being learned and spiritual, had mastery in the science of meters. Madhu became popular by the name of Kilaka who performed Ramalila and was the follower of Ramananda. He became popular by the name of Vimaladivakara. While performing as Sita, he became a great devotee of Ramananda. Devavana came to be known as Kesava and embraced the path of Visnusvami, who had composed Kavipriya. But he had to embrace the death. He composed a treatise under the title of Ramajyotsna. On the other hand, Soma was bom as Vyasa and embraced the path of Nimbaditya. He composed an investigative treatise on Ekantakrida (sport in seclusion). Varddhana composed a work under the title of Jnanamala and followed the path Of Raidasa.

38-42. Vartaka on the other hand embraced the ideology of Ropana. Ruci became popular by the name of Rocana and embraced the ideology of Madhavacarya. He created several types of vehicles and then proceeded on to the heaven. Mandhata was born in a Kayastha family and attained a royal position. Madhavacarya composed Srimadbhagavata in local language. Manakara gave importance to the female form and attained a female body, who was the princess of a king and became popular by the name of Mira. The learned people have interpreted that only a female having the beauty of Laksmi and the speed of an elephant can be called as Mira. She was the disciple of Madhavacarya.

43-56. Thus I have concluded the topic of the language or literature, which is form of a poetic composition and bestows comfort, in the terrific age of Kali. О Brahmana, thus I have spoken on the literary aspect of the matter which is quite soothing in the harsh age of Kali. The king named Akbara then proceeded to Vaikuntha with his fifty disciples in a peaceful manner. His son named Salima (Jahangir) ruled the country for the same period for which his father did so. Khurdaka (Khurram) was the son of Salimes, who ruled for a period of ten years. Of the four sons that he had, Navaranga or Aurangzeb was the middle son, who became victorious over his father and brothers, and usurped the kingdom. He was the daitya Andhaka in his earlier birth. At the command of the daitya king Bali, he was born in Bharata — the land of Activity. He desecrated several of the images of the deities, observing which the gods said to Krsnacaitanya- “He has been born of the amsa of the daitya and becoming the king, he is desecrating the images of the deities and is supporting the dailyas” Hearing these words. Yajnamsadeva, who was camping in the Nadiha orchard, pronounced a curse on him for his destruction with his family. The wicked ruler ruled for forty nine years. Thereafter, a ruler named Sivaji, who was the supporter of the gods and was born in a Brahmana family in Maharastra, fought with him. Killing the wicked ruler, his son was crowned as the king in his place, after which Sivaji returned to the southern country. The son of the ruler of Dehali known as Aloma ruled for five years, after which he attracted the disease of fistula in anus and met with his end. Aloma died when one thousand seven hundred and seventy years of vikrama era had passed. In the race of Talana, Bali was reborn in the Mleccha race. At the end of the Mleccha rule, the kingship was usurped by him. He ruled the earth for ten years.

57-70. Thereafter, he was killed by his enemies and he proceeded on to the daityaloka. His son Mahamada ruled the country for a period of twenty years. Subsequently, a daitya named Nadara attacked his country and was victorious over him. He reached Khurja country. Subsequently, his son named Mahamatsya usurped the throne of his father and occupied his position. He ruled for five years. After the death of the wicked ruler of the Talana family, Madhava ruled for ten years over the throne of Dehali. He established suzerainty over the entire kingdom of Aloma. In that country, several of the native rulers were included besides a number of the village heads. At that point of time, with the disappearing of the concourse of rulers, each head of the village was known as Raja. Thus, such Rajas ruled the village for twenty years. Thereafter, all the gods went to Krsnacaitanya and said to him about (their grievances). Hearing them and finding that the people on earth had been badly suffering, Yajnamsadeva meditated for some time and then said to the goddess- “In earlier times, the intelligent Raghava defeating Ravana - the chief of the Raksasas, sprinkled the rain of nectar and brought back the monkeys to their lives. At that point of time, the monkeys like Vikata, Vrjita, Jala, Varlina, Simhala, Java and Sumatra said to Sri Rama- “You grant us the boon desired by us.” Hearing them, the lord Rama being aware of their desire, gave them the girls who were bom of the divine damsels by Ravana and then he spoke to them with delight-“The island created by Jalandhara which are popular by your names, you would be bom as some of those kings and became their well wishers. The terrific Mlecchas were bom of the body of the divine cow Nandini. From them, the Gurunda race was bom. Those people are stationed there.

71-80. You patronize that country by defeating the Gurundas.” On hearing the words of Rama, the monkeys offered their salutation to Sri Rama and proceeded on to their respective islands. The Gurundas who had been bom in the Vikata race and whose faces compared with those of the monkeys, were the followers of the Buddhist faith. They reached there for the purpose of trade, but their hearts were more inclined towards Isa. They were truthful, overpowered the passions and devoid of anger. They adored the Sungod as well. All of you should go there and work for the welfare of the people rapidly.” On hearing these words, all the gods offering their salutation to £rl Rama, proceeded on to journey and established their capital city at Kalikata. The queen of the king Vikata of the western island was known as Vikatavati, who ruled the country in eight excellent ways. Her husband was known by the name of Pulomarci. At that point of time, a thousand eight hundred and forty of the vikrama era had lapsed, when he became the king. There were seven kings in the Gurunda country. During the time of the eighth king of the Gurunda country, daityaraja Bali who was the supporter of the side of Kala, summoned the demon Mura 'and captured the king named Vadila and exercised his control over his heart.

81-84. He polluted his wisdom in such a way that he started desecrating the images of the gods. At that point of time, the gods who had been enshrined in those images, went to Yajnamsadeva and offering their salutation to him, narrated the entire story of the Raksasa. On hearing the tale of the Raksasa, Yajnamsadeva pronounced the Gurundas, who were the followers of Bauddha dharma- “All the Gurundas who live under the Buddhists, shall get destroyed.” When he so cursed the Gurundas, their number was thirty thousand. All of them met with their death and proceeded to the abode of Yama.

85-97. Because of that curse, even the king Vadila was also killed. Thereafter, the ninth Gurunda king known by the name of Mekala, who was extremely powerful, ruled judiciously for twelve years. At that point of time, the judicious mode of governance of the Arynas was becoming more and more popular everywhere. Thereafter, the tenth Gurunda king known by the name of Lardala ruled the country for thirty two years with a religious mind. After the death of Lardala, the silent Aryans of Makaranda race, who had been living in the Himalaya, who were of tawny brown colour, vast and round foreheads, besides having small noses, one lakh of them reached in Dehali. Out of them, Arjika occupied the throne of DehalL Devakarna, his son belonging to the Gangotri mountain, with the intention of expanding the kingdom, performed severe tapas for twelve years, as a result of which the goddess Ganga went to Brahmaloka of her own accord. Thereafter, Kubera went to the prince and bestowed on him the great title of Arya-mandalika. Since that date, the king Devakarna came to be known by the name of Mandalika. The same king ruled over the earth for sixty years. Eight of his descendant kings occupied that throne for two hundred years each and then proceeded on to the heaven. Their eleventh king known as Pannagari, who was silent, ruled for forty years, making all the efforts. He was ultimately bitten by snakes and then proceeded on to the heaven. Thus, the rule of the Maurya tribe on earth has been described.

1-14. Suta said- After the lapse of two thousand two hundred and sixty four years of the vikrama era, a king named Bhutanandi defeated the descendants of the Mauna-vamsa, who were living there with their riches, cereals or wealth and prosperity. They were a lakh and a half in number and were also called the Kuberas. He exercised his control over their territory. At that point of time, the royal race of Nagas ruled over the area of Kilakila which was a popular city in the south-east. The Nagas including Pundarika and other kings ruled there. While they were ruling, they became adorable in every house. The worship of Svaha, Svadha, Vasatkara and other gods started there. Leaving aside the gods, the people started living over the peak of the Meru mountain. Kubera collected the cereals from all the sides for Sakra and gave the sixth part of it to the gods. Whatever valuables like gems and gold were available in the Mauna country, were ail deposited in the treasures. Creating the position of a Mandalika, Bhutanandi was placed over the same. He ruled the country for a period of fifty years. Thereafter, Sisunandi was crowned as the king. He adoring the Nagas, neglected the gods and ruled the country for twenty years. After him, his younger brother Yasonandi ruled the country, who also worshipped the Nagas. He ruled for twenty five years. After him, his son named Praviraka was crowned as the king. He ruled for eleven years over the land of activity. Once the said king invaded the Bahlika country with his army and fought a terrific battle with the Pisaca Mlecchas. A lakh of Mleccha were killed in that war. At the same time, eight thousand of the devotees of Nagas were killed. During the same period, the king Badala had been quite powerful in Roma country.

15-28. Yasonandi called him from Roma and had with him his daughter Jalavati in marriage. Thereafter, by getting the daughter of the king of Mlecchas, Badala returned to his country. After some time, with the union of both of them, a powerful son was born to the royal couple, who came to be known as Bahlika. He adored the Nagas. Having been born in that race, thirteen kings respectively ruled for four hundred years and then came to an end. During the time of rule of Bahlika ruler Ayomukha, the Pitrganas approached Krsnacaitanya and offering their salutation to him, said- “O lord, you listen to our prayer respectfully. The rulers of Naga dynasty have driven us out of our country. We had been flourishing because of the performing of the sraddhas and oblations. With the expansion of pitrs, Soma get an increase. With the increase of Soma, the gods flourish and with the flourishing of the gods, Brahma also flourishes. With the flourishing of Brahma, the people of several houses flourish. Therefore, О lord, you kindly save the traditional people like us.” On hearing these words, lord Yajnamsa, for the flourishing of the Arya race, took birth as a son of Pusyamitra. Soon after his birth, the child appeared like the child of eight years. That boy was born without the human touch. Defeating the Ayomukha Bahlika rulers, he drove them out of the country. Thereafter, he himself became the ruler. As the king Vikramaditya having been bom of the amsa of Siva, had defeated the rulers who were the supporters of Gandharvas and he himself became the adorable by all, similarly, at that point of time, the king Pusyamitra defeated the rulers of Naga dynasty who had awful and round face and was himself adored by all. At the time of the crowning of the king Pusyamitra, two thousand seven hundred and seventy two years of the vikrama era were passed.

*chadmanā mayadevena pitṛpūjā vinirmitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vṛthā śramaṃ vṛthā karma nṛṇāṃ ca pitṛpūjanam \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ vihasyāha mahīpatiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bhavānmūrkho mahāmūḍho na jānīṣa paraṃ phalam \|*  
*bhuvarloke na ye dṛṣṭāḥ śūnyabhūtāśca bhāsvarāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ye tu te vai pitṛgaṇāḥ piṇḍarūpavimānagāḥ \|*  
*satputraiśca vidhānena piṇḍadānaṃ ca yatkṛtam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tadvimānaṃ nabhojātaṃ sarvānandapradāyakam \|*

*gītāṣṭādaśakādhyāyaiḥ saptaśatyāścaritrakaiḥ \|*

*śrāddhatarpaṇahīnā ye dṛśyante mānavā bhuvi \|*  
*te sarve nārakā jñeyāḥ kulamekottaraṃ śatam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*śrāddhakarma mahāndharmaḥ śrāddho'yaṃ sarvakāraṇam \|*  
*iti śrutvā sa gandharvaḥ kalīrājo'tra dehinām \|\| 42 \|\|*

29-42. That Dharmamtirti king ruled the country for a hundred years. The same king carried on the works of the repair and upkeep of the temples at Ayodhya, Mathura, Haridvara, Kanci, Kasi, Avantika as well as Dvaraka. It is he who established several of the places of pilgrimage on earth, including those at Kuru, Sukara (Varaha), Padma, Naimisaranya, Utpalaranya and Vrndavana. At that point of time, Kali, who denounced the gods and the manes, took to the form of a Brahmana and along with a Gandharva, proceeded to the place of king Pusyamitra. Reaching there, offering their salutation to him, they said- “O compassionate king, kindly listen our prayer. The practice of performing of sraddha and oblation which is meant for the adoration of manes and which are in vogue in the country, is not considered to be appropriate. Because to worship the manes on earth is the display of ignorance. Therefore, in this land of activity, one who proceeds to the heaven, he reaching there has to go through eighty four lakhs of births. Therefore, the gods have considered in detail about the practice of worship of manes and found that the rites performed for the manes are of no consequence.” On hearing these words, the king laughed and said- “You are not fools, but great fools. Therefore, you cannot be aware of the excellent merit earned by a person for performing these rites. Whatever void is visible in the Bhuvarloka or the glittering found therein, are the pitrs moving over the flames. The pindas which are offered by the noble people, they reaching the sky, become the planes which provide all the comforts. Subsequently, the planes which are built by the pindas of payasam remain there for full one year. It is mentioned in the eighteenth chapter of Srimadbhagavadgita and in the Durga-saptasati that the pindas which are offered, remain there for three hundred years. Such of the people who are deprived of the sraddha and oblation, their descendants have to remain in the hell for a hundred generations. Therefore, the performing of the sraddha is extremely auspicious and is the cause of all.” On hearing these words, the king Kali along with the Gandharvas were immensely pleased and offered salutation to the king.

43-56. Thereafter, the excellent king Pusyamitra was addressed by Kali thus- ‘О king, I happen to be your slave. I intend to be friendly with you. By so doing, you in the world would be known as Pusyamitra - the friend of Kali and which shall be established in the world for all times to come. As Vaitala - the friend of Vikramaditya, performed all his tasks, similarly, while serving you, I shall perform all your tasks.” Thus speaking, the valorous Kali made the king to mount his back, flew in the sky and travelled through all the seven islands. The king Pusyamitra together with Kali propagated the Aryadharma, which had been extinguished since long at certain places. At the time of his death, the lustre of Pusyamitra was absorbed into the body of Yajnamsadeva. At that point of time, the king Sugada of Andhradesa merged the country of Pusyamitra into his own country and ruled over it. He ruled the land of Aryas for twenty years and thereafter, he proceeded on to the heaven. Subsequently, sixty rulers of his race, who were the followers of different faiths, occupied the throne. After the death of Pusyamitra when three hundred years passed, the king of Andhradesa also met with his end. For fifty years thereafter, the land was without a ruler. During that period, the thieves and the decoits looted the small people and made their lives miserable. This resulted into the spread of poverty among the people. The land was deprived of gold, observing which the gods again offered prayers to the lord- “In the country of Kausala, there is a king who is the amsa of Surya besides being the enemy of the Raksasas. He is devoted to the gods. At my command, he would be the king of the river bank ” Thus speaking, lord Visnu disappeared from the scene and reached the Devaloka. Subsequently, the enemy of the Raksasas was crowned as the king of Ayodhya. The same king recovered the wealth usurped by the Raksasas from the people after defeating them. In every village, the price of each bead was fixed at eight gold coins.

57-70. Similarly, the hundred brass coins were made equal to one silver coin, five brass coins were equal to one copper coin, five copper coins were made equal to Nagadhatu. Accordingly, the sequence of Nagavamsa was established. The price of iron was fixed at a hundred vamsa. He ruled the country for fifty years and then he proceeded onto the Suryaloka. After him, sixty rulers of his family ruled the country. After the passing of seven hundred years, subsequent to the death of Pusyamitra, the rulers of Kausalavamsa proceeded to the heaven. Subsequent to that, the land was without the Mandalika rulers. At that point of time, many of the small rulers were ruling the country. In the meantime, the king of the Vaidara country reached the Arya country and with a lakh of his soldiers, conquered the small principalities and became leader of a Mandallka. The said king deputed artisans in each and every village for the creation of the attractive art works, who believed in the mixed breed. During the ruler of that king, the Brahmanas and Ksatriyas remained there by name only. The Arya people took to trade of Vaisyas, while the Sudras became the masons. In his regime, the people adored the deities only casually. Thus he ruled over the land of activity for sixty years. Subsequently, six rulers of his race ruled the country, one after the other. After the lapse of sixteen hundred years of the death of Pusyamitra, during the time of the terrific age of Kali, the kings of the far off places were completely wiped out and again the countries was divided into small principalities. Then after a lapse of four hundred years, a king named Kalamali was crowned as the king of the Naisadha country. He conquered the small states and established his capital in the same city, which was located over the river Yamuna and was spread in an area of one yojana. came to be known as the Kalakala country.
